**“What blemish he gave, the like shall he be compelled to suffer.”** — Namely, whosesoever virtue he has bruised, his own virtue shall be bruised and reckoned as nothing.
24.21:
**“He that striketh a beast,”** — a foolish, dull man
**“shall render another.”**
• himself for the beast
• HE THAT STRIKETH A BEAST etc. These things according to the letter were necessary for the Jews, who could not take in: If one strike thee on thy right cheek, turn to him also the other. But since they were ill-willed, they wished to inflict evils and not suffer them. Therefore they had to be called back from crime by fear of a penalty in return.
**“He that striketh”** — by harming in any way
**“a man”** — a discerning, rational man
**“shall be punished.”** — himself as a man
24.22:
**“Equal”** — or: right
**“judgment let there be among you, whether he be a stranger,”** — newly joined
**“or a native”** — brought up in the Church from infancy
24.23: **“And Moses spoke to the children of Israel: and they brought forth him that had blasphemed, without the camp, and they stoned him. And the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses.”** — AND THEY BROUGHT FORTH etc. He shows the law confirmed by the very trial, that you too may fear to blaspheme and flee sin, which not only the ruler but the whole multitude avenges. For all ought in common to punish blasphemers, who did not fear to disparage the author of all, and all to separate them from him.

25.2:
**“Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: When you shall have entered into the land”** — good conversation
**“which I will give you,”** — in the Law and the precepts
25.3:
**“Six years”**
• through the whole time of the present life
• thus
**“thou shalt sow”** — that afterward the land may keep sabbath
**“Thy field”** — the law, in the working of which the people of the Jews laboured
**“and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard,”** — the Gospel life, whose true vine is Christ, we the branches, the Father the husbandman.
**“and shalt gather the fruits thereof:”** — THOU SHALT SOW THY FIELD etc. By the field and the vineyard, when he forbade the one to be sown and the other to be pruned, every kind of land is to be understood: for neither in an olive yard nor in a field of any other kind is anything to be worked.
25.4:
**“in the seventh year”** — in eternal rest
**“there shall be a sabbath to the land, of the resting of the Lord:”**
• because there will be no need to work at anything, neither the works of the Law nor of the Gospel
• WHEN YOU SHALL HAVE ENTERED etc. HESYCHIUS. The land is good conversation, of which it is said: "Thy good spirit shall lead me into the right land." Six years thou shalt sow thy field etc.: while, namely, we are in this life and in the visible creation, which the number six signifies. For in six days all things that are seen were created; but in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath to the land, of the resting of the Lord. For when after the present time the sabbath comes, of which Paul says: "There remaineth a sabbatism for the people of God", which the seventh day marks, on which God "rested from his works", namely the visible ones, there will no longer be a time for working.
**“thy field”** — fulfilling the commandments by this common tillage
**“thou shalt not sow, nor thy vineyard”**
• he names the whole from a part
• by keeping the commandments of the Gospel purely
**“prune.”** — thou shalt tend
25.5:
**“What the ground shall bring forth of itself, thou shalt not reap:”** — What the natural law suggests needs neither teacher nor letters.
**“WHAT IT SHALL BRING FORTH OF ITSELF”** — Of the things, namely, which we do here, we shall eat the fruit in the future. Whence: "For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands: blessed art thou, and it shall be well with thee" etc.
**“neither the grapes of thy firstfruits”** — Septuagint: the grape of sanctification, that is, the mysteries of Christ
25.6:
**“But they shall be unto you for meat, to thee and to thy manservant, to thy maidservant and thy hireling,”** — Whom you invited, you did not subject as a servant and a handmaid.
**“and to the strangers that sojourn with thee:”**
• Septuagint: to the sojourner, that is, to the philosopher, who lies near thee, who hast entered the good land
• BUT THEY SHALL BE etc. The Lord does not forbid eating what has sprung up of itself, but storing it up for one's own use.
25.7:
**“to thy beasts”** — to the unlearned
**“and to thy cattle.”** — to unbelievers who have been tamed
**“All things that grow shall be meat”** — they will think to live for ever and ever
25.8:
**“Thou shalt also number to thee seven weeks”** — Septuagint: seven rests
**“THOU SHALT ALSO NUMBER”** — Let us ask the Jews: if the lawgiver honoured the seventh day (as they say) and commanded rest from works, why did he command the fiftieth year to be celebrated? For seven weeks of years make forty-nine. There would therefore be no need to rest in the fiftieth, unless the law marked a mystery which the weakness of the Jews did not grasp. For a twofold consummation of all things is signified by God: one, of each singly; the other, common to all, when there will be no time of working. In the earlier passages he hints at the first, in these the second.
25.9:
**“And thou shalt sound the trumpet in the seventh month, the tenth day of the month,”** — It signifies perfection, because the number ten is perfect.
**“in the time of the expiation in all your land.”**
• because all shall be freed from corruption, to whom it was said in Adam: "Earth thou art, and into earth thou shalt go."
• SEVEN WEEKS etc. Human time is divided into a week of days. When therefore this number has been multiplied in itself, and the whole age of the world completed, and the time rolled round has come to its end, the fiftieth will follow, as if upon the forty-ninth year, in which will be the resurrection. Whence he adds: Thou shalt sound the trumpet in the seventh month etc. Whence the Apostle: "With the trumpet of God he shall come down from heaven, and the dead who are in Christ shall rise" incorrupt. For the trumpet must go before him who raises them: therefore he commanded the trumpet to sound in the forty-ninth year, in which is the common consummation.
**“IN THE SEVENTH MONTH”** — Because Christ came as it were in the seventh month of the age of the world: the first month, which was in paradise; the second, up to the flood; the third, up to Abraham; the fourth, until the going down into Egypt; the fifth, up to the transmigration; the sixth, up to the coming of Christ; the seventh, the coming itself.
25.10:
**“AND THOU SHALT SANCTIFY THE YEAR”** — As if it is to be awaited and thought on in holiness. For we ought to follow peace and holiness, without which no man shall see God.
**“and shalt proclaim remission”** — of all sins, of all labours
**“to all the inhabitants”** — because it is the general resurrection
**“of your land:”** — or: thy
**“for it is the jubilee.”** — initiated, or remitting
**“Every man shall return to his possession,”** — Septuagint: to his country, namely paradise, which is the true country.
**“EVERY ONE”** — Of the patriarchs and prophets. There is a certain family of hospitality, over which Abraham presides. There is also another of chastity, over which Joseph presides. There is also another of meekness, over which Moses presides.
25.11:
**“Because it is the jubilee and the fiftieth year. You shall not sow,”** — as above
**“nor reap the things that of their own accord”** — because it is the time of enjoying, not of working
**“grow in the field, neither shall you gather the firstfruits of the vines,”** — by storing up for one's own use
25.12: **“Because of the sanctification of the jubilee: but as they grow you shall presently eat them.”** — because he will render to every man according to his works
25.13:
**“In the year of the jubilee all shall return”** — We came from God, to whom we must return.
**“to their possessions.”** — the heavenly country, the reward of each, because: "In my Father's house there are many mansions."
25.14:
**“When thou shalt sell”** — by teaching
**“any thing”** — some good doctrine
**“to thy neighbour,”** — to a churchman
**“or shalt buy”** — by discerning
**“of him; grieve not thy brother:”**
• By pressing doctrine beyond his strength, by laying on burdens that cannot be borne.
• WHEN THOU SHALT SELL etc. Each can sell or buy. Whence Paul: We are all yours, as you also are ours.
• According to the letter this instructs us morally to have compassion on our neighbours in contracts, that no one, being too troublesome, should trade upon the necessities of the poor, nor strive to acquire the possessions of others, but lend to the needy and receive back what was lent little by little from the fruits of the fields.
25.15:
**“but according to the number of years of the jubilee”** — or: of praise
**“ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER”** — That is, according to the strength of each. For the years signify age, in which is shown what each can do according to the body.
**“And according to the computation of the fruits”** — according to what the disciple can bear fruit
25.16:
**“The more years remain after the jubilee, the more shall the price increase: and the less time is counted, so much the less”** — or: of less
**“shall the purchase cost.”** — or: the purchase
**“THE MORE”** — That is, if he can work much, he will demand much fruit; if he cannot do much, he will repay little: for this one shall bear thirtyfold fruit, that one sixtyfold, the other a hundredfold.
25.17:
**“Do not afflict”** — by laying on a heavy burden
**“your countrymen, but let every one fear his God:”** — who says: "Take up my yoke upon you, for it is sweet" and: "My burden is light."
**“because I am the Lord your God.”** — who said: "All men take not this word." "He that can take, let him take it."
25.18:
**“Do my precepts, and keep my judgments,”**
• in memory
• DO MY PRECEPTS etc. Lest anyone, having heard of the moderation in selling and buying, become more slothful, and the very condescension do harm, he cautiously adds: Do my precepts etc. For he wishes no one to be idle, but to bear fruit according to his strength. And each one's conscience examines his strength.
• AND MY JUDGMENTS etc. Not corrupting their intention or working; as if someone gives alms, let him not harm one to profit another: for the precept which commanded alms to be given willed it to be just.
**“and fulfil them: that you may dwell in the land”** — that is: by the divine law of spiritual scripture and good conversation, which God commanded to be possessed and tilled.
25.19:
**“And the ground may yield you its fruits,”** — eternal life
**“of which you may eat your fill,”** — "I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear."
**“fearing no man's invasion.”** — either of the devil or of any persecutor
25.20: **“But if you say: What shall we eat the seventh year,”** — in the consummation of each
25.21:
**“I will give you my blessing the sixth year,”** — in which man was reformed
**“and it shall yield”** — man
**“the fruits of three years:”**
• By which we who here, with Christ's help, have cast the seeds of virtues and works may be nourished in eternal beatitude.
• BUT IF YOU SAY etc. Because he had commanded the land to lie idle for two years, lest they be troubled, as if anxious what they should eat or what they should drink, he says: I will give you my blessing etc. And it is to be noted that, whereas Christ says: Be not solicitous for tomorrow, the law commands them not to be solicitous for three years.
• I WILL GIVE YOU MY BLESSING etc. Christ. Whence: "We have blessed you in the name of the Lord", that is, in Christ, who is the name of the Father; who named and manifested the Father to us. He came in the sixth year, that is, in perfection, which the number six signifies; and that he might reform man, whom he had formed on the sixth day: what there is the sixth day, here is called the sixth year, because between our formation and reformation many times flowed by.
25.23:
**“The land also shall not be sold for ever: because it is mine,”**
• not yours, who are strangers
• THE LAND ALSO etc. AUGUSTINE. Other codices have: The land shall not be sold unto profanation; that is, lest anyone dare to sell the land which he received from God to the profane, who would practise impiety in it and worship strange gods. Others: unto confirmation; that is, let the sale not be so confirmed that in the time of remission the seller does not receive it back, because it is mine etc. Therefore whoever has it ought to use it according to my precept.
**“strangers also”** — by being born
**“and sojourners”** — by living, who are compelled to move away by dying
**“with me.”** — Who fill heaven and earth.
25.25:
**“If, being impoverished,”** — having lost spiritual riches
**“thy brother”** — the faithful one
**“sell”**
• to the devil
• taking up the thought of sin
**“his little possession,”** — his conversation
**“and his kinsman will,”** — by kinship of faith
**“he may redeem what he had sold.”**
• IF, BEING IMPOVERISHED, THY BROTHER etc. He teaches in order what our substance is, how we alienate it, how we receive it back. Each one has a good possession, a holy conversation: one has virginity, another is strong in continence; this one excels in the priesthood, that one in the patronage of the poor; each has a possession according to his virtue. But through sloth our thoughts grow weak, and we fall in part from our own possession: he teaches how it is restored.
• HE MAY REDEEM etc. According to that: "If a man be overtaken in any fault, you, who are spiritual, instruct such a one in the spirit of meekness", "bear ye one another's burdens" etc. And so we can free a brother from poverty and redeem his possession, so that in a manner it is common.
25.26:
**“But if he have no kinsman,”** — who may have compassion on him
**“and he himself can find the price”** — of satisfaction
25.27:
**“The value of the fruits shall be counted”** — of good conversation
**“from that time when he sold it:”** — he sinned
**“and the overplus”** — of satisfaction and correction
**“he shall restore to the buyer,”** — he shall set against the devil
**“and so shall receive his possession again.”** — satisfaction being rendered
25.28:
**“But if his hands find not”** — working
**“the means to repay the price,”**
• either by himself or by his neighbour
• so that the wicked thought comes to the act
**“the buyer shall have”** — the devil
**“what he bought,”** — by suggesting wicked things
**“until the year of the jubilee.”** — UNTIL THE YEAR etc. The year, because it has in itself all the hours, and days and months, and all the cycles, signifies perfection. But a sin that is perfected and long-standing is amended only by a perfect penance, in which fasting, prayer, haircloth, almsgiving and tears are carried out: for through these full remission is acquired.
25.29:
**“He that selleth his house”**
• The Synagogue is sold by those to whom it was given to dwell in.
• HE THAT SELLETH HIS HOUSE etc. The seller is not named, nor is a kinsman spoken of. For it is not one, but the whole people; nor of the kindred of the Jews, but of Sodom and Gomorrha.
• HE THAT SELLETH etc. In the chapter above he set out the spiritual conversation of each; here he means to treat generally of the Synagogue or the Church, because the Church of the Gentiles receives liberty, the Synagogue serves for ever, except the Levites, that is, the apostles and those who cleave to them.
**“within the walls of a city,”**
• of the law, of prophecy
• Jerusalem
**“shall have the liberty to redeem it, until one year be expired:”** — that is: in one year only, in which Christ gave remission to all, and above all to the Jews; whence: "That I might preach the acceptable year of the Lord" etc.
**“ORIGEN”** — HE THAT SELLETH etc. Of Jacob it is written: a plain man, dwelling in his house; and of the midwives of the Jews or Hebrews: Because the midwives feared God, they made themselves houses. Fear therefore was the cause of houses for the midwives. But the simplicity and innocence of Jacob made him dwell, or gave him to dwell. This is the house not made with hands in heaven, which no one can build except with the fear of the Lord, no one dwell in except with simplicity of mind and purity of heart. But often he who by acting well, living well and believing rightly has built this house incurs the sin of some debt, and is compelled to sell it to the cruellest of usurers, and to pour his labours over to others. But the clemency of the lawgiver comes to meet him, that within a set time it may be redeemed, if only his hand find the price of penance, gathered namely by tears and found by hands, that is, by the labours of good work. And the year is that in which the Lord came to set at liberty them that are bruised and to give salvation to the penitent. But the house which is in heaven is in a walled city. The wall of heaven is the firmament. Few can have this, those namely who have their conversation in heaven, to whom it is said: "You are God's building." Others have houses in villages which have no wall, but a fruitful field lies beside them; those perhaps who prepare for themselves a dwelling in the land of the living, of whom it is said: "Blessed are the meek: for they shall possess the land." These houses, if perchance a fall has happened, can always be recovered. For if some fault has overtaken us, not a deadly crime, not blasphemy of the faith, which is girt with the wall of the Church's and the apostles' teaching, if it consists in a fault either of speech or of manners, this is to have sold a house which is in a field, or in a village which has no wall. This fault therefore, this sale, can always be repaired, nor is it ever forbidden to do penance for such things; but not for the graver crimes, which is to persevere impenitent in unbelief, to continue in iniquity to the end. For in the graver crimes place for penance is granted only once; the common faults, which we often incur, always admit penance and are always redeemed.
25.30:
**“If he redeem it not,”** — at the coming of Christ
**“and the whole year be fully out, the buyer”** — the devil
**“shall possess it, and his posterity”** — the demons
**“for ever, and it cannot be redeemed, not even in the jubilee.”** — Septuagint: the remission which Christ asked for them, saying: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.
25.31:
**“But if the house be in a village,”** — the Church of the Gentiles
**“that walls”** — the patriarchs, the prophets, the law
**“hath not, it shall be sold according to the same law as the fields:”**
• IT SHALL BE SOLD ACCORDING TO THE LAW OF THE FIELDS. Because they are near to the Gospel, not to the law. Therefore they can always be redeemed; from the time Christ came until the second coming they are redeemed in parts.
• Septuagint: They shall be reckoned as the field of the land, of which, namely, it is said: "The kingdom of heaven is like unto a treasure hidden in a field", that is, in the Gospel, in which the treasure is, namely, the mystery of Christ.
**“if it be not redeemed before,”** — by the remission of the cross
25.32:
**“The houses”** — as many as are joined to them
**“of Levites,”** — of the Apostles, who possess no inheritance on earth.
**“which are in cities, may always be redeemed:”** — THE HOUSES OF LEVITES etc. If the house be priestly or Levitical, wherever it be, whether in a city or in a field, it always has redemption. The priest is said to be a mind consecrated to God, and is called a Levite because he always stands before God and ministers to his will: the one perfect, therefore, in virtue and work, in faith and acts, is to be taken as priest and Levite. If it befall him to sell the heavenly house, as David, who looked upon the wife of Urias, he at once redeemed it, saying: "I have sinned." Also, if we read the divine Scriptures and recount in them certain faults of the holy fathers, if according to the Apostle we say that "all these things happened to them in figure" and "are written for our correction", in this way their house is always redeemed, because satisfaction is always rendered for their faults by the teachers, who show from the divine Scriptures that these things were forms and images of things to come, not by which the faults of the saints might be reproved, but by which sinners might be shown in the fellowship of the saints. So therefore the priestly possession is never separated from the priest; even if at some time it has been sold off, it is always redeemed, because charity suffereth all things, hopeth all things, charity never falleth away. But it can be sold off, that is, fall into sin, because one can build upon it wood, hay, stubble, which are the works of sin; he who builds these sells the house to the devil, and pays the price of sin, namely the satisfying of desire.
25.33: **“If they be not redeemed, in the jubilee they shall all return to the owners, because the houses of the cities of the Levites are for their possessions”** — All the families cleaving to the apostles were their possessions.
25.34:
**“But let not their suburbs”**
• of the apostles
• BUT THEIR SUBURBS etc. Other fields, that is, conversations, virtues and doctrines. These are set apart from their cities, which stand and are saved through them, and are not sold, because they are freely received and freely given.
25.35:
**“If thy brother be impoverished,”** — in dignity and conversation
**“and weak of hand,”** — in the working of virtues
**“and thou receive him as a stranger”** — who now comes to the faith
**“and sojourner,”** — who still wanders hither and thither
**“and he live with thee,”**
• by the bread of the Word of God
• IF THY BROTHER BE IMPOVERISHED etc. Admire the wisdom and piety of the lawgiver: for in lowly things he sets forth sublime ones, and according to the letter he gives a rule of piety.
25.36:
**“Take not of him”** — lest he die estranged from God
**“usury nor more than thou gavest:”** — that is: do not exact the working of virtues too abundantly
**“fear thy God,”** — lest thou oppress him too much with exactions
**“that thy brother may live with thee.”** — as if: imitate Paul, who says: "I became weak to the weak."
25.38:
**“I am the Lord your God.”** — Whose yoke is sweet, who do not wish man to sin, nor exact beyond anyone's strength.
**“who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might give you the land of Chanaan, and might be your God.”** — WHO BROUGHT YOU OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT etc. As if: As I freed you from the dominion of the Egyptians, and, the sinners being cast out, led you into the land of the Chanaanites now cleansed, so I do not wish you to be held under the dominion of sinners, nor to embrace the fellowship of sinners. But when they wish to repent, sustain them both by dwelling with them and by bestowing your means.
25.39:
**“If by poverty”** — by the weakening of virtue
**“constrained he sell himself to thee,”**
• for the price of doctrine and correction
• He has given himself over to thee to be converted and corrected.
**“thy brother,”** — the faithful one, equal in calling and conversation
**“thou shalt not oppress him”** — afflicting him with too much cruelty
**“with the service of bondservants:”**
• that is: He shall not be subject to thee as a slave, but in the liberty wherewith Christ has made us free.
• IF CONSTRAINED BY POVERTY etc. The letter is full of much piety, but the spiritual understanding fuller.
25.40:
**“But he shall be as a hireling, and a sojourner:”** — not truly, because he will soon recover house and field
**“BUT AS A HIRELING”** — Both are subject, but yet this one is free: so he who has been converted through you is indeed subject, but by the dignity of divine grace is a brother.
**“he shall work with thee until the year of the jubilee,”** — because through perfect penance, wholly cleansed and made perfect, he can work by himself
25.41:
**“And afterwards he shall go out with his children,”** — with the virtues which he had before he was sold
**“and shall return to his kindred”** — of the saints
**“and to the possession of his fathers,”** — of conversation, the lot and the grace which God, his true Father, gave
25.42:
**“For they are my servants, and I brought them out of the land of Egypt:”** — as if: Once made my servants, and freed from the bondage of the world and the devil, even if they have fallen a little, yet I do not wish them to lose their dignity for ever.
**“let them not be sold as bondmen:”** — as if: They are bought with a great price: I do not wish them to become the servants of men.
25.43:
**“Afflict him not”** — whom thou hast converted
**“by might,”** — AFFLICT HIM NOT etc. Because: With what judgment you judge, you shall be judged; and with what measure you mete, it shall be measured to you again.
25.44:
**“Let your bondmen, and your bondwomen, be of the nations”** — the Gentiles, who do not yet believe, yet have hope of faith and salvation.
**“that are round about you.”** — BONDMAN AND BONDWOMAN etc. He shows the difference between those whom we save for God from among unbelievers, and those already faithful, like us in the dignity of calling and conversation, whom, weakened for a time in virtues, we correct. For these work with us until the jubilee; but those are servants for ever.
25.45:
**“And of the strangers that sojourn among you,”** — the Jews, who read the law and the prophets with us, but do not understand with us
**“or that were born of them in your land,”** — THAT WERE BORN OF THEM etc. The heretics, kinsmen of the Jews, who preach the same mysteries with us, as if they were in your land, but do not believe rightly and perfectly.
25.46:
**“And by right of inheritance shall leave them to your posterity,”**
• your disciples
• THESE YOU SHALL HAVE etc. Those whom we convert from the Gentiles or from the Jews or from the heretics we acquire as bondmen and bondwomen for ever, because we spend the money of doctrine for them, and we can hand them over to our sons, that is, disciples, to be taught, as Paul committed the Cretans to Titus and the Ephesians to Timothy to be taught.
**“and shall possess them for ever.”** — that is: they shall be released by no remission
**“But your brethren”** — nourished in your faith
**“the children of Israel oppress not by might.”** — BUT YOUR BRETHREN etc. As if: those whom you have converted from the impious will not be of the same dignity with you as those whom you have restored after a fall.
25.47:
**“If the hand grow strong among you”** — working, namely strength
**“of a stranger or a sojourner, and impoverished”**
• having no one to exhort or counsel him
• IF IT GROW STRONG etc. According to the letter, he shows how much he loves liberty. For therefore he does not permit an Israelite to serve strangers, but commands him to be redeemed.
**“IF IT GROW STRONG”** — That is: if one newly joined to your faith, whether Gentile or Jew or heretic, has shone with virtues, so that he can reprove and exhort.
**“thy brother”** — who once was instructed in the faith, and was perhaps equal to thee in conversation
**“sell”** — for the word of doctrine
**“himself”** — giving, namely, his conversation
**“to him, or to any of his race:”** — to his disciple, namely
25.48:
**“After the sale he may be redeemed. He that will of his brethren”** — proven faithful ones
**“shall redeem him:”**
• by giving doctrine, lest he seek their doctrine any longer
• HE THAT WILL OF HIS BRETHREN etc. For it is shameful that a man nourished in the faith from infancy should come under the teaching of such as have suddenly been made masters. Whence Jerome: Yesterday in the forum, today at the altar; yesterday the companion of actors, today the consecrator of virgins.
25.49:
**“Either his uncle, or his uncle's son,”** — HIS UNCLE AND HIS UNCLE'S SONS etc. The uncles are those who begot us in the faith; their brothers, preachers like them; the sons of the brothers, the disciples of those like them.
**“HIS KINSMAN BY BLOOD”** — One more remote than the uncle or the uncle's son, but nearer than one by affinity. For he that hath not care of his own, and especially of those of his house, hath denied the faith.
**“BY AFFINITY”** — In the kinship of the faith of Christ's incarnation, we who are of his flesh and of his bones.
**“But if he himself be able also, he shall redeem himself,”**
• BUT IF etc. The Holy Ghost acts for our liberty and glory, and commands every servant of sin to be redeemed by virtues.
• AND HE HIMSELF etc. LET HIM REDEEM. He who has become poor in sin, though before he was rich in virtue and doctrine, rightly frees himself when by exhorting and counselling he calls himself back to virtue.
25.50:
**“Counting only the years from the time”** — from the time he sinned
**“of his selling unto the year of the jubilee:”**
• the perfect remission of sins
• COUNTING ONLY THE TIME etc. That is: considering with himself by what virtue, by what correction of zealous penance he may lay hold of the remission of sins and go forward. For as he who has paid the money to the buyer does not wait for the year of remission, so he who seeks out virtues equal to blotting out the sin anticipates penance. As Zacheus, who had taken away much, says: The half of my goods I give to the poor, and if I have wronged any man, I restore him fourfold. Therefore the Lord says to him: This day is salvation come to this house.
**“and counting the money that he was sold for, according to the number of the years and the reckoning of a hired servant,”** — the measure of the sin being considered: Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.
25.51:
**“If there be many years that remain until the jubilee,”** — that is: if many virtues and actions and corrections are needed
**“HE SHALL ALSO REPAY THE PRICE”** — That is: according to what he has sinned, he must pay the price. What gluttony has sinned, let fasting correct; what talkativeness has committed, let silence blot out; and likewise contraries are cured by contraries.
25.52: **“If few,”** — if, namely, he can be amended by few virtues and corrections
25.53:
**“His wages being allowed for which he served before:”** — that is: considering, namely, the sins in which he served, sold under sin
**“he shall not afflict him violently in thy sight.”** — as it were by having compassion rather than by giving full succour
25.54:
**“And if by these means he cannot be redeemed,”** — that is: If he cannot redeem himself by virtues equal to the sin.
**“in the year of the jubilee”** — by perfect and strict penance
**“he shall go out with his children.”** — with the good works which he had before the sin
25.55:
**“For my servants”** — sighing for liberty
**“are the children of Israel, whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt.”** — out of the world

26.1:
**“I am the Lord your God: you shall not make to yourselves any idol or graven thing,”** — Covetousness is the service of idols.
**“YOU SHALL NOT MAKE”** — He forbids the worship of idols, invisible as well as visible.
**“GRAVEN THING”** — Desiring to carve some memorial of yourselves in the buildings of houses and the possessions of fields.
**“neither shall you erect pillars, nor set up a remarkable stone in your land, to adore it:”** — NOR A REMARKABLE STONE etc. A heap of gold and silver or of precious stones, by which the covetous are led astray, as the Gentiles by idols.
**“for I”** — not another, not idols
26.2:
**“Keep my sabbaths,”** — not yours
**“KEEP”** — By abstaining from all evil and being free for all good: for this is the true sabbath.
**“and reverence my sanctuary:”** — striving after perfect holiness
**“I am the Lord.”** — The Holy One dwelling in the holy, destroying those who defile the temple of God.
26.3:
**“If in my precepts”** — which are the right way
**“you walk,”**
• thus
• by going forward
• IN MY PRECEPTS etc. He has foretold what ought to be done and what avoided. At the end he enumerates what rewards are due to those who observe, what punishments to transgressors.
• IF IN MY PRECEPTS etc. Yet these things cannot stand according to the letter. For many have walked in the precepts of God and suffered many adversities. Rather this must be attended to: that for those who keep the commandments the law foretells thirty blessings in the present chapter, which you will find set apart in the edition of the Septuagint translators; because the Lord, being thirty years of age, came to baptism, that in the perfect age he might show the perfection of the gifts. For from then he preached the Gospel, in which is all the fulness of life and retribution, which are signified in this chapter.
**“ORIGEN”** — If the law is carnal, observed carnally, it bestows carnal blessings. But if, as it seems to Paul, it is spiritual, understood spiritually, it gives, when observed, a spiritual blessing, or, when not observed, a curse. Whence: "Who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings" etc. And he says "with all blessings" because he knew that many things commanded in the law are to be fulfilled, and in each one its own contests, in which he who conquers merits the blessing. But each just and perfect man can be blessed with every blessing, so as to receive the blessings of Leviticus and of the book of Numbers, and of Genesis, and of Noe to Sem and Japheth, and the blessings of Isaac to Jacob, and of Jacob to Joseph, and Ephraim, and Manasses, and at last to the twelve patriarchs. For lest they should seem to belong to these alone, the Apostle named them spiritually, so that whoever is in the spirit or power of all or any of these can become partaker of any or all of the blessings, if he has had a like spirit and power, as John came "in the spirit and power of Elias".
**“and my commandments”** — by which tithes are commanded to be offered, and the like
**“MY COMMANDMENTS”** — Such as that: Let him that keeps not the sabbath be stoned by all the congregation, and the like.
**“keep,”**
• in memory
• understand
**“and do them,”** — fulfil
**“in due seasons.”** — IN DUE SEASONS etc. ORIGEN. At the fitting time: not to one drunk, not to one occupied in other things. The teacher therefore should look wisely to whom he ministers rain and the measure of wheat, and to whom he ought to give milk and not give meat.
26.4:
**“I will give you rain”**
• not that which falls on the just and the unjust
• of the Word of God; whence: Let my speech be looked for as the rain.
• I WILL GIVE YOU etc. Septuagint: And I will give; the "and" is superfluous: not according to the custom of our speech, but added after the manner of the Scriptures.
**“And the ground”** — the body
**“shall bring forth its increase,”** — chastity, sobriety, abstinence
**“THE GROUND SHALL BRING FORTH”** — Septuagint: The trees of the field shall give their fruit; that is, the motions of the soul, which are higher than the motions of the earth, that is, of our flesh, whose fruits are charity, justice, meekness and the like.
**“and with fruit”**
• with works
• the virtues, namely piety, wisdom, discipline and the others
**“the trees shall be filled.”** — THE TREES WITH FRUIT etc. ORIGEN. An evil tree cannot bring forth good fruit, neither can a good tree bring forth evil fruit. A good tree: justice, prudence, piety, wisdom and many others with which Paradise is planted. Above all is the tree of life, namely wisdom, of which it is said: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her.
26.5:
**“The threshing of your harvest shall reach unto the vintage,”**
• HESYCHIUS. The goods of the body: for threshing is of the fruits of the earth.
• THE THRESHING OF YOUR HARVEST SHALL REACH etc. The soul which sprouts from the word of God, watered by the heavenly rain, brings forth its shoot to the harvest. But the harvest is to be cleansed on the threshing floor, that is, the meaning is to be brought into the open and compared with the other teachers or the divine books, so that if anything is empty, or like chaff or beards, it may be shaken out by the spirit of discernment, and only the wheat may remain, to be dispensed to fellow servants in due time.
• THE THRESHING OF YOUR HARVEST SHALL REACH etc. For bread strengthens man's heart, wine gladdens it. The things said of continence, of observances and of the keeping of the commandments seem to be wheat, from which bread is made, which comforts hearts. But the things that pertain to knowledge and gladden the mind by the searching out of hidden things are compared to wine and the vintage. For the heart rejoices when obscure things are explained.
• THE VINTAGE etc. The fruit of the soul. For the vintage is of a tree. To have these together, that is, to bear fruit in body and soul, is of great blessing.
**“HESYCHIUS”** — For the soul, gathering its virtues, soon desires others. Whence it follows: Forgetting the things that are behind, I stretch forth myself to those that are before.
**“and the vintage shall reach unto the sowing time:”** — of other virtues and actions
**“THE VINTAGE SHALL REACH”** — ORIGEN. As if we should say: I sowed the things of the law; afterward I prayed that the Lord would give us rain in its time; the harvest came; again I sow from the prophetic scripture the fallow ground of the hearers; after this I sow from the Gospels. We can sow through the whole year; we can also cast many seeds from the apostolic letters. Let us sow in the spirit, that of the spirit we may reap life everlasting.
**“and you shall eat”** — by working
**“your bread to the full,”**
• that you may work sufficiently
• YOUR BREAD etc. Which came down from heaven and gives life to the world: not that which abounds more in evils than in goods.
**“and dwell in your land without fear.”**
• whose house is upon the firm rock
• WITHOUT FEAR etc. If the body be steady and the soul bear fruit, we shall be secure in our land, because the flesh will not lust against the spirit.
26.6:
**“I will give”** — in the future
**“peace”**
• perfect
• not of this world; whence: I came not to send peace etc.
**“in your coasts:”** — "Who hath placed peace in thy borders" etc.
**“you shall sleep,”**
• you shall die
• from the din of the world
**“and there shall be none to make you afraid.”**
• The just, bold as a lion.
• because you will have nothing for which to be afraid
**“I will take away evil beasts:”**
• not these bodily ones, because they are neither good nor evil
• the demons
**“and the sword”** — affliction from the enemy
**“shall not pass through your quarters.”**
• body and soul
• AND THE SWORD SHALL NOT PASS etc. Because there will be peace in your borders; now wars and strifes come from concupiscence.
26.7:
**“You shall pursue”** — armed with the law of God
**“your enemies,”**
• the demons
• slain by fasting
• YOUR ENEMIES etc. Slain by fasting, prayer and the like. Whence: This kind is not cast out but by prayer and fasting.
**“and they shall fall before you.”**
• If one is chaste, lust falls before thee; if pious, impiety.
• THEY SHALL FALL BEFORE YOU etc. Septuagint: In your sight, by your death; namely, your members which are upon the earth being mortified, that is, fornication, uncleanness and the like.
26.8:
**“Five shall pursue”** — who use the five senses spiritually
**“of yours a hundred others,”**
• perfect in cunning
• FIVE OF YOURS SHALL PURSUE etc. ORIGEN. As the number five marks the wise and the foolish, so the hundred marks the faithful and the unfaithful. Abraham at a hundred years is described as having believed and been justified, and the sinner of a hundred years shall be accursed. Here too five wise shall pursue a hundred unbelievers, and a hundred faithful, marked not so much by number as by perfection, many thousands of unbelievers. These are the teachers who put to flight countless demons, lest they deceive believers.
• SEPTUAGINT: Fifty shall drive out a hundred. Fifty signifies the spiritual man, because he judgeth all things and he himself is judged of no man, who uses a perfect and discerning knowledge: he can pursue and conquer the demon, however cunning and strong, who is above a hundred, or who is called legion because of the multitude of the others disobedient to him.
**“and a hundred”** — a finite number for an infinite
**“of you ten thousand:”**
• the contrary virtues
• AND A HUNDRED OF YOU etc. Those who have not only subtle knowledge but also a perfect life, who are spiritually multiplied tenfold, and therefore are called a hundred, namely those who bring forth fruit a hundredfold.
**“your enemies shall fall”** — the spiritual ones
**“by the sword”** — of the Spirit, which is the Word of God
**“before you.”** — not bearing your face
26.9:
**“I will look on you, and make you increase: you shall be multiplied,”**
• I WILL LOOK ON YOU etc. Whose look is salvation. The Lord looked on Peter and he wept bitterly. If the sun does not look upon the corn, it remains fruitless. God looks upon the corn of our heart, and with the rays of his word enlightens us, increases and multiplies us, that we may be made great, as Isaac was made great, and Moses great, and John great.
• AND MAKE YOU INCREASE etc. In good works, so that little things become great. Whence: What you did to one of my least, you did to me.
• YOU SHALL BE MULTIPLIED etc. So that few things may become great or many. Whence: If there be any other commandment, it is comprised in this word: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
**“and I will establish”** — I will fulfil in deed
**“my covenant”** — foretold
26.10:
**“You shall eat the oldest of the old store,”** — the things promised through the law and the prophets, and in the blessings of the patriarchs
**“and the old”** — the promises of the law and the prophets
**“new”** — the Gospel promises
**“coming on,”** — as greater
**“you shall cast away.”**
• as superfluous, compared with the new
• YOU SHALL EAT THE OLDEST OF THE OLD STORE etc. ORIGEN. The law and the prophets are old; the oldest of the old are those which were before the law, from the beginning of the world; the new Gospels have come, and, these with the Apostles coming on, we shall cast away the old, namely the law according to the letter, that we may establish it according to the spirit. Also, before the man from heaven came and the heavenly man was born, we were all earthly, according to the image of the earthly. The new man coming on, we put off the old and put on the new.
26.11:
**“I will set”** — firmly
**“my tabernacle”** — the Church
**“in the midst of you,”**
• because it is catholic and common
• I WILL SET MY TABERNACLE etc. If we have the things aforesaid, the old man being cast off, our heart is renewed. God comes to us and will dwell in us.
**“and my soul shall not cast you off.”**
• SHALL NOT CAST YOU OFF etc. ORIGEN. I dare to say that the soul of God is Christ, as also the Word of God, the wisdom of God and the power of God. It is therefore as if he said: My Son shall not cast you off.
• MY SOUL etc. AUGUSTINE. God calls his will his soul. For he is not a living being having body and soul; nor is his substance like the soul, which is his creature, as he himself testifies: I have made every breath. As therefore when he speaks of his eyes and his lips and the other names of members we do not take him as bounded by the form of a body, but by these we understand the effect of his operations or powers, so when he says: My soul, we ought to take it as his will. For that perfect and simple nature which is called God does not consist of soul and body and spirit, nor is he changeable in spirit as the soul is; but God is a spirit and is always the same, "with whom there is no change". Yet from here the Apollinarists took occasion, who say that Jesus did not have a soul.
26.12:
**“I WILL WALK AMONG YOU”** — Made man. Whence: This is our God, and there shall no other be accounted of in comparison of him. Afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men.
**“and will be your God,”** — I will show myself to be
26.13:
**“I am the Lord your God: who have brought you out”** — when you were serving
**“of the land of the Egyptians,”** — of the demons
**“that you should not serve them,”** — "Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin."
**“and who have broken the chains”**
• of sins
• which those had laid on you who had led you into captivity by work
**“of your necks, that you might go upright.”** — toward God
26.14:
**“But if you will not hear me,”** — with the ear of the heart
**“nor do”** — with the work of the heart
**“all my commandments,”**
• but your own traditions
• BUT IF YOU WILL NOT HEAR etc. In the preceding chapter he set out the goods of the obedient; in the present chapter he shows what the evils of transgressors are, some of which the Jews suffered according to the letter, but all according to the spirit.
26.15:
**“If you despise”** — by expounding them at your pleasure
**“my laws, and contemn my judgments”** — interpreting them not according to my will but your own
26.16:
**“WITH POVERTY”** — Of the Word of God. Whence: This saying is hard, and who can hear it? Because they transgressed the understanding of the law so as to make void the testament of the Gospel, he spoke to them obscurely, lest they should understand.
**“and burning heat,”** — of anger, of envy
**“which shall waste your eyes,”** — the inward ones; whence, blinded, they said: "If we let him alone so, all will believe in him."
**“and consume your lives.”** — whence they cried: "How long dost thou hold our souls in suspense?"
**“In vain”** — because the ground is not fertile
**“you shall sow your seed,”** — the doctrine of the prophets
**“which by your enemies”** — by the Gentiles believing in Christ, whom you envy
26.17:
**“I will set my face”** — The countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things etc.
**“against you, and you shall fall down before your enemies,”** — stumbling at the salvation of the Gentiles
**“and shall be made subject”** — as to teachers
**“to them that hate you, you shall flee when no man pursueth you.”** — YOU SHALL FLEE WHEN NO MAN PURSUETH YOU. Because the Gentiles will not pursue to drive them out, but hasten toward their salvation, according to that: But I follow after, if I may by any means apprehend.
26.18:
**“But if you will not yet for all this obey me:”** — in correction
**“I will chastise you seven times more for your sins,”**
• you have willed the fulness of punishment
• BUT IF etc. He often uses distinctions of this kind, because Jesus often wished to convert the people of the Jews, but they would not. Whence: How often would I have gathered together thy children, and thou wouldst not. But this above all is to be attended to: that while he threatens seven corrections, the breaking of proud hardness and the giving of an iron heaven etc., yet he enumerates six, not seven. But because seven is the perfect number of the present life, it signifies a vengeance in every way full and entire.
**“I WILL ADD CHASTISEMENT”** — Septuagint: And I will add to chastise you seven times etc. This too is superfluous. And seven times is to be taken for every number.
26.19:
**“And I will break the pride of your stubbornness, and I will make to you the heaven above”** — that it may not rain doctrine upon you
**“as iron, and the earth as brass:”**
• the divine Scriptures unfruitful to you
• AND I WILL BREAK THE PRIDE etc. Because you say: "We are the seed of Abraham, and we have never been slaves to any man", therefore you shall serve the Gentiles.
26.20:
**“Your labour shall be spent in vain,”** — which you spend on the divine Scriptures, because you understand them wrongly
**“the ground shall not bring forth”** — the outward man
**“her increase,”** — of virtues
**“nor the trees”** — minds
**“yield their fruit.”** — fruits acceptable to God
26.21:
**“If you walk contrary to me,”** — For they do not walk rightly who overturn the sense of the law and the prophets.
**“and will not hearken to me, I will bring plagues upon you”** — no longer corrections, but punishment according to your iniquity
**“seven times more”** — perfect vengeance
26.22:
**“And I will send in upon you the beasts of the field,”** — the demons, of whom it is said: All the beasts of the field play there.
**“to destroy you and your cattle,”** — a nation like cattle
**“and to fewness”** — in number as well as in dignity
**“make all things, and your highways shall be desolate.”** — because they neither have the water of life nor receive God as a guest
26.23: **“And if even so you will not amend, but will walk contrary to me:”** — transgressing the law
26.24:
**“I also will walk contrary to you,”** — by bringing on vengeance
**“and will strike you seven times”** — I who before had corrected, that as iniquity grows, punishment may also grow
26.25:
**“THE SWORD”** — Of the Spirit, which is the word of God, which through the preachers convicts the Jews, lest they gainsay that the Old Testament agrees with the Gospel.
**“that shall avenge”** — or: of vengeance
**“INTO THE CITIES”** — The prophets, in which the faithful find fortresses and salvation; the enemies, fleeing, are taken, and die there, unable to resist the plain prophecies of Christ.
26.26:
**“After I shall have broken the staff of your bread:”** — the support of spiritual doctrine
**“so that ten women”** — the ten commandments of the law
**“in one oven”** — the law
**“shall bake your bread,”** — of doctrine
**“and give it out by weight:”** — of a narrowed sense
**“and you shall not be filled.”**
• because the doctrine is narrow and wrong
• SO THAT TEN etc. The Jews have no bread of doctrine except the ten commandments, because they flee the true exposition of the prophets, which preaches Christ in most of the prophets. The other things that are in the law they will not take spiritually, nor can they stand according to the letter. For the place is destroyed in which the sacrifices and oblations were made; moreover many things in them are laughable, such as the leprosy of walls and garments and the like. But it is fitting that the letter even of the ten commandments be kept and fulfilled; nor is the commandment of the sabbath contrary to this. For although it is set among the ten commandments, yet it is not of them. But if we set down as a special commandment: "I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage", we find the perfect number of ten commandments. Moreover it marks the spiritual rest, in which it is not lawful to do servile works. These alone therefore make bread among the people of the Jews, in one oven, namely the legal one, and give it out by weight, namely not by widening but by narrowing the senses. But the heavenly doctrine of the Gospel widens the sense, so that it calls looking on a woman to lust adultery, and hatred of a brother murder. Therefore those who are nourished by these loaves are not filled.
26.27:
**“But if you will not for all this hearken to me,”**
• the voice of Christ, who says: If you did believe Moses, you would perhaps believe me also: for he wrote of me.
• BUT IF etc. Moses is not only lawgiver, but also prophet. For he says: The Lord will raise up to you a prophet of your brethren; him you shall hear as me. And as he bore the figure of Christ in other things, in this also he expressed him. For as the Lord foretold of the destruction of the city and of the end of the world, so did he too. For what he says here pertains to the last captivity which the Jews endured because they laid hands on Christ; and they were punished not only according to the letter but also spiritually, because they both transgressed the law and blasphemed the author of the law.
**“but will walk against me:”** — disparaging his doctrine and miracles
26.28:
**“I also”**
• by bringing in captivity
• With the holy thou wilt be holy, and with the perverse thou wilt be perverted.
**“will go against you with opposite fury, and I will chastise you with seven plagues”** — with perfect vengeance
**“for your sins,”** — that is: As you have multiplied sins, I will multiply punishments.
26.29:
**“So that you shall eat the flesh of your sons and of your daughters.”** — as Mary, the daughter of Eleazar
**“THE FLESH OF YOUR SONS”** — That is, the disciples whom you take to yourselves as sons, whom you lead to the same doctrine by crafty words that corrupt the soul.
26.30:
**“I will destroy your high places,”** — princes, teachers
**“and your idols”** — false virtues
**“YOU SHALL FALL AMONG THE RUINS”** — For the people fall with the Pharisees, who fall spiritually, whom the people admired as idols, intent on their traditions.
**“and my soul shall abhor you.”** — which I laid down for sinners, and you neglected it
26.31:
**“YOUR CITIES”** — According to the letter, or the books of the prophets, in which they find no fruit of holiness.
**“I will bring to be a wilderness, and desolate”** — in which I may not dwell
**“I will make your sanctuaries,”** — the temple, the sacrifices
**“and will receive no”** — as before
**“more your sweet odours.”** — of the sacrifices
26.32:
**“And I will destroy”** — by taking it away from you
**“your land,”** — the Scripture
**“and shall be astonished”** — by wondering
**“at it your enemies,”** — the Gentiles, whom you think your enemies
**“when they shall be the inhabitants thereof.”** — understanding the Scripture
26.33:
**“And you”** — or: but
**“I will scatter among the Gentiles,”** — that you may be as the Gentiles were before, not having God
**“and I will draw out the sword after you,”** — of the word of God
**“and your land shall be desert,”** — of God, or of the saints
**“and your cities destroyed.”** — according to the letter, or the fortresses of the Scriptures
26.34:
**“Then shall the land enjoy”** — namely to the Scripture, the Old Testament
**“her sabbaths all the days of her desolation:”** — in which it will be alone and deserted by you
**“THEN SHALL THE LAND ENJOY HER SABBATHS”** — That is, rest; namely, while you keep holiday and are removed from the law, since in the law and the prophets you do not find your own will.
**“When you shall be”** — joined and subject to the New Testament, even if you will not
26.35:
**“In the enemy's land,”** — defiled by your iniquities
**“she shall keep a sabbath,”** — because: "Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner."
**“and rest”** — from our searching
**“in the sabbaths of her desolation, because she did not rest in your sabbaths when you dwelt therein.”** — in the time of the Old Testament
26.36:
**“And as to them that shall remain of you”** — after the slaughter and captivity
**“I will send fear”** — For they fear the letter of the Law, which they think disagrees with the newness of the Gospel.
**“in their hearts in the countries of their enemies,”** — of the Gentiles converted to the faith
**“the sound shall terrify them”**
• not their voice, but only their sound
• THE SOUND SHALL TERRIFY THEM etc. As the leaf hides the fruit, so the letter hides the spirit: take away the leaf, receive the fruit.
**“of a flying leaf,”** — of the letter of the law, which they see the Church neglect, and seek the spirit in it
**“THE SOUND OF A LEAF”** — Hyperbole. Because they will dread even the lightest things.
**“and they shall flee”** — the fellowship of the faithful
**“as it were from the sword:”** — of the word which they will hear from the faithful
**“they shall fall, when no man pursueth them,”** — THEY SHALL FALL, WHEN NO MAN etc. For we do not pursue them, but follow them to call them back.
26.37:
**“And they shall every one fall upon their brethren as from wars”** — disputations
**“fleeing,”**
• as if conquered
• THEY SHALL EVERY ONE FALL etc. When we dispute with them, they bring forth different testimonies in turn, but they will be confounded by each other's words; one confounds the other while he seems to come to his help.
26.38:
**“You shall perish among the Gentiles, and an enemy's land”** — the New Testament
**“shall consume you.”** — the support of your error
26.39:
**“And if of them also some remain,”** — converted
**“they shall pine away”** — in the study of the law
**“in their iniquities, in the land”** — as above
**“of their enemies,”** — which even the converted defile by always sighing after the law
**“and they shall be afflicted for the sins of their fathers,”** — which they imitate
26.40:
**“Until they confess”** — by repenting
**“their iniquities and the iniquities of their ancestors,”** — like whom they are
**“whereby they have transgressed me,”** — by neglecting my words
**“and walked”** — either wholly turned away or feignedly converted
26.41:
**“I will walk”** — perverse against the perverse
**“Therefore I also against them, and bring them”** — whence: "I will provoke you to jealousy by that which is not a nation."
**“into their enemies' land”** — whence: As concerning the Gospel, enemies for your sake.
**“until be ashamed”** — by repenting
**“THEIR UNCIRCUMCISED MIND”** — Because they are uncircumcised in heart, defiled with the foreskin of vices: for it is not the circumcision which is in the flesh.
26.42:
**“And I will remember my covenant,”** — MY COVENANT etc. Septuagint: They shall be pleased with their sins, namely the punishments which they shall suffer for their sins.
**“that I made with Jacob,”** — the Gospel
**“and Isaac,”** — the prophets
**“and Abraham.”**
• the law
• THAT I MADE etc. Note that he changed the order of time and of generation. The Septuagint too does not say: The covenant of Jacob and Isaac and Abraham, but: The covenant of Jacob, the covenant of Isaac, the covenant of Abraham, hinting at three testaments, namely the law, the prophets and the Gospel. The law is the more ancient, the prophets ancient, the Gospel new, which is set first for the fulness of grace, like Jacob, who was the last in time and in the order of generation. But they are joined together as kindred and agreeing.
**“I will remember also the land:”** — ALSO THE LAND etc. The Scripture, namely, which I will commit to others, the Jews being cast out, who transgressed it, or were transgressing it and interpreting it wrongly.
26.43:
**“Which when she shall be left by them, shall enjoy”** — because made desolate by them
**“her sabbaths, being desolate for them.”** — For they themselves made it a wilderness.
**“But they”** — or: but
**“shall pray for their sins,”** — conscious of their transgression
**“because they rejected my judgments,”** — not doing them, or understanding them wrongly
**“and despised my laws.”** — not: yours
26.44:
**“And yet for all that when they were in the land of their enemies,”** — the Gospel Scripture
**“I did not cast them off altogether,”**
• "A remnant shall be saved."
• AND YET etc. Well at the end of the chapter he speaks gently, and those whom he had terrified with threats he consoles with promises.
• NOT ALTOGETHER etc. Blindness in part has happened in Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles should come in etc.
**“neither did I so despise them that they should be quite consumed, and I should make void my covenant with them.”** — NEITHER DID I SO DESPISE etc. I who will the salvation of all therefore, after so great iniquities, save even the remnant of the Jews.
26.45:
**“And I will remember my former covenant,”** — that I may be the Lord their God in the sight of the Gentiles
**“when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, in the sight of the Gentiles, to be their God. I am the Lord God. These are the precepts”** — given with no one asking
**“and my judgments,”** — which were judged by the Lord when asked
**“and laws,”** — general
**“which the Lord gave”** — before he came
26.46:
**“THESE ARE THE PRECEPTS”** — He signifies that the letter of the law is to be observed until a set time. He also stops the mouth of the Jews, who even now wish to fulfil the letter, since he has now come who then gave the Jews milk through Moses, not meat, but by himself bestowed perfect things. Therefore he says: Between him and the children of Israel. Until, namely, he should come, and the eyes of the blind be opened and the ears of the deaf hear? So that, the surface of the letter being left, he might carry the law over to the perfection of grace, not by destroying but by fulfilling.
**“in mount Sinai”** — In mount Sinai, not in Sion. Whence: "The God of gods shall be seen in Sion." And elsewhere: "Out of Sion the loveliness of his beauty: God shall come manifestly." And in Malachias: Suddenly the Ruler whom you seek shall come to his holy temple.

27.2:
**“Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: The man that shall have made a vow,”** — THE MAN THAT SHALL HAVE MADE A VOW etc. These words are full of prudence: above he commanded what ought or ought not to be done; now he sets forth the dignity of those who act, wholly or in part: what the perfect life has, what the middling, what the one beginning the knowledge of God; he also describes the differences of ages.
**“and promised his soul to God,”**
• his whole life
• HIS SOUL etc. Aquila and Theodotion: a wonderful thing. Symmachus: if he shall set apart. Septuagint: the honour of his soul.
**“shall give the price according to estimation.”** — that is: forty drachmas
27.3:
**“If it be a man”** — firm and strong
**“from twenty years old unto sixty years old, he shall give fifty sicles of silver,”**
• or: didrachmas, that is, the hundredfold fruit
• eternal life
• FROM TWENTY YEARS OLD etc. When grown, strong, mighty in virtues and works against the spiritual enemies. Whence: Every male from twenty years and upward. All who walk in their strength: the price of such a one is, namely, his conversation and life, the retribution which he offers to God for himself. There are fifty sicles, that is, the spiritual life. For on the fiftieth day the Holy Ghost came, and in the fiftieth year liberation and restitution of land are fully given. From twenty years to sixty: perfect understanding, strength and the begetting of sons. And he who has both understanding and strength, so as to do what he understands, and can make spiritual sons for God, his price is fifty didrachmas, that is, the perfect fruit and the didrachma of perfection, of which it is said: "Be you perfect, as also your Father is perfect."
**“SICLES”** — Or didrachmas: the sixtyfold fruit, namely, great indeed, but less than the hundredfold, because it is the woman, who is less than the man. Yet women, if they have come to the highest measure and have passed beyond their weakness by the striving of strength, can be called males. Whence: "Who shall find a valiant woman?" Because therefore she has true continence, her estimation is thirty sicles or didrachmas, that is, the sixtyfold fruit. Whence: "Let a widow be chosen of no less than sixty years."
27.4: **“If a woman, thirty.”** — as one who lacks this perfection, but desires to be brought on to another
27.5:
**“But from the fifth year”**
• having sense, but not yet perfect
• BUT FROM THE FIFTH etc. One who has sense, so that he has begun to be perfected, but cannot yet be adorned with the conversation of fasting.
**“until the twentieth,”** — UNTIL THE TWENTIETH etc. One who has begun to make progress in the five senses: for this one is advanced toward virtue and perfection. For those of twenty years are strong and mighty.
**“a man shall give twenty sicles:”** — didrachmas
**“A MAN SHALL GIVE TWENTY SICLES”** — Or didrachmas, that is, forty drachmas; that is, four hundred obols. And the number forty signifies progress in fasting and prayers. For so many days Moses fasted, and Elias, and Christ himself, and afterward was tempted by the devil.
**“A WOMAN TEN SICLES”** — Or didrachmas, or two hundred obols. Namely the keeping of the ten commandments, which are doubled according to the letter and the spirit, among which there is no precept of fasting, which befits those who have advanced but are not yet perfect.
27.6:
**“FROM ONE MONTH”** — He is of one month who has now been begotten in the faith; to whom it is said: As newborn babes, desire the rational milk without guile etc.
**“until the fifth year, for a male shall be given five sicles:”** — FIVE SICLES etc. Or didrachmas, namely, that the male may have twofold senses, and receive intelligibly what he hears sensibly. For so he is led to perfection, for which reason his price is a hundred obols: for a hundred is perfect.
**“for a female”** — because she is less and simpler
**“three.”** — FOR A FEMALE THREE etc. For a female three didrachmas, that is, the faith of the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost, that she may believe with the heart and confess with the mouth, and there may be two didrachmas for her. And let such faith be for her unto perfection. For three didrachmas are six drachmas, and sixty obols, which number marks perfection. Whence the people of Israel have six hundred thousand, that is, sixty myriads. For there were among them those moderately perfect, as already partakers of the Gospel conversation.
27.7:
**“SIXTY YEARS OLD”** — He who promised excellence of conversation, such as virginity or renunciation of the world, but has grown weak.
**“or upward,”** — For the old man is weak in his purpose.
**“a man”** — the stronger
**“shall give fifteen sicles:”** — or: drachmas
**“SHALL GIVE FIFTEEN SICLES”** — Or didrachmas, which are thirty drachmas. For the good ground yielded three fruits: the hundredfold, that is, to be a virgin or to renounce the world; the sixtyfold, namely continence; the thirtyfold, that is, the conversation of chaste wedlock.
**“a woman ten.”** — namely the keeping of the commandments
27.8:
**“If he be poor,”** — IF HE BE POOR etc. One who has sinned much; therefore Aquila translated: if he has gone beyond.
**“and not able to pay the estimation,”** — any of those mentioned above
**“he shall stand before the priest:”**
• offering a second time
• HE SHALL STAND BEFORE THE PRIEST etc. For if we have offered anyone subject to us to the service of God, we ought not to take him back into our own service, promising in his place either a better or a less good.
**“AS MUCH AS HE SHALL VALUE HIM AT”** — That is: as much satisfaction as he sees him able to bear, he will impose; namely, if he is wealthy, that he distribute money; if healthy, that he fast, pray, labour.
27.9:
**“But a beast that may be sacrificed to the Lord, if any one shall vow, shall be holy,”**
• BUT A BEAST etc. Because he has set forth the differences and degrees of the oblations which are from ourselves, he now sets forth, of those who are subject to us as cattle, when the oblation is holy.
• SHALL BE HOLY etc. According to the law, spotless and clean; as if we have offered to God a son, a disciple, a servant or anyone subject to us.
27.10:
**“And cannot be changed,”** — that is: we ought not to repent if we have offered
**“that is to say, neither a better for a worse,”** — for the less good
**“nor a worse for a better.”** — the less good
**“And if he shall change it:”** — that is: if he has had the will to change
**“both that which was changed, and that for which it was changed,”**
• what had been given before
• AND IF HE SHALL CHANGE IT etc. That the oblation may be double, and the enemy, who suggested changing the oblation, may be ashamed.
27.11: **“An unclean beast, which cannot be sacrificed to the Lord,”** — this cannot stand according to the letter
27.12:
**“Who judging whether it be good or bad, shall set the price:”**
• AN UNCLEAN BEAST etc. HESYCHIUS. Those which do not both divide the hoof and chew the cud are unclean. They divide the hoof who distinguish the letter and the spirit; they chew the cud who in meditating the laws have continual attention. He therefore who offers to God such a son or servant or disciple, who not from malice but from weakness neither chews the cud nor divides the hoof, let him bring him to the priest, who, judging whether he be good or bad, shall set the price, that is, shall impose a moderate yoke, that is, a middling conversation, that he may turn aside from evil and be advanced to better things, between the worse, namely, and the better, according to Symmachus, so that he can be offered to the Lord.
• It is to be known that it is one thing to be sanctified, another to be holy. For what is sanctified and offered begins to be holy, which it was not, and is increased little by little. What is holy and is God's needs no increase, because it is perfect. It is good therefore to be sanctified by the doctrine and help of others, but better to be such a one as can sanctify himself and others, which belongs to few. He therefore sanctifies before the Lord who wishes his family and kindred, sensible as well as intelligible, to live purely and holily, that it may be the Church of God. But if he is not fit to do this by himself, the priest ought to consider whether it be good or bad. For it consists of diverse persons, and he ought to enjoin on them according to what they can do.
27.13:
**“Which if he that offereth it will not give, he shall add above the estimation the fifth part.”**
• wisdom of mind
• THE FIFTH PART etc. The mind, namely, which rules the five senses, without which the foolish virgins are not received to the marriage.
27.14:
**“If a man shall vow his house, and sanctify it to the Lord, the priest shall consider it, whether it be good or bad, and it shall be sold according to the price, which he shall appoint.”**
• then
• IF A MAN SHALL VOW etc. In what follows he will say: Everything that is consecrated to the Lord, whether man or beast or field, cannot be redeemed; but here he commands the house and the field to be redeemed. But perhaps he decides this according to the diverse intentions of the offerers, as if there one no longer has the will to keep what he has wholly consecrated.
27.15:
**“But if he that vowed, will redeem it, he shall give the fifth part of the estimation over and above, and shall have the house.”**
• because the sanctification of the house is ascribed to him
• BUT IF HE THAT VOWED etc. To redeem is to free the family by doctrine and a pattern of life, and to wash away whatever stands against holiness. And he will add understanding and frequent remembrance to the admonition and edification of the priest.
27.16:
**“And if the field of his possession”** — AND IF THE FIELD etc. That is, the divine Scripture, whose vine is Christ, the Father the husbandman. In this the treasure is hidden, that is, the saving preaching; in this each one's possession is different, namely the manner of knowing which each has been able to obtain for himself.
**“he vow and consecrate”** — that he may begin to be holy
**“to the Lord.”** — by assigning it to the priest
**“according to the measure of the seed”** — the doctrine of the word, by which he has been instructed in the spiritual law
**“the price shall be rated. If the ground be sowed with thirty bushels of barley, let it be sold for fifty sicles of silver.”** — IF WITH THIRTY BUSHELS etc. In the thirty bushels of barley understand the Old Testament; in the fifty sicles, or didrachmas according to the Septuagint, the spiritual and perfect doctrine. But when this rule is to be given perfectly or diminished, understand from what follows: "If immediately from the year of the beginning jubilee" etc.
27.17: **“IF IMMEDIATELY FROM THE YEAR”** — That is: If he wishes the way of grace which he has chosen to be governed and drawn out by the priest, let the priest demand this. What he received when he was taught by perfect and spiritual doctrine, not condescending to him, because there is no need for him who has received the gift of calling; but let him make him abide in the doctrine which he delivered. But if something has been diminished of the gift which he received, and he has fallen from it in conversation, this is to consecrate the field some while after the jubilee. And the priest reckons the silver for the years remaining until the jubilee, namely, that he may define the remaining time of penance, and it is taken off the price. For in that he did less and lived worse, he diminished the gift and became weaker and more abject. Yet he can redeem the field, adding the fifth part of the silver to its price, namely, his own understanding to the doctrine of the priest, so that he becomes the governor and teacher of himself. For so the field which the offerer consecrated to the priest will be possessed by him.
27.19: **“And if he that had vowed, will redeem his field, he shall add the fifth part of the money of the estimation, and shall possess it.”** — HE SHALL ADD THE FIFTH PART etc. His own understanding to the doctrine of the priest: for at first we are governed by the doctrine and instruction of the priest, but afterward we ought to make progress and add our own understanding.
27.20:
**“And if he will not redeem it,”** — that is: to rule himself by his own understanding
**“but to another”** — teacher
**“man whatsoever it be sold,”** — for the price of doctrine, namely, that he may be taught
27.21:
**“For when the day of jubilee cometh,”** — that is: in the time of remission, namely when the time of the present life passes
**“it shall be sanctified to the Lord, and as a possession consecrated, pertaineth to the right of the priests.”**
• who taught him continually
• AND IF HE WILL NOT etc. He consecrates the field and redeems the field who has let his conversation be governed by another, but, with his help, having advanced, adds his own understanding so that he can rule himself. But he who, with another teaching, makes no progress and adds no understanding, who must always be taught and often acquiesces in wicked teachers, cannot seek the reward of virtue by which he might redeem the field; when the jubilee comes, that is, the time of remission, namely when the time of the present life passes, it will be a possession sanctified to the Lord. For the conversation which he once attained, even with another governing, will be holy to the Lord. But as a possession consecrated it pertains to the right of the priests: for the gain is his who continually governs.
27.22:
**“If a field”** — the virtue or life of his father, which he himself lost by neglect
**“AND NOT OF THE POSSESSION”** — Because it had been neither of the keeping of his ancestors nor of the buyer himself
**“be sanctified to the Lord,”**
• Offered to the priests, that the conversation of the sinner may be made holy.
• by exhorting, by reproving, lest the land be wholly lost
27.23:
**“The priest shall reckon according to the number of years”** — THE PRIEST SHALL RECKON etc. Rightly the priest, with him who admonished his brother to penance, reckons the true redemption, namely how he ought to repent. For he who corrected him knows his action and conversation strictly; but this one, as priest, the perfect redemption.
**“ACCORDING TO THE NUMBER OF YEARS”** — From the things, namely, which he preaches concerning penance: for the Scripture by the estimation of the jubilee, or of remission.
**“AND HE THAT HAD VOWED SHALL GIVE IT TO THE LORD”** — He does not say "they shall give", but he shall give. For although the definition of the estimation is given by the common counsel of the priest and of him who admonished to penance, yet he who roused him to repent will offer him: for this one will obey him, who himself is also bound to the penitent, that he may finish what he began.
27.24: **“But in the jubilee, it shall return to the former owner, who had sold it, and had it in the lot of his possession.”** — BUT IN THE JUBILEE IT SHALL RETURN etc. Because one is not wholly cleansed at once when penance is given or defined, but when it is completed, therefore he rightly says: But in the jubilee etc. For, penance completed and remission received, he will receive back the field of his conversation.
27.25:
**“All estimation by the sicle”** — or: by the didrachma
**“of the sanctuary shall be weighed.”** — ALL ESTIMATION etc. That every definition may be made by holy weights, that is, those coming from sacred Scripture: for outward weights, such as those of philosophers or heretics, by which they weigh the truths and perfections of men, are neither holy nor just.
**“A sicle hath twenty obols.”** — A SICLE HATH TWENTY etc. That is, the ten commandments, understood according to the letter and according to the spirit. But whoever rejects either the law or the Gospel does not have the didrachma, nor are his weights holy.
27.26:
**“The firstborn, which belong to the Lord,”** — THE FIRSTBORN WHICH etc. Those who obey us, sons, servants and disciples, are as our cattle. But the firstborn of these are those who obey in such a way as to give others example and teaching. Of whom it is said elsewhere: "Every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord." For he opens the womb of sons to be begotten who begins to obey according to God. Whence Paul says of Timothy: "Who is my dearest son in the Lord, who will put you in mind of my ways" etc.
**“no man may sanctify”** — NO MAN MAY SANCTIFY etc. Not because they are unworthy of sanctification, but because they are holy and need not be sanctified; as a son who so honours father and mother as also to become an example to others, as offering honour to God who commanded this. A servant also who "serves even his carnal masters in simplicity of heart, not serving to the eye", renders service to God himself.
**“and vow: whether it be bullock,”** — zealous in the working of the commandments of God
**“or sheep,”** — pleasing by simplicity
27.27:
**“And if it be an unclean beast,”** — AND IF IT BE AN UNCLEAN etc. The sinner, who neither meditates the law as he ought nor tries to distinguish. Whoever therefore is very obedient to father, master or teacher, and yet does not meditate or distinguish the law, is indeed a firstborn among the cattle, but unclean.
**“he that offereth it shall redeem it, according to its estimation, and shall add the fifth part of the price.”** — HE SHALL ADD THE FIFTH PART etc. Offering him doctrine with understanding, and ruling him wisely. For it belongs to a senseless father, master or teacher not to teach obedience to those subject to him who belong to him, and not to order their life so that they work according to the law. Let him therefore add understanding to subjection and doctrine. For he alone is the gift in the present case. Therefore he says: He shall add the fifth part of the price. Therefore he did not say: The priest shall estimate him, as above.
**“If he will not redeem it,”** — to make him sensible by admonition
27.28:
**“Any thing that is devoted to the Lord, whether it be man,”** — namely, in his own power
**“or beast,”** — subject to others
**“or field,”** — anyone's conversation
**“shall not be sold, neither may it be redeemed.”** — ANY THING THAT IS DEVOTED TO THE LORD etc. To anathematize is one thing, to sanctify another. For what has been anathematized cannot return to anyone's human use, not even the priest's. Therefore he who stole something of Jericho perished, because those things were anathematized. And whatever the children of Israel seized, at the Lord's command, by right of war from enemies with whom they ought not to be joined in friendship, they made anathema. We therefore, if in fighting we have gained spoils of war from the demons, ought to consecrate them to God, so that we keep nothing of our own will in them, whether it be man, that is, in his own power and equal to us in conversation; or beast, that is, one subject; or field, that is, the conversation of our lot.
**“Whatsoever is once consecrated”** — wholly estranged from the world
**“shall be holy of holies to the Lord.”**
• because he imitates the holy of holies with all his power
• WHATSOEVER IS ONCE etc. No one can despoil an enemy of what is gained by right of war unless he has perfectly subdued him. For when the strong man is bound, his goods are plundered.
