It is written in Genesis: "And these kings came together to the fountain of judgment, that is Cades, and they slew all the princes of Amalec and the Amorrhites." But it is asked whether there are two nations of the same name Amalec? For in the catalogue of the sons of Esau it is written: "These are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, in mount Seir. And these are the names of the sons of Esau: Eliphaz the son of Ada the wife of Esau. And the sons of Eliphaz were: Theman, Omar, Sepho, Gatham, Cenez. And Thamna was the concubine of Eliphaz the son of Esau, and she bore him Amalec. These are the sons of Ada the wife of Esau." And after a little: "And these are the dukes of the sons of Esau, the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: duke Theman, duke Omar, duke Sepho, duke Cenez, duke Core, duke Gatham, duke Amalec." This Amalec, therefore, was the son of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau by the concubine Thamna. But let us return to the first mention of Amalec, where those who returned "and came to the fountain of judgment, which is called Cades, slay all the princes of Amalec". For Cades is interpreted "sanctification" or "holy"; but Amalec, "licking up the people" or "turning the people aside". Those, therefore, who return to the holy and turn themselves to sanctification slay Amalec, who namely licks up the people or turns it aside. This is the contrary power and the spiritual wickednesses which turn the people aside from God. Their princes are the principalities against which the saints have their wrestling; whom yet they will not be able to overcome unless they are turned to holiness. He has always before his eyes the fountain of judgment; for he looks forward to the day of judgment, and, his heart purified, beholds both the punishments of the wicked and the beatitudes of the godly; and doing this he lays low the princes of the Amalecites. But others are subjected to the princes of Amalec. For these he licks up and consumes, and turns such a people aside from God. These things are referred to that first Amalec. Let us see this Amalec too, the son of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau, whom Thamna the concubine bore him; whose father Eliphaz is interpreted "God hath scattered me"; the mother Thamna, first indeed "degenerate", then "a moved failing"; necessarily he who is begotten of these is the enemy of Israel, licking up or turning aside the people. For he was the first who attacked the Hebrews when they had gone out of Egypt, in Raphidim, when Moses said to Jesus: "Choose out men, and go out and fight against Amalec" etc. And after a little it is written: "That Jesus put Amalec to flight, and his people, by the edge of the sword. And the Lord said to Moses: Write this for a memorial in a book, and deliver it to the ears of Jesus; for I will destroy the memory of Amalec from under heaven. And Moses built an altar, and called the name thereof: The Lord my refuge. Because with a hidden hand the Lord fights against Amalec from generation to generation." See what is to be understood by Amalec, against whom God fights with a hidden, that is, invisible, hand from generation to generation. In Deuteronomy too it is written: "Remember what Amalec did to thee in the way when thou camest out of Egypt: how he met thee, and slew the hindmost of the army, who sat down being weary" etc. Note how Amalec withstood the people of God in the way, yet could not cut off its head, but the tail; that is, those who followed last behind and, not forgetting the things that were behind, did not stretch themselves forth to those before. Whence: "No man putting his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God." For he who is found behind in the tail, Amalec will cut him off. In the book of Kings too Samuel says to Saul: "Thus saith the Lord of hosts: I have reckoned up all that Amalec hath done to Israel, how he opposed them in the way when they came up out of Egypt. Now therefore go, and smite Amalec, and utterly destroy all that he hath; spare him not" etc. A little after: "It repenteth me that I have made Saul king." And here too, then, observe how God through the prophet commands Saul to fight against Amalec and spare none; and because he spared, he incurred an inexpiable offence, so that against his own nature God said: "It repenteth me that I have made Saul king." Let us not spare, therefore, him who turns aside the people or licks up and devours it. The invisible Amalec, who resists in the way and assails those who wish to go up out of Egypt and climb from the darkness of the world to the land of promise, and if he finds them weary, failing, looking back, set at the last and in the tail, will cut them off and destroy them. Therefore we must hold to the things before, and go up to the top of the mountain, and the hands must always be lifted in prayer to heaven, that so at last Amalec may be conquered. David, when he had waged many wars and there had been very fierce and frequent conflicts against the foreigners, is not written to have obtained the kingdom until he had first subdued Amalec. Whence also David returned after he had slain Amalec, and took up the kingdom of Saul; though Amalec is written to have first made great slaughter among the people of Israel and burned very many cities. For before the coming of the true David, who was born of the seed of David, the spiritual Amalecites, that is, the contrary powers, made great slaughter among the people of Israel and took captive the two wives of David himself, namely the Jewish and the Gentile people. For it is clear that all were under sin; but the issue of things did not remain in these. But David, coming, found the Amalecites scattered, eating and drinking and exulting in the prey, and slew them; and after this slaughter he returned and took up the kingdom. Of this Amalec, therefore, Balaam says: Amalec the beginning of nations, and their seed shall perish. Their seed is the persuasion and doctrine by which they teach men to turn aside from God. This, therefore, shall perish, not they themselves in whom it was sown; for they, when they are converted and lament, shall be saved. This exposition stands against those who accuse the God of the law of hardness and cruelty, who pronounce that not only the nation of Amalec but its seed too will perish; since the nation is referred to the spiritual wickednesses, and the seed is expounded as the doctrine of Gentile superstitions and the worship of idols and every sect which turns the people aside from God.
24.21:
**“He saw also the Cinite: and took up his parable, and said: Thy habitation indeed is strong: but though in a rock”**
• Christ
• He does not seem to name the Cinite very culpably, to whom Saul said: "Go, depart from Amalec, lest I destroy thee with him; for thou hast shewn kindness to Israel" etc. His habitation is strong if he puts his nest in the rock, which is Christ.
**“HE SAW ALSO THE CINITE”** — THE SAME. And seeing the Cinite he said: Strong is thy habitation, and if thou put thy nest in a rock; and if there be to thee for Beor a nest of cunning, the Assyrians shall lead thee captive, etc. Beor is the father of Balaam, figuring the heretics. And it is said that the Cinite can be safe if he puts his nest, namely his hope, in the rock, that is, Christ; and the cunning of the heretics does not surround and hem him in. For if this happens, it will profit nothing that he seems placed in the rock; for he will be led captive by the Assyrians, namely the evil spirits, by whom the heretics are taken captive. The conjunction too seems to trouble the sense of this exposition; but it is native to the Hebrew tongue to use the conjunction frequently, so that at times it is redundant. For each tongue has something proper to it which among others seems faulty. Here, therefore, the conjunction is redundant and superfluous. Let the Cinite, therefore, who is interpreted "possession", beware; although, if he possesses and turns aside to wicked dogmas, he is delivered to the Assyrians. For those who blaspheme, set in the Church, are delivered to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme. And they are delivered to the Assyrians, which is interpreted "directing", not that they may perish utterly, but that they may be directed and corrected and learn not to blaspheme.
**“GREGORY”** — The Cinite is "possessor". Those who possess present things, who are strong in wit, who are skilled in the wit of worldly wisdom, truly build themselves a strong habitation if they feel themselves weak, and set the confidence of the mind to be nourished in the lofty humility of Christ, and by the flight of the heart pass beyond all that passes away.
**“thou build thy nest,”** — hope
24.22:
**“And thou be chosen of the stock of Cain,”** — my nest, or possession
**“CHOSEN”** — The chosen from the number of the wise, the seekers of truth, live a perpetual life. Whence: "They that explain me shall have life everlasting."
**“how long shalt thou be able to continue? Assur”** — directing
**“ASSUR”** — The devil, namely, to whom the heretics are delivered to be directed and corrected.
24.23:
**“And taking up his parable, again he said:”** — the conclusion of the prophecy of Balaam
**“PARABLE”** — He is often said to speak in parables, lest we take anything in these things not as a parable but according to the letter.
**“Alas, who shall live”** — according to God, not by the common life
**“WHO SHALL LIVE”** — So happy is he who sees, feels, understands and believes that God has done these things so.
**“WHEN THE LORD SHALL DO THESE THINGS”** — When, namely, a star shall rise out of Jacob, a man shall rise up out of Israel, and shall destroy Amalec, and his seed shall perish; that is, when Christ shall come and destroy the worship of idols and subject the power of demons.
24.24:
**“They shall come in galleys from Italy, they shall overcome the Assyrians,”**
• the nations of demons
• THEY SHALL COME, etc. It seems to signify that about the time of the Lord's incarnation the Romans would come to overcome the Assyrians, the Hebrews and all the eastern peoples, and at last to lose the kingdom, according to the statue of Daniel; or that at the coming of Christ, at the end of times, which the western part signifies, all the kingdoms of the world are overcome by the sword of the spirit, that is, the word of God, and in the time of antichrist the preaching of the Gospel ceases.
**“ORIGEN”** — And they shall come out of the hands of the Cetheans and shall afflict the Assyrians. Cetheans are interpreted "the blow of the end". Those, therefore, who, converted to God and taught by Christ, escape the blow which shall come upon the wicked at the end of the world, shall afflict the Assyrians; that is, those set in the contest, under whose feet God shall crush Satan, shall afflict the Assyrians, that is, the demons. For they shall tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy.
**“and shall waste the Hebrews, and at the last”** — when they have poured out their strength
**“THE HEBREWS”** — He is a Hebrew who passes over from Egypt to the land of promise, from darkness to light, from death to life. But he cannot obtain it without great struggle. He afflicts, therefore, and is afflicted; he strikes the adversary and is struck. The Assyrians, therefore, afflict the Hebrews, that is, the people of God, as they are afflicted by them.
**“they themselves also”** — not the Hebrews
**“shall perish.”** — the just Judge saying: Depart, ye cursed, into everlasting fire.
**“THEY THEMSELVES ALSO SHALL PERISH”** — THE SAME. And they themselves likewise shall perish. Not with the Hebrews, namely, but likewise, that is, at once, as soon as they have afflicted the Hebrews. For the Greek word puts likewise for at once. This, therefore, will be the end of all: that Assur, to whom offenders among the people of God were delivered, either for the destruction of the flesh that the spirit might be saved, or that he might learn not to blaspheme, should himself also perish by him who has power to destroy in gehenna, who will say to them: "Depart into everlasting fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels." One sheep of a hundred perished; but the good shepherd, leaving the ninety-nine on the mountains and coming down to this vale of tears, sought it and found it and carried it back laid on his shoulders. But this Assur, who is said to perish at the end of all things, I do not know whether he can ever be either sought or found; he perished therefore not by straying but by judgment, not moved by a slip but stopped up by perseverance. For as to what is written: "I will kill and I will make to live; I will bring down to hell and bring back again", I do not know whether it looks to all generally or only to those whom the deceit of the devil has brought down to death.
24.25: **“AND BALAAM ROSE”** — Because Balaam, constrained by the power of God, could not curse Israel, wishing to please the king, he says: "Come, I give thee counsel"; but he did not disclose the counsel; which yet is related at the end of this book, but more fully where John says: "Thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat, and to commit fornication." As if: this people conquers not by its own strength, but by seeking God and by keeping chastity. Cast down its chastity and it will be conquered of itself; the fight must be not by the strength of soldiers but by the comeliness of women; beauty conquers armed men, loveliness takes iron captive. When the women have perceived that they have surrendered to lust, let them not give themselves to them in their desire before they eat of the sacrifices of idols and are consecrated to Beelphegor. And king Balac at once obeyed the counsel.

25.1:
**“And Israel at that time abode in Settim,”**
• SEPTUAGINT: Israel put in at Sethim.
• Sethim: answer, or refutation
**“and the people committed fornication with the daughters of Moab,”**
• Because it did not put in well, it was refuted by God.
• THE SAME. John says in the Apocalypse: "Thou hast there some that hold the doctrine of Balaam" etc. He who does what Balaam did seems to teach his doctrine. As the doctrine of Jezabel is mentioned there, not that anyone of the disciples of Jezabel teaches what she handed down; but he who persecutes the prophets as she did, or takes some by guile, or destroys the innocent by false charges, he holds the doctrine of Jezabel. So therefore he who by wicked counsel begets a stumblingblock in the people, and provokes the offence and wrath of God, either by communicating in the sacrifices of idols or by serving lust, holds the doctrine of Balaam. Execrable, then, is even the fornication of the body, which violates the temple of God and takes the members of Christ and makes them the members of a harlot. But more execrable is the general fornication, in which every kind of sin is contained alike; when the soul, namely, taken into the fellowship of the word of God and joined to him in marriage, is corrupted by the adversary of him who espoused her to himself in faith. The bridegroom and husband of the clean soul, then, is the word of God, that is, Christ. Whence: "For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ" etc. While, therefore, the soul cleaves to the bridegroom, and embraces and hears his word, she receives from him the seed of the word, and conceives and bears sons, that she may be saved through the bearing of children, if she continue in faith and charity (even if before, like Eve, she was seduced). Where the union of the soul with the word of God has been made and the embrace given to each other, a noble offspring is born: chastity, namely, justice, patience and all the virtues. But if she prostitutes herself to the devil and the demons, she will bear sons of adultery, namely all sins. Through each thing, then, that we do our soul begets sons, namely thoughts and works. And if what it does is according to the law and the word of God, it brings forth the spirit of salvation and will be saved through the bearing of children, of whom it is said: "Thy children as olive plants round about thy table." But if what it does is against the law, from the conception of the contrary spirit it brings forth sons of sin and cursing. The soul always brings forth, always begets, conceiving either of the word or of the contrary spirit. Perhaps to these generations looks what was said: "For when they were not yet born, nor had done any good or evil" etc. For these generations of the soul, begotten of the Holy Ghost, are loved before they do anything good; but if of the wicked spirit, before they accomplish anything evil, by this very fact that the soul has brought forth a will of this kind, the execrable conception of an evil will is worthily held in hatred. Therefore perhaps the child Chanaan too is cursed before he was born, because his father had sinned; and Noe, prophesying, when he marked out all the best things for each of his sons, when he came to Cham said: Cursed be the child Chanaan. Whence: "O daughter of Babylon, miserable! Blessed shall he be who shall repay thee thy payment which thou hast paid us. Blessed be he that shall take and dash his little ones against the rock." And if the Babylonian conception has not yet done any work in us, while it is little, do not pity it; kill it at once, for it is hateful; dash it against the rock, lest it grow, lest the works of confusion be increased in it. The rock is Christ; set in the sight of his dread judgment, let this offspring perish. These things have been said of the general fornication, of which bodily fornication is a species. Hence Paul says: "He who is joined to the Lord is one spirit, and he who is joined to a harlot is one body." As if every soul is joined either to the Lord or to a harlot. But by the Lord he meant the virtues: Christ is, that is, the word, wisdom, virtue, justice and the like; but by the harlot every species of malice. Whence: A woman meets him, having the appearance of a harlot, who makes the hearts of young men fly away. This harlot is malice; he who joins himself to this harlot is made one body of malice. As therefore he who joins himself to the Lord joins himself to wisdom, justice, piety and truth, and with them all is made one spirit, so he who joins himself to this harlot joins himself to unchastity, iniquity, lying and all evils, with which he is made one body.
**“AND THE PEOPLE COMMITTED FORNICATION”** — ORIGEN. The history itself edifies us, teaching that fornication wars against us. But if we have the arms of the Apostle, the darts of luxury will not harm us; that is, if we have the breastplate of justice, the helmet of salvation, the sword of the spirit, which is the word of God, and the shield of faith, our feet shod in the preparation of the Gospel of peace. If we cast away these arms, we give place to the devil, and the whole choir of demons takes us captive, and God is angry against us; and not only in the present, but in the future we shall be punished. Chastity and justice, prudence and the other virtues make us conquer; but luxury, lust, avarice, impiety and all malice make us be conquered.
25.2:
**“Who called them to their sacrifices. And they ate of them,”** — they were consecrated, namely, to the idols of the Gentiles
**“THEY ATE”** — As though he had eaten even of the things sacrificed to idols, which are execrable before God. For what agreement has God with idols?
**“ORIGEN”**
• The Apostle says: If anyone sees one having knowledge sitting at meat in the idol's temple, will not his conscience, being weak, be emboldened to eat things sacrificed to idols? Where he seems to pronounce the thing itself not so much grievous as the offence of him who, seeing these things, is provoked to the same, since he is not fortified by a like judgment; so that he is guilty not so much for himself as for another. Perhaps men studious of Greek letters and lovers of philosophy, held by desire of the old studies, ate the dogmas of the philosophers as things sacrificed to idols; which perhaps did not unsettle those who had received the knowledge of the truth; but those less learned in Christ, if they read such things imitating them, could be wounded. Because, therefore, charity seeks not what is profitable to itself but what is to many, let us take such food of the word as not only edifies and delights us but does not offend those who see. There is, then, a thing sacrificed to idols not only in foods but in words. Every speech which teaches piety, justice and truth is sacrificed to God; but that which teaches unchastity, injustice, impiety, to idols; and he who receives it eats things sacrificed to idols.
• Solomon, though he was most wise, bowed his sides to many women; therefore he was deceived. Yet I do not think that the many women are not called many dogmas; which, when the most wise man wished to search out and know each, he could not keep himself within the rule of the divine law. The Moabite philosophy deceived him, so that he sacrificed to the Moabite idol, and of the Ammonites and the other nations whose women he is said to have received; he built temples, sacrificed to idols. It is a great work to be mingled with so many dogmas as with women and not turn aside from the truth, but to say steadfastly: "There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and young maidens without number. One is my dove."
**“and adored their gods.”** — not only that, but they ate
**“AND THEY ADORED”** — Note the order: concupiscence first deceives evil servants, then gluttony, last impiety takes them captive, whose wage, fornication, is paid out.
25.3:
**“And Israel was initiated to Beelphegor: upon which the Lord being angry,”** — because the law reproves them as negligent and slothful
**“AND HE WAS INITIATED”** — Consecrated, namely, to the mysteries of the idol which among the Madianites is worshipped chiefly by women, and is a species of foulness; but what it is, or of what kind or form, is hardly found written, perhaps lest it pollute the hearer. Since, then, there are many species of foulness, one is called Beelphegor. Everyone, therefore, who commits anything foul in any species of foulness is consecrated to Beelphegor.
**“ORIGEN”** — And he was initiated to Beelphegor, etc. Through all the sins we commit, above all if we sin not by some stealing upon us but by set purpose, we are consecrated to that demon to whom what we commit is a care. And perhaps we are consecrated to as many demons as the sins we commit, and we receive the mysteries of this idol or that. Whence: "For the mystery of iniquity already worketh." Going about, therefore, they seek how to consecrate each one to their mysteries. If you feel the wicked spirit speak in your heart to lead you to some work of sin, understand that he wishes to bind you over to some demon, that you may receive the mysteries of the devil. There is present to each of us a good angel, who rules, who warns, who for the correcting of our acts and the begging of mercies daily sees the face of God. And according to the Apocalypse of John an angel presides over each Church in general, who is either praised for the good deeds of the people or blamed for its offences. In which I am moved to wonder at a stupendous mystery: that God has such care of us that he suffers even his angels to be blamed and confuted for us. For as when a boy is handed over to a tutor, if he appears trained in less worthy disciplines, the blame is referred to the tutor, and the boy is not so reproved by the father as the tutor; unless the boy, hard and wanton and froward, has spurned the wholesome warnings of the tutor. But what becomes of that soul the prophet teaches, saying: "And the daughter of Sion shall be left as a covert in a vineyard" etc. For the soul is of its own choice, and therefore the judgment of God is just, because of its own will it obeys either good or evil counsellors. But the salvation of man is a greater care to God than his perdition to the devil. For as though the diligence of the angels were not enough against the snares of the demons and of those who draw to sin, the only-begotten of God himself is present, defends, guards and draws us to himself. Whence: I am with you even to the consummation of the world. Nor is it enough to be with us; he uses force on us and draws us to salvation. Whence: "I will draw all things to myself." See how he draws not only the willing but also the hesitating. Whence to one who wished to bury his father he gave not even a space of time, but said: "Let the dead bury their dead" etc. The Father too draws us. Whence: "No man cometh to me, unless my Father draw him"; who says to his servants: Whomsoever you shall find, compel them to come in. The Holy Ghost also says: Separate me Paul and Barnabas, etc. He also forbids Paul to go into Asia, and compels him to go to Jerusalem, foretelling that bonds and prisons await him there.
25.4:
**“Said to Moses: Take all the princes of the people, and hang them up against the sun”**
• from whom nothing is hid
• TAKE ALL THE PRINCES OF THE PEOPLE, etc. ORIGEN. Perhaps these things are referred to the angels. For they will come to judgment with us and stand before the sun of justice, lest perhaps there was some cause in them of our having sinned, lest perhaps they spent less work to call us back from sins. Whence in the Apocalypse: I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, and the like. For if the angel who received us sealed from God hopes for a reward for the things we have done well, he fears also to be blamed for things done ill. And therefore they are said to be shown against the sun, that it may appear by whose fault the sins were committed through which we are consecrated to Beelphegor or to any idol, according to the quality of the sin. But if the prince, that is, the angel assigned to each, did not fail, but warned of good things and spoke in my heart, at least in that wherein conscience calls me back from sin, and I, spurning his warnings and the rein of conscience, broke out into sins, the penalty will be doubled for me, for contempt of the warner and for the crime committed. Do not wonder if angels come with men to judgment. For the Lord himself will come to judgment with the princes of his people. Let the princes be shown, then, and if the fault is in them, the wrath of God ceases from the people. We ought therefore to be the more anxious, knowing that not only for our own acts shall we stand before the tribunal of the Lord, but the angels too, as our princes and leaders. Whence: "Obey your prelates, for they watch as being to render an account of your souls."
**“ORIGEN”** — The people sins, and the princes are shown against the sun to be examined, that they may be reproved by the light. For they are reproved not only for their own offences; for the princes are compelled to render account for the people, lest perhaps they did not teach, did not warn, did not carefully reprove those who first sinned, so that the contagion should not be spread among the peoples. For the wrath of God would be turned upon them, and would cease from the people. If men thought on these things they would not canvass for headships. It is enough for each to be reproved and render account for his own sins. What need is there to be shown against the sun for the sins of the people, before which nothing can be hidden, nothing obscured?
**“AUGUSTINE”** — And the Lord said to Moses: "Take the leaders of the people and show them to the Lord against the sun, and the wrath of the anger of the Lord shall be taken away from Israel." The Lord was angry at the fornications of Israel, carnal, namely, and spiritual. For they had both mingled themselves with the daughters of Moab and been consecrated to idols. He told Moses to show the leaders of the people to the Lord against the sun, that is, openly, in the sight of this light. For the Greek says paradeigmatison, which could be called "make examples", because paradeigma is called an example. For Aquila said: Fasten, or rather fasten up; but Symmachus: Hang. But it is a wonder that the scripture left off relating whether this was fulfilled according to the Lord's command; which I do not see could have been disregarded, or, if disregarded, disregarded with impunity. But if it was done and passed over in silence, why does the scripture say that the Lord was appeased, and the plague ceased, by Phinees transfixing the adulterers? As though, the leaders having been crucified as the Lord had commanded, the indignation still persisting seemed to need appeasing in another way; since what he had foretold could not be false, saying: "The wrath of the Lord's punishment shall be turned away from Israel." If therefore it had been done, who would doubt that the wrath had been turned away? What need was there, then, that Phinees should take vengeance on the adulterers to appease God, and the scripture testify that the Lord was thus appeased? Unless perhaps we understand that, when Moses was arranging to fulfil what the Lord had commanded concerning the leaders of the people, he wished also according to the law to punish such crimes, so that he commanded each to kill his neighbour consecrated to strange gods; and meanwhile Phinees did that; and so, the wrath of God being now appeased, there was no need for the leaders of the people to be crucified. This severity, surely fitting to that time, shows clearly enough to the prudent of faith how great an evil is fornication and idolatry.
**“on gibbets”** — openly, namely, that they may be an example to all
25.7:
**“And when Phinees saw it,”** — Christ
**“AND WHEN PHINEES SAW IT”** — ORIGEN. These things edified the former people; but you who have been redeemed by Christ, from whose hands the bodily sword has been taken and to whom the sword of the spirit has been given, seize this sword. And if you see the Israelite sense whoring with the Madianite harlots, that is, the will with devilish thoughts, do not spare, do not pretend otherwise; strike at once, destroy the sin; striking and piercing the womb itself too, that is, the secret places of nature, cut out the very tinder of sinning, lest it conceive and beget further, and the cursed offspring of sins defile the camp of Israel. For so you will allay the wrath of God. For you have forestalled the day of judgment, which is called the day of wrath and fury; and the tinder of sin, which here is called the womb of the woman, being destroyed, you come secure to the judgment. Let us pray, then, that I may always find this sword of the spirit ready, through which the very seeds and conceptions of guilt may be destroyed, and God become propitious to you through the true Phinees, our Lord Jesus Christ.
**“the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, he rose up”** — we too must rise up against such things
**“from the midst of the multitude, and taking a dagger,”** — the sword of the Spirit
**“TAKING A DAGGER”** — It signifies that through the cross of Christ not only idolatry but every affection or concupiscence of the flesh is destroyed, and so God is appeased.
25.8:
**“Went in after the Israelite”** — the Israelite sense
**“into the brothel house, and thrust both of them through together, to wit, the man and the woman”** — the devilish thought
**“in the genital parts.”** — the very tinder of sin
25.9: **“THERE WERE SLAIN FOUR AND TWENTY THOUSAND”** — Because, forsaking the light of truth and justice, they loved the blindness of idolatry and fornication, deprived of the light of the eternal sun they run into the darkness of death. For the visible sun lights the world for twenty-four hours, and by its circuit puts to flight the darkness of night; so too Christ, to put to flight the darkness of sin, lights the world through the apostles and prophets.
25.13: **“THE COVENANT OF THE PRIESTHOOD FOR EVER”** — Whoever, pricked with the zeal of God, despises and presses down the goads of the flesh, or corrects those subject to him lest they wanton, acquires an everlasting priesthood, belonging to the same one of whom it is said: "Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech"; with whom they shall possess an everlasting kingdom. Phinees is interpreted "sparing with the mouth", or "rested with the mouth", or "augury of the mouth"; Eleazar, "God my helper", or "help of God"; Aaron, "mountain of strength", or "strong mountain". These names fittingly express the aforesaid sense. For he who spares with the mouth, lest he speak wicked things, and expounds heavenly mysteries, fulfilling a godly labour for his hearers through the help of God, happily ascends to the mountain of strength, that is, Christ.
25.14:
**“And the name of the Israelite, that was slain with the woman of Madian, was”**
• psalm, or song
• AND THE NAME, etc. The Israelite who committed fornication with the Madianite woman signifies those who, separated from the Church by error or wicked working, stir up blasphemy of God among the faithful; to whom it is said: Through you the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles; whom they show in name only as Israelites. For Zambri too is interpreted "psalm" or "song"; Salu, "looking to temptation"; Simeon, "he heard sadness" or "name of a dwelling"; Cozbi, "immeasurable cup" or "sacrifice to me"; Sur, "wall" or "straitness"; Madian, "contradiction" or "answer". Zambri therefore signifies the bodily or spiritual fornicator, who stirs up among the enemies of Christ not a song of praise but a psalm of mockery. Whence: "They that drank wine made me their song." This one, then, looking to temptation and consenting to temptation, under the name of a dwelling, that is, of a churchman, brings sadness upon the faithful by his fall; because he is filled with love of the immeasurable cup, that is, serving gluttony, he sacrificed himself to the devil when he gave his members over to lust. This one, by his wicked work producing the answer of contradiction from the adversaries of God, plunged himself into the walls and straitness of the eternal prison, where he will be tormented day and night until the last farthing.
**“Zambri the son of Salu,”** — looking to temptation
**“a prince of the kindred and tribe of Simeon.”** — He heard sadness, or name of a dwelling
25.15:
**“And the Madianite woman, that was slain with him, was called Cozbi”**
• others: Cozbi
• 'immeasurable cup' or 'sacrifice to me'
**“the daughter of Sur,”** — 'wall' or 'straitness'
**“a most noble prince among the Madianites.”** — Madian: 'contradiction' or 'answer'
25.18:
**“Because they also have acted like enemies against you, and have guilefully deceived you by the idol Phogor,”** — of that place
**“and Cozbi”** — or: Cozbi

26.1: **“AFTER THE GUILTY”** — ORIGEN. Because those who had been enrolled first fell for their sin, a second people now, succeeding in their place, is called to the numbering. And what had not been said of those is said of these, namely: "To these shall the land be divided for a lot according to the number of names" etc. If it had been said of the former it would have been false, because they fell in the desert for their sin; but for these all that is promised was fulfilled.
26.2: **“Number the whole sum of the children of Israel from twenty years old and upward, by their houses and kindreds, all that are able to go forth to war.”** — NUMBER THE WHOLE, etc. Again the people are numbered, and the Levites, that, the first carnal ones having been slain, a new people of God may be enrolled, which passes over through the baptism of the Jordan and receives the promise of the heavenly inheritance.
26.15: **“The sons of Gad by their kindreds: Sephon, of him is the family of the Sephonites: Aggi, of him is the family of the Aggites: Sumi”** — elsewhere: Suni
26.23:
**“The sons of Issachar, by their kindreds: Thola, of whom is the family of the Tholaites: Phau,”** — elsewhere: Phua
**“of whom is the family of the Phauites”** — elsewhere: of the Phuaites
26.36: **“Now the son of Suthala was Heram”** — others: Herat, or Heran
26.53:
**“To these shall the land be divided according to the number”** — TO THESE SHALL THE LAND BE DIVIDED. ORIGEN. The former people, which is in circumcision, is rejected, and the second is brought in from the uncircumcision, which obtains the father's inheritance not from Moses but from Jesus. For Moses, if he gives an inheritance to any, gives it not within the Jordan, which he does not cross at all; he gives land outside, not flowing with milk and honey, but fit for cattle, nourishing dumb and irrational animals better than men. My Jesus gives the second people a land flowing with milk and honey, nay rather one that is a honeycomb above every land. And Moses indeed does not give the inheritance by lot, nor can he weigh by peoples, houses, families, names and the merits of each, and by divine lot. This Jesus alone does, to whom the Father has given all judgment. He knows too how to assign each a worthy mansion. Yet there are some among these who stand out above, and are not brought to the lot at all: all the Levites, namely, that is, all who remain intent in the ministry of God, wakeful in his service, keeping the watches; they do not seek or receive a lot among the rest; nor is their lot on earth, but the Lord himself is their lot and inheritance. These are they who, dulled by no obstacles of bodily nature, having passed beyond the glory of all invisible things, have set the use and exercise of living in the sole wisdom and word of God; who seek nothing bodily, but only the knowledge of the secrets of God; and where their heart is, there is their treasure; they will always delight in the Lord and in his word and in wisdom. This is their food, this their drink, these their riches, this will be their kingdom. But those who are lower receive an inheritance of land, though of some more sublime and more powerful land. For the land of the living is promised, which is called of the living because it knows not death. And these indeed are great and blessed; but more blessed are those who shall see God no longer through a glass and in a dark manner, nor in bodily substances, but face to face, irradiated with the light of wisdom and made capable of pure divinity through purity.
**“ORIGEN”** — The division and inheritance of this land holds the form of the heavenly inheritance which shall be divided to the saints. "There are many there, and there are few, but the few more blessed. For many go by the broad way that leads to death; but those who make for the narrow way that leads to life are called few, because few are they who are saved." And elsewhere: "Because iniquity hath abounded, the charity of many shall grow cold", not of few. In the ark of Noe (where the measure was given from heaven) the length in the lower parts is set at three hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty; but the top is finished in the space of one cubit. For in the lower parts were beasts and cattle; in the upper, birds; but in the highest, rational man. The top itself is gathered into one cubit; for all things are led back to the monad. Set down the whole number of the human race; choose the faithful, they will be fewer than all; from the faithful choose the better, you will find fewer; from these again choose the more perfect, they will be fewer; and the further you proceed in choosing, the fewer you will find, until at last you come to some one who may say confidently that he laboured more than all. Those who in this way are more receive more of land and bodily inheritance; but the few, little, because they have more in the Lord. Others receive nothing at all of earthly inheritance, who are worthy to be priests, ministers of God; for the Lord himself is wholly their inheritance. Yet for their beasts they receive some land, but of that which is adjoining the cities.
26.54:
**“To the greater number”** — in worthiness of life
**“TO THE GREATER NUMBER A GREATER”** — That, namely, the more numerous tribe should obtain greater spaces of land, but the one that is less in number of men, a lesser.
**“thou shalt give a greater portion, and to the fewer a less: to every one, as they have now been reckoned up, shall a possession be delivered:”** — One just man, according as he is accepted by God, is held for many. Whence: "By one wise man the city shall be inhabited; but the tribe of the wicked shall be made desolate"; and one just man is for the whole world. "But the wicked, even if they are many, are reckoned small and as nothing with God." There is, then, also a praiseworthy multitude. Whence to Abraham, whom he brought forth abroad, he says: "Look up to heaven, and number the stars if thou canst; so shall thy seed be" etc. In which it is to be noted that the just man always abides in the inner things, because he prays to the Father in secret, and all the glory of the king's daughter, that is, of the royal soul, is within; but God brings him forth abroad when the matter and the order of visible things requires it.
26.55: **“THAT BY LOT THE LAND”** — The inheritance is commanded to be divided by lot; but I see Moses himself, to whom these things are commanded, dividing the inheritance not by lot to Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses. Jesus too gives an inheritance outside the lot to the tribe of Juda and to Caleb and to the tribe of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasses. For the rest the lot is cast. Whence I think that in the heavenly inheritance some will not come to the lot, nor be numbered with the rest (although they are saints), but their inheritance will be choice, as was Caleb's and the tribe of Juda's and Jesus the son of Nave's. For as, when victory has been won, the spoils are divided, the choice warriors are not brought to the lot with the rest, but receive all the best things by the merit of their virtues, while the rest by lot use the right of victory; so it seems to me Christ my Lord will do. For to those he will decree special and sublime honours whose magnificent deeds and sublime virtues he knows. Whence he says: "Father, I will that where I am, they also may be with me"; and elsewhere: "You also shall sit on twelve thrones"; and elsewhere: "As thou, Father, in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us." All these come down not by lot but by the prerogative of love.
26.60: **“Of Aaron were born Nadab and Abiud”** — others: Abiu
26.65:
**“For the Lord had foretold that they should all die in the wilderness. And none remained of them, but Caleb the son of Jephone, and Josue the son of Nun.”**
• the faithful, namely, of both peoples, or the followers of action or of contemplation
• BUT CALEB, etc. ISIDORE. Six hundred thousand armed men are said to have gone out of Egypt, and only two entered the land of promise. For many pass through baptism to the faith, but very few come to the heavenly fatherland, according to that: "Many are called, but few chosen." Only two enter, on account of those who from both peoples obtain the heavenly kingdom, or who through action and contemplation are predestined to eternal beatitude.

27.7:
**“They demand a just thing,”** — because the people of the law is not shut out from the possession of the Gospel
**“the daughters”** — daughters: that is, works accomplished by the ministry of the body.
**“of Salphaad:”** — of him, namely, who has the shadow of the law in his mouth, perceiving nothing deep, nothing spiritual
**“Give them a possession among their father's kindred, and in his inheritance”** — the heavenly
**“let them succeed him.”** — among the people, namely, not among the Levites, whose inheritance is God alone
**“GIVE THEM A POSSESSION”** — ORIGEN. Thou shalt give a possession, etc. What force these things have according to the history is plain to all who know that these laws are kept not only among the children of Israel but among all men who live by laws at all. Whence it appears that the freedom of the daughters of Salphaad not only conferred an inheritance on them but gave perpetual rights of living to the world. You see how great is the usefulness even of the history: who can dissolve these laws which the whole world uses? But let us seek how we may be edified spiritually. For it can happen that I have neither daughters according to the flesh nor a right of inheritance; then for someone the law which was sanctioned by the divine voice will be idle. Let us inquire, then, in the spiritual law, who these five daughters are, who, even if their father died for some sin, yet themselves receive an inheritance by the command of God. The virtues of the soul and the senses of the mind are sons; but the daughters are the works fulfilled by the ministry of the body. For there are five senses of the body, by which every work in the body is accomplished. These five daughters, then, that is, the perfection of works, even if they remain bereft of a father, are not cast off from the inheritance; they are not shut out from the kingdom, but receive an inheritance in the midst of the people of God. Salphaad is interpreted "shadow in his mouth". This is understanding, the father of works. There are many brethren in whom there is no higher and deeper understanding, but the sense in them is deadened; whence his heart too died within him. This one, then, if he savours nothing for spiritual understanding, but is deadened, yet if he has begotten daughters, that is, the works of God's commandments, they will certainly obtain an inheritance with the people of God. He will not indeed be able to be numbered among those whose portion is the Lord himself; for many are called but few chosen. And it is shown by the very name why he could not beget sons. For it is interpreted "shadow in his mouth": he who has the shadow of the law in his mouth and not the very image of the things can perceive nothing spiritual, nothing of deep understanding; only the shadow of the law is in his mouth; he cannot beget manly and spiritual senses, but works and acts, which are the simpler mysteries of life. And therefore it shows in these the clemency of the Lord: that the more innocent, even if they fall short in sense but have good works, are not shut out from the inheritance of the saints. Rightly, then, did the daughters of Salphaad speak.
27.8:
**“When a man dieth without a son,”** — who is strong in wisdom and understanding
**“WHEN A MAN DIETH”** — ORIGEN. A law of succession is set down: that first the son, in the second place the daughter should succeed, third the brother, fourth the father's brother; the fifth degree does not mark out anyone certain, but whoever is nearer out of the whole family should succeed. In these the sense of the history is whole and perfect, so that it seems to require nothing. But he who is learned in the spiritual laws can understand the different degrees of succession, and how the first degree of obtaining the heavenly inheritance is by merit of doctrine and knowledge, which is the male son; the second by the prerogative of works, which is the daughter; the third of fellow-feeling and imitation, whence it is also named brother. For there are some who do nothing of their own accord and by their own understanding, but, set among brethren, by imitation seem to do the things which those do who are moved by their own understanding. To these too the third degree of inheritance is given, as to brethren. The fourth, which he names the father's brother, can be understood as the order of men who try to fulfil the things heard from the fathers, moved not so much by their own senses, nor stirred by present doctrine, as by the tradition of the elders; yet they do something good. But the last degree is written as whoever in any way shall have been next to these; as if he said: whether by occasion or by the truth of doctrine anyone has done something good, he shall not lose his reward.
**“to his daughter.”** — him, namely, who is strong by the prerogative of works
27.9: **“If he have no daughter, his brethren shall succeed him.”** — who act by imitation of the wise
27.10: **“And if he have no brethren, you shall give the inheritance to his father's brethren.”** — those, namely, who do something good by the tradition of the elders, not by their own sense nor by the admonition of present doctrine
27.11: **“But if he have no uncles by the father, the inheritance shall be given to them that are the next akin.”** — namely, those who do something good either by occasion or by the truth of doctrine: for they do not lose their reward.
27.12:
**“The Lord also said to Moses: Go up into mountain”** — The perfect man dies not in the valley but on the mountain, that is, in a high place: because the perfection of his life was held on high.
**“this Abarim, and view from thence the land which I will give to the children of Israel.”**
• It was fitting that nothing should remain unknown to one about to attain the height of perfection.
• GO UP INTO THIS MOUNTAIN, etc. ORIGEN. See how he who is perfect, who is blessed, dies not in a valley, not on a plain, not on a hill, but on a mountain, that is, in a high and steep place; because the consummation of his life is held on high. But he is commanded to behold with his eyes all the land of promise and diligently survey all things from on high. For it was fitting that nothing should remain unknown to one about to attain the height of perfection, but that he should have knowledge of all things that are seen and heard. Therefore I believe it was so that, of all the things which, set in the flesh, he took in by bodily sight, when made in spirit and with naked mind hastening to the lecture halls and discipleship of wisdom, he might swiftly attain their reasons and causes. For what use was it to show one about to depart from the world lands and places whose toil he would not undergo nor glory receive? It terrifies me that things so perilous are said of Moses, the servant and friend of God, to whom the Lord spoke face to face, through whom he did signs and wonders. Thou shalt be gathered, he says, to thy people, as Aaron thy brother was gathered on mount Hor. He sets out the cause, saying: because you transgressed my word in the desert of Sin; you did not sanctify me at the water before them. So not even Moses is without fault; he too transgressed and was made under sin. Whence: "Death reigned from Adam unto Moses"; for it did not spare even him. For God hath concluded all under sin, that he may have mercy on all. But thanks to Christ, who has delivered us from the body of this death. For Moses could not deliver, since he too transgressed. He alone, then, must be sought who did no sin.
• THE SAME. The death of Moses is the end of the law which is spoken according to the letter; namely, the breaking off of the sacrifices and of the other things which are likewise commanded in the law. When these, then, receive their end, Jesus receives the leadership; for the end of the law is Christ, unto justice to everyone that believeth. And as it was said of the former: "That all in Moses were baptized, in the cloud and in the sea", so let it be said of Jesus, that all in Jesus were baptized in the Holy Ghost and water. For it is Jesus who crosses the waters of the Jordan and in them in a manner already then baptizes the people. He it is who divides the holy land to all, not to the former people but to the second; for the former fell in the desert for its sin. In the times of Jesus the land rested from wars, not in the times of Moses. But this was said of Jesus Christ, not of the son of Nave. And would that my land might cease from wars! And it would cease if I served faithfully under my prince Jesus; my flesh would not rise up against my spirit, nor would my land be assailed by contrary nations, that is, goaded by divers concupiscences. Let us pray, then, that Jesus may reign over us, and our land cease from wars, namely from the assaults of carnal desires; and then each will rest under his vine and under his fig tree and his olive; that is, under the covering of the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost our soul will rest.
27.14:
**“Because you offended me”**
• Even Moses transgressed. For all have sinned: Christ alone, then, could deliver from sin, who did no sin.
• BECAUSE YOU OFFENDED, etc. AUGUSTINE. The Lord gives the same cause for the death of Moses as for that of his brother: namely, because they did not sanctify him before the people at the water of contradiction; that is, because they doubted that by his gift water could flow from the rock. But mystically it is signified that neither the old priesthood, whose person Aaron bore, nor the law itself, whose person Moses bore, brings the people of God into the land of the eternal inheritance; but Jesus, in whom Christ is signified, that is, grace through faith. And Aaron indeed died before Israel entered any part of the land of promise. While Moses was still alive the land of the Amorrhites was taken and possessed, but he did not cross the Jordan with them. For in some part the law is observed in the Christian faith; but that priesthood and the sacrifices hold no part of the Christian faith today, except that they were done and are past in shadows of things to come. But since it is said to both brothers that they be gathered to their people, it is manifest that the wrath of God, which separates from the peace of eternal fellowship, was not upon them. Whence it is clear: "Not only their offices but their deaths too were signs of things to come, not punishments of God's indignation."
27.16:
**“MAY THE LORD PROVIDE”** — Note: he does not choose his sons, nor his nephews, nor ask that they be appointed leaders; he commits the choice to the judgment of God.
**“ORIGEN”** — May the Lord God provide. About to depart from this world, namely, he prays God to provide a leader for the people. He had sons, Gersam and Eliezer, and the sons of his brother, great and excellent men; he does not pray God for them that they be appointed leaders of the people; that the princes of the churches may learn not to mark out their successors by a testament of near kinship of the flesh, nor hand down the headship of the Church as an inheritance, nor choose him whom human affection commends, but to leave the choice of a successor to the judgment of God. He could have chosen a prince by right judgment, he to whom God had said: Choose elders for the people, whom thou knowest to be elders; and he chose such that the spirit of God at once rested on them and they all prophesied. But he did not choose, and does not dare, lest he leave to posterity an example of presumption; but he says: May the Lord God provide, etc. Who then will there be from the people, which is often wont to be moved by clamours stirred up for favour or price, or even from the priests, who should judge himself fit for this? Unless it be revealed to someone praying and asking of the Lord; as God says to Moses: Take to thee Jesus the son of Nave, etc. You hear the ordination of the prince of the people described so plainly and manifestly that it almost needs no exposition. No acclamation of the people here, no regard of kinship; to kinsmen let the inheritance of fields and estates be left; let the government of the people be handed to him whom God has chosen; who, namely, has in himself the spirit of God and in his sight the commandments of God; who is known and familiar to Moses, that is, in whom is the brightness and knowledge of the law; that the children of Israel may be able to hear him.
27.18: **“THE SPIRIT”** — The Holy, namely. For he would not say this of the spirit of man, which there was no one who did not have. Yet he is commanded to lay his hand on him, that no one, however strong in grace, should dare to refuse the sacraments of consecration.
27.20:
**“And thou shalt give him precepts in the sight of all,”** — AND THOU SHALT GIVE HIM PRECEPTS, etc. ISIDORE. Jesus succeeds Moses and teaches what ought to be offered spiritually in the Church. For the Gospel succeeds the law; the law admonishes what is to be done, and grace fulfils it: first, what ought to be offered on each day; then, what on the sabbath, for the hope of eternal rest; what on the calends, for the renewal of life; what at the Pasch, in which we are buried together with Christ by baptism, as passing from the dead to newness of life; what at Pentecost, for the grace of the Holy Ghost and the remission of sins, etc.
**“AND PART OF THY GLORY”** — As if: thou shalt make him a sharer of thy glory. For things of this kind are not lessened as though divided into parts, but are whole to all and whole to each who have fellowship in them.
**“that all the congregation of the children of Israel may hear him.”** — THAT THEY MAY HEAR, etc. ORIGEN. If the sacrifices and legal institutions had remained until the present, they would have shut out the faith of the Gospel. For there was in them a magnificent religion, full of reverence, which at first sight would astound the beholder. For who, seeing the sanctuary, the altar, the priests completing the sacrifice, and the whole order of that thing, would not think this the fullest rite by which God the creator of all should be worshipped? But thanks to the coming of Christ, who destroyed those things which seemed great on earth and transferred the worship of God from visible things to invisible, and from temporal to eternal. But Christ himself requires ears that hear these things and eyes that see them.
27.21: **“If any thing be to be done, Eleazar the priest shall consult the Lord for him. At his word he shall go out and go in, he and all the children of Israel with him, and the rest of the multitude.”** — IF ANY THING, etc. Morally we are instructed that whoever receives power among the people of God should order and rule his own life and that of his subjects according to the teaching of the divine law, which is commended above all in the office of the priest.

28.1:
**“THE LORD ALSO SAID”** — ORIGEN. And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command the children of Israel and thou shalt say to them: My gifts, my presents, my victims for a sweet odour, observe to offer to me on my festival days. And thou shalt say to them: These are my victims which you shall offer to the Lord, etc. No one offers anything of his own to the Lord, but what is the Lord's; nor does he so much offer as render. Therefore he says: My gifts, my presents, etc. As if: the things which I am about to command you to offer on my festival days are my presents, that is, they are given you by me; lest anyone believe that in offering he offers something of his own to God. For he is impious who thinks he bestows anything on God as on one in need.
**“ORIGEN”** — On my festival days. God has his festival days; for human salvation is a great festivity to him. I think that through each of the faithful, through each who is converted to God and advances in faith, a festivity arises for the Lord. The unchaste man gladdens him if he becomes chaste, and the unjust when he cultivates justice. Christ, who pours out his blood for our salvation, keeps a feast when he sees that it profits that he, the holy one, humbled himself, obedient unto death. The Holy Ghost keeps feasts when he sees temples prepared for himself in those who are converted. The angels rejoice, to whose festivity the converted come. For there is joy in heaven upon one sinner that doth penance. We give God and his angels occasion of gladness when, walking upon the earth, we have our conversation in heaven. I fear lest, on the contrary, our evil conversation bring lamentations not only to the earth but to heaven too, and perhaps to God himself. For why does he say: It repenteth me that I have made man on the earth? And Christ, seeing the city, wept over it, saying: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that killest the prophets and stonest them" etc. And I today, if I do not hear the words of the prophet and spurn his warnings, stone the prophet, and as far as in me lies kill him, whose words I do not hear, as though he were dead. That too is the voice of God lamenting: "Woe is me, for I am become as one that gleaneth stubble in the harvest, and as the clusters in the vintage" etc. But because Jerusalem sinned a great sin, all her festivities perished; because in the holy place and on the festival day they killed Christ. Therefore it is said to them: Your new moons and your sabbaths and festival days my soul hateth. Where he commands concerning gifts, where as yet there are no sins, he says: my festival days.
28.2: **“Command the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: Offer ye my oblation and my bread, and incense of most sweet odour”** — All that we offer is God's: we give him nothing, then, but render.
28.3: **“THESE ARE THE SACRIFICES”** — Let us seek diligently, then, what is the order of the festivities, that from the orders themselves and the rite of the sacrifices we may gather how each one by his deeds can prepare a festivity for God. The first festivity of God, then, is the one called unceasing. For concerning these it is commanded that they be offered unceasingly in the morning and evening sacrifices. He does not command first concerning the festivity of the Pasch, or of the unleavened bread, or of tabernacles; he set this first, in which he commands the unceasing sacrifice to be offered; that he who wishes to be perfect may know that the festivity is not to be interrupted but always and unceasingly kept; which the unceasing sacrifice signifies, that is, one offered in the evening and the morning; that he may persist with unceasing intent in the law and the prophets (which show the morning time). But he who sins and keeps days of sin cannot keep a festival day and offer the unceasing sacrifice. But he who unceasingly keeps justice and abstains from sin offers the continual sacrifice. If the prayer of the just is offered as incense in the sight of the Lord, and the lifting up of his hands is an evening sacrifice; since the Apostle says: "Defraud not one another, except perhaps by consent, that you may give yourselves to prayer"; and again: "Return together again"; it is certain that the unceasing sacrifice is hindered for those who serve marriage. He alone, then, seems to offer the unceasing sacrifice who is devoted to perpetual chastity. But there are other festival days for those who cannot unceasingly sacrifice the sacrifice of chastity.
28.4:
**“One you shall offer in the morning,”** — attending to the law and the prophets
**“and the other in the evening:”** — in the Gospel doctrine
28.6: **“It is the continual holocaust”** — that we may pray without ceasing, and our prayer ascend as incense in the sight of the Lord.
28.9:
**“And on the sabbath day”**
• in which one ceases from every work of the world
• But let us go back higher to what the observance of the true sabbath is. It is beyond this world. For as to what is written, God rested on the sabbath day from his works, we do not see either that this was done then on the seventh day or that it is done even now. For we always see God working, nor is there a sabbath on which he does not work, bringing forth grass on the mountains and herb for the service of men, striking and healing, bringing down to hell and bringing back. Whence, when the Jews laid down rules to him about working and healing on the sabbath, he answered: "My Father worketh until now; and I work"; showing that God rests on no sabbath of this world from the governing of the world. That, then, will be the true sabbath on which God shall rest from all his works, when sorrow and sadness and groaning shall flee away, and God shall be all in all. On which we shall celebrate the festival day and the true sabbath with the angels, offering the sacrifice of praise through the great high priest, who is a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech.
**“AND ON THE SABBATH DAY”** — The second festivity, then, is of the sacrifice of the sabbath; and every just man ought to keep this festivity, of which the Apostle says: "There remaineth therefore a sabbatism", that is, an observance of the sabbath, for the people of God. Leaving aside, then, the Jewish sabbath, let us see what the Christian's observance of the sabbath ought to be. On the sabbath day one must do nothing of worldly acts. If, then, you do nothing worldly, but give yourself to spiritual things, come to church, lend your ear to the word of God, think on heavenly things, take care for the future hope, keep the coming judgment before your eyes, look not to things present and visible but to things invisible and to come: this is the Christian observance of the sabbath. These things the Jews ought to observe. Among them too the smith and the builder and workmen of this kind are idle on the sabbath day; but the reader of the divine law or the teacher does not cease from his work, and yet the sabbath is not defiled. Whence: "The priests in the temple break the sabbath, and are without blame." He, then, who ceases from the works of the world and gives himself to spiritual things keeps the sacrifice of the sabbath and the festival day. Nor does he carry burdens on the way; for every sin is a burden, according to that: As a heavy burden they are become heavy upon me. Nor does he kindle fire, of which it is said: "Walk in the light of your fire" etc. Each one sits in his place and does not go out of it. The place of the spiritual soul is justice, truth, wisdom, sanctification, and all that Christ is: this is the place of the soul. From this place it must not go out, that it may keep the true sabbaths and carry out the festival day with the sacrifices of the sabbaths; according to that: "He that abideth in me, and I in him."
**“you shall offer two lambs of a year old”** — He offers two lambs of a year old who shows God simplicity of mind and innocence of work.
**“without blemish, and two tenths of flour tempered with oil in sacrifice, and the libations”** — AND TWO TENTHS, etc. He offers these who, filled with spiritual grace, the Holy Ghost teaching him the knowledge of the two testaments, teaches his hearers by words and examples, not for temporal gain but for the reward of eternal life.
28.11:
**“And on the calends, that is, on the first days of the months, you shall offer a holocaust to the Lord, two calves of the herd, one ram”**
• of one year, namely
• THE SAME. The third festivity is the day of the new moon, on which a victim too is offered. Neomenia is called the new moon; and it is called new when next to the sun, so that it lies hidden under its brightness. But this festivity is a shadow of things to come, as the others are. The sun of justice is Christ; if the moon, that is, the Church, which is filled with his light, is joined to him so that it becomes one spirit with him, then it keeps the festivity of the new moon. For then it is made new, when it casts off the old man and puts on the new, which is created according to God. Then it can neither be seen nor comprehended by human eyes. For when it has wholly joined itself to the Lord and wholly yielded itself to his splendour, it thinks or seeks nothing at all earthly, nor studies to please men, but gives itself wholly to wisdom, wholly to the light, wholly to the warmth of the Holy Ghost, made subtle and spiritual. Therefore most worthily it keeps the festival day and slays to the Lord the victim of the new moon, as one renewed in spirit.
**“ON THE CALENDS”** — That is, at the new moons, when the Church or any soul so draws near to the sun of justice that it becomes one spirit with him, and, renewed by him, casts off the old man.
**“CALVES OF THE HERD”** — In the two calves can be marked the gladness of good work in the soul or in the body; which is offered to the Lord according to the two testaments, or to God in the two precepts of charity.
**“ONE RAM”** — In the ram, the rule of discipline, strong and immovable according to the unity of the catholic faith.
**“SEVEN LAMBS OF A YEAR OLD”** — Simplicity and meekness of manners, for the heavenly rest, through the grace of the sevenfold spirit.
28.12:
**“AND THREE TENTHS”** — He offers this who, enlightened with the oil of gladness, shows spiritual knowledge in the faith of the holy Trinity, with good work.
**“AND TWO TENTHS”** — He does this who studies to turn the Decalogue of the law, in the two precepts of charity, to his own and his neighbours' profit, and so to dedicate his whole life to the Lord for a sweet odour.
28.13: **“AND THE TENTH OF A TENTH”** — This is done when simplicity of manners is instructed and adorned according to the rule of the scriptures, the grace of the Holy Ghost working with it. And well are all these commanded to be offered to the Lord in holocaust; because we ought to do these things not that we may seek human praise or present recompense, but that we may please God, the giver of all good things, in all things, and merit the recompense of eternal life.
28.16:
**“And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, shall be the phase of the Lord,”**
• The Pasch, when the true Lamb is slain who taketh away the sins of the world.
• AND IN THE FIRST MONTH, etc. ORIGEN. In the fourth place among the festivities of God is set the solemnity of the Pasch, in which the lamb is slain; the lamb, namely, the true Lamb who taketh away the sins of the world; because Christ our Pasch is sacrificed. The Jews with carnal sense eat the flesh of the lamb; but we, the flesh of the word of God. For he says: Unless you eat... the flesh is that of the word of God. If we set forth herbs as for the weak, or the nourishment of milk as for children, [it is not flesh]; but if we speak perfect things, robust, strong things, we set out the flesh of the word to be eaten. For where a mystical speech, full and solid with faith in the Trinity, is brought forth; where, the veil of the letter of the law being removed, the spiritual sacraments of the world to come are laid open; where the hope of the soul, torn away from the earth, is set in those things which eye hath not seen nor ear heard: all these are the flesh of the word of God. He who can feed on the perfect, and with purified heart, truly sacrifices the sacrifice of the festivity of the Pasch and keeps the festival day with God and his angels.
28.17:
**“And on the fifteenth day the solemnity of the unleavened bread:”**
• of sincerity and truth
• THE SAME. All who are to be trained in higher disciplines find the labour of the rudiments irksome, since they do not know the usefulness of the discipline. Irksome, then, seem to us the rudiments of the Jews, who were trained in the first elements, when they are first heard. For each one wishes to learn of the things that pertain to salvation; but when the sacrifices of rams, goats and calves are recited, he thinks there is nothing useful in them. But if he can remove the veil of the old testament, he will see how magnificent are the things that are reckoned superfluous and superstitious. In the festivity of the Pasch it is a lamb that purifies the people; in others a goat, in others a calf or a ram or a she-goat or a heifer. One, then, of those which are taken to purify the people is the lamb, that is, Christ himself, who taketh away the sins of the world. But if the lamb which was given to purify the people signifies Christ, consequently the other animals too appointed for purification are referred to other persons who confer some purification on the human race. For as Christ, offered in sacrifice, granted remission of sins in the whole world, so perhaps the blood of the other saints which was shed, of one as of a heifer, of another as of a goat or she-goat or one of these, was shed to expiate the people in some part. Whether these are to be referred to the persons of the just and the prophets who were slaughtered in this world, or of those who say: "For thy sake we are put to death all the day long; we are accounted as sheep" etc., or to the higher powers to whom the care of the human race has been given, who would easily dare to affirm? For these animals are referred to this or that person not by appearance but by figure. As Christ himself is not called a lamb because he was changed into the appearance of a lamb, but because his will and goodness, by which he made God propitious to men and blotted out sins, was as the victim of a lamb, spotless and innocent, by which the divine is believed to be appeased toward men; so perhaps, if any of the angels or of just men intercedes more earnestly for the sins of men, for the divine propitiation he can be received as a ram or goat or calf offered in sacrifice to purify the people. Does not Paul seem to have offered himself as a ram or goat in holocaust for the people of Israel when he said: "I wished myself to be an anathema from Christ for my brethren" etc.? And elsewhere: "For I am even now ready to be sacrificed" etc. Figuratively, too, it can be seen that one is offered for the festivity of the sabbath, another for the festivity of new fruits, another for the festivity of tabernacles, as a goat or calf or ram, to reconcile God to men. For while there are sins, it is necessary that a victim for sins be sought. For if there had been no sin, it was not necessary for the Son of God to become a lamb and, set in the flesh, be slaughtered. But since sin entered into this world, whose necessity requires propitiation, which yet is made through a victim, it was necessary that victims be provided for sin. And because there were divers qualities of sin, victims of divers animals are provided. So, then, one of the angels or saints becomes a calf, who intercedes for the offences of the people at that festivity, another a ram at another festivity. But if men can be purified from sins, the victims are lessened. For as for the multitude of sins the victims are multiplied, so for their fewness they are lessened. Whence in the festivity of tabernacles, when victims are commanded to be offered for eight days, on the first day, as though in the abundance of sins as yet, fourteen calves are commanded to be offered; on the second, as though sins had been lessened, the victims are lessened and thirteen calves are offered; on the third twelve, after these eleven; as though, the multitude of sins failing day by day through the purifications, the number of victims is lessened. So too understand the reason of purification for the ordering of the whole world. For not only the things on earth need purification, but also the things in heaven. For perdition hangs over the heavens, because they shall perish, and all shall grow old as a garment, and shall be changed. Behold, then, the purification of the whole world, that is, of things in heaven, on earth and under the earth. See of how many victims all these have need, how many calves they require, how many rams, how many goats. But in all these there is one Lamb who could take away the sin of the whole world. Therefore the others ceased, because this one victim sufficed for the salvation of the whole world. For the others remitted sins by prayers, this one alone by power. For he said: Son, thy sins are forgiven thee. So, then, the world is trained, first to seek remission of sins through divers victims, until it comes to the perfect victim, the perfect lamb of a year old, who taketh away the sins of the world; through whom it may keep spiritual festivities, not to the satiety of the flesh but to the perfection of the spirit, with spiritual sacrifices offered in the purification of the mind.
**“ON THE FIFTEENTH DAY”** — THE SAME. There follows on this the continual festivity of the unleavened bread, which you will rightly celebrate if you drive out every leaven of malice and wickedness from your soul and keep the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. For it is not to be thought that God writes laws for men about leaven, and commands a soul to be cut off from his people if it has had a little leaven in its house, and is so offended for the sake of this leaven that he commands the soul which he made to his own image to be cut off and overthrown. But this God abhors: if the soul is leavened with the malice of anger or the wickedness of the spirit and swells to crimes. If we do not cast these out of the house of our soul, we shall rightly be cut off. But do not despise it even if you see a little malice leavening within you; because a little leaven corrupts the whole lump, and one sin begets another. For as one who has received the leaven of chastity is made daily more chaste, so one who has received the leaven of wickedness is made daily more wicked and worse.
**“seven days”** — all the time of the present life
28.18: **“And the first day of them shall be venerable and holy: any servile work”** — sin, namely: "Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin."
28.26:
**“The day also of firstfruits, when you offer new fruits”** — the fruits, namely, of the spirit: joy, peace, patience and the like.
**“THE DAY ALSO OF FIRSTFRUITS”** — ORIGEN. The sixth festivity is called that of new fruits, because firstfruits of the new fruits are offered. For where the field has been sown and diligently tilled, and the crop has come to ripeness, a festivity of the gift is kept at the perfection of the fruits. If you wish, then, to keep the festival day of new fruits with God, see how you sow or where, that you may reap such fruits as will make God glad and keep a festival day. Which you will not be able to fulfil unless you sow in the spirit, that of the spirit you may reap life everlasting and truly keep the feast of new fruits. Whence: "Break up your fallow ground", and "sow not upon thorns", but upon good ground, which will yield him fruit thirtyfold or sixtyfold or a hundredfold. He, then, is the one who sows in the spirit and gathers the fruit of the spirit. And the fruit of the spirit, first of all, is joy; and rightly does he keep the festival day of new fruits who reaps joy; above all if he reaps together peace, patience, goodness, mildness and the like.

29.1: **“OF THE SEVENTH MONTH ALSO”** — ORIGEN. There follows the festivity of the sevenths. For as among days every seventh is observed as a sabbath and is a festivity, so among months every seventh month is the sabbath of months. A festivity is kept, then, which is called the sabbath of sabbaths, and on the first day of the month there is a memorial of trumpets. But who is it that keeps the festivity of the memorial of trumpets, but he who commits to the treasury of memory the prophetic and apostolic scriptures (which sound like a heavenly trumpet), and meditates on the law of God day and night, and who can merit the graces of the Holy Ghost by which the prophets were inspired, and say in psalmody: Blow the trumpet at the beginning of the month? There is also another festivity, when those celebrating the feast afflict their souls and humble them. O wondrous festivity! the affliction of the soul is called a festival day. For this, it says, is the day of propitiation, the tenth day of the seventh month. See, then: if you wish to keep a festival day, if you wish God to rejoice over you, afflict your soul and humble it, lest it fulfil its desires, lest it wanton. Indeed the festivity of the Pasch and of the unleavened bread are said to have the bread of affliction; nor can anyone keep the festival day unless he has eaten the bread of affliction. And the Pasch is eaten with bitterness. You see, then, what the festivities of God are like: they do not admit bodily sweetness; they want nothing slack, nothing voluptuous; but they demand affliction of soul and bitterness and humility; because he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
