**“But departing also from the desert of Sinai, they came to the graves of lust.”** — where all concupiscences are buried and put to death
**“TO THE GRAVES OF LUST”** — JEROME. The thirteenth mansion, the graves of lust. And the sense is that of the Gospel, that the Lord Jesus, baptized, was at once led by the spirit into the desert and tempted by the devil. So Israel, after familiar speech with God, after it had stayed beside mount Sinai one year and some days, with a wonderful ordering of the camp went out into the wilderness of Pharan, which is interpreted "wild ass" or "wildness"; and there it succumbs to the evil beast, loathing the heavenly bread.
**“ORIGEN”** — After this one comes into Haseroth, which is interpreted "perfect courts" or "beatitude". Look more diligently, traveller, what is the order of the advances. After you have buried and put to death the concupiscences of the flesh, you will come to the breadth of the courts, you will come to beatitude. For blessed is the soul which is now pressed by no vices of the flesh.
33.17: **“And departing from the graves of lust, they camped in Haseroth.”** — Courts
33.18:
**“And from Haseroth they came to Rethma.”** — 'Sound' or 'juniper': that, fervent in spirit, we may preach the Gospel of the Lord with a clear sound: for the juniper is said to keep fire a long time.
**“IN RETHMA”** — JEROME. They camped in Rethma. This is the fifteenth mansion; and it is to be noted that the remaining eighteen mansions, of which a catalogue is briefly described, from Rethma as far as Asiongaber, that is, the thirty-second mansion, are contained under the name of the wilderness of Pharan. In these twelve spies are sent to the holy land, and the cluster is brought back on a pole; the people, fearing the giants, murmurs, and fights against Amalec and is conquered. The vengeance of God is brought forth on Dathan and Abiron and the sons of Core; the rod of Aaron buds; the red heifer is burned in holocaust. After the graves of lust and the forecourts, one must pass to the juniper, which keeps heat long, that we may be fervent in spirit and preach the Gospel with a clear sound.
**“ORIGEN”** — Thence one comes into Rethma or Pharan. Rethma is interpreted "consummated vision"; but Pharan, "visible mouth". What, when the soul so grows that, when it has ceased to be pressed by the troubles of the flesh, it has consummated visions, and will grasp the true and perfect understanding, namely the causes of the incarnation of the Word of God, knowing more deeply the reasons of his dispensations?
33.19:
**“And departing from Rethma,”** — whence the people, setting out from Haseroth, camped in the wilderness of Pharan
**“IN REMMOMPHARES”** — JEROME. Division of the pomegranate; in which the Church is signified, as many grains covered by one rind, while it encloses the whole throng of believers in the unity of the faith; or the variety and concord of the virtues. Whence: "The multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul"; and so the several steps are divided, that all are held by the same framework.
**“ORIGEN”** — Thence one comes into Remmompha, where, namely, the discerning of divine and heavenly things from earthly and weak ones is made. For as the understanding of the soul grows, knowledge of lofty things is given it and judgment granted, by which it may know how to separate eternal things from temporal, and fleeting from perpetual.
**“they camped in Remmomphares.”** — After this one comes into Lebna, which is interpreted "whitening". I know that in other places whitening is put in a blameworthy sense, as when it is said: whited wall, and whited sepulchres. But here it is the whitening of which it is said: "Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow." And: "If your sins be as scarlet, I will make them white as snow." And elsewhere: "They shall be whited with snow in Selmon." And the hairs of the Ancient of days are said to be white, that is, white as wool. This whitening, then, is understood to come from the splendour of the true light and descend from the brightness of heavenly visions.
33.20:
**“And they departed from thence and came to Lebna.”**
• or: Lebna
• In Lebna: brick, namely. For in this passage we now grow, now decrease; and after many advances we often return to the brick, that is, to carnal works.
33.21:
**“IN RESSA”** — Bridles, namely. For if we come down to muddy works, we are to be bridled, and, wandering and headlong in our course, directed by the reins of the scriptures.
**“ORIGEN”** — After this a mansion is made in Ressa, which is "visible" or "praiseworthy temptation". For although the soul has great advances, yet temptations are not taken away from it, because they are as a guard and defence to it. For as flesh, if it is not sprinkled with salt, is corrupted, so the soul, if it is not salted with temptation, is at once dissolved. Whence it is said that every sacrifice shall be salted with salt. Here Paul says: "Lest the greatness of the revelations should exalt me, there was given me a sting of my flesh." This, then, is the visible and praiseworthy temptation.
33.22: **“And departing from Ressa, they came to Ceelatha.”** — which is interpreted 'Church', that wandering courses may be brought back to the Church.
33.23:
**“IN THE MOUNTAIN SEPHER”** — JEROME. Of beauty: and the mountain of beauty is Christ. The twentieth mansion is set in the mountain of beauty, of which it is said: "Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? or who shall rest in thy holy mountain?" See what bridles profit. They draw us back from vices, they bring us into the couches of the virtues, they make us dwell in Christ, the most beautiful mountain.
**“And they removed from thence and camped in the mountain Sepher.”** — Thence one comes into the mountain Sepher, which is called "trumpeting". The trumpet is the signal of war. For when the soul feels itself armed with virtues so great and such, it necessarily goes forth to the war which is against the principalities and powers and the rulers of this world; or the trumpet sounds in the word of God, namely of doctrine and preaching, that he who has heard the trumpet may prepare himself for war.
33.24:
**“TO ARADA”** — JEROME. Wonder. And note the order: after the bridles one is brought into the Church, thence we ascend to the mountain of Christ, set on which we wonder at the things which eye hath not seen nor ear heard.
**“Departing from the mountain Sepher, they came to Arada.”** — From the mountain Sepher they came into Caradad, which is interpreted "made fit"; that, namely, he may say: He hath made us fit ministers of the new testament.
33.25:
**“MACELOTH”** — Assembly. This is the Church, of which it is said: "Behold how good and how pleasant it is to dwell"; or the concord of all the virtues.
**“From thence they went and camped in Maceloth.”**
• Thence one comes to Maceloth, which is interpreted "from the beginning". For he who tends to perfection contemplates the beginning of things; nay, refers all things to him who was in the beginning with the Father, namely God; nor does he ever withdraw from this beginning.
• And thence one comes into Maceloth, which is "headship" or "rods"; by both power is indicated, and that he has advanced so far as to rule over the body, as one holding the rod of power; nay, over the whole world, when he says: "The world is crucified to me" etc.
33.26:
**“THAHATH”** — Fear is the guard of beatitude, that he who has ascended so far may not be proud. As if: you have come to the Church, you have ascended to the most beautiful mountain, with amazement and wonder you confess the greatness of Christ; you see there many companions of virtue: be not highminded, but be wise unto sobriety. Fear is the guard of the virtues; security is slippery. Whence: "Thy rod and thy staff, they have comforted me." That is: while I dread torments, I keep the grace received.
**“ORIGEN”** — After this a mansion is made in Thahath, which is "confirmation" or "patience". For he who wishes to profit others must suffer much and bear all things patiently. Whence: "For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name's sake."
33.27:
**“THEY CAMPED IN THARE”** — JEROME. That is, "malice", or "pasture" according to some. Nor would they err if it were written with the letter ain; but because there is a double aspiration in the last syllable, the cause of the error is manifest. With the same name and the same letters I find the father of Abraham written; who, in the apocryphal volume of the Little Genesis, having driven away the crows which were laying waste men's grain, obtained the name of "driver away" or "repeller". Let us imitate Thare, then, and keep off the birds which devour the wheat beside the way. For Abraham the patriarch, in a type of Israel, divided the sacrifices by their members and drove away the birds; and the crows of the valleys dig out the scornful eye; and the true Moses takes the Ethiopian woman, and Elias is fed by crows.
**“From Thahath they camped in Thare.”** — Thence one comes to Thare, which is "contemplation of amazement", that is, ecstasy, when the mind is amazed at some great thing.
**“JEROME”** — Malice or pasture: which is referred to the prelates of the Church, or to the guarding of the soul, that he who feeds may be careful lest the devil [break] into the folds of the flocks, that is, the churches.
33.28:
**“METHCA”** — JEROME. Sweetness. Because you have ascended into the high mountain of the Father and wondered at the choirs of the virtues, have feared a fall, have driven off the ambushers, therefore the sweet fruit of labour follows you, that you may say: "How sweet are thy words to my palate!" Samson, who had driven the birds away from his fruits and had tied together the foxes which destroy the vineyards, and had killed the roaring lion too, found a honeycomb in the mouth of the dead.
**“And they departed from thence, and pitched their tents in Methca.”** — After this they came to Methca, which is interpreted "new death". And it is a new death when we die together with Christ and are buried together with him, that we may live together with him.
33.29:
**“HESMONA”** — Which is interpreted "haste"; because after the sweet fruits of labour we ought not to be idle, but, forgetting the things past, stretch ourselves forth to those to come.
**“ORIGEN”** — Thence one comes to Sema, which is said to signify "mouth" or "bones"; in which the virtue and strength of patience is declared.
33.30:
**“MOSEROTH”** — Bonds or discipline: that we may wear the thresholds of the masters, and think the precepts of the virtues and the mysteries of the scriptures to be eternal bonds against the power and bonds of the devil; bursting which Samson conquered the enemies; of which it is said: "Thou hast broken my bonds." He who is bound with the bond of Christ will say: "His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me."
**“ORIGEN”** — Thence to Moseroth, which is "shutting out": that he may now shut out the suggestions of the contrary spirit from his thoughts. Whence: If the spirit of him that hath power ascend upon thee, leave not thy place. The place, then, is to be held and the adversary shut out, lest he find place in our heart. Whence: "Give not place to the devil."
33.31:
**“And from Moseroth they camped in Benejaacan.”** — elsewhere: Baneiachan
**“BENEJAACAN”** — JEROME. Sons of necessity or of gnashing: the twenty-eighth mansion. Note the number: for if you begin from one and, adding little by little, come as far as the seventh, it makes twenty-eight.
**“JEROME”** — Benejaacan is interpreted "sons of necessity" or "of gnashing". Of these sons it is said: "Bring to the Lord the young of rams." But when you have been instructed in the divine scriptures, and know their laws and testimonies to be the bonds of charity, and, contending with adversaries, you bind them and lead them bound into captivity, you will make of enemies and captives free men of God. And the sons of gnashing, through fear of the judgment or of the punishment where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, putting off the bonds of the devil, will bow their necks to Christ.
**“ORIGEN”** — After this one comes to Benejaacan, which signifies "fountains" or "strainings"; where, namely, he draws the fountains of the divine words until he strains them by drinking, so that he passes over not even the least commandment, nay, not one iota or one tittle of the word of God is held idle in his understanding.
33.32:
**“And departing from Benejaacan, they came to mount Galad.”**
• or: Galgath
• 'expedition' or 'girding' or 'messenger' or 'cutting': whatever of these the master does stands firm on the mountain.
• After this one comes into Galad, which is interpreted "trial" or "crowding". Trial is a certain strength in God and a defence of the soul. For it is so softened in with the virtues that without it they seem to be neither comely nor full; and therefore for those advancing to virtue divers and frequent mansions are made in temptations; which when you have passed, you will put in at Jetebatha. Jetebatha is interpreted "good". To the good, then, one comes only after the experiences of temptations.
**“MOUNT GALAD”** — JEROME. Galad or Galgath is interpreted "messenger" or "action" or "cutting". For we cannot make sons of necessity unless we have slain their teachers, nor let our hand spare to drag the shoulder or the tip of the ear out of the lion's mouth, and have announced the rewards to come and taught them to be girded for resisting. Whence: "Cursed be he that doth the work of the Lord negligently, and that withholdeth his sword from blood"; and David: In the morning I put to death all the wicked of the land.
33.33:
**“From thence they went and camped in Jetebatha.”** — The thirtieth mansion
**“JETEBATHA”** — JEROME. Goodness, which is Christ; that when we have come to the perfect man, the priestly grade, and the age of the fulness of Christ, at which Ezechiel was beside the river Chobar, we may be able to sing with the thirtieth psalm: "In thee, O Lord, have I hoped; let me never be confounded"; "for the good shepherd giveth his life for his sheep."
33.34:
**“HEBRONA”** — JEROME. Passage, that is, the world. For the fashion of this world passeth away, which the saints, coming, desire to pass beyond to better things. To this mansion comes the true Hebrew, that is, the passer-over, who can say: I will go over and see this great sight. Whence: "And they that passed by have not said: The blessing of the Lord be upon you."
**“ORIGEN”** — Thence they put in at Hebrona, which is "passage". For all things are to be passed through; for even if you come to good things, you must pass to better, until you come to that good in which you ought always to remain.
33.35:
**“IN ASIONGABER”** — JEROME. Asiongaber, "woods of the man"; which, namely, the kinds of forests and of all trees can figure the multitude of the Gentiles. Thus far the wilderness of Pharan contains eighteen mansions, which, described in the catalogue, are not set down in the earlier journey.
**“ORIGEN”** — After this one comes to Asiongaber, which is interpreted "counsels of the man". If anyone has ceased to be a child in his senses, he comes to the counsels of a man, as he who said: "But when I became a man, I put away the things of a child." Great, then, are the counsels of a man. Whence: "Counsel in the heart of a man is like deep water."
33.36:
**“They removed from thence and came into the desert of Sin, which is Cades.”** — JEROME: 'Holy' by antiphrasis.
**“INTO THE DESERT OF SIN”** — JEROME. It is asked why the eighth mansion, namely, is called the twenty-third [as well]. But it is to be known that the former is written with the letter samech, and is interpreted "bush" or "hatred"; but this with sade, and is interpreted "commandment". Cades is not called "holy" (as most think) but "changed" and "transferred". Whence in Genesis Hiras asks, according to the Hebrew truth: "Where is Cadesa?", that is, the harlot, whose dress was changed from other women. But if it is interpreted "holy", it is by antiphrasis, as the Parcae are called so who spare least, and war (bellum) because it is not good (bonum), and a grove (lucus) because it does not shine (lucet). For in this mansion Mary dies and is buried; and because of the waters of contradiction Moses and Aaron offend the Lord and are forbidden to cross over the Jordan. And messengers being sent to Edom, passage is asked and refused. Who would fear, after such great advances, the murmur of the people and the offence of the masters and the refusal of passage on the way? And note that after the death of prophecy and the waters of contradiction they cannot pass through the Idumean, fleshly and earthly. But Edom goes out against them with much people and a strong hand. The interpretation of the name too suits the death and the offence and the refused passage. For where there is commandment, there is sin; where sin, there offence; where offence, there death. Of this mansion it is said: The Lord shall shake the desert of Cades.
**“ORIGEN”**
• Hence again Sin, that is, temptation; because there is no other way fit to make this journey. For a goldsmith wishing to make a needful vessel often puts it to the fire, sets it under hammers, scrapes it with files, that it may become purer and come to the form which the craftsman foresees.
• After this they came to Pharan Cades, which is "holy fruitfulness". You see where one comes; you see that after the furrows of temptation holy fruitfulness follows.
33.38:
**“HOR”** — JEROME. Some interpret it "teat"; nor would they err if it were written with the letter aleph; others "skin", who would say true if there were ain there; some "hole", which could be accepted if it had the element heth. But since it is read with he, rather mountain is understood. And it can be read: Aaron the priest went up into the mountain of the mountain, that is, to its summit. And note that the high priest dies not simply on a mountain but on a mountain [of a mountain], that the place may be worthy: one dies on a mountain, another on the mountain of a mountain.
**“And Aaron the priest went up into mount Hor at the commandment of the Lord: and there he died in the fortieth year of the coming forth of the children of Israel out of Egypt, the fifth month, the first day of the month,”**
• Thence one puts in at mount Hor, which is interpreted "mountainous". For he comes to the mountain of God, that he may become a fruitful mountain, a curdled mountain; or he is called mountainous from always dwelling in the mountain of God.
• AARON INTO THE MOUNTAIN, etc. ISIDORE. Aaron died in that year in which the new people was about to enter the land of promise. And although he left the priesthood to Eleazar on the mountain, and the law leads to the summit those who have fulfilled it, yet that very height is not beyond the stream of the Jordan, but in the furthest borders of earthly works. And all the people mourned him thirty days. Aaron is mourned; Jesus is not mourned. In the law, a descent to hell; in the Gospel, an ascent to paradise.
33.40: **“AND HE HEARD”** — ISIDORE. The Chanaanite also heard that Israel had come into the place of the spies, where he knew the people had once given offence; he joined battle and led Israel captive. Again in the same place he is fought down; by a vow the victor is conquered, the conquered overcome. By which we understand that when enemies have taken us captive, destitute of the help of God, we should not despair of salvation, but fight again. It can happen that we conquer where we have been conquered. And the name of that place is called Horma, that is, anathema.
33.41:
**“IN SALMONA”** — JEROME. They camped in Salmona, then in Phunon. These two mansions, the thirty-fifth and thirty-sixth, are not found in the order of the history; but it is written of them briefly: Setting out from mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea, to go round the land of Edom. By which it is shown that they were set in the borders and round about the land of Edom; nor is it read of the mountain. Setting out from mount Hor they camped in Salmona or in Phunon. But after the going round of the land of the Idumeans he comes to the end and says: The children of Israel setting out camped in Oboth. Nor did he say "they set out from that place into this", because he had passed over two mansions, which, though he kept silent about them in the reckoning, he renders in the sum. In these, Aaron being dead, the people murmurs against the Lord and Moses, loathes the manna, is wounded by serpents.
**“ORIGEN”** — After this follows the mansion Salmona, which is interpreted "shadow of the portion". This I think is the shadow of which it is said: "The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord", to whom we said: "Under thy shadow we shall live among the Gentiles." That shadow too is like this, of which it is said: "And the power of the Most High shall overshadow thee." The shadow, then, of our portion, which gives us shade from every heat of temptations, is Christ and the Holy Ghost.
**“JEROME”** — Salmona. A little image; because there the image of the Saviour was expressed through the brazen serpent which hung on the wood.
33.42:
**“PHUNON”** — Mouth: because when we know the passion of the Son of God, what we believe with the heart we pronounce with the mouth, according to that: "With the heart we believe unto justice."
**“ORIGEN”** — Hence one comes to Phunon, which we think is "sparing of the mouth". For he who has been able to behold the mystery of Christ and the Holy Ghost, and has seen or heard things which it is not granted to man to utter, will necessarily have sparing of the mouth, knowing to whom, when, or how one ought to speak of the divine mysteries.
33.43:
**“OBOTH”** — Magicians or pythons: because after the image of God, which is shown in the heart by reason, and the confession of faith, which is uttered by the mouth, serpents rise up and evil arts provoke us to wars. But keeping our heart with all watchfulness, let us stop our ears, lest we hear the voices of the charmers and the songs of the sirens.
**“ORIGEN”** — After this one comes into Oboth; of which name, although we have not found the interpretation, we do not doubt that, as in the others, so in this the sequence of the advances is kept.
33.44:
**“And from Oboth they came to Ijeabarim, which is in the borders of the Moabites.”** — heaps of stones of those passing over, that is, the saints passing through this world to other mansions.
**“IN THE BORDERS OF THE MOABITES”** — It signifies according to the letter that thus far they were in the borders of the Idumeans, and now they come to the bounds of Moab.
**“ORIGEN”** — After this follows the mansion Gai, that is, "chaos". For by these effects they draw near to the bosom of Abraham, who says: "Between us and you there is fixed a great chaos"; that he may rest with Lazarus.
33.45:
**“And departing from Ijeabarim they pitched their tents in Dibongad.”** — understood strongly: 'temptation'
**“IN DIBONGAD”** — JEROME. Dibongad, the thirty-ninth mansion. Instead of this one reads in the order of the history that after they camped in Ijeabarim in the borders of Moab towards the rising of the sun, they set out thence and came to the torrent Zared, and setting out thence they camped beyond the Arnon, which is in the wilderness of the borders of the Amorrhite; because the Arnon is at the bounds of the Moabites and the Amorrhites. After Dibongad war is waged against Sehon king of the Amorrhites and Og king of Basan. Whence we say that when we have come to the summit we should not be proud, but on the contrary should know that a wilderness is set before us.
**“ORIGEN”** — Thence one comes again to Dibongad, which is interpreted "beehive of temptations". O the wondrous care of divine providence! Now the heavenly traveller is made near to the highest perfection by the succession of virtues; yet trials are not lacking to him, but I hear of trials of a new kind. The bee is a praiseworthy creature in the scriptures, whose labours both kings and common folk use for health; which is rightly taken of the words of the prophets and apostles and of all who wrote the sacred volumes. And I think that this is the beehive, namely the whole number of the divine scriptures. There is, then, for those who tend to perfection, a temptation even in this beehive. I see a temptation in this beehive when it is said: "Lest looking up to the sun and the moon, thou adore them, which the Lord thy God hath set apart for the Gentiles"; and elsewhere: "Thou shalt not speak ill of the gods." And in the New Testament: "Why seek you to kill me, a man who have spoken the truth to you?" and elsewhere: "Therefore do I speak to them in parables, because seeing they see not, and hearing they understand not" etc. The Apostle too says: In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of unbelievers; and many trials of this kind you will find in the divine beehive, into which each of the saints must come, that through these too it may be known how perfectly and godly he thinks of God.
33.46:
**“HELMONDEBLATHAIM”** — Which is interpreted "contempt of palates" or "reproach": that we may understand that all sweet things and the allurements of pleasures in this world are to be despised, and reproaches loved; which, if they are cast at us falsely, bring forth beatitude. Honey is not offered in the sacrifices of God, and wax, which holds sweet things, does not give light in the tabernacle, but the purest oil, which is brought forth from the bitterness of the olive. For honey drops from the lips of a harlot; of which I think Jonathan tasted mystically, and was hardly freed by the prayers of the people.
**“ORIGEN”** — After this one comes into Helmondeblathaim, which is interpreted "contempt of figs", that is, where earthly things are utterly despised. For unless the things which seem to delight on earth have been despised, we cannot pass to heavenly things.
33.47:
**“And departing from Helmondeblathaim, they came to the mountains of Abarim over against Nabo.”**
• THEY CAME TO THE MOUNTAINS OF ABARIM, etc. The forty-first mansion is turned as "the mountains of those passing over", and is over against the face of mount Nabo.
• There follows the mansion Abarim, which is "passage", over against Nabo, which is "departure". For when the soul has passed through all these virtues and ascended the summit of perfection, it now passes from the world and departs, like Henoch, who was not found because God translated him. And if he seems still to be in the world and to dwell in the flesh, yet he will not be found in any worldly act, because God has translated him into the region of the virtues.
**“JEROME”** — Here Moses dies, the land of promise having been seen beforehand. Nabo is interpreted "conclusion", in which the law is ended and its memory is not found, but the grace of the Gospel endures without end. And it is to be noted that the mansion of those passing over is set in the mountains, and still needs advance. For after the mountains we descend to the plains of Moab and the streams of the Jordan, which is interpreted "descent". For nothing is so perilous as the desire of glory and boasting and a mind swollen with the consciousness of its virtues.
33.48:
**“TO THE PLAINS OF MOAB”** — JEROME. In the forty-second mansion, which is the last, the people, staying there, is blessed by Balaam, and the curse is changed into praises; it commits fornication with the daughters of Madian, and Phinees transfixes the fornicators with a dagger; the people is numbered again, and the Levites are numbered, that, the worst having been slain, a new people of God may be enrolled. The daughters of Salphaad receive an inheritance among their brethren by the judgment of the Lord, nor is the female sex shut out from the possession of the Lord. Jesus succeeds Moses on the mountain and learns from the law what ought to be offered spiritually in the Church: what on each day, what on the sabbath, what on the calends, what at the Pasch, what at Pentecost, what at the new moon of the seventh month, what at the fast of the same month on the tenth day, what at the feast of tabernacles, when tabernacles are pitched, on the fifteenth of the same month. The vows of wives and daughters without the authority of fathers and husbands are recorded as void. The war against the Madianites, the death of Balaam, the division of the booty, the oblation from it in the tabernacle of God. Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses receive a possession about the Jordan in the wilderness; for they had very many beasts, nor could they yet dwell in the temple. The people is taught to destroy the idols in the holy land, and that none of the former inhabitants be kept. The province long desired is described, and the inheritance of the two and a half tribes is separated; the princes of the tribes who are to enter the holy land are numbered; the Levites receive forty-two cities with their suburbs for a thousand paces round about, as many, namely, as there are mansions. Six cities of fugitives are added, three within the Jordan and three beyond, that there may be forty-eight; who of the fugitives ought to be received, who killed, and who kept until the death of the high priest. Deuteronomy follows, the second law, a preparation for the Gospel. There we learn briefly what things Moses spoke to the people between Pharan and Thophel and Laban and Haseroth and the places of gold, the most unhappy Juda being cast away, eleven days on the way from Horeb, by the way of mount Seir as far as Cadesbarne. And at the last he sings a song in which the synagogue is cast off and the Church joined to the Lord: He grew fat and thick and gross, and kicked, and forgot God his saviour, etc. The children of Israel are blessed, and again in Simeon the pitiable Judas is shut out. Moses goes up to mount Nabo, to the top of Phasga, which is over against Jericho; and the Lord showed him all the land of Galaad as far as Dan, and Nephthali, Ephraim, Manasses, and all the land of Juda as far as the great sea towards the south, and the plain country of Jericho, the city of palms, as far as Phogor. Who can explain such great mysteries? who, set in the furthest borders of the law of this life, does not understand that one must always fight there, and that full victory is given then, if he has been in the plains of Belsatim, which is interpreted "mourning of thorns", and has wept for his old sins, and the thorns which choked the seed of the word of God; of which it is said: "I am turned in my anguish, whilst the thorn is fastened."
**“ORIGEN”** — The last mansion is to the west of Moab beside the Jordan. For this course is run to this end: that one may come to the river of God, namely of wisdom and knowledge, that, purified, we may enter the land of promise. In the school of letters, where boys receive the elements, some are called abecedarians, others syllabarians, others nominarians, others are called reckoners. And when we have heard all these, we recognize the advances of the boys. Likewise in the liberal studies, when we have heard of reciting a passage, or a locution, or a praise, or other matters in order, from the name of the matter we notice the advance of the youth. Through these names of places, then, as through names of matters, advances in the divine learning are shown; and as those, tarrying in each, make as it were mansions and tend from one to another, so these names of mansions and the departures from one to another show the advance of the mind and the increase of the virtues.
33.51:
**“Command the children of Israel, and say to them: When you shall have passed over the Jordan, entering into the land of Chanaan,”** — the possession of the virtues
**“YOU SHALL HAVE PASSED OVER THE JORDAN”** — That is, when you have been baptized; which is when, having put off the old man with his acts, you have put on the new, who is renewed in the knowledge of God.
33.52:
**“Destroy all the inhabitants of the region”** — of the mind
**“DESTROY”** — When we enter the holy land of promise, together with idolatry we extinguish all vices too.
**“THE INHABITANTS”** — The wicked spirits, the phantasms of the vices with their suggestions. Whence: "Blessed be he that shall take and dash thy little ones against the rock."
**“of that land: beat down their calves,”** — others: titles, or idols
**“and break in pieces their statues, and all their high places”** — the pride of the flesh
33.53: **“Cleansing the land,”** — the carnal soul from the filth of vices
33.54: **“TO THE MORE YOU SHALL GIVE A LARGER”** — Because those who have an abundance of virtues hope for a breadth of rewards. But those who are content with fewness of virtues receive recompense according to their merit. Whence: "He who soweth sparingly shall also reap sparingly" etc.
33.55:
**“But if you will not kill the inhabitants”** — the wicked spirits and the vices
**“of the land:”** — of the mind or of the flesh
**“they that remain, shall be unto you as nails in your eyes,”** — prickings of conscience
**“and spears in your sides, and they shall be your adversaries in the land of your habitation.”** — that you may not rest
33.56: **“And whatsoever I had thought to do to them,”** — the destruction, namely, of enemies, not the solace of friends

34.1:
**“And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:”**
• AND THE LORD SPOKE, etc. ORIGEN. Not all are worthy of the divine numbers; but those who are comprehended within the number of God are marked out by certain prerogatives. Whence in this book neither women are named, because of womanly weakness, nor servants degenerate in life and manners, nor the Egyptians who were mingled with the people of God, who were foreigners and barbarians; but only the Israelites. Nor all of them, but from twenty years old and upward. Nor is regard had of age alone, but it is asked whether they have strength fit for war. For it is commanded that everyone be numbered who goes forth in strength. The age of boyhood is not numbered, unless perhaps they are firstborn, or descend from the priestly or Levitical stock. For if these things are considered according to the letter, what advance will be given to those who long to be instructed by the sacred volumes? But the present reading teaches what it is to pass beyond boyish folly. For if I cease to be a little one in my senses, and, made a man, put away the things of a little one, and, made a young man, overcome the wicked one, I shall go forth in the strength of Israel and be reckoned worthy of the divine numbers. But while there is in any of us a boyish or slippery sense, or a womanish and slack sloth, while we bear Egyptian and barbarous manners, we do not merit to be in the sacred number. For innumerable are they who perish, but numbered they who are saved. Whence: "Who telleth the number of the stars" etc. Christ too says that the hairs of the disciples are numbered; with the hair, namely, of that head which was in the Nazarites, in whom was the power of the Holy Ghost for laying low the foreigners; namely the virtues of the soul and the multitude of senses which proceeded from the ruling part of the mind as from the head of the apostles.
• The Lord spoke, then, to Moses in the desert of Sinai those things, namely, which we briefly gathered above, where it is commanded that everyone be numbered from twenty years old and upward who goes forth in the strength of Israel, etc. If anyone, then, goes forth in strength, he is numbered; nor in any strength whatever, either of the Egyptians or of the Assyrians or of the Greeks, but in the strength of Israel, which is taught by God through the divine scriptures and handed down through the apostolic and evangelical faith.
• It is to be considered too that the people, having gone out of Egypt, is not at once numbered; for Pharao was still pursuing. Nor when, crossing the Red Sea, it came into the desert; for it had not yet been tempted, not yet assailed by the enemy. It fights against Amalec and conquers, nor is it yet numbered; for one victory does not suffice for one tending to perfection. It receives manna and water from the rock, nor is it numbered then; for it had not yet grown up in the things that are fit for numbering. The tabernacle is built, the law is given through Moses, the rite of sacrifices and purifications is taught, the laws and sacraments of sanctifications are established; and then the people is brought to the numbering by the command of God. See how many things you must pass through, how many endure; in how many departures, how many temptations, how many battles you must fight and conquer, that you may be able to belong to the divine number and be numbered among the holy tribes and be visited, and be enrolled in the census of the numbers through the priests of God, Aaron and Moses. You must take up the law of God, offer sacrifices, fulfil purifications, and accomplish all things which the law of the spirit teaches, that you may be able to belong to the number of Israel.
**“ORIGEN”** — The reckoning of the tribes too, the distinction of orders, the fellowship of families, the ordering of the camps, show forth vast sacraments. Certain is our expectation of the resurrection of the dead, when those who are alive, who are left, shall not prevent at the coming of Christ those who have slept; but with them shall be taken up in the clouds to meet Christ in the air; whether all are to remain in the air (as Paul says), or some too are to be transferred to paradise or to any other places (of the many mansions which are with the Father). And the diversity of translation and glory will be granted to each according to merits. And each will be in his own order. Each one, then, in the resurrection will be enrolled either in the tribe of Ruben, because in manners or in acts or in life he had something like and akin to Ruben himself; another in the tribe of Simeon, perhaps for obedience; another in the tribe of Levi, who, namely, presided well over the priesthood, or, ministering well, purchased to himself a good degree; another in the tribe of Juda, who with a kingly spirit ruled his people well, namely the senses of the mind and the thoughts of the heart. And to each tribe will be joined he who had something akin to them, either in acts or in manners. That too, that by the joined connexion of the tribes the position of the camps and the order of encamping is described, pertains to some state in the resurrection of the dead. That three tribes are said to be to the east, three to the west, three to the sea, and the last three to the north (which is called a hard wind); and that the tribe of Juda, which is kingly, is set to the east, from which our Lord sprang, I do not think idle. And that Issachar is joined to it, and Zabulon; and that this threefold number is ordered into four parts. Which, although they have divers qualities of their positions, yet are all contained in the number of the trinity; because under the one number of the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost are enrolled all who, coming from the four parts of the world, call on the name of the Lord, sitting down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of God. But I judge myself unequal to telling the mysteries of the numbers. But we must hasten to the true Jesus, yet first using Moses as our tutor, and with him laying down many rudiments of infancy. Let us tend to the perfection of Christ. For Moses did not put down many wars; Jesus quelled all wars, gave peace to all.
34.4: **“Which limits shall go round on the south side by the ascent of the Scorpion and so into Senna, and reach toward the south as far as Cadesbarne. From thence”** — or: Whence
34.6: **“And the west side shall begin from the great sea, and the same shall be the end thereof.”** — "that is: from sea to sea, namely from the torrent of Rhinocorura, which flows into the sea, as far as Emath, a city of Syria".
34.7: **“But toward the north side”** — TOWARD THE NORTH, etc. The Hebrews say that the north side begins from the great sea, which stretches along the shores of Palestine, Phenicia and Syria (which is called Coele, of Cilicia), and goes on through Egypt to Libya. And as to what is said, "reaching as far as the most high mountain", they hold that mount Amanus is signified, or Taurus, which seems truer.
34.9:
**“And the limits shall go as far as Zephrona,”**
• whence today they call it Zephyrium, a town of Cilicia
• AND THE LIMITS SHALL GO, etc. From the end of the north side, that is, the village of Enan, the borders stretch as far as Sephama, which the Hebrews call Apamea; and from Apamea they go down into Reblatha, which is Antioch of Syria. Whence he adds: over against the fountain; which it is clear is the river from which Antioch enjoys most abundant waters.
34.11: **“And from Sephama the bounds shall go down to Reblatha over against the fountain of Daphnis: from thence they shall come eastward to the sea of Cenereth,”** — The lake of Tiberias: for any gatherings of waters are called seas.
34.12: **“And shall reach as far as the Jordan, and at the last by the most salt”** — The Dead, or the tongue of the Red Sea, on whose shore Aila is set.
34.13:
**“And Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying: This shall be the land which you shall possess by lot, and which the Lord hath commanded to be given to the nine tribes, and to the half tribe.”**
• THIS SHALL BE THE LAND, etc. ORIGEN. In the former division beyond the Jordan the land was divided by Moses to the two tribes Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses. Within the Jordan, through Josue the son of Nun and Eleazar the son of Aaron, Juda possessed it from the south, Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasses from the north. But afterwards, spies having been sent from Silo through the several tribes, and a description of the land having been brought to Josue and Eleazar, Benjamin received a possession by lot beside Juda and Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasses, from the south. The second tribe, Simeon, within the tribe of Juda, that what is written of Levi and Simeon might be fulfilled: I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel. The third, Zabulon, received Galilee, in which is mount Thabor. The fourth, Issachar, where Jezrael is, as far as the Jordan. The fifth, Aser, as far as mount Carmel, which overhangs the great sea, and Tyre and Sidon. The sixth, Nephthali, in Galilee as far as the Jordan, where Tiberias is, which was once called Ceneret. The seventh, Dan, as far as Joppe; there are the towers Achilon and Zelebi, and Emmaus, which is now called Nicopolis. Although we read afterwards that, passing over other tribes, they took for themselves the city Lesem in the tribe of Dan, which today is called Paneas. For these things, and the whole inheritance of that land which in Judea is called the holy land and the good land, are a shadow of good things to come. Every place, mountain, city and village in Judea is marked by certain names, with which, namely, either the Chanaanites in their places or the Pherezites, Amorrhites, Hevites or Hebrews named them. Perhaps, then, according to Paul, who says that earthly things are a shadow of heavenly ones, there are differences of places in the heavenly regions. For in the heavens the city of Jerusalem and mount Sion are plainly said by the Apostle to be. It follows, then, that there are there other cities set about the [heavenly] Jerusalem, and villages and regions, in which the people of God and the true Israel is to be placed through the true Jesus, and to take its inheritance by the distribution of the lot, that is, by regard of merits. For example: he who lived so negligently that for his faith indeed he merits to be held among the children of Israel, but for the negligence of his life [is placed] in the tribe of Ruben or Gad or the half tribe of Manasses, will receive his lot not within the Jordan but outside. But he who by amendment of purpose has rendered himself such that, according to reasons (which God alone knows), he ought to be assigned either to the tribe of Juda or to the tribe of Benjamin (in which Jerusalem, the temple and the altar stand), and one in one, another in another: in this way a certain foreshadowing is made of the future lot in heaven of those only who shall take the inheritance of heaven through Jesus our Saviour. There perhaps will be observed these privileges of the priests, to whom are set apart all places near the cities and joined to the very walls.
• Other consequences too are to be taken. For if God, when he scattered the sons of Adam, set the sons of the nations according to the number of the angels of God (or, according to other copies, according to the number of the children of Israel), at the beginning of the world, and so they were scattered as their merits or regard for Adam himself required; what shall we say will be when the divine condescension of the last Adam (who was made not a living soul but a quickening spirit) has begun not to scatter but to dispose the sons; not at the beginning but at the end of the world; nor those who all died in Adam, but those who have been quickened in Christ? There will without doubt be a certain distribution, which is to be disposed not only according to the merits of those who are disposed, but also with regard to the last Adam. But which of us is such that from this distribution he may merit to come to that lot of the heavenly inheritance? Who is so blessed that his lot may come in Jerusalem, where the temple of God is, nay, that he himself may be the temple of God? Who is so blessed that he may keep festival days there, where the divine altar is kindled with perpetual fires? Who is so blessed that he may lay his sacrifice and incense of sweetness upon that fire of which it is said: "I am come to cast fire on the earth" etc.? Who there keeps the Pasch in the place which the Lord his God has chosen, there Pentecost, the festivity of propitiation, and the solemnity of tabernacles, no longer through a shadow but through the truth itself? Which of us will be worthy, when God has begun to divide the sons of the last Adam, that he should say to him: Thou shalt be over five or ten cities; nay, not to whom he says: Enter into the joy of thy Lord, but: Sit you also with me upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel; and of whom he says: "Father, I will that where I am, these also may be with me; I will that these be kings with me, as I am with thee; I will that they have dominion, as I am Lord of lords"? These are they who are truly numbered with sacred numbers with God, nay, all whose hairs are numbered.
**“ORIGEN”** — It seems too to some that the position and site of each of the stars can be called or held a city in heaven; which I do not dare to define. For I see that every creature, made subject indeed in hope because of him that made it subject, yet awaiting the liberty of the redemption of the sons of God, without doubt looks for something more glorious and sublime. Those, then, who serve the example and shadow of heavenly things in the law, and now through a glass in a dark manner, but then face to face, will have their conversation in heaven according to merits, in this or that part. But as there is much difference in dwelling on earth, namely in fruitful and plenteous places, where there is a temperate air and liberal institutions, or in unfruitful places, torrid with heat, where there are no laws, and empty and wild barbarism, always wars, never rest; and this not without the hidden dispensation and just judgment of God; so in those places too there will be something such, that the shadow of heavenly things on earth may be held empty in nothing at all. There will, then, be there some city of refuge, and there will be another in the desert, like Bosor in the inheritance of Ruben.

35.11: **“Determine what cities shall be for the refuge of fugitives, who have shed blood against their will.”** — DETERMINE WHAT CITIES, etc. AUGUSTINE. What is it that he says: "And the cities shall be refuges for you from the avenger of blood, and he that killed shall not die until he stand in the sight of the synagogue in judgment", when he is speaking of those who killed unwillingly? And elsewhere he says: "then each one of those fleeing in such a cause goes out free from the city to which he had fled, when the high priest has died." How then does he say here: and he that killed shall not die until he stand in the sight of the synagogue in judgment? Unless that he is judged to this end, that it may then be lawful for him to be in the city of refuge, if it has been made manifest in the judgment that he killed unwillingly.
35.13: **“AND OF THOSE CITIES”** — RABANUS. Not if perhaps, from the consciousness of your sins, you do not dare to enter the cities of the land of promise, that is, of the Church, there is Bosor on this side of the Jordan in the wilderness, which is interpreted "straitness", that is, the little cell of a monastery; which is well of the tribe of Ruben, namely of him who defiled his father's bed. There is Ramoth of the tribe of Gad, which is interpreted "lofty death" or "vision of death"; for truly penance is to be called a lofty death, when, the members having been put to death, man is led to the heights of heaven whence he fell; or because it is nobler and more reasonable to die to sins by penance than to be dissolved by the common death. Doing penance too, we set before us the torments of hell; we see the very form of death from which we are freed by penance. And in the city of the son of the handmaid we do penance; because everyone who sins is the servant of sin, and taking the form of a servant he must humble himself even unto death. There is Gaulon in the borders of Manasses, which is interpreted "rolling", that you may remember that you must roll in sackcloth; and this in the borders of Manasses, which is interpreted "forgetfulness", that you may forget what you have done and stretch yourself forth to better things. Dwell here, then, that through the straitness of death and of rolling you may escape the wrath of the pursuer and find the hope of salvation. If you do anything profitably here, you will be able to come to Cades in the land of promise and in Galilee, which is interpreted "holy"; that when in tribulation you have cast off the work of corruption, access may be granted you to the holy Church, that in the lot of Nephthali, which is called "remission", you may merit to partake of the Lord's blood. Hebron too will lie open to you, which is interpreted "joining" or "marriage". For your soul will return to its bridegroom whom it had lost through sin. And at last you will enter Sichem, which our Joseph chose for himself as an inheritance, in which too he was buried; which is interpreted "shoulder" or "labour"; that you may show that through the labour of penance you have been carried back from your error on the shoulders of Christ, and, joined to the ninety-nine sheep, made the hundredth; because Sichem was bought from the foreigners with lambs.
35.14:
**“Three shall be beyond the Jordan,”** — Bosor in the plain wilderness of the tribe of Ruben, and Ramoth Galaad of the tribe of Gad, and Gaulon in Basan of the tribe of Manasses.
**“and three in the land of Chanaan,”** — Cedes in Galilee of mount Nephthali, and Sichem in mount Ephraim, and Cariatharbe: the same is Hebron in the mountain of Juda.
35.16: **“HE SHALL BE GUILTY”** — That is, liable to eternal death. Whence: "He that shall scandalize one of these little ones that believe in me" etc. And elsewhere: "Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer, and hath not eternal life." Such a one, according to Exodus, is commanded to be dragged from the altar; because, unworthy of the Lord's sacraments, he is removed from participation in the holy altar, nor is he called back to pardon except through worthy penance.
35.19:
**“The kinsman of him that was slain, shall kill the murderer: as soon as he apprehendeth him,”** — For there is no need that he be brought to judgment, since he has already been judged a murderer, and on that account driven out of those cities.
**“he shall kill him.”** — it condemns malice and takes thought for heedlessness
35.20:
**“If through hatred any one push a man,”** — It is one thing to bring harm or death with premeditation, another by chance.
**“or fling any thing at him”** — of malice or deceit
35.21: **“Or being his enemy, strike him with his hand, and he die”** — by the death of the soul
35.22: **“But if by chance medley,”** — through ignorance
35.25:
**“The innocent shall be delivered from the hand of the revenger, and shall be brought back by sentence into the city, to which he had fled,”** — the catholic Church, where he may do penance
**“and he shall abide there until the high priest,”** — Christ
**“that is anointed with the”** — of gladness, above his fellows, namely
**“holy oil,”** — by the Father
**“die.”** — on the cross
35.26: **“If the murderer”** — impenitent, namely, and therefore removed from the fellowship of the saints and the unity of the Church.
35.27: **“be found and struck by him that is the avenger of blood: he shall not be guilty that killed him.”** — Because by the sentence of the heavenly Judge, who according to the flesh is our neighbour, he is absolved who strikes him who has neglected to be careful of his own salvation.
35.28:
**“For the fugitive ought to have stayed in the city until the death of the high priest:”** — that is: the penitent, abiding in the catholic faith, ought not to hope for pardon of his crime except in the death of the Mediator of God and men.
**“and after he is dead, then shall the manslayer return to his own country.”** — that is: having done worthy penance, he merits to receive the fatherland of paradise.
**“AND AFTER”** — GREGORY. After the death of the high priest the murderer is commanded to return to his own land; because the human race, which by sinning brought death upon itself, after the death of the true priest, that is, Christ, received absolution of guilt.
35.33: **“DEFILE NOT THE LAND”** — Morally. He defiles the land of his habitation who does bloody and wicked works, scandalizing his neighbours and killing them spiritually. And unless the desires of the flesh are slain through confession of sins and worthy penance, the land of the body will in no way be cleansed, nor will the creator of all dwell in his soul where he sees the filth of a sordid conversation bearing rule.
35.34: **“And thus shall your possession be cleansed, myself abiding with you. For I am the Lord that dwell among the children of Israel.”** — seeing God with the heart and hearing him

36.1:
**“And the princes of the families of Galaad came”**
• 'heap of testimony'
• AND THERE CAME, etc. RABANUS. Godly thoughts ought to provide that the possession of good merits does not pass into the dominion of strangers, but remains perpetually with the lawful heir; and Moses, that is, the law, is consulted, that it may answer how they may become perpetual possessors of their own right; which the very names express. For Galaad is interpreted "heap of testimony"; Machir, "selling"; Manasses, "forgotten"; Joseph, "increased"; Salphaad, "shadow of fear". The princes of the families of Galaad, then, the son of Machir, the son of Manasses, of the stock of the sons of Joseph, speak for the daughters of Salphaad, when the thoughts of a godly mind contend, according to the testimonies of the scriptures, for the faithful soul which has sold the labour of the present life for the future, and, forgetting the things that are behind, stretches itself forth to those that are before, that through the increase of good works it may obtain eternal rewards. For the five daughters of Salphaad, that is, of the shadow of fear, signify outward things, which are accomplished by the five senses of the body. And it is necessary that those who in the shadow of the present life study good works should keep them in fear, lest they lose their labour. The princes of Galaad, then, fear lest their possession be transferred to another tribe; and each faithful man provides that the works which he does may profit him for salvation, lest, if they are done with wicked intent, they be invaded by unclean spirits. Whence: "Take heed that you do not your justice before men."
**“the son of Machir,”** — 'selling'
**“the son of Manasses,”** — Forgetfulness
**“of the stock of the children of Joseph,”** — Increased
36.2: **“The Lord hath commanded thee, our lord, that thou shouldst divide the land by lot to the children of Israel, and that to the daughters of Salphaad”** — 'Shadow of fear'
36.6: **“LET THEM MARRY TO WHOM”** — The Apostle says the like: "Let her marry to whom she will; only in the Lord", that is, to a catholic man; lest the possession, namely of good works and right faith, be lost if she marries a Gentile or a Jew. But tropologically, the woman, that is, the godly intention, may join herself through good action to whatever labour she will; yet so that she keeps godliness and religion in all things, lest she suffer loss of her work, for which she hopes for the possession of the eternal inheritance, if she joins herself to a stranger, that is, to an earthly one.
36.11:
**“And Maala were married,”**
• 'weakness'
• AND MAALA WERE MARRIED, etc. RABANUS. This happens when anyone of the number of believing Jews joins himself to a teacher believing from the Gentiles, that by his teaching he may beget sons, that is, works of godliness. For by name the elect from the Gentiles can be called cousins, because they are brethren of the holy preachers who were set in Judea. There ought to be no schism in spiritual kinship, where there is one faith in profession. And as there is one shepherd, there ought to be one fold. For we are all brethren.
• He who studies to have humility and is pleased in his infirmities keeps a solemnity, and gives acceptable gifts to God, and is king of his own conversation, and for the advance of the virtues is moved, walking from virtue to virtue.
**“and Thersa,”** — 'contemplating' or 'pleasing'
**“and Hegla,”** — 'solemnity' or 'calf'
**“and Melcha,”** — 'his king'
**“and Noa”** — 'motion'
36.12:
**“Of the family of Manasses, who was the son of Joseph: and the possession”** — godly action
**“that had been allotted to them, remained in the tribe and family of their father.”** — in the catholic Church
36.13:
**“These are the commandments and judgments, which the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses to the children of Israel, in the plains of Moab upon the Jordan over against Jericho.”**
• It happens that when the moon is fourteen days old at the vernal equinox, or on the fourth day of the third month, of that year there is a solar year and four days, up to the twentieth day of the second month of the second year; so that that month is called the first of each year whose full moon first occurs after the vernal equinox; and so it is believed to have been in the year of the going out of Israel from Egypt.
• This book is called Vaiedaber in Hebrew, but in Latin the book of Numbers; which among the five books of the law holds the fourth place; in which, although the order of the history is served, yet a mystical understanding is hinted. The order of the history is served because, since in Leviticus, which is the third, it treats of the consecration of the priests and the use of the sacrifices which were made in the tabernacle, in this is written the dedication of the same tabernacle and the gifts of the princes which they offered at that dedication. And since the tabernacle had to be taken down and carried to another place, it is assigned who should carry the things of the tabernacle and what, that is, what the Caathites, what the Gersonites, what the Merarites should carry. It is taught too which Levites, and according to what age, ought to minister in the tabernacle. Fittingly, then, after Leviticus, the third, this fourth is set. A mystery too is hinted to us in its being set in the fourth place. For as among all figures the square is the more perfect, so the perfection of this work is commended by the perfection of the number four. For as on the fourth day the lights were made, the fourth age under David was the most robust; the fourth age of man too, that is, youth, is the strongest among the others; and many other things set under the number four are signs of perfection. So the perfection of strength of those who are numbered in this book is shown, while only those are numbered who go forth in the strength of Israel. For from this number are excluded children, women, Egyptians, servants; of the children only the firstborn of the priests and Levites are numbered. For unworthy of the divine numbers is the childish and slippery sense, the womanish, slack and dissolute sloth, the Egyptians, that is, worldly manners, and those who fear servilely. Israel alone is numbered, yet not all, but only that which goes forth in strength to war against the spiritual wickednesses of the powers.
• But it is to be noted that the people of God is numbered neither in Egypt nor at once after the going out. For first Egypt is forsaken, the sea crossed, Amalec overcome, manna eaten and the tabernacle built, the law written by the finger of God received; and then the people of God from twenty years old and upward is reckoned worthy of the divine number. In which it is signified that unless one has left Egypt, that is, the world and its concupiscences, has received the Red Sea, that is, baptism consecrated by the blood of Christ, and been made the temple of God by the indwelling Holy Ghost, has overcome by the power of God Amalec, that is, licking blood, that is, the devil and vices, has received the body and blood of the Lord and used it as manna, has kept the law of God too in all things, he cannot come to the dignity of this number. The reckoning too of the tribes, which are disposed in four places about the tabernacle by threes, the order and number of the mansions, the fellowship of the families and the whole ordering of the camps breathe wondrous sacraments. For that the tribes are placed by threes through four parts hints that the faith of the holy Trinity is to be preached by the office of the teachers through the four regions of the world. In the very fellowship of the families too is hinted a sure hope of the resurrection: namely that in that resurrection each will be joined to that tribe or that order of angels which, abiding in this life, he has laboured to imitate according to his power. The catalogue too of the mansions, which, from the first, which was in Ramesses, to the last, which was beside the Jordan, we number as forty-two, hints at the number of the mansions by which we ascend to heaven (as we shall say in their dispositions). And we have the same number of our ascent into heaven as Matthew sets in the enumeration of the generation of Christ descending from the first patriarch; that we may know that we ascend to heaven in the same number by which the evangelist marked that Christ descended to the blessed Virgin as to the Jordan. Which virgin is well called the Jordan, because, flowing with full stream, she overflowed with the grace of the Holy Ghost. It is plain, then, from what has been said, that this book is called the book of Numbers because in it the people of Israel is numbered, or the catalogue of mansions is contained. In which Moses intends, through the number of the children of Israel who are said to have come down to the Jordan, and the catalogue of the mansions by which they came from Egypt to the land of promise, to mark out who come to heaven, and by what road. For by showing who are numbered, he shows who; but by numbering the mansions, he shows by what road one comes. The order is this: first he places the leaders of the people and the people numbered about the tabernacle in a square; he marks out the Levites, excepted from the number of the others, for the ministry of the tabernacle. Then the tabernacle is dedicated; the oblations are assigned which are offered at that dedication. Then Balaam is brought by king Balac to curse the people of God; afterwards the catalogue of mansions is described. At the end six cities are ordained, three on this side and three beyond the Jordan, to which he might flee who unknowingly shed his neighbour's blood. The Levites, keeping watch between the tabernacle and the other children of Israel, divided by the Aaronites on the east and the Caathites on the south and the Gersonites on the west and the Merarites on the north, signify the prelates of the Church, who are in the middle between the cloistered, who [are signified] by the tabernacle, for whom they provide in temporal things, and the laity, over whom they preside in spiritual things. The Aaronites, that is, both Moses and Aaron and the sons of these sons, fold and wrap the more secret things in the tabernacle, and bringing in the Caathites give them the wrapped things to carry on their own shoulders, lest seeing they die. For the mysteries of the Church are not to be published except to the highest men, that is, Moses and Aaron, because the weak would be scandalized by them. Whence too the book is carried open for the priest and the deacon, shut for the rest. The Gersonites and Merarites, who are less worthy than the Caathites, carry their burdens not on their own shoulders but with oxen and wagons. Because "he that will be my disciple, let him follow me", as it were through death. And the more anyone wishes to come near to God himself, the heavier persecution he incurs.
• You shall bless the children of Israel and you shall say to them: from this place is taken the blessing which the bishop makes with two fingers joined and raised. The two fingers joined and raised signify the law and the priesthood, which are understood by Moses and Aaron. The three verses which follow contain that threefold petition which is made in the words of the bishop, whatever they may be: the grace of the Holy Ghost, true salvation, eternal peace are asked. Then there always follows the distinction of persons in these words: which may he deign to grant, who with the Father and the Holy Ghost liveth and reigneth for ever.
• The cause of writing this book was that the things which had been done or said, briefly gathered, might be held more firmly in the memory of the people. What Moses spoke, after the manner of scripture, he speaks of himself as of another; as John says: "That disciple whom Jesus loved" etc.

1.1:
**“JEROME”** — These are the words which Moses spoke, etc. The beginning of Deuteronomy seems to be the title of the whole work, because it indicates the person of the author, and what he did, and the place and the time. The name of the book too shows the grace of the New Testament. For Deuteronomy is interpreted "second law", and signifies the Gospel, which explains spiritually the sacraments of the Old Testament; as the book of Deuteronomy is a repetition of the four books of the law. For those contain their own matters in themselves; this one goes over them all again. It has its own sacraments too.
**“These are the words,”**
• These are the words which Moses spoke, etc. He says this of himself as of another, after the manner of Holy Scripture; as there too: "Moses was the meekest of all men that dwelt upon earth." For so he avoids arrogance and shows that it is to be avoided. Likewise Job too says of himself: "There was a man in the land of Hus, whose name was Job" etc. And John: "This is that disciple who giveth testimony of these things" etc.
• He speaks of himself as of another, as John says of himself: "The disciple whom Jesus loved." Or the Holy Ghost bears witness to him, that no one might be able to doubt that Moses wrote these things.
**“which spoke”** — by teaching
**“Moses”**
• the law
• It is asked why he said "these are the words which Moses spoke" and did not say "which God spoke"? And why he commands this book to be put in the ark and not the other books, in which are the words of the Lord? Again, how could he speak those words to all Israel, when so great a multitude was there to be cared for? Answer: he said this to show that he spoke to the people the same words which the Lord spoke to Moses. To the second it must be said that the books, in so far as they are the words of the Lord, need no commendation; but the book of Moses needed letters of commendation. For the Lord wishes the sayings of his own to be held in veneration, and not only his. And because this book is more expressive of the Gospel, therefore it is commanded to be put in the ark and held in greater reverence. To the third question: that Moses spoke to some and commanded them to speak to others; as it is said in Mark 9: "what I say to one, I say to all."
**“to all Israel”** — the Jewish people, to whom the law was given universally
**“beyond the Jordan,”** — before baptism
**“in the plain wilderness,”**
• the Church, in which there is no bristling of thorns, that is, of vices
• MOSES SPOKE TO ALL ISRAEL, etc. Allegorically, Moses is the old law, which beyond the Jordan, that is, before baptism, taught the Israelite people. For by the Jordan is signified baptism, in which Christ was baptized. In the plain wilderness, that is, in the barrenness of the carnal people, which did not bear the fruit of virtues.
**“IN THE WILDERNESS”** — The barrenness of the people, to whom it is said: "Your house shall be left to you desolate."
**“over against the Red Sea,”** — baptism, red with the blood of Christ
**“OVER AGAINST THE RED SEA”** — Because a wicked and perverse generation would not believe in the washing away of sins in the blood of Christ.
**“between”** — names of places:
**“Pharan”** — increased: the Church spread or widened far and wide
**“and Thophel”** — insipidity: for the Church seems foolish because it despises things visible, desiring things invisible
**“and Laban”** — whitening: the Church whitened in baptism
**“and Haseroth,”** — courts, of which the Church says: "My soul longeth and fainteth for the courts of the Lord"
**“where”** — in the Church
**“gold”** — of wisdom
**“there is very much.”**
• It signifies that manifold mysteries and a spiritual treasure of wisdom are in the things that are said.
• These four mountains signify the four Gospels, by which the Church is surrounded.
**“BETWEEN PHARAN”** — Pharan: increased; Thophel: insipidity; Laban: whitening; Haseroth: courts. For the people was increased in the number of men by the doctrine of the law and the prophets; but it was insipid, because it did not have the salt of wisdom; and whitened by the ceremonies of the law and various cleannesses, which it believed it had from the letter of the law. Which is well signified by the courts, as prepared by the divine scriptures for the entrance of faith. Whence many at the coming of Christ more easily received him whom they recognized as foretold before. Whence Philip: "We have found him of whom Moses in the law and the prophets did write, Jesus the son of Joseph of Nazareth."
1.2:
**“Eleven days'”** — the number of transgression
**“ELEVEN DAYS”** — The law explained by Moses in eleven days signifies the transgression of the Jewish people in the commandments of the Decalogue. The eleven days are the eleven apostles, through whom, Judas having been rejected, the Gospel of Christ was preached in the world.
**“From Horeb”** — they came (understood)
**“by the way of mount Seir”** — because the law [came] from the mountain of God, Horeb
**“to Cadesbarne.”** — changed
**“FROM HOREB”** — Who too, beginning from Horeb, passing through Seir, that is, "hairy" and "filthy", the people [being filthy] with vices, came to Cadesbarne, which is interpreted "changed" or "chosen" or "noble"; signifying the literal sense of the law changed into the spiritual through the Gospel. "For all these things happened to them in figure, and they are written for our correction, upon whom the ends of the world are come." For the law is not dissolved but fulfilled; nor "shall one jot or one tittle pass, till all be fulfilled."
1.3:
**“In the fortieth year,”**
• as above
• IN THE FORTIETH YEAR, etc. ISIDORE. Allegorically, the forty years, which having been laboriously passed through, the children of Israel crossed over to the promised land, signify the whole time of this world, in which the Church, under labours and perilous temptations, by hoping waits with patience for what it does not see, until it comes to the promised fatherland. Therefore the Lord fasted forty days and was tempted forty nights in the wilderness. For the body of Christ, which is the Church, passes through temptations and labours until it comes to consolation. And that the clothing of the Israelites was corrupted by no age through so many years, and the skins of their shoes lasted without flaw, signifies the incorruptibility of bodies, when the things now corruptible shall remain without corruption.
• The number forty is signified, or consists, of ten and four, and signifies the fulfilment of both the law and the Gospel; for ten pertains to the law, but four to the Gospel.
**“the eleventh month,”** — IN THE ELEVENTH, etc. As in the eleventh the transgression of the law is expressed, so in the first day the watchful intent of the lawgiver to teach; who, from the time that the disobedient people did not fear to transgress the law, at once studied to make known the will of the Lord by preaching and correcting, and did not cease to draw or provoke them to better things by words and examples.
**“the first day of the month,”** — In the beginning of grace
**“Moses spoke”** — by writing
**“to the children of Israel”** — between whom and God he himself was mediator
**“all that had commanded”** — he had received them not from himself but from God
**“him the Lord”** — as mediator
1.4:
**“After that he had slain Sehon”** — useless sprout, or temptation of the eyes
**“king of the Amorrhites,”**
• of those embittering
• AFTER THAT HE HAD SLAIN SEHON KING OF THE AMORRHITES, etc. It is to be noted that, the two kings of the Amorrhites having been slain, the law is recapitulated and the people instructed; because, stumblingblocks having been removed and the troops of vices overcome, one is fittingly trained in doctrine, and the light of faith is opened to those who worthily desire it.
• We ought first to slay the vices in ourselves, and so hand on the divine commandments to the peoples.
**“who dwelt in Hesebon:”** — thought, or girdle of grief
**“and Og”** — which is interpreted shutting in
**“king of Basan”** — confusion
**“who abode in Astaroth,”** — forecourts or courts
**“and in Edrai,”** — flood of evils
**“SEHON KING OF THE AMORRHITES”** — ISIDORE. Allegorically: in these kings, although the deed done is known, yet through the interpretations of the names a spiritual signification is intimated. For Sehon is interpreted "useless sprout" or "temptation of the eyes", by whom the devil is figured, who transforms himself into an angel of light, that by schisms or heresy he may deceive the unwary. Him the Amorrhites, that is, the embittering, have as king. For unless some pretence goes before, there will be neither heresies of the embittering nor schisms of the provoking. He is slain in each one when pretence is condemned and truth is loved. But Og is interpreted "shutting in", Basan "confusion". For the devil does this, that he may shut off the way to God, setting idolatry in the way, lest anyone believe in Christ. For shutting in goes before as king, confusion follows as people. For those whom he shuts out from the faith of Christ will be confounded when Christ appears. And Sehon dwelt in Hesebon, because the devil, the king of vices, mingles himself with human thoughts and girds the mind with superfluous cares, lest it utter words of truth or exercise works of godliness. For Hesebon is interpreted "thought" or "girdle of grief". Og too, king of Basan, dwelt in Astaroth and Edrai. For Astaroth [means] courts; Edrai, flood of evils; they sound unbelief, namely with wicked works. For the devil strives for this: that those whom he rules may never enter the door of faith, but, remaining outside, may always be busy with wicked works.
1.5:
**“beyond the Jordan,”** — as above
**“in the land of Moab.”** — that is, lawless
**“IN THE LAND OF MOAB”** — For the people was lawless, which did not have the spiritual law.
**“And began”** — from the beginning
**“Moses to expound the law,”** — because it is obscure
**“and to say:”** — with feeling
1.6:
**“The Lord our God spoke”**
• he gains authority for himself while he brings in God as author
• whom love as God thy creator
• where they also struck their tents at his command
• THE LORD OUR GOD, etc. In the book of Numbers the departure of the children of Israel from the desert of Sinai is related, but the Lord's command to Moses about the same passage is not told, but only of the cloud which covered the tabernacle, and, when they were to set out, withdrew and went before to the place of pitching the camp. For so it is written: "In the second year, in the second month, the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle of the covenant, and rested in the wilderness of Pharan." But it is manifest that that passage was ordered by God's command, though it is not mentioned there. Whence elsewhere in the book of Numbers: at the command of the Lord they pitched their tents, and at his command they took them down.
**“to us in Horeb, saying: You have stayed long enough in this mountain:”** — YOU HAVE STAYED LONG ENOUGH, etc. Moses is commanded to withdraw from the mountain on which he had received the law; because the teacher ought not always to be intent on contemplation, but should sometimes come down to take care of himself and his neighbours. Whence: "For whether we be transported in mind, it is to God; or whether we be sober, it is for you."
**“GILBERT”** — Not all the things that are in a harp sound, but all help. So not the whole history sounds a spiritual understanding, but the whole helps. For unless the other things stood around, the things that sound spiritually would not stand out.
1.9:
**“And I said to you at that time:”** — AND I SAID TO YOU AT THAT TIME, etc. Of this division of powers it is written in Exodus, before they came to mount Sinai, that "Jethro the priest of Madian, the kinsman of Moses", suggested it to him. Whence it is rightly asked how these things agree with each other in manner and time. But what is said here, that Moses said at that time: I alone am not able to bear you, etc., does not signify the time at which they set out from Horeb, but the whole time in which, having set out from Egypt, they tarried in the wilderness. And Moses persuaded his people of these things not by his own counsel but by his kinsman's.
**“AT THAT TIME”** — The saints do all things "in due time"; God too, namely: "When the fulness of the time was come, he sent his Son."
**“I alone am not able”** — He does not withdraw from labour, but seeks helpers.
1.10:
**“to bear you: for the Lord your God hath multiplied you,”** — "They are multiplied above number."
**“and you are this day as the stars of heaven, for multitude.”** — this is said of the good
1.11:
**“The Lord God of your fathers add”** — THE LORD GOD OF YOUR FATHERS, etc. He teaches teachers to rejoice at the advance of those under them, to give thanks, and always to wish for better things.
**“TO THIS NUMBER”** — The number fixed with God he knows, who knows who are his, who telleth the number of the stars.
**“many thousands,”** — of the perfect: the thousand is perfect
