**“he shall have of her he shall call by his name,”** — that he may be called Christian from Christ
25.7:
**“But if he will not”** — if the doctor will not take counsel for the Church
**“take”** — to rule her
**“a wife,”** — the Church
**“of his brother,”** — of Christ
**“who by law belongeth to him,”** — by divine institution
**“the woman shall go”** — that is, the Church
**“to the gate of the city,”** — where judgments are made
**“and call upon the ancients,”** — the holier and worthier
**“and say: My husband's brother refuseth”** — the priest or bishop, the spouse of the Church
**“to raise up his brother's name in Israel:”** — among the saints who see God
25.9:
**“and shall take off”** — because he neglected the care of his neighbour
**“HIS SHOE”** — [The shoe] of which it is said: feet shod in the preparation of the Gospel of peace. If we bear the care of our neighbour as of ourselves, we protect each foot with a shoe; but he who, thinking of his own advantage, neglects that of his neighbours, as it were loses with disgrace the shoe of one foot.
**“FROM HIS FOOT”** — That is, she will show him deprived of the reward of preaching. For the doctors' feet are shod, because, protected by the examples of the fathers who went before, the steps of their preaching have imitated them. He is shod on both feet who profits himself and others.
**“and spit in his face,”** — she will reproach him openly and show him worthy of contempt
**“and say: So shall it be done to the man that will not build up his brother's house:”** — of Christ
25.11:
**“If two men have words together,”** — a disputation about the faith
**“AND ONE AGAINST THE OTHER”** — The Catholic and the heretic, whose contention is perpetual because their intention is unlike. For one defends falsehood, the other the truth; and one must resist error, lest the fool seem wise to himself.
**“begin to fight, and the wife willing”** — of the one subject
**“of the other to deliver”** — heretical depravity
**“her husband”** — the heretic
**“AND SHALL PUT FORTH”** — [If] through false ignominy or abominable action she wishes to stain the conversation of the Catholic or to defame his doctrine.
**“her hand, and take him by the secrets,”**
• with anathema
• the shameless working
**“THE SECRETS”** — The weaker members of the Church; [she] wishing, namely, to deceive them by flattering or to deride them by insulting.
25.12: **“Thou shalt cut off her hand, neither shalt thou be moved with any pity in her regard.”** — cruel
25.13:
**“Thou shalt not have”** — that is, do not teach [others] to do what thou wilt not do, because Jesus "began to do and to teach"
**“THOU SHALT NOT HAVE”** — In Leviticus the same is said against it. Solomon too says: a great weight and a small; and so double measures are unclean before God.
**“ISIDORE”** — Thou shalt not have in thy bag. Spiritually too we must take care not to have divers weights in the heart: that is, softening the rule of strictness for ourselves, [while] we bind those to whom we preach the word of God with stricter precepts as with heavier weights. When we do this, we weigh out the reward and fruit of the Lord's precepts with a diverse weight; whence: a double weight is an abomination to the Lord.
25.17:
**“REMEMBER WHAT”** — The Hebrews relate that Amalec killed the lepers and those having an issue of seed and the others placed outside the camp; and these, they say, are the hindmost of the Lord's army.
**“Amalec did to thee”** — Amalec: licking blood. These are the demons who oppose us as we come out of the spiritual Egypt through baptism, and strive, by suggesting sins, to kill those who are hindmost in virtues and wearied on the journey of this life. These, when the Lord gives the means, we ought utterly to overthrow, and to overthrow or blot out their suggestions in every way, lest, if we keep any remnants as Saul did, we be overthrown with them as disobedient.
**“in the way,”** — of the present life
**“when thou camest out of Egypt:”** — the spiritual
25.18:
**“How he met thee:”** — as it were gnashing with zeal
**“and the hindmost”** — the first they dare not attack
**“of thy army,”** — of the ecclesiastical army
**“who being weary”** — by weariness of labours
**“sat down,”** — those who keep going he cannot kill: "for blessed are they that walk in the law of the Lord"
**“he slew,”** — with the spiritual sword
**“when thou wast with hunger”** — those spent by hunger for the word of God and by labour are easily killed
**“and labour spent, and he feared not God.”** — who was made to fear no one
25.19:
**“Therefore when the Lord thy God shall give thee rest,”** — victory being gained over the harassment of demons
**“and shall have subdued all the nations round about”** — of the demons, who go about seeking whom they may devour
**“in the land”** — of promise
**“which to thee”** — when thou wast in Egypt
**“he hath promised:”** — this Samuel and Saul fulfilled
**“thou shalt blot out his name from under heaven.”** — from the dwelling of the saints
**“See thou forget it not.”** — this precept

26.1:
**“AND WHEN THOU ART COME”** — As the Israelites in their land of promise are commanded to offer the firstfruits in thanksgiving because they were rescued from Egypt, so let us, entering the land of the Church through the spiritual Jordan, that is, baptism, put in the basket of our conversation the firstfruits of good working and offer them to God on the altar of the Catholic faith, that our priest Christ may receive them; and there let us confess to the Lord, saying that the Syrian, which is interpreted lofty or moistening, that is, the devil, pursued our father, that is, the first-formed man, that, having deceived him through pride, gluttony and avarice, he might deprive him of the possession of Paradise. Whence, an exile, he sojourned in the Egypt of this world in a small number, because many followed idolatry and few faithful remained. But after the law was given, when more arose receiving the knowledge and faith of one God, the Egyptians, that is, the demons, afflicted them, laying on them most grievous burdens of sins. But God looked upon the affliction and labour of the human race and sent his Son, who is called his hand and arm, to rescue them from the power of darkness and translate them into the kingdom of light. So he gave us a land flowing with milk and honey, that is, the present Church, where is the milk of innocence and of easy doctrine, by which the little ones are nourished, and the honey of sweet and manifold wisdom, by which the perfect are filled.
**“the land”** — the Church
**“which the Lord thy God will give thee to possess, and hast conquered”** — the enemy being mightily overcome
**“it, and dwellest in it:”** — "Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle", etc.
26.2:
**“Thou shalt take of all thy fruits”** — with virtues, with works
**“the first, and put them in a basket,”** — a wicker vessel
**“and shalt go”** — of conversation, or of the Spirit of God
**“to the place”** — the altar of faith
**“which the Lord thy God shall choose, that [his name] may be invocated there:”** — "Whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved"
26.3:
**“And thou shalt go to the priest”** — Christ, according to the order of Melchisedech
**“that shall be in those days,”**
• that is, to be; he will appear
• in the time of this priest there is no night
**“and say to him: I profess”** — giving thanks, not [to] man
**“this day before the Lord thy God,”**
• in the sight of the Lord God
• according to the humanity
**“that I am come into the land,”** — the Church
**“for which he swore”**
• by firmly promising
• by faith or by flesh
**“to our fathers,”** — Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
**“that he would give it us.”**
• to the sons; whence: "The land wherein thou sleepest I will give to thee and to thy sons and to thy seed"
• who offers our goods to the Father, the mediator of God and men
26.4:
**“And the priest taking the basket at thy hand,”** — with the work
**“shall set it before the altar”** — the heavenly
**“of the Lord thy God:”** — or: of his
26.5:
**“who went down into Egypt,”**
• from Paradise; this is he who went down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers
• the world, dark with the night of sin
**“and sojourned there”** — "while we are in the body we are absent from the Lord"
**“in a very small number,”**
• in comparison with the unbelievers
• whence: "When they were but a small number, yea very few, and sojourners therein"
• of the faithful
**“and grew into a nation”** — when the law was received
**“great and strong”** — of the saints
**“and of an infinite multitude.”** — as the stars of heaven
26.6:
**“And afflicted us”** — visible or invisible
**“the Egyptians, and persecuted us, laying on us”** — of sins
**“most grievous burdens:”** — of the soul
26.7:
**“And we cried to the Lord God of our fathers: who heard us,”** — crying out
**“and looked down upon our affliction,”** — who looketh on the low, and the high he knoweth afar off
**“and labour,”** — of the body
**“and distress:”** — of the mind
26.8:
**“And brought us out of Egypt”** — from the power of darkness
**“with a strong hand,”** — by the Son, invincible and manifest
**“and a stretched out arm, with great terror,”** — of the Egyptians
**“with signs”** — the lesser
**“and wonders:”** — the greater
26.9:
**“And brought us into this place,”** — so precious, so pleasant
**“and gave us this land”** — the Church
**“with milk”** — of easy doctrine
**“and honey flowing.”**
• with sweetness
• abounding
• what he himself begins in us he himself perfects
26.10:
**“And therefore now I offer the firstfruits”**
• of virtues, of good works
• of the fruitful soul or of holy conversation
**“of the fruits of the land which the Lord God hath given”** — freely
**“me.”**
• to the servant
• WHICH THE LORD HATH GIVEN, etc. As if [to say]: I offer nothing but what he has given; for every good is from God.
**“And thou shalt leave them”**
• thou shalt commit them to be kept
• it pleases us
**“In the sight of the Lord thy God”** — OF THE LORD, etc. Who will keep them as it were under his eyes and will render them on that day, the just judge.
**“and adoring”**
• through such sacrifices
• according to that: "The Lord thy God shalt thou adore", etc.
26.11:
**“THOU SHALT FEAST”** — With the spiritual banquet, of which it is said: "Eat, O friends, and drink, and be inebriated, my dearly beloved."
**“in all the good things”** — spiritual
**“which the Lord thy God hath given thee, and thy house, thou and the Levite,”** — with thy imitators
**“AND THE LEVITE”** — The true minister of God, taken from among men and ordained for men in the things that pertain to God.
**“and the stranger”** — who truly says: "I am a stranger with thee and a sojourner, as all my fathers"
**“that is with thee.”** — he is of the same will; he is in heaven, he passes over on earth
26.12:
**“WHEN THOU HAST MADE AN END”** — We read that Tobias fulfilled this; but those who were far from the temple gave in the third year the tithes of three years collected to the poor and the Levites who dwelt with them.
**“of tithing”** — perfection
**“all thy fruits, in the third year of tithes”** — in the name of the Trinity, which gives us perfection
**“thou shalt give it to the Levite,”** — "Let him that is instructed in the word communicate to him that instructeth him, in all good things"
**“and to the stranger,”** — who has not here an abiding city
**“and to the fatherless,”** — whose father the devil is dead
**“and to the widow,”** — to whom the world is dead; "Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor"; whence: "but especially to those of the household of the faith"
26.13: **“And thou shalt speak”** — not boasting, but showing thyself not ungrateful
26.14: **“I have not eaten of them in my mourning, nor separated them for any uncleanness, nor spent any thing of them in funerals. I have obeyed the voice of the Lord my God, and have done all things as thou hast commanded me.”** — he signifies the funeral rites for parents which the Gentiles used to observe

27.2:
**“And when you are passed over the Jordan into the land which the Lord thy God will give thee, thou shalt set up great stones,”** — namely, the holy preachers, who from Christ the living stone are called living stones
**“STONES, AND WITH PLASTER”** — The doctors ought to put off all roughness and appear splendid to God, having the law written in their hearts.
27.4:
**“Therefore when you are passed over the Jordan,”** — WHEN THEREFORE YOU ARE PASSED OVER THE JORDAN, etc. ISIDORE. How this was done is read in the book of Josue: "Josue built an altar to God most high, and wrote on the stones the Deuteronomy of the law of Moses", etc. The stones of which the altar is built are all who believe in Christ, of whom it is said: "You are living stones", etc. On these no iron is laid, because they are uncorrupted and unspotted in flesh and spirit and have not received the fiery darts of the devil. These make one altar by the unity of faith and the concord of charity. On these our Lord Jesus wrote again the Deuteronomy, that is, the second law, that of the Gospel, who says: "Thou shalt not commit adultery. But I say to you, that whosoever shall look on a woman to lust after her hath already committed adultery with her in his heart." This law he sets in the hearts of believers who are worthy of the building of the altar.
**“set up the stones”** — living
**“which I command you this day, in mount Hebal,”** — which is interpreted old abyss, and is a figure of the law, which was under the curse, Moses saying: "Cursed is every one that abideth not in the words of this law"
**“and thou shalt plaster them with plaster:”** — namely, with the concord of charity
27.5:
**“And thou shalt build there an altar to the Lord thy God,”** — the unity of faith and of the saints
**“of stones which iron hath not touched,”** — who, unspotted and uncorrupted in flesh and spirit, have not received the darts of the devil
27.6:
**“And of stones not fashioned nor polished: and thou shalt offer upon it”** — the altar
**“holocausts to the Lord thy God:”** — the perfection of faith and charity
27.7:
**“And shalt immolate peace victims,”** — the virtues, which acquire for us true peace
**“and eat”** — of the fruit of the virtues
**“there, and feast”** — with spiritual delights
**“before the Lord thy God,”** — to whom such a banquet is pleasing
27.8:
**“And thou shalt write upon the stones”** — the saints, who have the writing of the Gospel in their hearts
**“all the words of the law”** — of the Gospel
**“[of] this, plainly and clearly,”** — without scruple of doubt
27.12:
**“These shall stand”**
• as serving out of charity and tending toward the blessing
• the nobler tribes
• THESE SHALL STAND, etc. Those who go beside mount Garizim, chosen to bless, figure those who come to salvation kindled not by fear of punishment but by love of the heavenly promise. Those who go beside mount Hebal, on which the curses were uttered, are those who do the precepts of the law not for love of the blessings or promises, but from fear of punishments. But all go round about the ark, because they do not depart from the bosom of the Church. But nobler are those who serve out of charity than those who serve from fear of punishment. Jesus alone can know such minds, and set some on mount Garizim to bless, others on mount Hebal to curse: not that they may receive the curse, but that they may beware of the curses written and appointed for sinners, and repent through fear of punishment.
**“upon mount Garizim to bless the Lord,”** — which is interpreted division, and signifies the doctrine of the New Testament
**“the Jordan:”** — with the sacrament of baptism
27.13:
**“And over against them these”**
• who [keep] the precepts from fear of punishment and of the curse to come
• the ignoble, among whom is Ruben, who went up to his father's bed; Zabulon, the last of Lia's sons; and the sons of the handmaids
27.14:

28.14:
**“TURN NOT AWAY”** — AUGUSTINE. The Seventy: "Thou shalt not pass from all the words which I command thee, to the right hand or to the left, to go after strange gods to serve them." The right hand is set for praise; but in the way of life he is blamed who turns aside to the right; not that the things on the right are blamed, but he who turns aside into them, that is, who arrogates to himself the things that are God's. Whence: "Decline not to the right hand nor to the left; for the Lord knoweth the ways that are on the right hand", etc. They are good, then, because the Lord knoweth the way of the just. To turn aside to the right, then, is to attribute the good not to the grace of God but to oneself; whence he adds: "But he will make thy courses straight", etc. "To the right or to the left, to go after strange gods to serve them": this is not said because strange gods can be taken as on the right, but [of] the earthly places which the nations that worshipped strange gods held on the right or the left. Or thus: "Thou shalt not pass from all the words", etc., so that by passing over what is commanded thou go after strange gods. For this he wished to commend separately after all [the rest]: that thou seek not help from strange gods for the sake of seeking felicity or fleeing infelicity, as though they were either to be won over that they may help or appeased that they may not harm; according to that: "Their right hand is a right hand of iniquity", [of those] who think, namely, that man is made happy by those things which both good and bad can have. And therefore it is a right hand of iniquity, because they are unjust who think it a right hand. For it is not a true right hand, but the right hand of those who have called the people happy that hath these things; whereas happy is the people whose God is the Lord. This is the true right hand, of equity and not of iniquity. One must not then go after strange gods, neither on the right, so that a man think himself made happy by them, nor on the left, thinking himself made wretched by their opposing; or, if we understand by the right hand eternal goods and by the left temporal, they are to be worshipped neither for these nor for those.

29.1:
**“THESE ARE THE WORDS”** — AUGUSTINE. The Seventy: "These are the words of the testament which the Lord commanded Moses in the land of Moab, beside the testament which he testified to them in Horeb." He shows whence this book is called Deuteronomy, as it were the second law, where there is more repetition than anything else. For there are few things here that are not in that which was given first. Nor are two testaments named, although these words seem to sound so; both are one testament, which is called the old. For if on account of these words two were to be spoken of, there would be not two but more, apart from the new. For in many places Scripture speaks of a testament, as that which was made with Abram concerning circumcision, or with Noe.
**“of the covenant”** — of the testament
**“which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab: beside”** — or, because of
29.3: **“The great temptations, which”** — THE GREAT TEMPTATIONS, WHICH, etc. "And the Lord God hath not given you a heart to know, and eyes to see, and ears to hear", etc. How does he say above: "You have seen the temptations", etc.? If the Lord did not give eyes to see, they saw with the body and not with the heart. Whence he put first: "The Lord hath not given you a heart to know." To this belong the two that follow: eyes to see and ears to hear, that is, to understand and to obey. But when he says "The Lord hath not given you a heart", rebuking and reproving, he would not say it unless it pertained to their fault, lest anyone think himself excusable on this account. For at once he shows that without the help of God they cannot understand and obey with the eyes and ears of the heart; and yet, if the help of God be lacking, the vice of man is not therefore excusable, since the judgments of God, though hidden, are just.
29.4:

**“to see,”** — understanding
**“and ears that may hear,”** — to obey

29.6:

**“YOU HAVE NOT EATEN BREAD”** — Hence it appears that the Israelites, when they went out of Egypt, carried with them only so much wine as they could quickly consume. For if they had brought none at all, whence would it be said: "The people sat down to eat and drink, and they rose up to play"? For this would not be said of water, since Moses says that that voice was not the beginning of war, but the beginning of wine.

29.18: **“LEST PERHAPS THERE SHOULD BE AMONG”** — AUGUSTINE. The Seventy: "Is there any among you, man or woman, or family or tribe, whose mind turneth aside from the Lord your God, to go and serve the strange gods of those nations? Is there in him a root springing up in gall and bitterness? And it shall be, when he shall hear the words of this curse, that he shall think in his heart, saying: Let holy things be to me", etc. When he says "Is there any among you?", he inquires lest perhaps there be. But if there were, he terrifies him vehemently, lest on hearing the curses he say "They are holy to me", that is, they are not evils to me but holy, that is, propitious and harmless. Let not the sinner destroy together with himself him who is without sin: namely, by persuading such things as he thinks; not that he whom he persuades is wholly without sin, but [without] that one. Similarly it is said: "If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin": namely, this, that they did not believe in him. God also says to Abimelech about the wife of Abraham: "I know that thou didst it with a clean heart"; he did not wish the clean heart of that man to be understood thus, that he was like those of whom it is said: "Blessed are the clean of heart, for they shall see God", but [clean] of that sin which was in question, because, so far as pertained to him, he had not desired to join another man's wife to himself.

**“and his jealousy against that man, and all should light upon him”** — any one of them all, that he be not immune from all
**“the curses that are written in this volume: and should blot out”** — others thus: and shall blot out above every [thing] his name, etc.
29.23:
**“with brimstone,”** — as Sodom and Gomorrha
**“and the heat of the sun,”** — in the days of Achab it rained not for three years and six months
29.29: **“Secret things to the Lord our God:”** — that is, with the Lord our God

30.3: **“will bring back again”** — when the remnant of Israel shall be saved at the preaching of Elias and Enoch
30.6: **“The Lord thy God will circumcise”** — an evident promise of grace; for God promises that he will do what he is wont to help to be done
30.11: **“This commandment”** — THIS COMMANDMENT. AUGUSTINE. The Seventy: "For this commandment which I command thee this day is not beyond measure, nor is it far from thee; it is not in heaven, saying", that is, that thou shouldst say, "nor is it beyond the sea, saying", that is, that thou shouldst say, etc. "The word is very near, that is, in thy mouth and in thy heart and in thy hands, to do it." The Apostle says this is the word of faith, which pertains to the New Testament. The things therefore that are written in the book of this law were spoken in figure, pertaining to the New Testament. But as for what is written, "Nor is it beyond the sea, that thou shouldst say: Who of us shall cross over the sea and receive it for us?", the Apostle said: "Or who shall descend into the deep?", and expounded: that is, to bring up Christ from the dead. But he called the sea the whole life in this world, which is passed over by death, so that in a manner the sea comes to an end; and death itself is called beyond the sea, as being beyond this life which is called the sea. As for what is added, "and in thy hands", the Apostle says only "in thy mouth and in thy heart", and following this to the end he says: "With the heart we believe unto justice, but with the mouth confession is made unto salvation." But in the Hebrew "in thy hands" is not found; yet not in vain did the Seventy add it, because they wished the hands, that is, the works, to be understood in the heart, where there is the faith that worketh by charity. For if [works] be done outwardly with the hands and are not done in the heart, the precepts of God are not fulfilled.
30.14: **“IS NIGH UNTO THEE”** — That is, the commandments of God are measured and tempered to human strength. This can be taken of the incarnation of Christ, who, having assumed humanity, was seen upon earth and conversed among men.
30.15:
**“Consider that I have set before thee this day”** — if thou obey
**“life and good, and on the other hand death”** — if thou despise

31.7:
**“AND MOSES CALLED”** — The words of Moses to Josue signify that Christ distributes the land of the living to each according to his own merits, and fulfils all the promises of God. For he brings the people into the promised land. For under his leadership we enter the heavenly fatherland, who says: "No man cometh to the Father but by me"; and "No man hath ascended into heaven but he that descended from heaven, the Son of man who is in heaven"; for he who is united to him ascends through him.
**“Josue, and said to him before all the multitude of Israel: Take courage, and be valiant:”** — the true Jesus
**“for thou shalt bring this people”** — the Christian seed
**“into the land”** — of the living
**“to their fathers”** — to the patriarchs and prophets
**“swore”** — firmly promised
**“the Lord, and thou shalt divide it”** — to each
**“by lot”** — by the election of divine grace
31.8: **“And the Lord who is your leader, he himself will be with thee:”** — he shows the unity of the Father and the Son; whence: "He that sent me is with me, and he hath not left me alone"
31.9: **“And Moses wrote this law, and delivered it to the priests”** — to whom most of all he committed the keeping of the law; whence: "The lips of the priest shall keep knowledge, and they shall seek the law at his mouth", etc.
31.10:
**“AFTER SEVEN YEARS”** — In which the present life is signified, which revolves in the number seven, or the time of the old law on account of the sabbath. After seven years, then, in the year of remission, the law is commanded to be read in the assembly, because when the observance of the law is completed the spiritual law succeeds. Whence: "When the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman", etc.
**“in the year of remission,”** — of grace; this is the acceptable year of the Lord; whence: "Thou shalt bless the crown of the year of thy goodness"
**“in the feast of tabernacles,”** — namely, of the present Church, in which we do battle for God
31.11: **“When all Israel come together, to appear in the sight of the Lord thy God in the place which the Lord shall choose,”** — of the Church
31.13: **“you are going”** — or, you shall go
31.24: **“Therefore after”** — THEREFORE AFTER, etc. Deuteronomy is entrusted to the Levites, because the Gospel of Christ is stored up through the ministry of true priests in the memory of the Church, which is the ark of the Lord, where the heavenly treasures are stored. There are the two tables of the testament, namely, the books of the law and of the Gospel. There the urn holds the manna, that is, the flesh of Christ, in which is the food of eternal life. There is the rod of Aaron that had blossomed, because there is the priesthood of Christ, which abides for ever or in perpetuity: that it may be there for a testimony against thee. The words of the law are unto salvation for those who keep them, for those who despise them a testimony of contumacy and disobedience. Whence: "There is one that accuseth you, Moses, in whom you trust. For if you did believe Moses, you would perhaps believe me also; for he wrote of me"; and elsewhere: "The word that I have spoken, the same shall judge."
31.25: **“He commanded the Levites,”** — by whom are understood the true priests, bearing up the ark, that is, the Church
31.26:
**“Take this book,”**
• Deuteronomy, that is, the Gospel
• as if [to say]: it is yours to store up the Gospel in the memory of the Church
**“and put it in the side of the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God: that it may be there for a testimony against thee.”** — there is one that accuseth you, Moses, in whom you trust
31.27:
**“For I know thy obstinacy, and thy neck”** — pride
**“most stiff,”** — untameable
**“While I am yet living, and going in with you,”** — so, when Christ conversed in the flesh with the Jews
**“you have always been rebellious”** — saying: Thou hast a devil, and such things
**“against the Lord: how much more when I shall be dead?”** — when Christ was dead according to the flesh, they persecuted the apostles and tried to blot out his name
31.28:
**“Gather unto me all the ancients”** — the wiser; in the old is wisdom
**“of your tribes, and your doctors,”** — to whom the law is to be committed
**“and I will speak in the hearing”**
• understanding
• that they may be inexcusable
• to whom more is committed, more is required of him
**“of them these words, and will call against them heaven”** — the heavenly [ones]
**“and earth to witness,”** — the earthly [ones]
31.29:
**“For I know that, after my death, you will do wickedly, and will quickly turn aside from the way that I have commanded you: and evils shall come upon you in the latter times, when you shall do evil in the sight of the Lord,”** — from whom nothing is hidden
**“to provoke him”** — because by nature mild
**“by the works of your hands.”** — not only by thoughts
31.30: **“MOSES THEREFORE SPOKE”** — The words of Moses are not to be taken simply, because according to the history he reproaches the Israelites, ungrateful to God the bountiful giver, with their faithlessness; allegorically he instructs holy Church; and through tropology he calls to honesty of morals. In the history, then, the truth is to be kept; in the allegory, the mysteries; in the tropology, the usefulness of discipline; that so we may be carried up to heavenly contemplation. Note also what is said: "Moses spoke the words of this canticle", etc., that he who praises God with the mouth may not contradict him in work. For "praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner."

32.1:
**“Hear,”**
• he makes [them] attentive
• "He that hath ears to hear, let him hear"
• with the memory
**“O ye heavens,”**
• the heavenly [ones]
• the greater, who can understand
• HEAR, O YE HEAVENS, etc. In the beginning he calls the greatest elements to witness, that if they neglect the commandments he may punish them convicted by their testimony.
• In Hebrew shamaim, that is, heavens, which is plural and of the masculine gender; but he wished it to be understood in the singular, as we say Thebes and Athens of single cities.
**“AUGUSTINE”** — Hear, O ye heavens, etc. Let the heavens hear the allegory, the earth the history. Some think that heaven and earth are called upon to hear as though they were animate, according to that: "Who looketh upon the earth, and maketh it tremble"; whereas this belongs to the power of God, not to their understanding.
**“the things I speak, let the earth hear”** — the earthly, intent on earthly senses
32.2:
**“Let gather”**
• that is, let it be multiplied like the rain, which has innumerable drops; and the judgments of God are unsearchable
• LET GATHER, etc. He compares the doctrine of the law to rain and dew, because it requires from the hearts of the faithful the shoots of spiritual fruit. For these are the field and vineyard of God. Such is that of Isaias: "As the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and return no more thither, but soak the earth, and water it, and make it to spring", etc.
**“As a shower upon the herb,”** — which it makes to live and grow; so doctrine [makes] the hearts of the hearers, that they may bring forth the shoots of the virtues
32.3:
**“Because the name”** — that is, I will sing the virtues and great works of God
**“I WILL INVOKE THE NAME OF THE LORD”** — He shows what the rain is. For to invoke the name of the Lord is to preach the Gospel, and he who hears and does it will possess the fruit of life.
**“Give ye magnificence”** — to magnify God is to proclaim his majesty with heart, mouth and work
32.4:
**“thy God”** — who is perfect
**“THE WORKS OF GOD ARE PERFECT”** — Whence: "The heavens and the earth were finished, and all the furniture of them." And God finished on the seventh day his work, which is the redemption of the human race; which he showed us when, completing the spiritual sabbath, he rested in the sepulchre.
**“and all”**
• because he does all things with discernment and in order
• that is, all his commandments are just; whence: "The judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves"; and elsewhere: "I have pronounced all the judgments of thy mouth"
**“God is faithful”**
• faithfully fulfilling his promises and his threats
• because he is equity
**“and without any iniquity, just”** — rendering evil to the evil according to their merits
**“and right.”** — by rendering good to the good
32.5:
**“They have sinned against him,”** — because they have degenerated from God the Father
**“THEY HAVE SINNED AGAINST HIM”** — AUGUSTINE. The Seventy: "They have sinned, not to him, blameworthy children." For he who sins does not sin to God, that is, harm him, but himself. But if this is said generally, how is it read: "To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee"? And that of Jeremias: "We have sinned to thee, O Lord, the patience of Israel"; and elsewhere: "Heal my soul, for I have sinned to thee"? It is to be asked also whether to sin to God is the same as to sin against God; whence: "And if a man shall sin against God, who shall pray for him?" I will say what seems to me at present, or at another time so far as God shall help. To sin against God is to sin in those things that pertain to the worship of God; so the sons of Heli sinned. So also one must judge that they sin [against God] who sin against men that pertain to God; whence it is said to Abimelech about Sara: "Therefore I spared thee, that thou shouldst not sin against me." They are said to have sinned to the Lord who do penance for their sin, that he may be glorified in forgiving. Therefore, when David had said: "To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee", he added: "that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged"; whether [this is said] as when the Lord God says: "Judge between me and my vineyard", or is understood of Christ, who alone truly says: "For the prince of this world cometh, and in me he hath not any thing", namely of sin that is worthy of death, "but that the world may know that I love the Father", etc. As if [to say]: even if the prince of this world pursues the lightest sins with the punishment of death, in me he hath not any thing; but arise, let us go hence, that is, that I may suffer; because in suffering I fulfil the will of my Father, I do not pay the penalty of my own sin. As for what Jeremias says, "We have sinned to thee, O Lord, the patience of Israel", it is said simply in [the voice] of penitence, with hope of salvation and pardon. And when it is said, "Heal my soul, for I have sinned to thee", he says this that God may be glorified in forgiving, because his mercy is great upon those who confess and return, who "desireth not the death of the sinner". Hence David, when he was reproved by Nathan, answered: "I have sinned to the Lord." For in a manner the wounded man who submits himself to the physician to be healed seems [to sin] to the physician, that in him the work of medicine may be fulfilled. But in this canticle the prophet foresaw some who would so sin that they would neither do penance nor be willing to return to the Lord to be healed; of whom it is said: "For they are flesh, a spirit that goeth and returneth not." It can also be understood thus: they have sinned, not to him, namely in this, that by their sin they harmed not him, but themselves.
**“and are not his children”** — the unbelievers, who are of their father the devil
**“AND ARE NOT HIS CHILDREN”** — Because they are not of faith. For he gave power to be made the sons of God to those who believe in his name. But to the unbelievers it is said: "You are of your father the devil."
**“in their filth.”**
• idols
• sins; nothing is filthy but sin, for all else is good by nature
**“A wicked generation”**
• in sense and will
• ungrateful for benefits
**“A WICKED GENERATION”** — Of which [it is said] in the Gospel: "A wicked and perverse generation seeketh a sign", etc. And elsewhere: "Ye brood of vipers, who hath shewed you to flee from the wrath to come?"
**“and perverse.”**
• in working
• that is, rendering evil for good
32.6:
**“Is this the return thou makest”** — for benefits
**“Is not”**
• IS NOT, etc. He who is the one God, "creator of all" and founder, of whom and by whom and in whom are all things.
• The order is reversed: for first God created by disposing that it should be; second, he made by forming; third, he possessed by ruling.
**“he thy father,”** — by creation, not by generation
**“that hath possessed thee,”** — he claimed [thee] for himself through faith, errors being driven out
**“and made”** — that is, he formed [thee] to [his] image
**“CREATED THEE”** — He created, when he founded the matter from which [man] could be formed. Foolish then and senseless is he who does not worship his creator and maker with fitting veneration, unmindful of that benefit by which God rescued him from the hand of his enemies and possessed him, led him through the Red Sea, gave manna from heaven; and he, ungrateful, worshipped idols, saying: "These are thy gods, O Israel, that have brought thee out of the land of Egypt."
32.7:
**“Remember”**
• that thou mayst return to God
• in which benefits were given
**“the days of old,”** — when he chose thy fathers to be a peculiar people to himself
**“think upon every generation.”**
• in which he chose Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
• for the liberality of the creator was wanting to none
**“Ask thy father”** — thy forebears
**“THY FATHER”** — The doctor of the law and the preacher of the Gospel, namely, that thou mayst be instructed by his doctrine and example.
**“thy”** — the works of God which he does for thy nation
**“thy elders”** — in the ancients is wisdom, etc.
32.8:
**“When divided”** — in the confusion of tongues
**“WHEN DIVIDED”** — As if [to say]: though the multitude of men is innumerable, yet the Lord chose the children of Israel for his inheritance, to whom he manifested his power and his secrets through the judgments of the law and of the prophets.
**“the Most High the nations: when he separated”** — by scattering them through all lands
**“He appointed”**
• or, he set
• a hyperbole, that is, he appointed as many several nations as there were several persons in the people of Israel, or as many as went into Egypt, that is, seventy
**“HE APPOINTED”** — GREGORY. Another edition: "He set the bounds of the nations according to the number of the angels of God." Where it seems to signify the ministries of angels ordained over the several nations, or even over men, by which they are ruled and defended. Whence: "Their angels always see the face of my Father." For the city of God consists of angels and men, to which as many men ascend as there remained angels there; which can be gathered from this: "He set the bounds of the nations according to the number of the angels of God." We ought therefore to draw something from the imitation of them to the use of our conversation, and to kindle ourselves by emulation to good pursuits, that we may be like those to whom we must ascend. For the distinct conversations of men correspond to the distinct orders of angels, and they ascend into their lot through likeness of conversation.
32.9:
**“BUT THE PORTION”** — When God created all the nations, he chose the Israelites alone, whom he glorified with knowledge [of himself], with signs and miracles.
**“of the Lord is his people:”**
• the faithful [people]
• the new people preferred to the old, as Jacob to Esau, namely, the Church preferred to the synagogue
**“Jacob the lot”** — the lines are fallen unto me in goodly places, etc.
**“of his inheritance.”** — the possession of the inheritance
32.10:
**“HE FOUND HIM”** — Because in Sinai he entered into a covenant with him, gave manna, brought forth water from the rock, provided quails, and in the same wilderness, leading them about for forty years, taught them his precepts.
**“in a desert land,”** — when he freed the Church from error, where there was the horror of idolatry and no mention of God
**“in a place of horror,”** — Arabia
**“and of vast wilderness.”**
• of the Gentile world, which is without God
• by the way of mount Seir
**“HE LED HIM ABOUT”** — Allegorically: by spreading the Church through the whole world, by directing it into the way of his commandments.
**“and taught him:”** — his law and precepts
**“and he kept him”** — most diligently
**“HE KEPT HIM”** — Many were laid low in the desert, but after they had transgressed the commandments of God.
**“as the apple”** — which has in it the light of truth
32.11:
**“As the eagle”**
• Christ
• AS THE EAGLE, etc. The eagle (as they say), when it sees its young fledging, turns them to the sun and nourishes the one that looks upon the rays of the sun with unblinking gaze; if it turns aside its eyes, it neglects it as degenerate. And it urges the young to fly and holds up the weary with its wings. So God invites us to the true sun, has compassion on our infirmities, and holds us up with the wings of grace.
**“AS THE EAGLE”** — The eagle, according to the natural philosophers, named from the sharpness of its eyes, sees so sharply that when it is borne over the seas on unmoving wing, so that it is not open to human sight, it sees the little fish swimming in the sea, and, descending like a missile from an engine, it seizes the prey and draws it with its pinions to the shore. It also beats its fledging young with its wings and urges them to fly. So Christ, exhorting us by words and examples, carries us up to the heights, that we may follow whither he has gone before; whence: wheresoever the body shall be, there shall the eagles also be gathered together. Exalted also above the heavens and withdrawn from human sight, he sees with the eyes of mercy those swimming in the sea of this world, and draws them with the pinions of love to the shore of eternal security; whence: "And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all things to myself."
**“enticing”** — by words and examples
**“ENTICING”** — The Lord urged his people to possess the land of Chanaan, helped them, and protected them from their enemies.
**“her young to fly,”** — whom he cherishes like a hen and gathers under her wings
**“He spread”** — [the wings] of twofold love, and the help of protection
**“his wings, and hath taken him and carried him”** — when on the cross he bore their sins
32.12:
**“The Lord”** — not the idols of the Egyptians as well
**“THE LORD ALONE”** — The Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost are one God. He does not say "the Father alone", lest he exclude the Son or the Holy Ghost, but "the Lord alone", that is, God.
**“leader”** — for them going out of Egypt; for us [going out] of the world, by the incarnate Son
**“was his: and there was not”** — for leadership
**“with him a strange god.”** — the devil, or an idol
32.13:
**“He set him upon high land:”**
• they say the summit of the earth is there, as it were its navel
• The Church, which is sublime in virtue and knowledge. In it the fruit of the fields is eaten, because there the good seed springs up, that is, the word of God. There is the fruit thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold, that each may eat sufficiently according to his capacity.
**“HIGH LAND”** — Palestine, which is mountainous; Egypt is flat and low.
**“that he might eat the fruits of the fields.”** — the abundance of all things
**“THAT HE MIGHT SUCK”** — GREGORY. "That he might suck honey out of the rock, and oil out of the firm rock." This is nowhere read to have been done according to the history; but they sucked honey from the rock, that is, Christ, who saw his deeds, that is, his miracles; and oil from the firm rock, because after his resurrection they were found worthy of the anointing of the Holy Ghost. The rock, while still weak, gave honey, when, still mortal, he showed the sweetness of miracles. The firm rock poured out oil, because after the resurrection, impassible, he gave the gift of holy anointing through the breathing of the Holy Ghost. Whence: "The yoke shall putrefy at the presence of the oil", that is, the dominion of the devil, through the anointing of the Holy Ghost.
**“honey”** — with the sweetness of miracles
**“HONEY”** — Indeed, according to the letter it signifies plenty of all things.
**“out of the rock,”** — Christ still mortal
**“and oil”** — the anointing of the Spirit
**“out of the hardest stone.”**
• Christ now immortal
• others: out of the firm rock
32.14:
**“Butter”**
• it signifies the fertility of the land of promise
• the richness of faith and charity, or solid doctrine
**“of the herd,”** — by the examples of the patriarchs
**“and milk”** — of the Godhead
**“of the sheep”**
• simplicity of mind, or easiness of doctrine
• drawn from the innocence of the fathers as an example
**“with the fat”** — with the richness of charity
**“of lambs,”** — of the sons of the apostles
**“and of the rams”**
• of the apostles, who are leaders of the flock; whence: "Bring to the Lord, O ye children of God: bring to the Lord the offspring of rams"
• of the masters
**“of the breed of Basan.”** — of the richness of the New, namely, Testament, where there is a multitude of knowledge and of virtues
**“OF THE BREED OF BASAN”** — Basan is a region that abounds in cattle because of its pastures; whence it was given "to the Rubenites and Gadites and the half tribe of Manasses", because they had many cattle.
**“AND GOATS”** — Who signify penitents, because they were offered for sin. It is not enough for the faithful to receive the gifts of the virtues unless they strive to repent for what they have committed; whence: "Wash me yet more from my iniquity."
**“And goats”** — He calls goats those who by their example minister the works of penance to others, though they have not committed grave things. For they bewail the sins of thought as though they were deeds.
**“with the marrow of wheat,”** — with the marrow of wheat he heaps up the aforesaid benefits with the greatest gift
**“WITH THE MARROW OF WHEAT”** — Of the body of Christ; whence: "Unless the grain of wheat falling into the ground die, itself remaineth alone."
**“and the blood”** — of which: this is the chalice of the new testament in my blood
**“of the grape might they drink, the purest.”** — without the corruption of falsehood or heresy
32.15:
**“Grew fat”** — by divine bounty
**“GREW FAT”** — As the Jews, fattened with benefits, became idolaters, so some Christians turn the mystery received of the body and blood of the Lord to their own perdition.
**“the beloved,”** — the Israelite or the Christian
**“and kicked:”**
• ungrateful and insolent to his benefactor
• by despising the precepts
**“he grew fat,”** — in knowledge and virtue
**“and thick and gross.”** — multiplied, so that he could not be numbered
**“He forsook”** — after so great benefits
**“God who made him, and departed”** — by following idols
32.16:
**“THEY PROVOKED”** — Some become heretics, others idolaters, who out of their heart fashion idols and abominations for themselves.
**“him”** — with idols or heresies
**“by strange gods,”** — that is, [what follows is] the explanation
**“and with their abominations”** — with idols
32.17:
**“NEW, NEWLY”** — Departing from the worship of God, they found for themselves gods whom their fathers did not worship.
**“come up, whom their fathers worshipped not.”** — the prophets, the apostles
32.18:
**“the God that begot thee”**
• [begot] the Jew through the law and circumcision, the Christian through baptism
• formed
32.19:
**“The Lord saw,”**
• thy turning away
• these evils
**“and to wrath”** — to vengeance
**“was moved:”** — not of himself
**“because his own sons and daughters provoked him.”**
• whom he had chosen as sons and daughters
• each sex
32.20:
**“And he said: I will hide”** — I will withdraw help
**“AND HE SAID: I WILL HIDE”** — Nothing is heavier than to be deprived of the sight of God; whence: "Cast me not away from thy face"; likewise: "Turn not away thy face", etc.
**“face”** — knowledge, goodwill
**“my from them, and will consider”** — I will not have mercy
**“their last end”**
• I will wait [to see] to what end they come
• the torments
**“for it is a perverse generation,”**
• rendering evil for good
• in will and in working
**“and unfaithful”** — not keeping the faith promised to God
**“children.”** — like their fathers
32.21:
**“They have provoked me”** — by worshipping idols
**“THEY HAVE PROVOKED ME”** — As if [to say]: as they angered me by worshipping a multitude of false gods and rejecting me, so I will anger them by taking up a multitude of nations and rejecting them.
**“with that which was no god, and have angered [me] with their vanities:”** — with superstitions
**“I WILL PROVOKE”** — By handing them over to the nations, which once were not a people but now are the people of God. Similarly Christians who, having forsaken the truth, turn aside to errors are handed over to the malignant spirits who lost the angelic dignity; who are well called a foolish nation, hating justice, loving iniquity.
**“them with that which is no people,”** — because they do not know the Lord, who truly is
32.22:
**“A fire”** — as if my vengeance were already burning
**“A FIRE IS KINDLED IN”** — GREGORY. Of those whom scourges condemn and do not deliver it is written: "Thou hast struck them, and they have not grieved", etc. For these the scourges begin in this life and will remain for ever; whence Moses: "A fire is kindled from his wrath, and shall burn even to hell beneath." For of the present striking it is said: "A fire is kindled from my wrath"; of the eternal it follows: "and shall burn even to hell beneath". Yet God does not judge twice for the same thing; for it is one scourge, which begins in time and is completed in eternal punishments.
**“my wrath, and shall burn even to the lowest hell.”** — by punishing even for ever
**“And shall devour”** — the reprobate who love earthly things
**“SHALL DEVOUR”** — Another [reading]: "shall eat the earth and what springs from it", that is, the eternal flame burns the flesh for the works of lust. For the things that spring from the flesh are the works of carnal concupiscence, which are fornication, uncleanness and the like.
**“the earth with her increase,”** — with evil works
**“and of the mountains”** — of the proud
**“the foundations”**
• the counsels by which they believed they could sin with impunity
• hope, confidence
**“shall burn.”** — with eternal flames
32.23:
**“I will heap”** — I will permit to be heaped
**“upon them evils,”**
• scourges, which are evil to those who suffer them but good to God, because just
• works, words, thoughts, by which they are punished
• who are to be punished
**“and arrows”** — the wrath of indignation and of vengeance, sharp, so that it pierces even the soul
**“my will I spend”** — through various torments
32.24:
**“They shall be consumed with famine,”** — of the word of God, and with the barrenness of good works
**“and shall devour”** — upbraiding their sins
**“them birds”** — the demons, light, unstable
**“with a bite”** — with a cursing mouth
**“BIRDS WITH A BITE”** — Which ate the seed by the wayside.
**“The teeth of beasts”**
• the demons are called beasts because of their ferocity
• THE TEETH OF BEASTS, etc. The beasts and serpents drag the reprobate over the earth with furious teeth when what they first persuaded the carnal by flattering, in order to seduce them, they furiously exact from the sinners, in order to torment them.
**“I will send upon them, with the fury of creatures that trail upon the ground,”** — they are dragged over the earth who are scattered among earthly things
32.25:
**“WITHOUT SHALL LAY WASTE”** — The burning of the eternal fire will torment the body, and the greatness of anguish the mind; whence: "Their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched."
**“them the sword”** — of the enemies
**“and within”** — those shut up in the cities
**“terror: the young man”** — the wanton
**“THE YOUNG MAN AND ALSO”** — That is, no age shall be spared, because idolatry has stained all.
**“that is a virgin”** — barren of good work
**“the sucking child”** — the little one, dull of sense
**“with the man in years.”** — slothful, useless
32.26:
**“I said:”** — I said, [that is,] I did, the city and the people being laid waste
**“Where are they?”** — he asks not from ignorance, but to rebuke the heart
**“I WILL MAKE TO CEASE”** — They were cast out of their land and scattered through the whole world. But generally the sinners will be taken away from the land of the saints, and the memory of them; whence: "Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from the land of the living", etc.
32.27:
**“But”** — what I threatened this
**“for the wrath”** — which is to be put down
**“of the enemies”**
• of the Gentiles
• of the demons
**“I have deferred it:”** — the damnation of wicked Catholics
**“I HAVE DEFERRED IT”** — Lest they should blaspheme my name; and yet I did not take away vengeance.
**“lest perhaps might be proud”** — arrogating to themselves
**“the enemies”** — the demons; "they that trouble me will rejoice when I am moved"
**“their, and should say:”** — attributing it to their own strength
**“hand”** — power
**“Our mighty”** — the Jews being overcome
32.28:
**“A nation”** — of the Jews, or of any of the wicked
**“without counsel”** — of salvation to come
**“they are, and without wisdom.”** — foresight
32.29:
**“O that they would be wise”** — of themselves
**“and would understand,”** — through the doctors
**“and their last end”** — the torments or the rewards
32.30:
**“HOW SHOULD PURSUE”** — He shows how great was the fear of the Jewish nation after they sinned against the Lord, so that one of the enemies put to flight a thousand of them and two ten thousand, that is, a few very many.
**“How should pursue”** — He who acknowledges the greatness of God understands that these things happen not from the weakness of divine power, but by the permission of just judgment.
**“one after a thousand, and two chase ten thousand?”** — as if [to say]: could it have been done so?
**“Was it not, because their God”** — God, who had made [them]
**“had sold”** — handed them over to their enemies
**“them, and the Lord”** — who was able
**“had shut up”** — in the hands of the enemies
**“them.”** — therefore they were punished
32.31:
**“For our God is not”** — who is just and true
**“as the gods”** — idols, false and vain
**“their: and enemies”** — firm testimony from the enemy
**“our”** — not only we
**“are judges.”**
• having experienced the wonders of our God
• of the house of Israel
**“JUDGES”** — Approvers. Even those who worship idols understand that there is one God, who made heaven and earth.
32.32:
**“Of the vineyard”**
• from which it gave Christ bitterness to drink, abusing the benefits of God
• OF THE VINEYARD, etc. It signifies the wickedness of the heretics, who received pure spiritual doctrine from the holy doctors but corrupted it with their venom and perverted it into the bitterness of gall and wormwood.
• Jerusalem is often compared to Sodom and Gomorrha; whence: "Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom" and of Gomorrha, etc.
**“of Sodom”** — not of Sorec
**“The grapes”** — because, turned into bitterness, it meditates on the death of Christ
**“their are grapes of gall, and their clusters most bitter.”** — from which they hanged the true cluster, that is, Christ, on the wood
**“CLUSTERS MOST BITTER”** — That is, the fruits, the works, are most bitter. For they offered wine mixed with gall.
32.33:
**“THE GALL OF DRAGONS”** — As if they keep the venom of malice within themselves, lest they receive the medicine of salvation and correction.
**“The gall of dragons”** — The heretics, like serpents, hide bitterness and venom, that they may harm the unwary.
**“is their wine, and the venom”** — Pliny says the venom of the asp is driven off with vinegar
**“of asps, which is incurable.”** — unless the supreme physician come to the rescue
32.34:
**“Are not these things stored up”** — to be brought forth in the judgment
**“with me,”** — to whom all things are present, therefore there is no forgetting; whence: "Thou hast sealed up my sins as it were in a bag"
**“and sealed up in treasures”** — in eternal memory
**“my?”** — it pertains to me
32.35:
**“REVENGE IS MINE”** — Paul took from this place: "Revenge is mine, and I will repay", namely, according to merits.
**“and I will repay them in due time,”** — in the fitting [time]; let us come before his presence with confession
**“IN DUE TIME”** — As if [to say]: when I shall take a time, I will judge justices. Hence he said to Moses praying for the people: "In the day of revenge I will visit this sin also of theirs."
**“that their foot may slide.”** — the affection
**“At hand is the day”**
• it will come quickly
• certain
**“AT HAND IS THE DAY”** — For each one. For whatever comes to an end is very brief if it is compared with eternity.
**“of destruction,”** — of vengeance
**“and to come”**
• although they seem to be far off in the future
• while others flee
**“the times make haste.”**
• the times to come
• According to the history of the Jews, vengeance makes haste, because in a short time they lost place and nation and all prosperity, because they killed the prophets and the Saviour.
32.36:
**“WILL JUDGE”** — By distinguishing them from the wicked, according to that: "Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause."
**“The Lord his people, and will have mercy on his servants.”** — by giving beatitude through eternal mercy
**“He shall see”** — he will make it to be seen
**“HE SHALL SEE THAT”** — Whatsoever thy hand is able to do, do it earnestly: for neither work, nor reason, nor wisdom shall be in hell.
**“weakened”** — profiting its author nothing
**“is their hand,”** — any works of the wicked, or their multitude, diminished
**“and they who were shut up”**
• besieged
• the Jews shut up in captivity, the wicked in the power of the demons
**“have also failed,”** — by famine, or taken by the enemies
**“and they that remained are consumed.”**
• by death
• others
• who trust in their own strength
32.37:
**“And they shall say:”** — seeing
**“WHERE ARE THE GODS”** — As if [to say]: the idols in which they trusted are of no profit, or riches, or honours, or the pleasures of the world. For they take nothing with them of all their labour.
**“their, in whom they trusted?”** — putting their hope in them
32.38:
**“Let them arise”** — mockery
**“and help you,”** — their worshippers
32.39:
**“See ye”** — understand
**“SEE YE THAT”** — A general admonition: as if [to say]: having left idolatry or heresy and spurned all uncleannesses, be converted to the true God.
**“I”** — properly
**“alone am,”** — God
**“I will kill”**
• the old man with his deeds
• the flesh
**“I WILL KILL”** — GREGORY. He kills that he may quicken, he strikes that he may save, he scourges the outward parts that he may pierce through the inward. For he strikes the hardness of our mind with desire of him, and by striking heals; for he calls us back, pierced with the dart of terror, to the sense of rectitude. For our hearts are unsound when they are wounded by no love of God, when they do not feel the hardship of pilgrimage and have compassion with no affection on an ailing neighbour. But God strikes the insensible with the darts of his love and makes them sensible through the ardour of charity.
**“and I”** — as the Lord of life and death
**“to live”** — the new [man], who is created according to God
**“will make:”** — the mind
**“hand”** — power
32.40:
**“I will lift up”** — I will show my power in the saints
**“I WILL LIFT UP”** — Another edition: "I will lift up my hand into heaven, and I will swear by my right hand, and I will say: I live for ever." To lift or raise the hand of God into heaven is to show the power of his eternity excelling over all things. To swear by the right hand, that is, by the Son, who is the right hand of the Father, is to confirm his promises in the sight of men and to reveal his eternity to those who believe in him through the Gospel, because his power is an everlasting power.
**“I live”** — because I am the life
32.41:
**“If I shall whet”** — that is, if I inflict sudden and inevitable vengeance on the enemies
**“as the lightning”** — openly
**“my sword, and take hold”** — unexpectedly
**“on judgment”** — just retribution
**“my hand”** — the divine power
**“I will render”** — which I shall owe
**“vengeance to the enemies”** — to the heretics, the Jews
32.42:
**“I will make drunk”** — it signifies full vengeance
**“arrows”** — sudden and unforeseen vengeances, which now [lie] hidden but will suddenly pierce the wicked
**“ARROWS”** — The demons, of whom Job says: "The arrows of the Lord are in me." As if [to say]: I will exercise so great vengeance as might suffice even for the demons.
**“my with blood,”** — with the damnation of the lost
**“and my sword”** — the divine sentence
**“shall devour”**
• in the last judgment
• wholly
**“flesh.”**
• those who savour carnal things
• the works of the flesh
**“Of the blood”** — with the eternal death of the damned
**“of the slain, and of the captivity,”**
• their vain counsel being laid open
• Of the captivity, etc. The head of the enemies is laid bare when the counsel of the wicked mind, by which it thought it could sin with impunity, is proved to be vain. The heads of the enemies are also the masters, upon whom the last vengeance will overflow; whence: "Blood came out of the press up to the horses' bridles", that is, the vengeance of torments [will reach] even to the rulers of the peoples.
**“OF THE CAPTIVITY”** — The heads of captives who were sold off were shaven, and they were said to be sold under the crown.
**“of the bare, of the enemies”** — of the captives
**“head.”** — of the mind, or the master
32.43:
**“Praise, ye nations, the people”** — the faithful [people]
**“his: for the blood”** — affliction or martyrdom
**“FOR THE BLOOD”** — In the judgment the people of God will be praised when it appears glorious, and the enemies will be punished with just retribution.
**“of the servants”** — of the saints; whence: "Revenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints"
**“and will render vengeance to their enemies, and merciful”** — pitying
**“he will be to the land”** — to the Church
**“of his people.”** — of the saints
32.46: **“And he said to them: Set”** — that you may understand and hold them in memory
32.49:
**“GO UP INTO THE MOUNTAIN”** — Abarim is interpreted passage; Nebo, in the conclusion. Mount Nebo is said to be in the land of Moab over against Jericho, beyond the Jordan, on the brow of Phasga, near mount Phogor, from which the surrounding region is called Phasga to this day. Moses therefore dies in Abarim and on mount Nebo over against Jericho beyond the Jordan, because the law and circumcision went forward until Christ and the sacrament of baptism, and there were concluded, because the end of the law is Christ. Moses saw the land of promise but did not enter, because in spirit he foresaw and in the law he foretold the grace of Christ to come, but did not see him present; whence: "Many just men and prophets have desired to see the things that you see, and have not seen them."
**“this, Abarim, that is to say, of passages, unto mount Nebo,”** — in the conclusion
**“which is in the land of Moab over against Jericho: and see”** — in spirit
**“the land”** — the future glory of the Church
**“of Chanaan, which I will deliver to the children”** — seeing God
32.50: **“When thou art gone up into it thou shalt be gathered to thy people, as Aaron thy brother died in mount Hor, and was gathered to his people:”** — the saints who went before
32.51: **“Because you trespassed against me in the midst of the children of Israel, at the waters of contradiction in Cades of the desert of Sin: and you did not sanctify me”** — that is, you did not show [me] holy

33.1:
**“THIS IS THE BLESSING”** — Well did he place the blessing at the end of Deuteronomy, because Christ, about to ascend into heaven after the completion of the Gospel, lifted up his hands and blessed his disciples. The blessing with which the children of Israel are blessed in Deuteronomy (which is the second law) pertains to the grace of the New Testament, in which the mysteries of the ancient law are unlocked, and the true Israelites obtain through the man Christ the blessing foretold through Moses, the man of God. And well is the blessing given when Moses' death is at hand, because when the shadow of the law dies, the truth of the heavenly gifts is opened. Moses therefore, foreseeing the coming of the Saviour and setting forth the grace of the New Testament as though past, exults rejoicing with the voice of the primitive Church, saying: "The Lord came from Sinai", etc.
**“AUGUSTINE”** — "This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before he died. And he said: The Lord came from Sinai, and shone forth to us from Seir; he hastened from mount Pharan with many thousands of Cades; at his right hand angels with him; and he spared his people, and all the sanctified are under thy hands, and these are under thee. And he received of his words the law which Moses commanded you, an inheritance for the congregations of Jacob; and there shall be a prince in the beloved, the princes of the peoples being gathered together with the tribes of Israel." This prophecy is not to be passed over carelessly; for it appears that this blessing pertains to the new people, which Christ sanctified.
**“MOSES THE MAN”** — Moses signifies the law, which before its death, that is, before it was ended in Christ, foretold that the Church was to be blessed in Christ.
33.2:
**“And he said: The Lord from Sinai”**
• in which the law was given; because through the law he was joined to the Jews
• Sinai: my jar, or measure, or commandment
**“THE LORD CAME FROM SINAI”** — Sinai is interpreted my jar, or measure, or commandment; Seir, hairy or shaggy; Pharan, their fierceness, or fruitful. Sinai, then, figures the Old Testament, because, holding a fixed measure of commandments according to the decree of the Decalogue, it knows how to forbid, not to help; nor does it set free by the spirit of love, but binds its subjects by fear of punishment. Whence: "The one from mount Sinai, engendering unto bondage", etc. The Lord therefore came from Sinai, that is, he became known to believers from the law and the prophets. For he comes thence when he becomes known there to one who reads and understands; whence: "Beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded to the disciples", to whose hearts he desired to come. He rose from Seir according to the flesh, namely from the Jews, most rough with the thorn-thicket of malice and faithlessness; with the rising of a new light, as the true sun of justice, he enlightened the faithful; whence: "Unto us the sun of justice shall arise"; and elsewhere: "A star shall rise out of Jacob, and a man shall spring up from Israel."
**“came”** — Allegorically. The Lord, etc. Sinai is interpreted temptation. The Lord therefore came from Sinai, because he took our flesh, in which he might be tempted.
**“FROM SEIR HE ROSE UP TO US”** — Which is also Edom, or Esau. This is the people of the Jews, which through the desire of the gullet, as it were for a dish of lentils, lost the glory of the primacy, and, supplanted by the faith of the younger people, lost the grace of the blessing.
**“and from Seir he rose up to us:”** — From Seir he rose up to us, etc. They went round this mountain for a long time, and in it received some precepts. Seir, that is, shaggy or hairy, signifies the Gentile world, which was horrid with sins; from which the Lord rose, because in faith he will be preached to the Jews from the Church of the Gentiles, because the remnant shall be saved.
**“he hath appeared from mount Pharan,”**
• which [is] their fierceness, or fruitful
• From mount Pharan. Pharan [is] their fierceness, or fruitful. Christ therefore appeared from Pharan, because the more the fierceness of the unbelievers blazed against him, the higher grew the knowledge of his divinity. For the more he lay hidden amid the insults of the passion, the more he shone forth through the power of the resurrection; and those who first persecuted him with the fierceness of unbelief afterwards cleaved to him with the ardour of charity; of whom is added: "and with him thousands of saints".
**“HE HATH APPEARED FROM MOUNT PHARAN”** — Which is interpreted fruitful, because from the Church of the Gentiles, fruitful in virtues, the faith of Christ is preached to the Jews.
**“and with him of saints”**
• the primitive Church
• gained through the Church from the Gentiles
**“thousands. In his right hand”**
• that is, to the saints, who, hearing the commandments of God, burn with the fires of love
• In his right hand a fiery law. The right hand is the Gospel, through which eternal beatitude is promised, which is called the right hand; not temporal [beatitude], as in the law, which is called the left; whence: "His right hand shall embrace me." In this right hand is the fiery law, that is, charity kindled by the Holy Ghost in the hearts of the elect; whence it is said: "Love is the fulfilling of the law"; and elsewhere: "A new commandment I give unto you, that you love one another." This, implanted in the apostles by the fiery tongues of the Holy Ghost, wrote the whole fulness of the law as by the finger of God, and made them fervent in spirit and shining in working. But because it was given not to one people, like the law of Moses, but to all, he adds: "He hath loved the people."
**“IN HIS RIGHT HAND”** — Namely, the tables on which [was] the law, which purges and burns away sins. The right hand of the Father is also the Son, who brought the law of charity, saying: "I am come to cast fire on the earth", etc.
**“a fiery”** — he first fulfilled the law of charity
**“law.”** — charity
33.3:
**“He hath loved”** — even unto death
**“HE HATH LOVED”** — "Greater love than this no man hath, that a man lay down his life", etc.
**“the people”** — both, of the circumcision and of the foreskin
**“ALL”** — Without respect of persons. He that feareth him and worketh justice is acceptable to him.
**“the saints”** — ALL THE SAINTS are in his hand: namely, those sanctified in his name, who have heard: "Be ye holy, because I am holy." In the hand, that is, the power, by which they are protected; whence: "No man shall pluck them out of my hand." These through charity are one kingdom in the hand of the Lord; whence Isaias: "And thou shalt be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God."
**“are in his hand:”** — in the power
**“and they that approach”**
• that they may learn humbly; or, who follow his footsteps
• by faith and love
**“to the feet”** — the apostles, evangelists, with whose doctrine the world is filled; whence: "How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace", etc.
**“AND THEY THAT APPROACH TO HIS FEET”** — As if [to say]: let not those who did not hear Christ teaching in the flesh be saddened, as though they were deceived by men. Through the mouth of the saints Christ speaks; through the feet the doctrine of the head is heard. Whence: "He that heareth you heareth me", etc. Or they approach to his feet to receive doctrine who, burning with spiritual desire, keep watch day and night over the evangelical and apostolic Scriptures. But because these things are written of the New Testament, there follows [a passage] in whose voice Moses speaks of the old law, saying: "Moses commanded us a law", etc.
33.4:
**“A law”**
• the Gospel
• the voice of the people
**“commanded”** — it did not help, did not justify; rather, by commanding it made transgressors
**“us Moses,”** — Christ, obeying whom they received the heavenly inheritance
**“THE INHERITANCE”** — As if [to say]: this is the usefulness of the law, the inheritance promised to Abraham: "If you be willing, and will hearken to me, you shall eat the good things of the land."
**“of the multitude”**
• of the multitude of believers there was one heart and one soul
• which, namely, having obtained the blessing of grace, is freed from the curse of the law
33.5:
**“AND HE SHALL BE WITH THE MOST RIGHT”** — Jacob, blessed by the angel, was called Israel, that is, upright of God and seeing [God]; [so the people], converted to the faith and blessed after the resurrection by him over whom it prevailed in the passion, is called most right on account of the perfection of justice; whence: "Hear, O Jacob my servant, and thou most righteous whom I have chosen."
**“KING”** — Christ. "But I am appointed king by him"; that is, that he who is the first king and power may make a kingdom and power.
**“being assembled”** — into the truth of the faith
**“the princes of the people”** — the apostles and their followers
**“WITH THE TRIBES”** — Of which [was] the primitive Church. Well are the princes said to be gathered first, then the tribes, because first the apostles [believed], afterwards others believed through them.
33.6:
**“LET RUBEN LIVE, AND NOT DIE”** — Having foretold the salvation of the primitive Church, he gives proper blessings to the several tribes, foretelling the true Israelites from both peoples; he prophesies now of Christ, now of the apostles, now of the primitive [Church], now of the whole Church.
**“Let Ruben live, and not die,”**
• Let Ruben live, and not die. As if [to say]: although Ruben violated his father's bed and lost the dignity of the firstborn, yet let him live, and doing penance not die. The sons of Ruben, that is, the Jews signified by Ruben, violated the father's bed, that is, defiled Christ his Son with unclean spittle; they are kept for penance, but few in number in comparison with the Church of the Gentiles.
• Ruben, son of vision, because his mother said: "God saw my affliction." He is the firstborn, signifying the elect from the Jews, who, dead through denying and crucifying Christ, were converted by the preaching of the apostles and quickened by faith in Christ. These are sons of vision, because they are saved by the regard of divine mercy.
**“and be he small in number.”** — in regard of the unbelievers; but in faith very great and glorious
33.7:
**“THIS IS THE BLESSING OF JUDA”** — Juda, who is interpreted confession and thanksgiving, signifies the universal Church, in which is the confession of divine praise and thanksgiving; of which his mother says: "Now will I praise the Lord." This is the true bride of Christ, who, adorned with the necklaces of the virtues, is not proud but gives thanks. For her he prays that she may be heard.
**“This is the blessing of Juda.”** — The blessing of Juda: namely, of the kings who were of Juda, who longed for Christ, and of Christ himself, who says: "I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth", etc.
**“Hear, O Lord,”** — of holy desire; of which: "I cried to the Lord with my voice"
**“the voice of Juda,”**
• of Christ
• of the Church praising
**“and unto his people”**
• the Gentile [people], namely, which is to be saved
• the patriarchs, prophets, apostles, through whom the Church was begotten
**“bring in”**
• that he may hear: "Enter thou into the joy of thy Lord"
• many shall come from the east and the west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven
**“him: the hands”** — power, working
**“his”** — of Christ
**“shall fight”** — on the cross, against the powers of the air
**“HIS HANDS SHALL FIGHT”** — He prayed the Lord for Juda, to whom he now promises the help of the Lord: as if [to say]: let not Juda presume on his own strength, but trust in him who says: "Have confidence, I have overcome the world"; whose hands fought on the cross against the spirits of wickedness, that through death he might destroy him who had the empire of death.
**“for him,”** — Juda, or the people
**“HELPER”** — That he may conquer and say: "He will lead me upon my high places, the conqueror." For he himself conquers in us, and for his own victory crowns us with mercy and compassion.
**“of him against his enemies”** — the demons, or any whatsoever
**“he shall be”** — to Christ and the choir of the perfect
33.8:
**“To Levi also he said: perfection”** — of which: "If thou wilt be perfect, go sell", etc.
**“THY PERFECTION”** — As if [to say]: how perfect thou art and how holy thy doctrine, thou hast declared through Moses; or, to thy holy man, that is, to the Levites, be thy perfection and thy doctrine. For they ought to keep, do and teach the law.
**“thy”** — Thy perfection, etc. These things are said to the choir of the angels and martyrs and of all the perfect, who fulfilled the perfection of charity by dying for the Lord, and, renouncing the world, attained the summit of ecclesiastical doctrine, as true Levites having no part on earth, but saying with the prophet: "The Lord is the portion of my inheritance"; according to that: "If any man will come after me, let him deny himself", etc.; and elsewhere: "He that shall lose his life for me", etc. But Christ is the true Levite, who did and taught all these things. To him the Levites cleave, imitating him even to blood; of whose passion it is added: "whom thou hast proved in the temptation", etc.
**“and doctrine”**
• Jesus began to do and to teach
• the evangelical [doctrine]
**“thy be to thy holy man, whom”** — the body of Christ, that is, the Church
**“thou hast proved”**
• O Father
• because he was proved in all things
**“in the temptation,”** — of tribulation, both when he was tempted by the devil in the desert and in the passion
**“AT THE WATERS OF CONTRADICTION”** — It is the place where he denied Moses and Aaron entrance into the land of promise.
**“and judged at the waters of contradiction:”** — The waters [are] the peoples who, gainsaying, cried out: "Crucify him"; "His blood be upon us and upon our children." To heap up the perfection of Levi he adds: "Who hath said to his father and to his mother", etc.
33.9:
**“Who hath said to his father”**
• to those who hinder the course of the mind
• In avenging idolatry they did not, as it were, know their own, because they killed without distinction.
• Unless he leave father and mother and wife and children for me, he is not worthy of me.
• Who hath said to his father, etc. We ought in temporal things also to profit more those to whom we are more nearly joined; we ought to acknowledge the bond of earthly kinship; but if it hinders the course of the mind, to ignore it; so that affection may fill the heart, but not turn it from the spiritual purpose. This the kine well hint at, which, going toward the hill country under the ark of the Lord, walk on with affection and with rigid sense: going on, they lowed for their calves, but having taken the road they did not turn aside their steps.
**“WHO HATH SAID TO HIS FATHER”** — When they made the golden calf, at Moses' command the Levites, girded with swords, killed the idolaters from gate to gate.
