**“and to his mother:”** — to those who lessen the force of divine charity
**“I do not know you; and to his brethren: I know you not:”** — wishing to be sons of God
**“and their own children they have not known.”**
• estranged from the world
• truly
• the word of God made to thee
**“These have kept thy word, and thy covenant”** — which the Lord made with thee
33.10:
**“Thy judgments,”** — which God judged in thee
**“O Jacob,”** — of the active [man]
**“and thy law,”** — the Decalogue, or charity
**“O Israel:”** — of the contemplative [man]
**“they shall put incense”**
• the incense of prayer and of good work
• MYSTICALLY. They shall put incense. The prayer of the saints [is] most sweet to the Lord in heaven, by which the wrath of the Lord against a sinning people is softened. For, cleansed from all earthly filth, that is, kindled with heavenly desire, it burns as incense in the sight of God, and as a holocaust it rises from the altar of the devout heart to heaven in the flame of devotion. This befits especially the apostles and martyrs, of whom it is said: "As gold in the furnace he hath proved them, and as a victim of a holocaust he hath received them."
**“THEY SHALL PUT INCENSE”** — As Aaron, standing between the dead and the living, prayed for the people.
**“in wrath”** — by appeasing
**“thy”** — themselves, kindled with the flame of charity
**“and holocaust upon the altar”** — the faith, the devotion of the heart
33.11:
**“Bless, O Lord,”** — by rewarding his unconquered patience with the glory of heaven
**“his strength, and the works of his hands”** — "the labours of thy hands, for thou shalt eat", etc.
**“RECEIVE”** — As if [to say]: as pleasing, that thou mayst reward them. Now white robes are given to each, namely the joy of souls; and in the judgment, immortality having been received according to the body, they shall shine as the sun, and as sparks among the reeds they shall run to and fro, burning up, namely, the empty and unfruitful adversaries, of whose punishment it is added [what follows].
**“Strike”**
• with eternal punishment
• that turning their backs they may flee
**“STRIKE THE BACKS”** — MYSTICALLY. As if [to say]: they seemed to shed the blood of the martyrs with impunity, but as it were behind their back an unforeseen punishment was being prepared, that is, eternal damnation, into which, rushing, they will not be able to rise; whence: "A rod for the back of the unwise."
**“of the enemies”** — who neglected to foresee
**“his, and them that hate him”** — when they have fallen
33.12:
**“And to Benjamin”** — whom Jacob loved tenderly
**“AND TO BENJAMIN”** — He seems to allude to the history, because the patriarch and prophet Jacob, full of the Spirit, loved Benjamin uniquely; and by the dispensation of God the place given over to divine worship is decreed to be kept by his tribe; whence he adds: "as in a bride chamber all the day", etc.
**“he said: The best beloved”** — Christ
**“of the Lord”**
• of the Father, or of God
• Otherwise. Benjamin, called son of the right hand instead of son of sorrow, expresses Paul, made from a persecutor an apostle and a vessel of election; for he was of this tribe. And it was fitting that, as the forerunner of the Lord was foretold by prophetic oracle, so the master of the Gentiles, who was to profit the whole world, should be foretold among the great mysteries of the Church. In his mind Christ dwelt confidently, when amid innumerable perils he preached him constantly before Gentiles and kings; of whose soul it is said: "as in a bride chamber he shall abide all the day": either enjoying with wondrous delight a spiritual marriage and making it fruitful with the offspring of the virtues, leaving the secret place of that most peaceful breast to no disquiet of vice; or, residing in it as in a bride chamber, as a beautiful bridegroom he joins to his embraces, through his preaching, the virgin minds of believers. Whence: "After her shall virgins be brought to the king." He himself also says: "For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ."
• The Godhead also dwells confidently in the humanity of Christ. "He shall abide in the bride chamber" signifies that in the womb of the virgin the Church was joined to the heavenly bridegroom, the Church which rests confidently in the strength of Christ's power and in his works.
**“THE BEST BELOVED OF THE LORD”** — ALLEGORICALLY. Christ is the best beloved of God the Father, who says of him: This is my beloved Son. He dwelt confidently at the right hand of the Father, to whom it is said: "Sit thou at my right hand."
**“shall dwell”** — "sit thou at my right hand"
**“confidently in him:”** — in the humanity of Christ, or in the mind of Paul
**“as in a bride chamber”**
• the temple of Jerusalem
• the Church
**“all the day long”** — never at any time estranged by any vice
**“shall he abide”** — God
**“and between the shoulders”** — the good works of the Church
**“BETWEEN THE SHOULDERS”** — Burdens are carried on the shoulders; therefore in them robust patience is designated. And the more gladly Christ rested in him, the harder the labours he bore for him; the more closely he embraced him, the less was he torn by any terror from his embrace; whence he says: "Who then shall separate us from the love of Christ?"
33.13:
**“TO JOSEPH ALSO”** — ALLEGORICALLY. Joseph is interpreted increased. This is Christ, who, cast off by the Jews his brethren, was made prince in the Egypt of this world, and freed the human race from the want of famine by the dispensing of the Gospel corn, who is truly the saviour of the world.
**“OF THE BLESSING OF THE LORD”** — According to the letter it signifies the fertility which the two tribes from Joseph, that is, Ephraim and Manasses, had in plenty of crops and fruits and in pasture of cattle. This is Basan, a most fertile region, whence it is interpreted fatness.
**“he said: Of the blessing of the Lord”** — "Lord, thou hast blessed thy land", [that is,] the Church, namely, which is filled not by its own virtue but divinely by the blessing of the virtues; whence: "Blessed be the God who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in Christ."
**“be his land, of the fruits”**
• with the fragrant fruits of the virtues, with which the Church is filled; whence: "I have appointed you, that you should go, and should bring forth fruit"
• Men delight in the mildness of the sky and the dew, in fruits, and in the abundance of springs and rivers, which are signified in the deep.
**“OF HEAVEN”** — The Apostles and Evangelists are called heaven on account of the unity of faith and doctrine; of whom it is said elsewhere in the plural: "The heavens show forth the glory of God", etc. For in them, shining in life and contemplation, God dwells as in heaven, thundering terror, raining consolation, flashing with miracles.
**“THE DEW”** — With the heavenly preaching, which is of wondrous fineness and grace, by which hearts are watered against the heat of temptation, that they may ever be green with virtues; whence: "God give thee of the dew of heaven", etc.
**“THE DEEP THAT LIETH BENEATH”** — That is, that it may become richer, watered from a rising spring as the paradise of God; whence: "A spring rose out of the earth, watering all the surface of the earth"; and elsewhere: "His thoughts are more vast than the sea, and his counsels more deep than the great ocean." For in vain does the word of the teacher water outwardly unless the grace of the creator water inwardly; whence he adds: "of the fruits of the hills", etc.
33.14:
**“Of the fruits”**
• which the heat of the sun and the moisture of the moon nourish
• of spiritual goods
**“OF THE SUN”** — Of Christ, who is the sun of justice, who says: "The just shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of their Father", because we shall be like him.
**“AND OF THE MOON”** — Of the Church, which receives these fruits from the sun, that is, from Christ. Let her therefore always look upon the sun with full devotion, lest at some time, turned away, she lose the light.
33.15:
**“Of the tops of the ancient mountains,”** — of the patriarchs, prophets, who are lofty in life and contemplation
**“of the fruits of the hills”** — it signifies a noble and famous land
**“OF THE FRUITS OF THE HILLS”** — The everlasting hills are the faithful of the Old Testament, who, humble sons, were founded with immovable firmness in the faith of the prophets and patriarchs (whence: "The mountain of the house of the Lord shall be exalted above the hills"); with whose fruits the land of Joseph is blessed when the Church of Christ bears fruit in faith by the doctrine of prophecy and the example of virtue. And note that above, in the fruits and dew of heaven, the doctrine of the Gospel is signified; here, in the tops of the ancient mountains and the fruits of the everlasting hills, the doctrine of the law and the prophets; and with both the land of Joseph is enriched, because holy Church is formed by the pages of both testaments and by the examples of the new and the old fathers. Whence: "All fruits, my beloved, new and old, I have kept for thee"; and every scribe instructed brings forth out of his treasure new things and old. The Manicheans therefore and the Jews (because those do not receive the Old Testament, these the New) cannot inherit in this rich land.
33.16:
**“AND OF THE FRUITS OF THE EARTH”** — The Church in the whole world, fruitful with the crop of justice and the bounty of the charisms, received of the fulness of her Joseph; whence it follows: "The blessing of him", etc.
**“and of the fulness thereof. The blessing”** — in thy seed shall all the nations be blessed
**“of him”** — of God
**“THE BLESSING OF HIM”** — The whole Joseph, that is, head and body, [is] full of blessing; but the fulness of blessing [is] chiefly in the head; whence: "Like the ointment on the head, that ran down to the beard, the beard of Aaron", etc. He, excelling his brethren, that is, the faithful, by the privilege of grace, with the sevenfold Spirit, as a true Samson, a Nazarite from the virgin's womb, that is, consecrated to God, shone forth as with seven untouched locks.
**“that appeared”** — not in his own substance but through an angel
**“OF JOSEPH”** — Of Christ, who is the head of the Church, in whom all nations are blessed; of whose passion and resurrection it is added: "As of the firstling of a bullock", etc.
**“and upon the crown of the Nazarite”** — that is, of Christ, who is the flower of the stock of David and the offspring of pure chastity
33.17:
**“AS OF THE FIRSTLING OF A BULLOCK”** — AUGUSTINE. "The firstling of a bull is his beauty": it is not to be read so that it says "of the firstborn bull"; but since he is the firstborn, his beauty is that of a bull, because of the horns of the cross.
**“as of the firstling of a bullock”** — Christ [is] the fatted calf, the firstborn from the herd of the fathers, whom the Father sacrificed when the son returned; who, raised on the third day, appeared glorious; who is the firstborn of the dead and the prince of the kings of the earth. After the glory of the resurrection he adds the horns, from the power of the passion.
**“His beauty, the horns”** — it signifies the singular principality of the tribe of Ephraim
**“THE HORNS”** — He compares Joseph to the horns of a rhinoceros, signifying that Ephraim would have the principality among the ten tribes, over which Jeroboam of the tribe of Ephraim reigned in the time of Roboam the son of Solomon.
**“of a rhinoceros”** — strong, unconquerable
**“his horns”**
• of the cross, in which the ram was caught
• THE HORNS OF A RHINOCEROS, HIS HORNS, etc. It signifies the horns of the cross, of which Habacuc says: "There is his strength hid." For through the weakness of the flesh, as a ram, he is crowned with the thorns of the mockers. In these horns he was caught; but by the incomparable strength of the passion he stood forth as the unicorn, victor over death and over him who had the empire of death. Whence: "The weakness of God is stronger than men."
**“with them”** — the hearts
**“shall he push”** — that he may spread the Church to the ends of the earth
**“SHALL HE PUSH”** — By the preaching of the cross, separating the chaff from the wheat; for the word of the cross is foolishness to them that perish.
**“THE NATIONS”** — Ask of me, and I will give thee the nations for thy inheritance. For all these things are said of the inheritance of the true Joseph, which is the renowned land; of whose tillers, gathered from both peoples, it follows: "These are the multitudes of Ephraim."
**“These”** — many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband
**“are the multitudes”** — innumerable
**“of Ephraim,”**
• of the fruitful one; "the labours of thy hands, for thou shalt eat"
• of the Gentile people, preferred to the Jewish
**“THESE ARE THE MULTITUDES OF EPHRAIM”** — These two tribes from Joseph are blessed not in themselves but in their parent. They signify the sons of both peoples, who are blessed in Christ, according to that: "In thy seed shall all the nations be blessed." The patriarch Jacob, blessing these, Ephraim and Manasses, with hands crossed in the form of a cross, and preferring the younger to the firstborn, signified that they were to be blessed in the faith of the cross of Christ: in the younger, the faithful people from the Gentiles, [unclear in the edition: "in Christi patria"] younger in time but greater in faith, to which the grace of the Israelite people passed; of whose inestimable multitude it is said: "These are the multitudes of Ephraim", etc. Whence: "Many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband." Manasses, deprived of the honour of the firstborn and yet blessed, is the Jewish people, which, rejected for unbelief in its greater part, yet in its remnant obtained the blessing; whence: "Blindness in part has happened in Israel."
**“and these the thousands”** — he sets a fixed number, because few of the Jews are saved
**“of Manasses.”** — of the Jewish people, which lost the birthright
33.18:
**“AND TO ZABULON HE SAID”** — Zabulon and Issachar received their possession in Galilee, where Christ taught most, whence he chose the apostles. By them therefore the apostles are designated, and joy is promised them in their going out, because, going out from their borders, they subjected the people of the Gentiles to Christ; and in the tabernacles, for the conversion of the Jews, from whom they themselves also were chosen. For both peoples, then, present and future joy is promised them, because in the present they rejoiced at their conversion and in heaven they were rewarded with eternal joy.
**“Rejoice, O Zabulon, in going out”**
• from the captivity of Egypt, or of the devil
• from the Jews to the Gentiles
**“thy”** — their sound hath gone forth into all the earth
**“and Issachar in tabernacles”** — as secure and quiet in the land of promise
**“IN TABERNACLES”** — Of the Jews; whence: "May God enlarge Japheth, and may he dwell in the tents of Sem", because the breadth of the younger people dwells in the churches of the Jews through the unity of faith.
33.19:
**“the people”** — both
**“to the mountain”**
• Christ. "Come and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord"
• who is the corner stone
**“TO THE MOUNTAIN”** — Namely, Sion, or Jerusalem, or contemplation and the height of the virtues.
**“they shall call”** — in Christ
**“THEY SHALL CALL”** — Teaching that justice is only in the faith of Christ; for the end of the law is Christ, unto justice to every one that believeth. On the mountain they sacrifice the victims of justice when they teach all who come to Christ, in whom the Church is built, that they are justified not by the works of the law but by the faith of Christ, according to that: "But the just man liveth by faith." True Christians, then, are the victims of justice, which are sacrificed by the apostles when they are taught to mortify earthly desires, that they may be quickened by the spiritual. Whence: "If by the Spirit you mortify the deeds of the flesh, you shall live."
**“there shall they sacrifice”** — teaching to mortify earthly desires
**“THERE SHALL THEY SACRIFICE”** — There is no place of true sacrifice outside the Catholic Church, which is set upon this mountain.
**“the victims of justice.”** — of praise: in me, O God, are thy vows, which I will pay, praises to thee
**“who”** — the apostles
**“the abundance”**
• the peoples flowing together to the faith
• Who the abundance of the sea, etc. It signifies the calling of the Gentiles. For the sea signifies the whole race of men; whence: "The kingdom of heaven is like to a net cast into the sea, and gathering together of all kind of fishes." The sea is the world, the net doctrine; by every kind of fish is understood every sex, age and condition. The apostles therefore sucked the abundance of the sea as milk, because they drew the crowds of peoples flowing together to the doctrine of the Gospel into the increase of the body of Christ.
**“WHO THE ABUNDANCE”** — These tribes gave themselves to trade, bringing back merchandise from lands beyond the sea, and hidden treasures, namely silver, gold or gems; they shall suck them as milk, that is, receive them easily.
**“of the sea”** — of the human race
**“as milk”** — the change of the right hand of the most High: sweet milk is sucked from the bitter sea
**“shall suck, and the treasures”** — they will pass into the body of Christ, that is, the Church
**“HIDDEN, OF THE SANDS”** — The Lord knoweth who are his. For many are called, but few chosen.
**“hidden, of the sands.”** — The sands are the multitude of the unbelievers; the treasures, the precious souls of the elect. So, then, they sucked, that of the hearers of the Gospel some, as vessels unto honour, are carried over into the treasures of the king; others, as barren and useless sands, remain empty.
33.20:
**“AND TO GAD HE SAID”** — In the blessing of Gad he seems to foretell the might of the strong men or judges who were of that tribe, as Jephte and many others.
**“IN HIS BREADTH”** — Because all the fulness of blessing rested upon Christ, whence he blessed his own.
**“GAD”** — That is, girded; it signifies Christ, who, about to fight against the spirits of wickedness, appeared in the weakness of the flesh girded with the power of the Godhead, according to that: "The Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself"; and elsewhere: "The Lord who is strong and mighty", etc. He is blessed in breadth, because he received a most ample kingdom not among the Jews alone but among all the nations. Thence the prophet says: "From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, the name of the Lord is worthy of praise." But because he came to this glory through the humility of the passion, he adds concerning his death: "as a lion", etc.
**“HE HATH RESTED AS A LION”** — "I have power to lay down my life", etc. The power of death, not its necessity, is expressed; whence: "No man taketh it away from me: but I lay it down."
**“he hath rested as a lion,”** — As a lion he roared. For whatever he said he fulfilled with power. He seized the arm when, rising from the dead, he subjected to himself the strength of his enemies. He seized also the top of the head, that is, he bowed the loftiness of worldly empire to receive the faith. Whence: "All kings shall adore him: all nations shall serve him." There follows, concerning the new state of his kingdom: "And he saw his pre-eminence."
33.21:
**“AND HE SAW”** — Kingdoms and nations being subjected to him, his power appeared, not by the terror of arms but by the power of doctrine.
**“WAS LAID UP”** — Hidden, while he writes his laws in the hearts of the faithful; whence John says: "You have the unction from the Holy One", "and you have no need that any man teach you; his unction teacheth you of all things." Or laid up, because in the law and the prophets he lay hidden and taught in figures; hidden, because he declared it openly in the Gospel. Whence: "Beginning at Moses and all the prophets, he expounded to them."
**“WHO WAS WITH THE PRINCES”** — A helper. Whence: the Lord working withal, and confirming the word with signs that followed; who says: "Without me you can do nothing."
**“AND DID”** — That is, justifying those who believe in him; and at last he will judge according to merits with Israel, that is, with the people chosen for the vision of God.
**“THE JUSTICES”** — The justifications of believers. He himself justifies the ungodly by faith. For by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified.
33.22:
**“TO DAN ALSO HE SAID”** — Some think the Antichrist is signified by Dan, who they reckon will be born of this tribe. He is the lion's whelp, that is, [the whelp] of the devil, who shall flow plentifully from Basan, because he is full of confusion. For Basan is interpreted confusion, or fatness, or locust.
**“To Dan also he said:”** — Dan also [is] judgment; Basan, ignominy. But Dan signifies Christ, who says: "For judgment I am come into this world." A lion's whelp, because of his strength, and because he deigned to become a little one. But taking on our weakness, he did not lose his power; for the weakness of God is stronger than men. Of him it is said: "The lion of the tribe of Juda hath prevailed", etc. He bore indeed the ignominy of the cross from the Jews, who thought his name would be blotted out through death. But he who through the weakness of the flesh was a whelp in the passion appeared through the power of the Godhead as an unconquered lion in the resurrection; whence the Apostle: "For although he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God." So, as it were, he flowed plentifully from Basan when, coming through the ignominy of death to the glory of immortality, he watered the whole world with the streams of the Gospel. Whence Isaias: "The earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the covering waters of the sea."
**“A YOUNG LION”** — He says this because of Samson, who was of the tribe of Dan, and as a strong lion; whose possession [reached] as far as Basan. But the Antichrist shall flow plentifully from Basan, because he will be glutted with the fatness of luxury and of all vices.
33.23:
**“HE SHALL POSSESS THE SEA AND THE SOUTH”** — Because his possession reaches from the southern part westward as far as the Tyrrhenian sea.
**“And to Nephtali he said: Nephtali shall enjoy abundance, and shall be full of the blessings of the Lord: he shall possess the sea and the south.”** — The sea, etc. For through the apostles the Church is gained for Christ from Jews and Gentiles. By the western sea (for this is what is understood) the Jews are figured, who serve the shadow and the pattern and have not the light of knowledge and truth. And because the sun of justice set for them, they remained in perpetual darkness. This west the Apostles possessed when they subjected to Christ very many of them, enlightened by the grace of faith, that they who were heretofore darkness might be light in the Lord. In the south is understood the Church gathered from the Gentiles, which, the veil of the law being taken away, enjoys the light of the Gospel, and, lying with the bridegroom at midday, with open face contemplates the glory of God.
33.24:
**“TO ASER ALSO HE SAID”** — Aser [is] blessed: namely Christ, the hope of our blessedness, the firstfruits of which he showed us rising from the dead. He is blessed in children, because those who believe, reborn through his grace, have filled the whole world with his likeness; to whom it is said: "Believe in the light, that you may be the children of light." They bring forth the fruit of light in all goodness and justice and truth. And this came about because he pleased his brethren, that is, the apostles, whom he chose from Judea, with true charity, so that, spurning the figures, they rejoiced in the truth of the Gospel and that they were accounted worthy to suffer reproach for the name of Jesus. And whence they had so great abundance of charity he adds: "Let him dip his foot in oil."
**“LET HIM DIP IN OIL”** — Christ our head, ascending into heaven, while yet standing on earth anointed most copiously with the oil of the Holy Ghost the apostles, namely his feet, who were to go about the world preaching, that they might fail in no labour, but be strong in the brightness of unfading joy. He provided also the incorruptible protection of a shoe, of which it is added: "His shoe shall be iron and brass."
33.25:
**“HIS SHOE SHALL BE IRON AND BRASS”** — GREGORY. This is said of the Church under the figure of Aser. The shoe [is] the protection of preaching; whence: "Your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace." Iron is understood as power, brass as perseverance. Iron and brass are called the shoe of the Church, whose preaching is protected by sharpness and constancy. For by iron it pierces what opposes it; by brass it keeps with long-suffering the testimonies that it sets forth. By iron indeed is signified the firmness or hardness of the ancient law, which, like iron that subdues all metals, either tamed the stubborn by the rigour of justice in rebuking them or punished them by crushing them; as the power of Christ also is compared to an iron rod, who testifies of the firmness of the law: "It is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fall." In brass, which is not marred by rust, grows stronger with age, and is the most resonant among metals, the doctrine of the Gospel is expressed, sounding far and wide, and, stripped of the oldness of the letter, it is strong, inviolate, in the newness of the spirit. For this is the everlasting Gospel. With these shoes the true Pasch is to be celebrated.
**“AS THE DAYS”** — It signifies that this tribe abounded in prosperity and delights until the old age of the captivity.
**“his. As the days”** — As the days of thy youth, etc. To the Church is promised a fresh and green old age, that, as in the beginning she bravely overcame all assaults, so when the end is at hand she may overcome the fury of the Antichrist. Whence: "I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the world"; and elsewhere: "My old age in plentiful mercy."
33.26:
**“THERE IS NO OTHER GOD”** — Marvelling at the things said above, he bursts forth rejoicing in the praise of Christ, who did all things.
**“HE THAT IS MOUNTED UPON THE HEAVEN”** — He ascended by his own power, and daily draws the Church to himself. "Draw me: we will run after thee to the odour of thy ointments."
**“is thy helper. By his magnificence”** — not their own
**“run hither and thither”** — by preaching through the world
**“the clouds”** — whose conversation is in heaven
**“THE CLOUDS”** — The Apostles, who rain with words and flash with miracles; whom, ascending into heaven, he sent to preach; whence: "The clouds sent out a sound." They, namely, run hither and thither with nothing delaying them, doing signs and wonders not by their own power but by Christ's, and as it were terrifying the hearts of mortals with lightnings; whence: "I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course."
33.27:
**“HIS DWELLING”** — The body raised from the dead and placed at the right hand of the Father; of which it is said: "Destroy this temple."
**“is above,”** — in heaven
**“and underneath”** — on earth
**“the arms”**
• the power by which he frees the good and condemns the wicked
• he is overcome not by thy strength, but by the might of the arms
**“THE ARMS”** — Namely, the power of the passion, which defends all, which he received on the cross with arms outstretched. Underneath the arms, namely: these arms defend those who fight against the true Amalec; they are not weighed down with weariness like those of Moses, but lift them up with unwearied power until they attain the true victory. Let us then venerate on high the firstfruits of our resurrection, below the sacrament of our redemption, that we too, the adversary being vanquished, may obtain the glory of immortality; of which it is promised to the true Israel: "He shall cast out the enemy from before thee."
**“everlasting: he shall cast out”** — into the exterior darkness
**“the enemy from before thee.”** — the devil and his body
**“And shall say”**
• the God of peace shall crush Satan under your feet
• he will cause him to be crushed
33.28:
**“shall dwell”**
• the chaff being separated into the fire
• in the land of promise
**“Israel”** — the people of the elect, seeing God face to face
**“in safety,”** — because there is no falling there, no snares
**“and alone.”** — he shows how the true Jacob fares there
**“ALONE”** — Living, namely, after its own manner and by its own laws. Whence Balaam: "The people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations."
**“THE EYE OF JACOB”** — He who here toiled at supplanting vices will there contemplate unceasingly, with the most serene gaze of the mind, the glory of Christ, who for our sake took the land of true flesh; so that he who here was fed with his body and blood through the sacrament of corn and wine may there be fattened with the perpetual vision of his Godhead. Whence: "I shall be satisfied when thy glory shall appear"; and elsewhere: "I will manifest myself to him." Then Jacob the imperfect, turned into Israel, will see God face to face, filled with so large, so fine, so delightful a knowledge of God, as with the lightest dew, that the knowledge of the preachers, by which we are instructed in the present, will seem to be dark. Whence: "Knowledge shall be destroyed"; and elsewhere: "Dark waters in the clouds of the air; at the brightness that was before him"; when that is reached all this doctrine will cease, "and they shall all be taught of God". Whence he fittingly adds: "Blessed art thou, Israel", etc.
**“in a land”** — because that people served the Lord for the goods of the land
**“of corn”** — with the flesh of Christ, with which it is now fed in the sacrament of bread and wine
**“and wine, and the heavens”**
• the apostles
• the doctrine of the preachers
**“shall be misty with dew.”**
• for the fine and lightest knowledge of God
• AND THE HEAVENS SHALL BE MISTY WITH DEW. As if [to say]: the dew will be poured out so abundantly to make the earth fruitful that the gaze of men will be darkened. In which is signified that the Jews, since they loved earthly wealth beyond measure, were darkened and could not know Christ; whence: "If we let him alone so, all will believe in him", etc.
33.29:
**“Blessed art thou, Israel.”** — Israel, strong with God, who is truly blessed, having received power over all the strength of the enemy
**“WHO IS LIKE TO THEE”** — As if [to say]: therefore blessed, therefore none is like to thee, because thou hopest for salvation not from thy own power but from the grace of Christ, who saves his people from their sins.
**“O people, that art saved by the Lord?”** — namely, he is
**“The shield”**
• protection
• in battle
• defending from every onset
**“of thy help, and the sword”** — the power to overcome the devil
**“of thy glory.”** — in the resurrection
**“AND THE SWORD OF GLORY”** — In the future, striking the adversaries with irrevocable severity, when he shall avenge the blood of his servants. The sword is now hidden here in the humility of those who suffer; it will be revealed in the glory of those who rise again. Therefore it is called the sword of the glory of Israel. Christ, then, protects him who fights as a shield, and avenges him who triumphs as a sword of glory. To him, as to the head, at the end of the prophecy the glory of the body is referred, when it is said: "Thy enemies shall deny thee", etc.
**“Shall deny”**
• in the present life
• unwilling to believe or be reconciled through the Gospel
**“SHALL DENY THEE”** — They shall abhor and hate [thee], as Balac, who asked Balaam to drive back the Israelites by cursing them.
**“the enemies”** — the devil and his members
**“thy, and thou”** — who art invincible
**“their necks”**
• which they proudly stretch out against thee
• with eternal punishments
**“THOU SHALT TREAD UPON”** — By subjecting them to the Church, which they abhor and persecute.
**“shalt tread upon.”** — Note that there are only eleven blessings. For Simeon is not found in these blessings; in which Judas is excluded from the apostles, eleven only remaining. Thence also in eleven stations the children of Israel came from Horeb to the place in which they received Deuteronomy.

34.1:
**“THEN WENT UP”** — Moses as well as the other fathers of the Old Testament, raised through the Spirit to the height of contemplation, could foresee the grace of the New Testament which is given in Christ, both in the bestowal of the virtues and in the receiving of the heavenly kingdom; but they could not await it in the flesh, and died in faith and hope.
**“AND SHEWED HIM”** — Moses saw the land of promise and did not enter, because the law foreshadowed the coming of Christ and the doctrine of the Gospel in words and figures, but led no one to perfection.
34.3: **“ALL THE LAND”** — The part of the whole land that he could see from the highest mountain. Or he showed him the whole land in spirit.
34.5:
**“And Moses the servant of the Lord died there, in the land of Moab,”** — AND MOSES DIED THERE, etc. God spares none of the elect, and avenges even the least sins, even in his friends; whence: "Moses and Aaron among his priests"; and he added: "Thou wast a merciful God to them, and taking vengeance on all their inventions."
**“by the commandment of the Lord:”**
• because by the dispensation of the Lord the law was ended, grace succeeding
• The law, namely, being ended, which served the Lord in its time: the city destroyed and the altar, nowhere sacrifices, nowhere libations, nowhere priest or pontiff.
34.6:
**“IN THE VALLEY”** — He died on the mountain, he was buried in the valley, because the law was glorious in its time, but compared to the Gospel it seems hidden and lowly; whence: "I gave them statutes that were not good."
**“AND NO MAN HATH KNOWN”** — The Jews think this was done lest the Jews, ever prone to idolatry, should worship him when dead as a god. But according to the allegory it signifies that the time and manner of ending the law are hidden in the foreknowledge of God alone, and that the depth of the wisdom of God or the secret of his counsel lies open to no one, "for his judgments are incomprehensible, and his ways unsearchable".
34.7:
**“a hundred and twenty years old”** — after the perfection of the commandments, namely, which is in the two precepts of charity
**“was dim”**
• with the cloud of malice
• the gaze of devout intention, the understanding of the mind, did not stray from the right
**“his eye, neither his teeth”** — the order of discretion or of reason was not depraved by the tempest of vices
**“MOSES WAS A HUNDRED AND TWENTY YEARS OLD”**
• If you add together the sums of the several numbers in natural order from one up to fifteen, namely one and two and three and so on, they make a hundred and twenty. But fifteen is made of seven and eight: seven refers to the sabbath, eight to circumcision, because "on the eighth day the child was circumcised". But if you look to the New Testament, you have the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost and in the eighth the resurrection of Christ. A hundred and twenty therefore signifies those who, whether in the Old or in the New Testament, strive to fulfil the precepts of the Law and of the Gospel.
• This signifies that both he and the other fathers of the Old Testament, after the perfection of the commandments of God, which is in the two precepts of charity, are fitted, through the grace of Christ and the redemption of his blood, for eternal rest and the life to come; whose eye was not dim, namely, the gaze of devout intention was not darkened by the cloud of malice; nor were the teeth moved, because the order of their discretion was not disturbed by the tempest of vices. A hundred and twenty are the years of the lawgiver; by this number the height of Solomon's temple was established. The primitive Church also, after the passion and resurrection and the ascension of the Lord, received the grace of the Holy Ghost in this number of men. For fifteen, which consists of seven and eight, signifies the life to come, which is now carried on in the sabbath of souls and will be perfected in the resurrection of bodies. Fifteen also, drawn out into a triangle, that is, added up with its parts, makes a hundred and twenty. Fitly therefore by the hundred and twenty the beatitude of the elect in the life to come is signified, and the third upper storey of the house of God is completed; because after the labours of the faithful, after the rest of souls, the full felicity of the Church will be completed in the glory of the resurrection.
34.8:
**“AND MOURNED”** — Because death reigned even over those who had not sinned, from Adam unto Moses, therefore tears follow him as he goes down to hell.
**“JEROME”** — It is no wonder if mourning is shown for Moses and Aaron, since also in the New Testament great mourning was made over Stephen. Of Jacob also it is said: "They mourned with a great and strong mourning." Jesus son of Nave is recorded as buried, not as wept for; for under the old law all were held under sin, and tears followed every one who went down to hell. Whence: "Death reigned from Adam unto Moses", etc. But in Jesus, that is, in the Gospel, through whom paradise is opened, joys follow death. To this day the Jews, weeping with bare feet, rolled in ashes and clothed in sackcloth, from the superstition of the Pharisees first take a meal of lentils, signifying that for such a dish they lost the birthright; and deservedly, because, not believing the resurrection of the Lord, they are made ready for the coming of the Antichrist. But we who have put on Christ, and are a royal priesthood and a chosen generation, ought not to be saddened over the dead, but rather to rejoice in the resurrection to come; because the days of those mourning Moses are completed, and the day of the Lord has drawn near, of which it is said: "Better is one day in thy courts above thousands." Whence Moses [said] to Aaron and to his sons who were left: "Uncover not your heads, and rend not your garments"; as if [to say]: do not mourn, lest you die; your death is sin. The high priest is forbidden to approach even his dead father, lest a soul given over to the sacrifices of God be hindered by any affection. In the Gospel also it is said: "Let the dead bury their dead." In Leviticus also it is added: "Neither shall he go out of the holy places, lest he defile the sanctuary of the Lord: because the oil of the holy unction of his God is upon him." For after we have believed in Christ and received his unction, we ought not to go out of the temple, that is, out of the Christian purpose, to mingle with the unbelief of the Gentiles, but to be within, that is, to minister to the will of the Lord.
**“And the days of their mourning in which they mourned for Moses were ended.”** — at the coming of Christ
**“AND WERE ENDED”** — Hence seems to have arisen the custom that the offices of piety are paid for the faithful departed for thirty days.
34.9:
**“And Josue”** — Christ Jesus, who succeeds Moses as the end of the law
**“the son of Nun was filled”** — whence: "The spirit of wisdom and of understanding, the spirit of counsel and of fortitude shall rest upon him", etc.
**“HAD LAID UPON HIM”** — In his writings he bore witness to him, saying: "God will raise up to you a prophet", etc. Whence: "For if you did believe Moses, you would perhaps believe me also."
**“May thy sons”** — predestined to life
**“of Israel, and did”** — because they believed in him whom the Lord promised to his people through Moses
34.10:
**“And there arose no more a prophet in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,”**
• he does not prefer him to the apostles, to whom it is said: "for many kings and prophets have desired to see the things that you see"
• AND THERE AROSE NO MORE, etc. This (as they say) Esdras added of his own, who with divine understanding restored the library burnt by the Chaldeans, and invented the letters which the Jews now use. Whence also he is called a swift scribe.
• [The edition here refers to the prologue "Bibliotheca interpretatur": "Bibliotheca is interpreted 'a storing of books'" (printed elsewhere).]
**“AND THERE AROSE NO MORE A PROPHET”** — Because Moses was more excellent than all the prophets of the Old Testament; whence the Jews arrogantly say: "We are the disciples of Moses." But after the Lord of the prophets came incarnate into the world, all that former dignity and shadow of things to come ceased; because the law and the figure were given by Moses, grace and truth by Jesus Christ, who is the end of the law unto justice to every one that believeth.

1.1:
**“Now it came to pass after the death of Moses the servant of God, that the Lord spoke”** — the Father
**“to Josue”** — to Jesus the Son of God
**“the son of Nun, the minister of Moses,”** — because "he came not to destroy the law, but to fulfil"
**“and said to him:”** — MOSES THE SERVANT. ADAMANTIUS. "Moses my servant is dead", etc. Mark how Jesus reigns. If you consider Jerusalem overthrown, the altar destroyed, nowhere any sacrifices or priests or pontiffs or any festivals of the Jews, you will say that Moses the servant of God is dead. If you consider the nations entering into the faith, churches built, altars not sprinkled with the gore of cattle but consecrated with the blood of Christ, priests and levites ministering not the blood of bulls or goats but the word of God through the grace of the Holy Ghost, you will say that after Moses Jesus holds the principality: not the son of Nave, but the Son of God; because Christ our Pasch is sacrificed, and we eat the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. And there are the fruits of the good land in the Church, thirtyfold, sixtyfold, a hundredfold: the married, the widows, the virgins; and the seed of Israel is multiplied from those "who are born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God"; and the children of God that were dispersed are gathered together in one. The people of God keeps sabbath not from common converse, but from every work of sin. Moses therefore, the servant of the Lord, is dead. Lastly, in a certain little book, although it is not held in the canon, the figure of this mystery is described. For it is related that two Moseses were seen, one living in the spirit and the other dead in the body. For the letter of the law, empty and void of all the things aforesaid, is Moses dead in the body; but the spiritual understanding of the law is Moses who lives in the spirit.
1.2:
**“Moses my servant”** — the law, which was as a pedagogue
**“is dead:”** — according to the letter; but he lives in the spirit
**“arise, and pass over this Jordan, thou and all the people with thee, into the land”** — of the living; "Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land"
**“which I will give”** — not Moses
**“to the children of Israel.”** — Moses being dead
**“ARISE, AND”** — "Now arise and pass over this Jordan", etc. See how Jesus the Son of God was the minister of Moses. "When the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law"; because he was made under the law of Moses, he was made the minister of Moses.
1.3:
**“EVERY PLACE”** — "Every place that you shall go up to with the soles of your feet I will give to you", etc. The letter of the law is laid on the ground and below. He therefore does not go up who follows the letter of the law. If you go up from the letter to the spirit, you go up to a high place, which you will receive from God as an inheritance. For if you understand that in the things that are written there are the forms of heavenly things, and seek the things that are above, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God, then you will receive that place as an inheritance; because where Christ is, there also shall his minister be. If then you come by faith, life, virtue and purity even to Christ sitting at the right hand of God, and with those feet which Jesus Christ washed you walk upon that place, God will give it to you, that you may be made not only heir of God but joint heir with Christ.
**“Every place”** — which is above
**“that the sole of your foot shall tread upon”**
• which Jesus Christ washed
• "where I am, there also shall my minister be"
1.4:
**“From the desert and from Libanus unto the great river Euphrates.”** — "The land that was desolate and impassable shall be glad", etc. And elsewhere: "Many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband."
**“FROM THE DESERT AND”** — "The wilderness and before Libanus", etc. He did not say Libanus, but before Libanus, which Jesus receives from God; and "before Libanus" is said as it were for "in place of Libanus". If then you look at the former people, that is, Israel according to the flesh, which was the true olive, understand that it was the true Libanus. But because through its unbelief the kingdom is taken from it and given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof, this nation is before Libanus, that is, in the Church gathered from the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.
1.5: **“No man shall be able to resist you all the days of your life: as I have been with Moses, so will I be with thee: I will not leave thee, nor forsake thee.”** — AS I HAVE BEEN WITH MOSES, SO WILL I BE WITH THEE, etc. AUGUSTINE. By this testimony and others Moses is proved to have died as the servant of God and pleasing to God, although in him that vengeance was fulfilled, that he did not enter into the land of promise; from which it is given to be understood that God takes some bodily or temporal vengeance on his good servants, and yet holds them among the vessels that are honourable and useful.
1.7:
**“Take courage therefore, and be very valiant:”** — in prosperity, lest it soften thee; in adversity, lest it overthrow thee
**“that thou mayst observe and do all the law, which Moses my servant hath commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayst understand all things which thou dost.”** — AND JOSUE COMMANDED, etc. AUGUSTINE. It is asked how he commanded this after the Lord had exhorted him and strengthened him, promising that he would be with him, since it was many more days after that he crossed the Jordan. For when he had commanded these things, he sent spies into Jericho, who turned in to Rahab, and were hidden by her, and sought by the king and not found, she letting them down through the window and warning them to stay three days in the mountains. Four days therefore seem to have been spent in these things. And when they had reported what had been done concerning them, Jesus moved with all the people from the place where he was, early in the morning, and coming to the Jordan he turned aside. Then the people are admonished again to prepare themselves to cross the Jordan after three days. It was therefore a human arrangement that he first had it announced. For, as a man, he hoped this could be done if the spies returned quickly; and when they delayed, it is understood, even if Scripture is silent, that the rest was fulfilled by the disposition of God, that so Jesus might begin to be glorified among the people; whence it was said to him as he was about to cross the river: "This day I will begin to exalt thee before the children", etc. For even those with whom God is said to speak wish to do some things by human arrangement, in which they trust God to be their ruler; but their counsels are often changed by him by whose providence they are ruled. Whence Moses, as a man, thought that all the causes of the people were to be heard by him; [but] his arrangement was changed, Jethro suggesting it by divine inspiration.
1.12: **“TO THE RUBENITES ALSO”** — ADAMANTIUS. Let us consider what figure the two tribes and a half hold, which receive their inheritance through Moses, and what the remaining nine and a half, which [receive] the promise of the holy land through Jesus. Those who receive their portion through Moses are all firstborn. For Ruben is the firstborn of Lia, Gad of Zelpha, Manasses of the daughter of the priest of Heliopolis, the wife of Joseph. In these, then, was already foreshadowed the figure of two peoples: one which should be firstborn by the order of nature, the other which should receive the inheritance through faith and the grace of the blessing. Nor is rest given first to those who receive the inheritance through Moses, that is, who pleased God through the law, unless they help their brethren in the battles. Yet the women and infants receive rest; the rest do not rest, but go out to the help of their brethren. When we strive in this life against the demons, there come to our help those who before the coming of Christ were justified in the law, as Isaias, Jeremias and the other prophets, by the reading of whom we are armed and enlightened. These are they who, as strong men armed and girded about the loins with truth, go out to our help and fight with us. But the infants and women do not go out to our battle. An infant is said to be one who does not speak. What then can he help me who has spoken nothing, whom I may read and whose word does not instruct me? The woman is the weaker vessel, nor does she come to the conflict, lest she be broken and perish; whence: the bruised reed he shall not break. Because, then, the women are commanded to be taught at home by their husbands, and signify those who learn rather than those who teach, they do not come to our help. For he can teach me nothing in whom I find nothing that I ought to imitate or hold.
1.14:
**“Your wives,”** — the weaker vessels, not fit for the conflict, lest they be broken and perish; who are not permitted to teach, but only to be taught
**“and your children,”** — who know not how to speak or teach
**“and cattle”** — the foolish, the unlearned
**“shall remain in the land”** — of the living, which they merited under the law
**“which Moses gave you beyond the Jordan: but pass you over armed”** — with the arms of faith
**“before your brethren, all of you that are strong of hand,”** — in working
**“and fight for them,”** — by doctrine or example
1.15:
**“Until the Lord give rest to your brethren”** — to the children of the New Testament
**“as he hath given you,”** — who were in the time of the Law
**“and they also possess the land”** — of the living
**“which the Lord your God will give them:”** — "I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living"
**“and so you shall return into the land of your possession, and you shall dwell in it, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave you”** — by instructing [you] how you should hold it
**“beyond the Jordan,”** — before the time of the New Testament
**“toward the rising of the sun.”** — from which all good rises
1.16: **“And they made answer to Josue”** — to Christ
1.17: **“As we obeyed Moses in all things,”** — whence: "If you did believe Moses, you would believe me also"
1.18:
**“He that shall gainsay thy mouth, and not obey all thy words, that thou shalt command him, let him die.”** — with eternal death
**“Only take thou courage, and do manfully.”**
• Nor does it seem idle to me that the tribes which are dispensed through Moses are not three whole ones, nor those which obtain the inheritance through Jesus ten whole ones, but two and a half here and nine and a half there. But one is divided, by which neither the number three is filled up nor the number ten; because the former did indeed touch the knowledge of the Trinity, but not wholly nor perfectly, because they did not know the incarnation of the Only-begotten. For although they believed in his coming and his other dispensations, and even preached them, yet they could not see and behold what they had believed; whence: many prophets and kings have desired to see the things that you see, etc. For their faith was not whole, because the dispensation of the flesh had not yet been fulfilled, and what we believe already done they believed would be done. Those tribes, then, are neither two, lest the fathers be outside the faith and salvation of the Trinity, nor three whole and perfect, lest the sacrament of the Trinity should seem fulfilled in them. But they did touch the third number, because they desired to see whom we see, and could not. Perhaps not even at the coming of Jesus do we learn what is perfect and whole, nor if he be led to the cross and consummated in all things, nor if he rose from the dead; [the Spirit] will show us through himself all things that are perfect. Whence: "I have yet many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now"; "But when the Spirit of truth is come, who proceedeth from the Father", etc. You see that not only with Moses is the number three imperfect, but Jesus still says to his disciples: You cannot hear them now. He hints at the Spirit of truth, because through the Holy [Spirit] and in him the perfection of the Trinity is fulfilled.
• There are nine and a half tribes which are governed under Jesus, not ten whole ones, which is a perfect number; so that what is said to be reserved by the Lord Jesus for the Holy Ghost may seem half full and in the middle. For although through Christ penance is preached, and conversion, and remission of sins is given, and all the things that seem to tend to the perfection of the number ten, yet the perfection and sum of all goods is if, after all these things, one merits to receive the grace of the Holy Ghost.
• Moreover, in this book it is written that the true altar was in that land which Jesus distributed. But Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses made for themselves an altar not true, but one that should bear the type of the true altar, which was with Jesus. What wonder, then, if they did not receive the whole knowledge of the Trinity, who had built neither a whole nor a true altar? Therefore neither many enemies nor more kings of the hostile powers were cast down by them. Only Sehon king of the Amorrhites, and Og king of Basan, and the Amalecites did they cast down beyond the Jordan. But where Jesus led the army, now five kings fall together, who had fled into caves, and are hanged on a tree; now thirty are slain together; and they exterminate all who possess the holy land with uncleanness, who hold the land flowing with milk and honey in the bitterness of malice.

2.1:
**“And Josue sent”** — Christ
**“the son of Nun, from Setim, two men, spies,”** — the two testaments, that he might prove the faith of believers or the unbelief of the rebellious before the coming of the judgment
**“secretly: and said to them: Go, and view the land and the city”** — the world
**“of Jericho. They went and entered into the house of a woman that was a harlot named Rahab,”** — namely, of the Church gathered from the Gentiles, which before committed fornication with idols in the desires of the flesh; whence: "The harlots shall go before you into the kingdom" of heaven
**“TWO MEN, SPIES”** — ADAMANTIUS. Spies are sent by Jesus into Jericho and are received by the harlot Rahab. These spies may be thought to be angels, according to that: "Behold I send my angel before thy face", etc.; which was fulfilled through others invisibly, but through John visibly, of whose baptism it is said that the scribes and Pharisees did not believe him; but the harlots and publicans, believing, were baptized; as the harlot received the spies of Josue, through whom she is rescued from the destruction of the hostile nation. Rahab is interpreted breadth. This is the Church of Christ, which, gathered from sinners as from harlotry, says: "The place is too strait for me, make me room to dwell in"; "and who hath brought up these for me?"; and to whom it is said: Enlarge thy dwellings. This is the harlot to whom Solomon, who came to make peace between the things that are in heaven and the things that are on earth, commanded the living child to be given back. But she who had the dead child is the synagogue of the former people, or of those who have turned aside into heresy. This harlot receives the spies of Jesus, and having received them sets them in the upper places, namely, in the high sacraments of the faith. For no one sent by Jesus is found below and lying on the ground, but he remains in the upper places. Nor does he alone remain in the upper places, but the harlot also who receives him from a harlot becomes a prophetess. For she says: "I know that the Lord hath given you this land", etc. You see how she who was once an impious and unclean harlot is now filled with the Holy Ghost: she confesses the past, believes the present, prophesies the future. So Rahab is enlarged and advances until their sound went forth into all the earth. Japheth also is interpreted enlargement, who himself bore the figure of the Gentile people; and Chanaan the boy is made subject to him as a servant by his father, and to his brother Sem, in the figure of those who are saved from the circumcision. In which is the wonderful kindness and providence of God, who, wishing to bestow remedy and salvation on the sinner Cham, made him the servant of his brethren, as Esau of his brother Jacob: not that he might perish, but that by obeying his betters he might gain salvation. For very much is bestowed on the wicked who know not how to rule themselves when they are not entrusted to themselves but become the servants of the saints and are subject to their betters. You see how great the kindness of the Lord, which he hides from the ears of the crowd and covers with harsher words, lest the bad and ungrateful servant become a despiser if he understand the goodness in the mercy of his Lord.
2.2: **“And it was told the king of Jericho,”** — to the devil, or the world, which would rather be in danger than lose the spies of Christ
2.4: **“And the woman taking the men, hid them, and said:”** — keeping them faithfully with her
2.5: **“And at the time of shutting the gate in the dark, they also went out together. I know not whither they are gone: pursue after them quickly, and overtake them.”** — or, you will overtake [them]
2.6: **“But she made the men go up to the top of her house, and covered them with the stalks of flax,”** — or, tow, or refuse
2.12: **“Now therefore swear ye to me by the Lord,”** — she makes a covenant for her own safety and that of her household with the testaments of the Lord
2.13: **“And that you will save my father and mother, my brethren and sisters, and all things that are theirs, and deliver our souls from death.”** — from the ruin of the world
2.16:
**“And she said to them: Get ye up to the mountains,”** — as if [to say]: flee lowly and abject things, preach heavenly things
**“lest perhaps they meet you as they return: and there lie ye hid three days, till they come back, and so you shall go on your way.”** — GET YE UP TO THE MOUNTAINS. ADAMANTIUS, etc. The wise harlot gives mystical and heavenly counsel, having nothing earthly. Go away, she says, by the mountains; do not walk through the valleys; flee lowly and abject things; preach the things that are lofty and sublime. And she herself puts a scarlet cloth in her house, through which she may be saved from the destruction of the city: scarlet, namely, because it bore the figure of blood. For she knew that there was salvation for none except in the blood of Christ. This commandment also is given her: All who shall be found in thy house shall be saved. If then any one wishes to be saved, let him come into this house in which the blood of Christ is in sign of redemption. For with those who said, "His blood be upon us and upon our children", the blood of Christ is unto damnation. For Jesus is set for the fall and for the resurrection of many. Therefore to those who gainsay his sign the blood becomes unto punishment, to believers unto salvation. No one therefore is saved outside the Church. He who goes out becomes guilty of his own death; this is the sign of blood, because this is the sanctification that consists through blood. That this sign hangs in the window I think indicates this: the window lights the house, and through it we take in as much light as suffices for our eyes and sight; and the incarnation of the Saviour did not bring before us the whole sight of the Godhead, but as through a window, through his incarnation he made us behold the light of the Godhead. Therefore it seems to me the sign of salvation was given through the window, by which all who are in her house, she who was once a harlot, obtain salvation, cleansed in water and in the Holy Ghost and in the blood of Christ.
2.18:
**“If when we come into the land, a sign”** — of redemption
**“this scarlet cord be,”** — the blood of Christ
**“and thou tie it in the window,”** — in the incarnation of Christ
**“by which thou hast let us down: and gather together thy father and mother, and brethren and all thy kindred into thy house.”** — into the Church
2.19: **“Whosoever shall go out of the door of thy house,”** — no one is saved outside the Church

3.3: **“And began to proclaim: When you shall see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and the priests of the race of Levi carrying it, rise you up also, and follow them as they go before:”** — WHEN YOU SHALL SEE. AUGUSTINE. The scribes say to the people: "When you shall see the ark of the testimony of our God, and the priests and the levites carrying it, set out from your places and go after it. But let there be a long space between you and it, as much as two thousand cubits; you shall stand, lest you come near it, that you may know the way by which you shall go in it; for you have not gone the way yesterday and the day before", etc. The ark was commanded to go far ahead, so that it could be seen by the people; for so great a host, if it went close behind it, would not see it going before, nor know where to follow. From this it is understood that the pillar of cloud, which used to give the signal for moving camp and to show the way, had already withdrawn and no longer appeared to them. Hence it came about that those three days were foretold by human arrangement. Now therefore, under the leadership of Jesus, they follow the ark of the Lord, the cloud being withdrawn as though a veil were taken away.
3.7:
**“And the Lord said to Josue: This day will I begin to exalt thee before all Israel:”** — Christ is exalted for each one when he is baptized in his death
**“THIS DAY WILL I BEGIN TO EXALT”** — ADAMANTIUS. Many wonders were done in the wilderness, and nowhere is Jesus said to be exalted. But where the Jordan is crossed it is said to him: "This day I will begin to exalt thee", etc. For the exaltation of Jesus in the sight of the people takes its beginning from baptism. For those who are baptized are baptized in his death, whose death is completed in the exaltation of the cross. Rightly, then, for each of the faithful Jesus is first exalted when he comes to the mystery of baptism; whence: God hath exalted him, and hath given him a name, namely, which is above every name, etc.
3.10:
**“THE LORD, THE LIVING GOD, IN THE MIDST”** — ADAMANTIUS. To the sinner every creature is an enemy, as to the Egyptians the river, the earth, the sky. To the just all things serve. He crosses the Red Sea with dry foot; the Egyptian is drowned. In the wilderness, that is, in the desert, horrible and vast, food is ministered from heaven to the just; and in the Jordan the ark of the testament is leader to the people; the waters failed before the priests and levites. Likewise to thee, who through the sacrament of baptism hast come forth from the streams of the Jordan, a passage through the very air is promised; whence: "We shall be taken up to meet Christ, into the air", etc. There is nothing then for the just to fear, whom every creature serves, and to whom it is said: "When thou shalt pass through the fire, the flame shall not burn thee", etc. And all the things that were done among the former are fulfilled in thee according to the mystical sense, who desirest, leaving the darkness of idolatry, to come to the hearing of the divine law. Thou leavest Egypt. When thou art gathered with the catechumens and hast begun to obey the precepts of the Church, thou hast also gone out through the Red Sea, and, set in the stations of the desert, thou givest thyself daily to hearing the law of God and beholding the face of Moses revealed through the glory of the Lord. But if thou come to baptism and, the order of priests and levites standing by, art initiated into the venerable sacraments, then by the ministry of the priests thou shalt cross the Jordan and enter the land of promise; in which, after Moses, Jesus receives thee, the leader of the new journey. And thou, mindful of such great powers, that the sea was divided for thee, that the water of the Jordan stood, wilt say: "What ailed thee, O thou sea, that thou didst flee: and thou, O Jordan, that thou wast turned back?" And the divine word will answer: "At the presence of the Lord the earth was moved, at the presence of the God", etc.
**“and that he shall destroy before your sight the Chanaanite”** — Chanaanite: possessing, or possession, or merchants, or changeable. Hethite: fearing, or astonished. Hevite: gathering stones. Pherezite: separating, or sowing abroad. Gergesite: bringing near a husbandman, or casting out a husbandman, or a stranger drawing near. Amorrhite: bitter, or speaking. Jebusite: treading, or their manger.
3.14: **“So the people went out of their tents, to pass over the Jordan: and the priests that carried the ark of the covenant, went on before them.”** — because through the teaching office of the priests the people is led to the land of promise; and if anyone today is worthy to be enrolled in that order, the very streams of the Jordan will yield to him and the very elements will reverence him
3.15:
**“And as soon as they came into the Jordan, and their feet were dipped in part of the water,”** — because [they are] a part of those who are baptized; they keep the sweetness of heavenly grace received
**“HARVEST”** — The Seventy: "As in the days of wheat harvest." This seems incredible in our regions. But there, as those who know it relate, at the beginning of spring is the wheat harvest; and then that river overflows and is filled more than in winter.
3.16:
**“The waters that came down stood in one place, and swelling up like a mountain, were seen afar off from the city that is called Edom, to the place of Sarthan: but those that were beneath, into the sea of the wilderness”** — because a part is turned into the bitterness of sins
**“THE WATERS STOOD”** — ADAMANTIUS. I think it is not written without a mystical reason that part of the waters of the Jordan is sunk into the sea and flows into bitterness, while part remains in sweetness. For if all who are baptized kept the sweetness of heavenly grace, none would be turned into the bitterness of sins. But often, having received baptism, they return to worldly things and drink the salt cup of avarice, and flowing into the sea they perish in the salt waves. But that part which remains in stability and keeps its sweetness signifies those who hold firmly the gift of God received. And rightly is the part of those who are saved one, because one is the bread that came down from heaven, and one faith, and one baptism, and one Spirit with which all are given to drink in baptism, and one God the Father of all.
**“which now is called the Dead [Sea], ran down until they wholly failed.”** — would perish by eternal death
3.17:
**“And the people marched over against the Jordan: and the priests that carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord,”**
• who teach the people to go out of Egypt, that is, out of the errors of the world, and to pass through the wilderness, that is, the temptation of the world
• THE PRIESTS that, etc. The same priestly and levitical order stands by the ark of the Lord, in which the law of God is carried. For they are those who enlighten the people from the commandments of God. Whence: "Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light to my paths"; this light is kindled through the priests and levites.
**“stood girded upon the dry ground in the midst of the Jordan, and all the people passed over through the channel that was dried up.”** — THE PEOPLE, he says, is to be far from the ark of the testament of the Lord, two thousand cubits; but the priests and levites near, that it may be carried on their shoulders. Blessed are they who merit to be near to God. But it is written: "They who draw near to me draw near to fire." If thou be gold and silver and draw near to the fire, thou wilt shine the brighter through the fire. If thou hast built upon [the foundation] wood, hay, stubble, thou wilt be consumed. Blessed then are they who are near, so that the fire enlightens them and does not burn them. Israel shall indeed be saved, but, set far off, it makes its journey not by its own power, [but] in the ministry of the priests.

4.7: **“FOR EVER”** — AUGUSTINE. How for ever, when heaven and earth pass away? Is it because they signify something eternal, though they themselves cannot be eternal? Although what is in the Greek could be said in Latin "unto the age".
4.10:
**“Now the priests that carried the ark, stood in the midst of the Jordan till all things were accomplished which the Lord had commanded Josue to speak to the people, and Moses had said to him. And the people made haste and passed over.”** — we are not to act idly or slackly, but all the precepts of the Lord are to be passed through and fulfilled with haste
**“AND THE PEOPLE MADE HASTE”** — ADAMANTIUS. Those who crossed the Red Sea were baptized in Moses, in the cloud and in the sea; and of those who cross the Jordan we can likewise say that all were baptized in Jesus in the Jordan. What is written, "and the people made haste and passed over the Jordan", I do not think is idle. For when we come to baptism and receive the sacrament of the word of God, we must not act sluggishly but make haste until we pass through all things, that is, fulfil all the commandments, that we may merit to come to the promised beatitude. But when we have passed through all things, we must walk diligently and warily, lest our steps be suddenly poured out; whence: My steps had well nigh slipped. Nor ought care to be slacker in keeping the virtues than in acquiring them; which is designated when it is said that forty thousand men girded in truth crossed over to take Jericho: girded, namely, with the girdle of truth; whence: "Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth." Our girdle too ought to be of truth, if indeed we keep the sacrament of this warfare and girdle; if we speak falsehood, we are ungirt of the belt of truth. Let us then be girded in truth, but ungirt in falsehood. Crossing the Jordan, we cross to wars against the spirits of wickedness in high places. For all these things were written for us. Let us go out then to war, that the first city of this [world], namely the malice of the world and its proud walls, may be taken by us. Within thee is the battle; within thee is the evil building to be overthrown; thy enemy proceeds from thy heart. "For from the heart come forth evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications", etc. You see how great and of what kind is the army of thy enemies. These must be overthrown by us in the first slaughter, that we leave none. Then through Jesus that rest will be given us, that "every one shall rest under his vine and under his fig tree, since there is none now to make the children of Israel afraid".
4.11: **“And when they had all passed over, the ark also of the Lord passed over, and the priests went before the people.”** — as teachers and leaders to the land of promise
4.12: **“The children of Ruben also and Gad, and half the tribe of Manasses, armed”** — because, when we have passed through all things, we must go diligently and warily, lest our steps be poured out
4.13:
**“And forty thousand fighting men by their troops, and bands, marched through the plains and fields of the city of Jericho.”**
• broad and spacious is the way of Jericho, that is, of the world
• the malice of the world and the proud walls of sin are first to be overthrown by us
4.14:
**“In that day the Lord magnified Josue in the sight of all Israel, that they should fear him, as they had feared Moses, while he lived.”** — he who is under the law fears Moses; when one passes to the Gospel, the observance being changed, the fear is changed; whence: "I through the law am dead to the law, that I may live to God", etc.
**“IN THAT”** — Jesus was always exalted with the Father, but there is need that God exalt him in our sight, that is, that we know the height of his divinity. And this is done if we cross the Jordan and are armed for the wars to come with the various defences of the sacraments.
4.16: **“COMMAND THE PRIESTS”** — AUGUSTINE. "Command the priests that carry the ark of the testament", etc. It is usually said the ark of the testament or the ark of the testimony. Now therefore it is said the ark of the testament of the testimony, so that not only the ark but the testament itself is called the testament of the testimony. For hence the Apostle says: "But now without the law the justice of God is made manifest, being witnessed by the law and the prophets"; because the Old Testament was given in testimony of the thing to come.
4.19:
**“THE TENTH DAY”** — That is, the day on which the mystery of the lamb was commanded in Egypt; because on the same day that we flee the errors of the world we enter the land of promise. For the whole present life is one day; today, then, that is, while we live, let us hasten to perfection, and not put it off till tomorrow.
**“AND THE PEOPLE”** — ADAMANTIUS. Not without cause is it marked when they come to the Jordan: on the tenth, he says, of the first month. This is the very day on which the mystery of the lamb was commanded in Egypt; on the same they enter the land of promise. And it is very blessed that on the very day on which one escapes the errors of the world he should enter the land of promise, that is, on this day on which we live in this world; for the whole present life is signified by one day. By this, then, we are taught not to put off the works of justice till tomorrow, but today, that is, while we live, to hasten to fulfil all the things that pertain to perfection. And so we shall be able on the tenth day of the first month to enter the land of promise, that is, the beatitude of perfection. And note that this day is often repeated, because, although there is for us one general perfection, yet if we can fulfil wholly one kind of virtue, that very virtue has each its own perfection. Thus through the several virtues many perfections are found. But that is the general one which contains in itself the sum of all perfections. Therefore on this day many deeds are recapitulated, to signify that many perfections pertain to one day.
4.20: **“THE TWELVE ALSO”** — ISIDORE. The children of Israel, crossing the Jordan, took from the midst of the river twelve stones, which they set up for a testimony in the place of the second circumcision, to signify to us that when we rise from the laver we ought to carry with us the most firm examples of the apostolic life, whose testimony we should ever look upon for the imitation of the virtues.

5.2:
**“At that time the Lord said to Josue: Make thee knives of stone,”**
• because in the rock, which is Christ, we are cleansed and lay aside the reproach of Egypt, that is, the observances of the Egyptians
• MAKE THEE KNIVES OF STONE, and sitting circumcise the children of Israel. Let the Jews say how one can be circumcised a second time with carnal circumcision. For one once circumcised has nothing that can be taken away a second time. But by us, to whom it is said that the law is spiritual, these things are fitly and suitably solved. For he who has been instructed in the law through Moses has laid aside the error and worship of idolatry. This is the first circumcision, through the law. But if he come to the Gospel, he will receive the second circumcision through the rock, which is Christ, and the reproach of Egypt will be taken away from him. For unless one has been cleansed by the second circumcision through the Gospel, he does not lay aside the reproach of Egypt. For even if all come from the law and are instructed through Moses, they yet have the reproach of sins; whence Paul also: "For we ourselves also were some time unwise, incredulous, erring, slaves to divers desires and pleasures", etc. But after Christ came, and through baptism circumcised a second time and cleansed our souls, we cast away all these things, and in their place took up the answer of a good conscience toward God. Let no one, then, if he has been wholly converted and has repented from the heart, faithfully crossed the Jordan and received the second circumcision, fear the reproaches of past sins, hearing: "This day I have taken away from thee the reproach of Egypt"; whence elsewhere: "Thy sins are forgiven thee"; "but now sin no more, lest some worse thing happen to thee". For if after the remission of sins thou sin no more, truly the reproach of Egypt is taken away from thee. But if thou sin again, the reproaches of Egypt will roll back upon thee again, and the more so because it is of greater crime to tread under foot the Son of God and esteem the blood of the testament unclean than to neglect the law of Moses. For he who commits fornication under the Gospel is of far greater reproach than he who does so under the law, because, taking the members of Christ, he makes them the members of a harlot. In short, no one charges him with lewdness, but condemns him for the crime of sacrilege, because it is said to him: "Know you not that your bodies are the temple of God?" If any man violate the temple of God, him shall God destroy. Moreover, he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body: not only this body, which by hearing the word of God and retaining it in the heart has been made the temple of God, but also that of which it is said that the whole church is the body of Christ; and he who has stained his own body seems to sin against the whole church, because through one member the stain spreads into the whole body.
**“MAKE THEE”** — AUGUSTINE. "Make thee knives of sharp stone, and sitting circumcise the children of Israel again." It is asked why he said "again". For not one man was to be circumcised twice; but because one people was in some circumcised, in some not circumcised, therefore it is said "again", that the circumcised might be circumcised again: not the man but the people. Some sons of those who went out of Egypt were uncircumcised in that people, whom Jesus could circumcise: their sons, namely, whom they begot in the desert and scorned to circumcise, because they were disobedient to the law of God. Why then do they think that those who have the sacrament of Christian baptism are to be rebaptized, as though helped by this testimony of the law? Since not one man was circumcised twice, but the people, which had been circumcised in some and uncircumcised in others; even if in some way it could happen that God commanded a man to be circumcised twice, can those who think men are to be rebaptized say that it was commanded because they had been circumcised by Egyptians, or by some heretics separated from the fellowship of the Israelites?
**“and circumcise the second time the children of Israel.”** — the people, namely, not one man
