But he who is a Jew inwardly, that is, the Christian, who follows Jesus not the son of Nave but the Son of God, understands that these are mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, and says that even now Jesus fights against the opposing powers and casts them out of the cities they possessed, that is, our souls, and kills the kings who reigned in our souls, that sin may reign in us no more; that, the law of sin being shut out, our soul may become the city of God, and God may reign in it, and it may be said to us: "Behold, the kingdom of God is within you." That, then, is mercy which seems cruelty to the heretics, which Jesus Christ fulfils or has fulfilled through the several cities, that is, the souls of believers: that those which were possessed by most wicked kings, these being driven out and slain, he may deign to make the dwelling of God and the temple of the Holy Ghost, and the members that had served iniquity may serve justice. So, then, understand that Jesus killed the king of Jericho, and the king of Hai, and the king of Lebna, and the king of Lachis, and the king of Hebron, so that all the souls which under the most wicked kings kept the law of sin may now live under the laws of God.
10.21:
**“And all the army returned”** — safe; for he who serves under Jesus does not receive the fiery darts of the enemy
**“to Josue in Maceda, where the camp then was, in good health and without the loss of any one:”** — because all are written in the book of life and numbered with him "who telleth the number of the stars"
**“and no man durst move his tongue against the children of Israel.”** — The Seventy: "No one muttered with his tongue", that is, no one boasted of his victory, knowing that it is Jesus who conquers
10.24:
**“And when they were brought out to him, he called all the men of Israel,”** — the strong, fighting manfully
**“and said to the chiefs”** — the prelates
**“of the army”** — of the Church
**“that were with him:”** — disagreeing in nothing
**“Go, and set your feet on the necks”** — "Thou shalt walk upon the asp and the basilisk: and thou shalt trample under foot the lion and the dragon."
**“of these kings.”** — namely, of the spirits and the vices
10.25:
**“He said again to them:”** — as if [to say]: "Do ye manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, all ye that hope in the Lord"
**“Fear not, neither be ye dismayed, take courage and be strong: for so will the Lord do to all enemies”** — spiritual
**“your, against whom you fight.”** — with spiritual arms
10.26:
**“And Josue struck,”** — Christ
**“and slew them,”** — by his death
**“and hanged them upon five gibbets,”** — by which he triumphed on the wood of the cross
10.36: **“He went up also with all Israel from Eglon to Hebron,”** — joining, or marriage
10.37:
**“Took it, and destroyed it”** — he destroyed evils, that they might build good things
**“with the edge of the sword”** — of the word of God
10.40: **“So Josue conquered all the country of the hills and of the south and of the plain, and of Aseroth”** — or: Asedech

11.1:
**“And when Jabin had heard these things”**
• sense, or prudence
• AND WHEN HE HAD HEARD. ADAMANTIUS. When Israel according to the flesh read these writings before the coming of Christ, understanding nothing in them but wars, it was sharpened to ferocity by the shedding of blood and fed on wars and seditions. But after the presence of Jesus Christ poured in the light of knowledge, since he is our peace, he teaches peace, the casting down of wars; for peace is restored to the soul if the enemies, namely sins and vices, are driven out of it. Therefore, according to the teaching of Jesus Christ, when we read these things we are armed and roused to battle, but against the enemies that proceed from our heart, namely evil thoughts, thefts, false witness and the like, that we may leave none to be saved or to breathe. For when these are conquered we shall conquer also the powers of the air, and drive them from their kingdom, which they had set up among us on the seats of the vices. Above, the king of Jerusalem gathered four kings with him against Jesus, otherwise Josue, and against the children of Israel. But now not one gathers four or five, but an exceeding multitude. Whence: "But when Jabin king of Asor heard, he sent to Jobab king of the Amorrhites", etc. You see how many of the opposing powers are stirred up against Jesus and the people of God out of the soul. For these demons, before the coming of Christ, reigned quiet and secure, possessing souls. But when the grace and mercy of the Saviour appeared and taught to live godly and holily, that the soul too might take up its freedom and the image of God, for this cause the old possessors are provoked to the fight; and if the first are overwhelmed, many more rise up and conspire in evil; and if the second are conquered, others more wicked rise; and perhaps the more the people of God is increased and multiplied, the more of them conspire to assail it. For the first and author of the war, who invites the rest to the conspiracy, is Jabin king of Asor. Jabin is interpreted sense or prudence. Of this sense Isaias: "And I will bring upon thee the great sense, the prince of the Assyrians, who said: By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; I have removed the bounds of the nations", etc. The serpent too in paradise is written to have been more prudent than all the beasts, and the unjust steward is said to have done prudently. Asor is interpreted court. The whole earth, then, is the court of this king, who is the devil. Whence it is written in the Gospel that the strong man is in his court, sleeping secure, until a stronger comes who binds him and takes away what he possesses. He sends to Jobab and to the king of Madon. Jobab is interpreted enmities, Madon bitternesses. The devil therefore sends to another hostile power, which is the king of bitternesses, by whose authorship, namely, all bitternesses are inflicted on wretched mortals: the various kinds, namely, of sin. For nothing is more bitter than sin, even if some things seem sweet at first; whence Solomon: "In the end thou shalt find it more bitter than gall", etc. But justice seems bitter at first; at the end it is sweeter than honey, when it has borne the fruit of virtue. The devil therefore sent to Jobab, the enemy, king of bitterness. He sent also to the king of Semeron, which is interpreted hearing. And hearing is twofold: either when God hears man (whence also the patriarch Simeon received his name, because God heard his mother's prayer), or when man hearkens to the command of the devil, who says: If falling down thou wilt adore me, I will give thee all these things. But he who follows Jesus says to him: I will adore the Lord God, and him only will I serve. Those hearken to him who are on his side; as this Semeron, hearkening to him, comes to battle against Jesus. He sends also to the king of Ziph, which is interpreted: how it flows! by way of wonder, namely; for it is to be wondered at how all the things of this world flow away, which among unbelievers are thought to abide. But he who considers the nature of things and the passing of all worldly things says: How it flows!
• The devil calls against the children of Israel those also who are over against great Sidon. I indeed have sometimes stayed in the regions of Sidon; I did not find that there are two Sidons, one small and the other great, so far as concerns the earthly place. But Sidon is interpreted huntress, or hunters, namely of demons, of whom there are many differences. Some are hunters in great sins, others in small. When the soul is deceived in the delights of the flesh, it is said to be caught in a small [thing]; but when it denies the providence of God, or worships demons as God, it is deceived in a great one. He sends also to the mountains: this is every sense that exalts and lifts itself against the knowledge of God. He sends also to Araba, that is, ambushes. For he hints at the ensnaring powers, which deceive human souls not by force nor openly, but by unforeseen ambushes; whence: he lieth in wait in secret, as it were "in his den, he lieth in wait to catch the poor", etc. Of which Paul says: "For we are not ignorant of his devices."
• He sends also into Ceneroth, which is interpreted as it were lamps, not lamps. For a lamp is one thing, as it were a lamp another. John was a burning lamp, because he was an angel of light. As it were a lamp is he who transforms himself into an angel of light. They too who teach the Catholic faith in the Church, and enlighten the people of God with the word of truth, are burning lamps. But those who, for heretical doctrines, use the testimonies of holy Scripture and false assertions are not lamps, but as it were lamps. He sent also to the plains: to those, namely, who are in the plains and savour lowly and earthly things. He sent also into Nephthed Dor, which is interpreted conversion. And conversion is understood as twofold: that by which one turns to him, either from God to good things [so the edition], or that by which king Jabin, that is, the devil, turns souls to himself. He sends also to those who were in the places by the sea, to the Chanaanites near the waves, which is interpreted as it were stirred up, that is, who disturb all things with commotions and waves; and to the Amorrhites of the sea, that is, the embittering, who indeed inflict bitternesses. Such is the roll of the army of the invisible enemies, who are gathered through king Jabin to assail us who follow Jesus our Saviour. But the Lord says: "Be not afraid of their face", etc.
**“king of Asor”**
• of the court
• the prince of the world
11.2:
**“And to the kings of the north, that dwelt in the mountains”** — this is every sense that exalts itself against the knowledge of God
**“and in the plains”** — following the broad way
**“over against the south side of Ceneroth, in the levels”** — who savour human and earthly things
**“and the countries of Dor”** — who are in the flux of this world
11.3:
**“To the Chanaanites also on the east and on the west,”** — as it were stirred up, who, namely, stirs up all things
**“and the Amorrhite,”** — the embittering, by whose authorship, namely, bitternesses are sent in
11.6:
**“And the Lord said to Josue: Fear them not: for tomorrow,”**
• not today, but after the consummation of the world
• FOR TOMORROW AT THIS SAME HOUR. ADAMANTIUS. I see that today we cannot overwhelm all of them, nor kill all; they will be destroyed tomorrow, that is, after the consummation of the world, when it will be said to them: Go into the everlasting fire which God hath prepared for the devil and his angels. For then, if we conquer, following Jesus as leader, we shall receive the kingdom which God has prepared for his saints through Jesus Christ.
**“ADAMANTIUS”** — Unless these wars bore the figure of spiritual ones, the apostles would never have handed them down to be read by the disciples of Christ, who came to teach peace. For Jesus says: "My peace I give unto you", etc. And the Apostle: "Not revenging yourselves, my dearly beloved", etc. Knowing that carnal wars are no longer to be waged by us, but [wars] against the spirits of wickedness, he commands the soldiers of Christ like a master of warfare: "Put you on the armour of God, that you may be able to stand against the deceits of the devil." And of spiritual wars we have examples from the deeds of the ancients, that we may be spiritual, hearing that the law is spiritual, comparing spiritual things with spiritual, considering from these nations which visibly assailed carnal Israel how many are the nations of opposing powers that fight against the Church of God to make it sin. For as the body, receiving a wound from iron, dies, so the soul wounded by sin. Jesus therefore did as the Lord commanded.
**“HE SHALL HAMSTRING THEIR HORSES”** — This, then, Jesus fulfilled according to the command of God. But if any of the enemies had survived, the horses would have had to be hamstrung, lest any of them should flee away. But since none was left that breathed, why are the horses hamstrung, which could have been of use to the victors? For the Israelites were wont, when their enemies were conquered, to keep the beasts for use, as when the Madianites were conquered they kept some thousands of asses. Nor is it written of the asses that they were hamstrung, nor are the spoils or animals of the Madianites said to have been killed, but kept for use. But because these had not asses but horses, the Lord himself commanded them to be hamstrung. Do we think this happened by chance, that the horses were killed and the asses kept, and that anything befalls by chance in the commands of God? In short, the children of Israel are never recorded to have used horses. The law also commands nothing about horses, but about asses, as about animals that are for the labours and burdens of men; for by horses wars are waged. For the horse is an animal of wanton motion and proud neck; but asses frequently signify the Gentiles, which the Saviour himself shows, sitting upon an ass, who is never recorded to have sat upon a horse; and sending the disciples to loose the ass and the colt he says: Say that the Lord hath need of it; and sitting upon it he enters Jerusalem. Whence: "Behold thy king, meek, sitting upon a beast of burden and a young colt of an ass; and he will destroy the chariot out of Ephraim and the horse out of Jerusalem." He then who sits upon an ass destroys the chariots of Ephraim and the horse of Jerusalem. The horses and chariots that are destroyed signify those who fell from heaven through pride and wantonness, when either they offered themselves as kindlers of lust for the daughters of men, or followed him who said: "I will set my seat above the clouds, and I will be like the most High." Hence perhaps it is said: "Vain is the horse for safety"; and of those who trusted in demons: "Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; but we will call upon the name of the Lord our God." For he would not have compared chariots and horses with God as to invoking; but the nations fighting against Israel invoked the demons, the horses. And the nations coming to the faith, which are signified by the asses, are rightly kept; but by the horses and chariots the demons, the enemies of human salvation, are rightly destroyed. The passions of the body too, that is, lust, pride, wantonness and levity, on which the unhappy soul is carried as on horseback to the precipices, can be understood by the horses and chariots which are commanded to be hamstrung. For the horse is hamstrung when the body is humbled by abstinence; and the chariots are burned with fire when that is fulfilled: "I am come to cast fire on the earth", etc., of which it is said: "Was not our heart burning within us", etc. Therefore, then, the horse is called vain for safety, if the motions of our body are carried away unbridled and not restrained by the yoke of abstinence. But if anyone is stung and pricked to the heart by the words of God that we speak, and he who yesterday was carried like a horse into lust today repents, is converted and embraces a chaste life, we shall seem to have hamstrung the horses with the sword of the word of God. And whose horses are hamstrung? Those of Jabin, namely, which is interpreted prudence or sense: of him, namely, of whom it is said that "the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God"; and elsewhere: "Puffed up by the sense of his flesh." Jabin was king of Asor, which is interpreted court, and is said to have held the principality of all the kingdoms. In this court the prince of this world reigns, that is, over the earth, or rather in the vices of the flesh. The horses also of all those kings whose force we have expounded according to their names were killed by Jesus; whose vices we who serve under Jesus ought to cut off in ourselves, and to hamstring with the spiritual sword all the cavalry of the vices; we ought also to burn the chariots, that is, to cut away from us every spirit of haughtiness.
**“at this same hour, I will deliver all these to be slain in the sight of Israel: thou shalt hamstring their horses, and thou shalt burn their chariots with fire.”** — Let us fulfil in ourselves also what is said, that none be left that breathes. If anger rises in thy heart, perhaps thou wilt not fulfil its works, whether from fear of men or from fear of the judge to come. But this is not enough; not even the very stirring of anger ought to have place in thee. The very disturbance is unbecoming in one who serves under Jesus as leader. The same is to be thought of all the vices: that nothing of them breathe at all in the heart; lest perhaps, if the habit or thought of some small vice be left, it grow strong in the course of time and, lying hidden, gradually gather strength, and at last bring one back to the vomit, and the last state become worse than the first. Whence: blessed is he that taketh and dasheth the little ones, namely, against the rock, [the little ones] of Babylon, namely the evil thoughts which confound and disturb the heart; which, at the beginning, while they are small, are to be seized and dashed against the rock, which is Christ, and at his command slain, that nothing may remain in us that breathes.
11.9: **“And he did as the Lord had commanded him, he hamstringed their horses and burned their chariots with fire.”** — the demons, the proud, the wanton; whence: "Vain is the horse for safety" and "Some in chariots, and some in horses"
11.11:
**“And he cut off all the souls that abode there: he left not in it any remains,”** — of the malignant spirits or of the vices
**“but utterly destroyed all, and burned the city itself with fire.”** — of the eternal fire, of which it is said: "I am come to cast fire on the earth"
11.12:
**“And all the cities round about,”** — the souls
**“and their kings, he took and put to the sword and destroyed,”**
• the opposing powers
• "In the morning I put to death all the wicked of the land: that I might cut off from the city of the Lord", etc.
**“as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded him.”**
• the law; whence: "They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them"
• AS MOSES APPOINTED HIM, etc. "This is the word of the law, according to that: They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them." The law therefore commanded us to kill all the kings of sin who provoke us to sin. So Jesus did, nor did he transgress anything. For it is he who destroys the vices in us and the kingdoms of sin. Christ himself also did all that Moses commanded in the law. Whence: "God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law", etc. For he fulfilled all that the law commanded, that he might redeem us from the curse of the law; who says: "I am not come to destroy the law, but to fulfil."
11.15:
**“As the Lord had commanded Moses his servant, so did Moses command Josue, and he accomplished all.”** — because he came not to destroy the law, but to fulfil
**“AS THE LORD COMMANDED MOSES HIS SERVANT, AND MOSES COMMANDED JESUS”** — AUGUSTINE. It is not to be thought cruelty that Jesus left no one alive in the cities delivered to him, because God had commanded this. But those who think from this that God himself was cruel, and therefore will not believe that the true God was the author of the Old Testament, judge as perversely of the works of God as of the sins of men, not knowing what each deserves, and thinking it a great evil when things that are to fall are cast down and mortals die.
11.17:
**“And part of the mountain that goeth up to Seir as far as Baalgad, by the plain of Libanus under mount Hermon: all their kings”** — of sin, namely, that sin may not reign in us
**“he took, smote and slew.”** — AND ALL THEIR KINGS HE TOOK AND SMOTE. ADAMANTIUS. Sin reigned in all of us, and there was in all a general kingdom of sin. Whence: "For all have sinned, and do need the glory of God." For each one had in himself a spiritual king: either avarice, or pride, or lying, or the like. Whence Paul says: "Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body", etc. But after Jesus came he killed all the kings who reigned in us, and commanded all to be killed; for he who keeps any alive in himself cannot be in the army of Jesus. If avarice, boasting, lust, pride or the like reigns in thee, thou art not an Israelite soldier, nor dost thou fulfil the command which the Lord gave to Jesus.
11.19:
**“AND THERE WAS NOT A CITY THAT WAS NOT DELIVERED TO THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL”** — AUGUSTINE. It is asked how this is true, since neither afterwards in the time of the Judges nor of the Kings could the Hebrews take all the cities of those seven nations without exception. But either it is to be understood thus, that Jesus approached no city in war which he did not take; or certainly that none of them was taken but of those that were in the regions mentioned above. For the regions are enumerated in which were the cities of which this conclusion was made: and he took all in war.
**“ADAMANTIUS”** — "And Jesus took in war all who had come out to war." For Jesus is superior to all, because it was brought about by God that they were emboldened and came out against Israel to battle. He did not say that Jesus took some in war and some not, but he took all and destroyed them. For the Lord Jesus purged all the kinds of sin and destroyed them all. For we were all unwise, incredulous, erring, serving divers desires and any sins whatever. Jesus therefore killed all who had come out to war. For Jesus, the Word of God and the Wisdom of the Father, is superior to all; whence Paul says: "And such some of you were; but you are washed, but you are justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ." So, then, he took and destroyed all, because it was brought about by the Lord that their heart was emboldened and they came out to battle against Israel, that they might be exterminated. For as long as the hostile powers which work sins in us do not come, nor provoke us to fight or to struggle, they cannot be killed nor exterminated. Therefore God is said to permit, nay almost to stir up, the adversary powers to come against us in battle, that we may conquer and they may perish. Their number seems to me infinite, because with almost each single man there are some spirits who contrive the different kinds of sins. There is a spirit of fornication, there is a spirit of anger, there is another of avarice, another of pride; and if it happen that there is someone who is driven by all these evils, or even by more, he is to be thought to have all these, or even more, spirits in him. Whence there are to be believed to be many with each, because single men have not single vices but many. Nor is it to be thought that one spirit of fornication seduces him who commits fornication in Britain and him who does so in India or in other places; nor that there is one spirit of anger which drives different men in different places. But I think rather that there is one spirit of fornication and innumerable ones who obey him in this office, and with each man different spirits serving under that prince, who solicit them to sins of this kind. Similarly I think there is one prince of anger and innumerable ones under him; and the same is to be thought of the other sins. Therefore not one principality is spoken of by the Apostle, but many, against whom we have to fight.
**“There was not a city that delivered itself to the children of Israel, except the Hevite, who dwelt in Gabaon: for he took all by fight.”** — Yet I think there is a prince of all these, more eminent in wickedness and stronger in crime, who, as the leader of all the princes and the master of the whole army, drives the whole world, which these solicit one by one; who is signified by Jabin. And I think that the saints, fighting against these instigators of sins and conquering them one by one, diminish the army of the demons, and as it were kill very many horses. For example, if one who by living chastely has overcome the spirit of fornication, it is no longer lawful for that spirit which was overcome by him to assail another man; but, like that spirit which asked Jesus not to be sent into the abyss, it seems to follow that each one, conquered, is led away either into the abyss, or into the exterior darkness, or into a place worthy of him, by the just judge Christ. And hence it is that, a very great number of demons being now conquered, the Gentiles are let come to the faith. But if it seems hard to anyone, or fabulous, that very many demons are in single sinners, let him return to the authority of the Gospel, and he will find that the demoniac who dwelt in the tombs, when he was asked by Christ, What is thy name?, answered, Legion. What wonder, then, if single demons are ascribed to the single kinds of sins, when it is written that a whole legion was in one man? There are, then, in their hands two-edged swords, which destroy the opposing powers. Hence Paul says: "The God of peace crush Satan under your feet speedily." For if Satan is one, how can he have been crushed and work again? Perhaps, then, there are to be thought as many Satans as there are who do his works. Whence it seems to be said in Wisdom too "that the wicked man, cursing Satan, curseth his own soul". In the little book also which is called the Testament of the Twelve Patriarchs, which is not held in the canon, I found that by single sinners single Satans ought to be understood. Moreover, Satan is called adversary; all, then, who oppose the will of God can be called Satans. Blessed then is he who, holding the spiritual sword, does not take it away from the necks of these enemies. Whence Jeremias: "Cursed be he that doth the work of God deceitfully, and that withholdeth his sword from blood" of the wicked. If we understand this according to the letter, we must needs shed blood unceasingly; which the Jews thinking, become cruel and swift to shed blood. But let us not take away the sword of the word of God from the blood of the opposing powers, which are slain when we do not do their works.
**“AUGUSTINE”** — "Because it was brought about by the Lord that their heart was emboldened, so that they went out to war against Israel, that they might be exterminated, so that no mercy was given them, but they were exterminated, as the Lord said to Moses", etc. It is said, "by the Lord to be emboldened", that is, their heart to be hardened, as of Pharao; that this is done by divine and deep judgment is not to be doubted, when God forsakes and the enemy takes charge; which is to be taken here as there. But here something else stirs us: how it is said that the heart was emboldened to this end, that they rose up to war against Israel, and therefore were not shown mercy, although [it would be] against God's command. It must be understood to have been said to this end, that these fought in such a way that they were not spared, nor were the Israelites, neglecting God's command, bent to mercy by them. Which indeed is not to be believed could have happened under the leadership of Jesus, who diligently kept the precepts of God. But neither would he have destroyed them so quickly unless they had come against him in closest conspiracy; and so it could happen that, if they had not been overthrown by him who took care to fulfil the precepts of God, they would have remained until that time when they could be spared. After the death of Jesus they spared them, only subjecting them to their rule; and some they could not even conquer. But these things were not done under his leadership, but when, now old, he was resting from war, only dividing the land to them, so that they themselves, without him making war, took the lands divided to them partly by fighting.
11.20: **“For it was the sentence of the Lord, that their hearts should be hardened, and they should fight against them, and fall, and should not deserve any clemency, and should be destroyed as the Lord had commanded Moses.”** — For the demons are permitted by the Lord, or rather stirred up, to come against us in battle, that we may conquer and they may perish.
11.23:
**“So Josue took all the land,”** — not the son of Nave, who held Judea alone, but Jesus Christ, to whom the multitude of believers runs together from every land and every nation
**“THE LAND RESTED FROM WARS”** — Not under Jesus son of Nave, under whom it hardly ever ceased from wars, but under Jesus Christ. For thou hast come to Jesus and in baptism obtained the remission of sins, and now in thee the flesh does not fight against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh. Thy land, then, has ceased from wars, if only thou bear about the death of Jesus in thy body, that, all battles in thee ceasing, thou mayst be made a true peacemaker and be called a son of God. But this will be when thou hast gone through the wars and subdued the adversaries; then thou shalt rest under thy vine, which is Christ, and under thy fig tree, which is the Holy Ghost.

13.1:
**“Josue”** — Jesus Christ, the beginning and "the firstborn of every creature"
**“was old, and far advanced in years”**
• advanced from "the evil days", and few, to the eternal days
• JOSUE WAS OLD, etc. Thou art grown old and advanced in age. ADAMANTIUS. Priests and elders are so called not for long life, but for ripeness of sense and the gravity of a life to be revered, especially when "full of days" is added. For if anyone were called a priest or elder for length [of years], the first Adam, or Mathusala, or Noe, who lived longer than the rest, would be ranked by this name. But Abraham, who lived less, is the first in the Scriptures to be called a priest or elder. For the Lord said to Moses: "Choose thee out of all the people elders whom thou thyself knowest" to be elders. Observe too whether anywhere you find a sinner called an elder and "full of days". Now therefore it is the voice of the Holy Ghost declaring Jesus an elder and advanced in days, which cannot be said of sinners. For the sinner is not advanced in days; for he does not stretch himself forth to the things that are before, but always turns back to his vomit. And therefore he is not fit for the kingdom of heaven. The Lord, then, was not speaking to Jesus of old age, which all saw and knew, but by this a great testimony of mystery was given to the son of Nave. For as this sun makes days for this world, so the Sun of justice makes spiritual days, which are lit by the brightness of truth and knowledge. If anyone, then, passes in the precepts of God this present life, which, as Jacob says, is of few and evil days, and keeps himself unspotted from this world, and subdues all his spiritual enemies, he will be advanced from these few and evil days to the eternal days, marked by the light of the eternal Sun. So, then, Jesus is said by the divine answer to be advanced in days.
• But who is so an elder and senior advanced in days as Jesus Christ, who is the beginning and the firstborn of every creature? Therefore perhaps he alone is truly called an elder, before whom there is none. Even if there are those who are called priests or elders or pontiffs, yet he, as among pontiffs he is the prince of pontiffs, so among priests or elders he is the prince of priests, as he is prince among all, because he is the head of all.
**“and the Lord said to him: Thou art grown old”** — by passing over to the eternal days
**“and advanced in age,”** — whence: "Until I make thy enemies thy footstool"
**“and there is a very large country left, which is not yet divided by lot.”**
• AND A VERY LARGE LAND IS LEFT. Another reading: And the land that is left is very much. Above it was said that the land ceased from wars, and that Jesus took all the land; yet it is not to be thought that Scripture is contrary to itself. For in the spiritual understanding you will find nothing contrary. Look at the first coming of our Saviour, when he came to sow the seed, or his word: for he took all the land by the mere casting of the seed, and put to flight the opposing powers which had besieged the minds of the Gentiles, and sowed the word, and spread the churches. This is his first possession of the whole land. See how he takes the land also a second time, which is now said to be left in great part. For Paul says of him: "For he must reign, until he hath put [all his] enemies [under his feet as] a footstool", etc. This is the land which is now said to be left, until all things without exception are made subject under his feet.
• THIS IS THE LAND THAT IS LEFT. All the borders of the Philistines, and the rest that follow. Many things remain which we see not yet subjected, all of which must be subjected. For there can be no end unless all things have been subjected to him. Whence all nations shall serve him. In the second coming, then, Jesus will obtain this great land. But blessed are they who were obtained at his first coming. For these will come into grace who, while many adversaries resist, receive the inheritance of the land of promise by war and arms. But he who will be subjected of necessity, when the last enemy, death, shall be destroyed, will not be in grace.
13.6:
**“Of all that dwell in the mountains from Libanus, to the waters of Maserephoth, and all the Sidonians. I am he that will cut them off from before the face of the children of Israel.”** — Sidonians, that is, hunters, of whom it is said: "Our soul hath been delivered as a sparrow out of the snare of the fowlers."
**“AND ALL THE SIDONIANS”** — I AM [HE]. ADAMANTIUS. When Jesus had enumerated very many nations, of the Sidonians alone he said: And all the Sidonians I will exterminate from the face of the children of Israel. Sidonians are interpreted hunters. These are the demons of whom the Prophet says: "They prepared a snare for my feet." These the Lord exterminates, that there be none to spread snares and nets to deceive souls, and that every one may rest under his vine and under his fig tree.
13.7:
**“AND NOW DIVIDE”** — AND NOW DIVIDE. After this it is read that Moses gave an inheritance to some, and afterwards Jesus, according to the command of the Lord, distributed the inheritance. By Moses understand the law: those who lived according to the law received the inheritance first, but outside the land of promise. And when they had received it, they do not possess it nor divide it among themselves, but wait until it be distributed to them by lot through Jesus. Hence the Apostle says: All these, being approved by the testimony of faith, received not the promises, God providing some better thing for us, that they should not be perfected without us. They have therefore their promise already, and have rested, judged worthy through Moses to take their inheritance; but they still fight for those who serve under Jesus. For all the fathers who have slept before us fight with us and help us with their prayers. Whence: That synagogue will lick up this synagogue, as the calf licketh up the green grass of the field. For the synagogue of the Lord that went before us will consume the opposing synagogue with mouth and tongue, that is, it will consume our adversaries with prayers. With prayers, then, and with meditation on the word of God and right sense, we must fight.
**“ADAMANTIUS”** — ADAMANTIUS. As they who receive the law, which is the shadow of the true law, serve the pattern and shadow of heavenly things, so they who divide the inheritance of the land in Judea follow the pattern and shadow of the heavenly division. For the truth is in heaven, the shadow on earth. While this stood on earth, there was an earthly Jerusalem, and a temple, and an altar, and a visible worship; there were pontiffs and priests, the cities and villages of Judea, and all the things that are written in this book. But when at the coming of Christ the truth, descending from heaven, sprang out of the earth, and justice looked down from heaven, the shadows fell; the altar and the temple fell, so that now there is no place, neither on mount Garizim nor in Jerusalem, where men ought to adore, but the true adorers adore the Father in spirit and in truth. The truth being present, then, the shadow ceased. And when the temple was present which was built in the womb of the virgin by the Spirit of God and the power of the most High, the temple built of stones was destroyed. The high priest of the good things to come is present, and the pontiffs of bulls and goats cease. The Lamb has come that taketh away the sins of the world, and the lamb taken from the flocks ceases, slain to no purpose for so many ages. It followed, then, that, the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven being opened, the earthly inheritance should cease, and, all these ceasing, every mouth should be stopped and all the world be made subject to God. For divine providence ordered all these things to be taken away for this reason, that, the figures ceasing, they might receive a certain way of truth. The whole earthly Jerusalem has been overthrown, but we have the heavenly, which is the mother of all. By the mercy of God, then, the earthly inheritance has been taken from us, that we may seek an inheritance in heaven. And so a first and a second division of the inheritance is related: the first indeed was made through Moses, the second and mightier through Jesus. Moses gave possession beyond the Jordan to Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses; but all the others receive their inheritance through Jesus.
13.14:
**“But to the tribe of Levi he gave no possession”** — because he could not say: "Sell all that thou hast and give to the poor", etc. For this is to give a portion to the Levites. For Christ, who said these and such things, gave the Levites a portion.
**“BUT TO THE TRIBE OF LEVI”** — But neither Moses nor Jesus gave an inheritance to the Levites, because God himself is their inheritance. These perhaps are they who in the Church go before others in strength of soul and grace of merits. These perhaps are they who among the people of the saved give their labour to wisdom and knowledge, and keep their mind pure and cultivate it with all excellent virtues, and teach the simpler how they may come to the Saviour. Their inheritance is the Lord himself, who is the wisdom which they have loved above all things.
13.15: **“And Moses gave a possession to the children of Ruben according to their kindreds.”** — TO THE TRIBE OF THE CHILDREN OF RUBEN, etc. Yet I find a certain difference between the things which Moses distributed and those which Jesus [distributed]. For Moses, giving inheritance to two tribes and a half, gave no portion to the Levites. But Jesus, not only in those tribes to which he divided the land, but also in those to which Moses had divided it, decreed dwellings for the Levites in each tribe. For the levitical or priestly order, which spends its labour on the wisdom and knowledge of God, could not receive a lot of habitation from Moses, who was the minister not of the truth but of the shadow and pattern. But our Jesus, who is the wisdom of God, provides dwellings for the wise. Moses could not say: "Sell all that thou hast and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me." This is to give a portion to the Levites. Nor could he say: "He that doth not renounce all that he possesseth cannot be my disciple", nor the other: "Every one that hateth not father and mother and brothers and sisters", etc. Therefore he could not dispense the dwellings of the priests and Levites. Blessed, then, is he who is found worthy to receive from Jesus a lot of the heavenly mansion, of which Jesus says: "Father, I will that where I am, these also may be with me; and as I in thee and thou in me are one, these also may be one in us." Yet those whose inheritance is said to be the wisdom of God, the Word, truth and justice, receive habitation meanwhile with those whose inheritance is on earth, that those who cannot by themselves may through them be made partakers of the wisdom and knowledge of God; and so the divine dispensation reaches to the least, that that may be fulfilled: He that had much had nothing over, and he that had little had no lack. And what the Apostle says: "That your abundance may supply their want", etc. Thus, then, the priest and the Levite, who have no land, are commanded to dwell together [with the Israelites], that the priest and the Levite may receive from the Israelite the earthly things which they have not, and the Israelite from the priest and the Levite the heavenly and divine things which he has not. For the law of God is committed to the priests and Levites, that they may give their labour to this alone and be free for the word of God without any care, sustained by the ministries of the laity. For if [the laity] do not provide them with necessaries, they will be less free for the law of God, being occupied with bodily cares, and the laity will be in peril. For the light of knowledge that is in them will be darkened, thou not supplying oil to the lamp; and by thy fault the blind leading the blind will fall with him into the ditch.
13.32: **“THIS POSSESSION”** — THIS POSSESSION. ADAMANTIUS. Let us learn from the law how necessarily the division of the land is described, which is said [to be made] first through Moses, secondly through Jesus, not that we may keep both, but that, learning the reason of each, we may hold that one alone which is delivered to us by Jesus Christ. That land, then, which is beyond the Jordan Moses distributed; but this which is in the holy land, Jesus and the princes of the tribes. You see that when the true inheritance of the holy land began to be distributed, the princes of the tribes of the true and spiritual Israel are taken up. These are the apostles, to whom it is said: You also shall sit on seats judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The priest too is taken up, that is, the mystical word of God. For so it says, that Jesus and Eleazar came together to divide the land.
13.33: **“But to the tribe of Levi he gave no possession: because the Lord God”** — who is wisdom and knowledge, to whom alone the Levites and priests give their labour

14.1:
**“This is what the children of Israel possessed in the land of Chanaan, which Eleazar the priest”** — the hidden and mystical word of God
**“and Josue”** — Christ
**“the son of Nun, and the princes of the families by the tribes of Israel”** — the apostles, to whom it is said: "You also shall sit judging the twelve tribes of Israel."
14.2: **“DIVIDING ALL BY LOT”** — ISIDORE. The nations destroyed, Josue divides the land of promise to the peoples by lot; Christ too cast out the nations, that is, the spirits of the errors of the Gentiles, from before the face of his faithful, and divided the land by lot, bestowing on each his own gifts.
14.3:
**“For to two tribes and a half Moses had given possession beyond the Jordan”** — lest, occupied with temporal things, they should serve heavenly things the less
**“FOR TO TWO TRIBES”** — ISIDORE. Moses decreed possession beyond the Jordan to two tribes and a half only, but all the rest receive it through Jesus, because more receive the heavenly promises through the faith of Jesus Christ than through the law. For the two and a half tribes figured the former people, which had indeed knowledge of the Trinity, but not perfect. But the nine and a half tribes which receive the promise of the holy land through Jesus signify the new people, which receive from Jesus Christ, through faith and grace, the inheritance of the eternal promise after the laver, as after the crossing of the Jordan. But these too do not reach the number ten, which is as it were perfect, because not even at the coming of the Lord itself were all things perfectly announced to us. Whence: I have yet many things to say to you, but [you cannot bear them now]; but the Spirit of truth, who proceedeth from the Father, will announce to you all things. The perfection, then, and sum of all good things is in the Holy Ghost.
**“BESIDES THE LEVITES, WHO [RECEIVED] NO [LAND]”** — ISIDORE. The Levites do not receive an inheritance of the land, because Jesus Christ is their inheritance, according to that: I am their inheritance, and no possession shall be given them in Israel; for I am their possession. For [he is] the inheritance and possession of the clergy. Therefore God willed it to be said, because they were made the ministers of his altar and [his] lot. Whence also clergy is interpreted lot. Rightly therefore do they possess God for an inheritance who, that they may be able to serve God without hindrance, desire to be poor in spirit, that they may be able to say: The Lord is the portion of my inheritance, etc.
14.4: **“NEITHER DID THE LEVITES RECEIVE”** — ISIDORE. Jesus decrees dwellings for the Levites throughout all the tribes, that those who in the Church of the Lord give their labour to knowledge and administer the grace of doctrine may receive earthly support from those to whom they dispense divine things. Whence Paul: If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great matter if we reap your carnal things? And rightly are they divided among all the tribes, who live by the dispensation of all.
14.6:
**“Then the children of Juda came to Josue in Galgal, and Caleb spoke to him”** — as it were heart
**“AND CALEB THE SON SPOKE”** — ADAMANTIUS. Caleb, who is interpreted as it were heart, first receives an inheritance from Jesus. This is he who in all things gives his labour to understanding, who is said to be no other member of the body of the Church than the heart, which is the most excellent thing in us; that is, he who does all things with reason and prudence, and so dispenses to all as if there were no other member but the heart. And Jephone is interpreted conversion. Caleb, then, is the son of conversion. For one converted to God brings forth such fruit from himself, and the heart begets a son. Every one, then, who is free for divine senses and does all things rationally is Caleb. He indeed was instructed first by Moses, secondly by Jesus, beside whom he stood, and says: Thou knowest the word that the Lord spoke to Moses, etc. Who else can know the word that the Lord spoke to Moses but Jesus alone? For none understood the law as Jesus taught it. For he taught and opened all things. He revealed to Paul that the law was spiritual, etc.
**“the son of Jephone”** — of conversion
**“the Cenezite: Thou knowest what the Lord spoke to Moses the man of God”**
• Christ alone knew what the Lord spoke to Moses. For none so understood the law. He taught and opened all things.
• THOU KNOWEST WHAT THE LORD SPOKE, etc. ADAMANTIUS. This is what the Lord said: If you did believe Moses, you would believe me also; for he wrote of me. And "of me", that is, Caleb, who is the heart, he said; for it is certain that Moses wrote of the heart, because he wrote all things wisely.
**“concerning me and thee in Cadesbarne”**
• Moses, of whom it is said: "For he wrote of me"
• "If you did believe Moses, you would believe me also."
14.11: **“As strong as I was at that time when I was sent to view the land: the strength of that time continueth in me until this day, as well to fight as to march.”** — AS STRONG, etc. For the saint is equally strong in things present and in things past, in new and in old, in the Gospels and in the law. This, then, is why he now says that he is strong under Jesus as he was then with Moses, because the watchful heart is strong in the mysteries of both testaments.
14.12:
**“GIVE ME THEREFORE THIS MOUNTAIN”** — The saint seeks nothing lowly, nothing cast down, but a high mountain, in which are great and fortified cities, because the wise man takes fortified cities and destroys the strongholds in which the wicked trust.
**“WHEREIN ARE THE ENACIMS, AND CITIES”** — ADAMANTIUS. The cities and walls are the doctrines of the wicked and the syllogisms of the Prophets [so the edition], by which they build up every impious thing contrary to the divine law. Those too are fortified cities set on mountains, which the heretics place by assertions from the Scriptures as on high mountains. These cities every wise man who preaches the word of truth destroys, and he overturns the cities of falsehood with the ram of truth. So the most wise Caleb, standing before Jesus, promises that he is the stronger for battle, and therefore asks that leave be granted him to dispute with the dialecticians of the world, who confirm false things for true, that he may overturn all that they build with false assertions. Jesus, seeing his eagerness, blesses him who asks and dares such things. Thou too, if thou wilt give thy labour to study and meditate prudently on the law of God and be made a heart in the law of God, canst overturn these great and fortified cities, that is, false assertions, that thou too mayst merit to be blessed by Jesus and to receive Hebron, which is interpreted joining or marriage. By this perhaps can be shown that the double cave bought by the patriarch Abraham is in it, in which lie the marriages of the fathers and their remains, that is, Abraham with Sara, Isaac with Rebecca, Jacob with Lia. Caleb therefore merited to receive the remains of the fathers for an inheritance, because by the wisdom in which he flourished under Moses and Jesus he had understood the reason of the joinings, and what cause there was that with Abraham Sara alone lay there, and neither Agar nor Cetura merited to be joined to him; or why with Jacob Lia alone lay, and neither Rachel, though more loved, nor any of the concubines was coupled with him in the tomb. In the memorials of the fathers, then, wise Caleb takes his inheritance. To him Jesus gives Hebron, the metropolis of the race of the Enacites, and it becomes his lot until this present day. Would that the lot of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were given to me too, that my God might be made [mine], as he was made the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, in Christ Jesus.
14.13:
**“And Josue blessed him”** — because he asks and dares such things
**“and gave him Hebron”** — which is interpreted joining or marriage
14.15:
**“The name of Hebron before was called Cariath-Arbe.”** — the city of four
**“Adam the greatest among the Enacims was laid there: and the land rested from wars.”**
• If thou wilt have an inheritance from Jesus, the land of thy flesh must rest and not fight against the spirit.
• AND THE LAND CEASED FROM, etc. ADAMANTIUS. This is not written in the distribution of Moses, but in the distribution of Jesus. If then thou wilt be made worthy to obtain an inheritance from Jesus, thou must first finish all wars and stand in peace, that it may be said of the land of thy flesh that the land ceased from wars. And whereas it is the custom of holy Scripture to name the four parts of the world, which they call axes or quarters, in the description of the borders of the tribe of Juda only two are named. And the borders, it says, of the children of the tribe of Juda according to their peoples were from the borders of Idumea, from the desert of Sinai, to the west. And when it had described the borders from the west, it says: and from the east the salt sea. But of the north and the south it was silent. The first borders of Judea, then, are the borders of Idumea, which is interpreted earthly; after earthly things, then, the borders of Judea follow at once, but from the desert, it says, of Sinai, that is, of temptations: after temptations, then, follow the borders of the inheritance of Juda. East and west name the neighbouring places of which we spoke above, that is, the confines. The valley of Egypt too is marked as neighbouring the western parts, which is from the desert on the west. But on the east the borders are girt by the salt sea. After this: from the hills, it says, which stretch to the west, and thence it goes up to the west as far as Cadesbarne, and so it stretches from the west to Cades. These are their borders on the side of the Africus, and thence it went on to the valley of Egypt. See how in the parts of the west it names the Africus, Egypt and the setting, that each may know that these must be passed through by him, and so at last he may come to the royal tribe from which our Lord sprang. Now from the borders of Idumea is the desert of Sinai. Therefore it is necessary for us to pass through the desert of temptations, that we may be able to come to the inheritance of the children of Juda. We must also go up the ascent of the hills of Accabim, which is interpreted scorpions, because the scorpions must be passed by us and trodden on, of which it is said: Behold, I have given you power to tread upon scorpions and serpents, etc. Let him, then, who will enter into the inheritance of the tribe of Juda go up these ascents, tread on and escape these scorpions. Perhaps to Ezechiel making this journey the Lord said: Son of man, thou dwellest in the midst of scorpions. And the borders are, it says, as far as Cadesbarne. Cades is interpreted holy or sanctification. The borders of Juda, then, reach as far as sanctification. It is said too that on the eastern side of the tribe of Juda is the salt sea, and after this, in its part, the fountain of the sun and the city of the sun are named; and in the same tribe is also the city of letters. Everyone, therefore, who would enter into the portion of the children of Juda must first pass the salt sea, that is, overcome the waves and whirlwinds of this world, and escape all the things of this world which, for their uncertainty and slipperiness, are compared to the waves of the sea, that he may be able to come to the land of Juda, and to the fountain of the Sun of justice, which is the fountain of water springing up into life everlasting, and afterwards find the city of the Sun of justice. There is in Egypt too a city of the sun, but that took its name from this sun which the heavenly Father commands to rise upon the good and the bad. But that which is in Judea is made [the city] of the saints only, because it is the city of God; and that fountain mentioned above, made a river, maketh the city of God joyful. Thou too, if thou be fortified on every side and girt with the wall of continence, perfected with the towers of patience and magnanimity, shalt be made a city of God. But if to this thou add the light of the knowledge of God, and the Sun of justice shine upon thee, thou shalt be made a city of the sun, or perhaps shalt inherit the city of the sun. And if thou study in the law of God day and night, and the book of the law depart not from thy hand, thy inheritance too shall be made the city of letters.

15.1:
**“ADAMANTIUS”** — ADAMANTIUS. Not a little profit is conferred on the soul when the reading of the divine word, even if obscure, glides into our ears. For it is believed by the Gentiles that by certain chants, which they call incantations, those whose art this is, whispering certain compiled names, even names which not even those who invoke them know, by the mere sound of the voice lull serpents to sleep or even draw them out of their holes; and often in human bodies swellings or fevers or other such things are said to be loosed or repressed by the voice alone; and sometimes too a certain stupor of sense is said to be inflicted on the soul, if only the faith of Christ have not resisted. If so, how much more must we believe that any naming whatever of holy Scripture, whether of its words or of its names, is to be held more powerful than every incantation and chant! For as among unbelievers the contrary powers, hearing those names, are present, and also give their labour to that for which they perceive themselves invoked by this or that name, spending the service of their office on the thing to which they have bound themselves, much more do the heavenly powers who are with us gladly receive it if we bring forth from our mouth the words of Scripture and the namings of these names as certain chants and incantations. And even if we do not understand them, those powers understand, and, as if invited by a chant, delight to be present with us and to bring help. For divine powers are not only around us but also within us; whence: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and let all that is within me [bless] his holy name, that is, all things that are within me. It is certain, then, that there are many powers within us, to which the care of our souls or bodies is committed. If they are holy, they are delighted when the Scriptures are read by us, and become stronger toward our diligence, even if our understanding be without fruit; according to that of the Apostle: If we speak with tongues and our spirit prays, but our understanding is without fruit. The Apostle once brought forth a wonderful mystery in this, namely that it can be that the spirit which is in us prays and our understanding is without fruit. For those powers which are given to help our soul are refreshed by the hearing of holy Scripture as by divine and rational foods, when we bring forth from our mouth according to the divine words. Christ himself too, if he find us free for such studies, not only deigns to be refreshed and fed in us, but, if he see these banquets prepared with us, will also bring the Father with him, according to that: I and the Father will come and will make our abode with him. But as by such meditations we call forth the fellowship and services of the divine [powers], so by the namings of such words and names we put to flight the snares of the malignant powers and the assaults of the demons. For example: as one may see a serpent lulled by incantations carried in the hands, or drawn out of its holes, able to do no harm, its poisons benumbed by the power of the incantations, so, by the power of the divine reading, if there be within us any serpent of the contrary power, it is driven out by the chants, if thou bear patiently, that is, if thou turn not away thy hearing for weariness. If, then, an obscure Scripture which thou understandest not is read to thee, receive this profit meanwhile; only take care that thou become not like the deaf asps, which hear not the voice of the charmer and of the wizard that charmeth wisely. For there is a chant that is chanted by the wise Jesus son of Nave and by all the prophets. Let us not, then, be weary of hearing the holy Scriptures, even if we do not understand; but it will be done to us according to our faith, believing that all Scripture divinely inspired is profitable, even if we do not perceive the profit. Physicians sometimes give a food or a drink, for example, to dispel the dimness of the eyes, and yet in eating or drinking we do not perceive that it helps; but when one day and another and a third have passed, in its own time the power of the food or drink, carried by hidden passages to the sight, little by little purges the vision.
**“Now the lot of the children of Juda by their kindreds was this: From the frontier of Edom”** — which is interpreted earthly
**“to the desert of Sin”** — of temptation
15.2: **“Its beginning was from the top of the most salt sea”** — of the fruits of the world, namely
15.3: **“And it goeth out towards the ascent of the Scorpion”** — "I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions."
15.7:
**“the fountain”** — "of water springing up into life everlasting"
**“of the sun”** — of justice
15.13:
**“But to Caleb the son of Jephone”**
• of conversion
• BUT TO CALEB THE SON OF JEPHONE HE GAVE, etc. ADAMANTIUS. The distribution of Jesus begins from Caleb. For the lot of his portion was given to him before his tribe, that is, the tribe of Juda, received [its own], and not in the outermost parts but in the midst of the children of Juda; and not by lot, but by the command of the Lord, a whole city is given him. For whom else was it fitting to obtain such an inheritance but Caleb, who alone was saved with Jesus out of the six hundred thousand armed men who had gone out of Egypt? And he it is who must receive the metropolis. Therefore Jesus gave him the city of Arboc, the metropolis of Enach, which is Hebron, in which were the memorials of the fathers; and he exterminated from it the three sons of Enach. First, then, let us discuss why Caleb received a metropolis, and that one which is called the first metropolis among all in the land, and the metropolis of Enach, which is interpreted empty humility. Now there are two humilities: one praiseworthy, of which it is said: Learn of me, because I am meek and humble of heart, etc.; and: He that humbleth himself shall be exalted, etc.; and: Be you humbled under the mighty hand of God; the other blameworthy, of which it is said that Ammon humbled Thamar his sister. This is the empty humility which comes down from sin. Caleb took and cut down its metropolis, and killed the three sons of Enach, that is, of empty humility, and dwelt in the city. The first is the son Susi, that is, outside me: this is outside the holy, for the son of empty humility is outside the holy, nay outside God. Another is Achimaau, which is interpreted my brother without counsel. For all the brothers who are born of empty humility are outside counsel. The third is Thalamin, which is interpreted a precipice or suspension, because there is nothing of stability in him, but all things wandering and rushing headlong. These exterminated, he went up into Dabir, whose name before was the city of letters. Now Dabir is interpreted speech. By the city of letters, then, understand the whole instrument of the Old Testament, such as this very scripture which we are expounding, which afterwards is made Dabir, that is, speech. For what before was in letters and was understood according to the letter has now in the churches of Christ been made speech, as they speak of it and discuss it: first the apostles, removing the surface of the letter and bringing it forth into spiritual speech; then the doctors one by one, making of the single letters speech and angelic disputation. And who are the three sons of Enach whom Caleb killed, to whose person we have ascribed the power of the law among earthly things? The empty humility is that which the poets or philosophers thought of the divinity. For the things they thought are lowly and unworthy of God. For what is so emptily lowly as to think wood and stones gods? Of this empty humility the first son is he who is called outside me, that is, their first sense is outside the truth and outside God. The second is Achiman, that is, brother without counsel, which is to leave God, who made us, and to follow strange gods, whom we made. The third sense of error is Thalamin, which is a precipice or suspension, because the last things of this error tend to the precipice and to the depth of hell. These senses of heathenism, as the sons of Enach of the old error, the law cut off, which even according to the letter preaches the true God, the creator of all. But now Caleb goes up to this city of letters and said: Whosoever shall cut down the city of letters and obtain it, I will give him Axa my daughter to wife, etc. Gothoniel, who took the city of letters, is interpreted the answer of God. And he is called the answer of God to whom God answers, that is, to whom he reveals secrets. He, then, who can take the city of letters of the Old Testament and cut away the letter that killeth is the younger brother of Caleb. This am I, who, the letter of the law being cut away, seek in it the spiritual sense. And I cut away the letter when I am not circumcised according to the flesh, nor eat unleavened bread according to the flesh, nor keep the Pasch with the Jews, or the like, etc. For there is promised to me, if I cut down the city of letters, the daughter of my elder brother. For he was the son of Cenez, which is interpreted contempt. For who was so a contempt as we Gentiles, alienated from the conversation of Israel? For my former brother, whose daughter I receive because I cut down the city of letters, was the son of Jephone, which is interpreted conversion. The law, then, gives to me, the younger brother, its daughter, that is, the understanding of itself; whence: The kingdom of God shall be taken from you and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof. Yet it must be known that the law, whose person we have now given to Caleb, is one thing, and the letter of the Old Testament, that is, the city of letters, another. Having received his daughter, then, I, his younger brother, lead her from her father's house. And as she was coming with me, sitting on the ass which the disciples of Christ loosed, she says to her father: Give me thy blessing, father. And she received the upper Gonechla and the lower Gonechla, that is, the promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come, a hundredfold in this present world and life everlasting in the world to come.
**“he gave a portion in the midst”** — not in the outermost parts
**“of the children of Juda, as”** — not by lot
**“the Lord had commanded him: Cariath-Arbe the father of Enac”** — which is interpreted empty humility or empty answer
15.14:
**“And Caleb destroyed out of it the three sons of Enac, Sesai and Ahiman”** — my brother outside counsel, that is, without counsel. For all the sons of empty humility are outside counsel.
**“and Tholmai”** — The Seventy: Thalamin, that is, a precipice or suspension, as it were wandering, namely, and headlong
15.15: **“And going up from thence he came to the inhabitants of Dabir”** — which is interpreted speech
15.16:
**“And Caleb said”** — that he may fulfil or understand it not carnally but spiritually
**“He that shall smite Cariath-Sepher”** — the city of letters, namely, of the Old Testament
**“and take it, I will give him Axa my daughter to wife.”** — the understanding of the law, namely
15.17:
**“And Othoniel took it”** — Gothoniel: the answer of God, namely he to whom God answers and reveals secrets
**“the son of Cenez, the younger brother of Caleb: and he gave him Axa his daughter to wife.”** — GOTHONIEL THE SON, etc. Note that Caleb is called the son of Jephone, and Gothoniel the son of Cenez, who is the younger Caleb, that is, of his blood.
15.18:
**“And as they were going together, she was moved by her husband to ask a field of her father, and she sighed as she sat on her ass.”** — the people of the Gentiles, of whom it is said: "Loose them and bring them to me."
**“AS SHE SAT ON HER ASS”** — GREGORY. Axa sits upon an ass when the soul presides over the irrational motions of the flesh. Sighing, she asks of her father a watered land, because the grace of tears is to be sought from the Creator with great groaning. For there are some who have already received [the gift] to speak freely for justice, to protect the oppressed, to give to the needy, to have the ardour of faith, but have not yet the grace of tears. These have a southern and dry land, but still need a watered one, because, placed in good works in which they are great and fervent, they ought, from fear of punishment or love of the heavenly kingdom, to lament also the evils which they committed before. Now there are two principal kinds of compunction, because the soul that thirsts for God is pricked first by fear, afterwards by love. For first it moves itself to tears by fear, because while it recalls its evils it dreads eternal punishments for them. But when the dread has been consumed by long grief, a certain security is born from the presumption of pardon, and the mind is inflamed with the love of heavenly joys; and she who before wept lest she should be led to punishment afterwards begins to weep because she is kept from the kingdom. Her father, then, gives her the upper watered ground when she afflicts herself in tears with the desire of the heavenly kingdom; but she receives the lower watered ground when by weeping she dreads the punishments of hell. Now the lower is given first and the upper watered ground afterwards; but because the compunction of love excels in dignity, it was necessary that the upper watered ground be named first and the lower afterwards.
15.63:
**“the Jebusite”** — the cockle, namely
**“But ... that dwelt in Jerusalem”** — of the Church
**“could not”** — lest they should root up the wheat also together with it
**“the children of Juda”**
• who are "without spot or wrinkle"
• BUT THE JEBUSITE THAT DWELT, etc. ADAMANTIUS. We understand spiritually that the Jebusites, otherwise the Jebusite, dwelt with the Jews in Jerusalem until the present day, according to the parable of the Gospel which says of the cockle: Suffer both to grow, lest you root up the wheat also together. For so in Jerusalem, that is, in the Church, there are Jebusites, namely those who lead a degenerate life, faithful indeed in name, but perverse in acts, or in action and the conversation of sin. For the Church cannot be purged to clearness while it is on earth. There are in it all the saints, in whom is no stain of sin. But lest the wheat be rooted up with the cockle, there are in it some in whom are sins either doubtful or hidden. For those who are manifestly and evidently criminal are to be expelled from the Church. The children of Juda, then, could not destroy the Jebusites, but dwelt with them in Jerusalem until the present day. Jebusite is interpreted treading underfoot. We ought, then, to have the utmost caution and zeal that no one give or suffer scandal, that no one polluted enter into this congregation of the saints. Yet if we cannot cast out those who tread us underfoot, let us at least cast out those whom we can, whose sins are manifest. For where sin is not evident we can cast no one out of the Church. Now those in the Church who tread underfoot are they of whom it is said: Give not that which is holy to dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest perhaps they trample them, etc. These, then, are the Jebusites, who hear the word of God unworthily, and having heard it neither depart like unbelievers nor remain like the faithful, but, having received the knowledge of the mysteries and searched out the more secret things of our faith, turn and assail us, and break our hearts with contradictions, trampling the pearls of the word of God and staining the ornaments of the faith. These the children of Juda could not cast out of Jerusalem until the present day.
**“destroy: and the Jebusite dwelt with the children of Juda in Jerusalem until this present day.”**
• UNTIL THE PRESENT DAY, etc. The same. [It means] the eternity of the age, after the manner of Scripture; but this cannot stand according to the letter. For how does the Jebusite dwell with the children of Juda in Jerusalem as long as this age lasts, when not even the children of Juda dwell there for ever?
• [By] treading underfoot, according to the second [sense, are meant] those who make scandal in the Church, and those who, having received the knowledge of the mysteries, trample the pearls of the word of God by assailing them.
• Jerusalem is interpreted vision of peace. If, then, Jerusalem, that is, the vision of peace, is built in our heart, and we behold and keep in our heart Christ, who is ever our peace, if indeed we are so fixed and steadfast in this vision of peace that no thought of sin rises into our heart, we can say that we are Jerusalem and that none is with us but the saints alone. But now, even if we come to great perfection and cultivate ourselves with the highest zeal, I think none is so pure as not to be stained by some thought. It is certain, then, that the Jebusites too dwell with the children of Juda in Jerusalem. Yet we must labour daily to cast them out of Jerusalem; but they cannot all be cast out at once.

16.10:
**“And the children of Ephraim slew not”** — who grow and bear fruit in God
**“the Chanaanite”** — the stirring of temptations
**“who dwelt in Gazer”** — in the binding together
**“and the Chanaanite dwelt in the midst of Ephraim”** — Often the least vices are kept back, that the virtues may be held most in humility and the vices be most kept down.
**“AND THE CHANAANITE DWELT”** — AUGUSTINE. And the Chanaanite dwelt in Ephraim until this day, until Pharao king of Egypt came up and took the city and burned it with fire, and slew the Chanaanites and Pherezites who dwelt in Gazer, and gave it to his daughter for a dowry. As to what is said of Pharao, I wonder whether it be a prophecy, since this history is believed to have been written in those times when those deeds were recent. And what great thing could be chosen to be spoken prophetically, when past things are narrated, and future things, greater and more necessary, are passed over in silence? It is rather to be thought, then, that the Seventy translators, who are proved to have prophetic authority by their very wonderful agreement in translating, added these things, not as foretelling things to come, but because they lived at a time when they remembered these things done and had read them in the books of the Kingdoms. For it was done in the times of the Kings; which therefore seemed the more credible to us, because we do not find it in this translation which is from the Hebrew; as neither that about Jericho, that whoever should raise it up again would incur the curse which Jesus had spoken. For so it is written: And Jesus adjured them in that day: Cursed be the man that shall raise up that city; in his firstborn shall he lay its foundation, and in his last shall he set up its gates. But what follows is not in our text: And so did Oza, who was of Bethel; in Abiron his firstborn he founded it, and in his last, who was saved [so the edition], he set up its gates. This is not read there. Whence it appears that it was inserted by the Seventy, who knew that it had been done.
**“GREGORY”** — GREGORY. The Chanaanite, a Gentile people, signifies vice. Often we enter the land of promise in great virtues, because we are strengthened by inward hope of eternity; but while among lofty and sublime things we retain certain little vices, we as it were allow the Chanaanite to live in our land. Yet he is made tributary, because this very vice which we cannot subdue we humbly turn to the use of our profit, that the mind may think lowly of itself in the highest things, since by its own strength it does not overcome the small things which it covets. Whence again it is well written: These are the nations which the Lord left, that by them he might instruct Jerusalem [so the edition]. For to this end certain very small vices are kept, that our intention may ever exercise itself anxiously in the struggle, lest it be proud of victory, when it feels enemies living in itself by whom it still fears to be conquered. And Israel is instructed by the nations that are left, when the elation of our virtue is kept down in certain least vices, and learns, in small things that resist it, that of itself it does not subdue the greater.

17.8:
**“ADAMANTIUS”** — ADAMANTIUS. Ephraim is interpreted fruitfulness. For he who bears fruit and grows in faith cannot exterminate the Chanaanite, the worst seed, cursed, movable, uncertain. For this is what Chanaanite is interpreted; and it is certain that with him who bears fruit and grows the Chanaanite always dwells. For the stirrings of temptations never cease from him. But thou, if thou truly bearest fruit in God and seest someone such, restless, turbulent and unstable, know that he is a Chanaanite. And if thou canst not cast him out of the Church, know that the children of Ephraim could not expel the Chanaanites.
**“THE SAME”** — THE SAME. This must be understood even of those who bear fruit, because they are named sons of Ephraim. For they ought always to cast out of their souls the Chanaanites, namely wandering and slippery thoughts. But God is able to subject the Jebusites and Chanaanites to us, as it is written: He subjected the Chanaanites to the children of Ephraim.
17.12:
**“NEITHER COULD THE CHILDREN”** — NEITHER COULD THE CHILDREN. ADAMANTIUS. The Chanaanites are said a third time to be among the children of Ephraim. But the order of the sayings is to be observed in each. First, then, it was said that the children of Ephraim did not destroy the Chanaanite who dwelt in Gazer, but the Chanaanite dwelt in Ephraim until this day and was made a servant under tribute, until Pharao king of Egypt came up and took the city and burned it with fire, and slew the Chanaanites and Pherezites and those who dwelt in Gazer, and Pharao gave it for a dowry to his daughter. Secondly: And it came to pass, it says, when the children of Israel grew strong, overthrowing the Chanaanites, that they made the Chanaanites subject, but with extermination they did not exterminate them. Thirdly, when the men of the tribe of Ephraim gainsaid Jesus, wishing to receive a greater lot according to their numbers, because they were more and stronger. And they are bidden to go up to the woodland and make themselves a larger place, and, that they may occupy wider spaces, they are bidden to exterminate the Chanaanite. Let us see, then, what this threefold narration means. First the Chanaanite is with us and under tribute, yet not obedient; then he is made a servant and obedient. By the Chanaanite here we take the flesh, or the things that are of the flesh. This is first with us, that is, joined to the soul, but it is not obedient, except only that it pays tribute, that is, the service of doing or moving something. Yet it lusteth against the spirit and is not obedient to the soul. But if we have made some progress, it is made a servant and obedient to the will of the soul. And this is the second progress of the soul, when it has made the flesh obey and serve it. But the third is that which is perfect. For if we come to the perfect, the Chanaanite is said to be even exterminated by us. Whence: Mortify your members which are upon the earth: fornication, uncleanness, etc. And elsewhere: And they that are Christ's have crucified their flesh with the vices and concupiscences, etc. So, then, the third time, that is, when we have come to perfection and have mortified our members, bearing about the death of Christ in our body, the Chanaanite is said to be exterminated by us.
**“ORIGEN”** — ORIGEN. This too is not to be passed over, that it says Pharao came and took Gazer, in which the Chanaanite dwelt with Ephraim, and gave it for a dowry to his daughter. For Gazer is interpreted constriction. If body and soul dwell in one constriction, joined to each other and companions, so that the soul too lives carnally and does not make the flesh obey it, it is to be feared lest Pharao come out of Egypt and take the soul captive and hand it over for a dowry to his daughter. For another law rises in our members and takes us captive in the law of sin, to which Pharao, that is, the king of sin, makes over as a dowry the soul that lives carnally. After this we must see that the sons of Joseph ask for a greater lot, saying: Why hast thou given us one lot and one portion? But I am a great people, and the Lord hath blessed me. If, then, we are a great and blessed people, let us hear from the Lord Jesus: Thou art a great people; go up into the woodland and clear it for thyself, and prepare a place in the land, and fight the Pherezites and the Raphaim. Let us, then, cast out the Pherezites, who are interpreted fruitfulness. Now one fruitfulness is good, another evil, because a good tree makes or brings good fruits, and an evil one evil. Let us, then, expel whatever does not bear fruit well, and the fruit of sin, and let us cleanse the fruit of justice.
**“Neither could the children of Manasses overthrow these cities, but the Chanaanite began to dwell in his land.”** — RAPHAIM, it says, expel, or rather purge from thee. Raphaim is interpreted loosened mothers. There is in our soul a certain power which brings forth senses like a mother, senses which proceed from us.
