Whence: Yet she shall be saved through childbearing, if she continue in faith. These mothers, then, that is, this power of the soul, in those in whom it is strong, beget strong senses, which cannot be overcome by a gainsayer. But in others it is loosened and slack, as the senses show which it brings forth, feeble and unfit. These mothers let us purge out of us, that is, let us purge away the filth and uncleanness which through our negligence come upon the natural motions of the soul, that the natural vigour of the inborn power may shine forth.
17.16:
**“WE CANNOT [GO UP] TO THE MOUNTAINS”** — WE CANNOT [GO UP] TO THE MOUNTAINS. ADAMANTIUS. The mountain is not enough for us, and the Chanaanite who dwells in the hill country has a choice horse and iron, etc. You will never find that an Israelite has a horse; but the Chanaanite has a horse, which is a false thing for safety, and the iron of war. But Jesus answered: If thou art a great people and hast strength, thou shalt not have one lot, because the woodland is thine, and thou shalt clear it, etc. Let us, then, clear the forest which is in us, namely the useless and unfruitful trees, and make there fallow lands which we may ever renew, and take fruit thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold. Whence: The axe is laid to the root of the tree; every tree, then, that bringeth not forth good fruit shall be cut down and cast into the fire.
**“And the children of Joseph answered him: We cannot go up to the mountains, for the Chanaanites that dwell in the low lands, wherein are situate Bethsan with its towns, and Jezrael in the midst of the valley, have chariots of iron.”** — If thou clear the forest, it says, it shall be thine also, when thou hast exterminated the Chanaanite from it. Let us strive, then, to subject the Chanaanite who is with us the more quickly and make him obedient; and after this to exterminate him too. But if we let him be and neglect him, Pharao king of Egypt will come and begin to give our place for a dowry to his daughter, and to hand us over captive to the law of sin. Let us take heed, then, that we prevail against the Chanaanites, lest, if they grow strong against us, they make Chanaanites of the Israelites.

18.6:
**“I WILL CAST LOTS FOR YOU HERE”** — I WILL CAST LOTS FOR YOU HERE. ADAMANTIUS. In the custom of men, when something is divided by lot, that lot seems to fall by chance to this man, or another to another. But in holy Scripture it is not so. For it would be no wonder if Gentiles did this; but the fathers took the judgment of so great a matter by lots, or cast them. But let us see whether anything is set down in the Scriptures that may show us what power there is in lots. In Leviticus it is written: Let him take two lots, one lot for the Lord and one lot for the apopompaeus, etc. Again there: Moses divided the land by lot to the tribe of Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses. Jesus too, according to the command of the Lord, gave a lot to Caleb and to the tribe of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasses. And after this, it says, he gathered the assembly of the children of Israel and said: I will cast the lot and bring forth the lot in the sight of the Lord, etc. And after this, the lots being cast, the inheritance is thus distributed to the people, and the lot is so moved, not by chance, but according to what is predestined by God. In fact, the tribe of Benjamin received the first lot there where Jerusalem was; after it the tribe of Simeon second, after it Issachar, then Zabulon, then Aser, after them Nephtali, then Dan; among whom come last those three tribes which are from the concubines. I find in the Scriptures that the Gentiles too cast lots, when Jonas was sailing and the tempest pressed them, as if the lot should or could betray for whose cause the danger hung over them; and although they were Gentiles, strangers to the knowledge of God, they were not deceived in this opinion. For the lot revealed the truth.
**“The land in the midst between these mark ye out into seven parts; and you shall come hither to me, that I may cast lots for you before the Lord your God.”**
• SOLOMON TOO says: The lot suppresseth contentions, etc., as showing that contentions cease where the lot is cast. In the New Testament too, the Apostles, coming together, much wiser than those who now ordain bishops or priests or deacons, chose two. Yet they did not judge of them so as to make him an Apostle whom they wished, but praying they cast the lot, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was numbered with the eleven apostles and made the twelfth. For, prayer going before, not by chance but by divine providence the lot brought forth the divine judgment. Paul too says of Christ: In whom we also are called by lot, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things, etc. And to the Thessalonians [so the edition], giving thanks to God the Father, who hath made us worthy to be partakers of the lot of the saints in light. From all these let it suffice to have said this, which the lot drawn by the Apostles shows us: that where the lot is drawn with entire faith and with prayer sent before, the lot declares openly to men the things which the will of God holds in secret. But according to the inner understanding, as Paul seems to indicate, saying: in the part of the lot of the saints, and: called by lot in Christ, we must see whether perhaps the lot is managed not only among men but among the powers above, and some power presides over this office, which, for example, when Jesus son of Nave was now distributing the inheritance by lot, would give the guidance of the lot not according to any favour, but according to what it knows to please God, and would make those things which are first fall to him whom it knows to hold the first place with God, so that what lies hidden with God may by the governance of the lot be shown to men also; and would make another of the second place and another of the third. This I think is done not only on earth but also in heaven; and that a lot of this kind, which with God is distinguished also by consideration of merits, was held at that time too when the most High divided the nations according to the number of the angels of God, and the portion of the Lord was made Jacob, Israel the line of his inheritance. For here it says that God obtained Israel as a part by lot and line. It is not, then, to be thought that by chance it fell through the lot that the nation of the Egyptians came to that angel, to another that of the Idumeans, to another that of the Moabites, and the like. But there too, if the nations are divided by lot according to the number of the angels of God, as we said among men, because the lot lays open to the public the hidden judgment of God, such a lot must be believed to have been, by which each received this or that nation according to his merit. Nor indeed is it to be said that among single persons it comes about without a lot dispensed by the judgment of God that one obtains such or such a life from his birth, or that good and contrary angels attend men, so that this angel has obtained by lot the keeping of the soul of Peter, another of Paul, another of any infant of the Church. For it is not to be doubted that by the judgment of God, who regards to clearness either their dignity or the quality of our soul, the keeping of each of us is given by a certain mystical lot directed by the dispensation of Christ. I think also of those powers which have received the ministries of the world, that not by chance does this power preside over the buddings of the earth or of trees, that one supply the flowing of fountains or rivers, another preside over rains, another over winds, another over the animals of the sea, another over those of the earth, or over each single thing that springs from the earth; and that there are in each ineffable sacraments of the divine dispensation, that all things may be ordered in their order through each power and in its fitting office. Whence: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent to minister for them who shall receive the inheritance of salvation? In imitation of these, lots are said to be drawn by Jesus, and the inheritance to be decreed to the tribes by divine dispensation, and by the ineffable providence and presence of God the pattern of the inheritance to come to be foreshadowed in these lots, because the law is said to have a shadow of the good things to come. Hence Paul says: You are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. There is, then, a city in heaven which is called Jerusalem, and mount Sion. Not without cause did Benjamin receive Jerusalem and mount Sion in his lot, but because the reason of the heavenly Jerusalem required that the earthly, which is the figure of the heavenly, be given to no other.
• Hence, then, it is that divine wisdom ordered certain names of places to be written which contain a mystical interpretation, by which it is shown that these things are ordered to be done by sure reasons, not by chance. For as not by chance is that angel called Michael, another Gabriel, another Raphael; and that patriarch Abraham, and that one Isaac, and another Jacob; or that one Abraham from Abram, that one Isaac [so the edition], and another Israel; but by sure reason too that one Sara from Sarai, that one Israel from Jacob, or that one Abraham from Abram; and each of the angels or men obtains his name from the offices and acts enjoined on him: so it follows that there are certain heavenly places and cities, as the heavenly Jerusalem is spoken of, and that there is mount Sion, and others too, whose figure these on earth contain, which are here mystically signified to us through Jesus Nave. Of the cities I think it said: The cities of Juda shall be built, and they shall dwell there; and: In my Father's house there are many mansions; and: Have thou power over ten cities. Do not, then, read this with distaste and think it a mean scripture woven of many names, but know that in these are contained mysteries greater than human speech can utter or mortal hearing hear. These things were known entirely to him who was caught up to the third heaven. For in heaven he saw the heavenly things, he saw the heavenly Jerusalem, the true city of God, and mount Sion, in whatever place it is. He saw Bethlehem and Chebron and all that are written as divided here by lot. Their reasons too he comprehended in the spirit. For he confesses that he heard words and reasons which it is not granted to man to utter; such, namely, as they were to whom he said: Are you not men, and walk according to man? He spoke them perhaps to those who walked not according to the flesh, Timothy and Luke and the other disciples, whom he knew to be capable of the ineffable sacraments. Whence he says to Timothy: Be mindful of the words which thou hast heard of me, which commend to faithful men who shall be fit to teach others also.
**“ADAMANTIUS”** — BETHLEHEM TOO is decreed to the lot of Juda not without sure reason, or Chebron; and single cities are assigned to single tribes. But did the heavenly places in which Jerusalem and Sion are named, and the rest that are near them, contain in themselves in heaven this reason which was governed by lot on earth?

19.32:
**“The sixth lot came out to the sons of Nephtali by their families”** — OF THE CHILDREN OF NEPHTALI. AUGUSTINE. And the Amorrhite remained to dwell in Helon and in Salamin, and the hand of Ephraim was made heavy upon them, and they became tributaries to them. This was now done against the command of the Lord, and Jesus was still living, but because of old age he was not the leader in those battles. Therefore it was said by the Lord: it was done that the heart of those should be emboldened who conspired together to enter into war against Jesus, lest this mercy should be shown them even against the command of God, if they had remained unconquered and, Jesus growing old or dead, had been left to be conquered by the children of Israel, who could spare them against the command of the Lord, which he would not do, etc.
**“ADAMANTIUS”** — ADAMANTIUS. According to the Seventy: The Amorrhite remained to dwell in Helon and in Salamin, and the hand of Ephraim was made heavy upon them. Amorrhite is interpreted bitter or bitterness. [They are] dwelling, then, in Helon, which is interpreted rams, or in Salamin, which is interpreted peaceable: the bitter ones. And the rams are those who, set in the contest, strive to storm the devilish structures; and the peaceable are those who, having overcome the carnal desires and concupiscences, keep peace in the soul. Yet in both the devil, that is, bitterness, strives to persist. If, then, a hostile power, that is, of a demon coming from the troop of bitterness, besiege someone's body, disturb and stupefy the mind, and many prayers be applied, many fasts, many invocations of exorcists, and to all these the demon remain deaf, persisting in the possessed body, bearing the punishments of the exorcists and the torments from the invocation of the name of God more tolerably than to depart: so it is to be understood that the Amorrhites persist in dwelling in Helon and in Salamin. And that the Scripture might show that they persist while bearing punishments and scourges, it says that the hand of Ephraim was made heavy upon them; which is done more vehemently through the laying on of the hands of exorcists, or through good acts and good works. For the better the things we do or perform, and the more we live among the best things, the heavier these are made to them. He is pleasing and acceptable to them who lives in baseness and crimes. But he who in good acts makes his hand heavy upon them, even if he cannot expel them utterly, will make them tributaries and subject. And the children of Ephraim went away to go through the land according to their borders.
19.49:
**“And when he had made an end of dividing the land by lot to each one by their tribes,”**
• he did not presume for himself, made the last of all that he might be the first of all
• AND WHEN HE HAD MADE AN END OF DIVIDING THE LAND, etc. ADAMANTIUS. See the meekness and humility of Jesus, who worthily bore the name of Jesus the true Saviour. The children of Israel, it says, gave a lot to Jesus the son of Nave among themselves by the command of the Lord, etc. He gave inheritance to all the children of Juda and Ephraim, and to the half tribe of Manasses, and to Caleb the son of Jephone. He sent three men from each tribe to go through the whole land and describe it in a book, and returning to show it to him; and he reserved himself for the last, and willed to be the last of all that he might be the first of all; nor does he presume an inheritance for himself, but receives it from the people to whom he gave. But these things happened to them in figure and are set before us, that we may keep that precept which he fulfilled in deed: The greater thou art, the more humble thyself, and thou shalt find grace before the Lord. And elsewhere: Have they made thee ruler? Be not lifted up, but be among them as one of them. See, then, how he was the leader of the people, who brought them into the holy land, into the land of promise. He was the successor of Moses, yet he does not allow himself to take a lot of the land, but, the leader of the people, he waits to receive a little portion from the people, and builds the place which he receives and raises it up, that he may truly make it worthy of the gift of God and of the divine inheritance.
• Perhaps the people too gives some part to our Lord Jesus, and allots him a place as for his dwelling. For he who is good gives the Son of God a place in himself. This place, received in the soul, Jesus builds and adorns, and makes in it impregnable walls and lofty towers, that he may build a mansion worthy of himself. He adorns the soul too and makes it capable of his wisdom and knowledge and reason and of all holiness, that he may make the Father enter with him and make an abode, and sup on the foods which he himself has prepared. That we may merit to obtain this, let us prepare a clean heart, that the Lord Jesus may gladly enter the lodging of our heart.
**“the children of Israel gave a possession”** — the indweller of the clean heart
19.50:
**“According to the commandment of the Lord, the city which he asked for, Thamnath Saraa, in mount Ephraim: and he built up”** — with virtues
**“the city”** — the soul of each one

21.1: **“AND THE PRINCES CAME”** — AND THE PRINCES CAME. ADAMANTIUS. All the children of Israel received their lots in the land. For the Levites God alone suffices for an inheritance. But because they receive tithes and firstfruits by the command of the Lord, they must also receive tithes of the land and of the dwellings. For this is to have received tithes of all things. Therefore the princes of the Levites, coming to Eleazar the priest, and to Jesus the son of Nave, and to the princes of the tribes, said: The Lord commanded cities to be given us to dwell in, and their suburbs for our cattle. A lot, then, must be made of the cities and the suburbs, lest the division to the Levites seem to be made indiscriminately and by chance. As, then, the distribution among the children of Israel had a reason, by which one was held worthy of the first lot and another of the second, among whom Dan was last, so it is necessary that here too there be some reason, that the first lot be drawn for some, the second for others, and the third for others. Now the sons of Levi are said to be Gerson and Caath and Merari, and Caath is shown to have held the honour of primacy, whose children were Moses, Aaron and Mary. From Caath, then, part of the people was made priestly, that is, Aaron and his sons. But Moses is to be held in the priestly order, or in whatever can be more; but the account of the children of Israel is another. And the rest of the sons of Caath held their order in the tribe of Levi, who are Isaar and Hebron and Oziel. Then after these, after Caath, Gerson of the sons of Levi receives a part. In the third place, last of all, Merari. And this is the difference of the first, second, third or fourth order which we observed first of all in Numbers. For after the twelve tribes were ordered to keep the watches about the ark of the testament of the Lord through the four quarters of the world, three were appointed on the east, three on the Africus, that is, the south, three toward the sea, that is, toward the west, and three on the north. There these too are assigned through the four quarters of the world in the same order. And on the east, where the tribe of Juda was, which is first among the rest, Aaron and his sons are placed. And the sons of Caath who were left are appointed to carry the ark of the Lord and to sound the trumpets, so that when the first trumpet had sounded, those who were on the east moved the camp; at the second, those who were on the south; at the third, those on the west; at the fourth, those on the north. Thou seest how great an order, how great a sequence of things, is kept in the holy Scriptures: nothing is done without reason and order. But mark more diligently what is related here. The first lot, it says, came out for Caath, and it fell to the sons of Aaron the priests who were among the Levites. To whom ought the primacy to be given but to Aaron, the first or high priest? First in the merits of life, in honours, in virtue. This lot, then, is not by chance, but a power above is present governing it according to the judgment of divine providence, and this lot decrees the first dwellings to the sons of Aaron: to the sons of Aaron, in the tribe of Juda and in the tribe of Simeon and in the tribe of Benjamin, thirteen cities by lot. Thou seest how dwellings are dispensed to chosen men in chosen tribes? And who ought to receive the second lot? The sons, it says, of Caath, who were left after the sons of Aaron. And what tribes do these receive? In the tribe, it says, of Ephraim, and in the tribe of Dan, and in the half tribe of Manasses, ten cities by lot.
21.7:
**“And to the sons of Merari by their kindreds, of the tribes of Ruben and of Gad and of Zabulon, twelve cities.”**
• And who are the third? The sons of Gerson. And in what tribes do they obtain their lot? In Issachar, it says, and in Aser, in Nephtali, and in the half tribe of Manasses which is in Basanitis, thirteen cities.
• And who are the last among the Levites? The sons, it says, of Merari. In what tribes do they receive? Of the tribe, it says, of Ruben beyond the Jordan, and of Gad, of the tribe of Zabulon, who is the last among the sons of Lia. They receive by lot twelve cities. Since there are four quarters of the world, Caath receives the first lot among the sons of Levi on the side of the east, with those tribes which hold the primacy of all. See how all things agree with the four quarters. The eastern quarter of the world is the nobler, in which the tribe of Juda, the noblest of all, was held. And the sons of Caath, the priests, draw the first lot in the first tribes and quarters of the world; Gerson and Merari, who were first among the sons of Levi [so the edition]. So, then, the three firsts of Levi receive the east. But the west [so the edition], where Ruben and Simeon and Gad were, Caath obtains by the second lot, and the tribe of Simeon. And Merari first obtains Ruben and Gad, and again Merari takes Zabulon, the third in number from the east, that justice may be kept in the lot, which is drawn according to God and directs the minds of believers to contemplate the mysteries of the world to come. After this, of those who were toward the sea, that is, Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasses: Caath, having received the tribe of Benjamin by the second lot, the rest of his family obtained Ephraim. After this Gerson obtains those who were of the half tribe of Manasses which was in the holy land, and the other half tribe of Manasses. But because those too who were in the north ought to obtain something of the priestly grace, lest they should seem altogether stripped of heavenly gifts, [so it was] among those whose order was last, in the north, that is, Dan and Nephtali and Aser: again Caath, not among the priests but among the rest, yet receives the first lot in Dan; and Gerson the second in Aser, and the same Gerson the third in Nephtali. Who can comprehend all these things? Who can even remember the very order of the mysteries, when it is difficult to unfold it even according to the letter, through the mixings of places and persons which are contained in the history? What shall we say of the sacraments which are described through these things, and in which the distributions of the inheritance to come are foreshadowed? Who may unfold the various seats of the camps? How in the resurrection the distribution is to be held for each of the saints in the priestly or levitical order, that in the resurrection all things may not be done confusedly, but every one may come in his own order: the firstfruits Christ, then they that are of Christ, who shall rise at his coming, when he shall have delivered up the kingdom to God the Father, when he shall have subjected to him all principality and power. There there will be certain such observances of the camps, and priestly descriptions and orders, and significations of the trumpets. Perhaps too, as God ordered the stars of heaven and placed them by wonderful reasons, some in the axis of the north, others in the parts of the east, others in the south, and others in the west, so those who from the resurrection of the dead will come like the stars of heaven in multitude and brightness, namely of the seed of Abraham, he will order in the kingdom of heaven according to the order of the stars and the parts of heaven; and he will give to some a lot toward the east, to others toward the west, to others toward the south, and to others, whom he himself knows, toward the north; because many shall come from the east and the west and the four quarters of the earth, and shall sit down with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
**“ADAMANTIUS”** — ADAMANTIUS. Above it was said that the children of Israel gave a lot to Jesus in mount Ephraim, and that he built a city there and dwelt in it. But the same scripture repeats it, to add that he hid there the stone knives with which he circumcised the children of Israel in the desert. Now we said that Jesus Christ asks of us a place which he may build, in which he may dwell; and that we ought to be made such in mind and body that he may deign to receive a place in our soul and build and dwell. And who is in all the people so acceptable as to be worthy of this? Perhaps not single persons, but the whole Church together can receive Jesus into itself, that he may dwell in it. What, then, is the place in which Jesus ought to dwell? In mount Ephraim, it says, that is, in the fruitful mountain. What are the fruitful mountains? Those, namely, in which are the fruits of the spirit: peace, joy and patience, charity, etc. These are ever lofty in mind and spirit; and though they be few, yet Jesus, who is the true light, dwelling in them, sends forth the rays of his light upon those whom he does not yet judge worthy to be principally his dwelling. Let us see, then, what are the stone knives with which Jesus circumcised the children of Israel. If you pray for us that our word may be living and effectual and sharper than any knife, the Lord Jesus Christ will grant to us too that the word of God which we speak to you may cut away all uncleanness and vices from the hearers, and cut off everything by which the force of the mind and natural efficacy is covered over. And so through the word of God, which is the stone knife, you will be circumcised by Jesus, and will hear: I have taken away the reproach of Egypt from you this day. For what does it profit to have come out of Egypt, that is, out of the world, and to walk through the desert, and keep the former filth of morals and the uncleanness of vices? After the passing of the Red Sea, then, the carnal vices of the old custom must be taken away through Jesus Christ, that at length we may be free of the reproaches of Egypt. And those stone knives with which we were circumcised the second time by Jesus are laid up in that place which Jesus asks, Jesus receives, Jesus possesses: namely, in the soul of the just. For the knife is the word of God, by which sins are purged from the minds of the hearers. This power, then, of the divine word is laid up in that place to which is given the word of wisdom and of knowledge, that at a fitting time that soul may bring forth these knives in the Church and circumcise a second time those who need the second circumcision. And that it says stone knives, that is, knives of rock and not made of iron by the work of a craftsman, shows this: that this word of God which circumcises the uncleannesses of hearts does not come from the art of grammar or rhetoric, nor is it tamed by the hammers of the doctors or polished on the whetstones of studies, but descends from that rock which, cut out of the mountain without hands, filled the world and bestowed spiritual gifts on believers.
21.41: **“So all the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Israel were forty-eight”** — SO ALL THE CITIES OF THE LEVITES, etc. ISIDORE. That the Levites receive [forty-]eight cities signifies the preaching of the saints. For they possess the doctrine which consists of the Decalogue of the law and the fourfold number of the Gospel, as it were having four times ten cities; to which two are also added, because all that they preach they announce in the moral and the mystical sense.
21.43: **“AND THE LORD GOD GAVE TO ISRAEL”** — AUGUSTINE. It is asked, since Israel did not root out the nations that held the land of promise, not only up to the day of the death of Jesus but even afterwards, though, being partly conquered, they remained there, how it is said: And the Lord God gave Israel all the land that he had sworn to give to their fathers, and they inherited it; and the Lord gave them rest round about, as he had sworn to their fathers, nor did any of all their enemies stand before their face; the Lord God delivered all their enemies into their hands; there failed not of all the words which the Lord spoke to the children of Israel; all came to pass. All things are to be considered diligently, and first, the land of what nations was promised to the Israelites. Seven nations seem to be mentioned constantly; whence in Exodus it is read: I will send my angel before thy face, and he will cast out the Amorrhite, the Hethite, the Pherezite, the Gergesite, the Hevite and the Jebusite and the Chanaanite. The land, then, of these nations God seems to have promised to the fathers. In Deuteronomy too it is written more expressly: If thou come to a city to fight against it, thou shalt first call them with peace; if they answer thee peaceably and open to thee, all the people that shall be found in the city shall be tributaries to thee and obedient. But if they will not obey thee and make war against thee, thou shalt besiege it; and when the Lord thy God shall deliver it into thy hands, thou shalt slay all the males thereof with the edge of the sword, except the women. The household goods and all the cattle and whatever shall be in the city, and all the utensils, thou shalt take for thyself as prey, and thou shalt eat all the spoil of thy enemies which the Lord thy God shall give thee. So shalt thou do to all the cities that are very far from thee, which are not of the cities of these nations. But behold, of these cities whose land the Lord thy God will give thee for an inheritance, thou shalt not suffer any to live, but shalt anathematize them, the Hethite and the Amorrhite, the Chanaanite, the Pherezite, the Jebusite and the Gergesite, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee. Here too it is manifest that the land of these seven nations was promised for an inheritance, which the Israelites should possess when these same nations had been subdued to utter destruction. For the other nations, which were far off, he willed to be tributaries if they did not resist; but if they resisted, that they too should be killed, except the cattle and the prey. Again in Deuteronomy: And it shall be, when the Lord shall have taken away many and great nations from before thy face, the Hethite, the Gergesite, the Amorrhite, the Pherezite, the Chanaanite, the Hevite and the Jebusite, thou shalt smite them with extermination and utterly exterminate them. Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor have pity on them, etc. By these, then, and other places of Scripture it is shown that the children of Israel so received the lands of these nations for an inheritance that they should dwell there not with those who held them, but in their stead. But in Genesis eleven nations are promised to the seed of Abraham thus: To thy seed will I give this land, from the river of Egypt even to the great river Euphrates, the Cineans and Cenezites and Cedmonites, the Pherezites, the Hethites, and the Raphaim, and the Amorrhites and the Chanaanites and the Hevites and the Gergesites and the Jebusites. This question is solved thus, that we understand that this prophecy went before, because Solomon was to stretch his kingdom to those borders, of whom it is thus written: And all the purpose of Solomon which he had resolved to build in Jerusalem and in Libanus and in all the land of his dominion: all the people that was left of the Hethite and the Amorrhite and the Pherezite, the Hevite and the Jebusite, who were not of Israel, and of their children who were left in the land with them, whom the children of Israel had not consumed, Solomon subjected to tribute unto this day. Behold, the remnants of the peoples that were to be subdued and utterly destroyed by God's command Solomon subjected to tribute. These indeed he ought to have destroyed according to God's command; yet, subjected, they were held as tributaries. And afterwards it is read thus: And he had dominion over all the regions from the river to the land of the Philistines, and to the borders of Egypt. Behold, that is fulfilled which was promised to Abraham in Genesis; for by the river here the Euphrates is understood, for in those places it can be understood as the great river even without its proper name added. For it cannot be taken of the Jordan, since the Israelites already held lands both on this side of the Jordan and beyond, even before the reign of Solomon. So, then, the Book of the Kings says that the kingdom of Solomon was stretched from the river Euphrates on the side of the east as far as the borders of Egypt, which part was on the west for them. Then, therefore, more was subjected than the seven nations held, and then not seven but eleven were brought into servitude. For what is written in the Book of the Kings, as far as the borders of Egypt from the river, when the Scripture would show from east to west how far the kingdom was stretched, is the same as was said in Genesis, when it was marked out from west to east: from the river of Egypt even to the great river Euphrates. For the river of Egypt, which divides the kingdom of Israel from Egypt, is not the Nile, but a river not great which flows by the city of Rhinocorura, whence the land of promise now begins toward the east. So, then, it had been appointed for the children of Israel that they should inhabit the lands of the seven nations, those being destroyed, and reign over the others, made subject and tributary, as far as the river Euphrates. And though they did not obey in this, because of those whom they ought to have exterminated they had made some obedient, yet God in the time of Solomon fulfilled the faith of his promise. Now, then, in the book of Jesus Nave, which we are considering, how will this be true: And God gave Israel all the land that he had sworn to give to their fathers, and they inherited it? How did he give all the land while Jesus was still living, when they had not yet overcome even the remnants of the seven nations? For what follows, And they inherited it, is true, because they had gone about it and settled there. Then what is added: And the Lord gave them rest round about, as he had sworn to their fathers, is true, because while Jesus was still alive the remnants of those nations did not indeed yield to them, but none of them dared to provoke them. Therefore it is said too, as is added: None of all their enemies stood before their face. And what follows: But the Lord delivered all their enemies into their hands, he meant to be understood of those, namely, who dared to go to meet them in war. And what he says afterwards: There failed not of all the good words which the Lord spoke to the children of Israel; all came to pass, he means to be understood thus: that though they had already acted against the Lord's command by sparing some and making them obedient, they were yet still safe among them. Therefore when he had said, of all the words, he added, good, because the curses appointed for the despisers and transgressors had not yet come. It remains, then, that what he says, The Lord God gave Israel all the land which he had sworn to give to their fathers, be understood according to this: that there were still remnants of those nations to be crushed and exterminated, or of others as far as the river Euphrates to be subjected, if they did not resist; yet they were left for their use, that they might be exercised in them, lest, weak with carnal affections and desires, they should be unable to bear a sudden prosperity modestly and wholesomely, but, being lifted up, should the more quickly perish. All the land, then, was given to them, because that part too which had not yet been given into possession had already been given for a certain usefulness of exercise.
21.44: **“AND NONE OF THEIR ENEMIES [DURST] STAND AGAINST THEM”** — AUGUSTINE. As to what it says: None of all their enemies stood before their face, it can be asked how it is true, since it was written above of the tribe of Dan that their enemies did not allow them to come down into the valley and prevailed against them in the mountains; but eleven tribes are reckoned for the whole people. But if it is asked why this tribe did not obtain sufficient lands in its lot, and was afflicted by those by whom they were held, it is in the secret counsel of God; since too, when Jacob was blessing his sons, he said such things of this Dan that from that tribe the antichrist is thought to be to come. This question can be solved thus also: that none stood before their face, namely, while they fought together under the command of one leader, before their own places were divided to the single tribes to be defended.

22.1: **“At the same time Josue called the Rubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasses”** — AT THE SAME TIME [JOSUE] CALLED, etc. ADAMANTIUS. Jesus gathers the children of Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses, who had served in war with him, and dismisses them to their inheritance, giving them certain gifts. In which he signifies that when the fulness of the Gentiles shall have entered, and received the things that are promised by the Lord Jesus, those who had been taught and instructed through Moses, and have helped us in the struggle by their prayers and examples, because they have not yet obtained the promises, waiting until our calling also should be fulfilled, will then at last obtain perfection, with the gifts which they receive from Jesus, that each may dwell in peace, every assault ceasing.
22.10: **“And when they were come to the banks of the Jordan, in the land of Chanaan, they built an altar immensely great near the Jordan.”** — AND WHEN THEY WERE COME TO THE BANKS, etc. ADAMANTIUS. The children of Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses built an altar beyond the Jordan; but the rest of the children of Israel, not knowing the cause, send Phinees the son of Eleazar with ten men chosen from each tribe, asking why they had done this. And they give satisfaction about the altar, saying: We know that the true altar is with you, where Jesus dwells, etc. But let us see the sacrament of this deed. The former people of the circumcision is figured in Ruben the firstborn, and in Gad, who too is the firstborn of Zelpha, and Manasses is a firstborn. And when I say firstborn, I speak according to time. These things are said lest any division should seem to be between us and those who were just before the coming of Christ, but that they might show that they too are our brothers; for though they then had an altar, they perceived that it was not the true one, but the form of the future and true altar. They knew that the true victims, which could take away sins, were not offered on that altar which the firstborn people had, but on this where Jesus was. There shall be, then, one fold and one shepherd: those just and these just Christians.
22.17: **“AND MANY OF THE PEOPLE PERISHED”** — AND MANY OF THE PEOPLE PERISHED. The people, then, once fell in the desert and died; Aaron came and stood in the midst between those who were dying and those who were living, that the havoc of death might go no further. Now too, then, my Lord, the true high priest, has come, standing between the dying and the living, that is, between those of the Jews who received his presence, and those who not only did not receive it, but killed themselves rather than him, saying: "His blood be upon us and upon our children." Whence: "All the just blood that hath been shed upon the earth" shall be required of this generation which said these things. These, then, are a part of the people dead, because they keep neither the unleavened bread nor the festival days fittingly; but their festival days are turned into mourning and their songs into lamentation. Even if they wished, they could [not] celebrate the festival day in the place which the Lord God chose. But we did not say to them: You shall have no part in this altar, or in the inheritance of the Lord; but they of their own accord refused the true altar and the heavenly high priest. Therefore they lost even the image. Whence: "Behold, your house shall be left to you desolate." For the grace of the Holy Ghost and the solemnities have been transferred to us, because the true high priest according to the order of Melchisedech has passed over to us, and he must offer the true victims, that is, the spiritual, among us, where the temple of God is built of living stones, which is the Church of the living God, and where the true Israel is, in Christ Jesus our Lord.
22.29: **“BY BUILDING AN ALTAR TO OFFER HOLOCAUSTS”** — AUGUSTINE. And in the sacrifices of our salvations: because the sacrifices are spoken of in the plural, the salvations also are in the plural. Where it is to be noted how the sacrifice is usually called salutary in the singular; because if we take Christ, who is called the salvation of God, it does not appear how it can be understood in the plural. For our Lord Jesus Christ is one, though many are called christs after him through his grace. Whence: "Touch ye not my anointed." But whether one may say salvation or salvations is not easily to be ventured. For he alone is the Saviour.

23.14: **“Behold this day I am going into the way of all the earth, and you shall know with all your mind that of all the words which the Lord promised to perform for you, not one hath failed.”** — BEHOLD THIS DAY I AM GOING INTO THE WAY. AUGUSTINE. As to what Jesus says: But I run back the way, as do all who are upon the earth: in the translation which is from the Hebrew we find, I am going into the way. So, then, what the Seventy said, I run back, is to be taken as it was said to man: Till thou return to the earth out of which thou wast taken, so that it is understood according to the body. But if we will take it according to the soul, as it is written in Ecclesiastes: And the spirit shall return to him that gave it, I do not think this can be said of all, but of those who have so lived that they merit to return to God as to the author by whom they were created; for this cannot be understood of those of whom it is said: a spirit that goeth and returneth not. And if Jesus had not added, as do all who are upon the earth, there would be no question; for we should believe nothing else of him than what we read is worthy of him. But since this is added, it is a wonder if the Latin translator put I run back, and did not rather say I run through, or I run out. For all run through or run out the way of this life when they have come to its end. But because this word is used where the kindred of Rebecca say to the servant of Abraham: Behold, take Rebecca and run back, and let her be the wife of thy master's son, therefore here too the word was so translated.

24.3: **“And I took your father Abraham from the borders of Mesopotamia: and brought him into the land of Chanaan: and I multiplied his seed”** — AND I TOOK YOUR FATHER. AUGUSTINE. Where the Seventy have: And I took your father Abraham from beyond the rivers and led him into all the land, the translation which is from the Hebrew has: And I brought him into the land of Chanaan. It is a wonder, then, if the Seventy chose to put all the land for the land of Chanaan, unless looking to the prophecy, that it might rather be taken as done, from the promise of God, which was announced as most certainly to come in Christ and in the Church, which is the true seed of Abraham.
24.11: **“And you passed over the Jordan, and you came to Jericho. And the men of that city fought against you, the Amorrhite, and the Pherezite, and the Chanaanite, and the Hethite, and the Gergesite, and the Hevite, and the Jebusite: and I delivered them into your hands.”** — AND THEY FOUGHT AGAINST YOU, etc. AUGUSTINE. With their gates shut they defended themselves within the circuit of their walls; but to shut the gates against an enemy belongs to war. For they did not send envoys to ask for peace. But if it had been said, they fought against you, it would be false [so the edition], because war does not have continual fighting, but sometimes frequent, sometimes rare, sometimes none. Yet it is war when there is in some manner an armed dissension.
24.12: **“And I sent before you hornets: and I drove them out from their places, the two kings of the Amorrhites, not with thy sword nor with thy bow.”** — HORNETS, etc. The Seventy: Wasps, that is, perhaps figuratively, the sharpest stings of fear, by which they were in some manner pricked with fears so that they fled; or the airy stings of the spirit, as is said in the Psalm, by evil angels; unless one should say that not all the things that were done have been written, and that they are to be understood as real wasps.
24.19: **“YOU WILL NOT BE ABLE TO SERVE THE LORD”** — AUGUSTINE. You will not be able to serve the Lord, because he is holy. Is it because it is impossible for human frailty to be in some manner matched to his holiness by perfect service? Hearing this, they ought not only to have chosen his service, but also to have presumed on his help and mercy, of which it is said: "Enter not into judgment with thy servant, for in thy sight no man living shall be justified." But these presumed rather on themselves, that they would serve God without any offence, so that even then they began what was said: "Not knowing the justice of God, and seeking to establish their own, they have not submitted themselves to the justice of God." So the law was now entering in for them, that sin might abound, and afterwards grace might more abound through Jesus Christ, who is the end of the law.
24.23: **“PUT AWAY STRANGE GODS”** — AUGUSTINE. What is it that he says: And now put away the strange gods that are among you, and direct your hearts to the God of Israel? For they did not still have the idols of the Gentiles, since above he had proclaimed their obedience. Or if they had them, after so many warnings of the law their prosperity would not have followed, since vengeance was so taken on them because one man stole of the anathema. Moreover, Jacob said this to those who had come out with him from Mesopotamia, where idols were so worshipped that Rachel even stole her father's. But after that admonition of Jacob they gave up what they had. Whence it appeared that he said this because he knew they had them. But after this admonition of Jesus no one brought forth any such thing. Yet it is not to be thought that he commanded this to no purpose; for he does not say: And now put away the strange gods, if there are any among you, but altogether as one who knows that there are: which are, he says, among you. The holy prophet, then, discerned in their hearts thoughts of God, and strange ones, alien from God, and he admonished that these be put away. For he who thinks of God as such as he is not carries a strange and false god in his thought. And who is there who thinks of God as he is? It remains, then, for the faithful, as long as they are absent from the Lord, to put away from their heart the phantasms which thrust themselves upon their thoughts, as if God were such or such as he is not, and to direct their heart to him faithfully, that he may make himself known in the way and measure that he knows to be expedient for you, until all lying be consumed, whence it is said: Every man is a liar; and, not only impious falsehood but the very glass and the dark manner being passed, we may know him face to face.
24.25:
**“Josue therefore on that day made a covenant, and set before the people commandments and judgments in Sichem.”**
• JOSUE THEREFORE MADE, etc. AUGUSTINE. And Jesus made a covenant with the people that day, and gave them a law and judgment in Silo, before the tabernacle of the Lord God of Israel; and he wrote these words in the book of the law of God, and took a great stone, and Jesus set it under the terebinth before the Lord, and said: [Behold this stone shall be a testimony unto you, that it hath heard all] the things which were spoken by the Lord, whatever he spoke to you today; and this shall be for a testimony to you in the last days, when you shall have lied to the Lord your God. Those who search these words more deeply do not think the man so foolish as to have believed that the stone heard the words of God which he spoke to the people; which, even if it were fashioned into a man, would have ears and would not hear. But by this stone he signified him who is a stone of stumbling to the unbelieving Jews and a rock of scandal, "which the builders rejected, and it is become the head of the corner", of whom it is said: "And they drank of the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ." Whence the excellent leader circumcised the people with knives of stone, which were buried with him, on the other hand [so the edition], that he might show a deep mystery that would profit those to come. So, then, we ought to take this stone too, set up visibly, spiritually, as a testimony that would profit against the unbelieving Jews, that is, the liars, of whom it is said: The enemies of the Lord have lied to him. For not in vain, when Moses, or rather God through him, had made a covenant with the people, which was in the ark of the covenant and in the books of the law written with so great a multiplicity of sacraments and precepts, is this said: Jesus made a covenant that day. For the repetition of the covenant signifies the New Testament, as does Deuteronomy, that is, the second law, and the second tables. For what was to be fulfilled in one way was signified in many ways.
• And that this stone was set under the terebinth signifies [the same as] the rod [struck] to the rock that water might flow forth, and that not even this stone was set without wood. And it was set beneath because he would not have been exalted on the cross unless he had been subjected in humility; or because at that time when Jesus Nave was doing this the mystery was still to be overshadowed. The terebinth too exudes a healing tear; this tree was put by the Seventy, but others in another word put the oak.
• It is a wonder that, at least in these last words in which he addressed the people, he did not rebuke those who spared those nations which the Lord commanded to be utterly destroyed. For so it is written: And it came to pass, after the children of Israel grew strong, that they made the Chanaanites obedient, [but] with extermination they did not exterminate them before them. For at first the Scripture testified that they could not. But now, after they prevailed so as to make them obedient, that they did not also exterminate them was done against the command of the Lord; which was done by no one while Jesus led the army. Or perhaps, because the Scripture said before that they could not, namely before they prevailed, they are to be believed to have feared even when they had prevailed, lest, if they did not spare those who were ready to obey, they should drive them from despair to fight more fiercely against them, and should be unable to overcome them. This human fear, then, the Lord willed to be imputed to them; and so there appears in them a certain slight failing of faith, which, if it had been strong in them, the things would have followed which followed Jesus when he made war. But because there was not so great a faith in them, even when they had prevailed they did not dare to fight to the utter destruction of their enemies; not from malice or pride or contempt of the Lord's command, but from weakness of soul. Whence the Apostle: "Alexander the coppersmith hath done me much evil; the Lord will reward him according to his works"; but of those who had forsaken him not from malice but from fear he says: "At my first answer no man stood with me, but all forsook me"; may it "not be laid to their charge".

1.1:
**“AFTER THE DEATH”**
• AFTER THE DEATH. The history of the book of Judges shows no small sacraments of mysteries. For after Josue the Judges succeed, as after Christ the apostles and the rulers of the Churches, to rule the faithful, whom he himself leads to the hope of the eternal promise. And throughout this volume are contained the sins of the Jewish people, and their servitude and their cry, and the compassion of God. For many years they served for their sins, and being converted they were set free; because our sins give strength to the enemies, and when we do evil in the sight of the Lord our adversaries, that is, the demons, are strengthened. But when we are converted, God raises up judges and saviours, that is, princes and doctors, whom he sends to the help of those who cry to God with their whole heart.

**“AUGUSTINE”**
• At the end of the book of Jesus Nave the narrator stretched the history briefly as far as [the time when] the children of Israel turned aside to worship strange gods. But in this book there is a return to the order [of events], how the things that followed were done after the death of Jesus Nave. The book, then, does not begin from that time when the people fell away to worship idols, but from the earlier times interposed, in which those things were done after which it came to these.

1.2:
**“And the Lord said: Juda”** — the tribe of Juda
**“shall go up: behold I have delivered the land into his hands.”** — JUDA SHALL GO UP, etc. AUGUSTINE. It is asked whether some man was called Juda, or whether it called the tribe itself so, after its custom. But those who had asked the Lord were seeking a leader; whence it is thought that the name of one man was expressed. But because Scripture is not wont to name leaders when they are appointed without mentioning also the origin of their parents, and it is certain that after Jesus the people of Israel had leaders, of whom the first was Gothoniel the son of Cenez, it is rightly understood that by the name of Juda the tribe of Juda was signified. For the Lord willed the crushing of the Chanaanites to begin from it. And when the people asked about a leader, the answer of the Lord served for this, that they might know that God did not will war to be waged against the Chanaanites by the whole people. He said, then: Juda shall go up; and there follows: And Juda said to Simeon his brother: tribe, namely, to tribe. For the sons of Jacob, who were so called, were no longer living. It is manifest that the tribe of Juda asked for itself the help of another tribe, which it would return when there was need.
1.3:
**“And Juda said”** — the tribe, namely, to the tribe
**“to Simeon his brother: Come up with me into my lot, and fight against the Chanaanite, that I also”** — when thou shalt have need
1.12: **“And Caleb said: He that shall take Cariath-Sepher, and lay it waste, to him will I give my daughter Axa to wife.”** — AND CALEB SAID: HE THAT SHALL SMITE. AUGUSTINE. Whoever shall smite the City of letters and take it, I will give him my daughter to wife. This is recorded in the book of Jesus. But whether it was done while Jesus was living and is now recapitulated, or after his death, after it was said, Juda shall go up, and Juda began to make war against the Chanaanites, in which war all these things are related as done, is rightly asked. But it is more credible that it was done after the death of Jesus, and was recorded then by prolepsis, that is, by anticipation, like other things. For now, when the deeds of the tribe of Juda against the Chanaanites are being set out, the order of the narration holds it thus among the other warlike deeds of Juda, of whom the Lord said after the death of Jesus: Juda shall go up; and after this the children of Juda went up to fight against the Chanaanite who dwelt in the hill country, the south and the plain; and Juda went to the Chanaanite dwelling in Chebron, and Chebron came out against him. Now the name of Chebron was Cariatharboc and Sepher; and he smote Sesi and Achiman and Tholmi, the sons of Enach; and they went up thence to the inhabitants of Dabir, whose name before was the City of letters; and Caleb said: Whoever shall smite the City of letters, etc. It is certain, then, from this order of events, that this was done after the death of Jesus. When, then, the cities given to Caleb himself were being recorded, the narrator, taking the occasion, anticipated what was done afterwards. Yet I do not think it is to no purpose that the Scripture has here recorded twice this of Caleb's daughter given as the victor's prize.
1.15:
**“But she answered: Give me a blessing”** — AUGUSTINE. The Seventy: The redemption of water: a land, namely, from whose fruits she might buy water, of which there was want in those regions to which she was being led as a bride.
**“for thou hast given me a dry land: give me also a watery land. So Caleb gave her the upper and the nether watery ground.”** — AUGUSTINE. The Seventy: The redemption of the high and the redemption of the low streams; understand: which flow either in the hill country or in the plains.
1.19: **“And the Lord was with Juda, and he possessed the hill country: but was not able to destroy the inhabitants of the valley, because they had many chariots armed with scythes.”** — NEITHER COULD HE DESTROY THE INHABITANTS, etc. In this very thing the Lord was with Juda. For God, being propitious, restrains even in the hearts of his saints the excess of too great prosperity, that he may turn the enemies to their use, not only when they are conquered but also when they are feared: the former to commend his bounty, the latter to repress their elation. For the enemy of the saints is the angel of Satan, who, the Apostle says, was given him to buffet him, lest he should be exalted by the greatness of the revelations.
1.20: **“And they gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had said”** — AUGUSTINE. This was said in the book of Jesus because it was said while he was alive; but here it is recorded by recapitulation, since the Scripture was speaking of the tribe of Juda, from which Caleb was.
1.21: **“BUT THE JEBUSITES THAT INHABITED”** — AUGUSTINE. Above it is read that the same city was taken and burned by Juda, and the Jebusites in it killed. But it must be known that two tribes, Juda and Benjamin, had this city in common, as the division of the lands which Jesus made shows. For it is Jebus, which is also Jerusalem. Therefore these two tribes remained with the temple of the Lord when the rest (except the tribe of Levi, which was priestly and did not receive lands in the division) separated themselves from the kingdom of Juda with Jeroboam. It must be known, then, that the city was taken and burned by Juda, those who had been found there being killed, but that not all the Jebusites were destroyed, either because they were outside the city or because they could flee; and that these Jebusites were admitted by the children of Benjamin, who had that city in common with Juda, to dwell in it together. What, then, is said: The children of Benjamin did not inherit the Jebusite, is to be understood that they could not, or would not, make them tributaries; or they did not inherit the Jebusite because they did not hold without him the land which they possessed.
1.27:
**“MANASSES ALSO DID NOT DESTROY”** — AUGUSTINE. And Manasses did not inherit Bethsan, which is a city of the Scythians; it is said today to be called Scythopolis. Now it may perplex one how there can be a city of the Scythians in those parts, far divided from Scythia. But it may perplex one similarly how Alexander the Macedonian founded the city of Alexandria so far from Macedonia, which he did by waging war far and wide. So the Scythians too could have founded this one. For it is read in the history of the nations that the Scythians once held almost all Asia.
**“Manasses also did not destroy Bethsan, and Thanac with their villages, nor the inhabitants of Dor, and Jeblaam, and Mageddo with their villages. And the Chanaanite began to dwell with them.”** — The Seventy: And Manasses did not inherit Bethsan, which is a city of the Scythians, nor its daughters, that is, the cities which it had established as their metropolis.
1.28: **“But after Israel was grown strong he made them tributaries, and would not destroy them.”** — Almost the same is said in Jesus Nave, and in the same words. [unclear in the edition: "Ioannes"] Either it is said here by anacephalaeosis or it was said there by prolepsis, that is, either here by recapitulation or there by anticipation.
1.31: **“Aser also destroyed not the inhabitants of Accho, and of Sidon, of Ahalab, and of Achazib, and of Amma”** — otherwise: Albia
1.34: **“AND THE AMORRHITE STRAITENED”** — AND THE AMORRHITE STRAITENED. AUGUSTINE. And the Amorrhite afflicted the children of Dan in the mountain, for he did not let them come down into the valley, etc. This was recorded either in the book of Jesus Nave by anticipation, or here by recapitulation.

2.1: **“AND AN ANGEL OF THE LORD WENT UP”** — AUGUSTINE. And an angel of the Lord went up upon Clauthmon, the mountain. The writer called the place by this name because he wrote afterwards. For when the angel of the Lord went up upon it, it was not yet so called. For it took its name from weeping, which in Greek is called klauthmos. For there the people wept, when they had heard from the angel the words of the Lord punishing them because they had been disobedient, since they did not exterminate, according to his command, the peoples over whom they prevailed, choosing to make them tributaries rather than to destroy them, as the Lord had commanded. Whether they did this in contempt of God's command or from fear (lest the enemy should fight more fiercely against them to keep their life than not to give tribute), without doubt they sinned, either by despising the command of God or by not trusting that he who had commanded could help them. He would not say this to them through Jesus (if indeed he had already commanded that it be done while Jesus was still alive, and it was not rather recorded by anticipation, since it began to be done when he was dead) because here he willed to reproach all through the angel. But all had not yet done this while Jesus was alive, even if some perhaps had already begun. Yet it is more credible that nothing of the sort had begun while Jesus was alive, and that under him the children of Israel held as much land as sufficed them to settle in, although they had in their lots [the means] by which, increasing and growing strong, they might exterminate their adversaries. Accordingly after the death of Jesus, when they had prevailed, they chose to have tributaries according to their own will rather than to destroy them according to the will of God. Therefore an angel was sent to rebuke them. As for what is recorded in the book of Jesus, I think rather that it was anticipated: what was done after his death, or what he himself knew by the prophetic spirit would be, if the book which is called Jesus Nave was written by him; or, if by another, he knew that what he recorded there by anticipation had already been done after the death of Jesus.
2.3: **“WHEREFORE I WOULD NOT DESTROY”** — AUGUSTINE. Hence we understand that certain sins come from the wrath of God. For that the gods of the nations, among whom, not exterminated, the Israelites chose to dwell, should be a scandal to them, that is, should make them stumble in their God and live having offended him, God threatened in indignation; which it is manifest is a great sin.
2.6: **“AND JOSUE SENT AWAY”** — This is repeated by recapitulation. For the death of Jesus Nave too is recorded in this book, that all things may be briefly set forth as from the beginning, from the time the Lord gave them the land, and how they lived under the Judges, or what they suffered; and again it returns to the order of the Judges, from him who was appointed first.
2.7:
**“And they served the Lord”**
• well pleasing
• Blessed is he who serves the Lord in the days of Jesus, who is enlightened by his word and wisdom, who is enlightened by his precepts and doctrine.
• But it must be known that our soul is enlightened either by the true light, which is not put out, that is, Christ; or, if it has not this eternal light in itself, it is enlightened by a temporal one that can be put out, namely by him who "transformeth himself into an angel of light" and with a false health enlightens the heart of the sinner, so that the things that are perishing seem to him to be true goods. By this light they are enlightened who call pleasure the highest good, who seek riches, the honours of the world and earthly glory as if eternal. These, then, are in the days of his light, which is put out. For whatever they do or desire shall be put out. Enlightened by this light Marcion says that the God of the law is just but not good. There are, then, the days of Jesus, of which it is said: The people served the Lord all the days of Jesus. For he who has in himself the days of Jesus serves the Lord. For he cannot serve the devil or avarice. Nor can it be that he who is enlightened by the light of truth should serve falsehood. Let us pray, then, that Christ, who is the true light, may ever make good days in us, lest, the devil enlightening us, we ever have evil days, of which it is said: "Redeeming the time, because the days are evil." So too [there is] an evil world, according to the Apostle.
• THEY SERVED THE LORD, etc. The people served the Lord all the days of Jesus. For it did not say that Jesus had one day, because his days are many: one day is justice, another sanctification, another prudence, another mercy, and the several goods of the virtues in which the Lord is served; and by these virtues of the soul the Lord is pleased. In all these days of Jesus thou shalt serve the Lord. Holy Scripture does not will that thou have some virtues and neglect others, but that, adorned with all these virtues and set in their acts, thou serve God. Similarly one has in himself the days of the elders, and serves God in their days, according to that: "Be ye followers of me, as I also am of Christ."
• In the days, it says, of their elders, who knew all the works of the Lord, etc. He knows all the works of the Lord who does them; as the sons of Heli [are said to be] not knowing the Lord, not that they were ignorant, since they taught others, but because they acted as those who know not the Lord. Similarly it is said here: Who knew every work of the Lord. Not only, it says, did they know the work of the Lord, but it added every, that is, who knew the work of justice and of sanctification and of patience and of meekness and the like. Whatever comes from the commandments of God is called the work of the Lord. The contrary is the work of the devil: injustice, anger and the like. They know, then, the work of the Lord who do his work. Whence: He that keepeth the commandment shall know no evil thing, that is, he shall beware of it. Of Christ too it is said that he "knew no sin", that is, he did not do the work of sin. He knows, then, the works of the Lord who does them; he is ignorant of them who does not.
• They knew, it says, the great works of the Lord which he did in Israel; as though some works of the Lord were small. I think that every work of the Lord is great; but according to the capacity of those in whom he works, if they are compared with one another, the works of the Lord are called great or small. For example: he brought the children of Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand, Egypt being scourged with heavenly prodigies. He made a way in the sea, gave manna in the desert, spoke to Moses from heaven, and gave the law on tables of stone. Are not these great works of God? But if thou compare with these that "God so loved the world as to give his only begotten Son", thou wilt find them small beside it.
**“AND THEY SERVED THE LORD”** — ADAMANTIUS. And the people served the Lord all the days of Jesus, and all the days of their elders, who were of longer days after Jesus. It must be known that each one brings it about for himself to be in good days or in evil, and to have the days of Jesus or of the just, or of the wicked. For if we understand "the true light which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world", and offer our souls to it to be enlightened, or if "the sun of justice" rise for us and enlighten the world of our soul, we have the days of Jesus Christ, the days of salvation. But if anyone has received the light that shall be put out, contrary to the truth, and has been enlightened by it, he will have days, but evil ones, and will not be in the days of Jesus, but in the days of Manasses or of Pharao or of any most wicked man. In fact, in the days of Acham [so the edition], a most wicked king, Isaias could not "see the Lord of hosts sitting upon a throne high"; but when the wicked king, whose days were evil, was dead, he saw by a vision of God. Now when the days of this or that man are spoken of in the Scriptures, the time of his life is not signified. Whence: "In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace, till the moon be taken away." If we take it that in the days in which the Saviour abode on earth there were days of justice and peace, how shall we prove that days of justice and peace arose for those who crucified him and did not receive his coming? Or how was there abundance of peace in his days among those who delivered him to death on false charges? How did they have days of peace and justice in whose minds the darkness of iniquity and fury dwelt? And so, because those days are not now, justice does not spring up, nor the abundance of the peace of Christ, among the faithful [so the edition]. Rather, then, each one by the conduct of his life acquires for himself days of iniquity and war, or of justice and peace. Whence: "Unto you that fear my name the sun of justice shall arise", namely, to make for them days of justice, days of Jesus. But of the wicked it is said that "the sun of justice" sets for them, in whom, namely, justice sleeps and the darkness of iniquity arises. And elsewhere on the contrary: "Much peace have they that love thy law, and to them there is no stumbling block." The wicked too have their own light, from which evil days arise for them. Whence: "The light of the just is always, but the light of the wicked shall be put out." I do not know whether anyone would understand so foolishly as to think that there is some substantial light, one which is called the light of the wicked and another that of the just; which cannot be. For there is one light of the world, made by God, which shines on all in common and equally.
**“all his days”** — in virtues
**“and the days of the ancients”**
• of the apostles
• It belongs to God alone to know which among the elders after Jesus made a longer day, that is, who sent forth from himself a greater light: whether Paul or Peter, Paul, Bartholomew or John. Yet the saints are said to be of long days. And on the contrary, when the world shall be filled with scandals, "when iniquity shall abound, the charity of many shall grow cold": then the days to come are not called long but shortened, according to that: "Unless those days had been shortened, no flesh should be saved." The evil days, then, are said to be shortened, but the good days, in which we serve the Lord, long-lived and of much space. But "for the sake of the elect" the evil "days shall be shortened", the days of iniquity and scandal; and, as I think, once the evil days have begun to be shortened for the elect, they are ever shortened and lessened to nothing and at the last perish. Of these I think was one he who said: "Let the day perish wherein I was born." But the days of the holy elders are long-lived and lengthy.
**“AND OF THE ANCIENTS”** — AND OF THE ELDERS. ADAMANTIUS. The elders who were with Jesus or after Jesus are the apostles, who enlighten our hearts by their Scriptures or precepts, and make in us certain days from the true light of which they partook, coming into this world. He, then, who is enlightened by their precepts is said to serve God in the days of the elders who were after Jesus. And as Christ "was the true light which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world", so they were the light of the world, according to that: "You are the light of the world." They enlighten for us, then, days in which we may serve the Lord.
**“that lived a long time after him”** — the days of the saints are long; the days of the wicked are shortened
**“and who knew”** — they did [them]
**“all the works of the Lord”**
• The Seventy: the great works of the Lord
• the work, namely, of patience, of justice and of all the virtues
2.8: **“AND [JOSUE] DIED”** — AND [JOSUE] DIED. In Paul Jesus lives, and in all who can say: "And I live, now not I; but Christ liveth in me", and: "To me to live is Christ, and to die is gain." In those he dies who, often repenting and sinning again, as it were insult the death of Jesus. Whence: "Crucifying again to themselves the Son of God, and making him a mockery." Not only, then, does he die in sinners, but he is also crucified and mocked. If thou thinkest of avarice, or of lewdness, if thou art driven by fury or by any vices whatever, Christ does not live in thee. Christ dies, then, to sinners, because in them justice, patience, truth and all those things which Christ is work nothing. But whatever works are done by the saints, it is Christ who works them. Whence: "I can do all things in him who strengtheneth me", Christ. Whence: He that shall confess me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven; but he that shall deny me before men, I will also deny before my Father. Of those who confess he said that they confess in him, because Christ lives and works in them; but he does not say the same of those who deny. For he who denies is outside him; he who confesses is in him. It is said, then, that Jesus died, and there arose another generation which knew not Jesus, etc.
2.10:
**“And all that generation was gathered to their fathers”** — the generation of evil thoughts, which proceeds from the heart and makes one forget the great work of God; fearing which the Apostle says: "Be mindful that the Lord Jesus Christ is risen again from the dead."
**“and there arose others that knew not the Lord, and the works which he had done for Israel.”**
• Augustine expounds: how did it say, they knew not the Lord? In those glorious works, namely, which were done before them, that Israel might know the Lord.
• that "he was crucified", namely, "for our sins, and rose again for our justification"
2.11:
**“And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and they served Baalim.”** — What each one loves and worships above all things, that is his god.
**“AND THEY SERVED BAALIM”** — AND THEY SERVED BAALIM. ADAMANTIUS. And they served Baalim and forsook the Lord God of their fathers. These things indeed the ancients did; but because these things are written for our sakes, let us see that the things said of them be not said for the greater part of us. Hear the Apostle: Know you not what the Scripture saith of Elias, how he calleth on God against Israel? Lord, they have slain thy prophets, they have dug down thy altars, and I am left alone, and they seek my life. But what saith the divine answer to him? I have left me seven thousand men that have not bowed their knees to Baal. Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant saved according to the election of grace. Thou seest, then, that he interprets those who bowed the knee to Baalim and those who did not of the remnant of the believers and the multitude of the unbelievers. For those who were unbelieving in the time of the Saviour bowed the knee to Baalim, but not those who believed and fulfilled the works of faith. For it is nowhere read that in the time of the Saviour anyone bent the knee to idols. But this is said of those who are held fettered by sins. Whence it is certain that when we sin we bow our knees to Baalim; we who have been called to this, to bend the knee in the name of Jesus, and to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom all paternity in heaven and earth is named. But it profits nothing if we bend the knees of the body to God in prayer, and the knees of the heart to the devil. For if I do not stand firm against his wiles, I have bent my knees to the devil; and if I do not stand constantly against anger, I have bent my knees to anger. The same is to be thought of all the vices. So did they who worshipped Baalim and forsook the God of their fathers. What each one worships, admires and loves before the rest, that is his god. This is what God asks of man before all things and above all things: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, etc.; desiring in a manner to take up for himself all the affections of the human mind, and knowing that what one has loved with his whole heart and whole soul and all his strength, that is his god. What, then, each one loves above all things, that is his god. With very many the love of gold and of avarice outweighs, and he says to them: "You cannot serve God and mammon", that is, avarice. In others the love of pleasure, or of worldly glory, or of human dignity. Few are they in whom the love of God outweighs. Hence the error of all heathenism took its beginning, while men will have the things they greatly love to be gods, and ascribe the divine name to human vices and desires. For those greedy of money and burning with the love of avarice call Mammon, among the Syrians, the god of covetousness; the lovers of lust and pleasure ascribe to themselves Venus as the goddess of this vice by which they are driven. Similarly in the other vices they made for themselves a god of the very affection by which they are urged. Whence the Apostle: Covetousness, which is the service of idols. When, then, we love any vices with our whole heart, our whole soul and all our strength, we adore idols.
2.13:
**“Forsaking him, and serving Baal and Astaroth.”** — See how much sins do: God, in whom there is no affection of anger, no motion of passion, is said to be provoked to wrath; but he remains unchangeable. I, when I sin, take wrath upon myself; whence: "Thou treasurest up to thyself wrath against the day of wrath", etc.
**“AUGUSTINE”** — AUGUSTINE. And they served Baal and the Astartes. Baal is said to be the name of Jupiter among those nations, and Astarte that of Juno. For the Punic people seem to call a lord Baal, and the lord of heaven Baalsamen; and without doubt they call Juno Astarte. And because these tongues differ little, the Scripture says here that they served Baal and the Astartes, that is, Jupiter and the Junos; nor did it say Astarte in the singular, but referred the sense to the multitude of the images. Yet I think that for the sake of variety it chose to mention Jupiter in the singular and Juno in the plural.
2.14:
**“And the Lord being angry against Israel, delivered them into the hands of plunderers: who took them and sold them to their enemies, that dwelt round about: neither could they stand against their enemies”** — AND THE LORD BEING ANGRY, etc. ORIGEN. According to the Seventy: and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about. But in the Psalm it is said: "Thou hast sold thy people for no price", and in the Prophet: You were sold gratis, and you shall be redeemed without money. Why, then, sold, if gratis, and not rather given? Or perhaps it is a manner of speech of the Scriptures that one is said to be sold even when given.
