That is, it filled the Synagogue, because the darkness of unbelief filled their minds; and the priests could not minister because of the cloud, because while they disdain to search out the mystical senses covered by the veil of the letter and the sacraments of Christ's nativity, they lost through the cloud of error the ministry due to their faith, so that, their deserts requiring it, they do not acknowledge the worship of belief, to whom in the cloud of his teaching the Lord told even open things about himself. But because the darkness of unbelief had filled the minds of the hearers, the cloud lying between hid as it were the ray of the sun sent forth.
8.12: **“Then Solomon said: The Lord said”** — that is, decreed
8.15: **“And Solomon said: Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth”** — through the prophets
8.21: **“And I have set there a place for the ark, wherein is the covenant of the Lord,”** — that is, the tables of the Testament
8.22: **“And Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord in the sight of the assembly of Israel, and spread forth”** — with bended knees
8.27: **“Is it then”** — not on this account, that thou needest it, for thou needest it not
8.38: **“Whatsoever curse or imprecation shall happen”** — or befall
8.55: **“And he stood and blessed”** — AND HE STOOD AND BLESSED etc. In Paralipomenon is related what is not said here: "Solomon had made a brazen scaffold, and had set it in the midst of the hall," standing upon which he blessed all the assembly of Israel.
8.58:
**“But may he incline our hearts to himself, that we may walk in all his ways, and keep his commandments, and his ceremonies,”** — that is, the legal ordinances
**“and all his judgments”** — the decisions of cases
**“which he commanded”** — as to the moral [precepts]
8.63: **“AND [THEY] DEDICATED THE TEMPLE OF THE LORD”** — RABANUS. The temple of the Lord is holy Church, according to that: "The temple of God is holy, which you are." This Christ the king dedicated when he cleansed it with his blood, sanctified it with the grace of the Holy Spirit, multiplied it with divers virtues. The children of Israel too dedicate it when the faithful, according to the gift bestowed on them, profit their neighbours by the word of preaching and the works of the virtues.
8.64:
**“IN THAT DAY THE KING SANCTIFIED THE MIDDLE”** — RABANUS. What is it that Solomon built [so the edition] the middle of the court, offering there because the brazen altar which was before the doors of the temple could not hold all, but that Christ now carries on fully in the Church the things that could not be accomplished in the law because of its weakness? For he himself is the court of the house of the Lord, because through him the entrance into the heavenly Jerusalem lies open. Because, then, holocausts and sacrifices could not be offered on the typical altar, in that all things were done there figuratively, our king raised up the altar of faith in the Church, on which holocausts and sacrifices are daily offered spiritually to God. Hence it is also that the Lord says: 'I would not holocausts and the blood of victims'.
**“THE BRAZEN ALTAR”** — [The altar] which Moses made was placed before the temple over against its gates; and because it was narrow and could not hold [all], he sanctified the middle of the court under the open sky, where he placed that very great altar which he had made of twenty cubits.
8.65:
**“A SOLEMN FEAST”** — RABANUS. In the Words of the Days it is written thus of the same matter: 'And Solomon kept the solemnity at that time seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from the entrance of Emath to the torrent. And he made on the eighth day a solemn assembly, because he had dedicated the altar seven days, and had kept the solemnity seven days.' 'So on the three and twentieth day of the seventh month, he sent the people away to their tents.' And the sense is that when the seven days of the dedication were completed, the days of Scenopegia followed, which began from the fifteenth day of the seventh month and ended on the twenty-second day. Both festivals, then, being rightly performed, and the eighth day of Scenopegia ended, the king sent the people away to their own, which Josephus also attests.
**“And Solomon made at the same time a solemn feast,”** — BEDE. Mystically. The solemnity which Solomon and all Israel kept signifies the joys of the saints which they have perpetually with Christ, the true peacemaker. The places too agree. For Emath is interpreted 'truth of the Lord'. The river or torrent of Egypt signifies 'temporal death', which no one dwelling in Egypt, that is, in the darkness of this world, can escape. All Israel, then, keeps the feast with Solomon from the river of Egypt to Emath when the saints, after the end of the present life, truly enjoy eternal joys with the Lord Christ. The feast is kept seven and seven days, because the elect, through sevenfold grace, now rejoice in hope in this life, which runs in sevens, and then in the true sabbath, that is, the rest of souls, they will rejoice in reality, that is, in the possession of the truth itself. The eighth day is the resurrection of the saints, which is to follow after the sabbath rest of souls. Then they will be placed in the heavenly mansions, five [so the edition], according to the qualities of their merits, where with eager heart they rejoice, praising God for the good things which the Father has bestowed in Christ on Christians.
**“FROM THE ENTRANCE OF EMATH”** — RABANUS. By the entrance of Emath he designates the northern quarter of Judea, by the river or torrent of Egypt the southern. This river is not the Nile, but another stream which flows into the sea near Rhinocorura [so the edition: 'Rivochorulam']. And Emath is a city of Syria, which is now called Epiphania, from Antiochus Epiphanes.
8.66:
**“And on the eighth day he sent away the people: and they blessed the king,”** — giving thanks for the works that he had done, and praying that Solomon might reign a long time
**“REJOICING”** — Singing hymns with delight, so that in that gladness they returned home without toil.

9.11: **“Hiram the king of Tyre furnishing Solomon with cedar trees and fir trees, and gold”** — HIRAM FURNISHING CEDAR TREES AND FIR TREES etc. RABANUS. The king of Tyre contributed much gold and silver, and cedar and cypress wood too, for the building; whom Solomon repaid with empty recompenses, among which he gave him twenty cities not far from Tyre. When these displeased him, he sent to Solomon and said he had no need of cities; and from then they were called the land of Gabaon [so the edition], which in the Phoenician tongue means 'to displease'. But Chabul is interpreted as it were 'bud'. How, then, were they called Chabul, unless perhaps it was said by irony, because they did not bear a bud with fulness of fruits?
9.13: **“And he said: Are these the cities which thou hast given me, brother? And he called them the land of Chabul,”** — that is, bad, not pleasing
9.14: **“And Hiram sent to king Solomon a hundred and twenty talents of gold.”** — before the towns were given him
9.17:
**“SO SOLOMON BUILT”** — RABANUS. The cities which he is said to have built, that is, Mello, and the wall of Jerusalem, Heser, Mageddo, Gazer and the rest, signify the beauty of the Church, which the true Solomon prepared for everlasting gladness. Now Mello is interpreted 'fulfilling', Heser 'separated' or 'sanctified', Mageddo 'his upper room', Gazer 'cutting off' or 'division', Bethoron 'house of the mountains', Baalath is interpreted 'ascending'. Holy Church, then, is itself the city of God, where the will of God is fulfilled. She, separated from error, is sanctified in faith and good works; there is the refreshment of the virtues. And she discerns the clean from the unclean, and is the house of the mountains, that is, the dwelling of the saints, and, as a flourishing palm, ascends with the fruit of justice "from virtue to virtue," that "the God of gods may be seen in Sion." Solomon fortified his towns that were without wall, because Christ so protects the companies of the faithful by his grace that they stand unconquerable by spiritual enemies.
**“So Solomon built Gazer, and Beth-horon the nether,”** — RABANUS. The cities which Solomon built were of the remnants of the Amorrhites, which the children of Israel could not destroy, as is read in Jesus son of Nave. These the king of Egypt afterwards overthrew and gave as a dowry to his daughter, the wife of Solomon, and therefore Solomon rebuilt them.
9.18: **“AND PALMIRA IN THE LAND OF THE WILDERNESS”** — An uninhabitable region, because water was found nowhere; but in that place where the city was built springs abound, and the palm, which in Greek is called 'palmyr'. It is Emath, or Epiphania, or Antioch.
9.20: **“ALL THE PEOPLE”** — RABANUS. Those who were not of the children of Israel our peacemaker made tributary when he uses those who are not in the number of the sons, but in the condition of slaves, for his own service. Such, though they oppose in many things, yet often serve the uses of the Church, when in the present time they afford comforts from their goods.
9.21: **“Their children, that were left in the land, to wit, such as the children of Israel had not been able to destroy, Solomon made tributary unto this day.”** — because he made the Chanaanites and Philistines serve and practise husbandry for the work of the children of Israel
9.22: **“But of the children of Israel Solomon made not any to be bondmen,”** — BUT OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL etc. RABANUS. Those who are not sons of the bondwoman but of the free, whom the Son of God freed by his blood, our Solomon did not appoint to serve, because he compels no one to serve with gentile rite, no one to keep the ceremonies of the old law in the times of the new Testament, but [makes them] to be warriors who fight against spiritual wickedness with the shield of faith and the sword of the Spirit, and to become his ministers, that is, to render him spiritual service in good works; and princes and captains, namely that they may rule themselves well and tame the wantonness of the flesh, or that they may rule well those subject to them and lead them into the paths of justice.
9.23: **“FIFTY”** — RABANUS. On the fiftieth day after the Pasch both the law was given on mount Sina and the Spirit Paraclete came upon the disciples. What, then, does this number of overseers signify, except that those who deserve to have knowledge of the Lord's law by the grace of the Holy Spirit can rule well both themselves and others?
9.25:
**“Solomon also offered three times”**
• at the Pasch, Pentecost, in Scenopegia, according to the precept of the law
• SOLOMON ALSO OFFERED etc. RABANUS. Our peacemaker offers three times when in his members he shows to God acceptable service through faith in the holy Trinity. For every faithful one offers holocausts to the Lord when he wears down the body by chastising it and hastens to consume the desires of the flesh with the fire of the Holy Spirit. He offers victims when he spreads out the vows of his lips in the praise of the Lord; peace offerings, when he shows the gift of good works. This he ought to offer upon the altar, because on the altar of the heart, where it is fitting that the divine fire always burn, that is, that the flame of charity always glow, whatever he labours at in abstinence, good working, giving of thanks, it is just that he offer it all to God in the sweetness of the Holy Spirit. And so he burnt incense when he prepares pure prayer to God in the secret of the heart and asks for the things that are pleasing to God.
9.26:
**“A FLEET”** — RABANUS. The fleet is the Church, which, set in the sea of the world, spends its zeal in acquiring the treasures of wisdom and knowledge and the riches of the virtues; where are the servants of Hiram, sailors skilled in the sea, with the servants of Solomon, when gentiles learned in worldly wisdom are joined in the unity of faith with those who are skilled in the law of Moses. These our Solomon sends to Ophir, which is interpreted 'weakening', that is, into the lowliness of the letter, that they may bring back the gold taken thence, that is, the precious sense, ascribing it not to themselves but to Solomon himself: as much as a hundred and twenty [so the edition] talents, that is, history, allegory, tropology, anagoge in the two Testaments.
**“And king Solomon made a fleet in Asiongaber,”**
• Asiongaber, which is interpreted 'hastening' or 'strong' or 'manfully'.
• it is an island at the Egyptian end of the Red Sea, where the fleet of Josaphat was broken by a storm
**“which is by Ailath on the shore of the Red Sea in the land of Edom.”** — or of Idumea
9.28: **“TO OPHIR”** — RABANUS. Ophir is the name of a province in India, named from Ophir of the posterity of Heber, which is also called the golden land, because it has golden mountains, which are inhabited by lions and most savage beasts. To these no one dares approach otherwise than standing in a ship by the shore and taking into their ship the earth which they find dug up by the claws of the lions, so that if the beasts perceive them they may easily withdraw to sea.

10.1:
**“And the queen of Saba”**
• Saba is a royal city of Ethiopia, whence was this queen, who ruled over two kingdoms, of Ethiopia and Egypt
• AND THE QUEEN etc. ISIDORE. Allegorically. This queen figured the Church to come from the gentiles, desiring Christ, which, clothed round with variety, and forgetting her people and her father's house, ran, barbarous in race not in mind, a stranger openly, in secret longing to become a fellow citizen of the saints.
10.2: **“And entering into Jerusalem with a great train, and riches, and camels that carried spices, and an immense quantity of gold, and precious stones, she came to king Solomon, and spoke to him all that she had in her heart.”** — She was eager to put forward questions and their solutions
10.4: **“And when the queen of Saba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house which he had built,”** — AND WHEN THE QUEEN OF SABA SAW etc. RABANUS. The queen, having seen Solomon and his glory, astonished at his wisdom, said: THE REPORT IS TRUE etc. So holy Church, having heard of the miracles of Christ, was stirred up to seek him. Having found him by faith, and having considered the testimonies of holy Scripture, acknowledging the power of his divinity, she thinks all that had been told her of him before to be little.
10.5:
**“And the meat of his table, and the apartments of his servants, and the order of his ministers,”** — the ministers of each order had garments of one colour only, that among so great a multitude of ministers there might be some recognition of the several offices
**“and their apparel, and the cupbearers, and the holocausts, which he offered in the house of the Lord: she had no longer any spirit in her,”** — RABANUS. The queen had no longer any spirit, namely as she considered his wisdom
10.8: **“Blessed are thy men, and blessed are thy servants, who”** — BLESSED ARE THY MEN etc. RABANUS. The queen, wondering, broke out in praise of Solomon, saying: BLESSED ARE THY MEN, AND BLESSED ARE THY SERVANTS etc. Truly blessed are they whose king is Christ, and who deserve to enjoy his eternal vision, and rejoice to behold the glory which he has with the Father and the Holy Spirit, and to perceive perpetually the wisdom which shows itself to the clean of heart.
10.10: **“And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices a very great store, and precious stones: there was brought no more such abundance of spices”** — that is, so precious
10.11:
**“THYINE TREES”** — RABANUS. Our maker sets the precious woods, that is, the holy teachers, whose greenness of faith does not decrease, nor do the words of their leaves fall, but they yield the fruit of good works in their seasons, for the defence of the house of God, that is, for the strengthening of his Church, that, walled about on every side by their doctrine and examples, it may not feel the ruin of crimes.
**“The navy also of Hiram, which brought gold from Ophir, brought from Ophir great plenty of thyine trees,”** — Incorruptible and thorny, in the likeness of the white thorn. Thyine woods are round and white; of them are made 'fulcra', so called from 'fulcire', to prop, namely supports for the strength of the temple, or the steps of the house of the Lord, and all the instruments of the musicians.
10.12: **“FOR SINGERS”** — RABANUS. These, whatever they do in word or work, do all for the praise of God; amid adversity and prosperity they do not cease to proclaim it in heart, mouth and work. Whence: "Upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen all the day and all the night, they shall never cease to praise the name of the Lord."
10.13: **“AND KING SOLOMON”** — RABANUS. And our peacemaker will give his Church all that she asks. Whence: 'Whatsoever you shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you.' Not only what we ask, but even what human frailty either does not know or does not presume to ask, he bestows as a free gift.
10.16:
**“TWO HUNDRED SHIELDS”** — RABANUS. In Paralipomenon golden spears are added to the shields, because the captains keeping watch before the door of the king's house used lances and shields. Whence: "Threescore valiant ones surround the bed of Solomon."
**“And Solomon made two hundred shields of the purest gold:”** — RABANUS. Those keeping watch at the doors of the royal house are the preachers, who guard the house of the Lord, to shut off the approach to those lying in wait. Two hundred spears were made from the sum of six hundred sicles, because the fathers of both Testaments were perfect in doctrine and working, since whatever they taught by word they proved by good works. The two hundred shields, each of which three hundred gold pieces covered, signify their perfect faith, which they had in the confession of the holy Trinity. Well, then, do the guards of the house of the Lord carry golden spears and shields, because the rulers of the Church, shining with the brightness of the wisdom above, both pierce the enemies with the darts of words and, repelling with the shield of faith, extinguish the fiery darts of the most wicked one.
**“he allowed six hundred sicles of gold for the plates”** — or plate
10.17:
**“And three hundred targets of fine gold:”** — targets are half shields, like the moon when it is half full
**“three hundred pounds”** — or mnae
**“OF THE FOREST OF LIBANUS”** — The forest of Libanus signifies the Church of the gentiles, which, cut off from the haughtiness of pride, is fitted into the building of the house of God. Whence: "We have found it in the fields of the wood."
10.18:
**“King Solomon also made a great throne of ivory:”**
• A THRONE OF etc. RABANUS. A throne or seat is the imperial chair, which in the Canticles is called a litter, because it carries those sitting in it, or carries them about from place to place. It was ascended by six steps of ascent. Under the seat was a golden footstool, and the top of the throne was round, held by two hands or arms on the outside, and beside them stood two lions helping to support the seat. Twelve little lions, because there were six steps of ascent, were placed on either side as a support for the ascending step.
• RABANUS. The throne of Solomon is understood to be the Church, in which our peacemaker, reigning, is known to do his judgments. Well is it said to have been made of ivory, since the elephant, whose bones these are, is very strong in sense among four-footed beasts, and mates temperately with its female and does not take a second mate; this fits the chaste, who follow the precepts of Christ through chastity. This he clothed with gold, because he made the splendour of his glory shine in it through miracles. In six days God finished the adornment of the world, which number by its perfection signifies the perfection of works. On the seventh God rested. And because [the world] consists of six ages, in which it is permitted to work, whoever desires the heavenly homeland, let him hasten to ascend by good works. The roundness of the throne behind signifies the eternal rest which is to be for the saints after this life, where whoever labours well here will, rewarded with his wage, enjoy perpetual quiet. The hands holding the seat signify the comforts of divine grace, which carry the Church forward to the heavenly kingdom. Therefore two, because it is preached in both testaments that one cannot advance to good except by divine help. By the two lions are figured the fathers of both Testaments, who learned by strength of mind to rule themselves and others. These will stand beside the hands, because the holy fathers ascribed whatever good they did not to themselves but to God. Whence: "Not to us, O Lord, not to us; but to thy name give glory." By the twelve little lions is signified the order of preachers following the apostolic doctrine. These stand on the six steps on this side and that, because they strive to fortify the steps of good works on this side and that by teachings and examples.
10.19: **“It had six steps: and the top of the throne was round behind: and there were two hands on either side holding the seat:”** — on the ascent of the steps there was a support on this side and that, that one might be better able to ascend
10.20: **“And twelve little lions stood upon the six steps on the one side and on the other: there was no such work made in any kingdom.”** — THERE WAS NO SUCH WORK MADE etc. This fitly suits the Church, to whom it is said: "Many daughters have gathered together riches: thou hast surpassed them all."
10.21:
**“Moreover all the vessels”** — MOREOVER ALL THE VESSELS etc. All the vessels which serve in the ministry of our Peacemaker are of gold, because all the souls of the saints, which are the vessels of God, shining with the splendour of wisdom and love that they may serve the divine will, hold the drink of life, and there is made in them a fountain of water springing up into life everlasting.
**“NOR WAS ANY ACCOUNT MADE OF IT”** — RABANUS. Because, according to the Apostle, 'the word of God is not in speech, but in power and the preaching of the gospel'. 'It consists not in the persuasive words of human wisdom, but in shewing of the Spirit and power; that our faith might not stand on the wisdom of men, but on the power of God.'
10.22: **“AND BROUGHT FROM THENCE GOLD, AND SILVER”** — RABANUS. What gold and silver signify is known. But the elephants' teeth signify teachers strong for the brightness of wisdom. By the apes are signified those who imitate human acts but live like beasts, who come to the faith from the gentiles, who seem to hold the faith and deny it by works. By the peacocks, whose flesh, if it be dried, is said to remain incorruptible, and because they are clothed with beauty of feathers, [are signified] the perfect, refined by the fire of tribulation so as to be adorned with various virtues. These are brought to our Solomon from Tharsis, that is, from the bitter waves of the world. Tharsis is called 'exploration of joy'.
10.23: **“exceeded”** — RABANUS. And our peacemaker is exalted above all the height of the saints, who are truly kings: "For who in the clouds can be compared to the Lord?"
10.24: **“And all the earth desired to see Solomon's face,”** — And the whole Church desires this, to come to the sight of the glory of our king. Whence: "I have sought thy face; thy face, O Lord, will I still seek."
10.25:
**“And every one brought him presents,”** — And each one, according as his strength suffices, is eager to render service to God in word or in deeds
**“vessels of silver and of gold, garments and armour,”** — ARMOUR [so the edition: 'prosequitur']. SOLOMON GATHERED TOGETHER CHARIOTS. RABANUS. Of these Josephus goes on: their riders were adorned, first, flourishing in comely youth, having great stature, letting their hair flow as they sat on the horses, clothed round with purple, who, being armed, and carrying bows, rode about the king before him when he was to go out to any place.
10.28: **“And horses were brought for Solomon out of Egypt, and Coa.”** — it is an island

11.1: **“And king Solomon”** — RABANUS. Scripture rebukes Solomon vehemently, and makes no mention of his penance or of God's pardon. Someone might perhaps say that the foreign women signify the Churches from the gentiles. This might perhaps be understood so if they had forsaken their gods for Solomon's sake; but since he for their sake worshipped their gods, there is nothing of true good that can be conjectured. There appears in the person of Solomon a wonderful excellence and a wonderful overthrow, a whirlpool to be wept over; what in him stood at different times, first good and afterwards evil, is shown in the Church at once. For his good things signify the good things of the Church, his evil things the evil things of the Church.
11.2: **“Of the nations concerning which the Lord said to the children of Israel: You shall not go in”** — or you shall go in
11.4: **“And when he was now old,”** — not in age but in manners or wisdom
11.5: **“But Solomon worshipped Astarthe”** — that is, Juno
11.11: **“And the Lord said to Solomon:”** — surely through Nathan the prophet or through another
11.13: **“Nor will I take away the whole kingdom, but I will give one tribe”** — besides his own
11.27: **“And this is the cause of his rebellion against him, for Solomon built Mello, and filled up the breach of the city”** — THE BREACH OF THE CITY. The wall of the city had fallen because on one side it overhung a precipice. When the king wished to fill up this breach level with the walls, he appointed captains to carry out this work; but Jeroboam, who was prince of the tribe of Joseph, would not obey the king, who had earlier set him over the buildings of the fortifications which he was making in Jerusalem, where he laboured so that the king conferred on him the command of the soldiery over the tribe of Joseph. But having become a rebel he goes out of Jerusalem, and the prophet meets him, turning him aside into a field, so that no one should dare to say anything to him. And, puffed up by the prophet's words, he urged the people to make him king; hearing which, Solomon sought to kill him.
11.28: **“And Jeroboam was a strong and valiant man.”** — AND JEROBOAM WAS A STRONG MAN etc. He refused this command of restoring the walls. But whence such boldness? Because the king had made him an overseer.
11.29: **“So it came to pass at that time, that Jeroboam went out”** — on account of the rebellion
11.31: **“TAKE TO THEE TEN PIECES”** — RABANUS. Ten tribes were separated from the house of David and two were left, because, as the Apostle says: "A remnant is saved according to the election of grace." Jeroboam, who, separating ten tribes from the temple of God, led them to idolatry, signifies the heretics who rend the unity of the catholic faith with heresies, and so subject [men] to the worship of evil spirits. Jeroboam is interpreted 'judging the people'. For heretics seem to judge the people when they make them followers of their error. They take ten pieces when they corrupt the precepts of the law by violating them; and one tribe remained with the offspring of David while the lot of the elect remained in the rule of the catholic faith, because: "One God, one faith, one baptism."
11.40: **“Solomon therefore sought to kill Jeroboam”** — because he urged the people to withdraw from Solomon
11.42: **“And the days that Solomon reigned”** — AND THE DAYS THAT. Josephus said that he reigned eighty years and lived ninety-four. But divine Scripture expresses only those years in which he reigned before he transgressed.

12.4: **“Thy father laid a most grievous yoke upon us,”** — A MOST GRIEVOUS YOKE. How is this true, since it was said above 'that Solomon did not appoint any of the children of Israel to serve'? Surely he did not make them serve in husbandry or other servile work. But he appointed princes from them throughout the several tribes, who rendered to the king by turns each month the provision and the other things which are related above of the king's expenses. This they now call a most grievous yoke.
12.6: **“And king Roboam consulted with the old men”** — these old men are thought to be Banaias and Joiada and the other princes of Solomon
12.8: **“THE YOUNG MEN”** — Of whom Aduram was one, who was afterwards stoned. Scripture does not always call men young according to age, but according to instability of mind. For Roboam began to reign in the fortieth year of his age.
12.11: **“SCORPIONS”** — It is a kind of scourge, as rods from thorns or fruit trees are also wont to be knotted; or else the scourge of the Saracens with two or three rods, which has leaden balls at the tip, otherwise called hailstones.
12.12: **“So Jeroboam and all the people came to Roboam”** — TO ROBOAM. RABANUS. Roboam was of the house of David, but did not walk in his way. "For Juda," Scripture witnessing, "did evil in the sight of the Lord in those days, and provoked him above all that their fathers had done; and did all the abominations of the nations." Roboam, then, signifies 'evil rulers in the Church', who, given to earthly desires and delighting in the multitude of those who wait on them, have no daily care for those committed to them. Roboam is interpreted 'breadth of the people', because such walk the spacious and broad way which leads many to death. And, leaving the counsel of the holy fathers, whose sayings and examples tend to the heights, they obey those who, enslaved to youthful desires, weigh them down with wicked praises and flatteries; whom wisdom threatens, saying: "Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and when the princes eat in the morning." And on the contrary: "Blessed is the land, whose king is noble, and whose princes eat in due season."
12.16: **“Then the people seeing that the king would not hearken to them, answered him, saying: What portion have we in David? or what inheritance”** — the driving home of the words
12.18: **“Then king Roboam sent Aduram, who was over the tribute: and all Israel stoned him”** — or Israel
12.20: **“And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam was come again, that they sent and called him, when they were assembled together, and made him king over all Israel, and there was none that followed the house of David but the tribe of Juda only.”** — therefore 'only', because it was the principal one, [and] the other two not, namely Benjamin and the Levitical
12.23: **“Speak to Roboam”** — this prophet is brought in suddenly, as are others
12.25: **“And Jeroboam built Sichem in mount Ephraim, and dwelt there, and going out from thence, he built Phanuel.”** — Phanuel, the chief city of the kingdom of Jeroboam
12.28: **“And finding out a device, he made two golden calves”** — HE MADE TWO CALVES. Why or how Jeroboam made calves Josephus explains sufficiently.

13.1:
**“And behold there came a man of God”**
• And behold a man of God, whose name is passed over here. In Paralipomenon he is called or named Gaddo. He is the Gad who warned David to go into the land of Juda.
• RABANUS. The prophet sent by God to rebuke Jeroboam, who, seduced by the false prophet, ate and drank against the Lord's command and therefore was killed by a lion on the way. What does this signify, except that when one is lifted up in prosperity so as to despise the Lord's commands, he is torn by the lion who goes about seeking whom he may devour, with the tooth of evil persuasion, and is killed through consent to sin? And therefore it is always necessary to seek the protection of the Almighty, which is thought less necessary if it is always had, but is often usefully withdrawn, that man may be shown to himself how he is nothing without it.
13.6: **“And the king said to the man of God: Entreat the face of the Lord thy God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored to me. And the man of God entreated the face of the Lord, and the king's hand was restored to him”** — or the king's
13.11:
**“Now there dwelt an old prophet in Bethel,”** — NOW THERE DWELT AN OLD PROPHET. This false prophet was the chief of the priests and was much honoured by the king as a diviner; and fearing lest through the word of the man of God the king should withdraw from the worship of idols and kill him as a sorcerer, he devised to deceive the man of God, acting quite craftily, that by transgressing God's command he might incur his wrath, as afterwards happened when he believed man rather than God; and that thereby the things he had foretold might be shown to be false, and so he might persuade the king, as he did. And the king, hearing the outcome, thought vain the things the man of God had said, and did not turn from his evil way.
**“and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Bethel:”** — ALL THE WORKS THAT THE MAN [OF GOD] HAD DONE etc. GREGORY. In the deeds of the prophet wonderful things go before, wretched things follow. In which matter what do we gather, except that, having gloried in himself on account of his great works, he was soon shaken from his inward firmness, and fault crept upon him in deed from the place whence glory crept upon him in heart, that, deceived, he might learn from a false prophet that what had happened before was by no means of his own strength.
13.20: **“And as they sat at the table, the word of the Lord came to the prophet that brought him back.”** — or brought him back
13.21: **“And he cried out to the man of God that came out of Juda, saying: Thus saith the Lord:”** — THUS SAITH THE LORD etc. GREGORY. Well did he receive the sentence of death from the mouth of him by whose bringing back he had strayed from the commands of life, that he might truly take the penalty from the same source whence he had negligently committed the fault.
13.24: **“AND THE LION STOOD BY THE BODY”** — Here it is shown that the sin of disobedience was loosed in death itself, because the same lion that presumed to kill him living did not dare to touch him slain. For he who had power to kill did not receive leave to eat of the body of the slain, because he whose fault had been punished in life was now just through death.
13.31: **“And after they had mourned over him, he said to his sons: When I am dead, bury me in the sepulchre, wherein the man of God is buried: lay my bones beside his bones.”** — BURY ME IN THE SEPULCHRE WHEREIN THE MAN OF GOD etc. The evil prophet, knowing that what the man of God foretold would come to pass, commanded that he be buried beside the man of God, so that his bones should never be dug up to be burnt, but be preserved through the holy prophet, as the same book witnesses below was fulfilled.

14.3: **“And take with thee ten loaves, and cracknels”** — a crustulum of bread, a crustum of gold
14.5:
**“And the Lord said to Ahias: Behold the wife of Jeroboam cometh in to consult thee concerning her son that is sick: thus and thus shalt thou speak to her. Now when she was coming in,”** — or was entering
**“and feigned herself”** — or was feigning
14.11: **“Them that shall die of Jeroboam in the city, the dogs shall eat: and them that shall die in the field, the birds of the air shall devour:”** — so it must be done
14.13: **“And all Israel shall mourn for him, and shall bury him: for he only of Jeroboam shall be laid in the grave,”** — with honour
14.19: **“And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he fought, and how he reigned, behold they are written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel.”** — Not in Paralipomenon, but in another book which we do not have
14.21: **“And Roboam the son of Solomon reigned in Juda.”** — Here a period
14.24: **“And there were also the effeminate”** — in act or by nature
14.28: **“And when the king went into the house of the Lord, they that were to go before him, carried them: and afterwards they brought them back to the armoury of the shieldbearers.”** — where arms are laid up; an 'armarium' is where the tools of any other arts [are laid up]
14.29: **“Now the rest of the acts of Roboam, and all that he did, behold they are written in the book of the words”** — that is, Paralipomenon

15.2: **“He reigned three years in Jerusalem: the name of his mother was Maacha, the daughter of Abessalom.”** — that is, Absalom
15.3: **“And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as the heart of David his father.”** — or his
15.13: **“And he also removed his mother Maacha from being the princess in the sacrifices of Priapus, and in his grove which she had consecrated: and he destroyed her den, and broke in pieces the filthy idol, and burnt it by the torrent Cedron.”** — perhaps it did not stand through him
15.22: **“Then king Asa sent word to all Juda, saying: Let no one be excused.”** — and they came
15.31: **“But the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the words of the days of the kings of Israel?”** — This book we do not have in our library

16.1:
**“And the word of the Lord came to Jehu”**
• or: Hieu
• AND THE WORD OF THE LORD CAME TO JEHU. Mention of this prophet is made in no other place, but he is brought in suddenly, as others are; whence Abdias is said to have fed seventy [so the edition] prophets in caves. And Elias says: "They have slain thy prophets," and the sons of the prophets are read to have met Eliseus, of whom no other mention is made, no particular naming.
16.3: **“BEHOLD I WILL CUT DOWN THE POSTERITY”** — Mystically. RABANUS. The Lord cuts down the posterity of this or of any wicked man when he punishes sins after the end of life. He cuts down the posterity of his house too when he condemns his imitator to eternal torments. Whoever, then, perseveres in evil works up to the end of life, his posterity will be cut down.
16.4: **“HIM THAT SHALL DIE OF BAASA”** — RABANUS. Of Baasa, that is, of the body of the devil, most full of confusion. He dies in the city who, persevering in the Church as far as faith, is liable to capital crimes. He is torn by the mouth of dogs when he is rebuked, reproved, condemned by the sentences of the teachers; of whom in the psalms: "Like dogs they shall go round about the city." For dogs, canes, are so called from singing, canendo. For it is the custom of dogs to defend those places in which they know they find food. O blessed dogs, who pursue the unbelievers, drive off the thieves, guard the holy sheepfolds! Those of Baasa die in the country who outside the Church serve idolatry or heresy with wicked mouth and work; these the birds of the air eat, those which eat the seed sown by the way, when they snatch them, laden with sins, with themselves to eternal destruction.
16.6: **“And Baasa slept with his fathers, and he was buried in Thersa:”** — that city
16.12: **“And Zambri destroyed all the house of Baasa, according to the word of the Lord, which he had spoken to Baasa, by the hand of Jehu”** — or: Jehu
16.23: **“In the one and thirtieth year of Asa king of Juda, Amri reigned over Israel twelve years: in Thersa he reigned six years.”** — IN THERSA HE REIGNED SIX YEARS. RABANUS. Six years he spent in Thersa, the rest in the city which is called Macheronta [so the edition] by the Greeks, Samaria. He named it Someron, from Somer its former lord, and it is the chief city of the kingdom, and afterwards the whole region was called Samaria from it, which is now called Sebaste, where the bones of blessed John the Baptist rest.
16.34:
**“AHIEL BUILT”** — RABANUS. Ahiel, [interpreted] 'living to God', [of] Bethel, interpreted 'house of God', restored the walls of Jericho, destroyed and laid under anathema by Josue. When one of those who had taken the habit of religion in the Church returns to doing the crimes which the Lord Jesus had forgiven him on the day of baptism, and seeks again by living luxuriously the pomps of the devil which he himself had anathematized; and when he prefers the dogmas of errors or the fables of the gentiles to the ecclesiastical truth in which he was steeped, he raises up the ruins of Jericho as one going out from Bethel. He loses both the foundations of faith, from which he might begin good buildings, and the gates of good action, by which they ought to have been completed.
**“IN ABIRAM HIS FIRSTBORN”** — RABANUS. When the builder of Jericho laid the foundations, his firstborn, Abiram by name, died; when he fortified the gates, he lost Segub, his youngest son, according to the imprecation of Josue.

17.1:
**“And Elias the Thesbite said”** — Thesba, whence Elias is called the Thesbite, is a city of the region of Galaad
**“ELIAS THE THESBITE”** — RABANUS. Elias is interpreted 'my God the Lord' or 'my God' or 'strong God', and signifies Christ. Thesbite is interpreted 'taking captive' or 'turning back', and it is written of the Lord: "Turn again our captivity, O Lord." As of Melchisedech, so the origin of Elias is passed over in silence, when his name is suddenly brought in; and this in prefiguration of the Saviour.
**“IN WHOSE SIGHT I STAND”** — RABANUS. The just man stands in the sight of the Lord now, and will stand also in the future: now, that he may bring the power of the creator home to his sense and so live faithfully; in the future, that he may truly receive the crown of life.
17.3: **“Get thee hence, and go towards the east, and hide thyself by the torrent of Carith, which is over against the Jordan,”** — HIDE THYSELF etc. Our Elias was hidden in the torrent of Carith, which is interpreted 'bald'. And he drank of the torrent when, in the place of Calvary, where his strength was hidden, he tasted of the torrent of our mortality. The ravens fed Elias, bringing him bread and flesh, when the gentiles, coming from the blackness of sins, enlightened through his grace, offer to Christ, hungering for our salvation, the bread of faith and flesh, that is, the hope of the resurrection: in the morning, namely at the beginning of the gospel preaching; and likewise in the evening, when, keeping the same faith undefiled to the end of the world, it presents it with the resurrection of the flesh to the coming judge. After some days the torrent was dried up, because when the course of the present life is completed death will be swallowed up in victory, and now 'death shall be no more, nor mourning, nor crying, for the former things are passed away'. The bread and flesh with which Elias was fed by the ravens' ministry are the works of piety and the service shown to the Lord by the faithful from among the Jews.
17.5:
**“BY THE TORRENT OF CARITH”** — The torrent Cison, which is also Carith, is interpreted 'knowledge' or 'cutting off' or 'division'; it suits the Jewish people.
**“which is over against the Jordan.”** — it notes the opposite position of the place
17.9:
**“Arise, and go to Sarephta of the Sidonians,”** — a city
**“and dwell there: for I have commanded a widow woman there to feed thee.”** — that is, I have given her wherewith to feed thee
17.10:
**“A WIDOW WOMAN”** — ISIDORE. The widow whom the Lord feeds not with the bread of corn but of the word is she who, her husband being dead, marries whom she will, that is, having shaken off the yoke of slavery she takes up Christ's 'sweet yoke and light burden'.
**“He arose, and went to Sarephta. And when he was come to the gate of the city, he saw the widow woman”** — RABANUS. This widow signifies the Church of the gentiles, which, long forsaken by her creator, did not know the people of true faith and right truth, [and] nourished as it were a poor son of needy stock, that is, taught in part with the fruit of the word, until the prophetic word came, which, the fleece of Israel being dried up, as the gate of heaven being shut, was in danger of famine in Judea, that it might there be fed and at the same time feed, namely received by those who believe and itself refreshing the believers. This widow is said to have dwelt in Sarephta of Sidon. For Sidon is interpreted 'useless hunting', Sarephta 'burning' or 'straitness of bread', because "where sin abounded, grace did more abound": where care was spent on acquiring superfluous things, where before there was the burning of dire thirst and straitness of spiritual bread. There the meal and oil are blessed by the mouth of the prophet. This is the grace of the Lord's body and the anointing of chrism, or the fruit and cheerfulness of charity. The oil of grace and the meal of blessing do not fail the widow, the famine remaining among almost all the nations, whose hunger for the food of life and want of the faith of the Trinity that famine of three years of old fittingly prefigured; which was followed by spiritual abundance, which, while it is spent, is said not to have failed.
17.12:
**“And she answered: As the Lord thy God liveth, I have no bread,”** — RABANUS. Straitness of bread is the hunger of the spiritual life and want of faith in the holy Trinity
**“but only a handful of meal in a pot, and a little oil in a cruse:”** — that is, in a vessel
**“behold I am gathering two sticks”** — ISIDORE. Both by the name of wood and by the number of the sticks the sign of the cross is expressed, by which the bread of eternal life has been prepared for us.
17.14: **“For thus saith the Lord the God of Israel: The pot of meal shall not waste, nor the cruse”** — the vessel in which I put the oil
17.17:
**“THE SON OF THE WOMAN FELL SICK”** — RABANUS. The widow with whom Elias lodged, and whose meal and oil he blessed, is 'the Synagogue of the Jews', which, widowed by the death of Moses, was nourishing a little son, that is, the carnal people of the Jews; at the entrance of Elias, that is, of our Saviour, it was sick with the fever of unbelief, because it did not believe in him but spurned him. Whence the mother Synagogue complains of the Saviour's coming, as though he were the cause of the people's slaying, saying: "What have I to do with thee?" etc. Hence it is that Caiphas said: "It is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not."
**“And it came to pass after this, that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick,”** — RABANUS. As the prophet is not exasperated by the widow's words but rather has pity, so our Redeemer is not exasperated by the malice of the Jews, but, pitying his people, took him from his mother's bosom when he took him from the carnal observance of the law, and laid him upon his own bed, that is, showed him that he had life in his death. And he stretched himself three times while he instilled the faith of the Trinity.
17.23: **“And Elias took the child,”** — AND ELIAS TOOK. RABANUS. Elias took the child and gave him back to his mother when our Lord, saving the believing people, showed signs and miracles to the unbelievers, that they might truly know that he lives who believes in his name. And so it will come about that the Jewish people, overcome by the truth, will cry out to Christ: Now by this I know that thou art a man of God.
17.24: **“And the woman said to Elias: Now by this”** — deed

18.1: **“After many days, the word of the Lord came to Elias, in the third year,”** — The three years of famine prefigured that the knowledge of the holy Trinity was lacking to the people of the Jews, or in the whole world. The six months pertain to good work, which had wholly ceased among them. Whence: There is none that doth good etc.
18.6: **“AND ABDIAS”** — Abdias, prince of the army of Israel, whose name is interpreted 'servant of the Lord', prefigured those of the princes of the Jews who believed and were secret disciples, as Nicodemus and Joseph.
18.16: **“So Abdias went to meet Achab,”** — This was the husband of that woman who had oil in a cruse; whence the miracle was done on account of the debt, because he fed a hundred prophets. She was pressed to sell her son, for his father was dead
18.23: **“Let two bullocks be given us, and let them choose one bullock for themselves, and cut it in pieces and lay it upon wood, but put no fire under: and I will dress the other bullock, and lay it on wood, and put no fire”** — or but
18.30: **“Elias said to all the people: Come ye unto me. And the people coming near unto him, he repaired the altar of the Lord,”** — HE REPAIRED THE ALTAR. RABANUS. And our Redeemer, fighting against the prince of the world and his attendants and overcoming them, cleansing the altar of the Lord which had been destroyed, that is, the hearts of the faithful, from the stain of iniquity, dedicates an altar to God, which is said to have been built of twelve stones, because of those who follow the prophetic and apostolic faith or doctrine a most pleasing altar is built to God, on which the sacrifice of praise is offered for an odour of sweetness.
18.32: **“AND HE MADE A TRENCH”** — RABANUS. Namely, from a contrite heart and humbled spirit, bringing forth rivers of tears for fear of hell and desire of eternal life. There too he laid the wood, because he set the sayings and deeds of the saints as an example for believers. And he divided the members of the bullock and laid them upon the wood, when he taught the faithful to form all their acts after the example of the holy fathers. And he commanded water to be poured on the holocaust and on the wood once, again and a third time, because at all times it is necessary to cleanse our words, thoughts and works in pure working and the compunction of tears, and not to cease before the trenches of the water-course are filled, that is, until the future joy, succeeding the present grief, is perfectly fulfilled. And so it will be according to what follows: The fire fell from heaven and consumed the holocaust etc., when the discernment of the judge above, perfectly examining our sayings and deeds and our whole life, proving us "as silver is tried by the fire," will set us, made immortal and blessed, in an everlasting seat, that after the likeness of the Israelites we may sing, rejoicing for ever: The Lord he is God.
18.40:
**“TAKE”** — RABANUS. So our Redeemer, when the day of judgment comes, will send his angels, and they will gather all scandals out of his kingdom, and cast them into the pool of fire, where they will be tormented according to their hardness and impenitent heart.
**“and let not one of them escape. And when they had taken them,”** — or seized
18.41: **“OF ABUNDANCE OF RAIN”** — ISIDORE. When Christ the Son of God was born among men and took the tenderness of our flesh, after he tasted death and ascended victorious from the world to heaven, he sent from on high to the earth the rain of divine grace through the sevenfold Spirit, to cleanse us from sin and make us bring forth spiritual fruits.
18.45: **“And while he turned himself this way and that way, behold the heavens grew dark,”** — or were darkened

19.1: **“And Achab told Jezabel all that Elias had done,”** — RABANUS. In the virtues of Elias, because he was strong with the power of God; in his weaknesses he recognized what he could do of himself. There he showed what he had received; here he guarded what he had received. In the miracles he was shown forth, in the weaknesses he was [unclear in the edition: "eruabatur"].
19.3: **“Then Elias was afraid,”** — THEN ELIAS WAS AFRAID. RABANUS. Holy men are caught up to the heights by the uplifting Spirit; but as long as they are in this life they are held down by temptations lest they grow proud. Hence it is that Elias, when he had advanced in so many virtues, afterwards fled from Jezabel, a queen indeed but yet a weak woman; and he who raised the dead, foresaw things to come, and did other illustrious things, struck with fear fled death from the hand of a woman, sought death from the hand of God, and did not receive it.
19.5: **“AND BEHOLD AN ANGEL”** — RABANUS. The angel who fed Elias signifies "the angel of great counsel," by whose works we subsist both in bodily and in spiritual nature.
19.6: **“He looked, and behold there was at his head a hearth cake, and a vessel of water:”** — AND BEHOLD etc. A HEARTH CAKE AND A VESSEL etc. RABANUS. Elias, fed with these, expresses the weakness of our nature, for which simple food does not suffice, but twofold, that we may be able to ascend to the heights. For as the body cannot subsist without bodily nourishment, so neither can the soul live without the word of God.
19.8: **“AND HE AROSE, AND ATE, AND DRANK”** — RABANUS. So we too, while we shake off from us the sleep of sloth, must, strengthened by divine comfort, hasten with the utmost effort by the step of good works through the whole time of the present life to ascend the mount of God and his holy place, that there we may find eternal rest.
19.11:
**“And he said to him: Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord: and behold the Lord passeth, and a”** — that is, wind
**“AND A GREAT AND STRONG WIND”** — RABANUS. The wind before the Lord overthrows mountains and breaks rocks, because the dread which rushes in at his coming both casts down the height of our heart and melts its hardness. But the Lord is said not to be in the wind of commotion and in the fire, but is not denied to be in the whistling of a gentle air, because when the mind is suspended in contemplation, whatever it sees perfectly is not God; when it sees something subtle, this is what it hears of the incomprehensible substance. For we perceive as it were the whistling of a gentle air when by sudden contemplation we taste subtly the savour of the uncircumscribed truth. After the whistling of the gentle air the prophet covered his face with his mantle, because in the very contemplation of truth man recognizes with how great ignorance he is covered. For to draw a mantle over the face is to veil the mind by consideration of its own weakness, lest it dare to seek things higher than itself. The cave is the dwelling of our corruption; but when we begin to perceive something of the divinity, we stand as it were already at the entrance of our cave. For because we cannot go forth perfectly, yet, gaping for the knowledge of truth, we already catch something of the air of liberty. To stand in the entrance of the cave, then, is, the obstacle of our corruption being checked, to begin to go out to the knowledge of truth.
**“before the Lord overthrowing the mountains, and breaking the rocks in pieces:”** — will pass
**“THE LORD IS NOT IN THE WIND”** — That is, do not think that the Lord comes with the wind; but after the wind of commotion, that is, the whirlwind and onset of the wind, the fire will pass, then THE WHISTLING OF A GENTLE AIR; after this the Lord will pass to speak with thee.
19.14: **“I ALONE”** — RABANUS. What was difficult for so great a prophet in knowing that servants had remained to God in this world? But he who, humble, knew even the hidden things of God, when lifted up did not know even the open ones. Whence it is certain that he enlightens himself with the ray of humility who weighs carefully the good of others, because while he sees the things which he himself has done done also outwardly by others, he presses down the swelling of pride which strives to burst out within from singularity. Hence it is that by the voice of God it is said to Elias, who thought himself alone: I have left me seven thousand men, that, knowing he had not remained alone, he might bow down the glory of elation which rose in him from singularity.
19.15: **“THOU SHALT ANOINT HAZAEL”** — Not otherwise than that he foretold he would be king; Eliseus not otherwise than by casting his mantle over him. Those two kings neither he himself nor his disciple Eliseus anointed, but one of the prophets was sent to anoint Jehu.
19.17: **“WHOSOEVER SHALL ESCAPE”** — RABANUS. Divine justice causes some of the guilty to be punished by kings with the sword; others it pierces through by prophets and priests with the sword of the tongue.
19.19: **“And Elias departing from thence, found Eliseus the son of Saphat, ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen:”** — AND ELIAS DEPARTING FOUND ELISEUS THE SON OF SAPHAT etc. When our Redeemer, coming down from heaven, acquired by divine judgment a people still gaping after earthly works, in which he wrought salvation when he converted it to faith. For Elias is interpreted 'Lord God', Saphat 'judging', Eliseus 'salvation of my God'. Over whom the prophet cast his mantle when the Lord clothed the people with the catholic faith. Whence the Apostle: "As many of you as have been baptized in Christ, have put on Christ." Leaving the oxen he runs after Elias, because the choir of the elect, having heard "Unless one renounce all, he cannot be my disciple," at once ceased to gape after earthly gains and to serve worldly desires, and so preached the word of life to others; for this is to kiss father and mother: to wish to correct by word whomever one can, whether of the Jews or of the gentiles.
19.21:
**“AND HE KILLED”** — RABANUS. The Christian people too, slaying carnal desires, turns its whole exercise to the work of evangelizing, whence it can provide sufficient food for its hearers.
**“HE FOLLOWED ELIAS”** — RABANUS. He follows our Elias and ministers to him who, following his footsteps, that is, keeping his commandments, is busy to show him worthily the ministry of good things.

20.1: **“BENADAD”** — RABANUS. Benadad signifies the devil, who draws together various armies of evil spirits to overthrow the people of God, but is conquered by the servants of the princes of Israel, that is, by the good hearers of the teachers; because when they fulfil in deeds what they hear with the ear, the ancient enemy is turned to flight, and all his army is thrown into confusion by the soldiers of Christ, who are well said to be two hundred thousand and thirty-two [so the edition], because those who perfectly hold the knowledge of both Testaments, and keep the faith of the Trinity with twofold charity, are proved fit for the warfare of the supreme king.
20.10: **“And the messengers returned to him, and he sent again, and said: The gods do so and so to me, and more also,”** — THE GODS DO SO TO ME AND etc. Samaria, after the manner of cities, had the ground inside almost level with the walls themselves, by which support it might resist the blows of the ram; outside, the height of the walls rose far above the surface of the ground. The proud king, then, terrifying the besieged, said that he had so great a multitude that if each of the soldiers brought one stone or stake or sod to build a mound against the city, a field would rise up which would seem level with the surface that was within the walls, so that, fighting on a level against the city, they might throw darts or torches.
20.11:
**“And the king of Israel answering, said:”** — checking the rashness of arrogance with a modest speech, he said
**“Tell him: Let not the girded”** — still clad in arms
**“LET NOT THE GIRDED BOAST”** — RABANUS. He is girded who is surrounded with a girdle; ungirded, who has laid aside the girdle. The king of Israel, then, says to the king of Syria, who was boasting as though he had already taken Samaria, which he had begun to besiege: LET NOT THE GIRDED BOAST HIMSELF AS THE UNGIRDED; as if to say: do not boast as a victor, you who, still set in the battle line, do not know whom victory will follow; for he who believed he was conquering was conquered.
**“boast himself as the ungirded.”** — the victor, his arms laid aside
20.20:
**“And they slew every one the man that came against him: and the Syrians fled, and Israel pursued after them. And Benadad the king of Syria fled”**
• AND BENADAD THE KING OF SYRIA FLED. RABANUS. That is, the devil, prince of the wicked, whose eyes are lofty (for Syria [is interpreted] 'lofty'), trusting in the horse of his pride, with the horsemen, namely all the proud, because he is head over all the children of pride, overcome by the army of Christ is turned to flight; and THE KING OF ISRAEL SMOTE THE HORSES AND CHARIOTS etc., because the King of kings overwhelms the spiritual wickednesses by blotting out the sins of the human race.
• RABANUS. The devil, though often conquered by the saints, yet renews the battle against them, and while he is conquered in one way he at once tries to conquer in another.
• RABANUS. The evil spirits, if they are conquered in spiritual things, prepare war in bodily things, busy to cast souls down from the heights to the depths, that they may conquer more easily. If they see them desiring heavenly things, they thrust earthly things on them to love; if thanks are given to God for prosperity granted, they strive that they may be broken by adversity. But as the Syrians, so the demons, where they trusted to overcome, there were overcome.
20.22: **“And a prophet came to the king of Israel, and said to him: Go, and strengthen thyself, and know, and see what thou dost: for the next”** — or for
20.35:
**“Then a certain man”** — Micheas
**“of the sons of the prophets said to his companion in the word of the Lord: Strike me.”** — on the head
20.36: **“Then he said to him: Because thou wouldst not hear the voice of the Lord, behold thou shalt depart from me, and a lion shall kill thee.”** — which when it had happened
20.38:
**“So the prophet went, and met”** — with his head bound
**“SO THE PROPHET WENT”** — Micheas used a parable on account of the words he was to say to the king, to show that this pertained to him rather than to himself.
20.41: **“But he forthwith wiped off the dust from his face,”** — his head unbound
20.42:
**“And he said to him: Thus saith the Lord: Because thou hast let go out of thy hand a man worthy of death,”** — Benadad the blasphemer
**“thy life shall be for his life,”** — because he himself will destroy thee
**“THY LIFE SHALL BE”** — The servants of God must take care lest, after the example of Achab, they flatter themselves with pernicious security as long as the enemy lives, lest, while they think themselves as it were victors, they be quickly dashed down through the fraud of the devil promising peace; because as then the prophet declared to the king that vengeance would come for his ill-considered pity, so now the prophetic word declares that if we make a pact with the devil eternal punishment hangs over us thereby.
20.43: **“AND FURIOUS”** — Achab, angered, commanded the prophet to be kept shut up, and, confounded by the words of Micheas, returned home.

21.2: **“NABOTH”** — [Naboth] is interpreted 'conspicuous' or 'possession'; Jezrahel 'honour of God' or 'seed of God'. This all fits the Son of God, 'who is the brightness of glory', 'whom God hath appointed heir of all things'. This Naboth had a vineyard, of which: "Thou hast brought a vineyard out of Egypt." This Achab coveted, who is interpreted 'brother of the father', that is, the Jewish people, of whom is Christ according to the flesh, to make a garden of herbs, that is, that where spiritual wine ought to have sprung up, there he might transplant the frail dogmas of the Pharisees. For Naboth, unwilling to give the vineyard, that is, for Christ, not consenting to the superstitions of the Pharisees, impious Jezabel, that is, the Synagogue, plotted death. For Jezabel is interpreted 'dwelling with' or 'vain' or 'empty flowing', because the Synagogue seemed to dwell in the house of the Lord, but flowed away through vain desires.
21.13: **“And bringing two men, sons of the devil, they made them sit against him: and they, like men of the devil, bore witness against him before the people, saying: Naboth hath blasphemed God and the king: wherefore they brought him forth without the city,”** — And Christ suffered without the gate by false witnesses
21.16: **“And when Achab heard that Naboth was dead, he arose, and went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezrahelite,”** — TO THE VINEYARD OF NABOTH. The vineyard of Naboth is 'the Church from the gentiles'. This, Christ being slain, the wicked husbandmen strove to snatch away, when they tried to extinguish the faith which is through him, and to set before [it] and plant in the gentiles who were to be instructed their own justice which is of the law.

22.19: **“And he added and said: Therefore hear thou the word of the Lord: I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the army of heaven standing by him on the right hand and on the left.”** — I SAW THE LORD SITTING ON HIS THRONE. The throne of the Lord is 'the angelic powers', presiding over whose minds God disposes all things below. The army of heaven is 'the multitude of ministering angels'. The right hand is 'the elect part of the angels', the left 'the reprobate part'. For God is not shut in by right or left, who is so within all things that he is also without. But how are the wicked of the army of heaven? Because, though driven from the ethereal heaven, they still dwell in the aery heaven. Whence Paul: "Against the spirits of wickedness in the high places." The whole army stands by God, because both the will of the elect spirits serves the divine power, and the sense of the reprobate, serving its own malice, obeys the judgment of the Almighty.
22.20:
**“And the Lord said: Who shall deceive Achab king of Israel,”** — What his deserts required
**“that he may go up, and fall at Ramoth Galaad? And one spoke”** — on the left

1.2:
**“And Ochozias fell through the lattice of his upper chamber, which he had in Samaria, and was sick:”** — OCHOZIAS FELL. The house of Ochozias is the synagogue, which was surrounded on every side by the legal precepts as by the lattice of an upper chamber. But as Ochozias, falling through the lattice by which he should have been protected, incurred a grievous sickness, so the Jew too, going beyond the safeguard of the law, fell into a desperate languor of sins; where, because he forsook the help of God, he did not find the remedy of salvation. For he fled, like the impious king, to false gods, and therefore he is rebuked by the prophetic mouth and his approaching death is foretold. Ochozias signifies above all the princes of the Jews, who, given to vices, persecute the truth. Whence: "The princes and Pharisees sent ministers to apprehend Jesus" etc.
**“and he sent messengers, saying to them: Go, consult Beelzebub,”** — El in Syriac [is] 'sun'; with b added, 'bel'; hence, according to the variety of tongues, bel, bal, baal, beelzebub.
1.9: **“HE SENT TO HIM A CAPTAIN OF FIFTY”** — The captain of fifty is the confession of penance, by which the remission of sins is declared. The Jews, then, unwilling that Christ be God or the prince of penance, say to him: "Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham?" And in the future they are burnt with fire. The third captain of fifty, because, converted to the faith of the Trinity, he knew the sacrament of penance, deserved pardon.
1.10: **“And Elias answering, said to the captain of fifty: If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty. And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and the fifty that were with him.”** — who, railing, said: Man of God, come down
1.13:
**“Again he sent a third captain of fifty men,”** — this is Abdias
**“and the fifty that were with him. And when he was come, he fell upon his knees”** — because he approached humbly
1.17: **“So he died”** — or then

2.1:
**“And it came to pass, when the Lord would take up Elias into heaven by a whirlwind,”**
• BY A WHIRLWIND. The whirlwind, that is, a most violent wind, caught Elias up into the aery heaven, whence the birds of heaven [are so called], that it might suddenly set him down in a certain secret region of the earth, where he might live now in great quiet of flesh and spirit until at the end of the world he pays the debt of death. The fiery chariot by which he is said to have been caught up is the angelic powers, by whose working he was lifted up.
• The taking up of Elias signifies the Lord's ascension. Elias went up in a chariot, because a mere man needed another's help. Our Redeemer [went up] not in a chariot, because he who had made all things was borne above all things by his own power. In designation of his ascension the Lord had forerunners and witnesses, one before the law, the other under the law, that at length he himself might come who would truly pierce the heavens; who would also bestow cleanness of flesh on believers, and under whom the virtue of chastity would grow through the increase of the times. For Henoch was translated, begetting and begotten through intercourse; Elias was caught up, only begotten through intercourse; the Lord was taken up neither begetting nor begotten through intercourse.
2.9:
**“And when they were gone over, Elias said to Eliseus:”** — Christ our head to the Church his body
**“Ask what thou wilt”** — which you also shall receive
**“that I should do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Eliseus said: I beseech thee that in me may be thy double spirit.”**
• the bestowal of thy spirit
• RABANUS. Having received from the Lord confidence to ask, the Church asks for the double spirit of Christ, both because she needs the remission of sins, which Christ did not need, and the gift of the virtues, which Christ bestows from his fulness through the Holy Spirit, who "ascending on high, led captivity captive; he gave gifts to men," namely to those who put their hope in him. Hence it is that he says: If thou see me when I am taken from thee, that is, if thou open the eyes of faith and believe faithfully my ascension also, with my passion and resurrection, thou shalt obtain the effect of thy petition.
**“THAT IN ME MAY BE THY DOUBLE SPIRIT”** — Elias was eminently strong in the prophetic spirit and the working of miracles. The twofold grace, then, which Eliseus knew to flourish in his master, he asked to be given to himself. Whence it is plain that he did not ask that the disciple be above the master.
2.13: **“THE MANTLE OF ELIAS”** — RABANUS. [The mantle] is the incarnation, through which he broke through the river of death and prepared for us the passage to life. This Eliseus kept after the passing of Elias, because the Church kept the faith of the incarnation after the ascension of Christ, through which she is busy to pass over the waves of the present life. But as Eliseus divided the waters only by calling on the name of Elias, so the Church can do no works of power except through calling on the name of Christ. For it is God who worketh in us both to will and to accomplish.
2.14: **“And he struck the waters with the mantle of Elias, that had fallen from him, and they”** — or and
2.15: **“And the sons of the prophets at Jericho, who were over against him, seeing it,”** — or over against
2.19:
**“And the men of the city said to Eliseus: Behold the situation of this city”** — Jericho
**“is very good, as thou, my lord, seest:”** — or foresee
2.20: **“And he said: Bring me a new vessel, and put salt into it.”** — PUT SALT INTO IT. ISIDORE. Salt, that is, wisdom, placed in an earthen vessel, that is, the human body, heals the waters, that is, makes the peoples fruitful with the sweetness of love and good works through the incarnation of Christ.
2.21: **“And he went out to the spring of the waters, and cast the salt into it, and said:”** — "The Word was made flesh"
2.23: **“AND HE WENT UP FROM THENCE”** — ISIDORE. Eliseus, 'salvation of God'. He is the one called Saviour, whom the Jews mock, because he was to go up on the cross in the place of Calvary. But Christ, after he ascended into heaven, as Eliseus went up to Bethel, that is, to the house of God, in the forty-second year sent two bears from the woods of the gentiles, namely Vespasian and Titus, who cast them down with cruel slaughter. And their blood was shed there where [they shed that of] the Lord.

3.9: **“So the king of Israel, and the king of Juda, and the king of Edom went,”** — THE KING OF ISRAEL, THE KING OF JUDA, THE KING OF EDOM. RABANUS. The three kings warring against Moab are the rulers of the faithful, who through faith in the Trinity contend with spiritual arms against the prince of the world and [his] people, that is, philosophers, heretics, schismatics and all the wicked. Moab is interpreted 'of the father'; it fits those to whom the Lord said: "You are of your father the devil." These oppose the Church with threats, persecutions and guile, but are put to flight through Christ, who is the head of Christians.
3.16:
**“Thus saith the Lord: Make the channel of this torrent full of ditches.”**
• MAKE THE CHANNEL. RABANUS. The prophet provides for the people wearied with thirst by a miracle, and the sayings of prophecy afford counsel to the faithful how they may refresh the mind with spiritual doctrine.
• RABANUS. He makes ditches in the channel of the torrent who seeks the deep mysteries in the Scriptures. These are filled with water without rain and wind, because divine power often confers wisdom on its searchers without human help. Whence John says: "You have no need that any man teach you; but as his unction teacheth you of all things." Whence men and beasts will drink, that is, the clever and the simple will receive doctrine.
3.18: **“AND THIS IS A SMALL THING”** — RABANUS. For it does not suffice the servants of God to know hidden mysteries; they ought also to preach them to others and refute the gainsayers; to whom sure victory over the enemy is promised, that they may smite every city.
3.19:
**“EVERY FENCED CITY”** — RABANUS. The city is worldly prudence, in which philosophers and heretics trust. This is overthrown by the preachers.
**“TREE”** — RABANUS. Not that which bears fruit, but deadly [fruit], which, cut down at the coming examination, will become fuel for the eternal fire. The fountains of waters are stopped up when the heresiarchs with their followers are condemned by the catholics. 'The goodly fields are covered with stones' when the comeliness of heretical and philosophical speech is overwhelmed by the weight of anathema. Only 'the walls of clay' remain, that is, false reasonings, which are brought to nothing by the slingers, that is, the holy preachers.
**“and every choice city, and shall cut down every fruitful tree, and shall stop up all the fountains of waters, and every goodly field you shall cover with stones.”** — RABANUS. So the philosophers, thinking the word of the cross foolishness, mock the passion of Christ and think the martyrdom of the Church madness.

4.1: **“Now a certain woman of the wives of the prophets”** — A CERTAIN WOMAN. Holy Church is the mother of two peoples, that is, the Jewish and the gentile, who formerly, by consenting in perverse work to the persuasion of the crafty spirit, had received from a creditor as it were a certain coin of sin, and feared to lose the two sons whom she had begotten in faith. But obeying the words of the prophet, that is, the precepts of sacred Scripture, she poured out from the little oil she had into empty vessels; because while the empty minds of many draw a little of the love of the divinity from the mouth of one teacher, they are filled to the top by the overflowing grace of the ointments of divine love; and now the hearts of many, which before were empty vessels, are full of the ointment of the Spirit, which seemed to be poured only from a scant amount of oil. While this is given to others and others, and faith is received by the hearers, the woman, that is, holy Church, rescued, is no longer held under the debt of her creditor. The woman who received the prophet as guest suggests the origin of the Israelite people, which was in the patriarchs. Whence, as she received the prophet Eliseus as guest, so they too received the Lord of the prophets as guest. For Abraham and Sara received and fed three men.
4.16: **“And he said to her: At this time, and this same hour, if life accompany, thou shalt have a son in thy womb.”** — the Lord [said] like things to Abraham: at this time Sara shall have a son
4.18: **“And the child grew. And on a certain day, when he went out to his father to the reapers,”** — AND THE CHILD GREW. RABANUS. So the Israelite people, after it grew up in Egypt and, led out into the desert by Moses, had heard the voice of the Lord, when it ought to have been enlightened with the light of knowledge, soon, running back in mind to idolatry, died.
4.25: **“So she went, and came to the man of God to mount Carmel: and when the man of God saw her coming towards,”** — or over against
4.29: **“Then he said to Giezi: Gird up thy loins, and take my staff in thy hand, and go. If any man meet thee, salute him not: and if any man salute thee, answer him not: and lay my staff upon the face of the child.”** — THEN HE SAID TO GIEZI. RABANUS. When the Lord gave the law through Moses, he sent as it were a rod by a servant; but the servant could not raise the dead by the rod, that is, by the terror of the law, because "the law brought nothing to perfection." Coming himself in person, he stretches himself upon the body, because "being in the form of God, he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant." He walked to and fro, because he calls both Jews and gentiles to eternal things through faith. He breathes seven times upon the dead, because by opening the divine gift he breathes the grace of the sevenfold Spirit upon those lying in the death of sin. And soon the child whom the rod of terror could not raise returned to life through the spirit of love.
4.34: **“And he went up, and lay upon him,”** — the child
4.38:
**“And Eliseus returned to Galgal. Now there was a famine in the land,”** — not indeed of bread, but of hearing the word of God
**“THE SONS OF THE PROPHETS”** — That is, of the preachers, who walk in the law of the Lord and search his testimonies, [and] live always in the presence of the Saviour.
4.39:
**“And one went out into the field to gather wild herbs: and he found something like a wild vine, and gathered of it wild gourds of the field,”** — that is, wild gourds, smaller than those that grow in gardens, and very bitter
**“HE SHRED THEM INTO THE POT”** — He who, intent on the letter of the law, or studious of philosophy, taking bitterness from the law or what is deadly from the philosophers, mixes it with gospel truth and, cooking it in the pot of his heart, prepares such a pottage, that is, teaching, for his hearers. For the Apostle says: "The letter killeth." "The wisdom of the flesh is death; but the wisdom of the spirit is life." The faithful, knowing this, cry: death in the pot. But meal is put into the pot when spiritual knowledge is brought into such a seasoning, that, the bitterness being shut out, the food becomes wholesome.
4.42: **“And a certain man came from Baalsalisa, bringing to the man of God, bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and new corn in his scrip. And he said: Give to the people, that they may eat.”** — AND A CERTAIN MAN CAME FROM BAALSALISA. RABANUS. This man is the company of the fathers, who is from Baalsalisa because it keeps the number three in the confession of the Trinity; for Baalsalisa is interpreted 'having a third'. This man offers to the man of God loaves of the firstfruits when, inspired by his grace, he offers to the Redeemer the books composed on the origin of creatures. He offers new corn in his scrip when he brings forth the New Testament in the writings of the gospel and the apostles. Our Eliseus commands his ministers, that is, the preachers, to dispense these to the faithful and "bring forth out of their treasure new things and old."
