Which mystery we read in the gospel in the breaking of the five and the seven loaves, where, the crowds being filled, they gathered twelve baskets or seven hampers of fragments, because no one grasps the sacraments of Scripture in every respect, but something remains over after he is filled, according to the word of the Lord.

5.1: **“NAAMAN”** — [Naaman] signifies the gentiles, holding sovereignty by strength in war and enjoying the beauty of things. Whence Naaman is interpreted [unclear in the edition: "decus suus commotio eorum"]. A valiant man and rich but a leper, because, though he seemed to have dominion through the power of his kingdom and the abundance of his goods, yet he appeared foul with leprosy through the error of idolatry.
5.2: **“NOW THERE HAD GONE OUT ROBBERS FROM SYRIA”** — RABANUS. The robbers went out from Syria, which is 'loftiness', when the gentiles, led by greed and entangled in various business, wandered through the whole earth. These led captive from the land of Israel the girl who testified of the prophet in Israel, because the fame of Israel, carried by the merchants of the gentiles through the whole world, made known to the curiosity of men, which the wife of Naaman signifies, that a true prophet and Saviour remained in Judea. Hearing this, Naaman told his lord, when those to whom knowledge of the word has come suggest to those over them the greatness of spiritual knowledge. The king of Syria sends letters to the king of Israel for the health of his servant, when the leaders of the gentiles, hearing that God is in Israel, providing for the health of their own, send an embassy into Judea, that it may receive faith in the Saviour through the apostolic doctrine. Whence Cornelius sends from Caesarea to Joppe to Peter. The king rent his garments, because the priests, scribes and Pharisees, the rulers of the Jews, seeing the peoples coming together from every side to redemption, thinking it as it were blasphemy, rent their garments, as the prince of the priests did in the gospel. Let him come to me, and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel; and the Lord, whom he foreknew, these he also called etc. The gentile people, coming to the house of Eliseus, namely holy Church, received through the messenger, that is, the gospel preachers, [the command] to wash himself seven times in the Jordan, "born again of water and the Spirit." The Jordan signifies baptism, because in it the Saviour consecrated baptism for us. Naaman, despising the washing in the Jordan, signifies the simplicity of the unlearned, who could not understand the spiritual efficacy, because "the sensual man perceiveth not these things that are of the Spirit of God." The servants with better counsel persuaded him to the prophet's command, because the Lord often reveals to the lesser what is better, since "God is not a respecter of persons." Having washed seven times, his flesh was restored like a child's, because each one, cleansed in baptism through the invocation of the sevenfold Spirit, is brought back to the infancy of an innocent life. Because in baptism we are commanded to renounce Satan and confess the faith of the Lord, Naaman declares he will no more offer sacrifice to the gods, [but] will serve God alone in all things. He takes a portion of the holy land with him, because the baptized must be strengthened by participation in the Lord's body.
5.15: **“And returning to the man of God with all his train, he came, and stood before him, and said: In truth, I know there is no other God in all the earth, but only in Israel.”** — This is the catholic profession, since "All the gods of the Gentiles are devils: but the Lord made the heavens"
5.17: **“And Naaman said: As thou wilt: but I beseech thee, grant to me thy servant, to take of the earth the burden of two mules: for thy servant will not henceforth offer holocaust, or victim, to other gods, but to the Lord.”** — I BESEECH etc. OF THE EARTH. Naaman took a portion of the holy land with him, to place it in the temple of the idols and, standing upon it, to adore the Lord whose land it was, lest he offend his own lord if he did not adore with him.
5.20: **“GIEZI”** — RABANUS. [Giezi] is interpreted 'seeing a precipice' or 'vision of the valley'. He is Israel, who was once the servant of God; whence: "Israel was a child, and I loved him." But after, spurning the gospel, he cast himself headlong into the pit of avarice, which the sons of God reborn through baptism spurned, by just judgment he brought on himself the leprosy of error which the believers had laid aside. So all who after baptism and amendment of life return to their former ways are wrapped again in the filth which they hoped they had put off: "This is the dog returned to his vomit."

6.2: **“Let us go as far as the Jordan, and take out of the wood every man a piece of timber, that we may build us there a place to dwell in.”** — or place
6.5:
**“And it happened, as one was felling some timber,”**
• Christ would rebuke the unfruitful
• would chide the wicked
• AND IT HAPPENED, AS ONE WAS FELLING SOME TIMBER. RABANUS. When the presence of Christ, working through the body, cut down the impious Jews as unfruitful trees. Whence: "Behold the axe is laid to the root of the trees." By them, the passion intervening, [the spirit] left the body itself [and] went down to the depths; which [body], laid in the tomb, rose again, the spirit returning as it were to the handle.
• RABANUS. Great care must be taken lest the understanding grow torpid in idleness, lest in the exercise of work it vanish through the vice of elation.
**“GREGORY”** — Morally. The iron in the handle is the understanding in the heart. With this wood is cut when evildoers are rebuked; which, while it is done loosely, while the slip of vainglory is not avoided [the iron flies off]. The iron is lost in the water, because through slack work the understanding is made foolish, which is given for this, that it be restored before the eyes of the giver by good action. Whence it follows: This very thing I had borrowed. But the elect, if ever they offend, quickly return to the heart and pursue the fault with tears. Whence: Alas, alas, my lord. Weeping, they carefully look not only at the evils they have committed, but also at the good things they ought to have rendered from the gift received. And this is: Alas, alas, alas, and this I had borrowed; as if to say: That I have lost through the slackness of negligence, which I received from the grace of the Redeemer that I might render it through good works. But God never forsakes the mind that truly acknowledges itself in sins. Whence Eliseus cast the wood down and brought the iron to the surface, because the Redeemer humbles the sinner's heart and restores the understanding which it had lost. Whence in another translation it is said: that he broke the wood and threw it, and so raised the iron. To break the wood is to crush the heart from elation; to throw it down, to humble it by the thought of its own weakness. At once the iron returns, because the understanding runs back to the use of its former exercise.
**“fell”** — went down
**“the head”** — the spirit
**“of the axe”** — of the body
**“into the water:”**
• into the depth
• the understanding of the heart is lost through the slackness of negligence
6.6: **“And the man of God said: Where did it fall? and he shewed him the place. Then he cut off a piece of wood, and cast it in thither: and the iron swam.”** — the spirit returned to the flesh
6.8: **“Now the king of Syria warred against Israel,”** — Earthly power, minded proudly, persecutes the sons of light
6.9: **“The man of God therefore sent to the king of Israel,”** — by the doctrine of our Lord the snares of the enemies are guarded against
6.14: **“AND WHEN THEY WERE COME”** — RABANUS. He who, trusting in the arms of wickedness, prepares snares for the servants of Christ, blinded by the night of perfidy, wages war against the Church.
6.15: **“ALAS, ALAS, ALAS, MY LORD”** — RABANUS. By these he notes those who through faintness of heart fear bodily punishments.
6.16:
**“FEAR NOT”** — "Fear ye not them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do to you."
**“FOR THERE ARE MORE WITH US”** — RABANUS. "I can ask my Father, and he will give me presently more than twelve legions of angels."
6.17: **“And Eliseus prayed, and said: Lord, open his eyes, that he may see.”** — LORD, OPEN THE EYES. RABANUS. It is very necessary that our Eliseus open the eyes of the heart to consider that all who trust in him shall not be confounded.
6.18: **“And the enemies came down to him, but Eliseus prayed to the Lord, saying: Strike, I beseech thee, this people with blindness: and the Lord struck them with blindness, according to the word of Eliseus.”** — STRIKE, I BESEECH THEE, THIS PEOPLE WITH BLINDNESS. RABANUS. It is good that the eye that scandalizes be plucked out, that the gaze of pride and malice may be stopped up, and the eye of sound faith and simplicity opened.
6.19: **“AND HE LED THEM INTO SAMARIA”** — RABANUS. After Eliseus led the enemies into Samaria, he did not permit them to be killed, but, preparing refreshment for them, sent them away in peace. And Saul, long kicking against the goad, the Lord first blinded, then enriched with spiritual knowledge. And he commanded us thus: "Love your enemies: do good to them that hate you."
6.22: **“And he said: Thou shalt not kill them: for thou didst not take them with thy sword or bow, that thou mayest kill them: but”** — that thou mayest kill them
6.24: **“And it came to pass after these things, that Benadad king of Syria gathered together all his army, and went up, and besieged Samaria.”** — BENADAD GATHERED etc. RABANUS. Benadad and his army are the devil and the wicked, namely pagans, Jews, heretics, whom he stirs up to wage war against the Church. By such the people of God is afflicted which is set in Samaria, that is, in the keeping of the law. And there is famine when the teachers are not permitted to preach the word of God. But when Eliseus reveals it, that is, when the Redeemer shows through the gospel, the salvation which is far from sinners is known to be near to those who fear God. For the Lord says: "Tomorrow a bushel" etc. The bushel of fine flour is the perfect measure of divine wisdom, which is in the New Testament. "Two bushels of barley" are the knowledge of the law and the prophets, which are compared to one stater, that is, the catholic faith. "In the gate of Samaria," that is, in the apostolic preaching, through which one enters the Church. For when the storm of persecution which happens today ceases, the Lord will give tomorrow, that is, in the time to come, tranquillity, that preaching may be perfectly fulfilled.

7.3: **“Now there were four lepers at the entering in of the gate: and they said one to another: What mean we to stay here till we die?”** — FOUR LEPROUS MEN. RABANUS. The lepers are those who, given to various vices or entangled in errors, bringing out foulness from an inward plague, show it on the skin. These the Lord often, converting them to faith and cleansing them from vices, makes messengers of true salvation. Whence Matthew from a publican [became] an apostle. And after the resurrection he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils; "she went and told them that had been with him, who were mourning." The lepers, entering the camp of the Syrians, were refreshed and carry off gold and silver, when the despised, giving their effort to the philosophy of this world, acquire both subtlety of sense and comeliness of speech, whence, well instructed, they can serve the uses of the Church. They are well said to be four, that, steeped in the teaching of the four gospels, they may preach the truth of the faith in the four parts of the world.
7.6: **“For the Lord had made them hear in the camp of Syria, the noise of chariots, and of horses, and of a very great army: and they said one to another: Behold the king of Israel hath hired against us the kings of the Hethites,”** — or of the Getheans
7.17: **“And the king appointed that lord on whose hand he leaned to stand at the gate: and the people trod upon him in the entrance of the gate: and he died, according as the man of God had said, when the king came down to him.”** — AND THE KING [APPOINTED] THAT LORD etc. The lord holds the type of the scribes and Pharisees, to whom the Truth says: "Woe to you scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites; because you shut the kingdom of heaven against men, for you yourselves do not enter in; and those that are going in, you suffer not to enter." Whom the people trod upon in the gate, because he hindered the step of those entering into faith. Whence, deservedly trodden down, that is, condemned by the examination of the just judge, he will be cast into perpetual darkness.

8.18: **“And he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, as the house of Achab had walked: for the daughter of Achab was his wife: and he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.”** — or in the sight of the Lord

9.2: **“And when thou art come thither, thou shalt see Jehu the son of Josaphat the son of Namsi: and going in thou shalt make him rise up from among his brethren, and thou shalt carry him into an inner chamber.”** — THOU SHALT SEE JEHU. RABANUS. Jehu designates the sovereignty of the gentiles, which the Lord destined to destroy with just vengeance the sacrilegious city that killed the prophets and the Lord of the prophets and persecuted his apostles, and to destroy the priesthood which it had held in vain after Christ, and overthrow the temple, and also to cast down from the height of the kingdom the impious Synagogue, which ever thirsted for the blood of the saints, and to kill its rulers.
9.28: **“And his servants laid him upon his chariot, and carried him to Jerusalem: and they buried him in the sepulchre with his fathers in the city of David.”** — OCHOZIAS REIGNED OVER JUDA. RABANUS. It is said of Ochozias that he was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and reigned one year. For his father Joram is said to have reigned eight years and lived forty; if so, he is two years older than his father. But the Hebrews hand down that Joram lived forty years and reigned twenty-eight, of which eight are given to him, because so long he lived justly; the twenty in which he afterwards reigned in sickness and tribulation are added to his son, who was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and reigned one.

10.5: **“Therefore they that were over the house, and the rulers of the city, and the ancients, and the bringers up of the children, sent to Jehu, saying: We are thy servants: whatsoever thou shalt command us we will do, we will not make us any king: do thou all that pleaseth thee.”** — otherwise: "whatsoever pleaseth thee"
10.22: **“And he said to them that were”** — otherwise: were over
10.30: **“And the Lord said to Jehu: Because thou hast diligently executed”** — or done

11.1: **“And Athalia the mother of Ochozias seeing that her son was dead, arose and slew all the royal seed.”** — RABANUS. Athalia, who strove to extinguish the seed of David, expresses the impiety of the Synagogue, which lay in wait for the seed of David, that is, Christ. She seemed for a time to reign, when she observed the ceremonies of the law temporally; for Athalia is interpreted 'temporal of the Lord'. But by the diligence of Josaba, who is interpreted 'fulness of the Lord', that is, of the Church, in which are true delights, Joas is kept, that is, 'memory of the Lord', namely Christ, in whom is the memory of the name of the Lord, lest he be destroyed in the hearts of the elect by the cruelty of the raging enemy. Rather he is nourished in the house of Joiada, which means 'beloved of the Lord', of whom the Father [says]: "This is my beloved Son." Whose house is holy Church, where, abiding in the holy faith of the elect, he daily makes increase of his body, until at the time of judgment he lifts up the sceptre of the kingdom and power against those who thought to bring him down, and has consigned the murderess of the saints to eternal punishments.
11.4:
**“And in the seventh year Joiada sent, and taking the centurions and the soldiers, brought them in to him into the temple of the Lord,”** — AND IN THE SEVENTH YEAR etc. There were twenty-four courses of priests, Levites and porters, and they had as many high priests, who each succeeded one another in order through as many weeks, each having under him twenty-four priests and as many Levites, and porters of the same number. When, then, a new high priest entered on his office on the sabbath with a new band of priests, Levites and porters, the high priest who had ministered for the past week with his band returned home to his wife after the sabbath. For as long as they ministered they abstained from the conjugal act, remaining in the porches about the house of the Lord until the sabbath. But then the chief priest, because of the need of increasing the force, both kept back those who had completed the week and received those who were to fulfil it. He also gathered other Levites from the cities and the heads of families, whom, being about to bring out the king's son, he arranged in such a manner that those who had completed the sabbath stood armed about the king in the inner places of the court; those who had come for the sabbath guarded the king's house, that is, the palace, and the gate of the shieldbearers, by which one went down from the temple to the palace; the rest of the multitude guarded the outer gates of the courts against the fury of the queen, if she attempted anything. Afterwards he brought the king out of the house of the Lord, where he had been hidden, and they came by the way of the gate of the shieldbearers into the palace, and he sat upon the throne of the kings.
**“and made a covenant with them:”** — that is, he made a compact with the chiefs of the Levites
11.6:
**“AT THE GATE OF SUR”** — RABANUS. The gate of Sur and the house of Messa, which are named with the gate of the shieldbearers, seem to be in the palace.
**“and let a third part be at the gate behind the dwelling of the shieldbearers: and you shall keep the watch of the house of Messa.”** — RABANUS. which is called the gate of the shieldbearers and the foundation
**“OF THE SHIELDBEARERS”** — RABANUS. The shieldbearers were the king's guards, keeping the vestibule of the palace.
11.10:
**“And he gave them”** — the Levites
**“the spears, and the arms of king David, which were in the house of the Lord.”** — which David, having slain his enemies, consecrated in the house of the Lord, with which the Levites might be armed in war
11.12:
**“And he brought forth the king's son, and put upon him the diadem,”** — the head ornament of kings
**“AND PUT UPON HIM THE DIADEM”** — RABANUS. In the book of the Days more plainly: "And they put upon him the diadem, and gave into his hand the law to hold." And it was indeed of wholesome prudence that, after the slaying of the tyrannical queen, to the king's son succeeding to the kingdom the discipline of God's law should be committed to be kept together with the very dress of royalty, and that he who saw himself set over the people to rule them should remember that he himself ought to be subject to the divine laws to be ruled.
**“and the testimony:”** — the law of God, by which he may be taught how to live and what to do
11.14: **“She saw the king standing upon a tribunal, as the manner was, and the singers, and the trumpets near”** — near
11.17:
**“And Joiada made a covenant between the Lord, and the king, and the people, that they should be the people of the Lord, and between the king and the people.”**
• JOIADA MADE A COVENANT BETWEEN THE LORD AND THE KING etc. In Paralipomenon: "between himself," because he set himself in the place of the king and of God, whose minister he was. Whence Joiada is interpreted 'recognizing the Lord' or 'loving', because he taught to know and love the Lord.
• He made a covenant between the Lord and the king and the people, that the king and the people should serve the Lord; he made [one] between the king and the people, that the people should deal faithfully toward the king, and the king rule the people with justice.

12.4:
**“And Joas said to the priests: All the money of the sanctified things, which is brought into the temple of the Lord by those that pass, which is offered for the price of a soul,”**
• Whence in Exodus: "When thou takest the sum of the children of Israel, every one of them shall give a price for their souls, and there shall be no scourge" for the price of a soul.
• AND JOAS SAID TO THE PRIESTS: ALL THE MONEY. Our king commands that the teachers receive all the money of spiritual knowledge or good examples which is brought by the just passing by into the treasury of the Lord, [and that it] be applied through the offices of the preachers to the restoring of the spiritual temple, so that they may repair there whatever they find torn by error or vices, lest perhaps the multitude of hearers perish through the negligence of the masters.
12.5:
**“Let the priests take it”** — the preachers
**“THE REPAIRS”** — RABANUS. He means the ruins of the house of the Lord, that what had begun to fall might be propped up. For it is read in Paralipomenon that Athalia and her sons, that is, the priests of the idols (because she is read not to have had a son), destroyed the house of the Lord and made Baal of the sanctified things.
12.6: **“NOW UNTIL THE TWENTIETH”** — RABANUS. Before the coming of Christ, though the teaching of the law was in the Jewish nation, yet it was corrupted in many things through the negligence of the teachers, until he should come who gave the law and should teach that the decalogue in the writings of Moses and the prophets is to be observed spiritually through faith in the holy Trinity.
12.7: **“GIVE IT FOR THE REPAIRING OF THE TEMPLE”** — RABANUS. The Lord says to the gospel teachers: "Preach the gospel to every creature," "heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers; freely have you received, freely give."
12.9:
**“AND JOIADA TOOK A CHEST”** — RABANUS. Our high priest, who offered himself a victim to God, set one chest, that is, he made one catholic Church, for which he opened a hole above, because from it he prepared a passage to heaven.
**“AND SET IT BESIDE THE ALTAR”** — RABANUS. The altar is the body of the Lord, beside which is the chest, when the Church is joined to Christ, on the right hand of those entering the house. Because those who enter the Church through faith aim to come to eternal beatitude, which the right hand signifies. Thither, then, the priests who keep the doors of the temple put all the money that is brought to the temple, when the preachers who keep the entrance of faith offer the vows of the faithful in words and works and duly commend them to God with prayers in the Church.
12.10:
**“THE KING'S SCRIBE, AND THE HIGH PRIEST”** — RABANUS. The chief ones are the teachers who gave the money collected, according to number and measure, to those who were over the carpenters and masons, that is, to the dispensers of the word of God, who gave the measure of gospel wheat to their fellow servants, to those who work in the house of the Lord and put together the works of the virtues in the divine building.
**“And when they saw that there was very much money in the chest, the king's scribe, and the high priest came up, and poured it out, and they counted the money that was found in the house of the Lord:”** — RABANUS. The apostles, whom divine election set as princes in the Church, scattered the seeds of the word through the whole world by their disciples, so that they might set over their hearers workmen fit for the will of God; of whom some wrought wood, when they strove to prepare themselves and those obedient to them as fruitful trees in the house of the Lord; others made the repairs of the temple, when they rebuilt what had been broken by heresy and schisms; others cut stones, when they strongly rebuked the hard of heart and unbelieving; so that the restoration was fulfilled in all things that needed expense for strengthening the house of the Lord, according to that: "But to every one of us is given grace, according to the measure of the giving of Christ."
12.13:
**“But yet there were not made of the same money for the temple of the Lord water pots”**
• containing the water of divine wisdom
• BUT YET THERE WERE NOT MADE etc. RABANUS. The method of forming vessels for the ministry of the Lord must be one thing, that of preparing wood and stones for the building of the house another; because the teaching by which the unlearned are steeped in faith must be one thing, and that by which those already perfect are instructed to the fulness of knowledge another. The vessels of the Lord are those who are already fit to receive the divine gifts and are apt for the ministry of God.
• There were not made of the same money water pots etc. In Paralipomenon: "And when they had finished all the work, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Joiada, and of it were made vessels for the temple." It is not contrary, because the vessels for the ministry of the temple were not made of the same money that was offered by the people for the repair of the house of the Lord, but of the remaining part of the money, which had been gathered also from other gifts.
**“FLESHHOOKS”** — RABANUS. [The fleshhooks are] the teachers, whose office is to distribute the body and blood of the Lord to believers, to deny it to unbelievers, and also to apportion the spiritual food of the word to each as is fitting; because there are things in the words of God which he has deigned to reveal to our lowliness, [and] there are others which transcend the measure of our capacity.
**“CENSERS”** — RABANUS. [The censers] are those who offer pure prayer to God from a pure conscience and faith unfeigned, and say: "Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight."
**“TRUMPETS”** — RABANUS. [The trumpets are] the teachers who send forth through the whole world the voice of gospel preaching. Whence: "Lift up thy voice like a trumpet."
12.15: **“AND THEY RECKONED NOT”** — RABANUS. They were so religious that no one doubted that they handled God's money without fraud. Whence it is clear how great discretion is needed by those who dispense to their fellow servants the money of the word of God, of which account must be rendered, that these may be found no less faithful in spiritual things than those in bodily.
12.16:
**“But the money for trespass, and the money for sins,”** — whence in Exodus: "When thou takest the sum of the children of Israel, every one of them shall give a price for their souls, and there shall be no scourge"
**“BUT THE MONEY FOR TRESPASS”** — RABANUS. Here it is shown that the confession of sins and penance is to be carried out not by each one's own judgment but by that of the priests, whose it is to discern between clean and unclean and to judge the spot of leprosy.

13.14: **“Now Eliseus was sick of the illness whereof he died:”** — NOW ELISEUS WAS SICK. RABANUS. Our Redeemer commands the rulers of the Church to put on spiritual arms and fight against the ancient enemy. The bow is the sacred word, which consists of both Testaments as of horn and string. The Old is the horn on account of its hardness, the New the string; and while the string is drawn the horn is bent, because when the New Testament is discussed the Old is bent from its rigour to spiritual understanding. The arrows are the words which the teachers bring forth. We, then, bend the bow when we weigh the sayings of sacred Scripture; we send forth arrows when we give words of doctrine.
13.16: **“ELISEUS PUT HIS HANDS”** — RABANUS. By his examples the Lord directs and strengthens the actions of teachers.
13.17:
**“And he said: Open the window to the east. And when he had opened it, Eliseus said: Shoot an arrow.”** — OPEN THE WINDOW TO THE EAST etc. RABANUS. He exhorts his own first to be enlightened with the light of knowledge, and so to send the darts of words.
**“And he shot. And Eliseus said: The arrow of the Lord's deliverance, and the arrow of deliverance”** — RABANUS. holy preaching
**“from Syria: and thou shalt strike the Syrians in Aphec,”**
• that is, in holding or seizing
• THE ARROW OF DELIVERANCE etc. RABANUS. Holy preaching is the surest slaying of spiritual enemies if it is carried on perseveringly. Whence the teacher ought not through avarice to neglect the care of souls, but rather through piety to press on to the eternal rest which Aphec signifies; for it is interpreted 'will hold' or 'will seize'. Whence the Apostle, having enumerated the vices, added: "But thou, O man of God, fly these things: and pursue justice, godliness," lay hold on eternal life.
13.18: **“TAKE THE ARROWS”** — AND WHEN HE HAD TAKEN THEM, HE SAID TO HIM AGAIN: STRIKE etc. RABANUS. The teachers are commanded to strike the earth, that is, the carnal, with the dart of preaching. To strike the earth three times with the dart is to instil the faith of the Trinity into the carnal by teaching. Afterwards let them be taught to command the five bodily senses and to spend their zeal on good works, which are expressed by six, and also to meditate earnestly on the spiritual knowledge which the sevenfold Spirit put forth in the twin Testament for the salvation of the human race. But those who believe that faith alone suffices for salvation are rightly reproved, because, according to James: "Faith without works is dead."
13.21:
**“AND WHEN IT HAD TOUCHED”** — RABANUS. The rising of the body through touching the bones of Eliseus signifies that whoever with firm faith touches the death of Christ and truly places his hope in him will without doubt be a partaker of his resurrection. Whence: "I am the resurrection and the life."
**“And some that were burying a man, saw the rovers, and cast the body into the sepulchre of Eliseus. And when it had touched the bones of Eliseus, the man came to life, and stood upon his feet.”**
• "After the death of Joiada, the princes of Juda went in, and worshipped the king" etc. The Jews say that the king was worshipped as God and gladly accepted from his subjects honours beyond human measure. Whence he suddenly experienced the wrath of God, like Herod.
• There is no God in Israel, because all were guilty and polluted with idolatry. See that these two glosses are taken over from the twenty-fourth [chapter] of Second Paralipomenon, and have their place there rather than here.

14.3: **“AND HE DID THAT WHICH WAS RIGHT BEFORE THE LORD”** — RABANUS. Amasias did good in the sight of the Lord, but not with a perfect heart. For he did the good works which please God, but not with a perfect heart, because he showed them under a feigned appearance before men, and so they were not acceptable before God.
14.6: **“But the children of them that were murderers he did not put to death, according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moses, wherein the Lord commanded, saying: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers:”** — in most [copies] it is wanting
14.7:
**“He”** — Amasias
**“slew of Edom in the valley of the Saltpits”** — the old edition put 'Gemela' as if the name of a region
**“IN THE VALLEY OF THE SALTPITS”** — RABANUS. The valley of the Saltpits was where they made salt: either from salt hay cut, dried and burnt; or from the salt waters of wells boiled and brought by cooking to the firmness of salt; or by any other method by which salt is wont to be made.
**“THE ROCK IN BATTLE”** — RABANUS. Petra is a noble city of Arabia in the land of Edom, which in the book of Numbers is called Recem, and is so named by the Syrians. But Josephus calls it not a city but a great rock set in Arabia.
**“JECTEHEL”** — [Jectehel,] the name Amasias as victor gave it, is interpreted 'assembly of God' or 'help of God', he acting faithfully, that it might seem of everlasting memory that either the assembly of the people of God, or he with God's help, took it.
14.25:
**“He restored the borders of Israel from the entrance of Emath, unto the sea of the wilderness,”** — HE RESTORED THE BORDERS OF ISRAEL FROM THE ENTRANCE. RABANUS. It is said of Jeroboam: He restored the borders of Israel from the entrance of Emath unto the sea of the wilderness. Emath, which is now called Epiphania, was the northern border of Israel. And the sea of the wilderness is the Dead Sea, which extends in breadth five hundred and eighty stadia as far as Zoara of Arabia, in length one hundred and fifty as far as the neighbourhood of Sodom. Jeroboam, then, encamping against the Syrians, laid waste all their province, as Jonas had prophesied.
**“according to the word of the Lord the God of Israel, which he spoke by his servant Jonas the son of Amathi, the prophet, who was of Geth, which is in Opher.”** — or Ophal
**“WHICH IS IN OPHER”** — Ophel was a tower not far from the temple, of enormous size and height. Whence it is called Ophel, that is, 'of darkness' or 'of the clouds', because it lifts its head to the clouds; which in Zacharias is called 'the cloudy tower'.
14.26: **“For the Lord saw the affliction of Israel that it was exceeding bitter, and that they were consumed even to them that were shut up in prison,”** — or of the prison

15.1: **“AZARIAS”** — RABANUS. He is Ozias, who, when he wished to sacrifice in the temple against the law of Moses, was struck with leprosy. He signifies the devil, to whom the leprosy of iniquity is incurable; who, when he sought things greater than himself, being made notable by the foulness of the worst leprosy, was cast out of the house, and remains a leper to the end, separated from the people of God. While he reigned, Isaias the prophet did not lift his eyes to heaven; the heavenly things were not unbarred to him, except after he died. While Pharao lived, the people of Israel did not sigh to God out of the work of clay and straw; but after Pharao's death their cry went up to the Lord. If, then, you understand contrary powers in Ozias and Pharao, you will see how, while they live, none of ours sees and sighs. While sin reigns, we build cities for the Egyptians, we are busied in filth. Ozias built the gate of the valley, which above is called the gate of Ephraim.
15.5: **“And the Lord struck the king, so that he was a leper unto the day of his death, and he dwelt in a free house apart: and Joatham the king's son”** — of Azarias
15.35: **“But the high places he took not away: the people still sacrificed, and burnt incense in the high places: he built the highest gate of the house of the Lord.”** — HE BUILT. RABANUS. Joatham built the high gate of the house of the Lord, which in the Acts of the Apostles is called the Beautiful, and by the Hebrews is called 'the gate of Joatham'.

16.3:
**“But he walked in the way of the kings of Israel: moreover he consecrated also his son,”** — as a holocaust
**“making him pass through the fire,”** — in the valley of Beennom; this is the valley of the son of Ennom
**“HE CONSECRATED, MAKING HIM PASS THROUGH THE FIRE”** — RABANUS. Beennom, 'of the son of Ennom'. Topheth or Thaphet is in the valley of Beennom near Haceldama, a place once most pleasant, where they used to sacrifice to demons. In Hebrew Gehennom, that is, 'valley of Ennom', whence in the gospel it is called 'gehenna'; because as those who worshipped idols perished there in body and soul, so sinners who pass to hell will be punished with eternal damnation.
16.18:
**“The Musach also for the sabbath, which he had built in the temple: and the king's entry from without he turned into the temple of the Lord,”** — not for the sake of religion but of light
**“because of the king of the Assyrians.”**
• THE MUSACH OF THE SABBATH. RABANUS. It is a building placed in the vestibule of the temple, where kings, when they went to the temple on the sabbath, put in alms. And so the Musach of the sabbath is the treasury of the kings, as the corbona is of the priests.
• MUSACH etc. AND THE KING'S ENTRY FROM WITHOUT. RABANUS. He did not turn it into the temple of the Lord in order that it might serve the worship of God in it, but that it might be profaned with the temple, he being eager to please the king of the Assyrians rather than God, so that when he came there, seeing it, he might covet it and carry it off, as many other things, Achaz giving them to him, by which he might find his favour.

17.9:
**“And the children of Israel offended”** — otherwise: provoked
**“the Lord their God with things that were not right: and built them high places in all their cities from the tower of the watchmen”** — that is, from the fort to the city
17.13: **“And the Lord testified”** — He warned thus, as in the second to Timothy: "I charge thee, before God."
17.15:
**“And they rejected his ordinances, and the covenant that he made with their fathers, and the testimonies”**
• that is, by the law
• or the testimony
**“which”** — or by which
17.18: **“And the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them from his sight, and there remained only the tribe of Juda.”** — or the kingdom of Juda, as Benjamin and Levi too were commonly called
17.24: **“And the king of the Assyrians brought”** — AND THE KING OF THE ASSYRIANS BROUGHT. RABANUS. The Assyrian king, that is, the devil, with his army daily afflicts the ecclesiastical people by besieging and laying it waste, when, tearing them from their own seats for sins committed, he carries them into a strange land. Whence: "Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and wept: when we remembered Sion."
17.29:
**“And every nation made gods of their own,”**
• AND EVERY NATION MADE. RABANUS. In the book of places it is read that Benoth and Nerguel were cities which those who had passed over from Babylonia built in Judea. Asuna too was a town built by those who had come to it from Emath. Nebaam and Tharcha are cities which the Hevites founded in Judea.
• RABANUS. It seems, according to the sequence of the discourse, that the names here can also be understood of the idols which these nations had formerly served; because when it had been said, And every nation made gods of their own, it is added as if to complete the sentence: For the men of Babylon made Socoth Benoth, that is, the tabernacles of Benoth, which is the name of an idol. In what follows Adramelech and Anamelech are shown to have been idols of the city of Sepharvaim. So it seems to follow that Nergel of the Cutheans, Asuna of the Emathites, Nebaath and Tharcha were idols of the Hevites.
17.31: **“And the Hevites made Nebahaz”** — or Nebaan
17.33: **“AND WHEREAS THEY WORSHIPPED THE LORD, THEY SERVED ALSO THEIR OWN GODS”** — The heretics have certain sacraments in common with holy Church, and understand rightly certain sentences of the Scriptures, but yet they serve the idols of unclean spirits. It seems to them that they rightly keep the fear of God when they think they favour the truth according to their own sense. But because they spurn the unity of the catholic faith, they obey the wills of evil spirits. And not only the first inventors of errors, whom the fathers of the Samaritans signify, do this, but also their followers, whom we understand by the name of sons and grandsons.

18.1: **“In the third year of Osee the son of Ela king of Israel, reigned Ezechias the son of Achaz king of Juda.”** — EZECHIAS: 'laying hold of the Lord' or 'strength of the Lord'. For our Redeemer, the Lord strong, the Lord mighty in battle, not only crushed the idols of the gentiles and scattered the worship of idolatry, so that they might have the knowledge of one God and be worthily given over to his worship, but also crushed the very letter of the law of Moses, which that legal people sounded forth in assiduous reading and held as a great thing, and taught them to understand the spiritual sense in it.
18.4:
**“He destroyed the high places, and broke the statues in pieces, and cut down the groves, and broke the brazen serpent, which Moses had made: for till that time the children of Israel burnt incense to it: and he called its name”** — otherwise: its name
**“AND HE BROKE THE BRAZEN SERPENT”** — Ezechias broke the serpent because he hoped in the Lord God, not in a brazen serpent. He called it Nohestan, which is interpreted 'their brass', that they might acknowledge from his words that what they worshipped as a divinity was metal, not God.
**“Nohestan”** — that is, their brass, not God
18.5: **“He trusted in the Lord the God of Israel:”** — not in the serpent
18.8: **“He smote the Philistines as far as Gaza, and all their borders, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city.”** — or: walled
18.17: **“RABSACES”** — RABANUS. Because he speaks in Hebrew, they think he was a son of Isaias who was a traitor with Sobna, or a Samaritan, and therefore knew the Hebrew tongue. Who, as a kind of contrary power, imitated the prophets in his arrogance. The prophets say: Thus saith the Lord. He said: Thus saith the great king, the king of the Assyrians.
18.18:
**“And they called for the king: and there went out to them Eliacim the son of Helcias, who was over the house,”** — that is, the high priest
**“ELIACIM”** — RABANUS. Of this Eliacim Isaias said: "I will call my servant Eliacim." He was high priest after Sobna, who, the Hebrews hand down, terrified by the threats of Rabsaces, betrayed Jerusalem, and the Assyrians took the whole city except the citadel and likewise the temple; [and] some suppose that Sobna too went out with Eliacim to Rabsaces.
18.21: **“Dost thou trust in Egypt, a staff of a broken reed, upon which if a man lean, it will break and go into his hand, and pierce it? so is Pharao king of Egypt, to all that trust in him.”** — DOST THOU TRUST IN etc. No history relates that Ezechias asked for Pharao's help.
18.22: **“IN THE LORD OUR GOD”** — RABANUS. It is true that they had confidence in God, but it is false [to charge] that Ezechias took away the high places and altars of God; for this he did not against God but for God, that, the old error being destroyed, he might command God to be adored in the temple of Jerusalem.
18.23: **“I WILL GIVE YOU TWO THOUSAND”** — RABANUS. Rabsaces, to show the fewness of the besieged, promises two thousand horses, for which Ezechias would not have riders; [this] came not from weakness of the people, as if they did not know how to ride, but because God commanded that the king of Israel should not multiply horses and wives to himself.
18.25: **“THE LORD SAID TO ME”** — RABANUS. To what he had said, If you say: We trust in God, he craftily answers that he has come not by his own will but by that of God, saying: Go up. And the argument is: since I have taken many cities and part of Jerusalem remains untouched, it is manifest that I have come by the will of God.
18.26: **“WE PRAY THEE TO SPEAK”** — RABANUS. The sense is: What need is there for the people to be stirred by false terrors and to boast a vain strength? Speak a tongue which the people do not know. To which he arrogantly [replies]: Hath my master sent me to thy master and to thee? etc., up to: that they may eat their own dung. By which he shows that they are to be taken by hunger and thirst. And at the same time he joins enticement to fear, that those whom he did not conquer by terror he might deceive by persuasion. And he says in the person of the king: Make with me a blessing, that is, do what may turn to your blessing. Bless the Assyrian king and confess him lord, that you may obtain rewards, until I return from Egypt, or, Lobna being taken, I come back. Dwell in your city and enjoy your goods, and afterwards I will lead you into a land like your land. Which yet he did not name, because he could not find one like it, but puts a likeness. For each one wants only that in which he was born. Others think the land of Media is promised them, which has a likeness to the land of Judea both in situation and in fruits.
18.29: **“LET NOT EZECHIAS DECEIVE YOU”** — The accusation of Rabsaces is a testimony to Ezechias, that when the cities were taken he trusted in the Lord and strengthened the people to hope in the Lord. Whence Rabsaces wants to destroy what he built, and says to the people: Let not Ezechias deceive you, and let him not give you confidence in the Lord your God.
18.33: **“Have any of the gods of the nations delivered their land from the hand of the king of Assyria?”** — If we have conquered with so many gods present, how much more easily shall we conquer Jerusalem alone, with one god as its protector
18.34: **“Where is the god of Emath, and of Arphad? where is the god of Sepharvaim, of Ana, and of Ava? have they delivered Samaria out of my hand?”** — WHERE IS THE GOD OF EMATH etc. RABANUS. He shows that the Samaritans had served the gods of these cities or nations, and because they were not gods but idols, he said that the worshippers of vanity had been deservedly overthrown. Emath is a city of Coele-Syria, which is now called Epiphania; Arphad a city of Damascus. Sepharvaim, which in the plural number means 'books' or 'letters', is the name of the places from which the Assyrians migrated into Samaria, as we find in the books of places. The true name of the city is in Isaias, saying: "Where is the god of the city of Sepharvaim?", said in the plural like 'Thebae'. For Ana and Ava the old edition put Anerigaven as if the name of one city. And indeed it is so written in the Hebrew. But what is in the middle also signifies a conjunction; it can therefore be divided so as to say Ane and Gave according to Aquila, or Ana and Gava as our interpreter has turned it.
18.36:
**“But the people held their peace,”** — Lest he provoke him to greater blasphemies
**“and answered him not a word:”** — all acting with counsel
18.37: **“And Eliacim the son of Helcias, who was over the house, and Sobna the scribe, and Joahe the son of Asaph the recorder, came to Ezechias, with their garments rent,”** — because of the blasphemy of Rabsaces

19.1:
**“And when king Ezechias heard it, he rent his garments,”** — because he believed it was for the sins of the people and his own that Rabsaces had spoken such things against the Lord
**“AND WHEN HE HEARD IT”** — RABANUS. Wonderful the humility and prudence of the king. Laying aside royal dress and wrapped in sackcloth, he goes from the palace to the temple. He sends the chiefs of the priests, clothed not in stoles but in haircloth, to Isaias, and says: "This day is a day of tribulation, and of rebuke, and of blasphemy." And he puts the likeness of a woman in labour who has come to the birth and cannot bring forth. The Lord thy God: for we do not dare to say the Lord our God, at whose anger we suffer such things. And we have this confidence of vengeance, that the living God is blasphemed by a worshipper of dead idols. Lift up, then, our prayer that lies low, for the remnant of the people which is besieged. Isaias anticipates them, because by the spirit by which he knew the future he had also heard the absent king: Thus, he says, shall you say to your master: Thus saith the Lord: Be not afraid of the words by which not thou but I have been blasphemed. Nor will I tell all that I will do to the Assyrian king, but that there is to be given him a spirit, not of God but of the adversary, and having heard a message, returning to his own land, he will fall by the sword; so that Ezechias heard both things he desired at once: namely, that he was to be freed from the siege, and that the enemy was to die in his own land.
19.9: **“And when he heard say of Tharaca king of Ethiopia:”** — AND WHEN HE HEARD etc. RABANUS. God willing it, Rabsaces left the siege of Jerusalem and found his master, Lachis either taken or abandoned, attacking Lobna. Sennacherib, going to meet the king of the Ethiopians, sent letters to Ezechias, that those whom he had not taken by force he might terrify by words. That Sennacherib fought against the Egyptians and besieged Pelusium, and, the mounds being already raised and the city about to be taken, Tharaca king of the Ethiopians came to its help, Herodotus relates.
19.14: **“HE WENT UP TO THE HOUSE OF THE LORD”** — RABANUS. Before, Ezechias, struck with terror of the Lord, did not dare to adore in the temple or pour out free prayers there; now, Isaias saying, "Be not afraid of the words which thou hast heard," he boldly entreats the Lord.
19.21: **“THE VIRGIN DAUGHTER”** — RABANUS. Because, while all nations adore idols, she alone keeps the chastity of the religion of the one God; and she, lest she stir him up to greater blasphemy, did not answer him when present, [but] after he went away shook her head, to beseech God, or surely to deride his arrogance, certain of vengeance. Nor did he blaspheme the Lord by himself, but by his servants, that the arrogance might be greater.
19.23:
**“By thy servants thou hast reproached the Lord, and hast said: With the multitude of my chariots I have gone up to the heights of the mountains, to the top of Libanus,”** — Jerusalem
**“THE HEIGHTS OF THE MOUNTAINS”** — RABANUS. The height of the mountains and the ridges of Libanus, the tall cedars and fir trees. Either it is to be taken by metaphor of all nations and their princes, or of Jerusalem, which is Libanus, the cedars and fir trees [being] the mighty and the nobles.
**“and have cut down its tall cedars, and its choice fir trees. And I have entered into the utmost parts thereof, and the forest of its Carmel”** — The height of the top and the forest of Carmel is the temple
19.24:
**“I have cut down. And I have drunk strange waters, and have dried up with the soles of my feet all the shut up waters.”** — or I dug and drank water, and dried up with the sole of my foot all the streams of the banks
**“AND HAVE DRIED UP”** — RABANUS. Either through the multitude of his army he dried up all the streams, so that he was compelled to dig wells for himself; or all the people, whom the waters signify, are laid waste by his army.
19.25:
**“Hast thou not heard”** — RABANUS. The Lord's answer against the words of the Assyrian
**“HAST THOU NOT HEARD”** — RABANUS. These things are to be understood in the person of the Lord against the blasphemy of the Assyrian. You are not ignorant that what you have done was done by my will, and these things I foretold as to come and commanded to be done by you. So what I decreed of old has been fulfilled in time, that the hills and princes who fought among themselves before, and the most fortified cities, I drawing back my hand and not affording the wonted help, should be rooted out and tremble and perish, and be compared not to olives and vines and fruitful trees, but to hay and grass, which are hindrances to crops, and to the herbs of the housetops, which wither before they come to maturity. So I knew beforehand your sitting, and your going out and your coming in, and the madness with which you were to rage against me I spoke of through the prophets prophesying; through whom I had known of old that you would say: "I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God, I will be like the most High." So your fury and pride has come to my ears, and I will by no means bear you any longer, that you may understand that what you could do, you could not by your own strength, but by my decision. For the impious nations and unfruitful trees deserved to be cut down and fall by you as by my axe and saw. So I will put a ring in your nostrils and bind the blaspheming mouth, that you may never dare to speak such things again. "And a bit I will put between thy lips," to tame your ferocity and lead you back to the Assyrians.
**“what I have done from the beginning?”** — or of old
**“From the days of old”** — RABANUS. or I
**“I have formed it, and now I have brought it to effect: and fenced cities of fighters shall be”**
• What is rooted out is overthrown from the foundation.
• RABANUS. Or uprooting
19.26:
**“And the inhabitants of them of small strength”** — that is, shrunken and without strength
**“trembled,”** — before thy face
**“and were confounded:”** — perished by the sword
**“they became like the grass of the field,”** — RABANUS. They are compared to useless things
**“and the green herb on the tops of houses, which withered before it came to maturity.”** — RABANUS. They wither before they ripen
19.27: **“Thy dwelling”** — RABANUS. Thy dwelling and all that thou hast done I foreknew
19.28: **“Thou hast been mad against me, and thy pride hath come up to my ears:”** — RABANUS. As if to say: I will bear thee no longer blaspheming
19.29:
**“And to thee, Ezechias, this shall be a sign:”** — THIS SHALL BE A SIGN. RABANUS. Of the things I foretell: that this year you shall eat the things that spring of themselves; or, according to the Seventy, "what you sowed before". In the second year, according to Symmachus, "feed on fruits"; or, according to the same, the things that have sprung up from the past crops and those that fell to the ground. In the third year, the Assyrian now put to flight and the siege now lifted, sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit. For the remnant of this small city, which is now walled in by the enemy army and does not believe it will escape, will receive such abundance of all things and happiness that, like a tree founded with deep root, they will be filled with the thickest fruits. For out of Jerusalem the remnant will go forth and fill the land of Judea, emptied of inhabitants, not by their own merit but by the mercy of God, indeed by the zeal with which he was zealous for his people against the impious.
**“Eat this year the things”**
• or the things
• EAT THIS YEAR etc. Isaias thus: "Eat this year the things that spring of themselves, and in the second year eat fruits: but in the third year sow and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat the fruit of them. And that which shall be saved of the house of Juda, and that which is left, shall take root downward, and shall bear fruit upward: for out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and salvation from mount Sion: the zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this."
• All things being laid waste by the army, eat what could spring up again, or what could escape between the hoofs of the horses; in the second year, what springs of itself without labour. Or this was said by way of a figure [so the edition: 'simulatione'], because they thought they would perish of hunger.
19.30:
**“And whatsoever shall be left”** — RABANUS. or saved
**“of the house of Juda”** — RABANUS. Understand: in the fields and seeds
19.34: **“AND FOR DAVID”** — RABANUS. By hope of things to come he shakes off present fear. And he says that they are preserved not by their own merit but by God's clemency, and indeed by the memory of their father David, in which they are reminded both of their own negligence and of his faith and justice; because God so loves justice that he protects the descendants for the virtue of their forefathers.
19.35: **“AND IT CAME TO PASS THAT NIGHT”** — RABANUS. So many are slain by one angel in one night, and fierce death runs through without wounds. Concerning which it is read in Paralipomenon: "And the Lord sent an angel, who cut off all the stout men and the warriors, and the captain of the army of the king of the Assyrians: and he returned with shame into his own country." He was preserved to become a witness of the majesty of him whom a little before he had despised.
19.36: **“And Sennacherib king of the Assyrians returned, and abode in Ninive.”** — the first city of his kingdom
19.37:
**“AND AS HE WAS WORSHIPPING”** — RABANUS. As though bringing back victory over his enemies, the despiser of the true God is slaughtered in the shrine of a false divinity; nor does he perish by the angelic sword, which was common, but by the parricide of his sons.
**“And as he was worshipping in the temple of Nesroch his god,”** — RABANUS. Pharao too is kept through the ten plagues of Egypt, that he may perish last.
**“Adramelech and Sarasar his sons slew him with the sword, and they fled into the land of the Armenians,”** — RABANUS. Ararat
**“INTO THE LAND OF THE ARMENIANS”** — Ararat is a level region in Armenia, through which the Araxes flows, of incredible fertility, at the roots of mount Taurus. So the ark of Noe was not brought to the mountains of Armenia generally, but to the highest mountains of Taurus, which overhang the plains of Ararat.
**“and Asarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.”** — who sent inhabitants to Samaria, lest the lands should remain untilled.

20.1:
**“In those days Ezechias was sick unto death: and Isaias the son of Amos the prophet came and said to him: Thus saith the Lord God: Give charge concerning thy house, for thou shalt die, and not live.”**
• IN THOSE DAYS EZECHIAS WAS SICK etc. RABANUS. Lest the heart of Ezechias be lifted up after incredible triumphs, he is visited with bodily sickness; he hears that he is to die, that, turned to the Lord, he may bend the sentence.
• RABANUS. God, foreknowing all things to come, decreed before the ages how they should be disposed through the ages. It is therefore fixed how long one lives temporally in this mortal life itself. For although God added fifteen years to Ezechias, yet when he permitted him to die, he then foreknew that he would die. When the sentence of death was spoken to him, life was at once added at his tears. At that time indeed he deserved to die, who, puffed up, did not render thanks to the Lord for the unhoped-for victory, namely because he attributed it to his own justice and merits. Nor was the time of life fixed in the presence of God prolonged, but what he had lost by sinning was restored by God's bounty. He who foretold that he would die foreknew his penance before. He turned his face to the wall of the temple, because he could not go to the temple. He means the wall of the temple, beside which the palace was; or to the wall absolutely, lest he display his tears to the bystanders, that he might entreat God with his whole mind.
20.2: **“And he turned his face to the wall, and prayed to the Lord, saying:”** — AND HE TURNED HIS FACE etc. RABANUS. Happy the conscience that in the time of affliction remembers its good works, as it is written elsewhere: "Who can say: My heart is clean?" But he speaks of perfection of heart in that he destroyed the idols, opened the doors of the temple, broke the brazen serpent, and did the other things that Scripture records. Often the just are compelled by some necessity to declare their own works, which when the unjust hear, they think it pride; for they weigh the sayings of the just from their own hearts. As it is a grave fault for a man to claim for himself what is not, so it is no fault if he humbly tells what is good. Whence it happens that the just and the unjust have like words, and by the same words by which the Lord is offended by these, by those he is appeased. Behold, the Pharisee justifies himself in work, Ezechias even in thought. Whence the one offended, thence the other appeased God, whose confession of perfection the Lord did not despise, whom he soon heard in his prayers. For God weighs the words of each from their heart.
20.3: **“AND EZECHIAS WEPT”** — RABANUS. He wept on account of the Lord's promise to David, which he saw would perish at his death, because Ezechias did not yet have a son. For after his death Manasses began to reign when he was twelve years old. From which it is clear that Manasses was begotten after the third year of the life granted. Others bring forward that holy men, though [just], are terrified at death on account of ignorance of the sentence of God, [as to] what seat they are to have. After death at the same time the question of fate is solved, and the bonds of necessity and of causes, because the day of death is by no means fixed beforehand for each, but by the will of God and for causes unknown to mortals one either lives or dies; especially since even the fixed necessity of death is put off, and we have read that very many were raised up after death.
20.4: **“And before Isaias was gone out of the middle of the court, the word of the Lord came”** — RABANUS. That he who had struck might himself heal
20.5:
**“Go back, and tell Ezechias the captain of my people: Thus saith the Lord the God of David thy father:”** — RABANUS. As [the God of him] whose works thou followest
**“I have heard thy prayer,”** — Because he had walked before the Lord in truth and with a perfect heart, and had wept, and had done what was pleasing to God
20.6:
**“And I will add to thy days fifteen years:”** — RABANUS. Which he had not asked
**“and I will deliver thee out of the hand of the king of the Assyrians,”** — RABANUS. With life, security of the kingdom is promised
20.7: **“And Isaias said: Bring me a lump of figs. And when they had brought it, and laid it upon his boil, he was healed.”** — BRING A LUMP etc. RABANUS. The word 'sim', as the Hebrews say, means a boil, not a wound; this is not inflicted [but] springs of itself. For Aquila, Symmachus and Theodotion translated 'aroc', which they understand as the king's evil, to which all sweet things, whether taken in food or applied to the body, are thought contrary. The power of God, then, is shown when health is restored through harmful things. Others suppose 'sim' to be an abscess, when the swelling body is filled with ripe and putrefying pus. And according to the art of physicians all corrupt matter is drawn out to the surface of the skin by drier and crushed figs.
20.9:
**“WILT THOU THAT THE SHADOW GO FORWARD”** — RABANUS. A sign is given, that the sun go back ten degrees. Symmachus understood the degrees in the lines of a dial, in which degrees were built by mechanical art, so that the shadow, descending through each, marked off the spaces of the hours. It was the tenth hour of the day when the prophet spoke these things to the king. Wilt thou, then, he says, that the shadow go forward ten lines, the sun proceeding above the earth through the northern quarters to the east, which by the daily custom of its course it was to do under the earth? Or that the shadow go back as many degrees, the face of the sun turned backward, and itself returning through the southern quarter to the east? Which the king preferred, because it could be of greater miracle if the sun ran contrary to its own manner of course, than if, going in its accustomed advance, although raised above the earth, it should hasten to the east to make as it were the morning of a second day with no night between. For those who live in the island of Thule, which is beyond Britain, or in the borders of the Scythians, see plainly for some days every summer how the sun returns low from west to east. But those who dwell in the inner parts of the south never see the sun return from setting to the east through the southern quarters. Which sign was a type both of the present time and of the future: that as the sun returned to its beginning, so the life of Ezechias too returned to the years taken away; and for us, living in the hebdomad and ogdoad, the spaces of life are prolonged through the resurrection of Christ.
**“And Isaias said to him: This shall be the sign from the Lord, that the Lord will do the word which he hath spoken: Wilt thou that the shadow go forward ten lines, or that it go back so many degrees?”** — RABANUS. Some transfer the ten degrees of the lines to the mystery of Christ, and interpret the shadows of the figures of the descent of Christ, through which Christ, the sun of justice, after the resurrection ascended again. The first degree of the descent from heaven was in the angel, because he was the messenger of great counsel. The second degree of the descent from the angel was in the patriarchs, because "in all," as the Apostle says, "he himself worked." The third in the giving of the law, because in the law he himself spoke. The fourth in Jesus son of Nave, to lead the people into the land of promise. The fifth in the judges, because he himself ruled the same people through them. The sixth in the kings of the Jews, because he himself reigned in them. The seventh in the prophets, because he is announced through them. The eighth in the high priests, because he himself is the high priest of the Father. The ninth in man. The tenth in the passion. By these ten degrees, as by the shadow of the ancient law, Christ descended; and again, after his resurrection, Christ the sun of justice ascended upward into heaven by the same degrees, and lit up all that shadow of the law with the rays of truth.
20.12:
**“At that time Berodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, king of the Babylonians, sent”** — RABANUS. Nabuchodonosor according to the Hebrews
**“AT THAT TIME [HE] SENT”** — RABANUS. Above it is read that Sennacherib king of the Assyrians took the cities of Juda and sent part of his army to Jerusalem, and, a hundred and eighty-five thousand being slain by the angel, he himself fled to Ninive. He being killed, Asarhaddon his son reigned in his stead. Ezechias was sick and received health at the prophet's message. The sun returning to its rising, the day was made almost double. Now we read that at that time, that is, in the same year in which these things were done, Merodach Baladan sent books and presents to Ezechias, not Asarhaddon, of whose death or life Scripture is silent. From which it is clear that the kingdom of the Assyrians was then one thing, that of the Babylonians another. Lastly, the Assyrians took Samaria, that is, the ten tribes; the Chaldeans afterwards took Juda, whose king was Nabuchodonosor. Merodach had heard that at the petition of Ezechias the sun, which the Chaldeans adore, was turned back to its rising; and when they knew that their god had shown obedience to a mortal king, they believed him more to be adored than a man.
**“letters and presents to Ezechias: for he had heard that Ezechias had been sick.”**
• RABANUS. The Hebrews hand down that Ezechias fell sick because, on account of the unheard-of victory and the death of the Assyrian king, they did not sing praises to the Lord such as Moses sang when Pharao was drowned, and Debbora when Sisara was killed, and Anna when Samuel was born. And again, after the health of his body and the greatness of the sign, an occasion of pride came to him, which as a worshipper of God he ought to have avoided, and not shown to foreigners the riches which he had possessed by God's gift. From which, according to the laws of tropology, we learn "not to cast pearls before swine." For he who is faithful hides matters in his spirit. Why did the Lord not forbid Ezechias through the prophet to show the house of the Lord to foreigners? So that the things that were in his heart might be made known, that is, that the hidden pride of mind by which he sinned before the Lord might be brought to the knowledge of men through the deed of an evil work.
• RABANUS. Hypocrites too decline after great virtues, because they will not be hidden in those same virtues; who, while at the persuasion of evil spirits they consent to boasting, open as it were the door to the enemies, that they may lose what was long gathered. Whence: he delivered their strength into captivity. Paul declares that his glory is the testimony of his conscience, because he does not seek the favour of another's mouth. What we do, then, is to be hidden, lest, carrying it incautiously on the way of this life, we lose it by the attack of robbing spirits.
• RABANUS. He is silent about what he feared would give offence: that he showed them all that he had in his power, among which the chief was the furniture of the temple.
20.13:
**“AND EZECHIAS REJOICED”** — RABANUS. The Words of the Days say of Ezechias: "in the embassy of the princes of Babylon, that were sent to him to inquire of the wonder, God left him that he might be tempted, and all things might be made known that were in his heart." He was left to temptation for this reason, because after so great a victory and the return of the sun and the congratulation of the most powerful kingdom his heart was lifted up. Lastly, in the same volume it is written of Ezechias: "Ezechias was sick even to death, and he prayed to the Lord: and he heard him, and gave him a sign. But he did not render again according to the benefits which he had received, for his heart was lifted up: and wrath was enkindled against him, and against Juda and Jerusalem." And again: "And he humbled himself afterwards, because his heart had been lifted up, both he, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: and therefore the wrath of the Lord came not upon them in the days of Ezechias." He rejoiced, then, at the coming of the envoys and the giving of presents and the congratulation on his health, and showed them the house of his spices etc. There was not a word (which among the Hebrews is often taken for a thing) that he did not show them in his house and in all his dominion. Whence the most just anger of God, since he showed not only his own treasures and those of the palace but also those of the temple, which surely was in his power, from whose court doors he had already before taken the plates.
**“and he shewed them the house of his aromatical spices, and the gold, and the silver,”** — the treasures of gold and silver
**“THE HOUSE OF HIS AROMATICAL SPICES”** — RABANUS. Some think it means the tombs of the kings, which were full of spices, because of old the bodies of kings were embalmed with ointments. Others rather understand it to have been a storeroom of spices in the temple of the Lord, where the fragrant kinds were laid up from which the incense was made that was offered in the temple of the Lord.
**“and divers precious odours,”** — RABANUS. Perfumes
**“and ointments,”** — in the Hebrew: good oil
**“and the house of his vessels,”** — of treasure
**“and all that he had in his treasures. There was nothing in his house, nor in all his dominion, that Ezechias shewed them not.”** — Otherwise: there was nothing that he had not shown
20.14:
**“And Isaias the prophet came to king Ezechias, and said to him: What said these men? or from whence came they to thee? And Ezechias said to him:”** — RABANUS. To be read with a haughty brow
**“From a far country”** — FROM A FAR COUNTRY. RABANUS. As if to say: The farther the land from which they came, the more glorious I, on whose account they came.
**“they came to me, from Babylon.”** — RABANUS. Which is the most powerful in the world
**“TO ME”** — He ought to have said: to glorify God for the greatness of the sign.
20.17: **“Behold the days shall come, that all that is in thy house, and that thy fathers have laid up in store”** — acquired not by thy labour but by that of thy fathers
20.21: **“AND EZECHIAS SLEPT”** — In Paralipomenon it is said that "Ezechias was buried above the sepulchres of the kings," because his tomb was built higher on account of the piety with which he worshipped God.

21.1:
**“MANASSES”** — RABANUS. In whose time Isaias, as the Hebrews hand down, was sawn through the middle with a wooden saw, because he had called them princes of Sodom, they turning into a charge against him what he had said: "I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne high and elevated," since God says: "Man shall not see me and live."
**“Manasses was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned five and fifty years in Jerusalem: the name of his mother was Haphsiba.”** — RABANUS. Manasses turned himself to idols and abominations. When God, or the Lord, spoke to him, he would not attend; therefore he was led bound to Babylon; who, in distress, prayed earnestly to the Lord and did great penance, and his prayer was heard, and he brought him back into his kingdom, and Manasses knew that the Lord himself is God. Therefore after crimes committed let no one despair of God's mercy, but rather have hope of pardon through penance.
21.18: **“And Manasses slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Oza: and Amon his son reigned”** — an idolater
21.24:
**“But the people of the land slew all them that had conspired against king Amon. And they made Josias his son king in his stead.”**
• Josias is interpreted 'whose is the sacrifice to the Lord', or 'salvation of the Lord', or 'strength of the Lord'
• JOSIAS. RABANUS. Josias corrected all the filth of idols and exercised himself vigorously in the worship of God, as had been foretold of him long before by the prophet.

22.12: **“And he commanded Helcias the priest, and Ahicam”** — otherwise Ahicham
22.14:
**“So Helcias the priest, and Ahicam,”** — otherwise Ahicham
**“and Achobor, and Saphan, and Asaia, went to Holda the prophetess, the wife of Sellum the son of Thecua, the son of Araas, keeper of the wardrobe, who dwelt in Jerusalem in the Second:”** — IN THE SECOND. In Paralipomenon it is read of Ezechias that "he built up all the wall that had been broken down, and another wall without." Whence Sophonias: "A howling from the Second." The prophetess, then, dwelt in the Second, that is, in the part of the second wall.

23.10:
**“He defiled”**
• Josias
• HE DEFILED. RABANUS. Josias [defiled] Topheth, scattering there the bones of the dead, as he is read to have done in the following places, or any other unclean things, so that the place might appear fit for abomination rather than delight to all who looked on it.
**“IN THE VALLEY OF THE SON OF ENNOM”** — RABANUS. The valley of Ennom is beside the wall of Jerusalem toward the east, in which a most beautiful grove is watered by the springs of Siloe. Thaphet or Topheth was a place in the same valley, beside the field of Haceldama, to the south of Sion. In Topheth, because the place was most pleasant, whence today it affords the delights of gardens, they used to sacrifice to demons. The valley of Ennom is called in Hebrew Gehennom, whence the Lord Jesus named gehenna, because as in the valley of Ennom those who served idols perished in it, so sinners were condemned for their sins. Whence in Jeremias: this place shall no more be called Topheth, but the valley of slaughter: "And I will defeat the counsel of Juda and of Jerusalem in this place: and I will destroy them with the sword." Isaias calls Topheth hell, saying: "For Topheth is prepared from yesterday, deep, and wide." Beautifully he says 'wide', because Topheth is called 'breadth'.
23.11:
**“He took away also the horses”** — placed with a chariot in the courts of the temple of the Lord
**“HE TOOK AWAY ALSO THE HORSES”** — RABANUS. The Jews had given themselves over to the superstitions of the gentiles, who among other things are wont to paint or make an image of the sun as a beardless boy, because no old age befalls it through the ages, being born daily by a new rising. To it they assign a chariot and horses, because Elias was caught up to heaven in a fiery chariot and fiery horses, which among other things they see painted on a wall, and are deceived by the nearness of the name. For the sun is called Helios in Greek.
23.13:
**“THE HIGH PLACES”** — RABANUS. Scripture means places set on leafy hills, in which they sacrificed to demons; or, enticed by the pleasantness of the places, against the prohibition, leaving the altar which was in the temple, they flocked there to offer to the Lord. Whence it is often said in this book of the less perfect kings: But the high places he took not away.
**“on the right side of the mount of Offence,”** — that is, of the idol
**“WHICH SOLOMON HAD BUILT”** — RABANUS. Here it is shown that Solomon never fully repented of the crime of idolatry he committed; for if he had truly repented, he would have taken care before all things that the idols he had built be taken out of the city, and would not have left as a stumbling block to fools, as if done wisely, the erroneous things which he, though most wise, had made.
**“AND TO CHAMOS”** — RABANUS. Elsewhere it is read that Solomon built a shrine of Chamos on the mount which is over against Jerusalem. But it is not contrary, because this mount was in such nearness to the city that it seemed to belong to it, and also to defile it with the filth that was heaped up on it.
**“THE SCANDAL OF MOAB”** — RABANUS. Idols are called an offence, either because God is offended by them, or because they bring offence and ruin to their worshippers.
23.16: **“HE TOOK THE BONES OUT OF THE SEPULCHRES, AND BURNT THEM”** — Josias commanded the bones of the dead to be burnt upon the altar, because their sacrifices were profane, and through the error of idolatry they offered not only cattle to demons but also delivered themselves into the power of demons; who by the just judgment of God were to be scattered together with the altar which they had made for the idols. Mystically, those who, given over to the devil's service, end a sacrilegious life in time, will be consumed in eternal torments, God repaying according to deserts.
23.21:
**“And he commanded”** — Josias
**“KEEP THE PHASE TO THE LORD”** — RABANUS. Allegorically. Josias holds the type of the Saviour, who is called 'salvation' and 'strength of the Lord'. Whence: "The Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle," and elsewhere: "For he shall save his people from their sins." He indeed, with the zeal of God, cleanses the land of Juda and Jerusalem from uncleannesses and abominations. Whence: "The zeal of thy house hath eaten me up." And again: "Whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his floor," and elsewhere: "And he shall purify the sons of Levi." Our Josias, then, celebrates the true Phase in the eighteenth year of his reign, when in the eighth age, the general resurrection being accomplished, he leads his saints with the perfection of good works to the denarius of beatitude, all scandals being first cast out of his kingdom. Whence: "For behold the day shall come kindled, and all that do wickedly shall be stubble: and the day that cometh shall set them on fire; but unto you that fear the sun of justice shall arise."
23.22:
**“THERE WAS NO SUCH PHASE”** — Because, the figures being taken away on the day of judgment, the saints will pass from death to life, and so will rejoice in the sight of their creator, because "the God of gods shall be seen in Sion."
**“Now there was no such phase kept from the days of the judges, who judged Israel, and all the days of the kings of Israel, and of the kings of Juda,”** — RABANUS. That Josias, having cast out of the land the idols, the pythons, the soothsayers and all uncleannesses, is read to have celebrated the Phase of the Lord, teaches morally that we should first cleanse the land of the heart from vices, that we may be able to serve God. And so we celebrate a Pasch pleasing to the Lord: "not with the leaven of malice and wickedness; but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth."
23.29:
**“IN MAGEDDO”** — RABANUS. Josias was wounded in the plain of Mageddo, of which he at once died. And the people mourned him greatly, Jeremias most of all. For then he is said to have lamented thus: "How doth the city sit solitary." Of this mourning it is said: "There shall be a great lamentation, like the lamentation of Adadremmon," which is the name of the king who then reigned in Charcamis, to whose help Josias had come against Nechao king of Egypt.
**“In his days Pharao Nechao king of Egypt went up against the king of the Assyrians to the river Euphrates: and king Josias went to meet him: and was slain at Mageddo, when he had seen him.”** — RABANUS.
