The slaying of Josias by Pharao Nechao at Mageddo signifies the persecution of the ancient enemy against the preachers, whom out of envy he strives to deliver to death and tries to take away from the land of the Church, that he may more easily scatter the whole people. Pharao [is] 'scattering', Nechao 'striking', Mageddo 'of temptation'. For the devil, permitted to rise up against the saints, strives with all his strength here, that, striking the Lord's flock by tempting, he may scatter it, and first take away those by whose help they ought to have fought against the enemy.
23.30:
**“JOACHAZ”** — RABANUS. He is called by another name Sellum; but because he was most perverse, he reigned a short time. For Nechao bound him, because the people had made him king against his will, and led him into Egypt.
**“And his servants carried him dead from Mageddo: and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own sepulchre. And the people of the land took Joachaz the son of Josias: and anointed him, and made him king in his father's stead.”** — RABANUS. Joachaz held captive signifies the evil teachers whom the people of the land, namely those given to earthly greed, elect as prelates consenting to their vices; whom Pharao bound at Reblatha, when the devil, weakening the hearts of the prelates through a multitude of flatterers, deceives them, and so, bound with the chains of sins, plunges them into the dark abyss of the spiritual Egypt.
23.33:
**“And Pharao Nechao bound him at Reblatha,”**
• by the multitude
• Reblatha is interpreted 'multitude'
**“which is in the land of Emath, that he should not reign in Jerusalem: and he set a fine upon the land, of a hundred talents of silver,”** — that is, much money and tribute
23.34: **“And Pharao Nechao made Eliacim the son of Josias king in the room of Josias his father: and turned his name to Joakim:”** — or Joacim
23.35: **“AND JOAKIM GAVE THE SILVER AND THE GOLD”** — RABANUS. The evil one demands the task of his service in the carnal people, that both in sense and in speech they be ready in all things for his obedience. Joakim, at the king's command, exacts the tax, because the devil, through the masters given over to him, exacts from each one to pay the tax of sin according to his strength; and so in wickedly placed prelates he daily prepares perdition for those subject to them.

24.1:
**“In his days Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon came up, and Joakim became his”** — otherwise: Joachim
**“AND JOAKIM BECAME HIS SERVANT THREE YEARS”** — RABANUS. When once a man has given himself over to any vice, he will be liable not to one but to many masters. Whence Joakim, whom Pharao before compelled to pay him tax, the king of Babylon now compels to serve him three years. Nabuchodonosor is the same as Pharao, namely the prince of confusion and "the ruler of this darkness." So when the ancient enemy persuades someone to pay him the tax of sin, he soon urges him to bring himself wholly into his dominion and pay full service. To be servant to the king of Babylon three years, then, is to be subject to the ancient enemy by persuasion, delight and consent, and, wholly given to vices, to be possessed by him as it were freely. But sometimes such, warned by the mercy of God, rebel against the wicked spirit. Whence it is added: And again he rebelled against him. Nor does it suffice to rebel, if he does not persevere in the fight. For he who desires to go out from the power of the devil must fight bravely against him and implore help from God.
**“AND AGAIN HE REBELLED”** — RABANUS. Josephus relates that he was killed by Nabuchodonosor and thrown before the walls of Jerusalem unburied, of whom it had been foretold: "He shall be buried with the burial of an ass."
24.6:
**“And Joachin reigned”**
• whom Matthew calls Jechonias
• AND JOACHIN REIGNED. RABANUS. The name is written one way, Joakim, in designating the father, who is also Eliacim; another way, Joachin, when the son is signified, who is also Jechonias.
24.8:
**“Joachin was eighteen years old”** — or Joachin
**“when he began to reign, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem:”** — not longer, because he was impious
**“JERUSALEM”** — BEDE. Jerusalem and the land of Israel is the city of Christ, that is, the Church. The Babylonians, Chaldeans, Philistines are the city of the devil, that is, the whole multitude of the wicked, whether of men or angels. And Israel serves the Philistines or Chaldeans when the faithful, standing in the Church in name only, but otherwise deceived by unclean spirits or men, bow the neck of the mind to any sin. And Nabuchodonosor carries off the king of Jerusalem and all the princes, the mighty men of the army, ten thousand into captivity, when both the masters and those who seemed to serve the Lord with unconquerable mind and to keep the decalogue faithfully, suddenly subdued by enticements or adversities, are defiled with greater crimes, or surely fall into heresy. The arms by which, resisting the devil, we defend the liberty given us by God are the words of the Scriptures, in which, by the examples of the Lord himself and of the saints, we learn more clearly than light in what order the wars of the vices must be overcome. Of these arms the Philistines deprive the children of Israel when the evil spirits [turn] the minds of the faithful from meditation on the sacred reading, lest either they themselves take confidence through the practice of resisting, or kindle others perhaps who do not know how to read to resist vices by exhorting or rebuking. They take away the smiths of arms when they so overwhelm those who know the sacred words with crimes that they are altogether ashamed to speak the good things they had learned. They carry every artificer and smith from Jerusalem into Babylon when they turn from their purpose those who profited many by the manifold working of virtues and were wont to fortify the city of God against the corrupters of temptations, and compel them to spend the talent which they ought to have devoted to the protection of holy Church rather at the will of the king of vices. And if we understand smiths not of doors or walls but of gold and gems, the exposition looks to the same end. For it is said of wisdom that gold and a multitude of gems cannot be compared to it; and therefore we call the smiths of these the teachers, who, as long as they live and teach rightly, spend the industry of their art on the adornment of the holy city. But if perhaps they go astray, what else [happens] but that they are carried captive to Babylon by the king of the Chaldeans? So the talent of the word received from heaven is buried in the earth, that is, spiritual knowledge is turned to the works of sinners.
24.14: **“THE ARTIFICERS AND SMITHS”** — RABANUS. What the Philistines reigning over the people of Israel are related above to have done, when it is said: "Now there was no smith to be found in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines had taken this precaution, lest the Hebrews should make them swords or spears," so now the Chaldeans take care that no artificer or smith remain in it who could put together or repair the ruined walls of the city.
24.17:
**“And he appointed Mathanias”**
• or Mathanias
• who was the son of Josias, the brother of Joakim
24.18: **“SEDECIAS”** — Evil are the rulers who abuse the gift and divine present, and falsely usurp for themselves the name of justice. For Mathathias or Mathanias is interpreted 'gift' or 'present', Sedecias 'just one of the Lord'. He reigned eleven years, because he was a transgressor of the law, which is signified by the number ten. Nine, which has less than ten, signifies the imperfection of the law, as eleven its transgression. Rightly, then, Nabuchodonosor in the ninth year of the reign of Sedecias besieged the city in the tenth month and the tenth day of the month, because when evil shepherds neglect to fulfil by work and teaching the commandments of the decalogue which they hold in knowledge, the ancient enemy with his army must surround the people committed to them with a siege, and, a fortification of error and vices being built, shut them in by walling the city. And so famine prevails in the city, the famine indeed of the word of God, when the bread of doctrine is not spent on the people of the land.

25.4: **“And a breach was made into the city: and all the men of war fled in the night between the two walls by the king's garden (now the Chaldees besieged the city round about) and Sedecias fled by the way that leadeth to the plains of the wilderness.”** — AND A BREACH WAS MADE etc. RABANUS. The guard of the peoples being broken through by the various temptations of demons, those who ought to have defended the city with arms, walled in by the night of ignorance and sins, flee, because "the hireling, and he that is not the shepherd, seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and flieth: and the wolf catcheth, and scattereth the sheep." By the way of the gate which is between the two walls by the garden he lays bare the sloth of the teachers, who, set between the double wall of the two testaments, seek not to make war but to escape, and rather to flow away in delights, which the garden signifies, than to resist the enemies with the shield of faith. Sedecias flees, because when the demons surround the people the ruler flees, not to the mountains of which [it is said]: "Mountains are round about it," but to the plains, that is, to the delight of luxury. Whence: "Narrow is the way that leadeth to life, broad that which leadeth to death." They overtook him in the plain of Jericho, and the warriors were scattered and left him. For when the virtues, which ought to have defended a man, desert him, he is taken in the plain of Jericho, that is, in the failing of carnal sense. For Jericho is interpreted 'moon', and signifies the failing of the flesh. Whence he who went down from Jerusalem to Jericho fell among robbers. He slew the sons of Sedecias before him and put out his eyes. The king of Babylon is the devil, possessor of inmost confusion, who first slaughters the sons before the eyes of the father looking on, because he often so kills good works that the mind which is taken captive sees with grief that it is losing them. For the mind often groans [so the edition: 'genuit'], and yet, overcome by the delights of the flesh, loses, though loving them, the good things it has begotten. It considers the losses it suffers, yet does not lift the arm of virtue against the king of Babylon. But while, seeing, it is struck by the committing of wickedness, it is at length brought by the habit of sin to be deprived also of the very light of reason; because the devil first withdraws good works and afterwards takes away the light of understanding. Which Sedecias rightly suffers at Reblatha. For Reblatha is here interpreted 'much', because at length the light of reason is shut off for him who is weighed down by evil habit and the multitude of his iniquity.
25.6: **“So they took the king, and brought him to the king of Babylon to Reblatha: and he gave judgment upon him.”** — because he exercised just judgment upon him
25.8:
**“IN THE FIFTH MONTH”** — RABANUS. The order of time agrees with the reason of the vengeance. In the fifth month the city was laid waste, which scorned to keep the Pentateuch of the law; and on the seventh day of the month, because it did not keep the rest of the sabbath, and acted contrary to the commands of God, flattering itself in vain about security on account of dwelling in the holy places.
**“NABUZARDAN CAME”** — RABANUS. [Nabuzardan,] who is interpreted 'fan' or 'prophecy of another's judgment', by the just judgment of God upon sinners, the prince indeed of the army of the king of Babylon, [came] into the spiritual Jerusalem and burnt the house of the Lord, when the devil, who is both king of confusion and prince of all the wicked, both evil spirits and impious men, invades the people of the faithful, and overthrows the king's house and the houses of Jerusalem, that is, the rulers and those who seemed to abide in the vision of peace, inflamed with greed. And he burnt every house with fire, when he troubled the conscience of each one through the flame of unlawful love. And he destroyed the walls of Jerusalem round about, when he loosens in the despairing the intention of prayer and the studies of the virtues, which he knows avail against him, lest through hope of pardon they run to the divine helps and lay hold of the defences of amendment of life. And leading the people into captivity, he left of the poor of the land vinedressers and husbandmen, because, taking captive through vices those who could be useful by word and example, he commits husbandry to the foolish and dull, so that not the wine of spiritual grace and the corn of sound doctrine may bear fruit in the vineyards and fields of the peoples, but rather the thorns and thistles of vices may grow.
25.13: **“THE PILLARS”** — RABANUS. [By the pillars] and the bases we understand 'the teachers', who by the resonance of preaching and firmness of faith ought to have supported others; by the brazen sea 'the laver of baptism' or 'the compunction of tears'. All these the spiritual Chaldeans strive to carry off from the house of the Lord through the sloth of the masters and to break in pieces.
25.14: **“THE CALDRONS ALSO”** — RABANUS. Because, taking away the various offices in the ecclesiastical orders from the service of God, they have turned them to their own most wicked use.
25.15:
**“THE CENSERS ALSO, AND THE BOWLS”** — When by hindering they overthrow the prayer by which the divinity could be appeased, and the cup of the word by which the weary ought to have been refreshed.
**“such as were of gold, in gold”**
• things and sense were not found for the sake of letters, but letters for the manifestation of things
• a transcription
**“SUCH AS WERE OF GOLD, IN GOLD, AND SUCH AS WERE OF SILVER, IN SILVER”** — Because the wicked enemy strives to carry off from the house of the Lord both the precious sense and the comeliness of speech, and to lead them with him into confusion.
25.18: **“TOOK ALSO”** — RABANUS. The devil is busy to deceive and take captive as sinners not only the common people but also the strong and the princes in the Church. Whence in Job of him: "His food is choice." He took Saraias, who is interpreted 'bound', the chief priest, when he binds with the chain of vices the first order of the Church, which is in the bishops, through love of earthly pleasure. Likewise Sophonias, who is interpreted 'hidden', the second priest, when he subjects to his dominion the men of the second order, that is, the presbyters, who, digging in the earth, had hidden the talent of the word. And the three doorkeepers, who ought to have opened the door of faith, and holding the key of knowledge neither entered in themselves nor permitted others to enter. The eunuch signifies the foolish virgins, who held in their hands vessels empty of oil, abstaining from bodily intercourse, yet unwilling to have the oil of grace and mercy in their breast; who are set in vain over the warriors, since they do not guard against arrogance. The five men who had stood before the king, that is, those who, serving pleasure with the five senses of the body, always stood by the king of vices.
25.19:
**“SOPHAR”** — RABANUS. [Sophar] is interpreted 'scattering' or 'dividing', signifying those who, scattering by evil examples the unlearned in the Church whom they ought to have nourished for the warfare of Christ, separate them from the company of the faithful through error. And six men of the common people, that is, foolish workers, who are rightly 'of the common people', because they had neglected to learn the divine counsels and fulfil them in deeds.
**“SOPHAR, AND SIX MEN”** — RABANUS. All these Nabuzardan led to the king of Babylon, and they were killed, because the devil seeks to bring the prey which he tears from the Church to the slaying of perpetual death; whom the king of confusion strikes at Reblatha, that is, in the multitude of crimes and the love of pleasures.
25.21: **“AND JUDA WAS CARRIED AWAY OUT OF HIS LAND”** — When those who seemed to have the confession of the name of God in the Church are carried away through manifold crimes from the land of the living and led off into the kingdom of confusion and error. Whoever persevere under this rule will not deserve to return under the leadership of Jesus to the land of Juda and rebuild the temple of the Lord there. For hereafter, after the present life, they will be delivered to the prison of perpetual death, "where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not extinguished." But let it be granted us, in the pilgrimage of the passing world, to bear true penitence for what we have committed, and after the course of seven days, as after the seventy years of this captivity, stripped of all the power of the king of Babylon, to be able, the Spirit who is called sevenfold helping us, to enter the heavenly Jerusalem and contemplate the face of our creator through the ages.
25.23: **“AND SARAIAS”** — The son of Saraias the priest was preserved and the father killed. From whom afterwards in the captivity was born Jesus the high priest, who brought back the people with Zorobabel.

1.4: **“Noe,”** — NOE. RABANUS. Noe is shown tenth from Adam both in Genesis and in Paralipomenon, and fittingly tenth, because he is perfect. Whence: "Noe was a just and perfect man in his generations" etc. He begot Sem, Cham and Japheth, through whom after the flood the revived progeny of men is spread abroad.
1.5:
**“The sons of Japheth:”**
• these possessed the land in Asia from Amanus and Taurus
• these seven nations dwell to the north
**“THE SONS OF JAPHETH”** — JEROME. These possessed the land in Asia from Amanus and Taurus, the mountains of Coele-Syria and Cilicia, as far as the river Tanais; in Europe as far as Gades [so the edition: 'Gadara'], leaving names to places and nations, of which afterwards very many were changed; the rest remain.
**“Gomer,”** — Galatians
**“and Magog,”** — Scythians
**“and Madai,”** — Medes
**“and Javan,”** — Ionians, who are also Greeks, whence also the Ionian sea
**“TUBAL”** — RABANUS. The Iberians, who are also the Spaniards, from whom Celtiberia, though some suspect the Italians.
**“Mosoch,”** — Cappadocians
**“MOSOCH”** — RABANUS. The Cappadocians, whence their city is called Mazaca to this day. But the Seventy translators think Caphtorim to be the Cappadocians.
**“Thiras.”**
• Thracians
• [unclear in the edition: "Trao"]. These seven nations dwell to the north
1.6:
**“And the sons of Gomer: Ascenez,”**
• Sarmatians.
• These the Greeks call Rhegini
**“and Riphath,”** — Paphlagonians
**“and Thogorma.”** — Phrygians
1.7:
**“And the sons of Javan: Elisa,”** — from whom the Eliseans, who are called Aeolians
**“AND THE SONS OF JAVAN”** — GREGORY. By these were divided the islands of the nations, the tongues, kindreds and peoples. From the Ionians, that is, the Greeks, are born the Eliseans, who are also the Aeolians. Whence that dialect of Greek is called Aeolic.
**“and Tharsis,”** — Cilicians
**“THARSIS”** — RABANUS. These Josephus thinks are the Cilicians, whence their chief city is called Tharsis, glorious through Paul the Apostle.
**“Cethim,”** — Cyprians
**“CETHIM”** — RABANUS. From whom the Cithei, otherwise Cicii, from whom a city of Cyprus is called Cithia, otherwise Citium, to this day.
**“and Dodanim.”** — Rhodians
**“RABANUS”** — Dodanim, the Rhodians; for so the Seventy translated. Let us read the books of Varro on antiquities, and of Sinnius Capito, and the Greek Phlegon and the rest, and we shall see that almost all the islands, and the shores of the whole world, and the lands by the sea were occupied by Greek settlers, who possessed all the coasts from Amanus and Taurus as far as the British ocean.
1.8:
**“The sons of Cham: Chus,”** — Ethiopia is called Chus by the Hebrews to this day
**“and Mesraim,”** — Egypt
**“and Phut,”** — from whom Libya
**“PHUT”** — RABANUS. The Libyans, from whom also a river of Mauritania is called Phut, and the Phutensian region. Many writers, both Greek and Latin, are witnesses of this. But why in one part of the zone the ancient name of Libya remains, and the rest of the land is called Africa, is not for this time to discuss.
**“and Chanaan.”** — he obtained the land from which [so the edition: 'in Dei'] they cast out the Chanaanites
1.9:
**“And the sons of Chus:”** — from whom the Africans and Phoenicians
**“Saba,”** — from whom the Sabaean Arabs
**“SABA”** — RABANUS. From whom the Sabaeans; Saba is now interpreted Arabia. Whence in the Psalm, where we have: "The kings of the Arabians and of Saba," in the Hebrew is had: "The kings of Saba and Zaba," the first with shin, the second with samech.
**“and Hevila,”** — the Gaetulians in part of remoter Africa, adjoining the desert
**“and Sabatha,”** — from whom the Sabathenians, who are now named Astobori or Astabari
**“and Regma, and Sabatacha.”** — these two have lost their ancient names, and what they have instead we do not know
**“And the sons of Regma: Saba, and Dadan.”** — a nation of Ethiopia in the western quarter
1.10: **“HE BEGAN”** — Because he first seized an unaccustomed tyranny. He was a stout hunter before the Lord, because he turned men away from the worship of God. Whence Josephus: And he made them lifted up to the injury and contempt of God. Nemrod, the son of Cham the son of Noe, being bolder and very strong of hand, persuaded men to ascribe their happiness not to God but to their own strength. Thus he called men back from the fear of God, that they might put their hope in their own strength. And therefore they thought God threatened a flood; whence they urged that a tower be built which the water could not climb. And the multitude was ready to obey Nemrod, thinking it a grievous servitude to obey God. And Nemrod reigned in Babylon and in Areth, which is Edessa, and in Acha, which is Nisibis, and in Chalamne, which was called Seleucia by king Seleucus, or which is now called Ctesiphon.
1.11:
**“And Mesraim begot Ludim, and Anamim, and Laabim, and Nephtuim,”**
• the Libyans, who before were the Phuteans
• AND MESRAIM etc. RABANUS. Except the Laabim, from whom the Libyans are named, who before were the Phuteans, and the Casluim, who were afterwards called Philistim, whom we corruptly call Palestinians, the other nations are unknown to us, because, overthrown in the Ethiopian war, they passed into oblivion of their former names. And they possessed the land from Gaza to the farthest borders of Egypt.
1.12: **“Phetrusim also, and Casluim”** — who are also the Philistim, whom we have corruptly called Palestinians
1.13: **“And Chanaan begot Sidon”** — from whom Sidon, a city in Phoenicia
1.14: **“and the Jebusite,”** — from whom the Jebusites, whose was Jerusalem
1.15:
**“And the Hevite,”** — from whom the Hevites, who are also the Gabaonites, from the city of Gabaon, who came as suppliants to Josue
**“THE ARACITE”** — He founded the town of Arca over against Tripolis, at the roots of Libanus, not far from which there was another city named Sin, which, overthrown by the varying fortune of wars, kept for the place only its former name.
**“and the Asenite,”** — from whom the Asenites
1.16:
**“THE ARADIAN ALSO”** — From whom the Aradians, who possessed the island of Aradus, separated from the coast of Phoenicia by a narrow strait.
**“AND THE SAMARITE”** — From whom Samaria, a city of Coele-Syria, is even now so called, both by Syrians and by Hebrews, as of old among the ancients.
**“THE HAMATHITE”** — RABANUS. From whom the city of Emath. This the Macedonians who reigned in the east after Alexander named Epiphania. Others think Antioch was so called. Others, not truly comforting their opinion with a likely name, think that Emaus, the first station from Antioch for those going to Edessa, is so called, and that it was Emath among the ancients.
1.17:
**“THE SONS OF SEM”** — These hold the parts of Asia from the Euphrates to the Indian ocean. And Elam is he from whom [are] the princes of Persia [so the edition: 'perfidis'].
**“Elam,”** — from whom the Elamites
**“and Assur,”**
• who founded the city of Ninive
• from whom the kingdom of the Assyrians sprang
**“and Arphaxad,”** — from whom the Chaldeans
**“and Lud,”** — from whom the Lydians
**“and Aram,”** — from whom the Syrians, whose chief city is Damascus
**“and Hus,”** — or Us
**“HUS”** — Or Us, founder of Trachonitis and Damascus, held the principality between Palestine and Coele-Syria; from whom the land of Hus. Whence according to the Seventy: "There was a man in the region of Ausitis, named Job," as if Husitis.
**“and Hul,”** — from whom the Armenians
**“and Gether,”** — from whom the Carnani or Carians
**“and Mosoch.”** — who are now called Maeonians, but before Mes
1.18:
**“And Arphaxad”** — from whom the Chaldeans
**“begot Sale,”** — from whom the Bactrians
**“who also himself begot Heber.”** — from whom the Hebrews
1.19:
**“And to Heber were born two sons, the name of the one was Phaleg, because in his days the earth was divided: and the name of his brother was Jectan.”** — from whom the nation of the Indians
**“PHALEG”** — By a certain prophecy. For Phaleg [is] 'division', because in his days the tongues were divided in Babylon. Philo relates in the book of questions on Genesis that of the three sons of Noe, while he was still living, there were born fourteen thousand one hundred men, besides women and children, having leaders over them: the sons of Sem Jectan as leader, the sons of Cham Nemrod, the sons of Japheth Suphene. But after the death of Noe the leaders came together with their bands into the plain of Sennaar, to build a tower there. And while they were building, God divided their tongues and changed their appearances, and no one knew his brother, nor heard the tongue of his neighbour. When the master builders asked for stones, the servants brought water, and when they asked for water, they brought straw. And so, their design frustrated, they ceased to build and were scattered over the face of the earth.
1.20: **“AND JECTAN”** — JEROME. The later names of these nations I could not find, but up to the present, because they are far from us, they are either called as at first, or what they have been changed to is unknown. And they possessed from the river Cophen the whole region of India which is called Hieria.
1.24: **“Sem, Arphaxad, Sale,”** — SEM, ARPHAXAD. RABANUS. As at the beginning he set ten generations from Adam to Noe, so from Sem to Abraham, not without the mystery of a sacrament.
1.29: **“THE FIRSTBORN OF ISMAEL”** — JEROME. Twelve sons are born to Ismael. The firstborn Nabaioth, from whom the whole region from the Euphrates to the Red Sea is called Nabathena, which is a part of Arabia. For their families and towns and villages and small forts and tribes are celebrated by their name: from one of them Cedar in the desert, and Duma another region, and Thebaran to the south, and Cedema toward the eastern quarter.
1.32:
**“And the sons of Cetura Abraham's concubine, whom she bore: Zamran, Jecsan,”** — or Jacsan
**“Madan, Madian, Jesboc, and Sue. And the sons of Jecsan: Saba, and Dadan. And the sons of Dadan: Assurim,”** — merchants
**“and Latussim,”** — forging the metals of brass and iron
**“and Laomim.”**
• or Lomim
• phylarchs, that is, princes of many tribes
1.33:
**“OF CETURA”** — RABANUS. [Cetura means] as it were 'joined'. Whence the Hebrews suspect that she was Agar, who after Sara's death passed from concubine to wife, lest the old man be charged with having wantoned in new nuptials.
**“And the sons of Madian: Epha, and Epher, and Henoch, and Abida, and Eldaa. All these are the sons of Cetura.”** — RABANUS. The sons of Cetura, according to the historians of the Hebrews, occupied Troglodytis, others Trachonitis and Arabia, which is now called [unclear in the edition: "Eidormo"], up to the bounds of the Red Sea.
**“ASSURIM”** — From Assurim some contend that the Syrians were named, and that the regions of India were occupied by many sons of Abraham by Cetura.
**“EPHER”** — RABANUS. He is said to have led an army against Libya, and, victorious, to have settled there, and his descendants named Africa after his name.
1.34:
**“And Abraham begot Isaac:”** — who alone [was born] of Sara by promise
**“whose sons were Esau and Israel.”** — from one conception of Rebecca
1.35:
**“The sons of Esau: Eliphaz,”** — whom Ada bore
**“Rahuel,”** — whom Basemath bore
**“Jehus, Ihelom, and Core.”** — these three, the sons of Oolibama
1.36:
**“The sons of Eliphaz:”** — of whom mention was made in Job
**“Theman, Omar, Sephi, Gathan, Cenez, Thamna, Amalec.”** — THAMNA. It is asked, since Thamna is read in Genesis to be the concubine of Eliphaz, of the race of the Horrites, who dwelt among the Idumeans in the land of Seir, who bore him Amalec, how she is numbered among the sons, when in what follows that same Thamna is read to be the sister of Lotan the son of Seir, who is also Edom. But Seir in Hebrew means 'hairy', who was rough like a skin; and Edom in Hebrew 'red' or 'tawny'. From this, then, that he sold his birthright for red food, he was called Edom. But the Hebrews solve it thus: they say that Thamna was the concubine of Eliphaz and bore him Amalec, but was brought up by him as a daughter among his sons. Alian, who is of the race of the Horrites, is written Alvan in Genesis, that is, 'exalted'; but in Paralipomenon Alian, that is, signifying 'cast out', because the Horrites were exalted before Edom took their land, but afterwards cast out.
1.40:
**“JEROME”** — Sephi, that is, 'one-footed'; in Genesis Sepho, that is, 'two-footed'. Both, however, with the letter shin. And he is called two-footed who in the course of time had greater efficacy through a multitude of offspring than at first.
**“and Onam. The sons of Sebeon: Aia, and Ana. The son of Ana: Dison.”** — of whom it is said in Genesis that he "found hot waters in the wilderness, when he fed the asses of Sebeon his father"
1.41: **“The sons of Dison: Hamram,”** — Hamram: in Paralipomenon Hamran, that is, 'reddened with filth' or 'drunken'; in Genesis "Hamdan", that is, 'desirable'; but both are names of one man.
1.42: **“JACAN”** — RABANUS. Jacan, son of Aser, of the race of the Horrites, is named Zavan in Genesis, that is, 'troubler'; in Paralipomenon Jacan, that is, 'troubled'. For names are changed by various events, that various mysteries may be signified.
1.43:
**“Now these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there was a king over the children of Israel: Bale the son of Beor: and the name of his city was Denaba.”** — or Dennaba; others Dannaba
**“DENABA”** — The city of Bale the son of Beor, king of Edom, after whom Jobab reigned. There is, however, to this day a village Denaba at the eighth milestone from Areopolis for those going to the Arnon [so the edition: 'Armonem'], and another Denaba upon mount Phegor, at the seventh stone from [unclear in the edition: "Hiebus, Hieronymus de Iesbii"].
1.44: **“BOSRA”** — Which is Bosor, a city in the desert beyond the Jordan in the tribe of Ruben. There is also called another Bosor, a city of Esau in the mountains of Idumea, of which it is said: his garments dyed from Bosra.
1.45:
**“JOBAB”** — The son of Zara, whom they suspect to be Job; but the Hebrews assert that he was born of the stock of Nachor. And Philo, in the book of questions on Genesis, relates that he lived in these times and took to wife Dina the daughter of Jacob, and says that before the contest of his temptation she bore him seven sons and three daughters, who were destroyed in the temptation. But when he was healed the Lord restored to him all things double, and again the said wife bore seven sons and three daughters, whose names were the same as those of the former, that is, Eliphaz, Armoe, Diasath, Philasias, Diphar, Celuth, Thelon; and of the daughters Meru, Lizath, Zeli.
**“OF THE THEMANITES”** — Theman, a region that took its name from Theman the son of Eliphaz. There is to this day a village Theman, five miles distant from the city of Petra, where a garrison of Roman soldiers was stationed; from which place was Eliphaz, king of the Themanites. One of the sons of Ismael too was called Theman. And it is to be known that every southern region is called Theman in Hebrew.
1.46:
**“And Husam also died, and Adad the son of Badad reigned in his stead, who smote Madian in the land of Moab: and the name of his city was Avith.”** — a village in the land of Basan, beside mount Galaad, in the tribe of Manasses
**“MADIAN”** — A city so called from the youngest of the sons of Abraham and Cetura. It is beyond Arabia in the desert of the Saracens, toward the east of the Red Sea, whence they are called Madianites and the region Madianea. The daughters of the father-in-law of Moses too are called daughters of Madian. But this is another city, [unclear in the edition: "Ononimos eius"], beside the Arnon [so the edition: 'Armorem'], and Areopolis [so the edition: 'Aeroplim'], whose ruins are still shown.
1.47: **“And when Adad also was dead, Semla of Masreca reigned in his stead.”** — a city of the kingdom of Edom, about Gebalene
1.48: **“ROHOBOTH”** — It is a city by the river, where the king of Edom was, and to this day there is a garrison in the region of Gabalena, and a large village which is so called.
1.50:
**“He also died, and Adad reigned in his stead,”** — eminent
**“and the name of his city was Phau,”** — This Adad founded the city of Phau in the Gabalitic region
**“and his wife was called Meetabel”** — the kindness of the Lord
**“the daughter of Matred”** — of a stewardess
**“the daughter of Mezaab.”** — of a goldsmith
**“OF MATRED THE DAUGHTER OF MEZAAB”** — Two mothers are numbered here to signify a mystery: that the goldsmith begot the stewardess, and the stewardess the kindness of the Lord; because from depth of sense is born fruitful speech, which by the pure grace of God deserves to beget faith in the hearts of the hearers.
1.51:
**“DUKES INSTEAD OF KINGS”** — It is to be noted that first he spoke of kings of Edom, afterwards of dukes, since earlier there were dukes, some of whose mothers he names, as Oolibama and Thamna.
**“DUKE ALIA”** — Alva is read in Genesis, whose interpretation is 'elevation'; in Paralipomenon Alia, that is, 'upon her'.

2.1: **“And the sons of Israel:”** — the twelve sons of Jacob
2.3:
**“The sons of Juda:”** — of these it is written most fully in Genesis
**“Her, Onan,”** — or: Aunan
2.4: **“And Thamar his daughter in law bore him Phares and Zara.”** — of these too many things are written in Genesis
2.5: **“And the sons of Phares: Hesron, and Hamul.”** — or: Hamul
2.6:
**“And the sons of Zara: Zamri, and Ethan, and Eman, and Chalchal, and Dara,”**
• otherwise: Darda
• otherwise: Daman
2.7: **“ACHAR, WHO TROUBLED”** — Achar, who in Josue is also called Achan, that is, 'a snake lying in wait'. Achar [is] 'troubled', because through avarice he lay in wait to snatch something by theft from the anathema; caught in the crime, he was troubled in the punishment. Mystically suggesting that he who after the garment of faith brings in the worship of a worldly life takes as it were a cloak from the anathema. He too takes from the anathema of Jericho who brings into the Church the dogmas of heretics or the superstitions of worldly letters. For this is the golden rule fitted with splendid speech. This Arius, Marcion and others stole, who tried to bring into the Church the crooked sect of the philosophers, so that many perished through them. Therefore, cast down under a heap of stones, that is, by a multitude of sins, they were destroyed.
2.8: **“The sons of Ethan:”** — or Ethan
2.9:
**“And the sons of Hesron that were born to him: Jerameel, and Ram, and Calubi.”** — Calubi, that is, 'my dog', who is also Caleb, that is, 'dog', one of the spies. Hesron too and Jephone are the same. Whence Caleb is read as the son of Hesron and sometimes the son of Jephone.
**“this is Caleb.”** — or Caleb
2.11: **“And Nahasson begot Salma,”** — that is, peace; but in Ruth he is called Salmon, that is, peaceable
2.13:
**“AND ISAI BEGOT”** — In the book of Kings Isai is said to have eight sons; in Paralipomenon not more than seven. But the Hebrews say that Nathan the prophet, son of Samaa (or Sammaa, or Simmaa) the son of Isai, whom he brought up and nourished in the place of a son, was numbered among the sons. Among the sons of Isai too Nathan was brought to Samuel, who is also Jonathan, who struck the lion. And it is to be known that where he is called prophet, Nathan is written, not Jonathan.
**“his firstborn Eliab,”** — or Heliab
**“the second Abinadab, the third Simmaa,”**
• or Samma
• or Sammaa
• or Samaa
2.17: **“JETHER”** — In Kings, Jethra the Israelite; but the quality of merits makes the diversity of names. For Jethra is interpreted 'remnant', but Jether 'a small remnant'; and to the remnant are joined the Israelites, to the small remnant the Ismaelites.
2.19:
**“And when Azuba was dead, Caleb took to wife Ephrata: who bore him Hur.”** — after Azuba died, sons were born of Ephrata
**“EPHRATA”** — This is Mary the sister of Moses, mother of Hur, the father of Uri, grandfather of Beseleel. And Hur is he who with Aaron held up the hands of Moses while Josue fought.
2.21: **“And after this Hesron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Galaad,”** — the son of Manasses the son of Joseph, who received an inheritance beyond the Jordan in the land of Galaad
2.22: **“JAIR”** — He was a judge after Thola and judged Israel twenty-two years, having thirty sons, princes of thirty cities which were named after him, as is read in the book of Judges.
2.23: **“And he took Gessur, and Aram,”** — or Aran
2.24:
**“And when Hesron was dead, Caleb went in to Ephrata.”** — after his father's death Caleb joined Ephrata to himself; but whether in Egypt or in the desert does not appear
**“Hesron had also a wife Abia,”** — whether among the other wives or after them it does not clearly show
**“who bore him Assur the father of Thecua.”** — a city
2.25: **“WERE BORN”** — Thus far the writer of the history has woven the generation of the two later sons of Hesron, that is, Ram and Calubi, of whom he spoke first, because he wished in some manner to make known the royal and priestly dignity. Now he returns to the genealogy of the firstborn, that is, Jerameel.
2.26: **“ONAM”** — He took his name from Onan the son of Juda, but they differ, because the son of Juda is written with nun, the son of Jerameel with mem.
2.27: **“And the sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerameel, were Moos, Jamin,”** — otherwise Joamin, otherwise Joanim
2.29:
**“And the name of the wife of Abisur was Abihail,”** — or Abigail
**“who bore him Ahobban”** — otherwise Achabon, otherwise Aahobbam
2.31:
**“SESAN”** — The Hebrews say this is Elimelech, the husband of Noemi, the father of Mahalon and Chelion; and therefore what is written in the following suggests that Sesan had not sons but daughters, because his two sons died without children.
**“And Sesan begot Oholai.”** — otherwise Ahalai, otherwise Oali
2.36: **“And Ethei begot Nathan, and Nathan begot Zabad.”** — or Zabuth, otherwise Zabad
2.37: **“And Zabad begot Ophlal,”** — or Ophel, otherwise Ophial
2.42:
**“Now the sons of Caleb the brother of Jerameel,”** — or Jeramel, or Jerameli, or Jeramuhel, or Jeramuheli, or Jeramehel
**“were Mesa”** — otherwise Mosa
**“his firstborn, he is the father of Ziph:”** — the name of a place, from which the Ziphites who said to Saul: "Is not David hid with us?"
**“and the sons of Maresa the father of Hebron.”** — a city
**“HEBRON”** — The city in which David reigned seven years before he reigned in Jerusalem. It signifies that these places received their names from the descendants of Caleb, who received Hebron and its suburbs by lot.
2.43: **“And the sons of Hebron, were Core, and Thaphua,”** — otherwise: Taphua, otherwise: Taphephu
2.44: **“And Samma begot Raham, the father of Jercaam,”** — otherwise: Hierthaam
2.46:
**“And Epha the concubine of Caleb, bore Haran, and Mosa,”** — or Mosa
**“and Gezez. And Haran begot Gezez.”** — otherwise: Gezen
2.47:
**“And the sons of Jahaddai: Regom, and Joathan, and Gesan,”**
• otherwise: Zesum
• this is interpreted 'shearer', whence he is thought by the Jews to be Nabal of Carmel, who, shearing his sheep, treated David's messengers with insult
2.50: **“THESE WERE THE SONS”** — He recapitulates the generation of Caleb by Ephrata, which he left off before when he related Hur to have been born of Ephrata, that is, of Mary the sister of Moses.
2.51: **“Salma the father of Bethlehem, Hariph the father of Bethgader.”** — because it received its name from him
2.52:
**“CARIATHIARIM”** — Which is also Cariathbaal, that is, 'city of the woods', one of the cities of the Gabaonites, at the ninth milestone for those going from Aelia to Diospolis, in the tribe of Juda.
**“who saw”** — otherwise saw
2.54:
**“BETHLEHEM”** — The city of David in the tribe of Juda, in which the Lord was born, at the seventh milestone from Aelia toward the southern quarter, beside the road that leads to Hebron, where the tomb of Jesse and David is shown; and about a thousand paces away the tower of Ader, that is, 'the tower of the flock', by a certain prophecy signifying beforehand the shepherds who were made aware of the Lord's nativity.
**“and Netophathi, the crowns of the house of Joab,”** — because they kept mutual fellowship in battles
**“and half of the place of rest, Sarai.”** — it signifies that they had possession in the place called the tomb of Sarai; whence it was said above that the Sarites and Esthaolites took their lot in the names of places
**“WHO SAW HALF OF THE PLACES OF REST”** — Half of the places of rest, that is, the lots of Madian [so the edition], beside the tombs of the patriarchs which are in Cariatharbe, he received; and his sons were the Jethrites etc. The Sarites and Esthaolites took the names of places, which are Sarai and Esthaol, where Samson was buried. For a place of rest means a tomb. Others understand half of the rest as half the time in which the children of Israel began to possess the land of promise, namely from the time when Moses gave the land of Galaad beyond the Jordan to Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses, until the other tribes received their lots. In the middle of this time they say Sobal died, and so saw half of the rest, that is, reached the middle of that time. But mystically Sobal, that is, 'vain old age' or 'a bar for carrying', signifies the Jews, who of old were called the people of God and first received the law of the letter; who carried the books of the law and the prophets but did not understand the mystery of the incarnation of Christ. Whence they saw half of the places of rest, that is, the history. But he possesses the fulness of the places of rest who after very good works rejoices in eternal quiet. Or he sees half of the rest who after the labour of the present life has rest of soul; but he will see the perfection of the places of rest when he enjoys the perfection of quiet in both soul and body.
2.55:
**“The families also of the scribes that dwell in Jabes, singing and making melody, and abiding in tents.”** — because they have not here a lasting city
**“These are the Cineans, who came of Calor the father of the house of Rechab.”**
• because they were of the stock of Rechab, of whom Jeremias tells
• Jabes signifies Christ, the true master of the saints who sing praises to God. For Jabes is interpreted 'drying up'; and Christ dried up the flow of carnal desires in his faithful. The Cineans, that is, 'possession' or 'possessing', are all the elect, of whom it is said: "Israel my inheritance," and "whose possession is the Lord." Rechab is interpreted 'charioteer' or 'ascending'. And these came of the heat of the father of the house of Rechab, because, inflamed by the grace of the Spirit from the Father of lights, they ascend to heaven by the four-horse chariot of the virtues; of whom it is said: "Whosoever are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God."
**“THAT DWELL IN JABES”** — The Hebrews hand down that Jabes was a most learned teacher of the law, in whose presence sat the sons of the Cinean, who is also Jobab, the kinsman of Moses. They are therefore called scribes, singing and making melody, because they were continually occupied in the speaking of the law of God. That they abode in tents, too, the history of Kings relates.

3.1:
**“Now David had these sons, that were born to him in Hebron:”** — NOW DAVID etc. He returns to setting out the progeny of David, which he left off before when, enumerating the offspring of Ram the son of Hesron, he came to Isai and his sons, of whom David was the youngest.
**“the firstborn Amnon”** — or Amnon
**“of Achinoam the Jezrahelitess,”** — JEZRAHELITESS. RABANUS. Jezrahel is the city in which Naboth lived, whom [Jezabel] killed.
**“the second Daniel of Abigail the Carmelitess.”** — who was the wife of Nabal of Carmel
**“DANIEL”** — RABANUS. Daniel, who in the book of Kings is Cheleab, that is, 'avenging the father', because, according to the Hebrews, disputing with Miphiboseth on questions of the law, he came off victor and seemed to avenge his father in him, lest a warlike man should be mocked in disputation by a weak man.
3.2: **“The third Absalom the son of Maacha the daughter of Tholmai”** — or Tholomei, or Ptholomei
3.3: **“OF EGLA HIS WIFE”** — It is asked why this Egla alone is called the wife of David. But this is Michol, who among many is alone called wife, because he took her first as wife in his youth; she is said to have died in childbirth. And Egla is interpreted 'heifer', which signifies the Synagogue, which took up the yoke of the law but corrupted it by wantoning. Whence: "Ephraim is a heifer taught to love to tread out corn." This our David took when he joined her to himself in the testament given. She died in childbirth, because when the Word of God appeared in the flesh and preached the gospel, when she ought to have brought forth the offspring of good works through faith, scandalized at his passion she brought eternal death on herself.
3.4:
**“IN HEBRON, WHERE”** — What is understood by the reign of David in Hebron or in Jerusalem we touched on in expounding the book of Kings.
**“So six sons were born to him in Hebron, where he reigned seven years and six months.”** — It is written in what follows: all the time that David reigned was forty years; he reigned in Hebron seven years, in Jerusalem thirty-three. Whence it is asked why forty years and six months are not numbered in the sum. The Hebrews say that David fled from Absalom his son for six months, and these were rightly excluded from the sum of his reign. They also say that for six months in Hebron he laboured with sickness of body, and therefore they are not rightly counted in the reign. For they say he reigned in Hebron from the time when, having conquered the Amalecites, he sent of their spoils to the ancients of Juda, namely to those who were in Hebron and others.
3.5: **“And these were born to him in Jerusalem: Simmaa, and Sobab, and Nathan, and Solomon, four of Bethsabee”** — otherwise Bethsabee
3.7: **“and Eliphaleth, and Noge, and Nepheg, and Japhia,”** — these two are not numbered in the book of Kings
3.9:
**“All these the sons of David,”** — because all the sons of Christ await the eternal palm
**“ALL THESE THE SONS OF DAVID”** — Because all the sons of Christ await the eternal palm; but the sons of the concubines are excepted, who did not deserve to be numbered by name among the rest. For Jews, heretics or schismatics cannot have a share in this fellowship. For the glory of the heavenly kingdom awaits only the sons of David of the noble marriage. For the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the free woman.
3.10: **“And Solomon's son was”** — he numbers the generation of David by the succession of the kings up to the transmigration of Babylon, as in the book of Kings
3.15: **“AND THE SONS OF JOSIAS”** — RABANUS. Four sons of Josias are read here, but at the end of this book and in the book of Kings, where the succession of the kings is, only three are numbered: the first Joathan [so the edition], the second Eliacim, whom Nechao king of Egypt, changing his name, called Joakim, the third Sedecias. Johanan and Sellum are not read there. Whence the Hebrews think that Johanan the firstborn son of Josias was called Joachaz and Sellum. Whence Jeremias: "Thus saith the Lord God to Sellum the son of Josias the king of Juda, who went forth out of this place: He shall return hither no more" etc. For Sellum is interpreted 'carried over'. And as to his saying that Jechonias and Sedecias were born of Joakim: Jechonias is the same as Joachin, who after his father Joakim reigned in Jerusalem three months and ten days. But Joakim, who is also Eliacim, Nabuchodonosor led in chains to Babylon with part of the vessels of the house of the Lord, with whom Ezechiel, still a boy, was carried away, as Josephus testifies; Daniel too and Ananias and Azarias and Misael, as is shown at the beginning of Daniel. Though some affirm that they were carried away with Jechonias the son of Joakim, because Nabuchodonosor carried him too to Babylon with the rest of the vessels of the Lord, and the treasures of the king's house, and the king's mother, and his eunuchs, and the judges of the land, and all the strong men of the army, ten thousand; in whose place was substituted Mathathias, who is also Sedecias, his uncle, the son of Josias, who likewise was carried away to the Chaldeans.
3.17: **“ASIR, SALATHIEL, PHADAIA”** — These are the names of one man, as the Hebrews will have it: he is Phadaia, the father of Zorobabel and Semei. Whence in Esdras and in Matthew Zorobabel is written [son] of Salathiel. And Phadaia is interpreted 'redeemed of the Lord', Asir 'imprisoned', Salathiel 'shrub of the Lord', all of which suit the holy teachers, by whose office the ecclesiastical people is begotten; who, chastened by various afflictions, redeemed by the grace of the Lord, bring forth the buds of virtues both in themselves and in those under them.
3.18: **“SENNESER”** — He is Sassabasar, to whom Cyrus numbered out the vessels of the house of the Lord, as is said in Esdras. And Senneser is 'fashioned', Sassabasar 'troubled', which fit the keepers of the vessels of God, that is, of holy souls; to whom Christ, whom Cyrus signified by name and by release, to whom it is said, "Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance," and who released the captivity of the human race, numbered out holy souls to be kept, which are the numbered vessels of the Lord, because "the Lord knoweth who are his."
3.21: **“And the son of Hanania was Phaltias the father of Jeseias, whose son was Raphaia. And his son was Arnan, of whom was born Obdia,”** — or Aboia
3.22:
**“And the son of Sechenia was Semeia: whose sons were Hattus,”** — or Archtus
**“and Jegaal,”** — otherwise Egiaal, otherwise Joagal
**“and Baria, and Naaria, and Saphat, six in number.”** — the sons of Semechia with their father Semeia; for his sons are only five
3.24: **“And the sons of Elioenai: Oduia, and Eliasub, and Pheleia, and Accub, and Johanan, and Dalaia, and Anani,”** — or Anani

4.1: **“The sons of Juda: Phares, Hesron, and Charmi, and Hur, and Sobal.”** — How are Phares and Esrom and the three who follow said to be sons of Juda, when elsewhere we read Phares and Zara as sons of Juda, [and] Esrom as son of Phares? But the Hebrews assert that the same sons of Juda whom Scripture elsewhere names by other names are expressed here with names changed. For they say that Phares, which is interpreted 'division', has his proper name here; but that Esrom is Zara, and Esrom is interpreted 'court', Zara 'rising'; Charmi too is Heber, for Charmi is interpreted 'my vineyard', Her 'watching'. And they say Ur is Onam, and Ur is interpreted 'left', Onam 'murmuring'; and Sobal is Sela, the youngest of the sons of Juda whom Sue bore him. And Sobal is interpreted 'ear of corn' or 'vain old age', Sela 'sent' or 'his shadow'.
4.2: **“And Reaia the son of Sobal begot Jahath, of whom were born Ahumai, and Laad.”** — otherwise Alech
4.3:
**“And this is the stock of Etam: Jezrahel,”** — from whom the city of Jezrahel
**“and Jesema, and Jedebos. And the name of their sister was Asalelphuni.”** — ASALEL. RABANUS. They suspect that this is the mother of Samson, born of the stock of Juda, whose husband Manue, of the tribe of Dan, is read in the book of Judges to have been of Saraa.
4.4:
**“And Phanuel the father of Gedor, and Ezer”** — otherwise Ozer
**“GEDOR, AND EZER”** — RABANUS. They are places possessed by the sons of Hur; but it is strange that here they call Hur the father of Bethlehem, when above Salma was called its father; unless perhaps here he calls 'father' an ancestor, because Hur was the father of Salma, who was the father of Bethlehem.
**“These are the sons of Hur the firstborn”** — of the sister of Moses and Aaron
4.5: **“And Assur”** — the son of Hesron and Abia, the brother of Caleb
4.6: **“And Naara bore him Oozam, and Hepher,”** — otherwise Opher
4.8: **“And Cos begot Anob, and Soboba, and the kindred of Aharehel”** — otherwise Aral
4.9:
**“And Jabes was more honourable than his brethren,”** — because our Redeemer stood out above all the height of the saints by the power of his virtue. Whence: "Thou art beautiful above the sons of men" etc., and: "God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows."
**“AND JABES WAS”** — RABANUS. The order seems confused, because, having numbered the sons of Halaa and Naara, he suddenly brings in the kindred of Aharehel the son of Arum, and next tells of Jabes. But the Hebrews say that Assur begot Ethan of Halaa, and he Cos, and Cos Soboba, and Soboba Jabes, who was the teacher of the scribes. Between Cos and Jabes are inserted the kindreds of Aharehel (or Aharahel, otherwise Aral), because he is Obab the son of Aram, that is, Jethro the kinsman of Moses; and because Jabes taught them, they are inserted in his progeny as if born of his forefathers.
**“AND HIS MOTHER”** — [His mother is] the Synagogue, of which Christ was born, who bore him in sorrow, because she grieved at his coming on account of unbelief. Whence the Jews, envying, said: "If we let him alone so, all will believe in him."
4.10: **“AND JABES CALLED UPON”** — This fits Christ, whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world; of whom it is said: "Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world" etc. Him God blessed well with the multiplication of sons, whom holy Church brings forth through the water of baptism. He enlarged his borders, because he gave him the inheritance of all nations and extended his possession to the ends of the earth. With him was the hand of the Lord, because the power of the Godhead did works of power and miracles through him: "He too is the power of God and the wisdom," through whom the Father founded all things that are in heaven and on earth; whom the malice of the Jews could not harm, who says of himself: "The prince of this world cometh, and in me he hath not any thing." Through him too are blessed his members, that is, the Church, to whom it is said through Isaias: "Enlarge the place of thy tent" etc. With her is the hand of the Lord, because the Son of God, who is the arm and right hand of the Father, works in her, "and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it," nor shall the devil have dominion over her, because "power is given over all the might of the enemy."
4.11: **“AND CALEB THE BROTHER”** — RABANUS. We read above that Caleb was the son of Hesron, whose brothers were Ram and Jerameel. The Hebrews therefore say that Ram, Caleb's brother, is here called Sua. And Ram is interpreted 'lofty', Sua 'humble', which fits the Jewish people, because it was lofty in the worship of the one God and the power of the kingdom; but because it would not receive the Son of God, it was made humble and vile, that the first may become last.
4.12:
**“And Esthon begot Bethrapha, and Phesse, and Tehinna the father of the city of Naas:”** — namely Bethlehem, or of the mother of Isai, who elsewhere is called Naias
**“RECHA”** — RABANUS. Some think David is named by the name Recha. For Recha is 'tender'. Whence David says of himself: "I am tender, and anointed king." He too is said to be tender as the little worm of the wood. And they are called the men of Recha because they are noted here to set out the genealogy of David.
4.13: **“And the sons of Cenez were Othoniel, and Saraia. And the sons of Othoniel, Hathath.”** — or Atthat
4.14: **“AND SARAIA BEGOT JOAB”** — From Saraia Joab is said to have come, who, according to the interpretation of the name, [is] father of the valley of craftsmen, because of his sons were the architects who built the house of the Lord. And the craftsmen who dwell in the valley can be called the teachers of the law, whom "knowledge doth not puff up, but charity edifieth," whom modesty and humility exalt, as Gamaliel and Paul his disciple.
4.17:
**“EZRA”** — RABANUS. JEROME. The Hebrews say that Ezra, which is interpreted 'helper', is Amram the father of Moses and Aaron; [that] Jether, that is, 'help', is Aaron; and Mered, which [is] 'rebelling', is Moses; Epher too, or Opher, that is, 'dust', was Eldad, and Jalon Medad, who were two of the seventy elders whom Moses received from God for help in ruling the people. For they hand down that Moses, after receiving the law in the desert, persuaded his father to put away his mother, because she was his aunt, for she was the daughter of Levi; after which Amram married another, from whom he had Eldad and Medad.
**“AND HE BEGOT MARIAM”** — RABANUS. They want Moses to be understood by Sammai, which is interpreted 'heavenly'; Jesba [is] Aaron, which is interpreted 'praise', the father of Esthamo, that is, 'of abiding fire', because the sons of Aaron burnt the sacrifices with fire. And the names that follow in a row are all names of Moses, understood according to his various acts: he is called Jared, that is, 'descending', because he came down from the mountain with the tables of stone; father of Gedor, that is, 'of a hedge', because he surrounded the people with the law as with a hedge; Heber, that is, 'victor', because he joined the people to the service of God; father of Socho, that is, 'of prophecy', because he was the teacher of the prophets; Icuthiel, that is, 'hoping in God', because he had hope of freeing the people from Egypt; father of Zanoe, which is interpreted 'governor', because he governed the people in the desert and governs them daily by his teaching.
4.18:
**“And his wife Judaia”** — they say this is Jochabed, the mother of Moses and Aaron
**“OF THE DAUGHTER OF PHARAO”** — RABANUS. He calls the mother of Moses the daughter of Pharao, who also, according to the proper meaning of the name, is called 'daughter of the Lord', namely because she had a good will in nursing the child; and she is said to have been taken by Mered, that is, Moses, because, leaving idols, she was converted to the worship of God.
4.19:
**“And the sons of his wife Odaia”** — otherwise Odaia
**“the sister of Naham the father of Ceila, Garmi, and Estamo”** — or Eschamoa
4.20: **“The sons also of Simon, Amnon, and Rinna the son of Hanan, and Thilon.”** — otherwise Ethilon
4.21:
**“The sons of Sela the son of Juda: Her”** — he is set here in memory of the former name of him who was struck by the Lord for his impiety
**“HER THE FATHER”** — RABANUS. He returns to the progeny of Phares, from which David sprang, to finish the progeny of Juda, from which the royal tribe arose, in David. For they hand down that this was Elimelech, the husband of Noemi, in whose time, because of the transgressors of the law, the sun stood still, that, seeing the miracle, they might be converted to the Lord; and because they despised it the famine grew strong, and he who seemed foremost in the tribe of Juda, driven from his country by want with his wife and sons, died with his sons in a strange land.
**“the father of Maresa,”** — who with Beseleel completed the work of the tabernacle
**“and the kindred of the house of them that wrought fine linen in the house of oath.”** — in the tabernacle of the covenant
4.22:
**“SECURE AND GOING”** — RABANUS. Mahalon and Chelion, who here are called 'secure' and 'going', were in Moab, because they married Moabite wives. Whence in the Hebrew they are called not princes but husbands, as the teachers of that tongue hand down.
**“and who returned into Lahem.”** — bread
**“Now these are old words.”** — because this history is written in Ruth
**“WHO RETURNED”** — Noemi and Ruth, who returned to Bethlehem, having heard of the abundance of bread.
4.23:
**“POTTERS DWELLING”** — By the potters who labour in plantations and hedges we understand the teachers who form and put together the vessels of the Lord; for we say 'fingere', to fashion, for 'componere', to put together; whence we call the fashioners of clay potters. These plant and cultivate the vineyard of the Lord by doctrine, defend it by exhorting and praying. These abide with the king in his works, because, remaining in the faith of Christ, whatever they say, whatever they do, they do for the glory of God.
**“DWELLING IN PLANTATIONS”** — The progeny of Ruth, which is said to have dwelt in the hedges and plantations themselves, when this planting came to royal dignity and the defence of the people.
**“and in hedges, with the king for his works.”** — because from them king David sprang, whose works are extolled with exceeding praises
**“and they abode there.”** — in Bethlehem
**“AND THEY ABODE THERE. THE SONS OF SIMEON”** — In Genesis six are written, but here Sober is passed over, because there is no progeny of him. But certain names are changed for their own reasons. For in Genesis Gemuel, that is, 'sea of God'; here Nabuel, that is, 'reading with God'. One in Genesis is called Echa, here Jarib, that is, 'striving', because from him came Zambri, who, committing fornication with the Madianite woman, was slain by Phinees the priest. Jachim in Genesis, that is, 'preparation', here is named Zara, that is, 'rising'.
4.27: **“AND ALL THEIR KINDRED COULD NOT EQUAL”** — Because Simeon did not have as great offspring as Juda. Whence in Josue it is said that Simeon received his inheritance by his kindreds in the midst of the children of Juda.
4.28: **“And they dwelt”** — these cities for the most part belong to the tribe of Juda
4.30: **“And in Bathuel, and in Horma, and in Siceleg,”** — or Siccileg
4.31: **“THESE WERE THEIR CITIES”** — Because Siceleg and Bersabee, which were Juda's and had been seized by Simeon, returned under David to the former inheritance of Juda.
4.33: **“and all their villages round about these cities as far as Baal.”** — a place which elsewhere [is] Cariathbaal
4.38: **“THESE WERE NAMED PRINCES”** — The stock of Simeon and their acts having been described, it is mystically signified that the holy teachers, that is, the princes of the Church, providing pastures for the flocks of Christ, set out into Gador or Gader, which is interpreted 'his hedge'. This is the Church, which is the defence of the faithful; there are pastures as far as the east of the valley, that is, the incarnation of the Word, who "emptied himself, taking the form of a servant." In him are found pastures. For he himself says: "By me, if any man enter in, he shall go in, and go out, and shall find pastures," namely the virtues. In him is a land most broad and quiet, that is, the abundant grace of the Holy Spirit, in which those of the stock of Cham had dwelt before; it signifies that the multitude of the gentiles left idols and flocked to the worship of the one God. These, then, whose names we have written above, came in the days of Ezechias king of Juda, that is, at the coming of Christ. For he is Christ the power of God, whom Ezechias, namely 'strength of the Lord', signifies. They destroyed their tents etc. He strikes by faith the tents of the impious and the inhabitants of the impious when, denying all impiety and worldly desires, he is washed from the filth of sins through the baptism of Christ, afterwards striving to live soberly, justly and piously in this world, that what is written may come to pass: and it shall be in the place where it was said: "You are not my people," there they shall be called the sons of God.
4.39:
**“And they went forth to enter into Gador as far as”** — otherwise: into
**“the east side of the valley, to seek pastures for their flocks.”** — or sheep
4.41: **“These therefore whose names are written above, came in the days of Ezechias king of Juda: and they destroyed their tents, and the inhabitants that were found there, and utterly destroyed them unto”** — or to
4.42: **“FIVE HUNDRED MEN”** — [They are] the fathers of the new Testament, who went into mount Seir and smote the remnant of the Amalecites, because, trampling on the pride of this world, they crush the deformity of vices. These are said to be four, because, truly instructed by gospel doctrine, they wage spiritual war fittingly against the demons. The remnant of the Amalecites being smitten, they dwelt there, because, the demons being driven out, they put virtues in the place of vices, the possession of which makes a man blessed unto this day; which can always be said until the end of the world, because the Church remains until the end of the world, in which the ancient enemy is daily triumphed over.

5.1: **“Now the sons of Ruben the firstborn of Israel, (for he was his firstborn: but forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his first birthright was given to the sons of Joseph the son of Israel, and he was not accounted for the firstborn.”** — BUT FORASMUCH AS HE DEFILED THE BED etc. The birthright was therefore taken from Ruben, because "he slept with Bala the concubine of his father." And it was given to Joseph, the younger son, whose progeny is multiplied and excels in power of kingdom among the ten tribes. But mystically it signifies the ruin of the former people, which as firstborn ought to have received the priesthood and the kingdom; but because it defiled its father's bed, that is, hung on the cross and killed the body of Christ, in which was "the fulness of the Godhead," the dignity of the firstborn was transferred to the spiritual Joseph, that is, to Christ and the people of the Church, to whom the Father [says]: "Thou art a priest for ever according to the order of Melchisedech."
5.2:
**“But Juda,”** — Christ, of whom: "The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations"
**“who was the strongest”** — because "God hath anointed him with the oil of gladness above" etc.
**“among his brethren, of his stock princes”** — the apostles and teachers of the new Testament, of whom it is said: "Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: thou shalt make them princes over all the earth"
**“sprung: but the birthright was accounted to Joseph.)”** — the dignity of the firstborn and the sovereignty of the kingdom belong to Christ, who is "the firstborn of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth"
5.6: **“Beera his son,”** — they say this is the father of Osee the prophet, whom the king of the Assyrians took captive with the ten tribes
5.10: **“AGAINST THE AGARENS”** — It is likely that Agar was Cethura, since in what follows he says that "the Rubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasses" fought with the Agarens, and that the Itureans, Napheans and Nodab, sons of Ismael, gave them help. And Nodab, it seems, is the one called Cedma in Genesis, that is, 'of the ancients' or 'going before'.
5.14:
**“These were the sons of Abihail, the son of Huri, the son of Jara,”** — otherwise: Jora, otherwise: Joara
**“the son of Galaad, the son of Michael, the son of Jesesi, the son of Jeddo,”** — otherwise: Jeddu, otherwise: Geddo
5.15: **“the brethren also, the sons of Abdiel, the son of Guni,”** — or Goni
5.20: **“gave them help. And the Agareans were delivered into their hands, and all that were with them, for they called upon God in the battle: and he heard them, because they had believed in him.”** — while the children of Israel served God, they had him propitious and a defender against their enemies; but when, leaving him, they worshipped idols, they felt him an avenger whom they had had as protector
5.22:
**“And many fell down wounded, for it was the battle of the Lord.”** — that is, carried through to the destruction of the enemies by God's help
**“And they dwelt in their stead until the captivity.”** — namely until they were delivered to the Assyrians for their sins
5.24:
**“And these were the heads of the house of their kindred: Epher, and Jesi, and Eliel, and Ezriel,”** — otherwise: Zerihel
**“and Jeremias, and Odoia,”** — or Odoia
5.26:
**“And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Phul king of the Assyrians,”** — AND THE GOD OF ISRAEL STIRRED UP etc. It is to be noted that in Kings it is said that Phul king of the Assyrians received a thousand talents of silver from Manahem the son of Gaddi king of Israel, to be his help and strengthen his kingdom, not that he carried him over to the Assyrians; and that Theglathphalasar king of Assur in the days of Phacee king of Israel took Ahion, and Abel the house of Macha, and Janoe, and Cedes, and Asor, and Galaad, and Galilee, and all the land of Neptalim, and carried them over to the Assyrians. Lastly it relates that Salmanasar king of the Assyrians, besieging Samaria three years, took Osee the son of Ela, king of Israel, and carried Israel over to the Assyrians, and placed them in Hayla and in Abor by the river Goram [so the edition], in the cities of the Medes. Whence it is asked how in Paralipomenon we say that Phul and Theglathphalasar, kings of the Assyrians, carried Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses to Hayla and Abor and Aram and the river Gozan, when Malachim relates that Salmanasar did this, who carried Israel over to the Assyrians and placed them in the aforesaid places. But the former kings of the Assyrians are said to have done this because they began with the Assyrian nation what that same nation completed in their successors. Aram, which Paralipomenon mentions, Malachim passes over. The Hebrews suppose it to be a city [so the edition: 'reges civitatem'] of the Medes.
**“and the spirit of Theglathphalnasar king of Assur: and he carried away Ruben, and Gad, and the half tribe of Manasses, and brought them to Lahela,”** — or Ala

6.4: **“Eleazar begot Phinees, and Phinees”** — or Finees
6.6:
**“Ozi begot Zaraias,”** — or Zarazam
**“and Zaraias”** — or Zarazas
6.9: **“JOHANAN”** — The other sons of Levi who likewise were priests in the house of the Lord being passed over, Johanan is especially praised, because he manfully withstood king Ozias when he would sacrifice by himself, and with constancy of mind and zeal for the law fulfilled the office of a priest.
6.15: **“NOW JOSEDEC”** — They say Josedec is Esdras the priest, who, returning from Babylon with Zorobabel and the sons of Juda, restored the temple of the Lord and the city of Jerusalem; which he seems to show in his book when he says: "After these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of the Persians, Esdras the son of Saraias, the son of Azarias, the son of Helchias, the son of Sellum, the son of Sadoc, the son of Achitob, the son of Amarias, the son of Azarias, the son of Maraioth, the son of Zaraias, the son of Ozi, the son of Bocci, the son of Abisue, the son of Phinees, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron." They also hand down that Esdras is Malachias the prophet, because he also records here many things which are contained in his book, saying: "The lips of the priest shall keep knowledge, and they shall seek the law at his mouth" etc. Others assert that Josedec is the father of Jesus the high priest, but that Esdras is a priest, a just and glorious man.
6.17:
**“And these are the names of the sons of Gerson:”** — of these in Numbers
**“Lobni”** — or Lobni
6.19:
**“The sons of Merari: Moholi and Musi.”** — or Mosi
**“And these are the kindreds”** — or kindreds
6.20: **“Of Gerson: Lobni”** — or Lobni, or Lobena
6.28:
**“The sons of Samuel: the firstborn Vasseni,”** — who in the Book of Kings [is] Joel
**“ABIA”** — This man, as the Hebrews hand down, when appointed judge took gifts, which Joel, who is also Vasseni, his elder son, knowing it, did not correct. Therefore both are said to have sinned, according to the Hebrews. Whence: "And it came to pass, when Samuel was old, that he appointed his sons to be judges over Israel" etc.
6.29: **“And the sons of Merari, Moholi: Lobni”** — or Lobeni
6.31: **“THESE ARE THEY WHOM”** — By anticipation, while he was telling their genealogy, he touched beforehand on the offices of the singers of David who sang praises to God on musical instruments; but in its own order he will show how they did it.
6.34: **“the son of Elcana, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Thohu,”** — or Thau
6.35: **“the son of Suph, the son of Elcana, the son of Joel, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,”** — otherwise: Masai
6.39: **“And his brother Asaph,”** — by kindred; for Scripture calls near kinsmen brothers
6.44: **“ETHAN THE SON OF CUSI”** — Ethan [was] one of the three singers who sounded the praise of God on cymbals before David. And it is to be noted that as there were three sons of Levi, Caath, Gerson and Merari, so [there were] three singers: Heman of Caath, Asaph of Gerson, Ethan of Merari. But mystically it signifies the holy teachers who, imbued with the faith of the holy Trinity, according to the dispensation of the true David announce the preaching of the gospel to the whole world.
6.48: **“Their brethren also the Levites, who were appointed for all the ministry of the tabernacle of the house of the Lord.”** — THE LEVITES WHO WERE APPOINTED etc. Because every ecclesiastical order, according to the tradition of the apostles, and those who hold the primacy, carry out the whole ministry in the Church of God. Whence: "That thou mayst know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God" etc.
6.49: **“AARON”** — [Aaron] signifies Christ; his sons, the people of the Church, to whom it is said: "You are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood" etc.; whom the high priest taught to offer upon the altar of faith the holocaust of good works and the incense of prayer, and to pray for Israel, that is, for the state of the Church, according to the precepts of the law given through Moses. And he repeats the genealogy of Aaron as far as Achimaas, which seems to have been done for his praise, because he was faithful to David in all things.
6.66: **“And to them”** — otherwise: and of these
6.70: **“And out of the half tribe of Manasses, Aner and its suburbs, Baalam”** — otherwise: Baalam
6.78: **“Beyond the Jordan also over against Jericho, on the east side of the Jordan, out of the tribe of Ruben, Bosor in the wilderness with its suburbs, and Jassa”** — or Jassa

7.1: **“Now the sons of Issachar were Thola, and Phua, Jasub, and Simeron,”** — otherwise: Samrom
7.2: **“The sons of Thola: Ozi, and Raphaia, and Jeriel,”** — otherwise: Hieriel
7.3:
**“The sons of Ozi: Izrahia, of whom were born Michael, and Obadia, and Joel, and Jesia,”** — otherwise: Isai
**“five all great men.”** — counting the father, who was the only son of his father
7.8: **“And the sons of Bechor were Zamira, and Joas, and Eliezer, and Elioenai, and Amai, and Jerimoth, and Abia, and Anathoth, and Almath: all these were the sons of Bechor.”** — ALL THESE WERE THE SONS. Wherever it is written in the law, "All these [were] the sons" of this man or that, it is either for the excellence of their merits or for the worsening of their merits, so that they are said to be the sons of him whose imitators they were.
7.10:
**“And the son of Jadihel:”** — otherwise: Jadihel
**“Balan. And the sons of Balan: Jehus and Benjamin”** — from whom came forth the Benjamites who by abominable lying with her killed the wife of the Levite
**“and Aod, and Chanana, and Zethan”** — otherwise: Jona
7.11: **“All these were sons of Jadihel,”** — or: Jedihel
7.12: **“Sepham also and Hapham the sons of Hir: and Hasim the sons of Aher.”** — otherwise: Aser
7.13: **“And the sons of Nephtali were Jasiel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Sellum, sons of Bala.”** — the concubine of Jacob, the handmaid of Rachel, the mother of Nephtali, from whom these were begotten
7.14: **“And the son of Manasses, Ezriel: and his concubine the Syrian bore Machir the father of Galaad.”** — AND HIS CONCUBINE etc. She is said to have been the daughter of a son of Balan, who, brought into Egypt by her father to be sold when famine compelled, was mercifully received in marriage by Manasses, who was over the granaries, food being given to her father.
7.15:
**“And Machir took wives for his sons Happhim,”** — otherwise Happhim
**“and Saphan: and he had a sister named Maacha: the name of the second was Salphaad, and Salphaad had daughters.”** — who in the Book of Numbers ask of Moses an inheritance among their brethren
**“HAPPHIM AND SAPHAN”** — These two names are said to be those of the first son of Machir; but [they say] the second is Salphaat, and their sister Maacha, whom Esrom took to wife when he was sixty years old, who bore him a son Segub, as was said above.
7.16: **“And Maacha the wife of Machir bore a son, and she called his name Phares: and the name of his brother was Sares: and his sons were Ulam and Recen.”** — otherwise Reben
7.18: **“AND HIS SISTER”** — The sister of Ulam the son of Phares, the son of Machir, as was said before. Some hand down that she was the mother of Jesus the son of Nave, who is called 'goodly man' for the distinction of his virtue and leadership. Others say [she was] Debbora the prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth.
7.20:
**“And the sons of Ephraim were Suthala, Bared his son, Thahath his son, Elada”** — otherwise: Eladan
**“his son, Thahath”** — otherwise Thaath
**“his son, and his son Zabad,”** — otherwise Zadaph
**“AND THE SONS OF EPHRAIM”** — The Hebrews tell the tale that the sons of Ephraim, gathering a multitude while their father was living, tried to return to the land of promise and were slain in Geth of the Philistines. Hence the other tribes are led through the desert, lest they should see the bones of their brethren; and in the psalm it is said: "The sons of Ephrem turned back in the day of battle."
7.22: **“And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came”** — the patriarchs who still survived, or kinsmen, who are often called brothers
7.29: **“And by the borders of the sons of Manasses Bethsan and her daughters, Thanach”** — otherwise Thanaz
7.30: **“The children of Aser were Jemna,”** — otherwise Jemna
7.32: **“And Heber begot Jephlat, and Somer, and Hotham,”** — otherwise Jotham

8.2: **“Nohaa”** — otherwise: Nabua
8.4: **“And Abisue, and Naaman, and Ahoe,”** — otherwise Achoe

**“These are the sons of Ahod,”** — otherwise: Aoth
**“heads of kindreds that dwelt in Gabaa, who were removed to Manahath.”**
• a sepulchre

8.7:
**“And Naaman,”** — otherwise: Nooman
**“and Achia”** — otherwise Haia

**“And he begot of Hodes his wife, Jobab, and Sebia, and Mosa,”** — or: Mosa

8.10: **“And Jehus, and Sechia, and Marma.”** — otherwise: Marmath

**“And the sons of Elphaal, Heber, and Misaam, and Samad:”** — otherwise: Samad
