**“And David could not”** — as was commanded in the law; but he had not the time to go there, or perhaps it did not come into his mind
**“go to the altar there to pray to God: for he was seized with an exceeding great fear, seeing the sword of the angel of the Lord.”** — the stroke of death brought on by the ministry of the angel, as was done in Egypt

22.1: **“Then David said: This is the house of God, and this is the altar for the holocaust of Israel.”** — he thought this was the place in which Abraham sacrificed the ram for his son
22.2:
**“And he commanded to gather together all the proselytes of the land of Israel, and he appointed of them hewers of stones to cut and polish them, to build the house of the Lord.”** — or of God
**“TO GATHER TOGETHER”** — From the Church Christ chose the craftsmen of his house, who should hew and polish the rough manners of men, so that in the spiritual building they might fit together with him through the various joinings of faith and charity. Whence: "For this reason have I hewed them by the prophets, I have slain them by the words of my mouth" etc.
22.3:
**“IRON”** — He ordered the firmness of faith by sacred doctrines, so that those entering the Church might be pierced through with the goads of fear, and so be bound to one another by the faith of love and fellowship. Whence: "Pierce thou my flesh with thy fear." And elsewhere: "Jerusalem, which is built as a city, which is compact together" [so the edition: 'cuius participatio eius in'] etc.
**“OF BRASS”** — The resounding readings and spiritual songs which the holy fathers prepared for the instruction of the Church for Christ the true peacemaker.
22.4:
**“CEDAR TREES”** — Men renowned for virtues, whom they set forth as an example or inserted in their Scriptures.
**“THE SIDONIANS AND TYRIANS”** — Because through the preachers who were chosen from the gentiles such men came to the knowledge of the Church.
22.5:
**“IS A CHILD AND TENDER”** — In the time of the old Testament the knowledge of the incarnation of Christ was obscure, and the number of the faithful, who are the members of Christ, was small.
**“HE PREPARED MATERIALS”** — Moses prepared the charges of the house of the Lord, saying: "And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee, but that thou fear the Lord thy God, and walk in his ways" etc., and in other like things.
22.8: **“THOU HAST SHED MUCH BLOOD”** — It signifies that the Jews, because of the carnal observance of the law and their bloody works, could not prepare a spiritual building for the Lord. Or because they had hands polluted with the blood of Christ and of the prophets. Whence: "Jerusalem, that killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee" etc.
22.9:
**“The son”** — Christ
**“that shall be born to thee”** — of thy seed
**“shall be a most quiet man: for I will make him rest from all his enemies round about: and therefore he shall be called Peaceable:”** — "In his days shall justice spring up, and abundance of peace"
**“and peace”** — "For he is our peace"
22.10:
**“He shall build a house”** — the Church
**“to my name, and he shall be my son, and I will be a father to him.”** — "He shall cry out to me: Thou art my father; and I will make him my firstborn"
22.14:
**“Behold I in my poverty”** — it signifies the poverty of the letter of the law; for "the law, having a shadow of the good things to come", brought nothing to perfection
**“have prepared the charges of the house of the Lord, of gold a hundred thousand talents,”** — by perfect numbers perfection is designated
**“OF GOLD”** — The fathers of the old Testament put into their Scriptures depth of sense and beauty of speech.
**“and of silver a million of talents: but of brass, and of iron, there is no weight,”** — because the firmness of the divine testimonies is beyond reckoning; whence: "Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away"
**“for the greatness of the number exceedeth it: timber”** — those lifted up in mind
**“and stones”** — those stony in hardness
**“OF TALENTS”** — The talent excels the other weights and signifies the greatness and perfection of a thing.
22.15: **“ARTIFICERS”** — The preachers, who are called hewers of stone, masons and craftsmen in wood, and in many other ways, because the teaching of the preachers is shaped according to the quality of the hearers. For the wise are to be taught in one way, the foolish in another, the proud in one way, the humble in another.
22.17: **“DAVID ALSO COMMANDED ALL THE PRINCES TO HELP”** — It signifies that the law and the prophets teach with firm authority that those who hold the first place in the Church in holiness and virtue should help the true Solomon in his building, namely by teaching and working. Whence: "Adore ye the Lord in his holy court."
22.18:
**“Saying: You see that the Lord your God is with you, and hath given you rest round about, and hath delivered all into”** — or hands
**“your hand”** — or your
22.19:
**“Give therefore your hearts and your souls, and”** — otherwise: that
**“seek the Lord your God: and arise, and build a sanctuary to the Lord God,”** — "The temple of God is holy, which you are"
**“A SANCTUARY”** — "The soul of the just is the seat of wisdom." In this house the ark rests, that is, the faith of the incarnation of Christ.

23.1: **“SO DAVID BEING OLD”** — After the fulfilment of the old Testament followed the incarnation of the Saviour, of whose kingdom there shall be no end. Whence: "When the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son."
23.2: **“And he gathered together all the princes of Israel, and the priests, and the Levites.”** — the several orders of divers offices are gathered to the office of Christ
23.3: **“And the Levites were numbered from twenty [so the edition] years old and upward, and there were found thirty-eight thousand men.”** — THE LEVITES WERE NUMBERED. Those who discharge the ministry of the Lord ought to keep the faith of the holy Trinity and the fulfilment of the commandments. Whence: There were found thirty-eight thousand men. For whoever serves God with sound faith and right work to the end will come to the grace of the resurrection and the eternal blessedness which are signified in the eight.
23.4:
**“TWENTY-FOUR THOUSAND”** — Because true ministers of the light ought to be instant and not turn aside from the way of justice. For in twenty-four hours the whole world is lit round its circle and the shadow of darkness is driven out. Hence seventy-two disciples were sent to preach, because the faith of the holy Trinity with the works of light suffices for justice; for three twenties and four threes make seventy-two. By which number the diversity of tongues and the series of the books of both Testaments is comprised.
**“OF OVERSEERS”** — Because no one ought to seek the dignity of this order but he who urges toward perfection and doctrine. For the world was made in the number six, and man was created on the sixth day, on which also he was redeemed.
23.5: **“And four thousand porters,”** — for he who wishes to do the office of porter or psalmist worthily ought to keep the gospel teaching
23.6: **“AND DAVID DISTRIBUTED THEM”** — Because the law and the prophets instil the faith of the holy Trinity and the carrying out of the virtues in those who have been taken up through grace and added to the number of the faithful. For Levi is interpreted 'added' or 'taken up'; Gerson, 'a stranger there' or 'their casting out'; Caath, 'grinding teeth' or 'patient'; Merari, 'embittering' or 'bitterness'. For he who through grace has been taken up and added to the faithful ought to cast out all the uncleanness of vices, that he may become a stranger and pilgrim; then he should have discernment of morals and bear his life to heavenly things on the four-horse chariot of the virtues, which are prudence, justice, fortitude, temperance; and should patiently bear all things, bitter and angry at his own sins.
23.13:
**“The sons of Amram: Aaron”** — Christ
**“and Moses. And Aaron was separated”**
• Christ
• coming of himself to God, ever coming to intercede for us
**“to minister”** — because he alone [is] "without sin"
**“in the holy of holies,”** — because he "hath passed into the heavens"
**“he and his sons”** — the members of Christ
**“for ever, and to burn incense before the Lord according to his rite,”** — that is, of prayer; whence: "Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight"
23.14: **“The sons also of Moses”** — because many of the former people belong to the priesthood of the Church
23.24: **“These are the sons of Levi by their kindreds and families, chiefs by their courses, and the number of every head, who did the works of the ministry of the house of the Lord from twenty years old and upward.”** — those who minister in the house of the Lord ought to keep the decalogue in the two precepts of charity, and to carry out their office according to them
23.25: **“For David said: The Lord God of Israel hath given rest to his people, and a habitation in Jerusalem for ever.”** — FOR DAVID SAID etc. While the children of Israel were in the desert and were conquering the land of Chanaan, the tabernacle was carried through divers places; but when the temple was built, change of place was not necessary. So too the worship of the old Testament was changeable through various figures, but the gospel stable and fixed.
23.28:
**“And they shall be under the hand of the sons of Aaron for the service of the house of the Lord, in the porches,”** — the porch [vestibulum] is so called because it clothes [vestiat] the doors of the temple or of any building
**“AND THEY SHALL BE UNDER THE HAND OF THE SONS”** — That the lesser may learn to obey the greater, and the greater, helped by the lesser, may fulfil their office more worthily, as is done in the Church today.
**“IN THE CHAMBERS”** — That is, the chambers or rooms in which the Levites and priests dwell. They too, the ministers of the true temple, ought to watch the entrance diligently, to let in the worthy and drive back the unworthy.
23.29: **“FOR THE FINE FLOUR THAT IS FRIED”** — That is, the ears of the firstfruits, which were parched, and the grains eaten, which they commonly call graneas. In some copies it is had: For the fine flour that is fried; in others: For the frying only; but in the Hebrew it is had: For parching.
23.30:
**“And the Levites”** — the priests do the aforesaid things
**“are to stand in the morning to give thanks, and to sing praises to the Lord:”** — morning and evening the continual sacrifice was made
**“and in like manner in the evening,”** — so the ministers of the Church ought always and everywhere to praise God

24.2: **“AND ELEAZAR DID THE OFFICE OF THE PRIESTHOOD”** — By Eleazar, the elder son of Aaron and high priest, can be understood the priesthood of the Church and the spiritual sacrifice. For we read that bread and wine were offered by Melchisedech, in sacrifice of the body and blood of Christ, that is, as a sacrament, before the victims of cattle [were offered] by Aaron. But by Ithamar, which is interpreted 'bitter', who through David rose to the summit of Levitical honour, can be figured those who have been transferred through Christ from figurative observance to the gospel; to whom it is said: "How then art thou turned unto me into that which is good for nothing, O strange vineyard?" More were chosen of the sons of Eleazar than of the sons of Ithamar, because "many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband".
24.4: **“BY SIXTEEN FAMILIES”** — The eight is doubled. In the law carnal circumcision is celebrated on the eighth day; but in the gospel, in the present the circumcision of hearts, and in the future that of bodies.
24.5: **“And he divided both families one with another by lots: for there were princes of the sanctuary, and princes of God”** — otherwise they are excluded from the ministry of the sanctuary and the princedom of the priesthood, unless they be chosen by God
24.6: **“WROTE THEM DOWN”** — The order of preachers handles purely and sincerely, before God and men, all the mysteries that are contained in the law, and instils them into the hearers, which the names themselves show. For Semeias [is] 'hearing the Lord', Nathanael 'gift of God', Sadoc 'just', Achimelech 'my brother [is] king', Abiathar 'my father [is] superfluous'. He then who hears God, by rightly learning his law and obeying his commandments, is himself the son of the gift of God, because he has this grace from the divine gift; and as a scribe instructed in the kingdom of heaven and a minister of the true temple, he writes down the rite of the priesthood before Christ the king and the Christian people, which also can be called king, because it rules well the body of Christ and its own life. And though born of a superfluous father, he yet has priestly and royal dignity and is deservedly reckoned by the name of justice.
24.7:
**“AND THE LOT CAME FORTH”** — If any think that God is to be consulted by lots in necessity, after the example of the apostles, let them see that the apostles did this when the number of the brethren had been gathered, and after first pouring out prayers to God.
**“And the first lot came forth to Joiarib, the second to Jedei,”** — FIRST, SECOND, THIRD etc. David distributed the Levitical tribe and the priestly order into twenty-four lots, showing that the Church fully has priestly and royal dignity and perfectly keeps the doctrine of the law and of the gospel; or [showing] the perfection of work, which is commended by the six, and the brightness of the gospel preaching, which is figured by the four. For four sixes make twenty-four.
24.19: **“These are their courses according to their ministries, to enter into the house of God, and according to their rite under the hand of Aaron their father: as the Lord the God of Israel had commanded.”** — that is, of the high priest who, chosen from each lot, in the order of his course was over the lesser ones, and ministered from sabbath to sabbath

25.1: **“Moreover David and the chief officers of the army separated for the ministry the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Idithun: who should prophesy with harps, and with psalteries, and with cymbals according to their number serving in their appointed office.”** — THEY SEPARATED FOR THE MINISTRY THE SONS OF ASAPH etc. Because the true David, our king and Lord, wills that every order of the ecclesiastical ministry should do its office in the faith of the Trinity; nor can anyone praise him worthily but he who praises by the confession of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, through faith, hope and charity. For Asaph [is] 'gathering', Heman 'their heart', Idithun 'leaping over'. For he who shrewdly gathers the mysteries of divine Scripture and leaps over all desire of earthly things pays praises worthily.
25.4:
**“And of Heman: the sons of Heman, Bocciau, Mathaniau,”** — or Mathaniu
**“Oziel, Subuel, and Jerimoth, Hananias, Hanani, Eliatha, Geddelthi,”** — Geldelthi
25.7: **“ALL THE TEACHERS, TWO HUNDRED EIGHTY-EIGHT”** — These are they who today expound the canons of the divine books in the gospel sense; for four seventy-twos make two hundred and eighty [so the edition]; and that the books of the old and new Testament are seventy-two is not doubtful. Hence whoever discharges a divine office, pressing on in the four principal virtues, should apply himself to the gospel teaching, and strive to shape whatever he has learned or taught according to its rule.
25.8: **“And they cast lots by their courses equally, the great as well as the less, the learned and the unlearned together.”** — lest anyone presume either to give or to receive a degree of ecclesiastical order; whence: "Impose not hands lightly upon any man"
25.29: **“The two and twentieth to Geddelthi”** — otherwise: Godoliathi
25.30: **“The three and twentieth to Mahazioth”** — or Aziud

26.1: **“And the divisions of the porters: of the Corites, Meselemia the son of Core, of the sons of Asaph.”** — SELEMIAS. Which is interpreted 'the Lord repaying', and signifies the order of the apostles and the first teachers, to whom the eastern gate, that is, the primitive Church, is committed; to whom the promises of the ancient fathers were repaid.
26.2: **“OF ZACHARIAS”** — [Zacharias,] which is interpreted 'memory of the Lord', and signifies the teachers of the gentiles, because they were ordained to preach by the first preachers. Whence: "As the apostles were praying and fasting, the Holy Ghost said: Separate me Paul and Barnabas."
26.4: **“And the sons of Obededom,”** — Obededom, 'red': those who were begotten in servitude and, steeped in the redness of the blood of Christ, had their guilt in the open, are rightly brought back to their former rank by the condescension of the masters. Whence Paul: "I made myself the servant of all, that I might gain all."
26.11: **“Helcias the second, Tabelias the third, Zacharias the fourth: all these the sons and the brethren of Hosa”** — or Hosa
26.12: **“These were divided into porters,”** — the keepers of the Church, who examine the faith of each before baptism
26.13: **“And they cast lots equally”** — "Because God is not a respecter of persons; for whoever worketh justice is acceptable to him"
26.14: **“And the lot of the east fell to Selemias. But to Zacharias his son, a very wise and learned man, the north side fell by lot.”** — the gentile world, cold with unbelief; but very many of them come to the faith
26.15:
**“And to Obededom”** — serving
**“and his sons toward the south”** — because there were the prophets and apostles
**“TOWARD THE SOUTH”** — The southern gate signifies the Jewish people, enlightened by the law and the prophets, near to receiving the warmth of faith and the light of wisdom.
26.16:
**“TOWARD THE WEST BY THE GATE”** — By the western quarter the end of the world is signified, in which will be the persecution of Antichrist, and "iniquity shall abound, and the charity of many shall grow cold". The porters of this gate are the teachers of that time, who strengthen the Church by teaching and exhorting. Hence Sephphimia is interpreted 'humble' or 'of the plain', and Osa 'divining'. For the Church will be humbled in the persecution, and will be loosened in the plain of wantonness; but raised up in the action of the perfect, which is foreshown in the divine words. Whence: "The words are shut up until the appointed time."
**“that leadeth to the way of the ascent:”** — because the judgment will be near, in which the saints will ascend to the kingdom of heaven
**“ward against ward.”** — the concord of the two Testaments
26.17:
**“Now on the east were six Levites: and on the north four a day: and on the south likewise four a day:”** — SIX LEVITES. The six signifies the good work of the ministries of God; the four, the gospel teaching and the fulness of the principal virtues.
**“TWO AND TWO”** — He says the porters were two and two in the cells and on the way, because, whether they take care of the cells of their heart, or outwardly on the way set forth the word of God, they should wholly keep the two precepts of charity and the rule of both Testaments.
26.20:
**“And Achias”** — my brother
**“was over the treasures of the house of God, and the holy vessels.”** — in Christ "are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge", who says: "I will declare thy name to my brethren"
26.21:
**“The sons of Ledan,”** — or Leedan
**“the sons of Gersonni.”** — or Gersoni
26.24: **“THE SONS OF MOSES”** — Those who, according to Josephus, were especially honoured by David and were set over the treasures signify the teachers from the Jews, to whom the adornment of the Church, that is, the beauty of the soul, is committed.
26.25:
**“HIS BROTHER ALSO ELIEZER”** — It shows that the gifts of the princes were the treasures of the holy things; for what they took from the enemies they gave for the furniture of the temple. For whoever, labouring well, gains anything of virtue or good work should attribute it to God, not to himself. Whence: "Not to us, O Lord, not to us; but to thy name give glory."
**“whose son was Rohobia, and his son Isaias, and his son Joram, and his son Zechri,”** — otherwise: Jechri
26.29:
**“And over the Isaarites was Chonenias”** — 'my treasurer', or 'mountain' or 'possession', that is, upon which the Lord rests
**“OVER THE ISAARITES”** — These are they who in the Church receive humbly and obediently, with devout mind, what they hear from their masters, and who, though they cannot with the tongue, show the teaching of the virtues by doing.
26.30: **“And of the Hebronites, Hasabias and his brethren most valiant men, a thousand seven hundred, had the charge over Israel beyond the Jordan westward, in all the works of the Lord, and for the service of the king.”** — ISRAEL BEYOND THE JORDAN. The Israelites who received possession beyond the Jordan signify those who, content with a middle state, do not seek the citadel of the virtues by passing beyond the turbulence of this world, but yet do not neglect to carry out the commandments of God in work. But because no one does these things except by the gift of God, Hasabias, that is, 'the Lord making', is said to be set over them, that they may say with the prophet: "Thou hast wrought all our works for us."
26.31:
**“And the chief of the Hebronites was Jeria according to their families and kindreds. In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were numbered, and there were found most valiant men in Jazer Galaad,”** — that is, they were found in the last [year], in which he arranged all things and set out to Solomon all that was to be done
**“AND THE CHIEF OF THE HEBRONITES”** — In Hebron David began to reign. This signifies those who begin to live well and prepare a kingdom for David in their life. Jerias, that is, 'fearing the Lord', is chief of the Hebronites, because "the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom". And Hebron is interpreted 'marriage'. For he who fears advances so that he loves, and "casteth out fear".
26.32: **“And his brethren of the stronger age, two thousand seven hundred chiefs of families.”** — the apostles and apostolic men

27.1:
**“Now the children of Israel according to their number, the heads of families, captains of thousands, and of hundreds, and officers, that served the king”** — Christ
**“by their companies,”** — that is, orders
**“coming in”** — to God
**“and going out”** — to preach
**“every month in the year,”** — of [his] goodness
**“twenty-four thousand”** — as above
27.6: **“This is that Banaias the most valiant among the thirty, and above the thirty. And over his company was Amizabad”** — otherwise Amizadab
27.7: **“The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zabadias”** — otherwise: Zabedias
27.11: **“The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sobochai the Husathite”** — otherwise: Usathites
27.12:
**“The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, of the stock”** — or of the sons
**“of Jemini”** — otherwise: Jemin
27.13: **“The tenth, for the tenth month, was Marai,”** — otherwise: Manai
27.19: **“Of the Zabulonites, Jesmaias the son of Abdias: of the Nephthalites, Jerimoth”** — or Hierimoth
27.24:
**“Joab the son of Sarvia began to number, but did not finish: because upon this there fell wrath upon Israel: and therefore the number of them that were numbered was not set down in the chronicles of king David.”**
• the annals, called fasti from the fasces, in which the acts of kings or consuls are written
• WAS NOT SET DOWN. Because, wrath coming upon them, the number was thrown into confusion, and the ministries were not distributed according to it.
27.25:
**“OVER THE TREASURES”** — The treasure of Christ [is] knowledge, wisdom, virtues; with these he honours those who serve him. Over these is set Azmoth, which is interpreted 'strong in death'; for a man's teaching is known by patience. Whence: "The patient man is better than the valiant." Azmoth also [is] the son of Adiel, which is interpreted 'my father [is] God'. For whatever of virtues the saints have, they attribute to God.
**“AND OVER THESE TREASURES”** — For he is rightly set over the treasures of the true Solomon in the cities, villages and towers who sets forth in faith and work the dignity of the name of Jonathan and of his father Ozias. For Jonathan [is] 'house of God' [so the edition], and Ozias 'strength of the Lord'. For he who by the gift of God receives the light of knowledge and keeps strongly in work the rightness of faith, not undeservedly receives the care of the churches of God.
27.26: **“And over the work of the field, and the husbandmen that tilled the ground, was Ezri the son of Chelub:”** — he will bring those evil men to an evil end, and will let out his vineyard to other husbandmen, that is, to the preachers; and at various hours workmen are sent into the vineyard, which is the house of Israel
27.27:
**“And over the dressers of the vineyards, Semeias the Romathite: and over the wine cellars,”** — the pleasant dwellings, of which it is said: "In my Father's house there are many mansions"
**“Zabdias the Aphonite.”** — EZRI, SEMEIAS, ZABDIAS etc. Ezri [is] 'helped by the Lord', Semeias 'hearing the Lord', Zabdias 'vehement' or 'abundant fruit'. For he who hears the precepts of the Lord, helped by the aid of his mercy, gathers abundant fruit of good work unto eternal life.
27.28:
**“THE OLIVEYARDS AND FIGYARDS”** — In these are olives and figs, and they signify the companies of the saints, who have the oil of mercy in the breast and the sweetness of meekness [unclear in the edition: "immortalitate"]. These virtues [are] in the plains, which are in the open and at hand for all, and seek not respect of persons but rightness of good will in their hearers.
**“which were in the plains, Balanan the Gederite: and over the oil cellars”** — of eternal life
**“BALANAN”** — JOAS. Balanan, which is interpreted 'having grace', is set over the oliveyards and figyards. For by the grace of God the richness of good works is given. And Joas, which is interpreted 'hoping' or 'strength of the Lord', keeps the oil cellars, because no one comes to the reward but he who by strength of mind, in confidence of hope, strives toward the heavenly kingdom.
27.29:
**“And over the herds”** — the synagogues of the Jews, which had drawn the yoke of the law and had given the milk of simple teaching
**“that fed in Saron, Setrai the Saronite:”** — 'my hearer' or 'my hiding place'. This is the choir of the prophets, who hear hidden things from God
**“and over the oxen”** — the teachers, ploughing the hearts of those under them with the gospel ploughshare
**“in the valleys,”** — the humble
**“Saphat”** — 'judging' or 'he judged'
**“the son of Adli:”** — otherwise: Adli
**“SAPHAT”** — [Saphat,] which is interpreted 'he judged', the son of Abdi, that is, 'of the father of grace', signifies the apostles, set over the other teachers by the Lord's choice. To whom it is said: "You also shall sit on twelve seats, judging the twelve tribes of Israel."
27.30:
**“And over the camels, Ubil the Ismahelite: and over the asses,”** — the foolish or unwise
**“Jadias the Meronathite.”** — [unclear in the edition: "dimidium fuit"], which signifies imperfection
**“OVER THE CAMELS AND OVER THE ASSES”** — These animals are misshapen and unclean, and signify the gentiles, distorted by sin and unclean with lust; but coming into the kingdom of our David they have as masters Ubil and Jaas, who, spurning philosophy and the vain deceit of the world, chose the simplicity of the gospel, as humble and despised. Whence: "If any man among you seem to be wise, let him become a fool."
27.31:
**“And over the sheep”** — the simple and meek, to whom it is said: "Learn of me, because I am meek and humble of heart"
**“Jaziz”** — Jaziz, who is turned to God with his whole mind and confesses himself a stranger and pilgrim, rightly, helped by the Lord, feeds the Lord's flock
27.32:
**“And Jonathan”** — 'the Lord a gift' or 'a dove gave'. These are the apostles and prophets who, instructed not only in the letter of the law but also in spiritual prudence by the gift of the Holy Spirit, merited to be sharers in the secrets of the true David. Whence: "All things whatsoever I have heard of my Father, I have made known to you"
**“David's uncle, a counsellor, a mighty, wise and learned man: he and Jahiel”**
• the holy teachers
• keepers
**“the son of Hachamoni were with the king's sons.”**
• regenerated by the grace of baptism
• JAHIEL THE SON OF HACHAMONI. With Jonathan was the counsellor Jahiel, that is, 'rest of God', the son of Hachamoni, that is, 'of thorns'. This signifies the preachers of the gospel, who, converted to the faith from the error of the gentiles and the thorn-thickets of vices, are made the rest of God. Whence: "Upon whom shall my spirit rest, but upon him that is humble and quiet and trembleth at my words?"
27.33:
**“ACHITOPHEL”** — He who afterwards, depraved by covetousness, plotted with Absalom the death of David; and he is interpreted 'my brother falling', or 'rushing upon', or 'plotting'. This is Judas Iscariot, who was intimate with the Lord among the apostles, but afterwards, corrupted by avarice, by plotting his death with the Jews earned the ruin of everlasting death; who also, according to the book of Kings, hanged himself with a halter. By Achitophel can also be signified the Jews, who by the prerogative of the fathers were once most dear and most renowned for converse with God, but afterwards, giving help to the death of Christ, were destroyed by the Romans in their own house, as Achitophel, that is, in Jerusalem.
**“CHUSAI”** — That is, the Ethiopian, and faithful to David in all things, signifies the gentiles, of whom it is said: "A people which I knew not hath served me: at the hearing of the ear they have obeyed me."
27.34:
**“AFTER ACHITOPHEL WAS JOIADA”** — When Judas fell away the twelfth place did not remain empty, but Matthias succeeded, knowing the grace of God, humble and faithful, who humbly kept the grace which he received by the gift of God. For Joiada is interpreted 'knowing' or 'acknowledging', Banaias 'builder of the Lord'. For him whom the grace of God chose as an apostle the acknowledgment of sound faith made firm in that very dignity. Abiathar, who for a time is among David's counsellors, but in the election from the Lord went astray with Joab against Solomon, signifies those who, corrupted by covetousness, do not keep the rank of dignity which they received from the Lord. For these, if they will not remain in the prison of penance [unclear in the edition: "iuxta timorem Achitophel"], are to be punished for ever by the true Solomon.
**“JOAB”** — [Joab,] that is, 'enemy', signifies those in whose person it is said: "I was directed to all thy commandments: I have hated all wicked ways." To whom elsewhere it is said: "Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect." For Joab is interpreted [so the edition] 'the same father'.

28.1: **“WITH THE EUNUCHS”** — The law forbids Israelites to be castrated, and foreigners are not wont to be admitted to the secrets of counsel. But they hand down that in this place those are called eunuchs who, strangers to the actions of the world, gave themselves to prayer and reading, and had wives not for the sake of lust but of begetting offspring; whom Josephus calls Essenes.
28.6: **“And he said to me: Solomon thy son shall build my house, and my altars [so the edition].”** — otherwise: courts
28.11: **“AND DAVID GAVE”** — David the psalmist and the other fathers of the old Testament foreshowed by figures and riddles all that the true peacemaker was to do in the Church: how all nations had entrance into the Church through the faith of baptism; what the state of the Church would be; what the perfection of the saints, and the reward in the heavenly kingdom, to be rendered to each according to his merits through the various cells and chambers; because "in the kingdom of God there are many mansions".
28.13: **“and of the divisions of the priests and of the Levites, for all the works of the house of the Lord, and for all the vessels”** — made in [his] honour
28.14:
**“gold”** — in which the splendour of wisdom is signified
**“by weight for every vessel of the service; of silver”** — in which the brightness of preaching
**“also the weight according to the diversity of the vessels and works,”** — as God "divideth to every one according as he will"
28.16: **“He gave also gold for the tables of proposition”** — of the table of proposition we have said enough in Exodus
28.17:
**“For fleshhooks also, and bowls, and censers of fine gold,”** — all these you will find fully expounded in Exodus
**“and little lions of gold, according to the measure, he distributed the weight”** — there are little lions and strong lions, that is, some stronger in sense, others silver in the brightness of their preaching
**“for every lion and lion. In like manner also for lions of silver he set aside a different weight of silver.”** — AND LITTLE LIONS OF GOLD. Neither in Exodus, in the construction of the tabernacle, nor in Kings, in the building of the temple, are lions and little lions anywhere read to have been made, except that in the temple carved work is related to have been made in the making of the ten bases, where lions and oxen and cherubim and palm trees are related to have been carved. Nor [is it read] that cherubim were formed in the likeness of a chariot, but only that two cherubim were made, covering the ark with their wings. But to Ezechiel by the river Chobar the likeness of four living creatures was shown, and here "their appearance: there was the likeness of a man in them, and every one had four faces, and every one four wings; their feet were straight feet, and the sole of their foot was like the sole of a calf's foot"; and after a little: "As for the likeness of their faces: there was the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right side of all the four, and the face of an eagle over all the four." And elsewhere: "And every one had four faces: one face was the face of a cherub, and the second face the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle." But we have touched briefly on the exposition of these and of what follows in our Ezechiel, as God granted us.
28.18:
**“And for the altar on which the incense is burnt, he gave the finest gold: and that the likeness of the chariot”** — this chariot is expounded in Ezechiel
**“of the cherubims”** — 'beauty of knowledge', that is, the knowledge of the sacraments of God, and his throne and rest. Whence: "Thou that sittest upon the cherubims, shine forth"
28.19: **“ALL THESE THINGS, SAID HE, CAME TO ME WRITTEN”** — The Hebrews hand down that the pattern of the temple and vessels shown to Moses on the mountain came to Josue, then to the judges, and to Heli, and to Samuel, and to David, at last to Solomon. Or the hand of the Lord is the Son, by whose gift David and the other saints received whatever they set forth about the structure of holy Church.

29.6: **“Then the chiefs of families, and the princes of the tribes of Israel, and the captains of thousands, and of hundreds, and the overseers of the king's possessions, promised”** — THEN THE CHIEFS PROMISED etc. He who has learned to rule himself and others well, with the grace of God going before, ought to carry out zealously and devoutly, as far as he can, the gaining of his neighbours and the doing of work acceptable to God; so that he may strive to build the house of God, that is, the Church, in the splendour of wisdom, in the brightness of words, in the resonance of preaching, in the firmness of faith, and with the gems of the various virtues: "For every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labour. If any man build upon [it] gold, silver, precious stones; but he who builds upon it frail works, that is, wood, hay, stubble, shall suffer loss."
29.10: **“And he blessed the Lord before all the multitude, and he said: Blessed art thou, O Lord the God of Israel our father from eternity to eternity.”** — AND HE BLESSED etc. Because the congregation of the faithful, admonished by the writings of the prophets and stirred by the words and examples of the holy fathers, sings praises and hymns to God, offering the sacrifices of devout confession and the fruitful works of holy living.
29.21:
**“And they sacrificed victims to the Lord: and they offered holocausts”** — devout labour
**“the next day,”** — for the perfection of eternal life
**“a thousand bullocks,”** — just rule
**“a thousand rams, a thousand lambs,”** — simplicity and innocence
**“with their libations,”** — with holy prayers
29.22:
**“And they ate, and drank before the Lord that day with great joy.”** — AND THEY ATE. This is the joy of the saints and their aim: that by works of virtues they may guard themselves against the famine to come, and may feast and rejoice in the sight of God.
**“And they anointed the second time Solomon the son of David. And they anointed him to the Lord to be prince, and Sadoc to be high priest.”** — THEY ANOINTED etc. Because Christ is celebrated by all the faithful, with sound faith and devout confession, in royal and at the same time pontifical dignity. Solomon is interpreted 'peaceable', Sadoc 'just'. And Christ is "our peace, who hath made both one"; he is the just Lord and loves justice, the judge of the living and the dead. Every faithful man first anoints him king and priest when in the perfection of baptism he confesses him true king and priest; he anoints him also a second time when by teaching and working he preaches the same to others. Whence: "Thy name is as oil poured out."
29.24: **“And all the princes, and men of power, and all the sons of king David gave their hand, and were subject to Solomon the king.”** — there is no dignity, no power, that does not obey this command; whence: "All kings shall serve him"
29.25:
**“And the Lord magnified Solomon over all Israel:”** — "Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised" and "a great king above all gods"
**“and gave him the glory of a reign,”** — "he hath given him a name which is above all names, that in the name of Jesus every knee should bow" etc.
29.28: **“And he died in his old age, full of days, and riches, and glory. And Solomon his son reigned in his stead.”** — AND HE DIED etc. It signifies that he ended the present life with an abundance of virtues and works of light, worthy of the rest to come and the glory of the heavenly kingdom. Abraham likewise "died in a good old age, and having lived a long time, and being full of days". Isaac "was gathered to his people, being full of days". Joseph "died in a good old age, having lived a hundred and ten years of his life, and being embalmed with spices". "Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died: his eye was not dim, neither were his teeth moved." "But bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days", who seem to themselves "to spend their days in wealth, and in a moment they go down to hell".

1.1:
**“And Solomon the son of David was strengthened in his kingdom,”**
• of the ancient fathers
• WAS STRENGTHENED. When in death he triumphed over him who had the empire of death, and gained for himself the kingdom of all. Whence: "All power is given to me in heaven and in earth."
**“and the Lord was with him,”** — "He that sent me is with me, and he hath not left me alone"
**“and magnified him to a high degree.”** — "He hath given him a name which is above all names"
1.3: **“GABAON”** — Which was the chief city of the Hevites, and fell to the lot of Benjamin, and was set apart for the Levites. It is strange, then, that Josephus says that Solomon came to Hebron to sacrifice on the brazen altar which Moses had made; unless perhaps he meant Hebron itself to be understood as the high place of Gabaon, because he first reigned there. For Gabaon is interpreted 'height' or 'hill of the kinsman'.
1.10:
**“Give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may come in and go out before thy people.”** — as an example to all
**“GIVE ME WISDOM”** — Give me wisdom etc. He asks of God not gold, not riches, not earthly glory, but that he may know how to rule and judge the people of God. If the ruler of bodies chose this, much more ought the rulers of souls to choose it, that they may show the people of God the entrance to faith and the going out to hope.
1.13: **“FROM THE HIGH PLACE OF GABAON TO JERUSALEM BEFORE THE TABERNACLE”** — It signifies the ark, in which were the tables of the testament. For it is written above: "But the tabernacle of the Lord, which Moses made in the desert, and the altar of holocausts, were at that time in the high place of Gabaon" etc. But the ark of the Lord, after David brought it into his house, remained there until the temple was built.
1.14:
**“And he gathered to himself chariots and horsemen,”**
• the saints, joined by the reins of charity and the yoke of God, whom he himself guides as a charioteer
• the ministries of angels and men; whence: "The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands; thousands of them that rejoice: the Lord is among them in Sina, in the holy place"
**“and there were gathered to him a thousand four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen:”** — forty tens, and they signify the times of the law, for whose receiving Moses fasted forty days, and the people who were instructed by it were forty years in the desert
**“and he placed them in the cities of the chariots, and with the king in Jerusalem.”**
• that is, in the towns or buildings which had been built for the stationing of the chariots
• AND TWELVE THOUSAND etc. This number signifies the time of grace, in which the apostolic doctrine forms the people of the new Testament. And well are the chariots and horsemen of Solomon numbered by the number forty or twelve, because through both Testaments holy men, learned in the sacred letters, are fitted for God to sit upon, whom he, the supreme charioteer, guides at his nod.
1.16:
**“And there were horses brought to him”** — the men of Cyrene in work and understanding, in whom, converted to the faith, Christ may worthily sit
**“from Egypt,”** — the spiritual [Egypt]
**“and from Coa,”**
• from every nation that is under heaven
• which they say is one of the Cyclades; but the Hebrews interpret Choa 'gathering'
**“by the merchants”** — that is, by the preachers, who give preaching and receive the faith of their hearers
1.17:
**“FOR SIX HUNDRED PIECES OF SILVER”** — Because by the preaching of the two Testaments men are brought through the preachers to know the truth of faith, for the use of the true Solomon. Six hundred, then, that is, sixty tens, signify the perfection of the gospel teaching, in which the perfection of the law wholly consists; especially since our Redeemer, suffering on the sixth day, fulfilled all things that were written of him in the law and the prophets; whence he says: "It is consummated. And bowing his head, he gave up the ghost."
**“A HUNDRED AND FIFTY”** — [A hundred and fifty,] which are three fifties, and plainly signify the old Testament, because of Pentecost and the jubilee and the threefold division of Scripture; for it is said: "All things must needs be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me."

2.1:
**“And Solomon determined to build a house to the name of the Lord, and a palace for himself.”** — AND SOLOMON DETERMINED etc. BEDE. The house which Solomon built in Jerusalem signifies the universal Church, because from the first elect to the last it is built daily through the grace of the true peacemaker; which is still partly a pilgrim in the world, partly, having escaped its toils, already reigns with him in heaven, where it is all to reign when the judgment is finished. To this house belong the angels, likeness to whom is promised us, the Lord saying: "For they are equal to the angels, and are the children of God" etc. To it belongs Christ himself, who says: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. But he spoke of the temple of his body." Of us the Apostle says: "Know you not that you are the temple of God?" etc. If then he, by the humility he took on, was made the temple of God, and we by his Spirit dwelling in us, it is plain that that temple was a figure of all of us and of Christ himself: but of him as of the cornerstone, of us as of living stones built upon him. The tabernacle made in the desert designates the same house of God. But because that house [was made] on the journey by which they were coming to the land of promise, while this was built in the land of promise and in the city of Jerusalem; that, so that, carried from place to place by the Levites, it might at length be brought into the land of promise; this, so that, built at once in the homeland and the royal city, it might stand on an immovable foundation until it should fulfil the very reality of the heavenly figures: in that can be figured the labour and exile of the present Church, in this the future rest and blessedness. Or because that was made by the children of Israel alone, but this by proselytes and gentiles also, in that can be figured chiefly the fathers of the old Testament and the ancient people of God, in this the Church gathered from the gentiles; although the building of each house, taken in particular, shows by manifold figures both the daily labours of the Church and the future joys of the heavenly kingdom, and the election of the first Church from Israel and the salvation of all nations in Christ. And that Solomon is said to have determined to build a house to the name of the Lord and a palace for himself signifies the same thing, because the Church is both the house of God, which he inhabits for ever, and the palace of the heavenly king, in which he shows the greatness of his glory to all generations. The workmen of Solomon are all the elect who prepare themselves for the building of God by believing, working, and teaching others.
**“SOLOMON”** — Both by name and by his most peaceful reign he signifies him of whom Isaias says: "His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace." And Hiram, which is interpreted 'living on high', [signifies] the believers from the gentiles, glorious in life and faith, by whose work the Church is often helped and increased, and strengthened by imperial decrees against heretics, schismatics and pagans. Solomon, then, asks help of Hiram in the work of the temple, because Christ, wishing to build the Church, chose workmen not only from the Jews but also from the gentiles. Hiram sent to Solomon cedar and fir wood cut from Libanus, to be set in the house of the Lord; because the converted gentile world sent to the Lord men renowned in the world, but cast down and humbled from the mountain of pride by the axe of the Lord's rebuke, to be set at some time, in their measure, according to the rule of gospel truth. He sent also craftsmen to be set over the ruling of peoples, namely Dionysius the Areopagite, Cyprian, and many others. He sent also gold, that is, wise men, renowned also in genius. For all these, the gentile world, having given them, awaits from the Lord the gifts of heavenly grace: the wheat, that is, of the word of God, and the oil of charity, of the anointing and enlightening of the Holy Spirit.
2.3: **“He sent also to Hiram king of Tyre,”** — these things are told more fully in Kings
2.8:
**“Send me also cedars, and fir trees, and pine trees from Libanus: for I know that thy servants know”** — the teachers from the gentiles, who cast down those glorious in the world from the haughtiness of pride and transfer them to the service of the true Solomon
**“AND MY SERVANTS SHALL BE”** — My apostles and first teachers, who form and instruct the teachers from the gentiles, lest they presume to teach anything wrong. For Solomon wanted Hiram's servants to cut wood for him because they were more skilled in cutting than his own servants; but he wanted his own servants also to be present, to show the cutters of what measure the wood ought to be made. For the apostles knew the words of the gospel more surely from the Lord himself; but the gentiles converted from errors to the truth of the gospel knew the errors of the gentiles more surely, and therefore overthrew them more subtly.
2.13:
**“I have sent thee therefore a wise and most skilful man, Hiram”** — the teachers whom the gentile world sent
**“my father,”** — he calls him his father because, having travelled abroad from the land of Israel, he taught him the fear of the Lord and the knowledge of the truth
2.14:
**“THE SON OF A WOMAN OF THE TRIBE OF DAN”** — He shows that he was of the progeny of Salomith of the tribe of Dan, of whom we read in the book of Numbers. The Hebrews hand down that his father was a Hebrew of the stock of Ooliab of the tribe of Dan, who worked with Beseleel in the desert. And as to his calling him a Tyrian, the Hebrews say this was done by a transfer [of meaning]. For [unclear in the edition: "Zocri"] in their tongue is interpreted 'moulding'. For Tyre [so the edition: 'Chyros'], which they call Zor, sounds sometimes 'narrowness', sometimes 'moulding'.
**“whose father was a Tyrian, who knew how to work in gold,”** — of wisdom
**“and in silver,”** — of eloquence
**“in brass,”** — of preaching
**“and in iron,”** — by firmness of faith
**“and in marble,”** — by the beauty of the virtues
**“and in timber,”** — by the greenness of good work
**“in purple”** — through the martyrdom of shed blood
**“also and violet,”** — of heavenly conversation
**“and fine linen,”** — of chastity
**“and scarlet:”** — of charity
**“and who knoweth to grave all sort of graving, and to devise ingeniously all that there may be need of in the work, with thy artificers, and with the artificers of my lord David thy father.”** — WHO KNEW HOW TO WORK IN GOLD, SILVER, BRASS, IRON etc. In all these the spiritual Hiram knows how to work, so that the adornment of the house of God may shine with worthy beauty before the eyes of men, and be made acceptable to God by the odour of good repute.
2.16: **“And we will cut down as many trees out of Libanus as thou shalt need, and will convey them in floats by sea to Joppe: and thou shalt bring them to Jerusalem.”** — AND WE WILL CUT etc. It signifies that the gentile world, having heard the fame of the gospel, sends divers persons through faith to baptism. Yet it belongs to the true peacemaker alone to unite them to the unity of the Church by absolving their sins through the sacraments of baptism; of whom it is said: "He upon whom thou shalt see the Spirit descending, and remaining upon him, he it is that baptizeth."
2.17:
**“So Solomon numbered all the proselytes”** — who passed over from the gentiles into the fellowship of the people of God
**“SO SOLOMON NUMBERED”** — The workmen of the house of the Lord were of the children of Israel, of the proselytes, [and] of the gentiles: of the children of Israel, thirty thousand, who were sent to cut cedars from Libanus, as we read in Kings; of the proselytes, of whom namely he now speaks, the hewers of stones; of the gentiles, Hiram himself and his servants, who cut wood from Libanus with the servants of Solomon. All the races of men, then, by whom the Church was to be built went before in the building of Solomon's temple. For Jews, proselytes and gentiles converted to the truth of the gospel build the Church of Christ by living and teaching rightly.
**“THREE THOUSAND AND SIX HUNDRED”** — In Paralipomenon, instead of the three thousand three hundred overseers who are numbered in Kings, three thousand six hundred are written, for the perfection of lofty men. For in six [days] God completed the adornment of the world; and because holy Scripture teaches the faith of the Trinity and the works of justice, rightly are there said to have been three thousand six hundred.
2.18:
**“And he made of them”** — for the sabbath rest of souls
**“seventy thousand to carry burdens on their shoulders,”** — "Bear ye one another's burdens"; and elsewhere: "Rebuke the unquiet, comfort the feeble-minded" etc.
**“and eighty thousand”** — for the hope of the resurrection, which on the eighth day, that is, after the sabbath, both went before in the Lord and is hoped for in us
**“to”** — the preachers
**“stones”** — the hard minds of men
**“in the mountains:”** — who were born in the mind of pride, sprung from the transgression of the first parent
**“hew”** — with the axes of the word of God, that they might fit the building of the house
**“and three”** — for the faith of the Trinity which they preach to us
**“thousand six hundred overseers of the work of the people.”** — those entrusted with [so the edition: 'creditores'] sacred Scripture, by whom we are taught: to teach the ignorant, to rebuke the contemptuous [so the edition: 'contemptatores'], to bear one another's burdens

3.1:
**“And Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem”** — in the vision of peace, which is in the unity of the Church; whence: "And his place is in peace"
**“in mount”** — that is, in Christ, of whom it is said: "A city seated on a mountain cannot be hid"
**“Moria,”** — that is, 'of vision', because those whom he calls to the vision of his brightness he deigns to visit and help while they labour in this life
**“which had been shewn to David his father,”** — David foreknew that he would be born according to the flesh, as did the other prophets also
**“IN THE THRASHINGFLOOR OF ORNAN THE JEBUSITE”** — The Church is signified by the threshingfloor. Whence: "Whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his floor." Ornan, that is, 'adornment', a Jebusite by nation, signifies the gentiles, who are to be adorned by the Lord and changed into sons of the Church. Whence: "You were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord." Jebus is Jerusalem itself. Jebus is interpreted 'trodden down', Jerusalem 'vision of peace'; while the gentile Ornan reigned in it, it was called Jebus. But when David bought in it the place of the holocaust, and when Solomon built the temple, it was called Jerusalem. For the gentile world, ignorant of divine worship, is trodden down by the demons; but when Christ looked upon it, it found in him both the place and the name of peace.
3.2:
**“And he began to build in the second month,”** — this refers to the gentiles, who in the second place came together to the building of the Creator
**“IN THE SECOND MONTH”** — That is, May, namely soon after the Pasch, so that the people, consecrated by the mystical solemnity, might worthily undertake the mystical work.
**“IN THE FOURTH YEAR”** — After the fulfilment of the dispensation of the divine incarnation, which is written in the four gospels, the Spirit being sent from heaven, the Church was built. What we have expounded in the books of Kings we touch on briefly in Paralipomenon.
3.3: **“OF THE LENGTH”** — The length of the house signifies the long patience of the Church; the breadth, the charity by which it loves even its enemies, until it rejoices in God with friends alone; the height, the hope of the future life and reward, because it despises all adversities until it sees the good things of the Lord in the land of the living. It is to be noted that the thirty cubits of height which are read in Kings reached not to the roof of the temple but to the lower upper chamber. For here [it is said] that the height was a hundred and twenty cubits [unclear in the edition: "Hic enim quod"]. Another thirty will be counted to the middle chamber, another to the third, then another thirty up to the topmost roof of the temple; and so the whole height of the house is completed in a hundred and twenty cubits, the number of men with which the primitive Church in Jerusalem received the grace of the Holy Spirit. For fifteen, which is made up of seven and eight, signifies the future life, which is now passed in the rest of souls and will be perfected in the resurrection of bodies; and fifteen drawn into a triangle, that is, numbered with all its parts, makes a hundred and twenty, by which the future blessedness of the elect is designated. And well is the third chamber of the house completed in this number, [blessedness] which, after the present labours, after the rest of souls, will be fulfilled in the resurrection in the full glory of happiness.
3.4: **“AND THE PORCH”** — That is, the temple itself, which was before the doors of the oracle. For the structure had a threefold division: the porch before the temple; the temple itself, in which were the altar of incense, the table of proposition and the candlestick of light; and the oracle, that is, the Holy of holies, where the ark of the testament and the cherubim were placed behind the veil. The porch before the temple bears the figure of the faithful of old; the temple itself, of those who came into the world after the Lord's incarnation; and the inner house, of the joys of the heavenly kingdom given to both. It is to be noted, then, that the walls of the house were made of precious stones, covered with boards of cypress or cedar, clothed with plates of gold. Whence in Kings: "And all the house was covered with cedar" etc. The stones of the wall or of the pavement, the boards and the gold signify the life of the saints in the Church. The living stones are the saints joined into one rule by the strength of faith. The boards of cedar or cypress are the saints joined to one another in the same faith by the breadth of various virtues, according to the gift of the Holy Spirit. The plates of gold are the saints who have the charity that surpasses knowledge, and rejoice together in its most pleasing brightness.
3.5:
**“And the greater house he ceiled with deal boards, and overlaid them with plates of fine gold throughout: and he graved in it palm trees,”** — the carving of palm trees [is] the portrayal of the virtues, through which true victory and reward are gained
**“and like little chains”** — the offices of charity, by which the brotherhood of the saints is joined and built into the one house of Christ throughout the world
3.6:
**“He paved also the floor of the temple”** — in Kings thus: "He covered the floor with planks of fir". Hence it is plain that he laid the boards not on the earth but on marble, and thirdly laid gold upon them
**“HE PAVED ALSO THE FLOOR”** — He paved also the floor etc. As the breadth of the wall, rising on high and reaching to the ceilings, signifies the progress of the virtues by which the saints reach heaven, or the choirs of the saints succeeding one another through various times, so the evenness of the pavement [signifies] their harmonious humility, by which, placed in this life, they live together in social charity. The pavement was laid with precious marble of great beauty, and the marble covered with boards of fir, because the life of the just is first to be fortified in the heart by firmness of faith, afterwards to be adorned in work by the breadth of the virtues. For what does the beauty of marble covered with boards profit, unless it show something mystical? But it signifies that the breadth of good works is to be propped up by the strength of faith. The fir, tall and lasting, shows the mind of the elect, spurning the lowest things, cleaving to heavenly things, and excelling in the virtue of patience. The plates of gold laid upon the marble and the boards of fir are the breadth of charity from a pure heart and a good conscience and an unfeigned faith, which, as gold outshines other metals, so outshines the other virtues in the temple of God.
3.7:
**“And the gold”** — of charity
**“was most approved, of the plates of which he covered the house, and the beams thereof, and the posts,”** — the holy teachers
**“and the walls, and the doors:”**
• Solomon covered the walls of the temple with gold when Christ enlightened the company of the faithful with the light of wisdom and charity
• THE POSTS AND THE DOORS etc. He covered them when, the Lord himself opening the entrance of faith, he showed with what truth it shines for all who enter the Church. The door of the temple is Christ, through whom one comes to the Father, who says: "I am the door" etc. In Kings it is written thus: "The oracle was twenty cubits in length, and twenty in breadth, and twenty in height." The Holy of holies is called the oracle because there secrets are revealed to men by divine and angelic speech. Hence the oracle was made in a hidden place, that is, in the inner house, because in the heavenly homeland the vision and speech of angels and the very presence of God will be revealed. That he says twenty cubits of height signifies the wall of cedar which separates the oracle from the outer house.
**“and he graved cherubims on the walls.”** — the angelic manner of life in the morals of men, that as he is served by angels in heaven, so he may be served by men on earth
**“AND HE GRAVED”** — This house has, as is read in Kings, "carved work standing out", when the saints do the works of virtues not in secret, but set forth an example to all.
3.8:
**“HE MADE ALSO THE HOUSE OF THE HOLY OF HOLIES”** — The oracle, where the ark was, had twenty cubits in length, breadth and height, that is, it was square; because in the heavenly homeland, where the saints see the king in his beauty, charity alone, of divine and heavenly grace, shines through all things. Whence in what follows: He covered it with plates of gold, that is, he filled the walls of the heavenly city with the grace of charity.
**“SIX HUNDRED TALENTS”** — In talents [is] the perfection of weight, which expresses the perfection of charity, as [does] the perfection of the six, by which the hundred is multiplied to make six hundred.
3.9: **“He made also nails of gold, so that every nail weighed fifty sicles: the upper chambers also he overlaid with gold.”** — HE MADE ALSO NAILS etc. By the number fifty are figured the remission of sins, spiritual grace and eternal rest; and the nails fastened the plates of gold on the walls of the house of the Lord. The nails are the heavenly words by which we advance and are preserved in the love of good works; these promise us pardon of sins through the grace of the Holy Spirit, and an eternal sabbath rest in the future. These are the nails of love and the nails of fear, by which beginners, not yet come to perfection, mortify the allurements of vices, pierced, that is, by those words of truth by which we are taught to crucify our flesh with its vices and concupiscences. Whence the prophet: "Pierce thou my flesh with thy fear" etc. He who comes to more perfect things says of the nails of perfection: "But it is good for me to adhere to my God." The upper chambers also he overlaid with gold. As the Holy of holies, where the ark was, signifies the inward life of the saints in the sight of the Redeemer, whence: "Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy face, from the disturbance of men", so the upper chambers on high [signify] that the same life is in heaven and not in this world; whence: "Seek the things that are above, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God."
3.10:
**“He made also in the house of the holy of holies cherubims,”** — the two cherubim were of one measure and the same work, because there is no differing will in the heavenly homeland, where all are enlightened by the same vision and glory of God present
**“two,”** — because of the fellowship of charity, which cannot be between fewer than two. Hence the disciples are sent two by two to preach, that those who preach the word of faith may hold charity before all things
**“of image work: and he overlaid them with gold.”**
• HE MADE ALSO TWO CHERUBIM etc. This is read more fully in Kings, written thus: "And he made in the oracle two cherubims of olive tree, of ten cubits in height. One wing of the cherub was five cubits, and the other wing of the cherub was five cubits, that is, in all ten cubits, from the extremity of one wing to the extremity of the other wing. And the second cherub was also ten cubits, of equal measure, and the work was one in both the cherubims, that is, one cherub had the height of ten cubits, and in like manner the other cherub. And he set the cherubims in the midst of the inner temple: and the cherubims stretched forth their wings, and the wing of one touched one wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall: and the other wings in the midst of the temple touched one another."
• "And he set the cherubims", as is read in Kings, "in the midst of the inner temple: and the cherubims stretched forth their wings, and the wing of one touched one wall" etc. It is manifest from what has been said before that the cherubim, whose dwelling is in heaven, are as it were set in the midst of the inner temple. And they stretched forth their wings as if to fly, because the angels always have a mind ready for the service of the divine will. That one wing touched one wall, and the wing of the second cherub the other wall, belongs to that ministry of charity which the angels show us. That the other wings touched one another in the midst of the temple signifies that grace of love with which they embrace one another. "He overlaid also the cherubims with gold", because the Creator raised their nature with immortal brightness and filled their mind with the light of true love and humility.
• Cherubim is a name of angelic dignity. In the singular it is called cherub, in the plural cherubim. Hence by the cherubim can be understood the angels who in heaven always stand by their Creator. They were made of olive wood, because the angelic powers are anointed with the grace of the Holy Spirit, lest they wither from the love of God. And they are ten cubits high, because they enjoy the denarius of eternal life, having the inviolate image of the Creator, keeping the holiness, justice and truth which they received in their first creation. For the denarius consists of ten obols, and contains in itself the name and image of the king. Hence it signifies the heavenly kingdom, where the angels remain for ever in the image of the Creator to which they were made, and elect men receive the image which they had lost by sinning. Wings, when set down in figure of holy men, signify their virtues, by which they always fly to heavenly things and delight to dwell in them; but when in figure of angels, the grace of their perpetual and unfailing happiness, by which they persist always in heaven in the ministry of their Maker. Or because they are endowed with the lightness of a spiritual nature, so that wherever they will they arrive at once as if flying, both here they are figured with wings, and to the prophets they were shown with wings.
• The two cherubim, that is, the two Testaments, made in the oracle, in the secret counsel of the divine dispensation; of olive wood, because they give us the light of knowledge, the flame of the charity of God helping through the Holy Spirit; ten cubits high, because they preach the keeping of the Decalogue for the service of God, to be rewarded with the denarius of the everlasting kingdom.
3.11:
**“SO THAT ONE WING HAD FIVE CUBITS”** — "One wing of the cherub was five cubits" etc., because the angels keep with unwearied devotion the law of God written in five books, namely by loving God with all their strength and their neighbours as themselves: "And love is the fulfilling of the law." And the angelic spirits and elect men are neighbours to one another. Hence each wing of the cherub is of the same measure, because with the same devotion with which they love one another in God they desire also our fellowship as we ascend to them. Likewise then the wings make up ten cubits, when in the twofold showing of charity the angels rejoice in the presence of their Creator.
**“TOUCHED THE WALL”** — They touch the two walls equally with their wings, because they have with them Jews and gentiles as possessors of the heavenly court; not that there is any local distinction there between the two peoples, but because the festival of inward blessedness is greater from the fellowship of the brotherhood united in God. They stretch their wings, then, to both walls, because, rejoicing in the heavenly homeland, they stir the just of both peoples to the praise of the Creator.
**“and touched the wall of the house: and the other wing having five cubits, touched the wing of the other cherub.”**
• They stretch their wings, overlaid with gold, to the walls of the oracle, as they have their faces turned to the outer house; because the angels, as they keep their own innocence, so rejoice in the blessedness of the saints, that they bring help to those whom they still see on earth, until they bring them into the heavenly homeland: "For they are all ministering spirits, sent to minister for them who shall receive the inheritance of salvation."
• With the outer wings this one touches one wall, that one the other; because [unclear in the edition: "Vetus Testamentum antiquo populo scripto novum nobis"], who came to the faith after the Lord's incarnation; and we are rightly compared to the second wall, that is, the northern, who after the cold and darkness of idolatry have known the light of truth.
3.12:
**“In like manner the wing of the other cherub”** — the work was one in the two cherubim, because the writers of both Testaments serve God with the same chastity of work and devotion of charity, and preach God with one harmonious voice and faith
**“had five cubits, and touched the wall: and his other wing of five cubits”** — because in all the changeableness of passing things the saints stretch out the senses of their body in obedience to their Creator
**“touched the wing of the other cherub.”** — the inner wings touch one another over the ark, because the Testaments agree in equal witness concerning the Lord
**“THE OTHER WING”** — They stretch their wings to one another over the ark when they refer to the praise of the Saviour every good thing they had received. They stretch their other wings to the walls of the oracle when they rejoice to see the saints with them, and touch them as with the tips of their wings, exulting that they were imitators of their purity in this life.
3.13:
**“So the wings of both the cherubims were spread forth, and were twenty cubits in length: and they stood upright on their feet,”** — because they desire us, raised up from the toil of this pilgrimage, to come to their fellowship
**“and their faces were turned”** — they have their faces turned
**“toward the outward house.”** — AND THEIR FACES WERE TURNED TOWARD THE OUTWARD HOUSE, because for the sake of us, who still stand outside, but "are saved by hope", the divine books were composed, whose writers, already reigning with the Lord, take care of our salvation and intercede for us with God.
3.14:
**“He made also a veil of violet,”** — by the desire of heavenly things, in which we ought to be initiated by carrying our cross
**“and purple,”** — by the sacrament of the Lord's passion
**“and scarlet,”** — by the flame of spiritual love; whence those who walked with the Lord said: "Was not our heart burning" etc.
**“and fine linen,”** — by chastening of the flesh; whence: "Mortify your members which are upon the earth"
**“HE MADE ALSO A VEIL”** — This is passed over in Kings, but there is told what is not had here, namely that "in the entrance of the oracle he made little doors of olive tree, and posts". But this veil was made for the sake of beauty, that the silk might shine between the gilded walls. But it is of the same mystery as the little doors, hung with fitting signification before the ark and at the entrance of the oracle, so that, as the little doors were opened at fitting hours, so also the veil [was drawn] for those coming who were to enter the Holy of holies. Its drawing back according to the law signifies the opening of the heavenly kingdom, which is given to us through the flesh of Christ. Hence also when the Lord was baptized the heavens were opened, because through the baptism which he consecrated for us we enter the gate of the heavenly kingdom; and when he died the veil was rent in the midst, because the figures of the law had come to an end, and the truth of the gospel and the entrance of the kingdom are opened by the truth itself.
**“AND WROUGHT IN IT CHERUBIMS”** — The cherubim are woven into these four colours when in all that we do devoutly we are protected by angelic guard from the poisoned darts of the demons, and make unceasing use of the fulness of knowledge, ever looking to the divine words, lest we stray from the path of the virtues.
3.15:
**“BEFORE THE DOORS OF THE TEMPLE”** — They stood in the porch before the doors of the temple, and adorned the entrance of the temple on either side with their beauty. The door of the temple is the Lord, who says: "No man cometh to the Father but by me" etc. The pillars stand round the door on either side when the ministers of the word show the entrance of the heavenly kingdom to both peoples, so that whoever comes to the faith of the gospel from the light of the knowledge of the law or from the error of the gentiles may have them ready to show him the way of salvation by word and example.
**“Before the doors also of the temple two pillars”** — In Kings we read of these pillars: "And when he was come to king Solomon, he wrought all his work. And he cast two pillars in brass" etc.
**“THIRTY-FIVE CUBITS”** — This number signifies the perfection of the masters. For the number seven multiplied by five, or five by seven, gives thirty-five. Five expresses the law; seven, because of the sevenfold Spirit abiding on the flower of the root of Jesse, the gospel. Hence the Lord is related in one place to have fed five thousand men with five loaves, and in another four thousand men with seven loaves. The pillars of thirty-five cubits, then, signify that the teachers of the gospel have perfect knowledge of the two Testaments; whence: "To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God." And elsewhere: "He opened their understanding, that they might understand the Scriptures."
3.16:
**“AS IT WERE LITTLE CHAINS”** — The manifold weaving together of the chains, and the spreading of the net according to Kings, suggest the manifold persons of the elect, who, when they cleave to the words of the preachers by listening faithfully and obeying, offer to beholders the wonder of their joining, as nets and little chains laid upon the heads of the pillars.
**“ON THE HEADS OF THE PILLARS”** — The heads of the pillars, that is, the topmost part, are the hearts of the teachers, by whose thoughts devoted to God all their works and words are directed, as the limbs by the head.
**“POMEGRANATES”** — Many grains within are surrounded by one rind outside; hence they signify the Church, because it surrounds the innumerable hosts of the elect with the defence of one faith; or the life and morals of each just man, who walls in with the firm guard of faith and humility his many marks of thoughts and virtues, lest perhaps they flow away. And fitly were the heads of the pillars surrounded round about with pomegranates, because the holy teachers call to mind the life of the faithful of former times, and confirm their own words on every side by their examples, lest they err, if they live or teach otherwise than their rule holds.
3.17:
**“These pillars also he put in the porch of the temple, one on the right hand,”** — the right-hand pillar signifies the teachers, because they founded the primitive Church in Jerusalem
**“and the other on the left: that which was on the right hand he called Jachin:”** — firmness
**“and that on the left hand, Booz.”**
• in strength
• THESE PILLARS ALSO. Two pillars were made, and so placed, to teach us to keep the entrance of the heavenly kingdom before our eyes in prosperity and in adversity. And it is to be noted that the porch of the temple is also called the vestibule, and that what we read, between the vestibule and the altar, ought to be understood as between the porch and the altar.
• The second pillar signifies the preachers who were sent to preach to the gentiles. Or the right-hand pillar signifies those who prophesied that the Lord would come in the flesh; the second, those who testify that he has already come and redeemed the world with his blood. Both pillars are reckoned by a like name, since one is called 'firmness' and the other 'in strength', that one strength of faith and work may be shown to be in all teachers; and the teachers of our time are silently censured, who wish to seem and be called pillars of the house of God, when they have in themselves nothing of the strength of firm faith for despising the pomps of the world [and] desiring invisible goods, [nothing of strength] for correcting, or of diligence for understanding, the errors of those over whom they are set.

4.1:
**“HE MADE ALSO AN ALTAR”** — The altar of holocaust signifies those who consecrate their body and soul to God with the fire of love; whose perseverance in good work the length of the altar expresses, the breadth their largeness in the charity of God and neighbour, the height their hope in awaiting [God's] visitation.
**“of twenty cubits in length, and of twenty cubits”** — or by cubits
**“in breadth,”** — OF TWENTY CUBITS IN BREADTH etc. The twenty signifies the great perfection of unwearied longsuffering and sincere love, which is given us through the keeping of both Testaments. For four fives are twenty; and there are five books of the law and four gospels. And when, grace enlightening, we come to the understanding and keeping of the law, we complete the number twenty; and the same number is in the length and breadth of the altar when the hearts of the elect, both Testaments teaching them, keep perseverance in such work even in persecutions, and cheerfulness of love even toward those who persecute.
**“AND OF TEN CUBITS IN HEIGHT”** — In the ten the hope of heavenly rewards is signified. Hence those who labour in the vineyard of the householder are rewarded with a denarius. Hence the altar, which signifies the elect, is raised ten cubits, to signify their everlasting life.
4.2:
**“He made also a molten sea”** — A BRAZEN SEA ALSO etc. The saving laver in which we are washed for the remission of sins. For the priests were washed in it, as is said in what follows, who signify all the elect, because they are members of the true priest. And rightly is this vessel called a sea, namely in memory of the Red Sea, in which, the Egyptians being destroyed and the people of God freed, the form of baptism went before. And baptism seeks of us cleanness of life in this world and promises the glory of eternal life in the future. Hence the sea is said to be ten cubits from brim to brim, because all that we ought to do is expressed in ten precepts. By the denarius also is signified the reward of good deeds, when it is promised to those labouring in the vineyard. The sea was therefore ten cubits from brim to brim: from the first baptized in the name of Jesus Christ to the last, the whole choir of the faithful ought to enter the one way of truth and hope from the Lord for the common crown of justice.
**“of ten cubits”** — or of cubits
**“from brim to brim, round in compass:”** — that the whole world might be signified as to be cleansed by the laver of life
**“IT WAS FIVE CUBITS HIGH”** — Because whatever we offend by sight, hearing, smell, taste or touch is all loosed in baptism. But the remission of past sins does not suffice unless each one thereafter applies himself to good works.
