Otherwise the devil who had gone out returns more manifold, and the last state of the man is made worse than the first. Hence he adds: And a line of thirty etc.
**“A LINE OF THIRTY CUBITS”** — This is the discipline of the heavenly precepts, by which we are bound back from our own wills. Whence: "A threefold cord is not easily broken", because the keeping of God's commandments in the hearts of the saints, made firm by faith, hope and love of the heavenly reward, can be loosed by no adversity.
4.3:
**“And under it there was the likeness of oxen, and some engravings on the outside of ten cubits compassed the brim of the sea as it were with two rows. And the oxen were cast,”** — These are the twelve apostles and their vicars, who carry the sea laid upon them when with ready devotion they fulfil the office of evangelizing enjoined on them, and build up the faith of the holy Trinity in the parts of the four-square world
**“AND SOME ON THE OUTSIDE OF TEN CUBITS”** — The carving ran round under the brim, encircling the sea for ten cubits. Two rows of storied carvings were cast. Since it was said before that "a line of thirty cubits compassed the sea", and it is now added that the carving placed under the brim encircled it for ten cubits, it is plain that the vessel was spread out and widened in the manner of a bowl, narrowing from the thirty cubits it had at the brim to ten. And storied carving is that which imitates the histories of things. Hence by the storied carvings with which the sea is surrounded the examples of former times are designated, that we may see by what works the saints pleased God from the beginning, and in what great unhappiness the reprobate perished for their crimes.
4.4: **“and the sea itself was set upon twelve oxen, three of which looked toward the north, and other three toward the west: and the other three toward the south, and the three that remained toward the east, and the sea was upon them: and the hinder parts of the oxen were inward under the sea.”** — THE HINDER PARTS etc. Because with what reward the preachers will be endowed for ever is arranged by the judgment of God, but is still hidden to us, to whom this cannot be hidden: that everyone who receives baptism unto salvation ought to have faith, hope and charity, and without these three virtues can neither work nor enter into salvation. Hence in Kings it is said: "And the thickness of the laver [was] three inches." The thickness of the laver is the firmness of virtue; of three inches, because the receiving of baptism is fortified by the strength of faith, hope and love.
4.5:
**“Now the thickness of it was a handbreadth,”** — NOW THE THICKNESS OF IT etc. A thickness which Josephus said was of four fingers, showing what the size of the handbreadth was. And these signify the same thing. For whoever does works in faith, hope and charity according to the teaching of the four gospels receives the reward of justice and of eternal life.
**“and the brim of it was like the brim of a cup,”** — the taste of the Lord's passion
**“or of a lily that is bent back:”** — the open brightness of the resurrection
**“and it held three thousand measures.”**
• in Kings, two thousand bates
• The sea holds three thousand measures when the sacrament of baptism, given in the faith of the Trinity, confers on those washed in it the remission of all sins.
**“THREE THOUSAND MEASURES”** — The thousand signifies perfection, because the ten makes a solid square. For ten times ten make a hundred, which is as it were a square figure, but flat; but that it may rise in height and be made solid, multiply a hundred by ten and they make a thousand. By this number the stable, unconquerable and as it were four-square conscience of the just is signified. For whichever way you turn a square, it will stand. So the mind of the elect is bent by no temptation from its state of uprightness.
4.6:
**“He made also ten lavers,”** — how these lavers were made is written more fully in Kings
**“HE MADE ALSO TEN LAVERS”** — In Kings thus: "He made also ten lavers of brass: one laver contained forty bates, and was of four cubits. And upon every base, in all ten, he put as many lavers" etc. The apostles and apostolic men, who are signified by the oxen carrying the sea, are expressed also by the bases prepared for carrying the lavers, as the lavers themselves signify baptism, which the sea figured. For in them the priests washed all that they were to offer in holocausts. And by the holocaust of the Lord can be understood the whole multitude of the faithful, which is baptized by him in water and fire. As then the priests washed in the sea signify those who through baptism are made partners of the high priest, so the holocausts express the same when after the washing of baptism they are filled with spiritual grace. For the victim is washed in the laver when the faithful man is drenched with the water of baptism; it is offered in holocaust when through the laying on of the bishop's hand he receives the gift of the Holy Spirit.
**“AND HE SET FIVE ON THE RIGHT HAND”** — The bases of the lavers were set on both sides of the temple, so that the grace of the sacred font might be signified as to be opened to both peoples. And there are five on each side, so that, as in the exposition of the sea, which we have said was five cubits high, it might be typically shown that all that had been offended through the five senses of the body was to be remitted through the laver of baptism. As then in the one sea set upon twelve oxen is expressed the unity of baptism, which was to be preached through the apostles in all the world, so also by the two rows of lavers it is mystically shown that the gentile world with Judea was to be brought forth into the one fellowship of faith through the wave of baptism.
4.7: **“CANDLESTICKS OF GOLD”** — The divine words, which bring forth the light of wisdom; whence: "Thy word is a lamp to my feet, and a light" etc. Hence Solomon says: "Because the commandment is a lamp, and the law a light." The candlesticks are twice five, because there are five volumes of the lawgiver, in which also the whole series of the old Testament [and] the five ages of the world are comprised. Five are placed on the right and five on the left, when after the Lord's incarnation the same Scripture is committed to both peoples, or is shown to be full of gospel figures, which was once thought to be understood only according to the letter.
4.8:
**“And also ten tables,”**
• in Kings in the singular number: "And the table of gold, upon which the loaves of proposition should be set"
• The golden table is sacred Scripture, fruitful [so the edition: 'secunda'] with the brightness of spiritual knowledge; of which the Psalm says: "Thou hast prepared a table before me, against them that afflict me." The loaves of proposition are the holy teachers, whose works are set before us as saving breasts for examples of life.
**“AND ALSO TEN TABLES”** — It is credible that these tables were made both for the loaves of proposition and for carrying the vessels of the Lord. Or he put the plural number for the singular in the usual way, as in Jesus Nave: "But the children of Israel transgressed the commandment, and took to their own use of the anathema", though Achor alone did this. Or because the loaves of proposition used to be baked before the sabbath, so as to be set forth at once on the sabbath on the table of proposition. Yet it could be that the new loaves, newly baked, were laid on those tables and kept there covered that night, until early in the morning, the old ones being taken away, they were set warm upon the table of proposition. But as the one table laden with twelve loaves signifies the unanimous concord of all Scripture fortified by apostolic authority, so the ten golden tables [signify] the words of the divine law and of the prophets, which bring forth to us as loaves the refreshment of the word of God, as they set forth the examples of the faithful placed as it were upon them, the brightness and miracles of the vessels of God.
4.9:
**“He made also the court of the priests,”**
• the outer court
• In Kings thus: "And king Solomon built the inner court with three rows of polished stones, and one row of cedar beams." He speaks briefly of the inner court, of the outer he seems to be wholly silent. But in the Words of the days mention is made of both. The inner court, then, which is called that of the priests because the priests and Levites ministered in it, surrounded the temple on every side; but on the east, where the entrance of the temple was, it was set much further from the temple, because there, that is, in front of the temple, the ministries of the sacred rites were done. There [was] the brazen altar for offering victims; there the ten lavers for washing them; there the brazen sea for washing the hands and feet of the priests when they entered to minister. And this court had three cubits of height, according to Josephus, so as to keep others from the entrance of the temple and signify that these things were lawful for the priests alone. It had a gate on the eastern side, up to which the people brought victims and sacrifices, to be received thence by the priests and carried to the altar. What is said less fully here of the courts or porches we have set out more fully in the book of Kings, according to Bede.
**“HE MADE ALSO THE COURT OF THE PRIESTS”** — The court of the priests expresses in the Church the life of the perfect, who by excellence of virtues draw near to the Lord and are wont to show others the way by word and work. For a priest [sacerdos] is so called because he gives sacred guidance [sacrum ducatum] to the lesser. By this name not only bishops or presbyters, but all who excel in loftiness of life and saving doctrine are wont to be called: those, namely, who profit not themselves only but many, who, presenting their bodies "a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God", exercise the priestly ministry; to whom it is said through Peter: "But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood" etc.
**“AND A GREAT HALL”** — Which was outside the court of the priests, into which all the people flocked to pray or to hear the word. This signifies in the Church the life and morals of the carnal, to whom it is said: "I could not speak to you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal" etc.
**“and a great hall,”** — And a hall etc. Well are the carnal signified by the great hall, because the number of such in the Church is much greater than that of the perfect. But as much as they surpass in number, so much they fall short in merit. Hence this great hall, though it holds very many, does not admit them to the office of the altar, nor even into the court of the priests itself; because the carnal and weak, though for the merit of chaste faith and piety they belong to the lot of the elect, are yet far from those who say: "I dare not to speak of any of those things which Christ worketh not by me, for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed."
**“and doors in the hall, which he covered with brass.”**
• this signifies the life and morals of the carnal, to whom it is said: "I could not speak to you as unto spiritual, but as unto carnal" etc.
• AND DOORS IN THE HALL etc. These signify that the entrance of faith is prepared by the word of preaching, so that those who come may learn how they ought to enter the Church of God through faith in Christ or the saving sacraments, and, after they have entered, how religiously they ought to live.
4.11:
**“And Hiram made”** — or also
**“caldrons,”** — for receiving the ashes of the altar of holocaust
**“AND HIRAM MADE CALDRONS”** — The caldrons receive the sacred ashes when the faithful with devout mind turn over the examples and sacraments of the Lord's passion for their own keeping, or look diligently on the end of the just, who after great struggles endured rejoice without end in the prize received; so that, having considered the virtues of their elders, they too may be made great. Whence: "Considering the end of their conversation, follow their faith."
**“and fleshhooks,”**
• fleshhooks, by which the flesh of the victims was drawn from the caldrons and offered for men to eat
• Some things in Paralipomenon which have been expounded in Kings we pass over. Some we have not found expounded, and we do not wish to exceed the custom of our littleness. For nowhere have we expounded anything of ourselves.
**“AND FLESHHOOKS”** — The fleshhooks signify the preachers, who refresh the souls of the faithful with the word of God, comparing spiritual things with spiritual, but ministering to the carnal the milk of simple doctrine; and those who wish to know the sacraments of Christ in summary and take them up for imitation are, as carnal men, filled with the flesh of the saving victim. And because it belongs to teachers to divide to each what is fitting, rightly are fleshhooks made for the priests, by which they may arrange the flesh of the victims as is fitting, and bring some to clean men, and leave others to be consumed by the fires of the altar; for some things are revealed to our lowliness for refreshment, some are open only to the knowledge of the Holy Spirit.
**“and bowls,”** — for offering the libations
**“and finished all the king's work in the house of God:”** — AND BOWLS etc. The bowls signify the broader and more open speech of holy doctrine, which gives a draught of wisdom to those who thirst devoutly, and grants fitting refreshment to those who labour devoutly through the ministry of the preachers, that they may come to the fountain of eternal life, from which those who drink "shall not thirst for ever".
4.12:
**“That is to say, the two pillars,”** — the preachers of both peoples
**“and the chapiters, and the heads,”** — the hearts of the preachers
**“and a kind of net work”** — as above
4.13:
**“And four hundred pomegranates, and two little nets:”** — as above
**“so that two rows of pomegranates were joined to each net, to cover the chapiters and the heads of the pillars.”** — of these it has been treated above
4.16: **“and the caldrons, and fleshhooks, and bowls. All the vessels did Hiram his father make for Solomon”** — that is, as a father to be revered
4.17:
**“In the country near the Jordan”** — IN THE COUNTRY NEAR THE JORDAN etc. The Jordan, in which Christ was baptized, who, dipped in its waves, turned for us the element of waters into the washing away of sins. And because every baptism of the faithful, by which we are consecrated to the Lord, is celebrated after the example of that baptism, rightly were the vessels of the house of the Lord made in the country of the Jordan. For we cannot be made vessels of election otherwise than by looking to his baptism and striving to be washed in the life-giving river. And it is to be noted that he says the vessels were made not only in the country of the Jordan but in its plain country, signifying the multiplication of the faithful, which was to be not only in Judea but in the breadth of the nations; whence: "The plains shall be joyful, and all that are in them." And elsewhere: "We have heard of it in Ephrata: we have found it in the fields of the wood." The king therefore cast the vessels of the house of the Lord in the plain country of the Jordan, because the Lord filled the whole breadth of the world with the baptism of salvation, from which he might make vessels of mercy.
**“IN A CLAY GROUND”** — The clay ground, from which the moulds were made for casting the vessels, signifies sacred Scripture, from which we receive the rule of living well. For as clay hardened by fire shows the form of the Lord's vessel, how great and of what kind they ought to be made, so Scripture shows us the rule of justice which we are to follow, and the examples of the saints, who stood unconquered in all things in the fire of tribulation, so that we may desire to be precious vessels in the house of the Lord. And the brass melted by fire enters the moulds of clay so that a vessel fit for heavenly ministries may be made, when we, softened [unclear in the edition: "salubriter humilitati"] and by the flame of divine charity or of human adversity, enter the way of the fathers by working well, that by running well we may come to their rewards. For it is not always necessary for us to be confined by the rules of working well; but when good work is completed, the palm of blessed reward is to be hoped for. Because the vessels were not always kept shut in the moulds of clay; when they had come to perfection, the enclosures of the moulds being broken, they were brought out into the light and arranged in the temple of the Lord, each in its place. Not that the works of the saints will perish, but when they have received the crown of justice, the offices of laborious working will cease.
4.19:
**“AND SOLOMON MADE”** — He dictated what Hiram completed by the work itself. But allegorically our Redeemer prepares the adornment of the Church in the holy preachers and all the faithful, and effects the works of the virtues, he who says: "Without me you can do nothing"; and elsewhere: "Every best gift and every perfect gift is from above" etc.
**“and the golden altar, and the tables,”** — that is, ten, of which it has been said above
**“and upon them the loaves of proposition:”** — this too has been expounded above
**“THE GOLDEN ALTAR”** — The hearts of the perfect, shining with the light of inward charity and chastity, whose loftiness the place of the altar also signifies. For it stood before the door of the Holy of holies, as we read in the making of the tabernacle; on it neither the blood of victims nor libations but only incense was burned, the upper part of which, rising, covered the ark and filled the oracle with an odour of sweetness. In which the saints are figured, who, while neglecting the desires of temporal things they seek heavenly things with their whole intent, are as it were placed within, near the oracle, and not far removed from the veil by which the temple and the Holy of holies are divided; because only in body do they dwell on earth, but with their whole mind are in heaven. And the smoke of the incense rises from this altar within the Holy of holies, where the ark is laid up, so that the prayers of the saints, kindled by the flame of charity, may reach heaven, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God. For on this altar not the blood of victims but only incense is burned, because such men have not works of flesh and blood to slay to the Lord on the altar of the heart, but offer vows of tears and prayers out of desire for the heavenly kingdom.
4.20:
**“The candlesticks also”** — as above
**“with their lamps to give light before the oracle according to the manner, of the finest gold:”** — because most bright with the light of true wisdom
4.21:
**“and certain flowers,”** — shapes of lilies on the candlestick, upon which the lamps were set
**“and lamps, and golden tongs:”** — snuffers, with which the wicks of the candlestick were snuffed, that, renewed, they might shine better
**“AND TONGS”** — The tongs for the use of the altar were made of brass. But these too, with which the lamps were cleaned, signify the interpretation of the spiritual sense through the offices of the teachers. For, transferring the very words of the sacred speech from history to allegory, from shadow to truth, they multiply as it were the light of knowledge in the Church, placed upon the mystical candlestick.
4.22:
**“The vessels also for perfumes,”** — the vessels in which the incense was made fragrant are the hearts of the teachers, in which prayer is pure and sweetly burning; whence: "Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight"
**“and the censers, and the bowls, and the mortars,”** — of a pure conscience
**“of the finest gold. And he graved the doors of the inner temple,”**
• in Kings thus: "And the hinges of the doors of the inner house of the holy of holies, and of the doors of the house of the temple, were of gold"
• the angelic ministries which open to us, when we go forth from the body, the entrance of heavenly life
**“AND THE DOORS OF THE TEMPLE”** — These are the teachers and priests who, by instructing, baptizing and giving communion of the mysteries of the body and blood of the Lord, open to us the first thresholds of the Church.

5.1:
**“SO ALL THE WORK WAS FINISHED”** — When the true peacemaker on the last day glorifies all the elect with the immortality of the resurrection. But as long as the state of this world goes on, Solomon does the work of the house of the Lord but does not finish it; because the Lord inspires and helps the hearts of the elect to do good, yet grants to none to be without sin, which he reserves for the faithful in the future. But he finishes all the work of his temple and makes it ready for dedication when he leads the elect, taken from this life, to the eternal kingdom. Hence it is built in seven years, and dedicated finished in the eighth. For in seven days all time revolves; the eighth is the day of judgment and resurrection, to which what follows fits.
**“And Solomon brought in”** — Christ
**“all the things that had been vowed by”** — in Kings, 'that he had sanctified'
**“David his father,”** — God the Father
**“the silver,”** — the eloquent, whom Christ by the grace of his Spirit shapes for speaking the gospel
**“and the gold,”** — those endowed with natural genius, whom, filled with his Spirit, he enlightens to consider the wonderful things in his law
**“and all the vessels”** — all the sons of the Church, whom the grace of the Holy Spirit inflames to love and seek the gifts of everlasting salvation
5.4: **“And when all the ancients of Israel were come, the Levites carried the ark,”** — THE LEVITES CARRIED THE ARK etc. This is done when Christ, the universal judgment being finished, brings the company of teachers and other faithful into the joy of the kingdom. And he lays up the vessels of divers kinds, silver or gold, in the treasuries of the house of the Lord, when those who have merited to enjoy the multitude of his sweetness "he hides in the secret of his face from the disturbance of men". And fitly there are many treasuries in which the vessels of love are laid up, but one house of the Lord in which the treasuries are; because there is one Church in which all the elect are contained, though differing in merits, and one heavenly homeland promised to all, though "star differeth from star in glory". Whence: "In my Father's house there are many mansions." Solomon therefore made one house of the Lord, but prepared in it many treasuries, hallowed by one blessing only, to receive vessels of divers kinds; because the Father's house is one, but in it are many mansions for receiving all those who fear and love him: "The Lord hath blessed the little with the great."
5.7: **“And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the Lord into its place,”** — the ark brought into the Holy of holies signifies the humanity of Christ assumed and led within the veil of the heavenly palace
5.9:
**“And the staves with which the ark was carried,”** — these are the preachers of the word, through whom he became known to the world
**“because they were a little longer, the ends of them were seen before the oracle: but if a man were a little outside, he could not see them. And the ark was there unto this present day.”**
• AND THE STAVES WITH WHICH etc. It is to be noted that although the ends of the staves were seen before the oracle by those who came nearer and looked diligently, yet it could not be that those ends themselves stood out before the oracle; because it was necessary that, the oracle being shut and the veil hung before the doors, the staves too should be hidden within with the ark and the cherubim; which could not be if the staves, projecting further, did not give room for the doors to be brought forward to shut; whose position Scripture has so diligently set out in a great sacrament. For it is agreed that the outer house of the temple designates the Church on pilgrimage on earth, but the Holy of holies the happiness of the inner homeland.
• The tips of the staves appeared outside before the oracle, not always, but when the doors of the oracle were opened; and not to all, but to those who, coming nearer, looked more attentively at what was within. But what the ark itself was like and how it was placed was permitted to be seen only by those who entered the oracle; because none of the saints in this life, though he raise himself much in loftiness of mind, but only the citizens of that homeland fully behold the glory of their Redeemer. But the staves were hidden with the ark in the oracle, because all the perfect who have gone before us are hidden in the secret of God's face from the disturbance of men. Yet the tips of the staves are seen, when the oracle is open, by those who draw near, when divine grace has given to the more perfect, who purify the oracle of their heart with their whole intent, something inward of the joy of the heavenly citizens to contemplate. Which contemplation is not granted to those who have withdrawn a little further; for the more they remain outside with wandering mind, the less they see the inward joys.
5.10: **“AND THERE WAS NOTHING ELSE IN THE ARK”** — He shows generally that in the ark there was nothing contrary to the law of the Lord contained in the two tables, but that only those things were laid up there which according to the commandments of the law were made typically for the worship of the one God and the commendation of our faith; so that "the shadow of things to come" might in all things bear witness to the truth to come, and might receive its end when that appeared in the world. And there was in the ark, according to Paul, a golden pot that had manna, because in the man Christ "dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead corporeally". There was also the rod of Aaron, which, cut off, had flowered again, because all power of judging belongs to him whose judgment seemed to be taken away in the humility of the passion. There were also the tables of the Testament, because in him are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. The staves also by which it was carried cleaved to it, because the teachers who once laboured in the word of Christ now rejoice in the glory of Christ by present vision. Whence: "I desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ."
5.11: **“And when the priests were come out of the sanctuary (for all the priests”** — for the twenty-four courses had not yet cast lots who should minister first or second or third, but all, sanctified, served alike
5.12:
**“CLOTHED WITH FINE LINEN”** — By the robes of fine linen is designated bodily chastity, white with cleanness; with this all are clothed who stand in the office of God and sound his praises with mouth, morals and act. For the cymbals signify the confession of the mouth; the psalteries, mortality [so the edition]; the harps, instructed with twenty-four strings, that is, with the prophetic and apostolic teachings, the mortification of the flesh and the vigour of good action.
**“sounded with cymbals, and psalteries, and harps, standing on the east side of the altar,”** — because by the altar of faith they awaited the rising of the eternal light
**“and with them the singers”** — otherwise: the teachers
**“THE SINGERS”** — Or the teachers, that is, expressed by the hundred and twenty, because the lawgiver completed the sum of his years in this number, and on the day of Pentecost believers in the same number received the grace of the Spirit the Paraclete.
5.13:
**“So when they all sounded together, both with trumpets, and voice, and cymbals, and organs, and with divers kinds of musical instruments, and lifted up their voice on high, the sound was heard afar off, so that when they began to praise the Lord, and to say: Give glory to the Lord for he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever: the house”** — the Synagogue
**“of the Lord was filled with a cloud,”** — with blindness of understanding
**“SO WHEN THEY ALL”** — While all the priests and Levites sang the praise of God in the temple with instruments of divers kinds, the priests could not stand and minister because of the cloud, or according to Kings because of the mist; because when Christ and the apostles preached his gospel, the proud high priests of the Jews, as their deserts required, while they hear the divine mysteries in parables, cannot minister, as priests of the house of the Lord, because of the cloud. They too, in the old Testament, while they disdain to search out the mystical senses covered by the veil of the letter, lose the ministry due to their faith because of the cloud. To them too that was cloudy which the Lord said openly of himself: "I and the Father are one", and that: "Before Abraham was made, I am." But because the darkness of unbelief had covered the minds of the hearers, the cloud, lying between, had as it were hidden the rays of the sun. For the cloud signifies darkness of understanding. This filled the synagogue, that is, the house of God, and the priests could not minister because of the cloud, because while they were darkened by their unbelief from the understanding of the incarnation of God, they lost the ministry of the true priesthood.
5.14: **“so that the priests could not stand and minister by reason of the cloud. For the glory of the Lord had filled the house of God.”** — FOR THE GLORY HAD FILLED etc. Because the mysteries which lay hid under the veil were opened by the coming of Christ to those who believed and received them worthily. But for the rest, who would not come to the faith, the former blindness remained. Whence: "To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God" etc.

6.1: **“IN A CLOUD”** — Hence Job: "The clouds are his covert." And the Psalmist: "Darkness was under his feet", and: "He made darkness his covert." The covert of the Lord is sacred Scripture, which bears heavenly sacraments under parables and figures. Whence: "I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them to little ones."
6.13:
**“For Solomon had made a brazen scaffold,”** — the solidity of true humility, which Christ taught by word and showed by example
**“and had set it in the midst of the hall, it was five cubits long, and five cubits broad,”** — because, according to the tradition of the law, he commends to us that we should have the length of patience and the breadth of love
**“and three cubits high:”** — because he teaches us to hold the confession of the holy Trinity in faith, hope and charity, and to persist firmly in it by working well
6.21: **“and that thou wouldst hear the prayer which thy servant prayeth in it. Hear”** — or and that thou mayest hear
6.26:
**“If the heavens be shut up, and rain”** — or the rain
**“do not fall”** — or falls
6.30: **“Then hear thou from heaven, from thy high dwellingplace, and forgive, and render to every one according to his ways, which thou knowest him to have in his heart: for thou only knowest the hearts of the faithful”** — otherwise: of the children
6.42: **“O Lord God, turn not away”** — or thou turn away

7.2: **“Neither could the priests enter into the temple of the Lord,”** — because the majesty had filled the temple of the Lord
7.5:
**“Then king Solomon offered a sacrifice of oxen,”** — of those who work well
**“twenty-two thousand, of rams”** — of those who govern well
**“a hundred and twenty thousand: and the king and all the people dedicated”** — he cleansed it with his blood
**“the house”** — the Church
**“of God.”** — HE DEDICATED [so the edition: 'DEDICAVI'] THE HOUSE etc. Christ cleansed it with his blood, and sanctified it with spiritual grace, and multiplied it with divers gifts of virtues. And the children of Israel dedicate it, because every faithful man, according to the gift bestowed on him by God, converts and advances his neighbours by word and example to better and more perfect things.
7.6: **“And the priests stood in their offices: and the Levites with the instruments of music of the Lord, which king David made to praise the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever”** — otherwise: for ever
7.7: **“HE SANCTIFIED”** — Because Christ accomplishes in the Church the things which could not be accomplished in the law because of its weakness. For it is the court of the house of the Lord, through which entrance lies open into the heavenly Jerusalem. Because, then, holocausts and sacrifices could not be offered on the altar of the old Testament, since all things were done there in figure, our king and priest set up a new altar of faith in the Church, on which they daily offer fat holocausts and sacrifices acceptable to God. Whence: "The sacrifice of praise shall glorify me: and there is the way by which I will shew him" etc.
7.8:
**“And Solomon kept the solemnity at that time seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great congregation, from the entering in of Emath”** — that is, the northern quarter of the land of promise
**“to the torrent”** — Rhinocorura
**“of Egypt.”**
• the southern quarter
• AND SOLOMON KEPT etc. RABANUS. I do not think anything else is to be understood here than that, the seven days of the dedication of the temple being completed, the days of the Feast of Tabernacles followed, because according to the law they began on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and ended on the twenty-second. Both festivals, then, having been duly carried out, and the eighth day of Tabernacles finished, Solomon sent the people away to their homes, rejoicing and glad for the good which the Lord had done to David and to Solomon and to Israel his people.
• Solomon, the work of the temple being completed, held a solemn festival, and a multitude of people with him from the entering in of Emath to the torrent of Egypt; this is the inward joy of the saints which they have for ever with the true peacemaker. For Emath is interpreted 'truth of the Lord'. And by the brook or torrent of Egypt we understand temporal death, which no one in Egypt, that is, in the darkness of this world, can escape. Whence: "Who is the man that shall live, and not see death?" Of Christ also it is said: "He shall drink of the torrent in the way: therefore shall he lift up the head." All Israel, then, from the brook of Egypt to Emath, keep a solemn feast with Solomon, because the saints after the end of the present life enjoy eternal joys with Christ. They celebrate the festival for twice seven days, because the elect, enlightened by the grace of the sevenfold Holy Spirit, rejoice in this life, which runs by the number seven, in hope, and in the sabbath, that is, the future rest of souls, in reality, by the receiving of the truth itself.
7.10:
**“So on the three and twentieth day of the seventh month, he sent away the people to their tents, joyful and glad for the good that God had shewn to David,”** — that is, the sin which he had committed against Urias the Hethite being forgiven, he granted him an everlasting kingdom
**“and to Solomon,”** — whom, born of a foreign wife, the law forbade to enter the Church of God, he permitted [to enter] and raised to the kingdom
**“and to Israel his people.”**
• to whom, after so great a multitude of transgressions, he permitted to have a most magnificent temple for his worship, and for a long time granted rest from its enemies
• SO ON THE DAY etc. That is, after the eighth day of the solemnity of Tabernacles, as is contained in Kings. And it signifies that after the end of that life, and after the sabbath rest of the holy souls in which they rest before the judgment, in the eighth age, that is, on the day of resurrection, the saints will receive immortal bodies and be placed in the heavenly mansions according to the quality of their merits, where they will always rejoice, praising God in all the good things which the Father has conferred in Christ on the Christian people.

8.2: **“the cities which Hiram had given”** — HIRAM HAD GIVEN. That is, had given back; because when Solomon had given them, they did not please him. Therefore Solomon assigned them to his own uses.
8.4: **“And he built Palmira”** — which in Hebrew is called Thamar
8.5: **“And he built Bethoron the upper, and Bethoron the nether, walled cities, having gates, and bars, and bolts.”** — BETHORON THE UPPER AND THE NETHER etc. It is a city as far as which Jesus [Josue] pursued the enemy kings, in the tribe of Ephraim etc., as far as: and another Bethoron the nether, given to the Levites for a possession.
8.6:
**“Balaath also,”** — it is a city in the tribe of Juda
**“and all the strongest cities that were Solomon's, and all the cities of the chariots, and the cities of the horsemen. All that he would, did”** — "He hath done all things whatsoever he would"
**“king Solomon”** — Christ
**“and ordered: he built in Israel, and in Libanus, and in all the land of his dominion.”** — AND ALL THE STRONGEST CITIES etc. That is, Ezer, Mageddo, Gazer and Mello, which all show the beauty of the Church, because the true Solomon prepared it for himself for praise and joy in the gladness of his kingdom. And Mello is interpreted 'fulfilment', Ezer 'separated and sanctified', Mageddo 'his upper chamber', Gazer 'cutting off' or 'division', Bethoron 'house of mountains', Balaath 'ascending'. And holy Church is the city of the living God, where the will of God is daily fulfilled, and, separated from all error of unbelievers, it is sanctified by faith and good work. There is the refreshment of the virtues. It discerns clean and unclean, and vice from virtue; and it is the house of mountains, that is, the dwelling of the saints, and with the fruit of justice, "like a palm tree flourishing", it "goes from virtue to virtue, to see the God of gods in Sion". Solomon fortified all his villages, because Christ so fortifies the companies of his faithful with the protection of his grace that they can resist their spiritual enemies. In Libanus: that is, in the temple, which was clothed with the beauty of cedars, whence Zacharias: "Open thy gates, O Libanus"; or in the royal buildings, which were made of the wood of Libanus.
8.7:
**“All the people that were left”** — Jews, gentiles, heretics
**“of the Hethites, and Amorrhites, and Pherezites, and Hevites, and Jebusites, who were not of the stock of Israel,”** — of the number of the saints
8.8:
**“of their children, and of their posterity, whom they had not slain, Solomon made”** — Christ
**“to be tributaries unto this day.”** — the impious lives for the just
8.9:
**“But of the children of Israel he set not”** — because they are not children of the bondwoman but of the free, by which freedom Christ has made us free
**“to serve in the king's works:”** — to the observances of the law or to gentile rite
**“for they were men of war,”** — against the spiritual wickednesses
**“and chief captains,”** — leading themselves and others well
**“and commanders of his chariots”** — that is, of those who follow the teaching of the evangelists
8.10:
**“TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY”** — The hundred, which in counting on the fingers passes from the left hand to the right, signifies eternal life. The fifty signifies the remission of sins, eternal rest and the grace of the Holy Spirit; because in the Psalm of the same number penance, confession and the remission of sins are described, and by the jubilee the future rest; and by Pentecost, in the coming of the Holy Spirit, the sevenfold grace is expressed.
**“WHO TAUGHT THE PEOPLE”** — Because from both peoples he chose rulers of the Church who, enlightened by spiritual grace and fully taught, should teach by their example the remission of sins and the life of eternal salvation, and perpetual blessedness to be sought.
8.12:
**“Then offered”** — through his members
**“Solomon”** — Christ
**“holocausts”** — of good works
**“to the Lord upon the altar of the Lord,”** — of the catholic faith
**“which he had built”** — in the Church
**“before the porch,”**
• the entrance of the heavenly homeland
• HOLOCAUSTS TO THE LORD. A holocaust is called 'wholly burnt'. This is burnt on the altar when in the heart of each of the elect, who has vowed himself wholly, that is, in flesh and heart, to God, good work is kindled with the glowing fire of charity.
8.13:
**“that every day an offering might be made on it”** — through all the time of the present life until the consummation of the world
**“according to the ordinance of Moses, on the sabbaths,”** — for eternal rest
**“and on the first days of the months,”** — for newness of life
**“and on the festival days,”** — for the receiving of heavenly joy
**“three times a year,”** — in the faith of the holy Trinity
8.14:
**“And he appointed according to the order of David”** — according to what is written in the law of God and in the prophets
**“his father the offices of the priests in their ministries: and the Levites in their order, to praise, and minister before the priests according to the rite of every day: and the porters in their divisions by gate and gate: for so David the man of God had commanded.”** — ACCORDING TO THE RITE OF EVERY DAY etc. He orders all things in the Church according to what befits each time, that each order, performing its office, may minister worthily.
8.17:
**“TO ASIONGABER”** — It is said to be an island not far from Ailath in the Red Sea, where the fleet of Josaphat perished.
**“Then Solomon went to Asiongaber, and to Ailath on the coast of the Red Sea, which is in the land of Edom.”** — The fleet which Solomon made in Asiongaber, which is interpreted 'hastening' or 'strong' or 'manfully', is understood as the Church of the faithful, which, set in the sea of this world, strives to acquire the treasures of wisdom and knowledge and the riches of the virtues; where Hiram's servants, sailors and skilled in the sea, are with Solomon's servants, because gentiles learned in the wisdom of the world are joined in the unity of faith with those skilled in the law of Moses. These our Solomon sends to Ophir, which is interpreted 'weakening', to bring gold from there, when they labour to seek a precious sense in the lowliness of the letter; and, having received the sum of four hundred and fifty talents of gold, they bring it to the king, when through the grace of the Holy Spirit they find in the divine books the precious sense of history, allegory, tropology and anagogy, and render it [unclear in the edition: "eum sapientie et consilio divina ascribentes"].
8.18: **“TO OPHIR”** — Ophir, the name of a province, called after one of the descendants of Heber, of whose stock those who came, Josephus relates, dwelt from the river Cophen as far as the region of India which is called Geria.

9.1:
**“And the queen of Saba,”** — a royal city of Ethiopia, which Josephus relates was surnamed Meroe by king Cambyses from the name of his sister
**“AND THE QUEEN OF SABA”** — The queen of the south, who, roused from the furthest ends [of the earth], came to hear the wisdom of Solomon, figured the Church of the gentiles that was to come to Christ, which, "surrounded with variety in gilded clothing, forgetting her people and her father's house", was barbarian in race, not in mind, because she desired to become a fellow citizen of the saints. Whence: "The queen of the south shall rise in judgment with this generation."
**“SABA”** — Saba is interpreted 'conversion' or 'captivity', because the Church, converted to the faith of Christ, merited to belong to the lot of his captivity, of which it is said: "Ascending on high, he led captivity captive." She brought to the true Solomon on camels spices, gold and precious stones, when she brought to the faith of Christ gentiles misshapen by the strength of their sins, but flourishing in genius and study, and apt, as the preachers dispensed it, to receive the brightness of wisdom and the precious gems of the virtues; with which she honoured our Solomon with solemn worship, nay, honoured by him, received a greater grace of spiritual gift. Whence in what follows: King Solomon gave the queen of Saba all that she desired etc. For in the present he confers the grace of the Holy Spirit and wisdom and virtues; in the future, in the sight of his glory, he will bestow eternal life.
**“having heard of the fame of Solomon, came to try him with hard questions in Jerusalem, with great riches, and camels, which carried spices, and abundance of gold, and precious stones. And when she was come to Solomon,”** — to Christ
**“she spoke to him all that was in her heart.”** — what she thought to be wholesome and necessary for herself
9.2:
**“And Solomon explained to her all that she proposed:”** — through the knowledge of the law and the grace of the Holy Spirit
**“and there was not any thing which he did not make clear unto her.”** — because here she knows some things in part, but in the future "she will see face to face, and will know even as she is known"
9.3: **“AND WHEN SHE HAD SEEN”** — These things fit the Church, which, having heard the miracles of Christ, was stirred to seek him. But after she came to him through baptism and faith, having considered the testimonies of Scripture, she recognized the presence of the Godhead, and what she had heard of him before seemed little to her in comparison with the grace received. Hence also, in wonder, she bursts out in his praise, saying: Blessed are thy men etc.
9.7:
**“Blessed are thy men, and blessed are thy servants, who stand before thee at all times,”** — "Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: they shall praise thee for ever and ever"
**“and hear thy wisdom.”** — through which he deigns to show himself to clean hearts
9.8:
**“Blessed be the Lord thy God,”** — that is, the Father
**“who would set thee on his throne, king of the Lord thy God.”** — "He shall sit upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom"
9.10: **“And the servants of Hiram with the servants of Solomon brought gold from Ophir, and thyine trees,”** — these [are] round like pine wood, but much whiter and very shining
9.11:
**“And the king made of the thyine trees”**
• in Kings thus: "King Solomon made of the thyine trees the rails of the house of the Lord"
• OF THE THYINE TREES. Christ sets the precious trees, that is, the holy teachers, the greenness of whose faith never withers, nor do the leaves of their words fall, but "they bring forth the fruit of good works in their seasons", for the defence of the house of the Lord and of the royal house, that is, for the strengthening of the Church, that, walled about on every side by their teachings and examples, it may not feel ruin. These are said to be made as harps and lyres for praising the Lord, because "whatsoever they shall do shall prosper", and they proclaim the praise of the Lord in prosperity and adversity with heart and mouth and work, and do all things to the glory of God, and day and night do not cease to praise the name of the Lord.
**“stairs”** — others: rails
9.13:
**“And the weight of the gold that was brought to Solomon every year, was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold:”** — in the six, the perfection of the gifts which are to be brought by us to our king
**“SIX HUNDRED SIXTY-SIX”** — Six multiplied by six makes sixty [so the edition]. A hundred also, taken six times, gives a hundred and six [so the edition]. The ten signifies the perfection of the commandments, the hundred the reward of eternal blessedness. For the king desires our perfection, that he may have those to whom he may render a perfect reward. Whence: "Be you perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect"; "If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments." And after a little: "If thou wilt be perfect, go, sell what thou hast" etc.; "and every one that hath left house etc. shall receive an hundredfold, and shall possess life everlasting."
9.14: **“AND ALL THE KINGS OF ARABIA”** — Divers nations and merchants and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the lands offer gold and silver to Solomon, because every nation and every person vies, according to its strength, to offer our peacemaker the gift of right faith, purity of sense, fulness of holy confession, brightness of eloquence. Whence: "The kings of Tharsis and the islands shall offer presents" etc., "and all kings of the earth shall adore him: all nations shall serve him."
9.15:
**“AND SOLOMON MADE”** — Because the fathers of both Testaments, perfect in doctrine and working, proved by work whatever they taught by word.
**“two hundred golden spears of the sum of six hundred pieces of gold,”** — in Kings: of sicles
**“GOLDEN SPEARS”** — This is the armour of God, by which we stand against the snares of the devil; which the holy preachers have, who guard the house of God and keep watch at its door lest the ancient enemy steal in. Whence: "Threescore valiant ones surround the bed of Solomon."
9.16:
**“AND THREE HUNDRED SHIELDS”** — It signifies perfect faith in the confession of the holy Trinity. Well do the guards of the house of God carry golden spears and shields, because the preachers, who are the guards of the Church, shining with the brightness of wisdom, pierce the enemies with the darts of words, and "with the shield of faith extinguish all the fiery darts of the most wicked one".
**“with which each shield was covered: and the king put them in the armoury,”** — that is, the Church, where the spiritual armour is laid up, by which the faithful are protected and the enemies driven back
**“which was planted”** — through faith
**“with a wood.”** — with the gathering of divers nations, to show the beauty of the Church and the delights of the king
9.17:
**“The king also made a throne”** — That is, the Church, in which the just peacemaker reigns and judges, because "the soul of the just is the seat of God".
**“of ivory, great,”** — the Church is adorned with chastity; for the elephant is temperate and does not use a second mate
**“and overlaid it with the finest gold.”** — because he makes the splendour of his grace shine in the Church when he shows his presence with signs and miracles
9.18:
**“SIX STEPS ALSO”** — In the six [is] the perfection of good works. For in six days God made the world, and six is the first perfect number. And by good and perfect works one ascends to heaven.
**“A FOOTSTOOL”** — [It signifies] the saints shining with the splendour of the virtues, in whom God dwells. By the footstool can also be marked those who are weak in the body of Christ, as penitents, or those who will be converted last, namely near the end of the world, who yet are golden, refined and proved in the fire of the tribulations of that time.
**“and two arms on either side, and two lions standing by the arms,”** — the fathers of both Testaments, strong in mind, ruling themselves and others
**“STANDING BY THE ARMS”** — Because the holy fathers attributed whatever good they did in the gospel not to themselves but to God. Whence: "Not to us, O Lord, not to us; but to thy name give glory."
**“ARMS”** — In Kings thus: "And two hands on either side holding the seat." These are the comforts of divine grace, which advance the Church to the heavenly kingdom. Or this is designated by the two, because in both Testaments this is most commended: that nothing good can be accomplished except by divine help. Whence: "Without me you can do nothing."
9.19:
**“and twelve other little lions”** — the preachers following the apostolic teaching
**“SIX STEPS”** — Because they strive by teaching and example that the labour of the unwise may not totter in working, but may keep uprightness strongly in the progress of the virtues.
**“THERE WAS NOT SUCH A THRONE”** — Because of the Church it is written: "Strength and beauty are her clothing" etc., and: "Many daughters have gathered together riches: thou hast surpassed them all."
9.20:
**“ALL THE VESSELS ALSO”** — The souls of the saints, which serve the will of God, shining with the splendour of wisdom and charity, contain the drink of living water, "which becomes in them a fountain of water springing up into life everlasting".
**“SILVER”** — The word of God is not in speech but in power, as "in the preaching of the gospel, not in the persuasive words of human wisdom, but in shewing of the Spirit and power".
9.21: **“For the king's ships went to Tharsis with the servants of Hiram once in three years: and they brought from thence gold, and silver, and ivory, and apes, and peacocks.”** — FOR THE KING'S SHIPS WENT WITH THE SERVANTS etc. Christ sends into the world the apostles, teachers of the gospel, whom he chose from the Jews, together with the preachers chosen from the gentiles, with a threefold confession but one faith, that in those who believe they may bring him the gold of wisdom, the silver of eloquence and the ivory of chastity. And the ape is a clever animal and an imitator of man, and can signify the philosophers, who sometimes change the senses of true wisdom and set forth the acts of moral life in their disciplines. The peacock, which shows its praised feathers, signifies those who for the praises of men display the appearances of various virtues; but, instructed by the teaching of the preachers, they learn to do good in view of God alone, and are fitted for the delights of the eternal king.
9.22:
**“So king Solomon was magnified”** — "For who in the clouds can be compared to the Lord?" etc.
**“above all the kings of the earth”** — "Great and terrible above all them that are about him"
9.23: **“And all the kings of the earth desired to see the face of Solomon,”** — "My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: thy face, O Lord, will I still seek." And elsewhere: "As the hart panteth after the fountains of water, so my soul panteth after thee, O God"
9.25:
**“FORTY THOUSAND HORSES”** — The forty signifies the times of the ancient law. For Moses, about to receive the law, fasted forty days, and the people instructed by him went round the desert forty years. And the six [so the edition: 'senarius'] signifies the present time, in which the apostolic doctrine of the New Testament nourishes the people. Well then are the horses of Solomon placed in the stalls numbered by forty, because by the hardness of the old law the insolence of the former people was restrained. And the twelve signifies the present time, in which apostolic authority nourishes the people of the gentiles with the doctrine of the new Testament.
**“and of chariots, and of horsemen twelve thousand, and he placed them in the cities of the chariots,”** — in the keeping of the disciplines
**“and where the king was in Jerusalem.”** — IN JERUSALEM: in the vision of peace. The distance of the places shows a distinction of dispositions. For those who are in the cities of the chariots signify those who are taught in the various disciplines of the Church by spiritual masters. But others, already taught and fitted for the use of the heavenly king, merit to have his presence. Whence: "The chariot of God is attended by ten thousands" etc. And elsewhere: "Who wilt ride upon thy horses: and thy riding is salvation."
9.26:
**“And he exercised authority”** — "And he shall rule from sea to sea" etc.
**“over all the kings”** — that is, over all who exercise the power of right rule
**“from the river Euphrates”** — fruitful or increasing
**“OF THE PHILISTINES”** — Of those falling doubly. For Philistiim is interpreted 'double ruin'. This is done when, through the absolution of sins from its beginning in the Jordan of baptism up to the conversion of all nations to the faith of Christ, the grace of [his] power overflows; so that where there was the outflow of carnal desires, there the seed of the virtues may be established, and where the idolatry and shameful conduct of the peoples was a double ruin, there through the confession of right faith and the worship of piety the life of the faithful may rise to the heavenly kingdom. For his power reaches to the borders of Egypt, that is, the darkened minds of unbelievers, which he fills with the light of faith. Whence: "Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down" etc.
9.27:
**“And he made silver as plentiful”** — in the silver, the brightness of eloquence and the pleasantness of the Church's doctrine
**“in Jerusalem as stones,”** — of the hardness and insensibility of the gentiles
**“AND HE MADE AS PLENTIFUL”** — The true Solomon gives in the Church plenty of silver as of stones, when he turns the hearts of the gentiles, insensible to the understanding of the true God, who worshipped stones for God, to the meditation of the law and the preaching of the gospel. Of whom it is said: "Let them that make them become like unto them" etc. And elsewhere: "God is able of these stones to raise up children to Abraham." He gives also a multitude of cedars as of sycamores, because he advanced the barrenness of the gentiles, who would not raise themselves on high, to the fruitfulness of good works and virtues.
**“and cedars”** — in the cedars, the fineness and fragrance of the virtues
**“AND CEDARS”** — The cedar is of an incorruptible nature, pleasant in smell, bright in appearance, and when kindled it drives away and kills serpents by its brightness.
**“as many as the sycamores”** — in the sycamores, the vileness and unfruitfulness of unbelievers
9.29:
**“Now the rest of the acts of Solomon first and last,”** — the first, which he did before he transgressed, such as the building of the temple and the various offering of sacrifices
**“NOW THE REST”** — Those which he did after he transgressed the law of God, when his foreign wives drew him even to idolatry. Many indeed, like Solomon, begin well and end badly; and no one ought to be called blessed before his death and last funeral rites.

10.8: **“HE LEFT THE COUNSEL OF THE ANCIENTS”** — The Hebrews say these were Banaias the son of Joiada and Jahiel the son of Hachamoni, who is also called Chilla; whose counsel being left, Roboam began to deal with the young men, that is, Aduram, who in what follows is said to have been stoned, and the like. And we often call a man young not in age but in mind. For Roboam was not young in age but in sense, who began to reign in the forty-first year of his age.
10.13: **“AND THE KING ANSWERED ROUGHLY, LEAVING THE COUNSEL OF THE ANCIENTS”** — This signifies the bad rulers in the Church who, given to earthly desires, neglect the care of those under them and rejoice in the multitude of those who obey them. And Roboam is interpreted 'breadth of the people'. These are they who enter the broad way that leads to death, not the narrow that leads to life. And leaving the counsel of the fathers, whose words and deeds tend to the height of perfection, they choose to obey the counsel of young men, who weigh them down with praises and flatteries, who "are blind, and leaders of the blind" etc. Whence: "Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child" etc.
10.15: **“And he did not condescend to the people's requests: for it was the will”** — or of the will

11.19: **“who bore him sons, Jehus, and Somorias, and Zoom.”** — or -e-

12.2:
**“And in the fifth year of the reign of Roboam,”** — AND IN THE FIFTH YEAR etc. Bad rulers by their negligence provoke the prince of darkness against the Church, who carries off the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king, when he takes away the knowledge of the Scriptures and the works of the virtues from the incautious and slothful.
**“Sesac king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had sinned against the Lord,”** — SESAC KING etc. 'Fine linen of haircloth' or 'joy of haircloth'. Fine linen signifies subtlety; haircloth, which is made of goats' hair, sins. In the fine linen of haircloth, then, [is] the craft of devilish fraud in persuading to sin. Sesac carries off the riches of Jerusalem when the devil, who cunningly deceives and rejoices in the multitude of sins, strips churchmen of spiritual knowledge and the work of virtue, and plunges with himself into the pit of perdition, despoiled, those who seemed comely in the Church.
12.9: **“So Sesac king of Egypt departed from Jerusalem, taking away the treasures of the house of the Lord, and of the king's house, and he took all with him, and the golden shields which Solomon had made,”** — SHIELDS. Solomon made golden shields and gave them to the guards of his house, when Christ committed spiritual knowledge through the two Testaments to the teachers of the Church for protecting the people. This the ancient enemy draws away backward through neglect. For when they attend to earthly things and care less for heavenly ones, he leaves them stripped of their former office and knowledge, as it were despoiled of riches in their own house. And such, when they see themselves deprived of spiritual sense, seek abundance through eloquence of words, whose sonority they set against the enemies for those under them like the firmness of brazen shields. But as much as brass is cheaper than gold, so much is eloquence inferior to the fruit of true wisdom. Whence: "Where there are many words, there is oftentimes want."
12.15:
**“OF SEMEIAS”** — Who above rebuked Roboam and the sons of Juda for their sins.
**“and of Addo the seer,”** — Addo, who is also Abdo; this is he who was sent by the Lord into Samaria to rebuke Jeroboam for the altar which he had made, who was killed on the way because, seduced by a false prophet against the command of the Lord, he ate in that place.
**“diligently recorded. And Roboam and Jeroboam fought against each other all their days.”** — the Church, which persists in the unity of faith, always fights with heretics and schismatics and with all the enemies of the catholic faith

13.4: **“And Abia stood up upon mount Semeron, which was in Ephraim, and said: Hear me, Jeroboam, and all Israel.”** — SEMERON. It is a city which Jesus [Josue] took, its king being slain, which they say is now called Sebaste, a town of Palestine, where the relics of John the Baptist were laid. But we read in Kings that Amri king of Israel bought the mount Semeron of one Semer, and built a city on its top, which from the name of its owner, namely Semer, he called Semeron.
13.19:
**“And Abia pursued after Jeroboam as he fled, and took cities from him, Bethel,”** — Bethel: a city at the next milestone from Aelia, on the right for those going to Neapolis, which was formerly called Luza, that is, Amygdalon, and fell to the lot of Benjamin, near Bethaven and Hai, which Jesus [Josue] took by storm, its king being slain.
**“and her daughters, and Jesana”** — a city of the king of Juda
**“EPHRON”** — It is a city in the tribe of Juda. Hence too a very large village is still called Ephrea, toward the north, at the twentieth milestone from Aelia.
13.20: **“And Jeroboam was not able to resist any more in the days of Abia: and the Lord struck him, and he died.”** — IN THE DAYS OF ABIA. Not Jeroboam [so the edition], in whose twentieth year, according to the book of Kings, Asa the son of Abia reigned over Juda and Jerusalem; but Abia, who, having taken Bethel, kept the idols for a stumbling block to Israel, as the Hebrews assert.

14.1: **“And Abia slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead, in whose days the land was quiet for ten years.”** — this signifies those who begin well and end badly
14.2: **“And Asa did that which was good and pleasing in the sight of his God, and destroyed the altars”** — casting away idolatry

15.5:
**“At that time there shall be no peace to him that goeth out”** — or to the one going out
**“and cometh in”** — or to the one coming in

16.14:
**“And they buried him in his own sepulchre, which he had made for himself in the city of David: and they laid him on his bed full of spices and harlots' ointments,”**
• that is, with the scents which the luxurious use for lust
• SPICES AND OINTMENTS etc. This is the vain boasting of fame which philosophers or poets bestow after the death of their kings, or even false Christians on their masters when they die; and they cast these into the fire, because all the things which they put forth here without profit and edification of the brethren are shown to be liable to the fires of hell.
**“which were made by the art of the perfumers, and they burned them over him with very great pomp.”** — THEY BURNED OVER HIM WITH POMP etc. Note that, as the Hebrews hand down, for kings, out of reverence, burnings of precious garments were made together with spices. Hence elsewhere: According to the burnings of thy fathers they shall make for thee. For it was the custom among the ancients that the precious ornaments of kings were burnt on a pyre after their death for their obsequies, but without the bodies.

17.3: **“And the Lord was with Josaphat, because he walked in the first ways of David his father: and trusted not in Baalim,”** — HE WALKED IN THE WAYS OF DAVID HIS FATHER etc. It shows that he was a doer of the divine commandments, as David [was] before he sinned with the wife of Urias; the satisfaction for which sin gained him an eternal memory.
17.5:
**“And the Lord established the kingdom in his hand, and all Juda brought”** — every faithful man
**“presents to Josaphat:”** — of sound doctrine, of good working
**“and he acquired immense riches,”** — many daughters have gathered together riches
**“and much glory.”** — of spiritual wisdom
**“ALL JUDA BROUGHT PRESENTS”** — This signifies the faithful from the gentiles who, leaving the error of their fathers, come together to Christ, washed by baptism, anointed with chrism, receiving from Christ the Christian name and royal dignity. Whence: "You are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood" etc. For [it was] in the time of Josaphat, 'dowry of the Lord' or 'he who is endowed'; and because the Church of the gentiles, bought by the blood of Christ, given the pledge of the Holy Spirit, merited the fellowship of the heavenly Bridegroom and the society of the kingdom. To her infinite riches were made when divers nations believe, and in the acquiring of divers virtues.
17.6: **“And when his heart had taken courage for the ways of the Lord, he took away also the high places and the groves out of Juda.”** — every stumbling block from the congregation of believers
17.7: **“And in the third year of his reign he sent of his princes”** — that is, preachers, to preach the gospel of Christ and teach the precepts of the law
17.10: **“AND SO THERE CAME”** — Because of the virtues which are done in the Church, the boldness of the gentiles is taken away, and they are stirred to bring to Christ the gifts of faith and the tribute of good work and devout confession and the cattle of simplicity.
17.11:
**“The Philistines also brought presents to Josaphat, and tribute in silver, and the Arabians brought him cattle, seven thousand seven hundred rams,”** — that is, of prelates enlightened by the grace of the Holy Spirit
**“and as many he goats.”** — that is, sinners brought to the service of God through confession and penance

18.1:
**“Now Josaphat was rich and very glorious,”** — the Christian people, which keeps the catholic religion
**“and he was joined by affinity to Achab.”** — HE WAS JOINED BY AFFINITY TO ACHAB. These are the heresiarchs, who lead the crowd of the lost through the byways of errors and plunge them into the precipice of death. Josaphat was joined by affinity to Achab and went down to him to Samaria to help against the enemies, and he signifies those who from among the catholics lean to the friendship of heretics; who, though they do not depart from the path of right faith, yet do not avoid the society and communion of the erring. Against whom it is said: "A man that is a heretic, after the first and second admonition, avoid." Hence Josaphat is rebuked by Jehu the seer, the son of Hanani, that prophet, namely, who had rebuked Asa, because he had given help to the impious and was joined in friendship with those who hate the Lord.
18.18: **“But he said: Hear ye therefore the word of the Lord: I saw the Lord sitting upon his throne, and all the army of heaven standing by him on the right hand and on the left.”** — I SAW THE LORD SITTING UPON HIS THRONE. The throne of the Lord [is] the angelic powers, over whom God presiding on high orders all things below. The army of heaven [is] the breadth of the ministering angels on the right hand and on the left. God, who is so within all things that he is also outside all things, is not enclosed by right or left; but the right hand of God [is] the good angels, the left the reprobate. For not only the good, who help, minister to God, but also the evil, who, unwilling to return, oppress; of whom it is said: "Against the spirits of wickedness in the high places." On the right, then, and on the left the army of angels stands, because the will of the elect spirits agrees with the divine will, and the mind of the reprobate, serving its own malice, obeys the judgment of his strictness. Hence the lying spirit leaps forth into the midst, by whom Achab is stirred up as his deserts required. For neither does a good spirit wish to serve falsehood or to be a lying spirit in the mouth of the prophets. But because Achab was worthy to be condemned by such a deception, so that he who had often fallen willingly into guilt should be taken unwillingly to punishment, licence is justly given to the malignant spirits, that those whom they strangle willing in the snare of sin they may drag unwilling into the punishment of sin. And he who does not change his reprobate life, when he asks anything of a prophet, hears, God so disposing, what he deserves to hear as one to be condemned. For behold, the house of Israel had departed from the worship of God to the service of idols, and yet often came to the prophets by whom it had been wont to be deceived, asking for prosperity. But because, doing perverse things, it did not deserve to hear prosperous things, [it was done] that the people of sinners might be taken in its own heart; so that it, who had offended by following unbelief, might be so deceived by the flatteries of the prophets as not to fear because it had offended, and might be snatched to punishment the more harshly the more securely it lived in guilt.

19.10: **“Every cause that shall come to you of your brethren, that dwell in their cities, between kindred and kindred, wheresoever there is question concerning the law, the commandment, the ceremonies, the justifications: shew it them, that they may not sin against the Lord, nor”** — otherwise: and that ... not

20.1: **“After this the children of Moab, and the children of Ammon, and with them of the Ammonites, gathered themselves together against Josaphat to fight against him.”** — WITH THEM. It signifies the Edomites; but the writer of the history preferred to mark what was done by the name of the allies rather than publicly divulge the impiety of the shameless.
20.2:
**“And there came messengers and told Josaphat, saying: There cometh a great multitude against thee from those places that are beyond the sea, and out of Syria,”** — FROM THOSE PLACES etc. It signifies those places which are beyond the Salt Sea, which elsewhere is called the lake Asphaltites or the Dead Sea.
**“and behold they are in Asasonthamar,”** — it is interpreted 'palm tree'
**“ENGADDI”** — Even to this day a very large village of the Jews by the Dead Sea is so called, whence balsam comes; which Solomon calls the vineyards of Engaddi.
20.5: **“And when Josaphat stood up in the midst of the assembly of Juda and Jerusalem in the house of the Lord, before the new court,”** — the temple itself, which Josaphat cleansed [so the edition: 'purgabit'] of the uncleannesses of idolatry and renewed; and what the children of Israel had made old by sinning they renewed by repenting
20.16:
**“Tomorrow you shall go down against them: for they will come up by the ascent named Sis, and you shall find them at the end of the brook, which is over against the wilderness of Jeruel.”**
• FOR THEY WILL COME UP BY THE ASCENT NAMED SIS etc. Which according to the Hebrews is also Jeruel. For they say it is called Sis, that is, 'caldron' or 'pot', because a very great multitude of the enemies was slain there; and Jeruel, that is, 'fear of the Lord', because from the manifest help of God which he gave to those who hoped in him, dread was struck into the foreigners on every side.
• Mystically, the Moabites, Ammonites and Edomites signify pagans, Jews and heretics, who without cause stir up war against the faithful and strive to take away the Christian religion. But Josaphat, that is, the people of Christ, attacks them not with bodily but with spiritual arms, seeking heavenly help with inward devotion of heart.
20.22: **“And when they began to sing praises, the Lord turned their ambushments upon themselves, that is to say, of the children of Ammon, and of Moab, and of mount Seir, who were come out to fight”** — otherwise: that they might fight
20.25: **“Then Josaphat came, and all the people with him to take away the spoils of the dead: and they found among the dead bodies, various furniture, and garments, and most precious vessels: and they took them for themselves, so that they could not carry all, nor take away the spoils in three days, the booty was so great.”** — THEN JOSAPHAT CAME etc. The holy teachers with the crowd of the faithful gather of the spoils of the enemies; whatever of physics, ethics and logic they have believed useful, by reading, writing and teaching, they turn through the faith of the holy Trinity to the use of the whole Church, so that what those possessed unjustly and unprofitably the faithful, possessing it profitably, may possess for the salvation of souls.
20.26: **“THE VALLEY OF BLESSING”** — The humility of the Church, where praises are worthily rendered to God. And he who, instructed in the teaching of the four gospels, comes through the faith of baptism to the unity of the Church, there, praising duly and living worthily before God, will enter the vision of everlasting peace with praise and everlasting joy.
20.32:
**“And he walked in the way of Asa his father, and he turned not from it, doing that which”** — or the things which
**“pleasing”** — or pleasing things
**“was”** — otherwise: were
20.35:
**“After these things Josaphat king of Juda made friendship with Ochozias king of Israel, whose works were very wicked.”** — otherwise: most wicked
**“AFTER THESE THINGS HE MADE FRIENDSHIP”** — It has been said that the fellowship and friendship of Josaphat king of Juda with the kings of Samaria signifies those who pass from the Church to the society of heretics; but this fellowship is abominable to God. Therefore their ships are broken, because the Lord strikes their works; because whatever is done in the ship of the present life with the faction and counsel of heretics is proved to displease in the eyes of God. Whence: "He that is not with me is against me" etc.

21.2: **“ALL THESE WERE THE SONS OF JOSAPHAT”** — Imitators of his works, their brother Joram always sliding into worse things; hence Joram himself is read to have killed them with the princes of Israel.
21.14: **“Behold the Lord will strike thee with a great plague, with all thy people, and thy children, and thy wives, and all thy substance.”** — BEHOLD THE LORD WILL STRIKE THEE WITH A GREAT PLAGUE. By the Philistines and Arabians, who laid waste his land and plundered his substance, and his sons together with his wives. Joram, which is interpreted 'who is lofty', who from a religious father turned aside to unbelief and made the sons of Juda commit fornication, signifies those who, imbued with faith and regenerated by baptism, leave the truth of faith, following the error of heretics and perverting others with them. Hence Elias, that is, the prophetic word, rebukes them, because all the authority of the divine books reproves such, and deservedly chides their perversity with most grievous protestations.
21.15:
**“And thou shalt be sick with a very grievous disease”** — of unbelief
**“of thy bowels,”** — of the mind
**“till thy vitals come out by little and little every day.”** — until, that is, all the vigour of their sense, by growing foolish through madness, loses the understanding of true wisdom
21.16:
**“So the Lord stirred up against Joram the spirit of the Philistines,”** — of the demons
**“and of the Arabians,”** — of the proud
**“who border on the Ethiopians.”** — to those blackened in sin
21.17:
**“And they came up into the land of Juda,”** — of those confessing
**“and wasted it, and they carried away all the substance”** — of the virtues
**“that was found in the house”** — of good conduct
**“of the king, and moreover his sons”** — the fruits of working
**“and his wives:”** — carnal care
21.19:
**“And day came after day: and the space of time was running out, and now the course of two years was finished: and after being consumed with a long wasting, so that he voided also his bowels, he was delivered from his illness, and at the same time from his life. So he died of a very grievous illness,”** — of despair
**“and the people did not make for him a funeral according to the manner of burning, as they had done for his ancestors.”** — because they will be blotted out of the book of the living and not be written with the just in the heavenly kingdom, but their memory will perish and their name will not be in the memory of the saints
21.20: **“AND HE REIGNED EIGHT YEARS”** — Joram is said to have reigned eight years and lived forty. And his son Ochozias, when he began to reign, was forty-two years old; if that is so, he begot a son two years before the father himself was born. But the Hebrews say that Joram, who is described as having lived forty years and reigned eight, lived forty years and reigned twenty-eight. For the eight years which are assigned to him in the kingdom are those in which he reigned before he killed his brothers, while he still lived innocently. But the other twenty years in which he reigned afterwards are not counted, because he lived in sickness and tribulation; and therefore they are assigned to his son, who is said, according to the book of Kings, to have been no more than twenty-two years old; lest the years remaining from the sum of the numbers should cause an error in the reckoning of the times. For Ochozias lived thirty-three years and reigned only one. For the comparison with the book of Kings gives great help in solving this question.

22.7:
**“For it was the will of God against Ochozias, that he should come to Joram:”**
• AZARIAS. He who above [is] Ochozias, that is, 'grasping the Lord'; and Azarias, 'help of the Lord'.
• And therefore, according to the Hebrews, his name is changed for the better, because according to the Lord's precept he visited the sick.
**“AGAINST JEHU”** — Jehu signifies the princedom of the gentiles, which Christ appointed against the sacrilegious city which killed the prophets and the Lord of the prophets and persecuted the apostles, that he might punish it with fitting vengeance, and after the coming of Christ destroy the shrine of the priests and overthrow the temple, and cast down from the summit of the kingdom, as Jezabel, the impious Synagogue thirsting for their blood, and kill its rulers.
22.8: **“So when Jehu was overthrowing the house of Achab,”** — these things are written more fully in the Book of Kings, through Eliseus
22.10: **“NOW ATHALIA”** — Athalia, who tried to extinguish the seed of David and destroy the royal stock, signifies the impiety of the Synagogue, which through wickedness of mind lies in wait for the seed of Christ, raging with inexorable hatred; which once seemed to reign when it observed the temporal ceremonies of the law. Athalia is interpreted 'temporal of the Lord'.
