But by the diligence of Josabeth, which is interpreted 'fulness of the Lord', that is, of the Church, in which are true delights, Joas is preserved, which is interpreted 'memory of the Lord', that is, Christ, in whom is the memory of the name of the Lord, lest he be slain in the saints by the cruelty of the raging one; but he is nourished in the house of Joiada the high priest, which is interpreted 'beloved of the Lord', that is, Christ, of whom the Father says: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." Whose house is the Church, where, abiding in the faith of the elect, he daily makes the increase of his body, that in the time of judgment he may lift up the sceptre of the kingdom and his power against those who pressed him down.
22.11:
**“But Josabeth the king's daughter took Joas”** — memory of the Lord
**“the son of Ochozias, and stole him from among the king's sons, when they were slain: and she hid him with his nurse in the chamber of the beds: now Josabeth”** — fulness of the Lord
**“that hid him, was the daughter of king Joram, the wife of Joiada the high priest, and sister of Ochozias, and therefore Athalia”** — temporal of the Lord

23.1: **“And in the seventh year”** — these things are written and expounded in the Book of Kings
23.11:
**“And they brought out the king's son, and put upon him the crown, and the testimony,”** — which is added in most [copies]
**“and they gave him the law to hold in his hand, and they made him king: and Joiada the high priest and his sons anointed him:”** — synecdoche, for Zacharias alone, who was a prophet, whom the same Joas afterwards killed
23.13: **“And when she saw the king standing upon the step in the entrance,”** — UPON THE STEP. That is, the column and base which Solomon had prepared and placed in the midst of the hall, five cubits long and five broad and three high.
23.16:
**“And Joiada made a covenant”** — the covenant of God, that is, the law of God, that is, God himself, whose minister he was
**“between himself and all the people and the king, that they should be the people of the Lord.”** — AND JOIADA MADE. Joiada is interpreted 'knowing the Lord' or 'loving', because he taught the children of Israel to know the Lord. He made a covenant, then, between the Lord and the people and the king, that they should obey the Lord and his law. He made one also between the king and the people, that the people should deal faithfully toward the king, and the king rule the people justly according to the teaching of the priests and Levites, whose office it was to instil the precepts of the Lord.

24.4: **“AFTER THIS JOAS HAD A MIND”** — King Joas rebukes the priests because they had been less zealous in restoring the temple; and the money collected from the people is given by the king's command, through the hands of the masters, to the masons and craftsmen, to repair the cracks in the walls and restore the breaches. For Joas, both by this name and by this work, signifies Christ; for it is interpreted 'strength of the Lord'. He commands the teachers to receive all the money that is offered by passers-by into the house of God, that is, whatever of spiritual knowledge or good working has been brought by the saints into the treasury of the Lord, that it may be applied through the offices of the preachers to the restoration of the spiritual temple, so that they may restore whatever they find torn by error or hurt by vices, lest the multitude of hearers perish through the negligence of the teachers.
24.6: **“And the king called Joiada the chief, and said to him: Why hast thou not taken care to oblige the Levites to bring in out of Juda and Jerusalem the money that was appointed by Moses the servant of the Lord for all the multitude of Israel to bring into the tabernacle of the testimony?”** — of which in Exodus: "When thou shalt take the sum of the children of Israel according to their number, every one of them shall give a price for their souls to the Lord" etc. Which we have expounded in Exodus as we could
24.7: **“For that most wicked woman Athalia and her children have ruined the house of God,”** — AND HER CHILDREN etc. Not that she then had children; for when Ochozias died, because he had no son, she set about killing all the royal seed; but he calls her children the priests of the idols, who had despoiled the temple and adorned their idols with its ornaments; for imitators are often called children.
24.11: **“And when it was time to bring the chest before the king by the hands of the Levites (for they saw there was much money) the king's scribe came, and he whom the high priest had appointed: and they poured out the money that was in the chest: and they carried the chest back to its place: and thus they did every day, and there was gathered an immense sum of money,”** — of the divine word
24.12:
**“which the king and Joiada gave”** — Christ, king and priest
**“to them that were over the works of the house of the Lord:”** — to the dispensers of the gospel, who dispense the measure of wheat to those who work in the house of the Lord
**“and they hired with it hewers of stones, and workmen of every trade, to repair the house of the Lord: and smiths also of iron and brass, that what began to fall might be propped up.”** — AND THEY HIRED etc. This the apostles do when, through the disciples subject to them, they scattered the seeds of the divine word through the world, that they might set over the hearers workmen fit for the will of God; of whom some work wood, when they prepare themselves and those who obey them as fruitful trees in the house of God; others repaired the breaches, when they rebuilt those things that had been broken by heresy or schism; others cut stones, when they rebuke strongly the hard of heart and unbelieving; others [work] the metals of iron and brass, when they require of each the strength of faith and the confession of catholic truth, that the house of God may be filled, according to that: "To every one of us is given grace, according to the measure of the giving of Christ."
24.14:
**“And when they had finished all the works, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Joiada: and of it were made vessels for the temple for the ministry, and for the holocausts,”**
• who are fit for receiving the divine gifts and carrying out the ministries of God
• THE REST OF THE MONEY, OF WHICH etc. What we read in the book of Kings seems contrary: "But there were not made of the same money the waterpots of the temple, and the fleshhooks." But it is not said here that of the same money which was offered by the people in the temple of the Lord for the restoration of the house of God the sacred vessels were made for the ministry of the temple and for the holocausts, but of the rest of the money, that is, of that which had been collected by other gifts. For it could be that the money offered at different times provided material for different works; as one is the teaching by which the unlearned are imbued with faith, another that by which the perfect are instructed unto fulness.
**“bowls also, and other vessels of gold and silver.”** — these signify capacity of genius or breadth of love
24.15: **“But Joiada grew old and full of days, and he died when he was a hundred and thirty years old.”** — if we complete the time of the present life in the faith of the holy Trinity with the perfection of good works, we shall come to the eternal blessedness which is at the right hand of God
24.16: **“And they buried him in the city of David with the kings, because he had done good to Israel, and to his house.”** — because all the days of his priesthood he ruled the people of God well and instructed them in the worship of God
24.18: **“And they forsook the temple of the Lord the God of their fathers, and served groves and idols, and the wrath of the Lord came upon Juda and Jerusalem for this sin.”** — AND THE WRATH OF THE LORD CAME etc. The Hebrews hand down that the princes of Juda adored the king as God, and that he gladly accepted it. Hence he greatly offended the Lord and suddenly felt the wrath he deserved. For this fault also Herod is read in the Acts of the apostles to have been struck by an angel.
24.20: **“ZACHARIAS THE SON OF JOIADA”** — The Lord in the gospel, recalling Zacharias slain between the temple and the altar, calls him the son of Barachias, whom the present history testifies to have been the son of Joiada. But others say [it was] Zacharias the son of Barachias, who is the eleventh among the twelve prophets, and the father's name agrees in him. But where he was slain between the temple and the altar Scripture does not teach, especially since in his times [unclear in the edition: "vix ruine templi volunt ex quibusdam apocryphorum, somniis approbantes"] that he was slain because he preached the coming of the Saviour; this, because it has no authority from the Scriptures, is despised with the same ease with which it is proved. Others will have this to be the Zacharias who was slain between the temple and the altar by king Joas, as the history of Kings relates. But it is to be observed that this Zacharias is not the son of Barachias but of Joiada. Since then we hold to Zacharias, and the place of the slaying agrees, let us ask why he is called the son of Barachias and not of Joiada. Barachias is called 'blessed of the Lord', and the justice of the priest Joiada is shown by the Hebrew name. In the gospel which the Nazarenes use, 'son of Joiada' is read for 'son of Barachias'. Simpler brethren, among the ruins of the temple and the altar, or at the exits of the gates which they call Siloam, show red stones and think them stained with the blood of Zacharias.
24.24: **“And whereas there came a very small number of the Syrians, the Lord delivered into their hands all [the multitude]”** — otherwise: an infinite [multitude]
24.26: **“BUT THEY LAID WAIT FOR HIM”** — The Hebrews assert that the Ammonites and Moabites laid wait for king Joas because of the unjust slaying of Zacharias, to heighten the malice of the Israelites, who would not avenge the priest of God, whom the sons of foreigners avenged.

25.2: **“And he did that which was good in the sight of the Lord:”** — in the opinion of men, who saw and praised
25.4: **“But he slew not their children, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses, where the Lord commanded, saying: Let not [the fathers] be slain”** — otherwise: where the Lord commanded, saying: They shall not be slain
25.7: **“But a man of God came to him, and said: O king, let not the army of Israel go out with thee, for the Lord is not with Israel and all the children of Ephraim.”** — of which Jeroboam [was]; as it were, the Lord is neither with the subjects nor with the prelates
25.8: **“And if thou think that battles stand in the strength of the army, God will make thee to be overcome by the enemies.”** — of the ten tribes, who worshipped idols and were abominable to God
25.11: **“And Amasias courageously led forth his people, and went to the Valley of saltpits, and slew of the children of Seir ten thousand.”** — IN THE VALLEY OF SALTPITS. Where salt was made, either from salty hay [so the edition: 'feno salsuginis'], as in many places, cut, dried and burnt, or from the salt waters of wells heated and brought by boiling to the firmness of salt. Or otherwise, where Joab also is read to have struck twelve thousand of the Edomites. And for the Valley of saltpits the old edition set Gemel, as if the name of a region.
25.14: **“But Amasias after the slaughter of the Edomites, and bringing the gods of the children of Seir, set them up to be his gods, and adored them, and burned incense to them.”** — because, according to the Hebrews, when the twelve [so the edition] thousand were cast down from the rock, the idols answered that they had been killed because they had been negligent in their worship
25.15: **“Wherefore the Lord being angry against Amasias, sent a prophet to him”** — Eleazar the son of Dodai his uncle, as the Hebrews hand down
25.16:
**“And when he spoke these things, he answered him: Art”** — otherwise: art
**“I KNOW, SAID HE, THAT THE LORD HATH DETERMINED”** — Who wills no one to perish, but by just judgment condemns him who perseveres in sin. Therefore Amasias perished, because, admonished by the prophet to do penance, he did not obey but remained [so] to the end.
25.17: **“Then Amasias king of Juda taking very bad counsel, sent to Joas the son of Joachaz the son of Jehu”** — otherwise: Hieu
25.18: **“THE THISTLE WHICH IS IN LIBANUS”** — He hints at this likeness because Amasias, born of most noble birth, coming of the stock of David, degenerate through the foulness of idolatry and made vile, does not consider his own measure, but lifts himself beyond measure with the haughtiness of pride.
25.20: **“Amasias would not hearken to him, because it was the Lord's will that he should be delivered into the hands”** — or into the hands
25.21:
**“So Joas king of Israel went up, and they saw one another. And Amasias king of Juda went”** — otherwise: was
**“to Bethsames of Juda:”**
• a priestly city in the tribe of Benjamin; the other Bethsames is in the tribe of Nephtali, belonging to the kingdom of the ten tribes
• BETHSAMES. In Kings it is said: "Bethsames a town of Juda", because it belongs to the kingdom of Juda, that is, to the two tribes over which the house of David ruled; but according to the situation of the places it belongs to the tribe of Benjamin.
25.23: **“And Joas king of Israel took Amasias king of Juda, the son of Joas, the son of Joachaz, in Bethsames, and brought him to Jerusalem: and he broke down the walls”** — otherwise: the wall
25.24: **“AND WITH OBEDEDOM”** — Because he carried off not only the vessels which he found in the house of God, but also those which the porters and keepers of the temple kept. And in Kings [so the edition] we read that David chose of the sons of Obededom seventy-two to minister in the house of God and keep the temple.
25.27: **“AND AFTER HE REVOLTED”** — From the time that he did not hear the prophet's counsel, nor would be turned to the Lord, a conspiracy was prepared and deferred until it came to completion.
25.28: **“And they brought him back upon horses, and buried him with his fathers in the city of David.”** — because he adored the gods of Edom, which were carried on horses, not on the shoulders of men; because he neglected to serve the God of Israel, whose mysteries were carried on the shoulders of the patriarchs

26.3: **“Ozias was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned two and fifty years in Jerusalem: his mother's name was Jechelia of Jerusalem.”** — OZIAS, who is also Azarias. Ozias is interpreted 'strength of the Lord', Azarias 'help of the Lord'; because as long as he acted rightly, helped by divine aid, he fought very many wars happily and triumphed over his enemies. But when through pride he attempted unlawful things, struck with leprosy, he darkened the dignity of his name and honour, shut out from the people until the day of his death.
26.5: **“And he sought God in the days of Zacharias, who understood and saw God:”** — they say this was the son of Zacharias the son of Joiada, born after the death of his father and for that reason given his father's name. For he is called 'understanding' because of the priesthood, 'seeing' because of prophecy
26.7: **“And God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians, that dwelt in Gurbaal,”** — they say it is the place which in Genesis is called Gerara, where Abimelech reigned and where Abraham sojourned with Sara his wife
26.9: **“And Ozias built towers in Jerusalem over the gate of the corner, and over the gate of the valley, and the rest in the same side of the wall, and he fortified them.”** — OVER THE GATE OF THE VALLEY. This is the gate of Ephraim, which he related above was destroyed by Joas king of Israel. But the writer of the history would not put in the building the name which he put in the destroying; and because Ephraim sacrificed to idols and had destroyed this gate with Joas its king, it did not deserve in its building to be named by its own name, but is called by the name of the valley because of the humiliation and vileness of its author. Hence in Esdras it is said: "And the gate of the valley Hanun built, and the inhabitants of Zanoe." Of this gate and the other gates of Jerusalem we have spoken abundantly in Esdras, following Bede.
26.13: **“and under them the whole army three hundred and seven thousand five hundred: who were fit to fight”** — otherwise: for wars
26.15: **“And he made in Jerusalem engines of divers kinds, which he placed in the towers, and in the corners of the walls, to shoot arrows, and great stones: and his name went forth far, because the Lord helped him, and strengthened”** — otherwise: had strengthened
26.16:
**“BUT WHEN HE WAS MADE STRONG”** — Ozias was at first just and did right in the sight of the Lord; hence he both conquered his enemies and had many prophets in his realm. Hence as long as Zacharias the priest, surnamed 'understanding', lived, he pleased God, serving in the temple with all veneration. But after Zacharias died, wishing to offer gifts himself, he invaded the dignity of the priesthood not so much piously as boldly, and did not obey the protesting Levites and priests; hence he was struck with leprosy in the forehead, which the priest protected with a plate of gold, which in Ezechiel the Lord commands to be marked with the impression of the letter thau.
**“AND HE ENTERED INTO THE TEMPLE”** — Because, clothed with the priestly robe, as a solemn festival drew near, he entered the temple to offer incense on the golden altar, according to Josephus. Hence before the city, in the place called Erege, half the mountain on the west was split off, and, rolling forward four stades, stopped at the eastern mountain, so as to close the roads and overwhelm the royal cities. The Hebrews will have it that this happened in the twenty-fifth year of Ozias, whose remaining years are twenty-seven. And he reigned fifty-two years.
**“And going into the temple of the Lord he had a mind to burn incense upon the altar of incense.”** — Ozias reigned fifty-two years, at which time Amulius ruled among the Latins and Agamestor among the Athenians; at whose death Isaias saw the vision, as he himself testifies, namely at the time when Romulus, the founder of the Roman empire, was born.
26.23: **“IN THE FIELD OF THE ROYAL SEPULCHRES”** — Not in the royal sepulchres, not in the city of David. For heretics and schismatics are unworthy of the society and communion of holy Church, nor is their memory held among the catholics, because, stained with errors and foul with vices, they are separated from their fellowship.

27.1:
**“Joatham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem: the name of his mother was Jerusa the daughter of Sadoc.”** — because he gained for himself and his subjects the vision of eternal peace
**“TWENTY-FIVE YEARS OLD”** — At the beginning and at the end he numbers the years of Joatham, because as he began in justice he persevered to the end. Hence the times of his life are proclaimed worthy of praise.
27.3:
**“HE BUILT THE GATE”** — [The gate] which in the Acts of the apostles is called the Beautiful, according to the Hebrews, and by them is called to this day the gate of Joatham, because he built it.
**“OPHEL”** — It was a tower of wonderful height not far from the temple; hence too it received the name Ophel, that is, 'of darkness' or 'cloudy'. And where it is written in Micheas: "And thou, O cloudy tower of the flock of the daughter of Sion", in the Hebrew it is had: Tower of Ophel.
**“and on the wall of Ophel he built much.”**
• The tower of Ophel signifies the loftiness of Scripture, which, founded in history, hides the head of the spiritual sense among the clouds, while it conceals the greatness of knowledge from the eyes of men. Whence: "He made darkness his covert."
• Joatham, whose life is praised, signifies Christ, of whom it is said: "Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised" etc. For Joatham is interpreted 'consummated' or 'perfect'; and of Christ the Apostle says: "And being consummated, he became, to all that obey him, the cause of eternal salvation" etc. He built the high gate of the house of the Lord, and accomplished the mystery of his incarnation by wonderful power, who says of himself: "I am the door. By me, if any man enter in, he shall be saved." This gate was called high, of which the Psalmist says: "The Lord is high above all nations" etc.

28.3: **“IN THE VALLEY OF BENENNOM”** — This is the valley of Bennon, that is, of the son of Bennon or Ennon, by the wall of Jerusalem toward the east, in which a most beautiful grove is watered by the springs of Siloe. And Taphet or Tophet, for both are said, is a place in the same valley by the Fuller's pool and by the field Haceldama, which is shown to this day on the southern side of mount Sion. And they were wont in Taphet, which was a most pleasant place, whence even today it affords the delights of gardens, to sacrifice to demons on an altar set up, and to consecrate their children with abominable fire and offer holocaust. The valley of Bennon, then, that is, of the son of Ennon, is called in Hebrew Gehennom, by whose name in the New Testament the punishment of hell is called gehenna. For as those who served idols in the valley of Bennon perished, as the prophets attest, so sinners, of those who sinned, will perish in eternal damnation. Achaz, the son of a just father, fallen into unbelief and the crime of idolatry, signifies heretics who were imbued with the sacrament of faith by catholic fathers, but, turning aside to apostasy, give divine worship to images and sacrifice the fruit of their womb, that is, the effect of wicked thought, to demons with the fire of zeal. For all are adulterers; their hearts are as an oven.
28.27: **“And Achaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of Jerusalem: for they received him not into the sepulchres of the kings of Israel.”** — it is not fitting that heretics should rest in the future with catholics, from whom they differ here in faith and work

29.1: **“Now Ezechias began to reign, when he was five and twenty years old, and he reigned nine and twenty years in Jerusalem: the name of his mother was Abia the daughter of Zacharias.”** — the Hebrews assert that he was the posthumous son of Zacharias the prophet and priest, whom Joas killed
29.3: **“In the first year and month of his reign he opened the doors of the house of the Lord, and repaired them.”** — IN THE FIRST YEAR AND MONTH etc. He would not otherwise imitate David his father, who, given to God from infancy, magnified the worship of God at the beginning of his reign. But morally it admonishes the rulers of the Church not to be slothful in the office committed to them, but to do all things diligently. Mystically Ezechias, who not only by himself or by his own carried on the work of God vigorously, but also by messengers stirred others to the like zeal, signifies Christ, as the interpretation of the name also testifies. For Ezechias [is] 'grasping the Lord' or 'strength of the Lord'. And Christ [is] the power of God and the wisdom of God, who washed away with his blood all the transgressions of the fathers which had been under the law, and fully restored the worship of piety in the Church. He sent envoys to call the nations to the faith: first prophets, then apostles and their successors. He appointed the Pasch to be celebrated in the second month, because, the shadow of the law ceasing, he taught us to keep the true Pasch, of which Paul says: "For Christ our pasch is sacrificed."
29.4: **“And he brought the priests and the Levites, and gathered them together in the part”** — otherwise: the street
29.5: **“And he said to them:”** — or to them
29.27: **“And Ezechias commanded that they should offer holocausts upon the altar: and when the holocausts were offered, they began to sing praises to the Lord, and to sound with trumpets, and divers instruments which David the king of Israel had prepared”** — otherwise: had found

30.22: **“And Ezechias spoke to the choir”** — otherwise: the heart

31.1: **“And when these things had been duly celebrated, all Israel that were found in the cities of Juda went out, and they broke the idols.”** — THEY BROKE THE IDOLS. After the coming of the Saviour, idolatry was destroyed not only in Jerusalem and in Juda but in all the nations of the world, and the pride of the devil fell. And as the number of the faithful grows, the worship of demons decreases, until at the end of the world the last death shall be overthrown, and the Lord alone shall reign in that day.

32.4: **“he gathered together a very great multitude, and they stopped up all the fountains, and the brook that ran in the midst of the land, saying: Lest the kings of the Assyrians come, and find abundance of water.”** — THEY STOPPED UP THE FOUNTAINS. Those who fight against pagans and heretics must use diligent caution and veil the mysteries; whence: "Give not that which is holy to dogs; neither cast ye your pearls before swine."
32.5: **“HE BUILT UP ALSO”** — Christ built the Church, which is the city of God, and restores the wall [so the edition: 'inane'] of faith and true religion which is in some parts broken down by the malice of pagans or heretics. He raises the towers of the virtues; he sets another wall outside, that is, an outer wall, when he teaches us to hold fast the efficacy of good works. For the wall of faith does not suffice unless it be confirmed by good works. He makes armour and shields, namely of Scripture and its divers testimonies and the teaching of the Church, for the defence of his Church, and he appointed the doctors as princes of the spiritual wars.
32.8: **“With him is an arm of flesh: with us the Lord our God, who is our helper, and fighteth for us. And the people were encouraged”** — all these things are written more fully in Kings and in Isaias
32.21: **“And the Lord sent an angel”** — these things we have fully glossed in Isaias according to the plain sense of the history
32.24: **“In those days Ezechias was sick”** — these things are written more fully in Kings
32.31:
**“But yet in the embassy of the princes of Babylon, that were sent to him to inquire of the wonder that had happened upon the earth,”** — it signifies the return of the sun by ten lines
**“the Lord left him that he might be tempted, and that all things might be made known”** — that is, he did not restrain him through the prophet from showing his treasures and the treasures of the house of the Lord to foreigners
**“that were in his heart.”** — the hidden pride of the mind
32.33: **“And Ezechias slept with his fathers, and they buried him above the sepulchres of the sons of David:”** — because his sepulchre [was] higher by the prerogative of merit and piety

33.12: **“And after that he was in distress he prayed to the Lord his God: and did penance exceedingly before the God of his fathers.”** — AND HE DID PENANCE. Having heard of the penance of Manasses, no one ought to despair of the mercy of God, but rather through penance to be confident of pardon.
33.20: **“And Manasses slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the house of David.”** — otherwise: his own

34.5: **“And he burnt the bones of the priests on the altars of the idols, and he cleansed Juda and Jerusalem.”** — THE BONES OF THE PRIESTS ALSO. He therefore burnt the priests on the altars of the idols to show that their sacrifices were deadly, who not only offered victims of cattle to demons, but also handed themselves over to idolatry. This signifies that all who, bound over to the service of the devil, had ended a sacrilegious life in time, are to be consumed with eternal torments, each according to his deserts.
34.22:
**“And Helcias, and they that were sent with him by the king, went to Olda the prophetess, the wife of Sellum the son of Thecuath, the son of Hasra,”** — whom the Hebrews hold to be the uncle of Jeremias, the father of Hanameel
**“keeper of the wardrobe: who dwelt in Jerusalem in the Second”** — that is, 'the second part of the wall'; for which the old edition has 'in Massena', as if the name of a place, for Massena is interpreted 'second'

35.1: **“And Josias kept the phase to the Lord in Jerusalem, and it was immolated on the fourteenth day of the first month.”** — AND JOSIAS KEPT. We are admonished first to purge the land of our heart of all vices, and so to celebrate the Pasch to the Lord, "not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth." Mystically, Josias, that is, 'strength of the Lord', signifies Christ, of whom we read: "The Lord who is strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle." Josias is also interpreted 'salvation of the Lord', and Christ "shall save his people from their sins". He with the zeal of God cleanses the land of Juda and Jerusalem from all uncleanness, who said through the prophet: "The zeal of thy house hath eaten me up"; of whom it is said elsewhere: "Whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his floor." He celebrates the true Phase in the eighteenth year of his reign, because in the eighth age, the general resurrection having been granted, he brings his saints with the perfection of good works to the penny of eternal blessedness, all scandals having first been cast out of his kingdom.
35.3: **“He said also to the Levites, by whose instructions all Israel was sanctified to the Lord: Put the ark in the sanctuary of the temple”** — PUT THE ARK etc. The Hebrews hand down that in the time of Achaz the ark was carried out of the temple, when idols had been placed by him in the temple, and was taken into the house of Sellum, the husband of Olda, the uncle of Jeremias. For it could not be together with the idols.
35.18: **“There was no phase like to this in Israel, from the days of Samuel the prophet: neither did any of all the kings of Israel keep such a phase as Josias did, with the priests, and the Levites, and all Juda, and Israel that was found, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.”** — THERE WAS NO PHASE. Because, the figures being taken away, in the day of judgment the saints shall pass from death to life, from corruption to glory, and in the sight of their Maker shall rejoice for ever in the heavenly Jerusalem; because "the God of gods shall be seen in Sion", because "he hath shown his wonderful mercy in a fortified city".
35.21:
**“But he sent messengers to him, saying: What have I to do with thee, O king of Juda? I come not against thee this day, but I fight against another house, to which God hath commanded me to go in haste: forbear to do against God, who is with me, lest he kill thee.”** — namely of the king Adremmon the son of Thabrimon, who reigned in Charchamis, whom Nechao killed at the same time as Josias
**“TO WHICH GOD [HATH COMMANDED ME TO GO] IN HASTE”** — Because from the words of Jeremias and the other prophets he could know the will of the Lord, by which judgment was to be done upon the sinful people. Hence Rabsaces also said of Sennacherib king of the Assyrians: "The Lord commanded me to go up to the land", because the prophets had foretold that he would go up, which was by no means hidden from him.
35.23: **“IN THE FIELD OF MAGEDDO, AND THERE HE WAS WOUNDED”** — The killing of Josias, who was killed by Pharao Nechao in Mageddo, signifies the persecution of the ancient enemy against the preachers, whom he strives to put to death and to take away from the Church, that he may more easily invade and scatter the whole people. For Pharao is interpreted 'scattering', Nechao 'striking', Mageddo 'from temptation'. For the devil is permitted to rise up against the saints, and he strives with all his strength, by tempting and striking the flock of God, first to scatter and take away those by whose support the others fight against the enemy.

36.1: **“Then the people of the land took Joachaz the son of Josias, and made him king in his father's stead in Jerusalem.”** — THEN THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND TOOK JOACHAZ etc. Who is interpreted 'new', and signifies wicked rulers, whom the people of the land, that is, those given to earthly desire, choose according to their own ways, consenting to vices; whom Pharao conquers in Reblatha and leads into Egypt, because by the multitude of flatterers he weakens and deceives the hearts of prelates. For Rebbla is interpreted 'multitude'; and so he plunges them, bound with the chains of sins, into the abyss of the spiritual Egypt.
36.4:
**“AND HE MADE KING”** — Nechao made Joachim king. He laid a fine on the land of a hundred talents of silver, because the devil demanded a task of service from the people of the lost, that they might be ready for his obedience both in mind and in speech.
**“AND TURNED HIS NAME TO JOAKIM”** — It is to be noted that of this same Joachim the son of Josias it is written thus in Kings: "Joachim slept with his fathers, and Joachin his son reigned in his stead." Josephus, however, says: When the king of Babylon had entered the city, he by no means kept faith, but killed the strongest young men and those comely in beauty, together with king Joachim, whom he ordered to be cast out unburied before the wall. And he made his son Joachin king of the whole province. And those who were set in dignities, three thousand in number, he led into Babylon, among whom was Ezechiel, still a boy. This then was the end of king Joachim, who lived ten and thirty [so the edition] years and reigned eleven years. And the successor of the kingdom of Joachim was a king named Ononimus [so the edition]; he reigned three months and ten days.
**“and turned his name to Joakim.”**
• But it is to be known that when once a man has bound himself over to any vice, he will be subject to many masters. Hence Joachim, whom Pharao first compelled to pay him tribute, Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon compels to serve him three years. Nabuchodonosor signifies the same as Pharao, namely the prince of confusion and the ruler of this darkness. And when the devil has compelled someone to pay him the tribute of sin, he brings him wholly into his dominion and exacts full service, namely by suggestion, delight, consent, and also by thought, speech and deed.
• Joachin, led captive into Babylon, signifies the fall of rulers who, deluded by the art of the devil, are brought into the confusion of errors and vices; and those who ought to have taught others by word and deed and raised them up from sin are swallowed up by divers sins. For Joachin [is] 'raising up' or 'he who rises together in time'. With him the precious vessels of the Lord are taken captive. For those who excelled in sharpness of wit, or shone with honesty of manners, corrupted by the examples of those set over them, fall with them as a prey to the devil.
**“JEROME”** — It is to be known that the name of this Joachin, who by another name is called Jechonias, is not written among the Hebrews with the same letters at the end as that of his father Joachim, who is also Eliachim. But the former, that is, the father, they mark at the end of the name with coph and mem; the second, that is, the son, with caph and nun. Hence let no one think that he who in the beginning of Daniel is Joachim is the one written Joachin in the opening of Ezechiel. This one has the last syllable chim, that one chin. And therefore in the gospel according to Matthew one generation seems to be lacking, because the second fourteen ends in Joachim the son of Josias, and the third begins from Joachin the son of Eliachim. Ignorant of this, Porphyry builds a calumny against the Church, showing his own unskilfulness while he strives to convict the evangelist Matthew of falsehood.
36.8:
**“But the rest of the acts of Joakim, and of his abominations, which he wrought,”** — because he provoked God by his works, and perverted the words of the prophets who were sent to him, and, cutting the book of Jeremias with a penknife, cast it into the fire
**“and what was found in him,”** — according to the Hebrews, he shaved his head round over the dead, he made marks on his body, which were found on the body of the dead man
36.10:
**“And at the return of the year king Nabuchodonosor sent messengers, who brought him to Babylon, carrying away at the same time the most precious vessels of the house of the Lord: and he made Sedecias his uncle king over Juda and Jerusalem.”** — of this it is written more fully in the Book of Kings
**“BUT HE MADE KING”** — Sedecias signifies those who take up the government of the people of God. For Sedecias is interpreted 'the just one of the Lord'. For they receive the seat of justice to exercise the works of justice; they receive the dignity of honour and office, chiefly because they deserve to be named sons of Josias, that is, of the salvation of the Lord, through the grace of baptism and the anointing of chrism. But, degenerating, they fall back into the foulness of vices and turn their subjects to impiety, and neither keep the faith which they had promised to God, nor preserve the covenants of peace with men. Such men the divine law, the prophets and the miracles of the apostles daily warn to depart from sins and return to the Lord through penance. But, once hardened, they despise the words of salvation; whence God in anger sends against them the king of the Chaldeans, that is, the devil with his attendants, that is, the spiritual wickednesses, who, sparing no age and deferring to no dignity, carry whomever they take into Babylon, that is, into confusion, and burn the house of the Lord, because they compel the faithful, who are the temple of God, to blaspheme. They destroy the walls of Jerusalem when they cast down the guards of the pastors; they burn the towers when they burn up the prelates with unlawful desires; they demolish everything precious when they bring to nothing those who applaud themselves for the prerogative of virtue and knowledge.
36.12: **“And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord his God, and did not reverence the face of Jeremias the prophet speaking to him from the mouth of the Lord.”** — otherwise: from the mouth of the Lord
36.20:
**“If any had escaped the sword, he was led into Babylon, and served the king”** — the devil
**“and his sons”** — the vices
36.21:
**“and that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremias might be fulfilled”** — that is, until another kingdom, foretold by prophetic utterance, rises up, and the kingdom of sin falls by divine judgment
**“and the land might keep her sabbaths:”** — that is, until the seventy years are fulfilled
36.23:
**“Thus saith Cyrus king of the Persians: All the kingdoms of the earth hath the Lord the God of heaven given to me, and he hath charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judea. Who is there among you of all his people? The Lord his God be with him, and let him go up.”**
• The end of the book of Paralipomenon is like the beginning of the book of Esdras the priest; hence there is no need to repeat here what we have expounded there. Of Cyrus too, how he signifies Christ, and what things are said of him and what are referred to him, we have expounded in Isaias.
• Solomon built the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem in seven years, finished and dedicated it in the eighth year, because through the whole time of this life, which runs in seven days, Christ builds the Church of his faithful; in the future life he perfects it and raises it to the vision of the brightness of eternal life in the glory of the resurrection. As time went on, certain buildings of the temple were decayed by age, which signifies the daily and very light errors of the faithful, of which Solomon says: "A just man shall fall seven times and shall rise again"; who are corrected by the examples and exhortations of the just, as it were by the industry of kings and priests, who are members of the true King and High Priest. Afterwards, as evils increased, the temple profaned by the filth of idols, and at last destroyed and burnt by the Chaldeans, signifies the graver falls of those who were united to the members of the Church, but after the deceit of the devil, cast down from the state of faith, are burnt up with the flame of vices. When the temple and the city of Jerusalem were destroyed, the citizens removed into Babylon, having done penance, returned to their homeland after seventy years and with great labour again restore the same temple and the holy city. They signify those who, deceived by the devil, lose not only the sincerity of faith and the integrity of work, but also by the enormity of their crimes become like heathens and publicans. Some of whom, coming to their senses by divine grace, return to the Church, when, pricked to the heart by the illumination of the Holy Spirit, they begin to hear and keep the precepts of the law which they had left. For there are seven gifts of the Holy Spirit and ten precepts of the law, and seven multiplied by ten give seventy. Hence fittingly those who were captives in Babylon through perverse works are freed after seventy years and rebuild the house of God and the holy city. For those who by their sins were separated from the communion of the Church and joined to the number of unbelievers, again through the gifts of the Holy Spirit exercise themselves in the pursuit of good works, and so recover the fellowship of the faithful, that is, of the house and city of God from which they had been cast out.

1.1:
**“O Lord almighty God of our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and of their just seed,”** — He calls upon the almighty God whom he has experienced in his own ruin
**“O LORD ALMIGHTY GOD”** — "He is the almighty God of the just, not of the impious who make up new figments for themselves. Why is he the God of these three only, and not also of others? Because in these the fullness of the Christian mystery is figured. Through Abraham the nativity of Christ, through Isaac the gathering of the believing people, through Jacob the resurrection of the Saviour is intimated."
1.2: **“who hast made heaven and earth with all the ornament thereof,”** — the visible and invisible creation. Or heaven: the saints; earth: the flesh, which God made for his glory, each having its proper ornament
1.3:
**“who hast sealed the sea by the word of thy commandment,”** — "that, its bounds being moved, it may not wander further"
**“THE SEA”** — Tropologically. The sea [is] the people subject to idolatry, which wandered on the waves of unbelief, which the Lord sealed with his word when the cross of Christ (who is the Word of the Father) is signed on their hearts and foreheads; which is the sea being sealed by the divine word.
**“who hast shut up the deep, and sealed it with thy terrible and laudable name,”** — the womb of all waters, which is shut up by divine command. Understand: these things thou didst create, namely for the praises of thy name.
1.4:
**“WHICH ALL FEAR”** — "The angels tremble, contemplating his presence; men fear, awaiting judgment; the demons dread, feeling his most mighty power; because the face of the Lord looks round about upon all things."
**“and tremble at the presence of thy power.”** — "Every rational creature, even if not every one looks to the Creator, yet every one acknowledges his power."
1.5: **“And the anger of thy threatening upon sinners is unbearable.”** — Upon sinners, not against [them]; whence in the gospel: "But the wrath of God abideth on him", the force of original damnation or of the heavenly judgment, because sinners are judged not from things below but from things above. For judgment is hurled from heaven.
1.6:
**“BUT UNMEASURABLE”** — The mercy of the Lord is called unmeasurable because the gospel promises have no promised measure. But those of the law had been measured. Whence: "I will fill your storehouses with wheat, wine and oil" etc.
**“and unsearchable is the mercy of thy promise,”**
• For being weak we think weak things.
• "That which eye hath not seen, nor hath it entered into the heart of man" etc.
**“AND UNSEARCHABLE MERCY”** — For the divine promises surpass our weakness, and can neither be unfolded in words nor beheld with the eyes.
1.7:
**“GOD MOST HIGH”** — "There is nothing wonderful in the praises of God in what is said: Thou art God most high over all the earth. For the heavens and the angels are higher than the earth, unless we consider it more wonderfully. Surely it is foretold of the mystery of Christ, who, when he had been flesh (because 'the Word was made flesh'), was made most high over all flesh, which is called by the name of earth."
**“VERY MERCIFUL”** — For if he had granted indulgence once, he would be merciful; but now, since he frequently bestows mercy on those who frequently offend, he is called very merciful.
**“LONG-SUFFERING”** — [Long-suffering,] by deferring sinners to penance and not punishing them at the time of the offence; very merciful, by promising pardon as often as thou hast sinned; repenting upon the malice of men, as Jeremias testifies, showing that the Lord promises good things to the good and evil things to the evil, but yet turns himself back this way and that if a change has followed; so that thou mayest not seem more secure of the good promise when thou doest evil, nor despair of the evil threat if, converted, thou doest better.
**“But thou, O Lord, according to thy goodness, hast promised repentance”** — "Let the penitent hear, let the despisers understand. Penance of the remission of sins is promised if the perversity of the wicked be forsaken."
**“of remission of sins.”** — "Penance is the remedy of sins; but for the just no penance is appointed, to whom the fault has been forgiven through grace."
1.8: **“TO THEM THAT HAVE NOT SINNED AGAINST THEE”** — "They sinned indeed, and were born in the sin of their birth, heirs surely of Adam; but, prevented freely by grace, they are set without sin, who had been propagated from the seed of sinners."
1.9: **“ABOVE THE NUMBER OF THE SAND”** — "Sins are sometimes compared to the hairs of the head, as the excellent prophet [says]: 'My iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see. They are multiplied above the hairs of my head.' The one compares the multitude of sins to the sand of the sea, the other to hairs. But there is this difference: he [compares them to] the sand of the sea who is so very violently weighed down by the burdens of vices that under their load he cannot breathe; but he who is overcome by carnal incitements, and yet can easily cut away the rottenness with the healing knife, compares his offence to the hairs of his head."
1.10:
**“I AM BOWED DOWN”** — The comparison of evils is distinguished by a manifold diversity. A certain principle of truth seems to shine forth, that any one of the persecutors is punished according to the measure of the offence by which he inflicted the pain of torment on the saints, as Asa king of Juda. Manasses too was bowed down, not with one or two but with many a band of iron. For he imposed on himself as many bands of spiritual iron, in which he should be bound, as he himself had cast upon the limbs of the saints.
**“BECAUSE I HAVE STIRRED UP [THY] WRATH”** — [He stirs it up] by provoking it with restless acts; therefore he stirs up the wrath of God who commits evil before God. But it is to be seen that he testifies that he committed evil in the singular. This committing of one evil provoked the indignation of the Lord, while many have done many evils and vengeance has not followed at once. Which evil he explains: setting up abomination. In the sacred volumes idols are called abomination or offence, and he who worshipped them will be defiled with the crime of transgression. They can also be understood otherwise. Every sin is a stumbling block, on which one stumbles to ruin. Likewise also an abomination, because God abhors every offence, which, fixed in the heart of the transgressor, becomes an idol. It also fits to be applied to the doctrines of demons, which are truly abominations and most grievous offences, by which the wrath of the Lord is provoked.
1.11: **“AND NOW I BOW THE KNEES”** — "He bends the knees of the heart, that by simple petition he may blot out what he had done by insolent presumption. In the likeness of the outward man he describes the inner."
1.12:
**“I HAVE SINNED, O LORD, I HAVE SINNED”** — The repetition of confessing is the true humility of the suppliant, as if he were saying: I have sinned in spirit, I have sinned also in body; I have sinned in thoughts, I have sinned in deeds; I have sinned outwardly, I have sinned externally [so the edition]; I have sinned against God, I have sinned against my neighbour.
**“I have sinned, O Lord, I have sinned,”**
• "These words are to be read again not with a light pronouncing of grief, but with the same gravity with which they were spoken by the one praying."
• Let not the keen [so the edition: 'acer'] mind run over these things lightly, but with heavy grief and sad patience [so the edition: 'patentia'] let it perceive that the force of a great matter is compressed into few words. For the penitent should either, silent with his lips, beg indulgence with tears in silence, or, if he is moved to say something from the grief of a contrite breast, let him speak in few words, because contrition of mind, not speech of the mouth, bends the Lord's pity. "For a contrite and humbled heart God doth not despise."
**“and I know my iniquity.”** — "Which is the greater progress, since very many sin, but not all acknowledge their own iniquities."
1.13:
**“I ask, beseeching thee, O Lord, forgive me, forgive me,”** — Let those things alone perish which laboured to destroy me with them.
**“DESTROY [ME] NOT TOGETHER”** — He does not say: Do not condemn me with my iniquities. For what is condemned is turned back in its substance; but what is destroyed, and destroyed eternally, this is done so that what was had is brought to nothing.
**“WITH [MY] INIQUITIES”** — Note: "Iniquities have no substance. For every sin is a fever of the soul, which, when it is taken away, is reduced to nothing."
**“neither reserve evils for me for ever,”** — The course of the penitent is extended to this, that the things in which they have sinned be given over to oblivion, and not be laid up in the eternal memory of the Lord.
1.14:
**“FOR THOU WILT SAVE [ME] UNWORTHY”** — The Lord saves the unworthy, not paying back retribution for the merit of their offences, but pouring out pardon for the goodness of mercy. For he is worthy who saves the unworthy, and by his own worthiness makes worthy him whom guilty conduct made unworthy.
**“ACCORDING TO [THY] GREAT MERCY”** — He who seeks to be saved according to great mercy seeks the salvation not of temporal but of eternal life. Indeed I judge that mercy belongs to this temporal life, but that great mercy concurs with the everlasting reward.
1.15:
**“And I will praise thee always "all the days of my life"”**
• "Not on one day nor for a little time, but all the days. 'For he that shall persevere unto the end, he shall be saved.'"
• God is praised in the days of life; but in the days of death he cannot be praised. So then he who lies subject to the death of offences, wrapped in iniquities, cannot praise God. "For praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner." But when he has been converted, as one passed from death to life, he is at once found worthy of the office of praise and is judged a partner of the higher powers, while he praises on earth him whom they also glorify on high.
**“ALL THE DAYS OF [MY] LIFE”** — "The prudent awaiter of eternal salvation praises God not for a little time but for all the time of his life."
**“ALL THE POWER OF THE HEAVENS”** — Cherubim, seraphim, thrones and dominations, archangels, seats, virtues, angels, ministers; and there are many offices which perhaps either we cannot find set down in the sacred books, or, hidden from human senses, we are not able to search out.
**“GLORY FOR EVER”** — There is a temporal glory, of which: "Be not thou afraid when a man shall be made rich, and when the glory of his house shall be increased." There is also another, everlasting glory: "May the glory of the Lord endure for ever", which both the human and the angelic creature serves. Amen.

1.1:
**“In the first year of Cyrus”** — Christ
**“king of the Persians, that the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremias might be fulfilled,”** — Christ too says: "All things must needs be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me"
**“the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians:”** — having acknowledged the power and providence of the God of Israel; Christ too says: "I do nothing of myself, but as the Father hath taught me, these things I speak"
**“and he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and in writing also, saying:”**
• Christ sent the holy scriptures through the whole world
• IN THE FIRST YEAR OF CYRUS. As Cyrus, the empire of the Chaldeans being destroyed, freed the people of God, sent them back to their homeland, commanded the burnt temple to be rebuilt in Jerusalem, and made this edict known also by letters, so Christ, the kingdom of the devil being destroyed, gathered into the Church his elect who had been scattered by his tyranny; which, justified now by faith, has peace with God through him and hastens to the vision of everlasting peace, for Jerusalem is called 'vision of peace'. He also has the burnt temple restored, when, leading back to salvation those who had lost the faith through the snares of the devil, he makes them worthy of his dwelling; he also sends the sacred and holy Scriptures through the whole world, by which he preaches faith in his name and the hope of salvation to all who belong to his kingdom, that is, to the elect.
1.2:
**“Thus saith Cyrus king of the Persians: All the kingdoms of the earth hath given to me”** — because then he had no adversary, or, the empire of the Chaldeans being destroyed, he believed that no one could resist him; so too Christ says: "All power is given to me in heaven and in earth"
**“the Lord God of heaven,”** — he confesses the God of Israel to be the God of heaven, and acknowledges also that he has all the kingdoms of the earth in his power and can give them to whom he will
**“AND HE HATH CHARGED ME TO BUILD HIM A HOUSE”** — BEDE. Each of the doctors, and the whole Church together, is wont to be called in the holy Scriptures the house or temple of God, because he is wont to dwell in the hearts of those who believe, hope and love; whence: "If any one love me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him" etc. Hence the Apostle himself also says: "The temple of God is holy, which you are." And elsewhere: "But Christ as the Son in his own house: which house are we" etc. In figure of this spiritual house or temple Solomon made the temple to the Lord in Jerusalem. For he is interpreted 'peaceable', figuring him of whom it is said: "His empire shall be multiplied, and there shall be no end of peace"; of whom the Apostle says: "And coming, he preached peace to you that were afar off, and peace to them that were nigh" etc. And that he built the temple in seven years, but finished and dedicated it in the eighth, signifies that through the whole time of this world, which runs round in seven days, the Lord builds the Church, the faithful being gathered for the heavenly building, and in the future life, when the glory of the resurrection appears, he perfects it wholly and raises it into the joy of immortal life in the eternal brightness of his vision; for because he himself rose on the eighth day, that is, after the seventh of the sabbath, the time of our resurrection too is rightly expressed by the number eight. And that in the following age certain buildings of the temple began to be decayed by age, but were restored by the diligence of kings and priests, signifies the daily errors of the faithful, of which it is said: "A just man shall fall seven times and shall rise again"; who are corrected by the daily skill of the times through the examples or exhortations of the just who went before, as it were by the industry of the priests and kings of God. For all the perfect are called kings and priests, since they are members of the supreme King and Priest, and have learned to rule themselves well and to present their bodies a living sacrifice to God. That afterwards, as evils increased, the temple was profaned by the filth of idols and at last destroyed and burnt by the Chaldeans, signifies the graver falls of those who, united to the members of the Church by the confession of right faith and the sacrament of baptism, are again, by the fraud of demons, cast down from the state of faith and burnt with the flame of vices. That, when the temple and the city of Jerusalem were destroyed, its citizens were removed into Babylon, but after seventy years, having done penance, were sent back to their homeland by the Lord's mercy and again restored the temple and the holy city with great labour, signifies those who, deceived by the devil, lose not only the sincerity of faith and the integrity of good work, but also by the bitterness of their crimes are made like gentiles and publicans, whence: "Let him be to thee as the heathen and publican"; [some] of whom, pricked to the heart by the illumination of the Holy Spirit, again hear and keep the commandments of God which they had left. For there are seven gifts of the Holy Spirit, and the sum of the divine law is comprised in ten commandments, and ten times seven are seventy. Hence fittingly those who had been taken captive into Babylonia through perverse works are freed after seventy years and rebuild the house of God and the holy city; because sometimes those who, separated by their sins from the communion of the Church, were joined to the number of unbelievers, again through the gift of the Holy Spirit exercise good works, and so recover the fellowship of the faithful, that is, of the house and city of God, from which they had been cast out. For it is to be noted that the house of the Lord rebuilt after the burning, the city restored, the people sent back to their homeland after the captivity, and the holy vessels brought back, all proclaim the same return of penitents to the Church. But because Esdras unfolds all these things, it is pleasing to expound some things from his volume in a spiritual sense, that it may be made clearer how those who had perished through negligence or error must return to penance; with how great grace of God, with how great effort of their own, pardon for what they have committed must be sought and obtained; how the penitent, with those who have lately come to the faith, build the same house of Christ, and together await in the future the solemnities of its dedication.
1.3:
**“WHO IS THERE AMONG YOU”** — BEDE. In these words the great faith and great piety of the king shine forth. Faith indeed, because he understood that the people of Israel was God's before others. Piety, because he allowed all who wished, none excepted, to return free to their homeland. Faith, in that he confessed that the same God both dwells in the heavens and is in Jerusalem, and can go up with each of those returning. For it is plain that he believed him to be not bodily and contained in a place, but a spirit and present everywhere, whom he confessed so to have a place in Jerusalem and in the temple that he did not doubt that he at the same time presides over the kingdom of heaven; he believed him so to reign in the heavens that he is with his faithful on earth and directs their minds and hands to saving works.
**“His God be with him.”**
• as it were: he is not bodily nor contained in a place
• "Without me you can do nothing"
• otherwise no one can pass from the confusion of sins to the works of the virtues, that is, from the bondage of Babylon to the freedom of the homeland
**“Let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judea,”** — that is, in confession; that those who through forgetfulness of God are taken captive by the Chaldeans, that is, by the demons, may return through the confession of the divine goodness to the vision of peace and light
**“LET HIM GO UP TO JERUSALEM”** — BEDE. Those who sin or care for worldly things are below; those who desire to please God sigh for heavenly things; let them pass beyond all the pomps and allurements of the world through love of eternal things, and build a house to God in Judea, that is, in the confession of their own iniquity and of the divine mercy; let them prepare their hearts, which God may deign to inhabit and enlighten, and strive by words and examples to invite their neighbours to the same.
1.4:
**“And let all the rest”** — the rich, namely, who cannot preach
**“in all places wheresoever they dwell,”** — either in Chaldea, that is, or scattered elsewhere through fear of the Chaldeans
**“AND ALL”** — The distinction of the words is to be noted: for the king gave leave to all who were released from captivity, that whoever would might go up, with the Lord as leader, to build the temple; yet he did not command all to go up, but those whom, liberty being granted, it pleased to dwell elsewhere he commanded each from his own place to help those going up, namely by giving them money or cattle for the needs of so long a journey; he also desired them to give and entrust to them other gifts, which they should offer in the temple of the Lord as a memorial of the senders. All therefore were freed from captivity, all were given to works of piety, but the more perfect went up to build the temple to the Lord, the rest helped. For all the elect, rescued from the power of darkness, belong to the freedom of the sons of God and of glory; all rejoice to be numbered in the society of the holy city, that is, of the Church; but it belongs only to the perfect to labour in the building of that same Church by preaching also to others, who are given double honour by the Apostle, as the angel says to Daniel: "They that are learned shall shine as the brightness of the firmament: and they that instruct many to justice, as stars for all eternity." For the instructors of many, the more they train their hearers to love heavenly things, the less care they take for earthly things; nay, they leave what they have acquired for the hope of eternal things. Hence it is necessary that the rich, who cannot preach, stand by to relieve their want for preaching, that so they may be partakers of the preaching. Whence John: "We therefore ought to receive such, that we may be fellow helpers of the truth."
**“help him”** — for preaching
**“the men”** — that is, of whatever profession
**“HELP HIM”** — Those who abound in temporal things ought not only to minister necessaries to the poor of Christ, but also willingly to do for themselves what good they can, that by both benefits they may deserve to have a part in the temple of God, which is the Church.
1.5:
**“Then rose up the chief of the fathers”** — because they lie with a weak and sluggish mind, or have no care for their own or their brethren's love and salvation
**“THEN ROSE UP”** — Cyrus commanded all, or rather permitted [all], to go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the Lord; but only those of Juda and Benjamin and the tribe of Levi were willing to go up. For the ten tribes under king Jeroboam were estranged from the temple of God and the worship of piety, and therefore were [taken] into captivity by the kings of the Assyrians, nor, as they relate, did they ever all come into their homeland. But Juda and Benjamin and the tribe of Levi, to which the ministry of the temple belonged, although they imitated the sins of the ten tribes, never deserted the dwelling of the city and the ceremonies of the temple. Hence they were both taken last by the Chaldeans and allowed to return first under the reign of the Persians, because, namely, our Lord was born of the tribe of Juda and of Levi. The tribe of Benjamin also joined itself to them in religious faith, chiefly because Jerusalem was in its lot, and therefore it deserved to be partaker of the mercy bestowed.
**“of Juda and Benjamin, and the priests, and Levites, and every one whose spirit God had raised up,”**
• by admonishing through the Scriptures and pouring in grace
• Scribes instructed in the kingdom of heaven, who, skilfully examining the merits and understanding of their hearers, know how to judge whom to promote and to what grade of ecclesiastical ministry.
**“THE CHIEF OF THE FATHERS”** — For it belongs to the chief of the fathers, that is, to the masters, by work and teaching to build up the minds of those who err in the pursuit of good work.
**“TO GO UP”** — By daily advances, as by certain steps, one ascends to the summit of the virtues, which are in the vision of eternal peace. The first steps are to correct one's own life; the second, to labour over the errors of one's neighbours; the highest, after good works and teaching, to await the joys of everlasting reward.
1.6:
**“And all they”** — the rich, awaiting the joys of everlasting reward
**“that were round about helped their hands”** — of the preachers
**“HELPED THEIR HANDS”** — Companions who cannot build help the hands of the builders by giving money, when laymen commit their children or household to the preachers to be brought up for the Lord, that what they cannot do by themselves they may offer to the Lord as the gift of their devotion through those who can.
**“with vessels of silver, and of gold,”** — [men] illustrious in natural wit, shining with polished [so the edition: 'fixis'] eloquence
**“AND WITH BEASTS”** — BEDE. That is, the slower, but gentle for bearing the light yoke of the gospel. They give also cattle, namely the humble in spirit and the meek, who give freely to the poor of their substance as of milk and wool. They give both substance and divers furniture, when they commend to the doctors men or women distinguished with manifold flowers of works, parents or members of their household, through whom they may be consecrated to the Lord and advance in the building of the house of the Lord. For there are very many who by natural gift are chaste, patient, modest, liberal, lovers of justice and wisdom, instant in prayers and alms like Cornelius, and "who have not the law, do by nature those things that are of the law". When these are offered to the holy preachers to be born again in Christ or to be confirmed in the faith, they are given to the chief of the fathers as divers furniture for building the house of the Lord.
1.7:
**“And king Cyrus brought forth the vessels of the temple of the Lord,”** — the faithful
**“which Nabuchodonosor had taken from Jerusalem,”** — any unclean spirit whatever, which snatches the faithful from the Church and deprives them of the joy of eternal peace
**“and had put them in the temple of his god.”** — by joining them to the fellowship of the reprobate, who are the temple and city of the devil their head, that is, of all evil angels and men
**“BROUGHT FORTH THE VESSELS”** — BEDE. The divers kinds of vessels signify the divers persons or prayers of the faithful. In the Apocalypse we read that "the four and twenty ancients had golden vials full of odours, which are the prayers of saints". For vials are open and bright vessels, and signify the hearts of the simple, which have nothing of crafty thought, but bring forth with a pure tongue what they hold in their heart. In such, then, perfumes, that is, prayers acceptable to God, are related to be. The knives, which they used for cutting or dividing with fitting reason the limbs of the victims, so that, all being distinguished by reason, part was consumed on the altar, part given to the priests, part to the Levites, part to the offerers, signify those who have discretion, who know perfectly how to discern concerning the saving sacrifice, which is Christ, what is to be said to all, what to the more perfect, what, exceeding the measure of human thought, is to be given to the fire of the Holy Spirit. The golden cups [are] those who glow with the greater splendour of wisdom; but the silver ones those who, ruddy [so the edition: 'rutili'] with the beauty of teaching, expound more plainly what they know; distinguishing whom the Apostle says: "To one indeed, by the Spirit, is given the word of wisdom: and to another, the word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit." And that the number of the vessels is recorded both specially for each and generally in the sum of all signifies that the Lord holds written in the book of eternal memory the sum of his elect, not only of those who persevere in the cleanness of faith, but also of those who return to the faith by coming to their senses; in figure of whom it is fittingly added: Sassabasar took all etc.
1.8:
**“Now Cyrus king of Persia brought them forth by the hand of Mithridates the son of Gazabar, and numbered them out to Sassabasar the prince of Juda.”** — Judas is interpreted 'confession'
**“AND NUMBERED THEM OUT”** — This is done when Christ, who is the heir of all whom he predestined to salvation, rescues them from the power of Satan and offers them to the priests of the Church to be reconciled through penance.
1.9:
**“And this is the number of them: thirty bowls of gold, a thousand bowls of silver,”** — the simple and bright hearts of the saints
**“nine and twenty knives, thirty cups of gold,”** — who know how to divide and understand with discretion the sacrifice which is Christ
**“AND THIS IS THE NUMBER”**
• Because the Lord knows the number of the elect, nor does any of his sheep perish that confess his great and terrible name.
• Because none of the predestined can perish for ever; for if at any time they are carried off into Babylon, that is, into the confusion of sins, by divine providence they are brought back through the fellowship of the just to the peace of the Church. But the vessels which the army of the Chaldeans, when Jerusalem was taken, is related to have broken and, broken, carried into Babylonia, express those who are so taken by the devil that, before they repent, they are snatched away to everlasting punishment.
1.10: **“silver cups of a second sort four hundred and ten, other vessels a thousand.”** — who, with fervent charity, are wont to be inebriated with consolations

2.1:
**“NOW THESE ARE THE CHILDREN OF THE PROVINCE”** — Of Judea, that is, not of Babylonia. For to it belonged also those of the stock of the captives born in Babylonia. For they sighed with their whole soul for Judea and Jerusalem; whose figure their leader Zorobabel bears, who by his very name shows himself born in Babylon, but by intention and work a citizen of Jerusalem. In a higher sense the children of the Church are children of the heavenly homeland, not only those who are already imbued with the sacraments of the Church, but also those who, outside, that is, at times wandering among the impious, are by divine election foreordained to life before the ages and are to be consecrated by the ministries of divine grace; of whom it is well added: And they returned to Jerusalem.
**“AND THEY RETURNED”** — For when, freed from the power of Satan, those who had strayed from the faith, together with those who have lately learned the faith, have returned to Jerusalem of the longed-for peace and to Judea of confession or praise, each one soon seeks again and enters his own city, that is, devoutly carries out the keeping and practice of the virtues which the divine favour bestows according to the measure of faith. And well, when he had said generally that they returned to Juda and Jerusalem, he added: every one to his own city; because each so dwelt in his own city that all in general belonged to Juda and Jerusalem. Jerusalem therefore designates the universal state of the Church, and the cities belonging to it the several virtues of the faithful, in which they are defended from the attacks of demons. By the cities in which those dwelt who had come from captivity to Jerusalem and Judea can also be taken the divers churches throughout the world, of which the one catholic [Church] is made up; in which whoever live each profess themselves sons of the catholic Church, as it were citizens of Jerusalem. And before the others they had Zorobabel and Josue as leaders, of whom one was of the royal, the other of the priestly stock, who bore the one person of the true King and High Priest. He alone it is through whom we come to salvation, whence: "No man cometh to the Father, but by me"; who gathers each of the elect, either by himself through hidden inspiration or through preachers by open teaching, from the confusion of the present life to the vision of peace and the confession of divine praise, as it were to Judea and Jerusalem from Babylon. And the vision of peace and confession is begun in the present and perfected in the future.
**“EVERY ONE TO HIS OWN CITY”** — BEDE. Scripture therefore carefully distinguished from which generation of the captives they were released and returned to their homeland, that they might be admonished from this with how great certainty the Lord writes the sum of his elect in the book of life, and as it were marks down in the register of heaven how many souls each of the faithful converted by word or example, for whom he will reward them with a sure recompense.
2.2:
**“Who came with Zorobabel, Josue, Nehemias, Saraias, Rahelaias, Mardochai, Belsan, Mesphar, Belguai,”** — otherwise: Beguai
**“THE NUMBER OF THE MEN OF THE PEOPLE OF ISRAEL”** — BEDE. By the people of Israel he means the tribe of Juda and Benjamin, and whoever of the other tribes had once escaped the hands of the Assyrians but had been [carried] into captivity with these by the Babylonians. Finally it is to be noted that in the very order of the catalogue, and more where the same catalogue is repeated in the second part of the book, that is, in the words of Nehemias, the names of about fifteen cities are inserted which, unless I am mistaken, are found only in Juda and Benjamin. Hence it is probable that the people of Israel in this place is to be understood chiefly of these tribes, together with the priests and Levites who had had a lot among them.
2.4: **“The children of Gersephatia, three hundred seventy-five.”** — otherwise: two
2.5: **“The children of Arethi, seven hundred seventy-five.”** — in very many [manuscripts] it is lacking
2.20: **“The children of Gebbar, nine hundred”** — otherwise: ninety
2.33: **“the children of Lodadin and Ono, seven hundred”** — otherwise: six hundred
2.36: **“The priests: the children of Jadaia”** — otherwise: Idaia
2.40:
**“The Levites: the children of Josue and Cedmiel, of the children of Odevia,”** — otherwise: Odema
**“seventy-four.”** — otherwise: three
2.43:
**“The Nathinites: the children of Sia,”** — otherwise: Sisai; otherwise: Osai
**“THE NATHINITES: THE CHILDREN”** — BEDE. The Nathinites, who are described in order after the priests, Levites, singers and porters, were then those who are now called subdeacons in the Church, obeying the offices of the Levites and receiving the offerings from the people in the temple.
2.44: **“the children of Ceros, the children of Sisaa,”** — otherwise: Sisaia; otherwise: Siaa
2.45: **“the children of Lebana, the children of Azaba,”** — otherwise: Agaba; otherwise: Abaga
2.47: **“the children of Gaddel, the children of Gaer, the children of Raahia,”** — otherwise: Rahaia
2.55: **“the children of the servants of Solomon, the children of Sothei,”** — otherwise: Sophei
2.58:
**“All the Nathinites, and the children of the servants of Solomon, three hundred ninety-two.”** — these were the stewards [so the edition: 'auctores'] of the temple, who repaired the roofs if by chance they had been damaged, and restored them out of the sacred money
**“ALL THE NATHINITES”** — In this place, even according to the letter, the grace of God is shown, by which even in the Old Testament gentiles were received to salvation; for when the catalogue of those who were certainly known to belong truly to the people of God had been set out, those were added of whom it was not known whether they were of Israel or of the proselytes, and their number is set out together among the sons of Israel. For although, through the long separation of their fathers from the temple or people of God, they could not show how they belonged to it, yet because they had gone up from the captivity when general leave was given, they were received as companions; for the rest of the Israelites rejoiced to have them as brothers and acquaintances for love of the common faith and religion, even if they knew them less in the origin of the flesh. Allegorically, among the penitents who, freed from the captivity of vices, go up to build the house of the Lord in themselves or in others, there are some who, bound by very many graver sins, seem so estranged by God from every act of piety and chastity that nothing at all of the goodness and religion which they had received from the doctors seems to have remained in them; nor can they show whether they were begotten of Israel, that is, of holy Church, because by sinning such men have become as if they had never belonged to the Holy Spirit; yet by repenting they are corrected and converted, so that their number is written in heaven among the true Israelites in whom there is no guile.
2.59: **“And these are they that came up from Thelmala, Thelarsa, Cherub, and Don, and Mer: and they could not show the house of their fathers, and”** — or: from
2.61: **“And of the children of the priests: the children of Iobia, the children of Accos, the children of Berzellai, who took a wife of the daughters of Berzellai the Galaadite, and was called by their name.”** — AND OF THE CHILDREN OF THE PRIESTS. BEDE. The children of the transmigration act with the same caution toward the priests as toward the people. For they took care that it should be distinctly clear who truly belonged to the people of Israel or to the priestly race, and who were either suspect or certainly begotten of the stock of proselytes, that is, of strangers. The suspect priests therefore they removed from the office of the altar until their origin should be more certainly made clear; but nonetheless they kept them in the fellowship of those who returned with unanimous peace. Mystically, the sons of the priests going up from the Babylonian captivity seek the writing of their genealogy and, not finding it, are cast out of the priesthood, when ministers of the altar fall into such great crimes or wicked doctrines that, even if by repenting they return to the salvation of the soul, they are not worthy to be restored to the sacred grade. For although among the faithful they await eternal life, yet they do not find among the perfect priests the writing of their grade, which they cannot regain.
2.64:
**“All the multitude as one man,”** — "The multitude of believers had but one heart and one soul"
**“forty-five”** — otherwise: two
**“thousand three hundred and sixty,”**
• although so great an army, of such divers grades, such divers conditions
• ALL THE MULTITUDE etc. BEDE. These signify those who strive by the progress of a more amended life to overcome vices and climb to the summit of the virtues, yet are not yet sufficient of themselves to provide the way of the regular life, but are restrained and directed by the diligence of those who have gone before in Christ.
2.65:
**“besides their menservants and their womenservants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven: and amongst them”** — among the people
