**“singing men and singing women, two hundred.”** — who sounded the psalms with sweet melody, which the Levites did in the temple among the daily sacrifices, which it is credible that many of the people also did in their own places
**“AND AMONGST THEM”** — BEDE. Mystically, in the temple or people of God the singers are those who keep the heavenly commandments with greater sweetness of mind and commit them to their hearers to be kept with frequent exhortations. And well are singing women joined to the singers because of sex, namely the feminine, in which very many persons are found who not only by living but also by preaching kindle the hearts of their neighbours to the praise of their Creator, and as it were with the sweetness of their voice help those building the temple.
2.66: **“THEIR MULES”** — BEDE. The mule is begotten of an ass and a mare, the she-mule of a horse and a she-ass. Among the men who had gone up from the captivity the animals by which they were helped are also described, and their number is set down like that of the men; because there are many in the Church who are either slower in understanding or even carnal, yet devoutly obey their spiritual masters and bend the back of the mind to carry the burdens of their brethren's need, and, rescued with the rest of the elect from the confusion of the devil's captivity, make for the walls of the city above; whose number too is kept entire in the memory of God. Whence: "Thy eyes did see my imperfect being." And elsewhere: "Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord."
2.68:
**“And some of the chief”** — more eminent in life
**“of the fathers,”** — who are solicitous for others
**“when they came to the temple of the Lord, which is in Jerusalem, offered freely to the house of God”** — going beyond the precepts of the law
**“OFFERED FREELY”** — BEDE. It is a sign of great devotion to offer to the Lord freely not only the due offerings, that is, those commanded by the law, but also gifts not according to precept but according to counsel. It is commanded by the law: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God, and thy neighbour as thyself", and the rest of this kind. But a voluntary offering is: "If thou wilt be perfect, go sell what thou hast, and give to the poor." As the Apostle [says] of virgins: "I have no commandment of the Lord; but I give counsel." Rightly then the chief of the fathers offer freely for building the house of God; because the more each abstains even from lawful things, the more effectively he builds the Church of God, since those who see the examples of their perfection fear to commit unlawful things all the more, the more they consider that these do not even use lawful things.
2.69:
**“According to their ability”** — this is the measure of human perfection
**“ACCORDING TO THEIR ABILITY”** — For this is the measure of perfection, that each should labour for the Lord according to his power, and confirm the state of the Church first in himself, then in his neighbours. Those who so live are rightly called the chief of the fathers, because by living more loftily they have the primacy, in perfection of life and teaching, over those who in the Church are called fathers for their zeal of solicitude.
**“they gave towards the expenses of the work, of gold”** — of the brightness of wisdom
**“sixty-one thousand solids, of silver”** — of polished eloquence: "The words of the Lord are pure words"
**“five thousand pounds, and a hundred garments for the priests.”**
• works of justice surpassing the manners of the common people and worthy of hearts consecrated to God
• "Let thy priests be clothed with justice"
• But it is to be noted how much the captivity profited the people of God. For those who, according to Jeremias, four thousand six hundred, were [carried] into captivity, being multiplied among the enemies, returned to their homeland nearly fifty thousand men; and those who had been poor and servants return enriched with gold, silver, garments and servants; and those who lost their homeland because of the multitude of false gods now return home rejoicing in the faith of the one true God, worshipping that very faith with unanimous devotion, so that those who because of the diversity of religion were called by divers names, Juda and Israel, are now for the unity of piety all called by the ancient name Israel. For the worship of piety, which they despised in the holy land while the prophets cried out against them [so the edition: 'reclinantibus'] and showed examples of justice, they now loved in a foreign land, among enemies who served idolatry. For those whom liberty and plenty in their homeland made negligent of the heavenly commandments, servitude and want in exile brought to the obedience of the Creator. For the human body [so the edition] is loosened by riches and liberty, and by hardships and poverty is gathered back to itself. What therefore was done once in that people is wont to be done daily in all penitents, when those who through negligence fell into the snares of the devil rise again, divinely helped, through the diligence of penance; and those who, stripped of the works of the virtues by the devil, departed from the Church return to its communion to be exercised in greater virtues. For the more gravely they remember that they have erred, the more ardently they apply themselves to good works.
**“SOLIDS OF GOLD”** — BEDE. The chief of the fathers offer gold and silver and priestly garments, according to their ability, for the expenses of the works of the temple, when holy men, by living well, bestow on the edification of the faithful whatever of wisdom, eloquence and good action they receive. The weight of the gold and silver is fixed, the number of the priestly garments is fixed, that we may know that the Lord knows thoughts and words and deeds and rewards them worthily.
2.70:
**“SO THE PRIESTS AND THE LEVITES DWELT”** — The Levite taken captive by the Chaldeans recovers his city when a deacon, by the Lord's gift, restores the virtue of perfection which he had lost when seduced by the devil. But the one born in Babylon, coming into Judea, enters the city when one regenerated in Christ and well instructed in the Church keeps according to rule the diaconate once received. For as the former was freed by the grace of Christ as from the Chaldean bondage, so the latter, by carrying out the good works in which the predecessors of the same grade lived, ascend as it were to the walls of their own virtue or city.
**“AND ALL ISRAEL”** — BEDE. By all Israel he means not only the ten tribes, which were once called Israel to distinguish them from the two which were called Juda, but in general all who returned, whether of Juda and Benjamin or of the other tribes. For when the ten tribes had been carried over to the Assyrians and the Samaritans put in their land in their place, whoever had remained left [their land], and broke the idols, and began to serve the Lord with a whole heart and to sacrifice in the temple, as it is written in Paralipomenon. These then who were left were [carried] into captivity with the tribe of Juda and Benjamin, with whom they had been joined, and returned together to their homeland and to their cities, which they found empty with their fields and villages. For no settler had entered them while they themselves served in Babylon, as neither [had any entered] the lands of the two tribes. For the land kept her sabbaths all the days of the desolation. But the greater part of the ten tribes, taken captive by the Assyrians beyond the mountains of the Medes, never returned; nor, if it returned, could it enter its cities, which the Samaritans possessed; of whom the Jews promise themselves that, when their Christ reigns, they will return into Judea with the other men of their nation and will reign in the whole world. Allegorically. The priests, Levites, singers, porters and Nathinites, and all Israel dwell in their cities when the ministers of the altar and the doctors and the Christian people serve God faithfully in their grades, whether those who, the same grade having once been defiled or lost by vices, have been corrected through penance, or those who, coming lately from the kingdom of the devil to the Church, have acquired for themselves a good grade. For the Levites or sons of Israel entered their own cities, not only those who had lost them when taken captive, but also those who, begotten of the captives, had learned that they belonged to them by paternal succession. But whoever were so taken captive that, never returning, they left their estates to others to possess, signify those who by sinning so depart from the Church that they never come to their senses, and leave to others the rewards promised to them. Whence: "Be mindful from whence thou art fallen, and do penance, and do the first works. Or else I come to thee, and will move thy candlestick out of its place" etc. And elsewhere: "Hold fast that which thou hast, that no man take thy crown."

3.1:
**“And now the seventh month was come, and the children of Israel were in their cities: and the people gathered themselves together as one man to Jerusalem.”**
• AND NOW THE SEVENTH MONTH WAS COME, which with us is October, solemn above the others by the observance of the law, in which also the dedication of the temple was celebrated. Fittingly therefore, as soon as they had entered their cities and provided dwellings for themselves, they forthwith flocked together to Jerusalem and built the altar, and that at the time at which the temple with the altar and all the vessels had once been consecrated, and at which they were wont to come every year for the day of the consecration.
• Mystically. The seventh month signifies the grace of the Holy Spirit. In this month after the captivity we come together from our cities to Jerusalem when, the filth of vices being taken away, after the beginning of good works we are enlightened by the greater grace of the same Spirit and are kindled with love of the peace above, which is in true unity. For Jerusalem is called 'vision of peace'.
3.2:
**“AND JOSUE ROSE UP”** — Of the priestly tribe, which signifies Christ the true priest, who "hath washed us from our sins in his own blood" and "now appears in the presence of God for us".
**“and his brethren the priests, and Zorobabel”** — Christ, namely our king
**“the son of Salathiel, and his brethren,”**
• as the first masters
• AND HIS BRETHREN THE PRIESTS etc. Of whom it is said: "Go, tell my brethren." These are the higher in the Church and, cleaving more familiarly to Christ, build up the Church. To the whole Church too it is said: "But you are a chosen generation, a kingly priesthood." For the elect are members of the supreme Priest, offering their bodies a living sacrifice.
**“and they built the altar of the God of Israel, that they might offer upon it”** — because without it they do not please
**“holocausts,”** — renouncing the world altogether and following Christ
**“as it is written in the law of Moses the man of God.”** — acting manfully and strongly in all things
**“AND THEY BUILT”** — BEDE. With great foresight they first built the altar, so that, because the temple was not yet founded, they might yet have where, sacrificing, they could show the devotion of their mind. Which we too do spiritually today, when before all things we place in our heart the faith of the Lord's incarnation and passion and hand it on to our hearers; whence: "I judged not myself to know any thing among you, but Jesus Christ, and him crucified." On this altar we offer our holocausts, that is, perfect thoughts and works. For so the vows of our actions please God the Father, if we partake of the sacraments of Christ, if we are kindled by the power of the Holy Spirit as by the fire of the altar. For a holocaust is called 'wholly burnt', by which name those sacrifices were called of which nothing went to human uses, but the whole was given to God and consumed by the highest fire. By these is expressed the life of the faithful, who seek nothing of their own but spend all that they live in the service of God. And they rejoice not only to trample the will of body and soul for the Lord, but to lay down their very soul for him, saying with the apostles: "Behold we have left all things, and have followed thee" etc. To whom it is answered: "Every one that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters" etc. This holocaust is to be offered on the altar of God, because unless in the faith of Christ it cannot be accepted. For many philosophers left their own things and, leading a clean and poor life, seemed to make a holocaust, but they did not do this on the altar of God, because they left pleasures, but "did not have Christ as advocate with the Father".
3.3:
**“And they set the altar upon its bases, while there put them in fear”** — because opposition of wicked spirits or men at once withstands undertakings devoted to God
**“the people of the lands round about,”**
• not of those whose "conversation is in heaven"
• ITS BASES etc. That is, the hearts of the elect, prepared to receive the sacraments of faith by the precepts of the masters, as by the tools of craftsmen. And well is there one altar, but many bases which carry it; because there is "one God, one faith", but many hearts of the faithful, which, instructed by one rule of truth and as it were gathered into an equal bosom, carry with common devotion the burden of the heavenly sacraments. But he who commits the sacraments of faith to the less instructed and to those who do not forsake their vices, as it were sets the altar of the Lord on the earth without bases, because he hands heavenly things to minds still earthly. Whence: "Neither do men light a candle and put it under a bushel, but upon a candlestick" etc. For as Christ is called an altar, because he amends from iniquities and commends the vows of prayers to the Father, so also a candle, because he placed the light of divinity in the earthen vessel of humanity. And the bases are set under the altar and the candlestick under the candle when the faithful with humble intention submit their hearts and bodies to practising by work what they believe.
**“and they offered”** — yet persisting in the precepts
**“AND THEY OFFERED UPON IT A HOLOCAUST”** — BEDE. Morning and evening we offer a holocaust to the Lord upon his altar when, faith in him being established in our heart, we give our effort to good acts with entire devotion; and this morning and evening, namely when we remember that we received from him the beginnings of saving intention, and that we do not perfect what we have begun except through the help of his grace. And therefore we offer him vows of thanks in all things with ardent desire of a pious life. Again we make a holocaust in the morning when, for the light of spiritual knowledge received, we render God the return of living well; but in the evening when we burn with unceasing zeal for the everlasting rest which we hope for in him after good works. It can also rightly be taken according to the letter that we offer a holocaust morning and evening when we take care to please God at all times in such a way that, rising at dawn, we do not go forth to do the necessary things of human frailty before, inflamed with the fire of divine charity, we commend ourselves to the Lord with devout prayers; whence: "In the morning my prayer shall prevent thee." Likewise, when the works of the day are finished, let us not give sleep to our eyes before we consecrate a place for the Lord in ourselves by earnestness in prayer, according to that: "Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight; the lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice."
3.4:
**“AND THEY KEPT”** — BEDE. Those who had gone up from Babylon to Jerusalem, burning to fulfil all the commandments of the Lord, desired to celebrate this solemnity on each day of the week which the law had commanded, fulfilling what it befits us to fulfil spiritually. For we went out of Egypt through the blood of the lamb, that we might come to the land of promise, when, baptized with the sacrament of the Lord's passion, we cast off the heavy yoke of transgression, that, adopted "into the liberty of the glory of the children of God", we may be heirs of the heavenly kingdom. And we dwelt in tabernacles, going through the desert a long time until we should come to the homeland, when in baptism, renouncing Satan as the kingdom of Egypt, that is, of darkness, and all the pomps and works of the world, we promised that we were as pilgrims and wayfarers in the world, citizens of another life which we hope for from the Lord. In memory of this hope of promise we ought to dwell in tabernacles in the seventh month, and, the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit enlightening us, all the day long to forsake the world as dry and foreign, and with fixed intention to hasten to the unfading joys of paradise; and this for seven days, that is, through the whole time of the present life, which revolves in so many days. On each day of this week too we ought to make a holocaust, and the work of the day in its day: the offering, namely, wholly burnt, in those things which properly belong to the divine service, as prayers and fasts; and the work of the day in its day in those things which belong to the service of brotherly love, as ministering bread to the hungry, drink to the thirsty, and the like. Paul hinted that these solemnities of tabernacles were to be celebrated by us mystically, when in the midst of preaching he gave himself to the craft of tent-making. For he made tents to teach that he was a pilgrim, and that those whom he instructed were pilgrims in this life but hoped for a homeland in the future; whence: "While we are in the body, we are absent from the Lord"; and elsewhere: "For we have not here a lasting city, but we seek one that is to come."
**“THE FEAST”** — Which in Greek is called Scenopegia, that is, the pitching of tabernacles, which begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and lasts seven days, in which the Lord commanded the people to dwell in tabernacles and, searching the law daily, to offer holocausts to the Lord; because they once dwelt in tabernacles, namely in the wilderness, while Moses preached the law and God often appeared to them, long awaiting the promised rest; that, namely, the grace of so great a benefit might never come into forgetfulness.
**“ORDERLY”** — Because whatever is done without order loses the merit of perfection, for "the king's honour loveth judgment". For in what we do for the honour of the supreme King it is necessary that we distinguish with sure discretion of judgment when and how much is to be done.
3.5:
**“And afterwards the continual holocaust, both on the new moons, and on all the solemnities of the Lord, that were consecrated, and on all in which a freewill offering was made to the Lord.”** — as it were, namely, apart from the general commandments, we offer freely to God, of which it is said not by commanding but by counselling: "If thou wilt be perfect, go sell what thou hast" etc. And elsewhere by persuading: "He that can take, let him take it."
**“ON THE NEW MOONS”** — That is, at the beginnings of the months at the rising of the moon, from which the Hebrews always began their months, having no months except lunar ones; hence, for calends, the Greeks better call them neomenias, that is, new moons. And if the months, because of the thirty days by which they are filled, signify the fullness of the works of light, when in the faith of the holy Trinity we perfect the precepts of the decalogue, what do the beginnings of the months, in which the moon is said to be newly kindled by the sun that it may shine again, designate, if not the beginnings of good work, which by the gift of the Creator's grace we receive as by the presence of the sun of justice? For the signifying of which divine illumination, without which we can neither begin nor perfect anything good, God commanded all the calends, that is, the beginnings of the months, to be celebrated; whence: "Blow up the trumpet on the new moon, on the noted day of your solemnity." And well is it said that, the feast of tabernacles being ended, the children of the transmigration made the continual holocaust etc.; because after the mind has once perfectly renounced this world, it must spend itself wholly in the service of the divine will.
3.6:
**“From the first day of the seventh month”** — namely of spiritual illumination
**“FROM THE FIRST DAY”** — That is, from the beginning of divine inspiration, by which the human conscience is changed and, pleasures being neglected, burns for those things alone which are the Lord's; like the apostles, who, inflamed by the Holy Spirit and made as it were a holocaust, preached the wonderful works of God in all tongues. Hence among the Hebrews the seventh month is called the new year, because through the Holy Spirit it is given to the faithful to fulfil the new commandment of charity and to render a new song in the building of the house of God.
**“they began to offer holocausts to the Lord: but the temple of God was not yet founded.”**
• But it is to be noted that in the seventh month the people was gathered in Jerusalem, and, all being gathered, Josue and Zorobabel with their brethren are related to have built the altar and from the first day of the seventh month to have offered holocaust; from which it is gathered that this altar was very quickly put together of unhewn stones, not, as formerly, wrought of wood and covered with plates of brass. For not otherwise, even with a very great crowd of builders pressing on, could it be begun and finished in one day and prepared for offering holocaust. For in the book of Machabees it is said to have been made of stones: "And they took whole stones according to the law, and built a new altar according to the former."
• It is to be noted that the beginning of the fifth age, like that of the four preceding, is consecrated by holocausts offered to the Lord. For in the first, the protomartyr Abel, first of all the elect, offered God a holocaust of the firstlings of the sheep, and dedicated the entrance of the newborn world first with victims of cattle, at length with his own blood. Noe consecrated the rise of the second age by holocausts offered to God of those things which had been in the ark. Melchisedech and Abraham consecrated the third age, the one with bread and wine, the other by offering his own son. David consecrated the fourth age to the Lord, building an altar in the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite and offering holocausts to God, by which he appeased him whom he had offended by numbering the people; where Abraham is said to have offered his son, and where, after the temple was built by Solomon, the altar of holocausts is known to have been placed. Now Josue and Zorobabel offered the beginning of the fifth age, building an altar in the same place and offering holocausts to God as soon as the yoke of captivity was shaken off, and afterwards appeased the Lord to themselves with the continual holocaust. All these things went before in figure of him who in the sixth age redeemed the whole world with the victim of his flesh.
3.7:
**“And they gave”**
• that they might work more readily
• the chief of the fathers
• It can also be said that, the altar being built, they offer holocausts to God but do not yet build the temple, so that they can be numbered among the perfect even if they do not yet receive the time or means of doing or perfecting the good things they desire; as Abraham was already perfect in faith when he had not yet perfected works. Whence: "Abraham believed God, and it was reputed to him unto justice." But when he offered his son upon the altar, he rendered to God more perfect holocausts, as it were with the temple built. For the several acts or steps of pious devotion are the courses of polished stones with which we may build in our heart a dwelling beloved of God.
• The founding of the temple signifies those who, lately converted, prepare a place for the Lord in themselves; whence: "Your members are the temple of the Holy Ghost" etc.
**“THEY GAVE”** — BEDE. Those who, freed from the captivity, came to Jerusalem, purposed to make the temple and afterwards made it; but, the altar first being set up, they commended themselves to the Lord with daily holocausts, that they might deserve to build the temple itself worthily. Let him therefore who wishes to teach others first teach himself, lest he hear from the Apostle: "Thou therefore that teachest another, teachest not thyself." Whence: "I chastise my body, and bring it into subjection: lest perhaps, when I have preached to others" etc. Rightly therefore the children of the transmigration are related to have offered to God no other sacrifices than holocausts, that is, offerings wholly burnt; because he who desires by teaching to restrain those who live ill from unlawful things must give himself over wholly to the Creator by living well and by abstaining even from lawful things.
**“money”** — namely examples of the virtues, or the scriptures, strengthened by which they may not grow weary
**“to hewers of stones”** — to the preachers, the hewers of stones
**“TO HEWERS OF STONES”** — Mystically. BEDE. The hewers of stones in the building of the house of God are those who instruct the hearts of their neighbours by teaching or rebuking; whom, while they teach them to stand firm among others, they fit as it were by squaring. For whichever way you turn a square it will stand; and the mind of the elect, while it remains unmoved among adversities or prosperities, shows that it has in itself the square figure of virtue. Hence the ark of Noe is described as made of squared timber. For the same Church is figured by the temple made of stone, by the ark framed of timber, and by the tabernacle composed of curtains and boards.
**“and to masons:”**
• who make mortar to cement the stones. The pious diligence of the people is to be noted: from their own necessaries they either buy materials or hire workmen
• MASONS etc. The masons likewise are preachers who, while they bind one to another with the bond of charity those whom they train in good works, join them as squared and polished stones by pouring in mortar, lest they loosen the order of the structure, saying: "But before all things have a constant mutual charity among yourselves." Hence Paul: "But above all these things have charity, which is the bond of perfection."
**“and meat, and drink, and oil to them of Sidon and Tyre,”**
• Tyre and Sidon, most noble cities of Phenicia, near mount Libanus
• TO THEM OF SIDON AND TYRE etc. The chief of the fathers, namely Josue and Zorobabel and their brethren, give food and oil to those of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar wood from Libanus to the sea of Joppe, when they commend to the doctors, that they may be able to preach, the spiritual gifts which went before in Christ, to be imitated. Or when Christ, who is signified in Josue and Zorobabel, distributes the spiritual gifts of his word, enlightened inwardly by which they are made stronger to overthrow the boasting of the proud [so the edition: 'supernorum'] and foolish wisdom. Whence: "Thou hast prepared a table before me against them that afflict me. Thou hast anointed my head with oil." Money therefore is given to the hewers of stones and masons, and food, drink and oil to the cutters of timber, that they may prepare material for building the house of God, when an abundance of the virtues is divinely bestowed on the preachers by grace, helped by which they are sufficient to correct the hearts of the wicked and to fit them for the reception of good things.
• To those of Sidon, the hunters, who catch the wandering senses for Christ with the nets of faith. Whence: "I will make you to be fishers of men." The same are 'distressed', because they have distress in the world, though confident that the Lord has overcome the world.
**“TO THEM OF SIDON AND TYRE”** — Those of Sidon and Tyre also represent the preachers, who with the axe of the word of God cast down men once lofty and splendid in the glory of the world from the state of their former life, that, laid low to their salvation and as it were dried out from the corrupting moisture of their inborn sense, they may correct them from every crookedness of vices and fashion them for the adornment or defence of the Church. Hence in the Psalm which is entitled "At the finishing of the tabernacle": "The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars."
**“TO BRING TREES”** — They carry the felled timber into the sea, not to be sunk, but to be carried through it to Joppe, which is interpreted 'beauty', when the doctors foretell to the hearers called to the faith that temptations will meet them but are to be overcome by faith; that first the wild fruits [so the edition: 'feri fructus'] of vices or of wicked men may be taken away, and so one may come to the beautiful walls and the harbour of the virtues; as it were that we may first renounce the devil, namely the dragon, king of all things that are in the waters, that is, of the impious, who live in the sea, that is, in the turmoils of the world, and afterwards come to the beauty of the faith by which we confess the holy Trinity and one Godhead, the dispensation of the incarnation of Christ, the unity of the Church, the remission of sins and the resurrection of the flesh. Hence Peter raised Tabitha in this city, because in the perfection of this faith and of the universal Church we are raised from the death of sins through baptism; and when after baptism we incur the death of sin, through the same we revive by repenting and are joined again to the Church through the reconciliation of the priests.
**“to the sea of Joppe,”** — this is a maritime city about forty miles distant from Jerusalem
**“JOPPE”** — From where, that is, they might be carried by land for the work of the temple, as was done in the first building of the temple. But Solomon by royal power easily obtained what he wished from king Hiram; these, however, returning from captivity and not having the power of a kingdom, bought everything.
3.8:
**“AND IN THE SECOND YEAR”** — BEDE. Since it is said above that they came to Jerusalem in the seventh month, but here that in the second year of their coming, in the second month, they began the work of the temple, it is plain that for seven months they prepared stones, mortar, timber and the other necessaries, and began to work at the beginning of the eighth month. For there were six months of the first year and the seventh of the following. Mystically the seventh belongs to the sabbath, in which the Lord, the maker of the world, rested from his works, or Christ rested in the sepulchre after the passion; eight to the first of the sabbath, on which he rose; seven to the hope of our sabbath after death; eight look to the joy of our everlasting blessedness. Since therefore all the working of the elect, who are the house of God, is begun and perfected by the grace of the Spirit, and all is carried out with regard and intention to future rest and immortality, rightly the builders of the temple, holocausts being offered to God from the seventh month, begin to prepare the expenses for the building, and, these being prepared in seven months, they undertake the work in the eighth; nor is any other number set in the preparation of so great a work than that which proclaims the sevenfold grace of the Spirit by which we are helped in working, or the rest of souls or the resurrection of bodies which we hope for in working well.
**“IN JERUSALEM”** — That is, the place of the temple, where they desired to build the temple. For the Jews are mistaken who say that the walls of the temple were never overthrown by the Chaldeans, but only the roof, since it is plain that Esdras, a child of the transmigration, made the temple from the foundations.
**“AND ALL THAT”** — Great was the devotion of the whole people; for they rejoiced that they had returned from captivity, and as much as they abhorred the crimes of the proud city, so much did they desire to see the beauty of Jerusalem; as much as they abominated the shrines, so much did they strive to have the temple of God restored. So not only ought bishops and priests to build up the people of the faithful, that is, the house of God, but the people too, called from the captivity of vices to the vision of true peace, ought to require the ministry of the word from those who know how to speak; which ministers of the word, that is, Levites, are appointed from twenty years and upward, because such are to be appointed and preferred for preaching as not only show the Decalogue to their hearers by doing it, but also keep it undefiled in the sight of God by purity and integrity of heart.
**“FROM TWENTY YEARS OLD”** — It is not to be doubted that the state of the Church makes progress through the Spirit there where both the bishops, rightly keeping their grade, ordain masters of truth for the people according to rule, and the people itself, by diligently hearing and obeying, compels them not to cease from teaching. But the sloth of our times hurts the greater and the lesser alike, hindering these from preaching the word, those from hearing it, and both from doing it; because we weigh too little how great is the bitterness of the demonic captivity from which we have been rescued, or how great the solemnity to which we are called, of Jerusalem above, the mother of us all, whose pledge we have already received. But let us look upon the excellent works of the fathers, that we may be the more confounded at the faintheartedness of our own mind.
**“and they appointed Levites from twenty years old and upward, to hasten forward the work of the Lord.”** — But it is to be noted and very often remembered how much good the evil of the captivity brought; rescued from which, all apply themselves to the heavenly services with an earnestness such as never before. And today too it has profited many who had lived negligently in peace suddenly to have erred and sinned, when, raised up by repenting after the fall, they serve God more watchfully; and those who stood sluggish and idle in innocence, admonished after the ruin that befell them, are girded more skilfully against the snares of the enemy, so that those who had not even offended by caring for their own life, returning, have the care of restoring the temple. But above all the Levites and the sons of Juda, because of the priestly and at the same time royal dignity of the Church, which chiefly build the temple; because all who form the hearts of the faithful by teaching or by living well belong to the body of the true King and Priest, that is, Christ. Hence too the authors of the work were Jesus [Josue], sprung of the priestly tribe, and Zorobabel of the royal tribe.
3.9: **“THEN JOSUE STOOD”** — Not the son of Josedec, that is, but one of the Levites appointed from twenty years and upward to direct the work, of whom were Cedmiel and the sons of Enadab, who together with their sons and brethren took charge of the work enjoined. Above too, in the catalogue of the people, these are mentioned first of the Levites after the priests; from which it is gathered that they were the chiefs of the Levites of that time. Well are the sons of Juda put in the midst of the Levites, giving their effort together to restoring the temple, and because of the same agreement in piety they are said to have acted as one; for this is the order of virtue to be imitated, that all the grades dedicated to God and the common devotion of the people should each for his part build up the Church.
3.10:
**“WHEN THEREFORE [THE TEMPLE] WAS FOUNDED”** — Mystically. When the temple of the Lord has been founded by the masons, the priests stand in their ornaments with trumpets, when, sinners having been converted from error and faith and love of Christ founded in them, the masters of the churches rejoice together and, adorning themselves more diligently with good works, sound with the trumpets of saving doctrine, that by the example of virtues and the persuasion of words they may help the good beginnings of those who have lately come together to the grace of Christ by repenting, or [those who] convert others by teaching. And the Levites stand to praise God with cymbals, when the ministers of the second order serve their Creator with pious acts for the instruction of the neophytes, and this in the sweetness of mutual charity. For cymbals, which touch one another that they may sound, express the works of charity by which the saints stir one another to praise. They praise also by the hand of David the king when they diligently attend to the works of Christ which he did through the flesh, and imitate them as far as they can.
**“THE PRIESTS STOOD IN THEIR ORNAMENTS”** — Great devotion of all persons is shown, when, the temple being founded, all praise the mercy of the Lord according to their grade: the priests indeed, adorned with holy vestments as they had been wont while the temple still stood, sounding with trumpets and kindling the heart of the people to the sweetness of the praise above; the Levites singing hymns to the Lord with well-sounding cymbals; the people showing the affection of their heart by praising God with a common shout.
3.11: **“AND THEY SUNG TOGETHER HYMNS”** — That is, on the instruments which he made, or with the psalms which he instituted, or because David, at the placing of the ark, made Asaph and his brethren chief to give praise to the Lord, as Paralipomenon testifies; of whom again it is said that his sons were under his hand, prophesying by the king. Rightly here, when the sons of Asaph praised and gave glory to the Lord by the hand of David, they are to be understood to have done this according to his ordering.
3.12:
**“But many of the priests and the Levites, and the chief of the fathers, and the ancients that had seen the former temple, when it was founded, and this temple before their eyes, wept with a loud voice: and many shouting for joy lifted up their voice.”** — THEY WEPT, that is, seeing how far the poverty of that time was from the once magnificent power of Solomon, by which the former temple was founded; and they knew that the former temple had been destroyed for their crimes, whose greatness and beauty they could not equal. For what the prophet says: "Great shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first", does not belong to the greatness or adornment of the house, but to the thing itself; because it was a greater miracle and a more evident power of God that a few remnants of captives finished so great a work, even with enemies resisting, than that a most wealthy king, having no adversary at all, did as he wished with the help of king Cyrus [so the edition], his dearest friend. Again, the glory of the last house [is] greater than of the first, because in the former house the worshippers of the Old Testament preached to the peoples the Scripture of the law and the prophets; in the second, Christ and the apostles proclaim the grace of the New Testament and the entrance of the heavenly kingdom.
**“BEDE”** — They wept. In the building of the spiritual temple weeping and joy together arise in the chiefs. For the doctors rejoice in the salvation of the penitent, but mourn because they ever committed things to be repented of. They themselves who by penance have risen from the death of the soul exult over their salvation; they mourn because they lost it by sinning. The neophytes rejoice that they have been gathered by the grace of the Redeemer; they grieve that with the human race they perished in their first parent, and, the temple of God being as it were corrupted by the enemies, namely the state of immortal body and soul, were removed into Babylon, that is, into the confusion of the present exile. But because, as the progress of the good grows, the envy of the wicked grows, nor are the temptations of the wicked lacking amid the increase of the pious, who strive to hurt the saints either by feignedly showing good or by openly thrusting in evil, it is rightly added: Now [the enemies] heard etc.

4.1:
**“Now the enemies heard”** — the Samaritans, that is, wicked heretics
**“of Juda”** — of praise and confession
**“and Benjamin,”**
• catholics
• the peoples who will sit at the right hand
**“that the children of the captivity were building a temple to the Lord the God of Israel.”** — instructing the Church by word or example
**“NOW [THE ENEMIES] HEARD”** — BEDE. By the enemies of Juda and Benjamin he means the Samaritans, whom, when the ten tribes had been taken captive, the king of the Assyrians transplanted from divers peoples of the nations into their cities and lands, who afterwards kept in part the law of God which they had received, and no less the idols which they had served before. These, because they abhorred the true worshippers of God, promise help in the work, that, received into fellowship, they might inflict loss. These therefore express false brethren, that is, heretics and wicked catholics, who are enemies of Juda, that is, of confession and praise, which the Church offers through right faith and right and worthy working, and of Benjamin, that is, of the son of the right hand, when they separate those who hear them from the faithful, who are to receive the blessing and the eternal kingdom at the right hand of the Judge. They say therefore: Let us build with you, when heretics seek to have the authority of preaching among catholics given to them, promising that they hold with them the same chastity of right faith and working, that, having received the power of teaching, they may sow cockle in the midst of the good seed, from which Paul received the surname spermologus, that is, 'sower of words'. For they entered the land of the children of Israel not brought in by Josue, not subject to the rule of Jerusalem, but brought into its land by a faithless king, namely by an enemy of the people of God, not to serve the Lord but the adversary of the kingdom. So heretics and false catholics, since they attack the peace of the Church by living perversely [so the edition: 'puer se'] or by teaching, are strangers to the kingdom of Jerusalem and belong rather to the lot of the gentiles, whose idols they serve; and they enter the borders of holy Church not with Jesus Christ as leader but with the devil, whom the king of Assur signifies. So Simon Magus received baptism in the Church not for his own salvation but that he might search out the secrets of the Church more familiarly; which he showed by his end, when he most bitterly attacked as an open enemy the Church which he could not [attack] in the person of a feigned brother.
4.2:
**“And they came to Zorobabel, and the chief of the fathers, and said to them: Let us build with you,”** — let us have equal authority of preaching
**“for we seek your God as you do: behold we have sacrificed victims”** — unclean, namely, because they do not renounce idols; for what concord hath Christ with Belial
4.3: **“YOU HAVE NOTHING TO DO WITH US”** — It is not for heretics to build the Church, from which they are strangers, but only for those who, cleaving to Christ the true King and Priest, have deserved to be called chief of the fathers, and for the pious care which they have toward those who desire to see Christ.
4.4:
**“Then it came to pass that the people of the land hindered the hands of the people of Juda”** — well is he called the people of the land who tries to trouble the workers of virtue and to hinder the heavenly work
**“THEN IT CAME TO PASS”** — BEDE. How often heretics, not only in cities but also in provinces, by teaching perversely or even by raging, hindered the doctrine of true confession, would that we did not know! For, to say nothing of the master of the gentiles, who, bound for two years in Caesarea because of the persecution of the Jews, held back his tongue from building the house of God, through the snares of heretics Athanasius was a fugitive for many years, Ambrose was besieged in his own city, Hilary was banished into exile, Eusebius suffered martyrdom, many bishops in Africa with their tongues cut out were cast out of their province, others were harassed with divers punishments or slain; and they left the house of God which they had built to be profaned by the peoples of the land, that is, by men seeking their own things, "not the things that are Jesus Christ's", until at a time divinely foreseen the means should be available to wise architects for rebuilding the same house after the captivity.
**“OF THE PEOPLE OF JUDA”** — By the people of Juda, that is, confessing and glorifying, he means him who with an entire mind seeks to build for the Lord, that is, to turn the minds and mouths of all whom he can to doing his will and seeking his glory.
4.5:
**“THEY HIRED”** — BEDE. The distinction of the words is to be noted, because he says that counsellors were hired for a price against the workers of the temple to defeat their purpose; but neither was the purpose defeated nor the work interrupted until the letter of accusation was written to Artaxerxes, and at his command they hindered them by arm and strength. For then the work was interrupted, and it was not done until the second year of Darius king of the Persians. From which it is gathered that through the whole time of Cyrus, the work having been begun, they pressed on, though more slowly than was right; but when he was dead they were driven from the work, not hindered by wicked counsels but by open attack. For while Cyrus lived, who had commanded the work to be done, the enemies did not dare to oppose his edicts by open struggle, though they did so secretly by suggesting or counselling.
**“And they hired counsellors against them, to defeat their purpose all the days of Cyrus king of the Persians, even until the reign of Darius king of the Persians.”** — Mystically, heretics, according to the opportunity of the time, now pursue [the Church] in the counsels of malignant doctrines, now with the sharper fight of swords, and sometimes do not fear to harass it with the support of gentile princes. They hinder the hands of the people of Juda when they hold back the Church in its weaker members from the works of pious profession; they strive to defeat the purpose of working when they labour to call minds back even from the intention of good action [so the edition: 'bone ac omnis']. They accuse them before kings when they gain the protection of earthly princes against the Church; how much this harms the faith became known clearer than light in the time of the Arian faithlessness.
4.6:
**“AND IN THE REIGN”** — BEDE. This Artaxerxes, who, receiving the letter of accusation from the Samaritans, came to Jerusalem and builds [so the edition] the temple, Josephus thinks to be Cambyses the son of Cyrus, who, after his father had held the empire thirty years, reigned eight years; and after him the Magi, reigning one year, had Darius the son of Hystaspes as successor of the kingdom; in whose second year, in which he permitted the temple to be built, the angel, interceding for the people, said in Zacharias: "O Lord of hosts, how long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem, and on the cities of Juda, with which thou hast been angry? This is now the seventieth year" etc. But of Assuerus, to whom likewise the letter of accusation is said to have been sent, it is perhaps passed over in silence whether he wrote back or answered anything because, dying in the same year in which he began to reign, he left the height of rule to Artaxerxes, and to him the care of these things; or he was contemporary with Artaxerxes but, as being of lesser power, permitted him to handle and decide these things.
**“BEDE”** — Artaxerxes, who is persuaded and, persuaded, commands that Jerusalem be not built, signifies any gentile prince who is an enemy and persecutor of the Church, or the devil, the adversary of all good men. The Jews who are accused before the king [are] churchmen; the Samaritans who accuse [are] heretics. Hence with a voice fitting to themselves they call Jerusalem a rebellious and most wicked city; for such they judge the catholic unity which they attack. But in truth it is rebellious, and builds the walls and partitions of right faith with the stones of the heavenly testimonies against the darts of the attackers; of which Isaias says: "And salvation shall possess thy walls, and praise thy gates." But it is not to be called most wicked except by those who are wholly turned away from the best choice of their own judgment. Among which it is to be noted that the people of God began to be reckoned by the name of Jews at that time when those were chiefly of the tribe of Juda who, going up from captivity, restored the walls of the city of Jerusalem and the temple, and, the enemies who held the neighbouring places being overcome, again possessed the province emptied of inhabitants.
4.14:
**“But we, remembering the salt that we have eaten in the palace,”** — the Samaritans eat salt in the palace when heretics are trained in the savour of worldly wisdom and philosophy, with the sweetness of rhetoric and the craft of dialectic
**“and because we count it a crime to see the king wronged, therefore have we sent and certified the king,”** — the devil or any prince hostile to Christians
**“WRONGS”** — Because they cannot bear it if any try to attack the kingdom of the devil; they fear that wars be raised in the Church, lest their heresies and deceits be overthrown together with the doctrine of the gentiles, under that leader who said: "I came not to send peace, but the sword." And again: "I am come to cast fire on the earth" etc.; the sword, namely, of the word of God, with which he lays low the adversaries, the fire of charity, with which, kindling the hearts of his own, he burns all the arms and shields of the contrary sect.
4.15:
**“that search may be made in the books of the histories of thy fathers, and thou shalt find written in the records, and shalt know that this city”**
• the Church, the city of the great King
• THAT THIS CITY etc. The enemies themselves again confess of the city of the Lord that, if it be built after the captivity and its walls of living stones, that is, of holy souls, be raised against the pride of the world, its citizens, that is, the elect, will no longer pay the tribute of wicked servitude to the malignant spirits by sinning; nay, the building of piety will harm the princes of darkness, because daily through the laver of regeneration many are taken from the kingdom of the devil who are begotten corrupted by original sin into his service; who pay the tribute of servitude not undue to the enemy but commanded to the Creator, and render the yearly revenues of their firstfruits and tithes, that is, the beginning and the perfection of good things, to God, from whom they had received them, by living well and giving thanks.
**“is a rebellious city, and hurtful to the kings and provinces,”** — to heretics, namely, and enemies of the truth
**“and that wars were raised”** — I came not to send peace, but the sword
**“therein from days of old: for which cause also the city was destroyed.”** — by the persecution of heretics and gentiles
4.16:
**“We certify the king that if this city be built,”** — by faith and working
**“and the walls thereof”** — of living stones
**“repaired, thou shalt have no possession on this side of the river.”**
• namely in the baptized
• BEYOND THE RIVER etc. That is, the Euphrates, within which is Syria; which signifies baptism, because it is one of the four rivers of paradise which water the whole world, as the four evangelists, inspired from one fountain of life, that is, Christ, with harmonious voice preach the laver of salvation to all nations; or because Euphrates is interpreted 'fruitful', which fits the sacrament by which the world, washed and sanctified, brings forth to God fruit of souls thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold.
4.17:
**“SENT WORD”** — The king of the Persians, which is interpreted 'tempting', seeks the possession beyond the river when the ancient enemy, stirring up the assaults of temptations, tries to break into the borders of the Church and to subjugate those who have been redeemed by the sacred font. The Samaritans help him when heretics, attacking the Church, fight for the kingdom of the devil, and say grieving that, if the city be built and the walls repaired, namely through faith and right working, he will have no possession beyond the river, that is, in the hearts of those who have been baptized. For even those who do not understand the right faith understand that light and darkness, iniquity and justice, Christ and Belial, cannot possess the same mind together.
**“The king sent word to Reum Beelteem, and Samsai the scribe, and to the rest that were in their council,”** — The sense of the letter and of the allegory is plain: that the profane one, that is, the ancient enemy, most willingly favours those who persecute the Church and forbid it to be built.
**“INHABITANTS OF SAMARIA”** — The enemies of Jerusalem dwell in Samaria, which is interpreted 'keeping', not because those who obstinately resist the vision of true peace keep the precepts of faith and truth, but because they boast that the keeping of the virtues remains with them, while they fight through heresy against the walls of peace.
4.23: **“NOW THE COPY”** — BEDE. The order of the history is plain: that the enemies of the people of God first hindered the work by pursuing [it], then tried to scatter the purpose of their right intention by wicked counsels; nor were they at all able to draw them back from the work before, propped by royal help, they resisted with public authority. Their fraudulence in accusing is to be noted, by which they complained that those who were building the house of God were building a city against the kingdom; and, when the king commanded that the city be not built, at once seizing the authority, they opposed the building of the temple, though they had reported nothing about the construction of the temple and the king had only forbidden the city to be built.

5.1: **“PROPHESIED”** — BEDE. In their books it is written more fully with what words they rebuked the sloth of those who were more negligent toward the work of the temple, or kindled them to work by the promised help of God, and with what devotion too, at their exhortation, Zorobabel, Josue and all the people girded themselves to work. For Aggeus begins thus: "In the second year of Darius the king, on the first day of the aforesaid month, the word of the Lord came by the hand of Aggeus the prophet, saying: Speak to Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, and to Jesus the son of Josedec" etc. And a little after: "And the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zorobabel the son of Salathiel, the governor of Juda, and the spirit of Jesus the son of Josedec the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people: and they went in, and did the work in the house of the Lord" etc. And Zacharias begins thus: "In the eighth month, in the second year of king Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zacharias the son of Barachias, the son of Addo the prophet" etc. From which it appears why Esdras names Zacharias the son of Addo: namely because he was the grandson of him who is understood to have been a noble prophet, whose son Zacharias, excellent among the prophets, would rightly be called. Among which it is to be noted of how great spirit these prophets were, that against the edict of so great a king, and with the Samaritans and all the nations round about hindering the building of the temple, they commanded the temple to be built. Zorobabel too and Jesus [Josue] and the people who were with them are shown to have been of no less faith, who listened to the prophets commanding rather than to the command of the king forbidding.
5.2:
**“ZOROBABEL”** — 'Born in Babylon', or 'master of Babylon', because, according to the history, he was born there, though he was of the stock of David, who was born in Bethlehem. He signifies Christ, who, to free the world from the confusion of errors, deigned to be born and to live in Babylon, that is, in the confusion of the world. Who is also rightly called 'master of Babylon', not because he teaches the things which are of Babylon, that is, of the world, but because those whom he finds pressed by the Babylonian yoke he instructs to the grace of liberty, and, instructed, leads them to the heavenly homeland; whose father is Salathiel, that is, 'my petition, God', who says, namely in the Psalm: "Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance" etc. Each one too, when, calling upon God, he seeks nothing else but him, can call him Salathiel.
**“AND JOSUE”** — BEDE. Josue or Jesus is interpreted 'saviour', Josedec 'the Lord just'. He indeed, like the son of Nun, signifies Christ. For each brought the people into the land of promise, the one from the long sojourning of the wilderness, the other from the longer servitude of the captivity. So the true Jesus, rescuing his elect from all evils, brings them into the promised joys of the kingdom above; who is the son of Josedec, that is, of 'the Lord just', of whom it is said: "The Lord who is just will cut the necks of sinners" etc.
5.3: **“AT THE SAME”** — BEDE. The text of the letter is plain: that, strengthened by the words of the prophets, the nobles of the Jews could not be hindered by the attacks of the enemies from the holy work, from which, while the prophets were still silent, they had ceased through fear of the enemies; as is now done in the Church, when those who, held back by the snares of malignant spirits or men, were at times slower to good work, suddenly rebuked by the words of the doctors or of the divine Scriptures, can be overcome by no engines of temptations nor called back from the purpose of their intention.
5.4: **“WHEREUNTO WE ANSWERED”** — He who wrote this seems to have been present, though Esdras is said to have written it, who is found not to have been in Jerusalem at that time, but to have come there long after, in the reign of Artaxerxes. Either therefore he truly was there then, and when the temple was made returned to Babylonia to bring back more of the children of Israel to Jerusalem; or he joins himself to the builders as if what is done toward his brethren, or what they themselves do, were his own; as the Apostle says: "We who are alive, who remain unto the coming of the Lord, shall not prevent them who have slept."
5.6:
**“THE COPY OF THE LETTER”** — This letter is very unlike that which Reum Beelteem and Samsai wrote to Artaxerxes. For that one is full of accusation of the people of Jerusalem, this one of praise not only of the nation but also of almighty God. That one was written with snares, this one with friendly letters; because that one [was] from the Samaritans, enemies of the Jews, this one from the governor of the region beyond the river, that is, of lower Syria and Phenicia, and from his companions, who had no domestic enmities against the Jews but only took care to carry out the will of the king from whom they had received their power.
**“The copy of the letter that Thantannai the governor of the country beyond the river, and Starbuzannai, and his counsellors the Apharsathites, who were beyond the river, sent to Darius the king.”** — The Samaritans, who, writing the first letter, kindled the mind of the king against the builders of the temple, are compared to heretics, who so stain the Church with foul pestilence that they even make it hateful to the gentiles and stir up their fury against it. But the governor of Syria, who does not urge the king to stop the work of God but asks him by consulting, signifies those who, still placed in heathenism, do not refuse to believe if they understand that this Scripture of the Godhead is true and just. Finally, hearing from the ancients of the Jews when they gave their reasons, We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, building etc., he would not hinder them, but with a simple mind asked whether Cyrus had commanded the temple to be built and whether Darius wished it. And, the will of both kings being known, he diligently helped that the work might be finished more quickly. All which things fit those who, set in the gentile life, on seeing the life of the Church are suddenly astonished, then are eager to hear and learn the reason of religion, and at length, knowing that it took its origin from the God of heaven and earth, who alone is truly God, share in his sacrifices and rejoice to help the building.
5.8:
**“Be it known to the king, that we went to the province of Judea, to the house of the great God, which they are building with unpolished stone,”** — WITH UNPOLISHED STONE, that is, new, which they found unpolished but by polishing fitted to the building. For although of the old stones, which, according to Jeremias, "were scattered at the top of every street", some stones remained, new ones were to be polished with which the work of the temple could be completed. Which we see mystically done in the Church, when it is built not only of those who come to their senses by repenting, but also of those who, lately called to the faith, are framed by the instruction of the masters as by the rule of the craftsmen and placed in the building in fitting order. Of old and new stones too, that is, those long since set and those unpolished, the temple is built, when of both peoples, namely Jew and gentile, the one Church of Christ is gathered. For the one had long since been as it were polished by the knowledge and observance of the law; the other, bound over to idolatry, had put off the deformity of a rustic and earthly mind by no diligence of spiritual architects, by no worship of piety.
**“AND TIMBER”** — BEDE. The timbers which are set for the adornment or defence of the temple designate the same life of the saints in the adornment of the Church as the stones also do; of which it is said: "Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice" etc.

6.1: **“Then king Darius gave orders, and they searched in the library of the books that were laid up in Babylon.”** — THEN DARIUS etc. BEDE. Josephus has set down the name of the place in which these letters of Cyrus were found thus: And the book was found in Egbathana, a city built in the region of Media. Again, another translation has it thus: In Egbathana, in the safest building of the region of the Medes. Hence it seems that the name Medena signifies nothing other than Media.
6.3: **“THAT THEY LAY THE FOUNDATIONS”** — BEDE. It is not for us to expound, because neither in the former building of the temple nor in the later is anything found of these measures or of work of this kind; from which it is gathered that Cyrus put this forth from his own mind, and noted the measure or order of the time as seemed fitting to him. For the temple, as Paralipomenon relates, had in its first measure, that is, within the inner walls, sixty cubits of length, twenty of breadth; and of height, as the history of Kings writes, thirty cubits up to the upper chamber, then another thirty up to the higher upper chamber, as far as the height of the porches rose, as Josephus testifies, then sixty up to the top of the roof, that is, a hundred and twenty together, as Paralipomenon teaches. But how does he say that three rows of unpolished stones are to be laid, and so of new timber, when the whole temple was clothed with cedar within? Unless perhaps it was the custom of the Persians to make temples so with varied work, that there should be only rows of stones through the walls, and a fourth of wrought timber; and he thought that this ought to be done also in the temple of the Jerusalemites. Or perhaps it is to be understood that he spoke of the court of the priests, which, made round about the temple, had had three rows of polished stones and a fourth of cedar timber, and was as high as the breast of those standing by. Or of the porch of the house of the Lord, which was before the face of the temple, of which Scripture, when the palace of Solomon was being built, makes mention thus: "And he made the greater court round with three rows of hewn stones, and one row of planed cedar: and also in the inner court of the house of the Lord, and in the porch of the house."
6.5:
**“And also let the gold and silver vessels of the temple of God, which Nabuchodonosor took out of the temple of Jerusalem, and brought to Babylon, be restored, and carried back to the temple in Jerusalem to their place, which also were placed in the temple of God.”** — the Babylonian [temple], that is, in which Nabuchodonosor had placed them
**“BE RESTORED”** — Darius confirms the letters with his authority, restraining all the adversaries of the Jews, and commands the temple to be built in its place etc.
6.6: **“NOW THEREFORE, THANTANNAI”** — Artaxerxes, who forbids the house of God and the city to be built, signifies those who oppose the construction of holy Church by stirring up persecutions, amid which the Church flourished most of all with the victory of the martyrs. But Darius [signifies] the pious devotion of those kings who, having acknowledged the piety of the Christian faith, took care not to resist it but to help it by their decrees; of whom many, forbidding the persecutions of their predecessors, wished themselves with their subject peoples to be consecrated with the sacraments of the same faith; to whom what Darius adds fits well: I have also commanded what must etc. For who could unfold how much the Church has been helped and enriched by the liberality of kings?
6.8: **“I have also commanded what must be done by those ancients of the Jews, that the house of God may be built, to wit, that of the king's chest, that is, of the tribute that is paid out of the country beyond the river, the charges be diligently given to those men, lest the work be hindered.”** — THAT OF THE CHEST etc. BEDE. The charges for the work of God are given from the king's chest when, from the household of worldly princes, some come to the faith of Christ with their favour, who were as it were in the king's chest, since they were privy to the royal secrets. But they are given to the priests and ancients of the Jews for the charges of the work of the temple when they are committed to the masters to be united to the members. Such was Cassiodorus, once a senator, suddenly a doctor of the Church; who, while in his exposition of the psalms he diligently attends to what Ambrose, what Hilary, what Augustine, what Cyril, what John, what the other saints said, proved himself taught by the ancients of the Jews, that is, of those confessing and praising God.
6.9:
**“CALVES AND LAMBS”** — BEDE. These animals, which are clean, and the wheat and salt and wine and oil, which were offered according to the law, are often put in signification of good things, either of perfect works or of spiritual gifts; which are now, at the king's command, offered in holocaust to the God of heaven, when, with the princes of the world favouring, the affairs of holy Church grow, and the peoples subject to them are gathered into the one faith of truth to be consecrated to Christ, and whatever natural good each has had from God, whatever wholesome thing he has learned from the men of the Church, he spends wholly on the divine worship.
**“ACCORDING TO THE CUSTOM”** — Because the vows of those who offer will be accepted only when they are offered according to the custom of the catholic peace; but those that are mixed with gentile superstition or heresy are not good.
6.10: **“And let them offer oblations to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king, and of his children.”** — AND PRAY etc. According to that of the Apostle: "I desire therefore, first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all men: for kings, and for all that are in high station."
6.11: **“THEREFORE I HAVE MADE A DECREE”** — He willed to punish with the most grievous penalty him who should change the decree, namely by the loss of all that he had and of his life, which, fastened also to a beam, he would lose by long torment. Mystically, our works are compared to timbers, the good to fruitful ones, the wicked to willows and to those worthy of burning; and a beam is taken from the house of him who opposes the holocausts of the Lord, and is set up, and he himself is fastened on it, when the works of those who fight against the peace of the Church are made manifest to all, how useless and perverse they are, and they themselves are shown to have gained in them not the joy of life but the snare of death. The house of such men is also confiscated, that is, proscribed by public assessment, when their bodies, with which they lived in this life, are handed over in the resurrection to be punished with perpetual torment into the power of cruel exactors, the unclean spirits.
6.12: **“AND MAY THE GOD”** — He desires his decree to be confirmed by the divine power, and he himself, as a man endowed with a temporal kingdom, does by public law all that he can for the peace of the house of God. Which is now also done in the Church, when earthly powers converted to the faith set forth public edicts for the state of the Church, and desire [so the edition: 'capiunt'] always to have this peace calm, with the Lord helping and overthrowing the enemies.
6.14:
**“AND THE ANCIENTS”** — Now too, as the peoples flock to the faith, and sometimes with those who are outside favouring, the ancients of the Jews, that is, those who are worthy of the office of master, build up the Church daily by word and example, and prosper; because even if the devil attacks, the word of God yet finds those in whom it may conquer and, the adversaries being put to flight, may raise the walls of truth.
**“and they prospered according to the prophecy of Aggeus the prophet, and of Zacharias the son of Addo: and they built and finished, by the commandment of the God of Israel, and by the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius,”** — ACCORDING TO THE PROPHECY etc. For they had foretold that, if they pressed on with building the temple, soon, by the Lord's gift, they would both finish the work itself and abound in all good things.
**“BEDE”** — Let no one think that what Aggeus says, that the foundations of the temple were laid under king Darius, is contrary to this history, in which it is written that in the second year of king Cyrus the temple was founded by the masons, while the people praised God much and rejoiced together. For then the founding of the temple itself was described, that is, of the inner house, whose measures the history of Kings and Paralipomenon specially relates. But now, with the building of the house, those buildings are said to be founded, namely the porches and treasuries which surrounded the house on every side, of which mention is made thus in Paralipomenon: "He made also the court of the priests, and a great hall, and doors in the hall, which he covered with brass." In which hall, namely, set round the temple, the people stood to pray, and the keepers and porters of the temple kept watch [so the edition: 'exultabant'] by turns day and night, as Paralipomenon teaches. These are sometimes numbered generally with the temple itself, as in the gospel, where, while he was teaching in the temple, the Pharisees and scribes brought the woman taken in adultery, whom they could in no way have brought in except into some porch of the temple. Sometimes they are separated under the name of treasuries, or of exedra, or of porches, or of courts. Whence: "You that stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God."
**“and Artaxerxes kings of the Persians.”** — who reigned after Darius, in whose time Esdras went up from Babylonia to Jerusalem
**“AND ARTAXERXES”** — It is asked how the house is said to have been built by the command of Artaxerxes, since it is at once added that it was completed and dedicated while Darius still reigned; unless perhaps it is to be believed that Artaxerxes too, sending gold and silver, commanded that whatever was less completed in the building or adornment of the temple or of the vessels should be perfected. For when Esdras was hastening there it is written that the same king with his princes or counsellors sent very much gold and silver and vessels to the temple.
6.15:
**“OF THE MONTH OF ADAR”** — BEDE. On whose third day the house was completed. It is March, which Scripture is wont to call the twelfth according to the course of the moon. Nor is it without mystery that the house of the Lord, which was begun in the seventh month with the building of the altar, was perfected in the twelfth month. For it was begun at the beginning of the seventh month, because every good thing that we do we begin with the preventing grace of the Holy Spirit and perfect with the same accompanying. And it was completed in the twelfth month for the signifying of perfection, which is contained in this number, chiefly because of the sum of the apostles, in whose faith and teaching the Church is perfected. Again, the number twelve signifies the perfection of faith and working, because whether you multiply three by four or four by three you will make twelve. And three are referred to faith because of the confession of the holy Trinity, four to good work because of the four principal virtues, prudence, fortitude, temperance and justice, of which it is said: "For she teacheth temperance, and prudence, and justice, and fortitude, which are such things as men can have nothing more profitable in life." Rightly therefore the house of the Lord, begun in the seventh month, was perfected and dedicated in the twelfth, because the mind of the elect is enlightened by the grace of the Holy Spirit that it may come to the perfection of good working with the faith of the holy Trinity, and so, rejoicing, awaits the dedication of the reward. And since this reward of the future solemnity is perfected in the time of the universal resurrection and in the vision of the Trinity, rightly the house of the Lord is recorded as completed not only in the twelfth month [but] on its third day; for because the Lord rose on the third day, our resurrection can be signified by the number three, of which it is said: "On the third day he will raise us up." And the building of the temple was begun in the first year of king Cyrus and finished in the sixth year of Darius, which are, according to the chronicle, forty-five years. For Cyrus reigned thirty years; after him Cambyses his son eight, who in this volume, as Josephus holds, is called Artaxerxes; after him the Magi, who killed him, one year; after them Darius, up to the finishing and dedication of the temple, six years; which are forty-five years. But it is asked how the Jews answered: "Six and forty years was this temple in building" etc. But if we read the history of Josephus, which adds three years after the finishing and dedication of the temple, in which the peribolus, that is, the construction of fortifications set round the temple, and certain other things which remained, were perfected, we shall see that the sum of forty-six years could rightly be reckoned in the building of the temple, in which all the more eminent things were completed.
**“BEDE”** — But the temple, although it signifies the elect soul because of the Spirit of Christ dwelling in it, and the whole Church, that is, the congregation of all the elect angels and men, also expresses the very body of Christ, born of the virgin, living in the world without sin, loosed by death and raised on the third day; to which is specially fitted that it is said to have been built in forty-six years. For the natural philosophers say that in this number of days the human body grows in the womb from the time of conception to the perfect outlines of the members. And it was fitting that the house which signified the Lord's body [should be built] in that number of years in Jerusalem, that is, [which] is called the city of the great king and the vision of that peace of which it is said: "For he is our peace, who hath made both one." As also that: "The door for the middle side was on the right hand of the house: and by winding stairs they went up to the middle chamber, and from the middle to the third", specially figured the body of Christ, of which it is said: "One of the soldiers with a spear opened his side" etc. For the door of the middle side was on the right-hand part of the house, that is, beginning from the eastern corner of the southern side and leading little by little by a hidden way through the inner parts of the same side to the higher chambers; because Christ willed the door of salvation to be opened to us in his right side, washed and sanctified by whose sacred things we may enter into the higher hall of the heavenly kingdom. For we ascend through the door of the middle side into the upper chamber when, consecrated by the water of baptism and the draught of the Lord's chalice, we pass from this earthly consecration to the life of the heavenly souls. And from the upper we pass into the third when we crown the blessedness of souls with the receiving also of immortal bodies.
6.16: **“AND [THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL] KEPT”** — Rightly do the children of the transmigration rejoice, who escaped the captivity and deserved to build the house of God, and as devout servants of God offer victims at the dedication of his house, and as lovers of the brotherhood [offer] for the sin of all Israel, wherever they were, asking God to be propitious to them and either to keep them among the enemies or to call them back to the homeland. And rightly is the temple dedicated with joy by the priests and Levites and the rest of the children of the transmigration, because when sinners are corrected there is joy in heaven before the angels of God, and [to] the masters who laboured for their salvation, and [to] all who [unclear in the edition: "de re transmigrarunt"]. The priests therefore and Levites and all the people rejoice at the dedication of the restored house, because all the orders of the Church rejoice over sinners reconciled through penance.
6.17:
**“AND THEY OFFERED”** — They offer victims at the dedication when they give thanks to God for the conversion of those who strayed, when many, seeing their devotion, gird themselves to greater works of the virtues, lest they be slower in working than those than whom they were more innocent by sinning less. Many too who went before in the faith emulate the more fervent zeal of the novices.
**“HE-GOATS”** — He-goats are offered in this life for sin when the elect beseech God that they may be freed from sins; they are offered in the future when those who have been freed give thanks. And therefore they will sing the mercies of the Lord for ever, because they will always remember that they were wretched and were freed by his gift.
**“FOR SIN”** — They offer also for the sin of all Israel, because it behoves us so to favour the good who are with us, so to make their good things ours by imitating them, that we pray the Lord also for the state of the whole Church. Hence in the Lord's prayer no one asks anything specially for himself, but for all who have the same Father in heaven. Again, when the temple is built the dedication follows, when, the sum of the elect being completed at the end of the world, it will come to the grace of the heavenly rewards, in which victims are offered, of which the same house, that is, the Church, rebuilt through the glory of immortality after the captivity of mortal hardship, says: "Thou hast broken my bonds, O Lord: I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise."
