And because they are offered not only for the gifts of the virtues but also for the worldly filth of vices, well, after the calves, rams and lambs, are he-goats offered for the sin of all Israel; for the grace by which he confers the benefits of the virtues also takes away crimes. Nor has Pelagius a place in the house of God, who persuaded himself and his followers that by freedom of will they could either be freed from evils or be confirmed in good things.
6.18:
**“AND THEY SET”** — Order required that, the house of God being built, priests and Levites should at once be ordained to minister in it. Which is to be observed by those who build monasteries magnificently, that they establish in them doctors who may exhort the people to the works of God, not serve their own pleasures there.
**“THE PRIESTS”** — BEDE. When he says that the priests were set in their orders and the Levites in their courses, he signifies the courses of the weeks, in which the whole company of each grade was distributed into twenty-four parts, so that each order in the turn of its week ministered in the temple for eight days, namely from sabbath to sabbath, and after twenty-four weeks, free from the offices of the temple, took care of its own affairs, as Paralipomenon relates. For they had already made the porches of the temple round about the inner sanctuary, at whose doors the Levites kept watch by turns, as is said there. But what he says, As it is written in the book of Moses, belongs not to the courses of the Levites but to the works of God. For Moses wrote what the priests, what the Levites should do in the house of God; but the courses of the Levites and the orders of the priests by twenty-four lots were described not by Moses but by king David with the prophets, priests and Levites of his time. And now too, the Church being built and dedicated through the regeneration of peoples new in the faith, it is fitting that priests and Levites be set in their orders and in their courses, who are over the works of God, that the peoples may not only rest on the sacraments of the faith, but may be girded by the examples and instruction of the just who went before to do the things that are God's; and this not according to the reach of human wit, but as it is written in the book of Moses; with which agrees that of the gospel: "Going therefore, teach ye all nations; baptizing them etc., teaching them to observe all the commandments of God." For we ought to teach our hearers not our own things but the commandments of the law and the gospel, if we take care to come together with them to the rewards of the Lord.
6.19:
**“AND [THE CHILDREN OF THE CAPTIVITY] KEPT THE PHASE”** — Therefore, the house of the Lord being built and dedicated, the celebration of the Pasch is specially recorded, though no one doubted that men so religious celebrated the Pasch at its time, that it might be mystically hinted that this is the summit of perfection, when, all the allurements of the world being passed by, we always meditate with the whole intention of the mind on the entrance into the other life. For Pasch is interpreted 'passing', because in it the children of Israel, through the immolation of the lamb, passed from Egyptian bondage to liberty; or the lamb itself, that is, Christ, immolated for us, passed out of this world to the Father; which we imitate when we pass from the lowest pleasures to seeking heavenly things, and truly perfect when, loosed from the prison of the flesh, we enter the heavenly kingdom.
**“BEDE”** — Why is the Pasch related after the house was built, when it was said before that from the first day of their coming to Jerusalem they offered lawful victims and holocausts on all the solemnities of the Lord, unless that it might be hinted that they completed the building of the temple with the same devotion of mind with which they began? For there it was said before that the people was gathered as one man, and Josue and his brethren rose up and built the altar to sacrifice holocausts on it. And now, the temple being dedicated as the forty-sixth year was at hand, the same piety of religion is recorded to have been in the minds of all, when it is said that the priests and Levites had been purified, all as one clean for sacrificing the Pasch. For what greater perfection can there be in this life than the unity of a clean multitude? For there were many thousands of priests, many of Levites, but all purified and clean to celebrate the Pasch "with one heart and one soul". Nor was the unity in the people unequal, when it is said: to sacrifice the Pasch for all the children of the transmigration and for their brethren the priests and for themselves; and at once it is added: And the children of Israel did eat etc. For all therefore the Pasch was sacrificed, all did eat, not only those who had returned from the captivity but also all who, settled anywhere before, separated themselves to them at that time. Which can be understood also of the proselytes, who, gentiles by nature, were converted to their rite by circumcision and purified with victims, that they might be worthy of participation in the saving sacrament. Nowhere else, unless I am mistaken, since they went out of Egypt, are they found to have been of such devotion together with the priests and Levites, namely their masters. But this devotion was made [so the edition: 'sacra'] by divine chastisement, because, handed over to enemies for their sins, but freed by penance and confession, they were to serve God better. We see also those who profaned the temple of their body by sinning, and through this were taken captive by the devil, return through penance, by which they might repair a dwelling for the Lord in themselves. For it is to be noted that Solomon finished the former temple in the greatest peace of the kingdom, in a short time and with no one opposing; but the children of the transmigration restored it, when destroyed for their sins, with great compunction of heart, persisting in long labour and often hindered by enemies, at length divinely helped. For it is easy for any convert to renounce the devil, to confess the one and true God, and to receive the sacraments of Christ, and, initiated by these in the remission of all sins, to be made his temple, and to keep the innocence of life received with his grace accompanying. But it is of much labour, if anyone despises by sinning the sacraments of faith received, to recover his former dignity; because he cannot be baptized again, but the sin must be washed away by the long labour of penance; to whose washing the very habit of vices, like the hostile crowd of the Samaritans, resists, the harder to overcome the longer it has possessed the land of the heart empty of virtue.
6.21:
**“And the children of Israel did eat”** — "Not with the old leaven" etc.
**“who were returned from the captivity, and all that had separated themselves from the filthiness”** — who, namely, serve defilements
**“of the nations of the earth”** — there are also nations of heaven, who, namely, separated from these, serve the Lord in unity and chastity and celebrate his solemnities with a sincere heart
6.22:
**“And they kept the feast of unleavened bread”** — "With the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth"
**“AND THEY KEPT THE FEAST”** — BEDE. In this place the celebration of the Pasch can be referred to the resurrection, so that the building of the temple signifies the present state of the Church, the dedication the future life, which is passed in the joy of souls when they have gone out of the body; the immolation of the Pasch the glory of the resurrection, when the spotless elect are refreshed with the flesh of the lamb, not believing in the sacrament but in the thing itself and in truth. Hence here all are said to have been present at the Pasch as one, because then truly [shall be seen] "the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sins of the world". Whence John: "The blood of Jesus the Son of God cleanseth us from all sin." Then will there be true unity, when "God shall be all in all", and the solemnity of unleavened bread in joy, when, no leaven of malice and wickedness remaining, all will cleave to the divine vision in truth and sincerity of heart, not for the seven days of the passing world but for the one day of everlasting life in the courts of the Lord, which is better above [thousands]. [unclear in the edition: "ratione tanti operis ponitur numerus, quam ille cui septiformem gratiam spiritus qua operantes adiuvamur, et requiem animarum aut resurrectionem corporum quam bene operantes speramus denuntiat"]
**“SEVEN DAYS”** — Because through all the time of the world life is to be led in sincerity and truth, nay in the victims and holocausts of all good things; because Christ at the paschal time tasted death in passing, but conquered it by the eternal power of the resurrection.
**“with joy, for the Lord had made them joyful,”** — WITH JOY etc. For this is the greatest joy of the just now and in the future: that the work of justice, or of the Church, has been perfected, the gentiles too being converted who once resisted, and [turned] to helping its state, that is, to confirming the peace of the Christian religion throughout the world.

7.1:
**“AFTER THESE THINGS”** — BEDE. Up to this point are described, under Zorobabel and Josue, the return of the people from Babylon to Jerusalem, the bringing back of the vessels, the dedication of the temple, the celebration of the solemnities, and the dedication of the canticles of the Lord, which could not be sung in a strange land; all which contain the pattern of human salvation in Christ, when those who had come into the world with original sin are saved, purified by the sacraments of faith, or those who corrupt the faith by sinning come to their senses by repenting, and both, through the same Saviour, the true King and true Priest, celebrating the Pasch, pass from the world to the Father, from death to life. But because, when the temple was burnt and the city overthrown, the Scriptures too were burnt up, and it was necessary by the Lord's mercy that these be repaired, so that those who had restored the overthrown buildings might have that by which, admonished, they themselves might learn to be restored within, there well follows: After these things etc.
**“OF ARTAXERXES THE KING”** — BEDE. This Artaxerxes, under whom Esdras went up from Babylonia to Jerusalem, Josephus thinks to be Xerxes the son of Darius, who reigned after him; but the books of chronicles [make him] the successor of that same Xerxes. For Darius, under whom the temple was built, reigned thirty-six years; after him Xerxes twenty years; after him Archabanus seven months, which the chroniclers set down as a year; after him Artaxerxes forty years.
**“Esdras the son of Saraias, the son of Azarias,”** — the generation being reckoned up to Aaron, he was reckoned a lawful priest
7.6: **“This Esdras went up from Babylon, and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the Lord God had given to Israel: and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of the Lord his God upon him.”** — AND HE WAS A READY SCRIBE. BEDE. Esdras is called a ready scribe in the law of Moses because Esdras restored the law of Moses, which had been consumed; and also, as is the common report of our elders, he wrote the whole series of sacred Scripture which the fire had consumed, as seemed sufficient to readers, and, as they relate, added some things which he thought fitting; of which is that: "And there arose no more a prophet in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face" etc. Which words no one could have said except one who lived long after Moses. And in the book of Samuel: "In time past in Israel, when a man went to consult God, he spoke thus: Come, let us go to the seer. For he that is now called a prophet, in time past was called a seer." And some whole volumes which were once had among the people of Israel, as is that in the book of Numbers: "Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord", and in Josue: "Is not this written in the book of the just?" In the volume of Kings and Paralipomenon too are mentioned historical books of the prophets Ahias the Silonite, and Semeias, Addo, and Nathan; of Isaias too, and of Jehu the son of Hanani, who is said to have written the book of the Kings of Israel; and many others, of which no traces can be found today. The Hebrews also relate for certain that he devised lighter letters under the names of those which they had had before, with which he might most quickly restore so great an abundance of books which had been consumed. Therefore he is named not only scribe but also ready. But the former letters remained with the Samaritans, with which they were wont to write those five books of Moses, which alone of holy Scripture they had received.
7.7:
**“And there went up some of the children of Israel, and of the children of the priests, and of the children of the Levites, and of the singing men, and of the porters, and of the Nathinites to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.”** — prolepsis. For in what follows it is written more fully how they came and gathered a host
**“AND THERE WENT UP”** — BEDE. It is to be noted that at the head of this book it is written that, by the permission of Cyrus, Zorobabel and Josue went up from Babylon, and of the children of Juda and Benjamin with the priests and Levites all whose spirit God had raised up; of whom it was added that they were of the captivity which Nabuchodonosor carried away into Babylon. But here, under Esdras as leader, there is no mention of Juda and Benjamin or of Nabuchodonosor, but only of the children of Israel and of the priests and Levites who went up with him. Hence it seems that those were of Juda and Benjamin whom Nabuchodonosor took captive; but these of the ten tribes, which after the division were specially called Israel, whom the kings of the Assyrians had taken captive long before and had made to dwell beyond the mountains of the Medes. Then therefore the two tribes for the greatest part returned and restored the temple with heavy labour. But the ten tribes, which had less care for religion, because, the empire of the Chaldeans being destroyed, they lived freely under the kings of the Persians, when they learned that the temple was built and the envy of the Samaritans repressed, at length some of them returned; more remained there, whose progeny is said to be kept to this day in the same parts and to serve the nation of the Persians. And as Zorobabel and Jesus [Josue] signify Christ, who by his grace releases the captivity of the human race and builds his house in us by sanctifying and possessing it, so Esdras, the priest and ready scribe, figures the same [Christ], who came not to destroy the law but to fulfil it; who could therefore be called the scribe of the law or the ready scribe in the law of Moses, because he himself gave the law to Moses through the angel, he himself taught the prophets the truth, he himself kindles the minds of the elect to understand and do the will of the Father. Whence: "For this is the testament which I will make to the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord: I will give my laws into their mind" etc.; and: "My tongue is the pen of a scrivener" etc. For the tongue of the prophet was the pen of a ready scribe, because what the Lord taught him within without delay of time, this he himself declared outwardly in time through the office of the tongue. Esdras also is interpreted 'helper', because Christ alone frees his people from tribulations and leads them from the confusion of vices to the peace of the virtues by advancing steps of merits. Whence: "My help is from the Lord" etc. Moreover, as Esdras brought back no small part of the people from captivity to Jerusalem, and money and holy vessels for the glory of the temple, and purged the people of foreign wives by his pontifical authority, so Christ, appearing in the flesh, entered the confusion of the world free from the confusion of vices, that, returning, he might lead us with him, freed from all confusion, into the tranquillity of the peace above; whose pledge of peace we receive in the present, according to that: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you"; that is, I leave temporal [peace] to those on pilgrimage, I give perpetual [peace] to those who come to the heavenly homeland.
7.9:
**“FOR UPON THE FIRST [DAY] OF THE MONTH”** — BEDE. On the first day of the month he began to go up from Babylon, and in the fifth, with the children of the transmigration, and on the first day of the month, he came to Jerusalem. For the beginning of the month, in which the moon is believed to borrow new light from the sun, signifies a new beginning of the heavenly gift; and well did Esdras go up from Babylon on the first day of the first month with those whom he was saving from captivity, because the beginning of the holy life, in which we renounce Satan and his kingdom, is brought about in us by the illumination of the divine goodness. On the first day of the fifth month too he came to Jerusalem, because this too comes about not by the freedom of our will but by the inspiration of the light above, that, having heard the gospel, we are incorporated in the members of the Church. And a beautiful and wholesome custom has grown up in the Church by the teaching of the fathers, that to those who are catechized the sacrament of the four gospels is explained and recited at the beginning. Again, he came on the first day of the fifth month to Jerusalem with those who had been freed from the enemies, because when, the precepts of the four gospels having been fulfilled, we enter the heavenly kingdom, we celebrate as it were a new beginning of the month, because we now behold the joys of new light in the sun of justice; as it were, after the four months of bright action which we have passed on the way, we spend the fifth month of everlasting reward in the light of the heavenly homeland.
**“BEDE”** — In the first month Esdras began to go up from Babylon, and in the fifth he came with the children of the transmigration to Jerusalem. For four months complete the journey from Babylonia to Jerusalem, because through the four books of the gospel we learn the faith and the sacraments of truth, by which, rescued from the captivity of the devil with the Lord as leader, we ascend to the liberty of the sons of God; and in the same books are contained the precepts of works, by which as by daily steps we may come to the promises above.
**“ACCORDING TO THE HAND OF GOD”** — Strengthened, that is, by the divine grace and protection by which he might prosperously finish what he had begun. So also Christ: because God "was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself", the hand of God too was upon his humanity, by which, exalted in the passion, he also ascended to the walls of the city above and opened the way to his faithful.
7.10:
**“Esdras”** — helper
**“had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord,”**
• which the flame had consumed
• BUT ESDRAS etc. Great is the virtue of a man to prepare his heart for the service of the divine will, and to be able to say: "My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready" etc.
**“BEDE”** — Christ too prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord, because he divinely provided to take to himself such a manhood as should be not only without sin but also "full of grace and truth", which, with no law of sin resisting it, might keep the law of God without any contradiction of mind or flesh. Whence: "In the head of the book it is written of me" etc. Again, the Lord sought the law of God, because, casting away the traditions of the Pharisees, he taught to understand holy Scripture mystically, and showed that the decrees of the gospel which he brought were more perfect and acceptable to God than those which he had sent before through Moses. Whence: "You have heard that it hath been said to them of old: Thou shalt love thy neighbour [so the edition: 'amicum'], and hate thy enemy. But I say to you, Love your enemies" etc.
**“and to do and to teach in Israel the commandments and judgment.”** — "Jesus began to do and to teach"
7.11:
**“And this is the copy of the letter of the edict, which king Artaxerxes gave to Esdras the priest, the scribe instructed in the words”** — by teaching
**“and commandments”** — by example
7.12:
**“Artaxerxes,”** — orator
**“king of kings, to Esdras the priest, the most learned scribe of the law of the God of heaven, greeting.”** — to distinguish him, namely, from those whom he knew to have been set up from dead men, or indeed from nothing
**“ARTAXERXES THE KING”** — Artaxerxes, who with devout mind venerated the temple and the priests of the Lord and served him, signifies Christian princes, as Darius also does. Nor is it wonderful if the successors of Cyrus, who had the temple and the city built, who loved and helped his servants and the law, figure Christian kings, since the Lord himself said through the prophet that Cyrus signified his Son, and honoured him with his name, saying: "Thus saith the Lord to my anointed Cyrus."
7.13:
**“IT IS DECREED BY ME”** — Because the fame of the divine power had reached the king, through which he had renewed the law burnt by the Chaldeans in the same proper words as before, though in another character of letters.
**“THAT ALL”** — He grants leave to go to all, he compels no one to go. Christian princes, compelling no one, lest the will of faith be uncertain, permit all whom it pleases to worship Christ in their kingdom.
7.14:
**“For thou art sent from before the king, and his seven counsellors,”** — AND HIS SEVEN COUNSELLORS. In the book of Esther we read that it was the custom of the kings of the Persians to use the counsel of seven in all things to be done or decided. The faithful use seven counsellors when in all that they do they follow the precepts of divine Scripture, of which it is said: "The words of the Lord are pure words: as silver tried by the fire, purged from the earth, refined seven times", that is, perfected by the holy illumination of the sevenfold Spirit.
**“THOU ART SENT”** — Esdras is sent from before the king and his seven counsellors to visit Judea and Jerusalem, when the princes of the world, converted to the faith and strengthened by the persuasions of the Scriptures, desire Christ to come to save the Church and gather it from the gentiles with daily help, which the name Esdras signifies, saying: "Turn again, O God of hosts, look down from heaven, and see, and visit this vineyard" etc.
**“which is in thy hand,”**
• not only on the tongue, because "Jesus began to do and to teach"
• Christ had the law in his hand, because he once established it through Moses as he willed, and now, changing the same through himself, carried it over to more perfect things.
**“WHICH IS IN [THY] HAND”** — It is wonderful that a phrase is found in the letter of Artaxerxes which the prophets are wont to use, when he says that the law of God is in the hand of his servant. For it is written: "The word of the Lord came by the hand of Aggeus the prophet", and: "The Lord hath done that which he spoke by the hand of his servant Elias", and: "The Lord testified to Israel and to Juda by the hand of all the prophets"; because, namely, the prophets preached the things of God no less by working than by speaking.
7.15:
**“AND TO CARRY”** — The faith and wisdom of the king and his counsellors are to be noted, who understood that their gifts were rather to be offered through him who had the law of God in his hand, that is, fulfilled it in work.
**“WHOSE [TABERNACLE] IS IN JERUSALEM”** — BEDE. Faithfully and learnedly he says that he has a tabernacle in Jerusalem whom he had called above the God of heaven. For we use a tabernacle on a journey, and the God of heaven has a tabernacle in Jerusalem because he who has an eternal seat in the heavens himself deigns to stay for a time with the saints on pilgrimage in this Church; whence: "Behold the tabernacle of God with men." And because Esdras bore the type not only of the preachers, of whom he was one, but also of Christ, to whose members he belonged, we offer gifts as it were through him when we need his aid in all things, that the good things we do may be acceptable to God the Father. "For no man", he says, "cometh to the Father, but by me." And of him Paul says: "He is the propitiation for our sins."
7.16:
**“AND ALL THE SILVER AND GOLD”** — With this money the faithful desire their good works to shine in their Church, that through this they may have a part [so the edition: 'patrem'] with the saints, and others may profit by their examples. For as it were with our silver and gold sacrifices, libations and victims are bought to offer to the Lord, when our neighbours, seeing the brightness of our works, are converted to the office of piety, by which they too are consecrated to the Lord by living well. But there are certain most brilliant virtues of the saints which cannot be shown to all as examples of work, but only recited to glorify the grace of God; as is that Daniel and Jeremias prophesied as boys, that John [did so] not yet born, that Cornelius with his house received the Holy Spirit not yet baptized, and innumerable miracles, like silver in the house of the Lord. Nor can the offerings which are placed upon the altar be bought only from this silver or gold; because when we hear such things we ought indeed to wonder at them as divine, but we cannot imitate them as possible.
**“that thou shalt find in all the province of Babylon, and that the people is willing to offer, and of the priests that shall offer of their own accord to the house of their God, which is in Jerusalem,”** — note that some priests remained in Babylonia with the rest of the people
7.17:
**“take freely, and diligently”** — for this reason the money was given
**“buy with this money calves, rams, lambs, with the sacrifices and libations of them,”** — which, namely, were offered of the fruits of the earth, as bread and fine flour and ears of corn
7.19:
**“The vessels”** — the hearts of the elect
**“THE VESSELS ALSO”** — The true Esdras delivered the vessels of mercy, which are delivered to him by men, in the sight of the Father into the Jerusalem above. Of which it is said: "How can any one enter into the house of the strong, and rifle his goods, unless he first bind the strong?" For the king of Babylon, that is, the devil, was strong, but, conquered and bound by the Lord, he lost the vessels which he possessed unjustly, that is, the hearts of the elect, nor could he oppose him who took them away and brought them back to the city above, whose own they were.
7.21: **“AND I”** — Christian princes command their subjects to give without delay whatever Christ our high priest has asked, holding back nothing at all: let them give gold in the confession of true faith, wheat in the showing of good working, wine in the fervour of love, oil in the cheerfulness of mercy; and all these are commanded to be given under the number of a hundred to the great priest and scribe of the law of the God of heaven, that is, to Christ, who, bringing us heavenly commandments from the Father, has promised heavenly rewards in the Father's house to the obedient. For the hundred, which in counting on the fingers passes from the left hand to the right, designates the joys which are at the right hand of the Judge [so the edition: 'indicis'], that is, eternal life. And the talent is handed down as of threefold measure: the least of fifty pounds, the middle of seventy pounds, the greatest of a hundred and twenty pounds; the core thirty measures; the bate, which is also the ephi, the tenth part of the core, that is, three measures.
7.22: **“AND SALT”** — BEDE. Salt signifies wisdom, and hence in common speech the dull are called saltless. But it matters of what kind the salt is; for the Lord too commanded through the law that salt be offered with every sacrifice, and in the gospel says: "Have salt in you, and have peace among you." Yet not in vain is David read to have struck the Edomites in the Valley of saltpits; because, namely, we are commanded to offer in all the sacrifices of our works the salt of heavenly wisdom, with which catechumens are initiated; but David strikes the saltpit of the valleys with its inhabitants because Christ destroys weak and worldly wisdom with its followers. Hence it is well commanded that salt be given without measure diligently in the house of the God of heaven, because it is necessary that whatever wisdom anyone has, he should show it wholly in the service of God. But it is to be recalled that the Samaritans, writing to the other Artaxerxes, said above that, mindful of the salt which they had eaten in the palace, they could not bear the temple and city of God to be built against his advantage. But here Artaxerxes commands all the keepers of the public chest to give, among other things, salt as much as is needed in the house of God. For there it is known that heretics are animated to attack the Church by the fraudulent taste of human wisdom; but here, that the wise, converted to the faith, help the Church through the discipline of worldly wisdom, while through it they overcome the adversaries.
7.24: **“TO YOU ALSO”** — By this privilege it is shown that the rest of the common people of the children of Israel, on reaching the homeland, paid the king's tribute; which the king is known to have done with discerning foresight, that those who were occupied with the divine service should be free from his own service, and that no one should exact tribute from those who possessed nothing of their own in the land but lived on the tithes of the people. By all these things it is proved that he not only loved but also learned very well what the worship of the divine service required.
7.25:
**“And thou Esdras, according to the wisdom of thy God,”**
• Artaxerxes plainly expresses what devotion kings would have in Christian times, or what they would do toward the faith of truth in all things
• AND THOU etc. BEDE. The king repeats what he had said above, and confirms with repeated speech the truth which he knew. For above he said that [the law] was in the hand of Esdras, because the law of God is wisdom. Whence: "The mouth of the just shall meditate wisdom: and his tongue shall speak judgment. The law of his God is in his heart." And the just man has the law of God and wisdom in his hand when in all that he does and says he shows himself mindful of the divine will. Mystically, our Lord has wisdom in his hand, "for he is the power of God and the wisdom of God". He appoints judges, that is, the rulers of the churches, who judge all things according to his will and preach the faith to the unlearned throughout the world; and everyone who despises the decrees of his law will be punished either with present or with future punishment according to the measure of his sin. In these things Artaxerxes expressed what devotion kings would have in the future Christian times, and what they would do toward the faith of truth.
• We can refer the person of Esdras also to any doctor of the Church, to whom kings and princes have often sent letters for the state of the faithful.
7.26: **“And whosoever will not do the law of thy God, and the law of the king diligently, judgment shall be executed upon him, either unto death, or unto banishment, or to the confiscation of goods, or at least to prison. And Esdras the scribe said:”** — Esdras, having received the letter, broke forth into the praise of God
7.27: **“Blessed be the Lord the God of our fathers, who hath put this in the king's heart, to glorify the house of the Lord, which is in Jerusalem,”** — it is not to be doubted that the king's words are holy and mystical, which the prophet confirms were divinely inspired in him, [and] by which he shows also that the house of God was glorified
7.28:
**“and hath inclined his mercy toward me before the king and his counsellors, and all the mighty princes of the king: and I being strengthened by the hand of the Lord”** — namely by the power by which he works all things
**“AND I BEING STRENGTHENED”** — So each one who is made fit by his teaching to gather others must first [so the edition: 'debrius'] be strengthened in mind by the grace of God against all things that hinder the work of the saints.

8.1: **“THESE ARE”** — He carefully enumerates the chiefs who went up with him from Babylon and unfolds their genealogy; he adds also their number, which came to one thousand four hundred and forty; hinting that the names of those who go up from the confusion of the world are written in the book of life, but that the doctors, that is, the chiefs of the families of the people of God, receive as much increase of everlasting reward as they gain souls for the Lord. Whence to the servant who says: "Thy pound hath gained ten pounds", it is answered: "Have thou power over ten cities"; that is, from the life of those whom thou hast taught thou shalt be more glorious in the kingdom of God.
8.15:
**“AND I GATHERED”** — BEDE. I do not remember having read the name of this place elsewhere. But since it is written in what follows: And I proclaimed there a fast by the river Hana on the tenth day of the first month, it seems that Hana is a river and that another river runs down into it, at whose meeting Esdras gathered the host. But Josephus puts the Euphrates; hence it seems that Hana is some stream of the Euphrates.
**“And I gathered them together to the river that runneth down to Hana, and we stayed there three days: and I sought among the people, and among the priests, for the children of Levi, and found none there.”** — Fittingly, before he began so long a journey, he provided himself with a supply of ministers of the house of God, through whom, coming to Jerusalem, he might accomplish what was necessary for the uses of the temple.
8.17: **“AND I SENT”** — BEDE. The Caspian Sea, according to Orosius, rises from the ocean under the northern quarter, along both shores of which near the ocean lie deserted and untilled places. From there it stretches toward the south through long narrows, until, widened over great spaces, it ends at the roots of the mountain. It has from the east to the ocean very many nations of the Hyrcanians and Scythians, wandering widely [so the edition: 'observantes'] because of the barrenness [so the edition: 'infusionem infecundam'] of the lands. On the west it has many nations, but in general the region, very large, of farther Albania under the Caspian sea and mountain is called [the region] of the Amazons. Where it is to be noted that, while the historians write Caspium, Esdras names it Casphia. For the Hebrews, not having the letter p, use ph instead of it in Greek or barbarian names, as Phetrus, Philatus. The children of Israel are therefore shown to have come into Casphia through the captivity of the Assyrians or Chaldeans, when Esdras sends there that ministers of the house of the Lord might be brought, namely Levites and Nathinites, whom Josephus names sacred servants. And it is to be noted that they lived in very free peace, though among foreigners, who were able at once to send so great a force. For their catalogue shows that there were two hundred and fifty-eight chosen men in that expedition; with whom added Esdras is found to have had in his host a sum of nearly one thousand seven hundred men.
8.21:
**“And I proclaimed there a fast by the river Hana,”** — otherwise: Havva
**“AND I PROCLAIMED”** — BEDE. An example of fasting and praying is given us when we wish to begin anything of great virtue; and because faithful hope in the Lord is never deceived, nor can it be that what we justly seek from a pious helper by continence and prayer with faith we do not obtain. But it is to be noted that the fast is put first and the prayer follows. For first he says: And I proclaimed there a fast etc. Then he added: And that we might ask of him a right way. And in the conclusion of the sentence: And we fasted, and besought our God etc. For it behoves whoever comes to beseech the mercy of the Lord first to show himself worthy to be heard by living more continently, and so to pray and not doubt that what he asks will turn out prosperously.
8.25:
**“AND I WEIGHED”** — BEDE. By the silver and gold vessels which are sent from Babylon to Jerusalem are signified the souls which are converted from the confusion of the world to the Lord. Hence well does Esdras the keeper commend the vessels to the priests, to carry them to Jerusalem; because whoever desire to attain to the fellowship of the Church are washed in baptism by the priests and consecrated to the Lord; and through them are reconciled by repenting those who had departed from the Church by sinning and, by persevering in sins, had fallen into the service of the devil, as into the captivity of the Babylonian king. And well are there twelve priests to whom this care is committed, because of the twelve apostles, through whose teaching the Church was first founded and through whose successors it is to be built up to the end.
**“BEDE”** — There is a difference between these vessels which Esdras offers with the priests at Jerusalem and those which Zorobabel and Jesus [Josue] are related to have offered; because those were carried from the temple of the Lord into Babylon and afterwards brought back to Jerusalem, but these were made in Babylonia and sent to Jerusalem by way of devotion by the king or the princes of the Persians, or even by the people of Israel who dwelt in those parts. Those vessels therefore signify those who, after receiving the knowledge and the sacraments of the faith, after beginning the works of the virtues, are deceived by the devil and snatched into his confusion, but are called back to salvation by the grace of Christ; but these, those who, born with the sin of the first transgression, expiated through the laver of regeneration by the ministry of the priests, are joined to the children of the Church.
8.28: **“And I said to them: You are the holy ones of the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and gold, that is freely offered to the Lord the God of your fathers.”** — YOU ARE THE HOLY ONES OF THE LORD. The doctors of the Church must never forget holiness, because they have been consecrated by the Lord through the Holy Spirit unto the day of redemption, to the receiving of which they should also train their hearers; that those who have already been offered to the Lord through the rudiments of the faith may be further confirmed by the examples and admonitions of those who have gone before in the faith, and be made worthy of entrance into the city above.
8.29:
**“WATCH YE”** — The priests must watch lest any of the souls entrusted to them, that is, the vessels of the Lord, perish; but [let them] be brought in their full number to the buildings of holy virtue.
**“TILL YOU WEIGH”** — That is, that you present those whom the providence above has committed to you, by instructing and teaching them, such as may be found irreproachable and fit for the treasury of the heavenly hall, that is, for the seats of inner peace and light; and this not by the judgment of any who can be deceived, but of the apostles and of those who are to judge with the Lord. For these are rightly understood [to be] the chiefs of the priests and Levites and the heads of the families of Israel, that is, of men or souls seeing God; of whom it is said: "Thou shalt make them princes over all the earth"; and elsewhere: "Her husband is honourable in the gates" etc.
8.31: **“WE SET FORWARD”** — BEDE. All things are full of mysteries. For above we read that on the first day of the month they began to go up from Babylon; now it is said that on the tenth [so the edition] day of the same month they set forward from the river Hana. On the first day of the month, therefore, they went out of the gates of Babylonia, but waited by the aforesaid river until the twelfth day, until the Levites and Nathinites came from Casphia, and they commended themselves to the Lord by fasting and praying the longer because of the dangers of the long journey. And we too, when we teach new peoples of the Church to renounce the devil and to believe in and confess the true God, go out from Babylon as it were at the beginning of the first month with money to be consecrated to the Lord, because we hand on the beginning of a new conversion to those whom, rescued from the devil, we lead to the heavenly kingdom. Hence the same month is called [the month] of new things or of new fruits. For in it, for the same signification of new life, the fathers were led out of Egypt. And when we hand on to the hearers of the new life the creed of faith, which was ordained by the twelve apostles and comprised in as many sentences, we stay as it were twelve days in the first station, and so undertake the journey begun to the land of promise; because after the knowledge of faith has been received we show them that the way of the virtues, by which one comes to life, must be entered on. In which days Esdras with the children of the transmigration was given to fasts and prayers and to the gathering of the Levites and Nathinites; because when we gain new peoples of the faith we must most of all strive after the virtues, by which we may commend ourselves more familiarly to the Lord and offer those whom we instruct an example of good work; we call also a religious band of brethren to our help, aided by which we may more effectively carry over the souls of the faithful to the society of the elect and the citadel of the more perfect life, as holy vessels to the temple of the Lord.
8.32: **“AND WE ABODE”** — Three days are spent in Jerusalem, which are three virtues, faith, hope and charity; these the doctors must first show in themselves, and so offer those whom they have taught and trained in the same virtues to the fathers who went before in Christ to be tested. For when the Church finds those whom we catechize upright in faith and action, it is as if, weighing what we offer in the temple by the hand of the priests, it found it of pure metal and perfect weight; which is done daily in this Church through the elect in examining the life of believers, and is more perfectly fulfilled in the Jerusalem above in those who deserve to enter. For in this life the doctors, as it were staying three days in Jerusalem, on the fourth day offer to the priests to be weighed the silver and gold which they had offered, when they show themselves strong in faith, lofty in hope, fervent in devotion, and show that their hearers shine through the confession of right faith as tried silver, gleam through purity of sense [so the edition: 'immolati'] as the finest gold, and stand out as consecrated vessels through the receiving of spiritual gifts. In the homeland above too, when they receive the grace of reward for faith, hope and charity, and afterwards also for those whom they have taught, it is as if after the joy of the three days' stay in Jerusalem they were honoured the more for the gifts and precious vessels which they offered.
8.34: **“AND IT WAS WRITTEN DOWN”** — BEDE. This is done when the doctors carefully examine the life of their subjects, namely how far each has advanced in faith or working, that they may order them according to the measure of their capacity in competent grades in the house of the Lord. But if the one set over them is sluggish through idleness, and either does not know the life of his subjects or pretends not to know it, the inner Judge, who keeps the number of believers and the weight of each in the balance of his examination, "will render to every man according to his works". It can also be said that, when the prelates come to the Jerusalem above, [all] is written down, when every work of good action of those whom they had instructed is at that time [written] in the book of life and given worthy recompense in heaven.
8.35:
**“MOREOVER THEY THAT WERE COME”** — BEDE. Great devotion and religion is shown when, coming to the temple, first of all they offer holocausts, not only for themselves but also for all Israel, that is, for those who had already returned home and for those who were still in exile. Mystically, those truly and perfectly escaped by repenting the captivity of the devil, in which they were held by sinning, who subject themselves with fixed intention to the divine service, who, drawn wholly away from lowest things, kindle themselves with the flame of heavenly desire. For this is to offer holocausts, that is, wholly burnt sacrifices, to the Lord: to think or do nothing in all things but his will.
**“OFFERED”** — Not only for himself. It is the sign of a perfect mind when one sacrifices for all Israel, that is, for the general safety of the faithful, beseeching the pity above as one mindful of unity and brotherhood.
8.36:
**“And they gave the king's edicts to the lords that were from the king's presence, and to the governors beyond the river, and they furthered the people and the house of God.”** — they honoured [them] by the royal authority with which Esdras had been raised up
**“AND THEY FURTHERED”** — By adorning it more grandly with divers gifts which the king and his counsellors and princes had sent, and by freeing its ministers and priests from all straits. Mystically, the people and the temple of God hold one and the same figure of the Church, which Esdras and the children of the transmigration lift up, the sacred vessels having been brought from Babylon, when preachers, joining to it with the Lord's help new peoples of believers, show it honourable and terrible to all. The same, when they advance or carry forward those whom they have trained by examples in good conversation or by words even to the receiving of the heavenly rewards, lift up the people into the house of God, because they make great joy both to the elect who abide in the homeland above and to those still on pilgrimage on earth.

9.1:
**“And after these things were accomplished, the princes came to me,”**
• who, namely, had come with Esdras
• AFTER etc. BEDE. This transgression is plainly described in the prophet Malachias and rebuked by prophetic authority: namely that, returned from the captivity, both the princes and priests and Levites and the rest of the people cast off their Israelite wives, who, worn out by poverty and the toil of the journey and the frailty of their sex, were weakened and disfigured, and married foreign women in the flower of their age, either more beautiful or daughters of the powerful and rich. Which is to be understood not of those who had then come with Esdras, but of those who had long since gone up from the captivity with Zorobabel and Jesus [Josue]. For those who had come with Esdras could not so soon despise the teaching of so great a leader as, having not yet stayed five months in the homeland, to leave their wives and take foreign [so the edition: 'eternas'] ones; of whose number the princes are understood to have been who, reporting this crime to Esdras, took care to correct it.
• It is to be noted that the princes strive to correct the sins which the princes committed and made the people committed to them commit; but because they cannot by themselves, they refer the case to the chief, that is, the archbishop, by whose authority the crime may be expiated. Mystically, the foreign wives signify heresies and the superstitious sects of the philosophers, which, when they are incautiously admitted into the Church, contaminate with error the holy seed of catholic truth and pure action. All the sins too with which the heathen are polluted, when Christians are not ashamed to imitate them, [make them] as it were through foreign wives degenerate from the seed of the word of God, by which they had been begotten, according to that: "Of his own will hath he begotten us by the word of truth" etc.; and as it were they beget profane offspring of the daughters of foreigners, when, following the allurements of those who err, they bring forth perverse acts from them to the notice of all.
**“[THE PEOPLE] HAVE NOT SEPARATED THEMSELVES”**
• It is to be noted that, Israel, that is, the ten tribes, having been carried away into captivity, the two tribes, that is, Juda and Benjamin, are called Israel indifferently by the former name. The people of Israel therefore are not here called the ten tribes to distinguish them from Juda and Benjamin; but to distinguish them from the peoples of the lands the people of God in general is understood, which polluted the dignity of the heavenly name by fellowship with the earthly. Hence in Malachias, whom the Hebrews think to be Esdras: "Juda hath transgressed, and abomination hath been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem" etc.; where, saying Juda, he plainly signifies that the people of the first transgression was polluted in this. And what he adds: "The Lord will cut off the master and the scholar" etc., shows that the princes and the people were polluted and were to be rooted out from the fellowship of the saints unless they repented. And what he joins: "Offering gifts to the Lord of hosts", warns them that they offer to the Lord in vain who do not fear to subject themselves to the devil.
• Wonderful is the faith of the princes and people rescued from the captivity, who, being the holy seed, call the other nations the peoples of the lands, to signify that, though created of earth, they dwell in heaven, while they believe above others in the God of heaven and hope to obtain heavenly benefits from him; whence rightly they grieve that their sanctification has been defiled by the abominations of the nations, and, what is graver, confess that the princes who ought to have corrected [it] were the first to err.
9.2:
**“For they have taken of their daughters wives for themselves and for their sons,”** — heresies, philosophical sects
**“and they have mingled the holy seed”** — of catholic truth and pure action
9.3:
**“And when I had heard this word, I rent my mantle”** — signifying the grief of his heart by a mourning habit, that, namely, he might the more quickly stir the minds of all to penance
**“and my coat,”** — by which works are signified
**“and plucked off”** — or: I plucked out
**“the hairs of my head”** — the thoughts of the mind
**“and of my beard,”** — which is the token of the male sex and age, and is therefore put in the designation of the virtues
**“and I sat down mourning.”** — teaching that pardon is to be obtained through the laments of penance
**“I RENT MY MANTLE”** — BEDE. By garments are wont to be designated works, with which we are clothed to glory if they are clean, or to shame if unclean. By the hairs of the head, thoughts, which rise from the hidden root of the heart as from the inner roots of the brain; which, if they are right, ought to be kept, but if reprobate, cut off. Hence of Samuel, who was to be holy, his mother says: "And no razor shall come upon his head." And the Lord says to the apostles: "A hair of your head shall not perish"; because all the thoughts of the saints are in eternal memory with God. But the sinner, that he may be cleansed from his iniquities, must cast away reprobate thoughts, namely the origin of evil works. Hence the leper in Leviticus, his health being recovered, is commanded among the other purifications to shave all the hairs of his flesh, that, so expiated with victims, he may deserve to enter the camp; because then at last are we perfectly cleansed from vices when we drive out even harmful thoughts. The beard too, the token of the male sex and age, is wont to signify virtue. The high priest therefore rent his mantle and coat, to signify that his subjects had works less perfect, which needed to be rent from their solidity by penance and renewed into a better habit; he plucked the hairs of his head, that they might root out wicked thoughts from the heart and give place to useful ones about to be born. He plucked also the hairs of his beard, that they might be humbled in the very virtues which they seemed to have, and might remember that those which were mixed with vices were small or nothing in the examination of the eternal Judge. He sat mourning, to teach that pardon is to be merited through the laments of penance.
9.4:
**“THERE WERE ASSEMBLED”** — Note how much the examples of the doctors help: Esdras is written to have said nothing, but only, on hearing of the crime, to have wept, and to have drawn the crowd of the faithful to himself not by shouting but by weeping.
**“And there were assembled to me all that feared the word of the God of Israel,”** — THERE WERE ASSEMBLED etc. A great change of affairs: through the faithlessness of the princes many had followed luxury; [now,] while the great prince mourns and hints what sinners must do, all who fear the word of God, by which he threatens that transgressors are to be punished, come together to him.
9.5:
**“And at the evening sacrifice I rose up”** — "The lifting up of my hands, as evening sacrifice"
**“from my affliction,”** — namely, the flesh of Christ on the cross
**“HAVING RENT MY MANTLE”** — BEDE. Typically, that, having rent his garment, he bends his knees and spreads out his hands to God, and, pouring out prayers and tears, turns the minds of very many to penance, shows Christ, who prayed for our sins before the passion and in it, and who, with his hands stretched out on the cross, willed the garment of his flesh to be rent with wounds and put to death; whence: "He died for our sins" etc. Which was fittingly done at the time of the evening sacrifice; either because the Lord at the end offered [the sacrament] of flesh and blood to the Father and commanded us to offer it in bread and wine; or because, as the legal sacrifice came to its end, he freed us by his passion and, separating us from the peoples of the lands, made us heavenly, and commanded us to cleave to him chaste in heart and body. His very prayer too, in which, being just, he associates himself with the sinful people, saying: My God, I am confounded etc., fits the humility of the Redeemer, who appeared in the likeness of sinful flesh to take away sin; whence: "O God my God, why hast thou forsaken me? Far from my salvation." Again: "O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my offences are not hidden from thee." Not that he could have offences or foolishness in himself, who "of God is made unto us wisdom, and justice, and sanctification, and redemption"; but, taking upon himself the [nature] of those whom he had come to save, he mercifully deigned to transfer to himself also those things which truly belonged to their frailty.
**“I bowed my knees, and spread out my hands to the Lord my God,”** — I BOWED MY KNEES etc. He prepared himself by compunction of heart and affection of body, that he might be made worthy to be heard by the pity above, and broke forth into these words of prayer. And he bends his knees, spreads out his hands and pours forth prayers at the time of the evening sacrifice, knowing that what is done in the spirit of humility and with a contrite mind is more pleasing than what is offered with the flesh and blood of cattle.
9.6: **“And said: My God, I am confounded and ashamed to lift up my face, my God, to thee: for our iniquities are multiplied over our heads, and our sins are grown up even unto heaven,”** — Christ too prayed for us, saying: "O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my offences are not hidden from thee"
9.7:
**“from the days of our fathers: and we ourselves also have sinned grievously unto this day, and for our iniquities we and our kings, and our priests have been delivered into the hands of the kings of the lands,”** — namely of the rulers of this darkness
**“and to the sword,”** — spiritual
**“and to captivity,”** — of sin
**“and to spoil,”** — because the spiritual "wolf catcheth and scattereth the sheep"
**“and to confusion of face,”** — of the inner [face]
**“as it is at this day.”** — namely, it appears
9.8: **“And now as a little, and for a moment has our prayer been made before the Lord our God, to leave us a remnant, and give us a pin [so the edition: 'pax illus'] in his holy place, and that our God would enlighten our eyes, and would give us a little life in our bondage.”** — the devil's
9.9:
**“For we are bondmen, and in our bondage our God hath not forsaken us, but hath extended upon us”** — condescending to us
**“mercy before the king of the Persians, to give us life,”** — spiritual
**“and to set up the house”** — the Church
**“of our God, and to build the desolations thereof,”** — "The land that was desolate and impassable shall be glad, and the wilderness shall rejoice"
**“and to give us a fence”** — of eternal life
9.11: **“which thou hast commanded by the hand of thy servants the prophets”** — that it might be fulfilled, namely, in work
9.12:
**“Now therefore give not your daughters to their sons, and take not their daughters for your sons, and seek not their peace, nor their prosperity for ever: that you may be strengthened, and may eat the good things of the land,”** — of the living, or of the Church, or of each soul
**“and may have your children your heirs”** — imitators, or good works
9.14:
**“that we should not turn away, nor make void thy commandments, nor join in marriage with the people of these abominations. Art thou”** — with the people of these abominations
**“angry with us unto utter destruction,”** — consuming
9.15:
**“O Lord God of Israel, thou art just,”**
• in thy works
• but we [are] wicked
**“for we are left to be saved, as at this day. Behold we are before thee”** — who seest all things

10.1:
**“Now when Esdras was thus praying, and beseeching God, and weeping, and lying before the temple of the Lord, there was gathered to him of Israel an exceeding great assembly of men and women and children, and the people wept with much lamentation.”** — the fruit, namely, of the prayer and lamentation of Esdras
**“THE PEOPLE WEPT”** — Those, namely, who had sinned, doing penance, or those who had remained in chastity, grieving at the fall of their brethren. And they are shown to have been much troubled at the prayers and laments of their high priest, since women and children too are related to have been present. And it can be understood to have been done with this distinction: that first the innocent and upright flocked to him, when he says: "And there were assembled to me all that feared the word of the God of Israel" etc.; but now those also who had sinned came together with their wives and children to do penance.
10.2:
**“And Sechenias the son of Jehiel of the sons of Elam answered,”** — OF THE SONS OF ELAM etc. Josephus says that this was the first of the people of Jerusalem, who, as befits a prince, at once helped the intention of Esdras with the greatest authority, by confessing that the people had sinned with him and by urging penance, the foreign wives with their children being cast off.
**“and said to Esdras: We have sinned against our God, and have taken strange wives of the people of the land: and now if there be repentance in Israel concerning this,”** — AND NOW IF THERE BE REPENTANCE etc. As if [to say]: If the people perfectly repents of this sin, let us first, turned to the Lord, promise amendment and ask pardon; then, returning to ourselves, let us root out every root of the sin and its shoot, namely by casting out the wives with all their offspring. For this is truly to do penance: to be turned to the Lord with the whole heart and within, and to cut off outwardly all matter of sinning from its very origin.
10.4: **“ARISE”** — He teaches fittingly how one should act in counsel with superiors: namely that each should say according to his own sense what he has understood, or seems to himself to have understood, to be best, and yet leave to him who presides the place of deciding, ready to obey all that he shall decree is to be done according to the will and law of God.
10.6:
**“THE SON OF ELIASIB”** — Who was then high priest; after Jesus the son of Josedec, Joachim his son, and after him Eliasib his son held the high priesthood.
**“HE ATE NO BREAD”** — BEDE. The priests have here an example not only of weeping and praying but also of fasting for those who have sinned. For blessed are they who mourn their own sins, because, having received remission, they are comforted; but more blessed are they who weep for the sins of others, so that they will not touch even bread and water, which is the refreshment of the abstinent, nor enter their house or go up into the bed of their couch, but pass the night praying in the courts of the house of the Lord. For there was the house of the priest which Esdras is said to have entered when evening came on. And another edition, for 'the chamber of Johanan', has 'the pastophorium of Johanan', by which name is often called the porch by which the temple is surrounded on every side, in which the ministers and keepers of the temple stayed. They mourn too now at the transgression of those who had come from the captivity, who grieve that those who had been rescued from sins by repenting have relapsed into them by sinning and have been as it were taken captive again by the devil. Of whose seducers, as of the parents of the unclean wives, Peter says: "For, speaking proud words of vanity, they allure by the desires of fleshly riotousness those who for a little while escape." And a little after: "For if, flying from the pollutions of the world through the knowledge of Jesus Christ, they be again entangled in them and overcome: their latter state is become unto them worse than the former."
10.9:
**“THAT IS THE MONTH”** — BEDE. Which by the Hebrews is called Casleu, by the Romans December, which is in the middle of winter, rainy and stormy. Hence it is to be noted that, when the people came together in the middle of winter, they are recorded as trembling because of the sin and because of the rains. For when they saw the rains greater than usual even in the very season of rains, returning to their conscience they imputed this to their sins and feared wrath from the very disturbance of the air; therefore they did not presume to do their business in private houses, but sat in the street of the house of the Lord, having put on the habit of penance and humility. This [is said] because of those who, when the elements are disturbed and the cold of the winds, or floods of rain, or heaps of snow, or the heat of drought, or even the destruction of men or animals weighs down from above, and the Judge himself shows the force of his wrath even by open signs, seek nothing of amendment of manners by which they may appease the Judge and escape the impending blow, but with worldly pride consider by what art they may either avoid or overcome the adversities which rage outwardly because of their sins.
**“AND ALL ... SAT”** — BEDE. That is, around the court of the priests, by which the house itself was surrounded on every side, having round about it on every side, in a square, very spacious buildings of courts, in which the people too, when there was need because of rain, could stand and see the things that were done at the doors of the temple, or around the temple; for they had the inner walls next the ground made on columns, the outer ones solid.
10.10: **“AND ESDRAS ROSE UP”** — BEDE. This place answers to what was said above: And Esdras rose up before the house of God, and went to the chamber of Johanan the son of Eliasib etc. Where the devotion of the high priest is to be noted, who, mourning, praying and fasting for the transgression of the people, remained in the courts of the temple, and would not enter his own house before, having received the consent of the people, he saw them penitent with their whole heart and converted to the Lord. Of which devotion the rest of the princes too seem to have been partners, when they are said themselves to have gone away, the synod being ended, into the houses of their fathers. For if Scripture does not signify this, what need was there to write that, the meeting being finished, Esdras and the heads of families went away from the enclosures of the temple into the houses of their fathers? For there is no one who does not know that they did this. What need was there to add: and all by their names, since this too was most well known to all, unless because it wished them to be understood as such men whose names and deeds should rightly be held in memory and handed on to posterity to be known?
10.16: **“And the children of the captivity did so. And Esdras the priest and the men heads of the families went into the houses of their fathers, and all by their names, and they sat down in the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.”** — AND THEY SAT etc. BEDE. Note that the number three is mystical. Above it was said that in three days all came together in Jerusalem, and now in three months, namely the tenth, eleventh and twelfth, they are cleansed from the foreign wives. For there are three virtues without which no one is saved: faith, hope and charity. In the third time of the world Christ, coming in the flesh into the world, bestowed on us the grace of the gospel. For he sent before the first time, before the law, in the patriarchs, the second under the law in the prophets; in the third he himself came with grace and, redeeming us by his passion, rose on the third day. Since by his grace we are joined to the fellowship of the Church and purged from the allurements of vices, fittingly the children of the transmigration came in three days to be cleansed and completed the cleansing in three months. According to the letter too they laboured opportunely, that before the beginning of the first month they might all be purged, that they might celebrate the Pasch and the very month in which it was to be celebrated cleanly and holily, and begin and finish the year cleanly and holily. Which it behoves us too to imitate every year in the Lent of the Pasch, that, the Lord's resurrection being at hand, "we may cleanse ourselves from all defilement of the flesh and of the spirit", that we may be able to be partakers of the resurrection.
10.18:
**“AND THERE WERE FOUND”** — BEDE. The Hebrews fit to this place that of the prophet Zacharias: "And the Lord shewed me Jesus the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord: and Satan stood on his right hand to be his adversary." And a little after: "And Jesus was clothed with filthy garments: and he stood before the face of the angel. Take away the filthy garments from him. And he said to him: Behold I have taken away thy iniquity, and have clothed thee with change of garments. And he said: Put a clean mitre upon his head." Rightly, they say, "Satan stood on his right hand to be his adversary", because the accusation was true, for he himself with the rest married a foreign wife. And what is said, that "Jesus was clothed with filthy garments", they interpret in three ways: either because of the unlawful marriage, or because of the sins of the people, or because of the squalor of the captivity. And the angel before whose face Jesus stood commanded the other angels to take away from him the filthy garments. Which done, the same angel said: "Behold I have taken away thy iniquity from thee"; these are the filthy garments; "and have clothed thee with change of garments", that is, I have joined to thee an Israelite wife. And what follows: "Put a clean mitre upon his head", they will have to be understood of the dignity of the priesthood, because, namely, the filth of sins being taken away, he had a clean priesthood. But it is to be observed that Esdras does not write that Jesus married a foreign wife, but some of his sons and brethren etc.
**“AND HIS BRETHREN”** — BEDE. Kinsmen, that is; for his brothers german in the flesh could not still live and give themselves to pleasure, since a hundred years and more had passed since Cyrus, beginning to reign, sent back Jesus and Zorobabel with the transmigration of Juda and Benjamin to Jerusalem to build the house of the Lord.
10.19:
**“And they gave their hands to put away their wives, and to offer for their offence a ram of the flock.”**
• AND THEY GAVE etc. BEDE. First they cast off the unlawful wives, and so offer a ram for themselves, that, the crime being taken away, they might come clean to the altar. For it is hard for the victim of one to be acceptable to God who has not first left the fault for which he offers; whence: "Cease to do perversely, learn to do well." And because those who had sinned first were sons or brethren of the high priest, rightly in amendment of the crime they offer a ram of the flocks, to signify that they had resolved to slay themselves, who seemed to be leaders of the people as leaders of the flock, from their former life, and, purged by worthy penance, to offer themselves to God through a better life.
• If anyone objects that it is not written that they cast out the sons of the adulteresses, but only the women themselves, although above, when Sechenias suggested and said: Let us make a covenant with the Lord our God, to put away all the wives, and such as are born of them, it was at once added: Then Esdras arose, and made the chiefs of the priests and of the Levites and all Israel swear that they would do according to this word, and they swore; let him understand that, if they did not cast out the sons, the reason was that they taught them to renounce their mothers' unbelief and, consecrated to the Lord by circumcision and the saving victim, joined them to their own faith and chastity. Mystically, the good works which we do with an eye to temporal advantage or favour or delight are either to be reckoned among evils, or to be separated from the low intention and done for the heavenly reward alone. For he who fasts, prays and gives alms that he may be seen and praised by men, such offspring of good action is born as it were of an unclean mother, and therefore cannot have a part among those who went up from Babylon to Jerusalem. For he who receives his reward in the present will lack it in the future, unless the author of the work, turning his mind to better things, begins to do for God what he was doing for empty praise, and, consecrating as it were the offspring unworthily brought forth to the Lord, makes it a citizen of Jerusalem, so that, correcting the work ill begun, he makes it worthy of everlasting reward in heaven.
**“AND THEY GAVE THEIR HANDS”** — BEDE. Note with how great art of fighting the devil attacks the faithful, so as to leave them no time secure. For behold, those who could not be overcome by adversaries were conquering the public enemies, the temple of the Lord being built and dedicated, but were conquered by love of women, so as not to keep the temples of their hearts or works worthy of God. The figure of which thing is plainly fulfilled in our times, when we see the minds of the faithful now tempted much more dangerously within, drawn away and enticed by their own concupiscence, than they were once tempted without, when the savage adversary raged against their constancy with iron and fire. But the pity of the Lord will be present, which, as it gave the virtue of patience [so the edition: 'pentientie'] against the open struggles of the raging, so will give us the guard of caution against the snares of stealthy flatteries. Finally, by the diligence of the high priest bringing this about, those who feared the Lord "were all compunct in heart", those who had sinned also cast out the foreign wives; and so, the foulness of luxury being expelled, the beauty of chastity returned, and in the city of the Lord, the rubbish of vices being cast out, the flowers and ornaments of the virtues were scattered.

1.1:
**“The words of Nehemias the son of Helchias.”** — understand: of the comforter of the Lord, or of the comforter sent by the Lord.
**“THE WORDS OF NEHEMIAS”**
• BEDE. Nehemias is interpreted 'comforter of the Lord' or 'comforter from the Lord'; who, since he renewed the walls of Jerusalem and raised up the people, freed from the enemies, in the observance of the divine law, plainly signifies Christ by name and work, who says: "And I will ask the Father, and he shall give you another Paraclete." Of whom the psalmist says: "The Lord buildeth up Jerusalem" etc. He signifies also the holy preachers, by whose ministry the comfort from above is given us, or when after the fall of sin they promise the penitent the hope of pardon and of the promise, as it were restoring the walls of Jerusalem destroyed by the enemies.
• BEDE. Up to here are the words of Esdras, in which he describes the deeds of Zorobabel and Josue, then described his own deeds. Here he plainly signified Christ, because he renewed sacred Scripture, brought the captives back to Jerusalem, enriched and exalted the house of the Lord with greater gifts, appointed leaders and governors beyond the river Euphrates who should know the law of God, and cleansed the children of the transmigration from foreign wives. For Christ renewed sacred Scripture, because what the scribes and Pharisees had defiled by their traditions or taught to be understood only according to the letter, he showed to be full of spiritual sense, and, having sent the Holy Spirit, had the New Testament written through the apostles and apostolic men. He led the people out of the Babylonian captivity and brought them, freed, into Jerusalem, the land of promise; because, having once suffered on the cross, he redeemed the world with his blood, and, descending to hell, led the true Israelites from there to the walls of the city above and opened [so the edition: 'inclusit'] to them the joys of the promised inheritance; and daily, gathering the faithful from the turmoil of the world, he calls them to the fellowship of the Church and the everlasting kingdom. He increased the adornments of the temple with gold and silver and precious vessels, which the people of Israel and the princes of the Persians had sent through him; because, leading into the Church those of both peoples who believe in him, he does not cease to adorn and glorify it with the brightness of their faith and work. He appointed leaders and chiefs for all the people beyond the river who should know and teach the law of God; because in the Church, which has been washed by the river of baptism and passes beyond the river of Babylon, that is, the turmoil of the fluctuating world, by sincerity of faith, he set apostles, evangelists, pastors and rulers. He cleansed the children of the transmigration from foreign wives, because he forbade those who renounce the world by the profession of faith to serve the allurements of the world. He cast the sons of such mothers out of the company of the transmigration, lest perhaps, grown up, they should follow the faithlessness of their mothers, not the faith of their fathers. For he taught that our works too, even those which seem good to men, are to be rejected if they are mixed with carnal delights, if they have taken their origin from the contagion of human favour, and do not befit those who perfectly leave the world and pass over with their whole mind to heavenly things; who rejoice not to be enervated by temporal flatteries, but to be exercised by adversities and prepared for everlasting rest.
**“And it came to pass in the month of Casleu,”** — which is interpreted 'his hope'
**“IN THE MONTH OF CASLEU”** — The month of Casleu is the one we call December; among the Hebrews the ninth, among us the last. Its name, which is interpreted 'his hope', fits well the vows of him who was intent on raising up the ruins of the holy city. For the first foundation of good action is to have hope of the Lord's help for perfecting what we desire. In this month the Lord was born; by whose name it was figured long before that in that month the true Nehemias, long desired, would come for the building of the Church.
**“in the twentieth year, as I was in the castle of Susa.”** — AS I WAS IN SUSA etc. Susa is the metropolis of the Persians, but of such strength that it seems to be a castle; and it is interpreted 'riding' or 'returning'; which are fittingly applied to the faithful, chiefly to those who have care for the captivity of Jerusalem, that is, for the salvation of those who, having at some time been snatched from the Church by the snares of the devil, have been brought back again, repenting, by the grace of God. For such are in the returning castle, that is, in the strength of a mind called back from the lowest things to the desire of the heavenly homeland, and in the riding of holy hearts, which, namely, carry God as their rider.
1.3:
**“And they said to me: They that have remained, and are left of the captivity there in the province, are in affliction”** — of mind
**“great”** — even if they seem to be in peace
**“and reproach:”** — of the enemies
**“and the wall”** — who, namely, ought to have defended others
**“of Jerusalem is broken down, and the gates”** — who ought to bring in the worthy, and keep the unworthy out of the Church
**“thereof are burnt with fire.”** — by the burning of vices
**“THEY THAT HAD REMAINED”** — BEDE. The sense of the letter is plain: for those who had remained of the captivity, though they seemed to live in peace, the king of the Persians being their friend, to whom a little before he had sent Esdras with letters to have power in the region beyond the river, were yet in great affliction of mind and in the reproach of the enemies, because the wall of the holy city was still broken down. And then the saints are rightly afflicted in the Church and pricked with worldly sorrow, when, at some time coming to their senses from sins, they see their neighbours still subject to vices, so that through the negligence of those who could have profited many the devil can enter the Church as through the walls of a broken city; which is the more to be grieved if those very ones who ought to have profited others by teaching and example become by their living an example of death. For this is that the gates of Jerusalem have been burnt up by the flames of the enemies: that those who ought by living and teaching well to have brought the worthy into the Church of the elect and kept out the unworthy perish in the burning of avarice, luxury and the other vices.
1.4: **“I WEPT AND MOURNED”** — If the holy man, hearing that buildings of timber and stone had been destroyed, rightly mourned, fasted and prayed, sitting long in sadness, how much more in the destruction and ruin of souls must we persist in continual mourning and prayers, that by God's mercy those may be raised to their former soundness who lay squalid in the long-standing filth of vices, to the reproach of religion, while the enemy triumphed.

2.1: **“IN THE MONTH OF NISAN”** — BEDE. Which, namely, is the first month of the year according to the Hebrews, in which they always celebrate the Pasch, which we call April. What therefore he said above, that he mourned, fasted and prayed for many days, plainly [means] that for four continuous months, namely the ninth, tenth, eleventh and twelfth, he persisted in holy devotion, waiting for when he could opportunely make known his desire to the king. He was indeed the chief cupbearer, he handed the cup to the king, he performed outwardly the office of gladness, but inwardly he mourned, because he remembered that the holy city was overthrown and the people of God afflicted by the reproach of the enemies; whence: "Upon the rivers of Babylon, there we sat" etc.
2.5:
**“And I said to the king: If it seem good to the king,”**
• IF IT SEEM etc. BEDE.
