This can also be taken mystically of the persecution of the gentiles, by which the Church was often shaken; which on the occasion of the martyrs seemed to be utterly destroyed, but, while they were crowned in secret, was built the better; and as miracles shone forth from them even after death, a greater people flocked to the confession of the faith, until the very summit of the worldly empire bent its neck to the yoke of Christ; so that the state of the holy city, that is, the Church, long attacked by kings and princes, was helped and spread by their earnestness; as the kings of the Chaldeans, who are interpreted 'fierce' or 'as demons', overthrew Jerusalem, but the kings of the Persians, who are interpreted 'tried', restore it with friendly provision and exalt it with due honour.
12.27:
**“And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought for the Levites”**
• spiritual men, namely, taken up into the lot of the kingdom
• because "the Son of man shall send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds"
**“AT THE DEDICATION”** — BEDE. The city had long since been built, but it was not fitting that it should be dedicated before, the inhabitants being gathered, fit ministers had been appointed for the temple and keepers for the gates and porches. And the holy city, when made, is dedicated when, the number of the elect being fulfilled at the end of the world, the Church is brought universally into heaven to the vision of its Maker; to whose life, whenever we are lifted up with desires in this life, we rejoice as it were over the future dedication of our city. Hence too the dedication can be taken in two ways: meanwhile, namely, in the hope of those who desire and cleanse the eyes of the heart with which they may see God; then in the very reality of blessed men enjoying the divine vision in spiritual bodies among the angelic hosts.
**“out of all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem,”**
• the heavenly
• rejoicing together, namely, in the receiving of eternal life, and giving thanks to him by whose gift they deserved [so the edition: 'incruerunt'] to enter that city
**“AND WITH CYMBALS”** — Cymbals, psalteries and harps can be understood as the bodies of the just, then immortal, in which they will render most sweet sounds to the Lord. In the present life too the Levites are gathered in Jerusalem when the faithful, kindled by the memory of the peace above, place in it the whole delight of their mind, and rejoice, if not yet by beholding, at least by desiring, over the eternal inheritance in heaven which they hope to receive, according to that: "Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye just" etc. For they keep the dedication with song and thanksgiving when, rejoicing in the Lord, they accept whatever adversity or prosperity befalls; they keep it with cymbals, psalteries and harps when they make the pleasing sounds of their works ascend to the ears of God and kindle the hearts of their neighbours to his love etc.
12.28: **“THE SONS OF THE SINGING MEN”** — That is, the imitators of those who strove to serve the Lord with devout and cheerful mind and to sing his word by preaching to others. Who make themselves villages round about Jerusalem when with lofty heart they dwell in the neighbourhood of the homeland above, saying: "But our conversation is in heaven." And they make the same villages in the plains around Jerusalem when, with heart enlarged toward God, they humble themselves the more, the more sweetly they touch the glory of loftiness by tasting it. All of whom are now gathered man by man to the heavenly homeland by the advances of their works, and in the very time of the dedication, that is, of everlasting reward, are united there together.
12.30: **“And the priests and the Levites were purified, and they purified the people, and the gates, and the wall.”** — AND [THE PRIESTS] WERE PURIFIED etc. BEDE. A wholly just order, that the doctors who desire to purify the people should first be purified, should chastise the body and bring it into subjection, lest perhaps, preaching to others, they be found reprobate. And the priests and Levites were purified by prayers and offerings of victims and by abstaining from their wives. And they purified the people by preaching the same continence. They purified the gates and the wall by going round with trumpets and canticles of psalms, the people accompanying, and, the circuit being completed, by offering victims for the state of the citizens and the city. And now too those who preside over the Church, taken by the Lord into the spiritual ministry, the greater memory they bear of our dedication, which will be in our resurrection, the more they strive to purify and sanctify themselves and those committed to them, lest perhaps anyone not having a wedding garment be cast out of the common joy of the holy city and, bound hand and foot, be sent into the exterior darkness.
12.31:
**“THE PRINCES OF JUDA”** — That is, of confession or praise; the more perfect doctors of the Church are those who go up upon the wall at the dedication of the city, because in the time of tribulation they are shown to have surpassed the general life of the Church by living more loftily. For of these it is said: "Upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen." Rightly therefore those who now preside over the walls of the Church as watchmen will then too stand above them in the glory of reward.
**“and I appointed two great companies of them that gave praise.”** — namely of Jews and gentiles praising God in the homeland above; which is also done daily in this life
**“AND I APPOINTED TWO COMPANIES”** — Either [it signifies that] they purge the filth of sins from the Church in the present by living more correctly and correcting those who err, and in the future expel from the city of the Lord, that is, from entrance into the heavenly homeland, by judicial power those who would not be corrected; or the companies of those giving praise, going to the right hand, go up upon the wall to the gate of the dunghill when they proclaim worthy of praise those who remove all uncleanness from the Church by preaching, rebuking and excommunicating.
**“And they went on the right hand upon the wall to the gate of the dunghill.”** — because the just, by living rightly, both hasten to eternal life in the present and will come to it in the future
12.35: **“AND OF THE SONS OF THE PRIESTS”** — In this life the sons of the priests sound with trumpets at the dedication of the city who by preaching kindle the hearts of their hearers to the memory of the heavenly homeland.
12.36:
**“WITH THE INSTRUMENTS OF THE SONG OF DAVID”** — Because they do not lean on their own sense or desires, but, following in all things the life and teaching of the fathers and prophets, persist in the word of preaching.
**“AND ESDRAS”** — Because in all that they do they have before their eyes the words of holy Scripture, by whose leading they may come to the entrance of eternal life, that they may be inebriated with the plenty of the house of God and the torrent of his pleasure, with whom is the fountain of life etc.
12.37:
**“And over against them they went up by the stairs of the city of David”**
• "strong of hand and desirable in aspect"
• And over against them etc. Not, that is, with the opposition of distance, but with the meeting of harmony, by which the elect in this life kindle one another to the love of God, and in that life, rejoicing together more perfectly in their mutual blessedness, praise him without weariness; as the seraphim, crying one to another, celebrate together the holy Trinity with fellow exultation.
**“AND OVER AGAINST THEM”** — BEDE. When the city was being built it was said that those who built the gate of the fountain carried the measure of their work up to the steps that go down from the city of God. There, therefore, a going down of the steps from the city is named; here, when the city is dedicated, a going up. And as there too a struggle with the enemy was carried on, here, the enemy conquered, joy is celebrated; because the saints who are humbled in the present under the mighty hand of God will be exalted in the future; who now build the walls of the Church on earth of living stones, that is, of holy souls, in affliction and perils and many watchings, then, the building completed and raised to heaven, rejoicing go up to contemplate the brightness of God.
**“at the going up of the wall above the house of David,”** — which is all the just, who are filled with the grace of the Creator and inhabited by him
**“ABOVE THE HOUSE OF DAVID”** — BEDE. The sons of the priests go up above the house of David when preachers or martyrs, as now they surpass the general life of the just in the ministry of the word or the struggle of martyrdom, so then go before their general rewards with the gift of a loftier recompense. Whence: Because thou hast been faithful in a little, thou shalt have power over ten cities. For as many as each instructs to life by word or example, for so many will he then be more gloriously honoured in the receiving of life. The priests also come up to the water gate toward the east when those who in this life, as the hart panteth after the fountains of water, so desired to come and appear before the face of God, attain to the fulfilment of their desire and deserve to see the rising of the sun of justice without setting.
12.38:
**“And the second company of them that gave thanks”** — to God
**“went on the opposite side,”** — that one might stir up the other
**“and I after them, and the half of the people upon the wall, and upon the tower”** — namely the loftiness and the guarding of works
**“AND UPON THE TOWER”** — BEDE. It is long to discourse specially on each of the gates or towers; let it suffice to have said only this: that those who finished the gates, towers and wall of the city with great labour, hardship, hunger, cold and many watchings, the enemy unwearied and lying in wait resisting, then, the enemy repelled and confounded, walking through the gates, towers and buildings of the same city with canticles, hymns and psalteries, cymbals, harps and trumpets, rejoice in thanksgiving together with the masters of the work and of the law of God. Which there is no doubt is done also in the spiritual building, when, the time of the last retribution being at hand, as at the long-desired dedication of the city of God, the faithful will obtain eternal rewards for their works; when, like Nehemias, Esdras and the other priests and Levites, each bringing forward his workers, all the masters of the faithful peoples lead those whom they have gained for the Lord to the walls of the heavenly homeland. Then among other things Nehemias goes with the company of those giving praise even upon the tower of the furnaces, in whose building he had toiled before, when the masters of truth rejoice over the lofty rewards of those whom they taught. For if the oven-baked loaves, which are baked in secret, signify the inner devotion of the mind of the faithful, strengthened by the fire of charity, whence also they are commanded to be offered in sacrifice to the Lord, what is figured by the furnaces in which the same loaves are baked if not the hearts of those who always burn with the flame of inward love and are wont to bring forth the deeds or words of the virtues? Of which it is well said: God, whose fire is in Sion, and his furnace in Jerusalem. They themselves too say of themselves: Was not our heart burning within us etc. But the hearts of the reprobate burn with the fire of crimes; whence: They are all adulterers, their hearts are as an oven. The builders of the holy city therefore build among other things the tower of the furnaces when the doctors instruct the hearts of their hearers in faith and work, that they may be kindled to receive the greater gifts of the Spirit and to bring forth daily new dishes of the virtues for the joy of the people of God. And rejoicing and singing praise to the Lord they walk upon the tower of the furnaces on the day of the dedication of Jerusalem when in the time of the future retribution they rejoice together over the glory of those whom they taught. The furnaces then are the hearts of the elect, in which the charity of God is poured forth by the Holy Spirit, who is given to them. And the tower of the furnaces is the loftiness and guard by which the same hearts must always be fortified with circumspect caution and solicitude, lest they can be hurt by malignant spirits, lest the flame of the virtues can be bent or troubled by the wind of pride.
**“of the furnaces”** — of hearts burning with the flame of the Holy Spirit
12.40:
**“And there stood”** — with firm heart
**“the two companies of them that gave praise in the house of God,”** — joined, namely, from both peoples in one melody of divine praise, or made of angels and men, because "men shall be equal to the angels of God"
**“and I and the half of the magistrates with me.”** — AND THERE STOOD etc. BEDE. Having walked round the walls and gates of the city with the song of joy and the instruments of musicians, they return to the temple of the Lord, that, standing there too, they may render praise to the Lord with trumpets sounding together and, victims being offered, fulfil the vows of the dedication. And the house of the Lord, like the city of the Lord, signifies the very homeland of the future life, as the penitent [so the edition] Church too is called the house of God and city; but there is a difference, because they are said to have gone up the buildings of the city praising with canticles of thanks and instruments, but in the house of God to have praised standing and to have sung loud. For the elect go up the walls of the city which they made when they enter the joys of the homeland above which they deserved by working well. They made the distributed loftiness of gates, steps and buildings when, entering the house of the Father, they behold there the distance of many mansions according to divers merits. In this life the just go up in the city of the Lord with hymns of dedication when, gaping with their whole heart toward the memory of the future reward, they advance daily in good works, according to that: "In his heart he hath disposed to ascend by steps, in the vale of tears." And: "Blessed are the undefiled in the way" etc. For so they hold the innocence of heart and work they have received as always to strive to grow to higher things. And they stand in the house of the Lord with praises who persevere unwearied in that very advance of works, according to that of Elias: "The Lord liveth, in whose sight I stand", that is, in fulfilling whose will I remain with untiring mind.
12.42: **“AND THEY SUNG LOUD”** — "Thou hast broken my bonds: I will sacrifice to thee the sacrifice of praise." "I will pay my vows to the Lord in the courts of the house of the Lord, in the presence of all his people: in the midst of thee, O Jerusalem." This is done when, the multitude of all the saints being gathered in the heavenly homeland, we offer those praises for which we groan in the present and which we thirst for with daily desire in thanksgiving.
12.43:
**“And they sacrificed on that day great victims,”** — namely of everlasting light, of which Zacharias: "And there shall be one day, which is known to the Lord, not day nor night", that is, removed from the custom of passing [days]
**“and they rejoiced:”** — because each, received in his mansion, perseveres in the perpetual vision of the Creator and celebrates his praises with harmonious voice
**“FOR GOD HAD MADE [THEM] REJOICE”** — BEDE. These things belong to the dedication of the holy city, namely the heavenly Jerusalem, in which God is king, who gladdens the citizens with his presence; great joy is had. Whence: "I bring you good tidings of great joy, that shall be to all the people"; to distinguish it, namely, from human joy, which is a small and passing joy and therefore to be little valued. This dedication can be understood as begun in this life in certain of the elect who, the eye of the heart being purified, contemplate in part the future joys of the Church, as Isaias, Ezechiel, Daniel and the other prophets, and the apostles who saw the Lord glorified on the mount; who, the higher they entered the heights of the city above, the more clearly they took care to sing the praises of the Lord and to sacrifice the greatest victims of good works.
**“AND THEIR WIVES ALSO”** — Because in the time of the resurrection not only those who built the Church by preaching or by working strongly receive the fruit of their labour, but the weaker sharers of the same faith also rejoice in the same receiving of life: "For the Lord hath blessed the little ones with the great."
12.44:
**“THEY APPOINTED ALSO”** — BEDE. While all rejoiced over the building and dedication of the city, care was earnestly taken that the worship of religion in it, which was to be carried out chiefly in the ceremonies through the teaching and offices of the priests, Levites, singers and porters, should be kept and should grow. Therefore vigorous men were appointed who should diligently gather into the treasury of Christ the money contributed by the people and keep it for the use of the ministries of the temple and altar; and should keep with careful attention the firstfruits of the crops and the tithes and the wine for the libations which were brought to the temple; that, namely, there being an abundant supply of the things which were to be offered to the Lord or on which the ministers of the Lord should live, they themselves might the more willingly remain in Jerusalem, by whom the people might be taught and sanctified. The Lord too ordained that they who preach the gospel should live by the gospel. But woe to the priests and ministers who delight to take from the people the expenses of their grade, but are proved to labour nothing for its salvation, to furnish nothing of holy guidance [so the edition: 'sacri ductus'] by living rightly, to sing nothing sweet of the sweetness of the heavenly kingdom by preaching, and not to open the doors of the city above but to shut them by acting perversely; by whose works the people does not rejoice in praising God but is afflicted. It is to be noted indeed that Juda, who in the building of the city spoke in despair: "The strength of the bearer of burdens is decayed, and the rubbish is very much" etc., had now already recovered strength of mind and body to carry out the earth which hindered the building of the wall which had fallen, and to overcome the snares of the enemies which threatened. Rightly therefore he rejoices in the priests and Levites, singers and porters, by whose labour and exhortation he escaped the danger of so great an affliction and found the glory of so great prosperity. And thou therefore, if thou seest thy heart weighed down with the earth of vices, so that thou art not able to build in it a city worthy of the divine dwelling, if thou seest the malignant enemy drawing thee back from purging the rubbish of vices and from building the walls of the virtues, hear the consolation and counsels of the priests and the reading of the divine Scriptures; for so, the snares of the demons being driven out, God the victor enters the dwelling of thy breast as his city, to sanctify it and make his abode with thee.
**“They appointed also on that day men over the storechambers of the treasure, for the libations, and for the firstfruits, and for the tithes, that the rulers of the city might bring them in by them in the honour of thanksgiving, for the priests and Levites: for Juda was joyful for the priests and Levites that assisted.”** — For this reason he wished the priests and Levites and the other ministers of the saints to dwell in Jerusalem among the peoples, that [Juda] might rejoice in the good works of those by whose earnestness the people was corrected and the city built, and dedicated with great praise and joy.
12.47:
**“And all Israel in the days of Zorobabel, and in the days of Nehemias, gave portions to the singing men,”** — that "they who preach the gospel should live by the gospel"
**“and to the porters day by day, and they sanctified the Levites,”** — they gave tithes as to the saints of God
**“and the Levites sanctified the sons of Aaron.”** — as offering to the greater the tenth part of their tithes

13.1:
**“And on that day they read in the book of Moses in the hearing of the people: and therein was found written, that there should not come in”** — unless, namely, they cease to be such
**“the Ammonites and the Moabites to the church of God for ever:”** — AND ON THAT DAY etc. These, because they were born of incest, express the heretics, whose authors, when by understanding it ill they corrupt the teaching of the fathers in which they were instructed, use the father's seed like the daughters of Lot, by stealth and in darkness and not lawfully. And therefore their offspring, that is, their followers, can never have a part in the Church of God. For if any are corrected, they are no longer sons of such mothers. And they met [so the edition] the children of Israel coming out of Egypt with bread and water. So too those living well and in the catholic peace bestow the comfort of the word of God on those who, lately rescued from the bondage of sins through the water of baptism and the waves of the sea, pant for the liberty of the heavenly homeland. Which Berzellai the Galaadite did, who met David with his army fleeing from the face of Absalom with food, by which, refreshing them, he might make them stronger against the new tyranny; signifying those who strengthen the Church scattered by heretics with the aids of the heavenly word and encourage it to overthrow their madness. But while heretics strive to destroy the neophytes by their depravities and by the examples of others shown or by malignant words, as those born of incest they attack the people of Israel come out of Egypt with their arms, and with the counsels and wicked curses of Balaam, who is interpreted 'vanity of the people'; but God turned the curse of Balaam into a blessing of his people and defended it from the arms of the enemies.
13.2:
**“because they met not the children of Israel with bread”** — of the word of God
**“and water: and they hired Balaam against them,”** — the vanity of the people
**“to curse them: and our God turned the curse into a blessing.”** — because "to them that love God all things work together unto good"
13.3:
**“And it came to pass, when they had heard the law,”** — concerning, namely, the two nations to be anathematized
**“that they separated every stranger from Israel.”** — AND IT CAME TO PASS etc. Because we must attend to the hearing of the truth, so that, when we are forbidden any one vice by the divine reading, we at once drive from our action and conscience whatever of defiling vice we detect in ourselves.
13.6: **“But in all this time I was not in Jerusalem, because in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes the king of Babylon I went to the king, and at the end of the days I asked the king.”** — BUT IN ALL THIS etc. BEDE. This sentence, in which Nehemias says that he was not in Jerusalem, seems to belong not to the things which he had narrated above up to this point, but only to the present place. For the things above seem to have been done or said when the city was built, while Nehemias still stayed in Jerusalem. Which being vigorously completed, he returned to the king; in whose absence Eliasib made there a great storehouse in which should be laid up the things necessary either for the ministry of the house of the Lord or for the uses of the ministers; who also did not fear to place certain unlawful things in the storehouse and in the house of the Lord, which Nehemias on his return at once rooted out.
13.8:
**“And it seemed to me exceeding evil: and I cast forth the household stuff of the house of Tobias out of the storehouse.”**
• AND I CAST FORTH THE HOUSEHOLD STUFF etc. He who is mentioned above as the servant, the Ammonite, the enemy of the people of God; hence Eliasib did ill, who made a treasury for him, though his kinsman, in the porch of the house of the Lord, the vessels of the house of God and the other things which the use of the ministry required being cast out. "For what participation hath justice with injustice? What agreement hath the temple of God with idols?" What communion have heretics and schismatics with the orthodox and peaceable sons of God?
• They too cast the stuff of Tobias the Ammonite out of the storehouse of the temple and put back the vessels of the house of God and the incense who, heretics being excommunicated or false catholics expelled from the Church, put in their grades those who will serve Christ, who may serve him with faithful acts and prayers. This deed of Nehemias is indeed to be compared with the zeal of Christ, who, finding in the temple of God those who sold and bought, made a scourge of little cords and cast them all out. For as Nehemias represented his person in the other things, so also in this.
**“AND I CAST FORTH”** — BEDE. Thou too, whatever of unbelief and uncleanness thou findest among the faithful, cast it out at once, that, the hearts of believers, which are the storehouses of the Lord, being cleansed, the vessels of the Lord may be brought in when they are full of the riches of the virtues; that is, that the hearts themselves, which a little before were vessels of error through fault, may become vessels of the Lord through correction; and there the sacrifice of good working and the incense of good prayer is made where before was a den of thieves.
13.15:
**“In those days I saw in Juda some treading the presses on the sabbath, carrying sheaves, and lading asses with wine, and grapes, and figs, and all manner of burdens, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the sabbath day. And I charged them that they should sell on a day on which it was lawful to sell.”** — when it is necessary, namely, to provide the necessaries for this world
**“IN THOSE DAYS”** — By the law we are commanded to work what is necessary for six days and to rest on the seventh, because all the elect in this world, which runs in six ages, ought to labour for eternal rest, but in the future day, as on the seventh, to hope for rest from the Lord. Tropologically, that is, morally, they keep the sabbath consecrated to the Lord when, separated for a time from the cares of this world, they give themselves to prayers and lift up a purified mind to the contemplation of heavenly things. For when we rightly do the things which the care of the flesh demands, we labour as it were on the six days at what is necessary. Since therefore we are occupied with those things which we need for this world, the sabbath-keeping of our prayers and devotion, in which we are free from temporal things that we may taste longer the joys of eternity, is rightly assigned to the seventh day, because it imitates the rest of the future life and of blessed praise. But foreigners seek to profane the sabbath day when earthly thoughts trouble us importunately in the time of prayer and draw us back from inner love by the memory or delight of temporal things. They lay on asses wine, grapes and figs and all manner of burdens and bring them into Jerusalem when, loading the foolish motions of the mind with carnal delights, they try to violate the rest of the heart dedicated to God. But Nehemias opposes these tumults of wicked thoughts, lest they disquiet our sabbath, when, with strict skill and the Lord's help, we shut out useless and foolish fancies from our heart in the time of prayer. For he charges them to sell such merchandise on a day on which it is lawful to sell when the soul devoted to God sets this measure to its thoughts: that in the time of prayer they abstain from the cares of passing things, yet at other times, when opportunity dictates, do not turn their regard altogether away from those things which belong to food and clothing, but dispense them with fitting moderation.
13.16: **“BRINGING IN FISH”** — The good fish is pious faith; he who asks it of the Lord does not receive the serpent of unbelief. But the bad fish is the weak thought which plunges itself beyond measure into the cares of this world; which the Tyrians, that is, 'the distressed', seek to sell us on the sabbath when the unclean spirits importunately try to overwhelm the rest of our thought with the deep cares of the world. But for such trade Nehemias rebukes the nobles of Juda and chastises them, when the divine inspiration purges from such thoughts those who strive to serve the profession of piety.
13.19: **“AND IT CAME TO PASS”** — Our conscience, if, purged from vices, it rejoices in God as its inhabitant, can be called Jerusalem; whose gates are the bodily senses, through which the things that are done outside come as it were by entering to the knowledge of our mind; which we are commanded to shut on the sabbath day, that, when we seek to give ourselves to God in psalms and prayers, we may drive from the mind whatever is done outwardly and with free mind pray to and praise the Judge alone in secret. And because no one becomes highest suddenly, but by long advance in holy living, while one [strives] to come, with grace as leader, to this perfection and peace of mind, it rightly follows therefore: I spoke also to the Levites etc.
13.22:
**“I SPOKE ALSO TO THE LEVITES THAT THEY SHOULD BE PURIFIED”** — Those must be purified from the daily exercise of work who desire to guard the gates of the senses from the assault of troubled thought.
**“I spoke also to the Levites that they should be purified, and should come to keep the gates, and to sanctify the sabbath day: for this also remember me, O my God, and spare me according to the multitude of thy mercies.”** — He who desires to sanctify the sabbath day, that is, to make the leisure of prayer, psalmody, holy reading and tears profitable to himself, must have his conscience purified with much skill, that he may be able to accomplish the intention of good action. Which can also rightly be taken in the allegorical sense of the doctors of the faithful. For whoever long to guard the gates of the Church, namely the faith and works of their hearers, through which alone the Church is entered, from the contagion of heretics and of knocking vices, must first purify their mind and acts from every stain of errors.
13.23: **“BUT IN THOSE DAYS ALSO”** — In the Church they marry foreign wives who defile their conscience with the delights of crimes, which are properly the gentiles'; and the sons born of these cannot speak the Jews' language when the works which come forth from a vitiated mind show in themselves nothing of pious profession, but sound rather of gentile folly than of ecclesiastical chastity. For Azotus, which in Hebrew is called Esdod, [is interpreted] 'fire of words' or 'of breasts'. And therefore tropologically the sons of the foreign wives speak the speech of Azotus when the works begotten through wantonness await the vengeance of eternal burning. Hence rightly the begetters of such were not only rebuked and cursed by Nehemias, but some were also beaten; because it is necessary that those who err be more sharply restrained by the doctors of truth, that they may be carried over from the breast of the avenging fire to the breasts of divine praise. Heretics too, when they give their effort to the studies of gentile philosophy, dialectic and rhetoric more than to ecclesiastical simplicity, it is no wonder if their hearers speak according to the language of this people and that people, turning over the holy Scriptures with the mouth indeed, but interpreting them with gentile sense.
13.30: **“So I cleansed them from all strangers, and appointed the courses of the priests, and of the Levites, every man in his ministry:”** — SO I CLEANSED etc. BEDE. An end open in all things and worthy of the building of the holy city and the temple of the Lord: that, the citizens being cleansed of pollution foreign to God, the courses of the priests and Levites be duly kept in their ministry, that the masters of the Church, established according to rule, may ever exhort the people, cleansed from all sin, to remain and grow in good for the rest.
13.31:
**“AND FOR THE OFFERING OF THE WOOD”** — Among other things the people offer wood to feed the fire of the altar when they work works of the virtues worthy of divine consecration. The wood burns and is consumed on the altar of holocausts when the works of justice are perfected in the hearts of the elect by the flame of charity.
**“and for the firstfruits:”** — or: firstlings
**“REMEMBER ME”** — Rightly does such a founder and dedicator of the city, after many labours of devotion, commend himself to the memory of the Creator and Giver of all good things.
**“remember me, O my God, for good.”** — BEDE. "And thou, supreme Father of lights, from whom every best gift and every perfect gift comes down, who hast given to me, the most humble of thy servants, both the love and the help of considering the wonderful things of thy law, and who hast granted to me, unworthy, the grace not only of embracing the old things in the treasury of the prophetic volume, but also of finding new gifts under the veil of the old and bringing them forth for the use of my fellow servants: remember me, my God, for good."

1.12: **“And they roasted the Phase with fire as was fitting, and boiled the victims in emolis [so the edition] and in pots with good will.”** — Also in chapter 1, before the middle of it: and they roasted the phase with fire as was fitting, and boiled the victims in emolis [so the edition] and pots with good will, that is, willingly and cheerfully. But it seems that 'benevolentia' would better be said in the feminine gender, so that it is a manner of speaking. Hence another translation has: with a sweet odor.
1.23: **“And the works of Josias were set right in the sight of the Lord his God, in a heart full of fear”** — And the works of Josias were set right in the sight of the Lord his God in a heart full of metuentia, that is, reverence, so that it is of the feminine gender; hence another translation has: in a heart full of piety.
1.27: **“I am not sent by the Lord. For my war is upon the Euphrates. Make haste and go down.”** — What have I to do with thee, king of Juda? I am not sent by the Lord. [As if to say]: Thus [sent], but not against thee. Hence there follows: For my war is upon the Euphrates; making haste I go down. In 2 Paralipomenon 35 he has this more fully.
1.29: **“but he set battle against him in the plain of Macedam, and the princes came down to king Josias.”** — Also, d. He did not heed the word of the prophet from the mouth of the Lord, but set battle against him in the plain of Macedo. Another translation says that the prophet who says these things was Jeremias. For 'Macedo' some wrongly have 'Matedo' or 'Metedem'. Hence in Theodotius [so the edition] two false things are read, where it is said: 'The towns of Juda wept for the setting of Josue; the fountain and the tree detest the plains of Macedo.' There 'Josue' is wrongly put for 'Josias', and 'Macedonia' for 'Magedon'. And this is because students of grammar do not know the histories of the Bible.
1.36: **“And he fined the nation a hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.”** — Also, e. And he fined the nation a hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold. Another translation has: and ten talents of gold.
1.38: **“and Joachim bound the magistrates; and Zaracele his brother he seized and brought back into Egypt.”** — Also, e. And Joachim bound the magistrates; Zarachele his brother, seizing him, he brought back Egypto, that is, into Egypt. Hence another translation: But seizing Zacharias his brother he brought him into Egypt.
1.40: **“But after him came up Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and binding him in a bond of areolo [so the edition] he led him into Babylon”** — Also, e. And binding him in a bond of brass. This is the true reading, as appears in another translation.
1.43: **“And Joachim his son reigned in his stead. Now when he was appointed he was eight years old.”** — Also, f. Now when he was appointed he was eighteen years old. So it is corrected; and in 2 Paralipomenon 36, as in 4 Kings 24, it is said: of eighteen years.
1.46: **“And he appointed Sedecias king of Juda and Jerusalem, when he was one and twenty years old. And he reigned eleven years.”** — Also, f. Also, a little after: when he was one and twenty years old. Some wrongly have twenty-eight.
1.51: **“But they mocked his angels (messengers). And on the day the Lord spoke, on the same day they made sport of his prophets.”** — Also, g. But they scoffed in their corners [so the edition: 'angulis'], and on the day God spoke they were mocking his prophets. Another translation: But they mocked his angels.
1.52: **“Until [so the edition: 'Quiusque'] he was stirred to wrath against his nation for its irreligion, he commanded the kings of the Chaldeans to come up.”** — Also, g. For their irreligions. Otherwise: or for their impieties. Also, g. And he commanded the kings of the Chaldeans to come up. Another translation agrees with this reading.
1.54: **“But all were delivered into their hands, and all the holy vessels of the Lord and the royal storehouses they took up and carried into Babylon”** — Also: And all the holy vessels of the Lord and the royal storehouses they took up and carried into Babylon. Another translation inserts: and the ark; which does not seem true, as appears in 2 Machabees 2.

3.1: **“King Darius made a great supper for all his household servants and for all the magistrates of Media and Persia”** — So Pharao, Assuerus and Herod; on the contrary, Luke 14.

4.34: **“O men, are not women strong? Great is the earth, and high is the heaven, and swift is the course of the sun; it turns round the heaven in a circle to its place in one day.”** — Also, e. O men, why are not women stronger? What follows in certain [copies], Great is the earth and high is the heaven, which do these things, is superfluous in this place and does not pertain to the matter, since the same comes a little after, where moravit [so the edition] to speak of truth, [unclear in the edition: "ut alia translatio hec habet non sit"].
4.37: **“Wine is wicked, the king is wicked, women are wicked, all the sons of men are wicked, and their works are wicked, and there is no truth in them”** — The Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
4.39: **“With her there is no accepting of persons nor differences, but she does what is just to all, the unjust and the wicked, and all are dealt with kindly in her works.”** — Also, e. With her there is no accepting of persons nor differences, but she does what is just to all, the unjust and the wicked. Iniustis can be one word or two. Another translation: She departs from all the wicked and deceitful.
4.44: **“and to send back all the vessels that were taken out of Jerusalem, which Cyrus set apart when he slew Babylon, and willed to send them back thither.”** — Also, f. which Cyrus set apart when he mated Babylon. Some wrongly have mactavit, that is, slew, which is nothing to the point. For matare is here put for to discomfit: a word common among those who play at chess [so the edition: 'scoqos'] and dice, because each intends to mate the other. Another translation: after he laid waste Babylon, which is the same, but is not in use.

5.1: **“And after these things the chiefs of the districts were chosen to go up according to their houses and tribes, and their wives, and their sons and daughters, and their menservants and maidservants, and their cattle.”** — 5.a. And after these things the chiefs of the districts were picked to go up by their houses and by their tribes. Some have 'were chosen', which is the same.
5.6: **“who spoke wonderful words under Darius king of the Persians, in the second year of his reign, in the first month, Nisan.”** — Also, a. The priests, the sons of Phinees, son of Aaron: Jesus son of Iosebeth. Here is a raised point. There follows: Joachim son of Zorobabel, son of Salathiel, of the house of David, of the stock of Phares, of the tribe of Juda. And here is a raised point. Who, namely Zorobabel, spoke wonderful words under Darius king of the Persians in the second year of his reign, in the first month Nisan; supply: day. The sense is confused unless it is pointed so.
5.8: **“And [so the edition: 'reliquit'] part of Judea, every one into his own city, who came with Zorobabel and Jesus: Neemias, Areores, Elimeo, Emmanio, Mardocheo, Beelsuro, Mechpsacocor, Olioro, Roebo, one of their princes.”** — Also, a. And they returned into Jerusalem and the remaining part of Judea, every one into his city, who came with Zorobabel and Jesus. Here is a raised point, because all who follow in this verse are of the nominative case, but in the first [book] of Esdras they are ablatives. With this reading also the first chapter of Esdras agrees, and another translation, which says: and they returned into Jerusalem and into all the cities of Judea, etc.
5.9: **“the sons of Phares, two thousand one hundred seventy-two,”** — Also, b. And the number of them by their nations and of their governors; supply 'this is', as another translation has, which says: This is the number of the nation and of the princes of the Jews. Some wrongly have 'by their gentiles'. The names and numbers of all who follow in this place we do not set down, so that they may be better corrected by the more studious; for as in the Hebrew and in ancient and modern books Esdras and Nehemias cannot agree in names and numbers through the fault of scribes, so also here. Note however that from this place, 'the sons of Phares', as far as 'and of these the kindred was sought, written in the register', all the 'sons' are nominative plural. In this interval, however: 'but the porters', supply 'were', the sons of Esnomu, the sons of Azer, the sons of Amon, the sons of Acuba, the sons of Atita, the sons of Tobi, in all one hundred thirty-nine; here let there be a verse. The priests serving in the temple, supply 'were', the sons of Sel and the rest who follow as far as the sons of Pedon; here is a verse.
5.34: **“the sons of Aggia, the sons of Sachareth, the sons of Sabathen, the sons of Caroneth, the sons of Malsith, the sons of Ame, the sons of Sasus, the sons of Addus, the sons of Suba, the sons of Eura, the sons of Rahothis, the sons of Phasphat, the sons of Malmon.”** — Salomon: here is a small point, and it is put absolutely so that the following relative may have place. His sons, that is, his boys or servants, were those who follow, the sons of Asophos and the rest. Hence also in the following verse it is said: all serving the holy [place], namely the temple, and the boys of Salomon, four hundred eighty-two. Salomon here is of the genitive case.
5.36: **“These are the sons who went up from Chermel and Thersa; their chief, Carmellan and Careth”** — There follows: these are the sons who went up from Thelmela, Thelarsa, that is, from Babylon. Some wrongly have Athehnel and Thersas, as though these were two places or two words, as appears from the Hebrew in Esdras 2; and there some, as also here, wrongly thought that Dethel and Mela and Thel and Arsa are the names of four men who went up, whereas it is one word in the Interpretations.

Another translation adds: and those who do not know. Hence Esdras 7.g.: 'But teach the unlearned also freely.' There follows: that whoever shall have transgressed the law be diligently punished, whether by death or by torment, or also by a fine of money, or by banishment, that is, exile. Also in Esdras 7.g. it is said: 'Whoever will not do the law of thy God and the law of the king diligently'. And so this word, 'diligently', can be construed with what precedes or with what follows: so that whoever sins diligently, that is, knowingly, is diligently punished. 1.1:
**“TOBIAS OF”** — BEDE. The book of Tobias is wholesome on the surface of the letter, for it abounds in the greatest examples and admonitions of the moral life. But as much as fruit excels leaves, so much does the allegory excel the history; for it contains the greatest sacraments of the Church. For Tobias himself signifies the people of Israel, which, while the other nations were given to idolatry, served God with right faith and works. Hence: when all went to the golden calves, etc. For Jeroboam, who made golden calves for the deceiving of his subjects, expresses the worshippers of idolatry, whose accomplices are signified in his subjects.
**“Tobias”**
• good of the Lord
• he describes a person suited to the business
• among those carried away, of whom it is said: 'At the first time the land of Zabulon [and the tribe of Nephtali] was lightly touched.'
**“of the tribe and city of Nephtali”** — NEPHTALI: breadth, of which: 'Thy commandment is exceeding broad'; whose tribe, that is, sons, is the faithful people; its city, the Church, of which: 'A city seated on a mountain cannot be hid.'
**“beyond the way that leadeth to the west”** — for he leaves behind the broad way that leadeth to death
**“of Sephet”** — for Sephet is interpreted 'of letters'
1.2:
**“which is in the upper parts of Galilee”** — of the wheel
**“above Naasson”**
• surpassing the wheel of this world, seeking the things above, leaving the lower and more changeable things
• ABOVE NAASSON: Naasson, 'augury'; the city of this one augurs the things above, that is, contemplates heavenly things.
**“having on the left hand the city”** — he reckons the knowledge falsely so called to be left and false, and condemns worldly philosophy
**“when he was made captive in the days of Salmanasar”** — of the devil
**“king of the Assyrians”** — of the proud; for Assyrian is interpreted 'directing'
**“even in his captivity, he forsook not the way of truth,”** — WHEN HE WAS MADE CAPTIVE: the captivity of Tobias designates the captivity of the human race by the king of all the wicked, that is, the devil, who cast us down from the heavenly fatherland into the valley of this exile.
1.3:
**“but every day gave all he could get to his fellow captives”** — to the Jews
**“SO THAT ALL”** — So the people of Israel, through the doctors of the divine word, ministered alms not only to the unlearned hearers of its own nation but to the gentiles coming to Judaism. For whatever natural good it had which the captivating enemy did not take away, this it showed to its own for an example of virtue; and it offered a portion of saving knowledge, as a tithe of its substance, to the strangers, that is, the gentiles.
1.4:
**“And when he was younger”**
• or less
• in his own eyes; hence: 'The greater thou art, the more humble thyself in all things.'
**“YET NOTHING”** — Already he bore in his breast that saying of the Apostle: 'Do not become children in sense, but in malice be children.' This however is said according to those who walked in the commandments of the Lord without blame, according to that rule of Tyconius by which, as if treating of the same, sometimes because of the good we praise all, sometimes because of the wicked we blame all; which is the second rule.
1.5:
**“Moreover when all went”** — the nations
**“to the golden calves”** — idols gilded under the appearance of wisdom
**“which Jeroboam”** — the prince of idolatry; for the ten tribes which are called Israel worshipped idols under Jeroboam
**“king of Israel had made, he”** — the people of Israel
1.6:
**“alone fled the company of all,”** — according to that: 'Fly fornication'; for idolatry is fornication. Hence a converted gentile may put away a gentile wife, but not marry another.
**“And went to Jerusalem to the temple of the Lord, and there adored the Lord God”** — 'The Lord thy God shalt thou adore.'
**“of Israel, [offering] all his firstfruits”** — natural goods
**“ALL HIS FIRSTFRUITS”** — It seems to contradict [this] that the first tithing went to the uses of the Levites, the second to spending on necessaries when the temple was visited. But the tithes of the third year, which they were then accustomed to make, they granted to the poor. And therefore we say all that, or all the second [tithes], because he could not approach the temple for fear of the king's guards.
**“and ceremonies”** — or tithes
1.8:
**“so that in the third year to the proselytes”** — to the gentiles
**“and strangers he gave all his tithes”** — saving knowledge
**“These and such like things according to the law of God”** — from the beginning of the law
1.9:
**“But when he was a man, he took to wife Anna”** — the Synagogue, established by Moses his kinsman
**“of his own tribe”** — by confessing, by believing
**“and had by her”**
• Christ
• the firstborn
**“a son, whom he called after his own name”** — believing it was to be given him
**“BUT WHEN HE WAS”** — So the people of Israel, multiplied in Egypt, received the Synagogue instituted with the legal ceremonies through Moses. It begot a son of her, because it knew that Christ was to be born of its race; hence: 'A prophet [the Lord] shall raise up to you', etc. And: 'Of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne'; to whom it gave its own name by believing and confessing what the Father says of him: 'I will make him my firstborn', that is, the name of Israel itself; hence: 'Israel is my firstborn.'
**“and from his infancy he taught him to fear”** — as a son
**“God, and to abstain from all sin.”** — WHOM FROM HIS INFANCY HE TAUGHT TO FEAR GOD, namely by believing and confessing that he would never commit sin, but would fulfil the very spirit of the fear of the Lord.
1.10:
**“And when by the captivity”** — of the devil
**“he with his wife”**
• the religion of the Synagogue
• the faith of Christ
**“and his son was come to the city of Ninive”** — the world; for Ninive is interpreted 'beautiful', and the world is called cosmos in Greek from its adornment.
**“with all his tribe”** — the others being given to idolatry
1.11:
**“(when all ate of the meats of the Gentiles) he kept his soul”** — he was polluted not only not in body, but not even in mind
**“and never was defiled with their meats.”** — an exposition
1.12:
**“he was mindful of the Lord with all his heart”**
• the effect: reward
• as to Daniel with Nabuchodonosor, and to Joseph in the sight of Pharao
1.13:
**“And because”** — the cause: merit
**“God gave him”** — who is mindful of all that hope in him
**“IN THE SIGHT OF SALMANASAR”** — It does not contradict [this] that elsewhere Salmanasar is called also Sennacherib, for he had two names. Or generally all the kings of the Medes were so called, as [the kings] of Egypt pharaos.
**“And he gave him”** — as Nabuchodonosor to Jeremias
**“He therefore went to all”** — through the doctors who carefully went round the flock, the city; hence: 'The just regardeth the lives of his beasts.'
1.14:
**“And when he was come to Rages a city of the Medes, and of that with which he had been honoured by the king”** — of kings
**“had ten talents of silver”** — the decalogue of the divine word
**“and when amongst a great multitude of his kindred, Gabelus in want”** — Gabelus, according to his action and not according to the interpretation of his name, signifies the gentiles
**“he saw, who was one of his tribe”** — for we are all from one father, God the creator, made by God,
**“taking a note of his hand”** — on condition of restoring
**“he gave him the aforesaid sum of money”** — the divine law
**“AND WHEN”** — BEDE. So the people of God through the Seventy translators committed to the gentiles the knowledge of the divine law, which is contained in the decalogue, that it might free them from the famine of the word of God. It gave under a note of hand, that is, under condition of returning, since he was rich, or so that he who had given might ask it back. The gentiles received the word of God and practise it as if trading, even after the coming of Christ, when they seek the spiritual understanding. They return it to the lender when at the end of the world they receive the believing Jews, and commit to those who are to be saved the sacraments of Christ, and open the secrets of Scripture.
1.16: **“Tobias went among all his kindred, and comforted them”** — lest they should fail in captivity
1.17:
**“The hungry”** — in body as much as in mind
**“he fed, and clothes to the naked”** — of body as much as of mind
**“he gave, and to the dead”** — in sin
**“and to them that were slain”** — by the devil
**“CAREFUL TO BURY”** — [The burial] of sins, so that not even the memory [of them] should remain in them. With such burial our fathers wished to be honored, near the burial of Christ. Hence Jacob wished to be buried in Judea, and Joseph gave command concerning his bones.
1.18:
**“And when king Sennacherib was come back”** — the enemy of the people of God,
**“AND WHEN [HE] WAS COME BACK”** — Well does Sennacherib flee from Judea. For the devil dreads true confession and does not stand before its face.
**“fleeing from Judea”** — having lost certain members and left them in Judea
1.19:
**“But when”** — by the wicked
**“it was told the king”** — to the devil
**“he commanded him”** — by the ministers of his iniquity
**“to be slain, and took away all his substance”** — virtues.
**“BUT WHEN”** — The devil wished to destroy the people of God with spiritual death through idolatry, and to take away the sure riches of virtues, and was not able, because in it there were many saints who provided for its life and salvation. And he fled WITH HIS SON AND WIFE, because he forsook neither the faith of the Lord's incarnation nor the state of the Synagogue, which shone forth clearer than light in the struggles of the Machabees. The king having been slain by his sons, all things were restored to Tobias; because when the devil had been often overcome by his own crimes, which he begot as a most wicked offspring, prosperity returned to the people of God; and we see the state of the Church still fluctuating with these alternations.
1.20:
**“But Tobias with his son”** — the faith of Christ, who was to be born of the same people
**“and with his wife”** — the institution of the Synagogue
**“fleeing naked away, lay concealed, for many”** — holy doctors
1.21:
**“But after forty-five days the king was killed”** — the devil
**“by his own sons”** — a wicked, most evil offspring.
1.22:
**“And Tobias returned”** — the people of God
**“to his house”** — peace
**“and all his substance”** — of virtues or of temporal goods

2.1:
**“AFTER THIS”** — He who is in the light keeps holiday from vices; hence: 'The remainders of the thought shall keep holiday to thee.' And elsewhere: 'Be still and see that I am God.'
For we ought not to cast ourselves into dangers or to tempt God while we can act by reason. Hence: 'When they shall persecute you in one city, flee into another.' And elsewhere: 'But Jesus hid himself, and went out of the temple.' And Paul was let down in a basket by the wall. And Jesus was in Egypt and was there until the death of Herod.
**“But after this, there was a festival of the Lord, and a dinner was prepared”** — spiritual, by which the mind is refreshed, or bodily, by which the body is sustained in the service of God. For no man ever hated himself.
2.2:
**“he said to his son: Go, and bring some”** — He does not wish to eat his morsel alone; hence Job: 'If I have eaten my morsel alone.'
**“of our tribe”** — But especially to them who are of the household of the faith.
**“that fear God”**
• Not those who kill the body only.
• Spiritually as much as bodily. Hence: 'Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.'
• 'Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor.' He is truly poor who fears after the manner of sons. Hence: 'Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord.'
2.3: **“And when he had gone, returning he told him that one of the children of Israel lay slain in the street. And he forthwith leaped up from his place at the table, and left his dinner”** — Preferring the food of the soul to the food of the body.
2.5:
**“And when he had hid the body, he ate bread with mourning”**
• for his neighbor.
• 'My tears have been my bread day and night.'
**“and fear”**
• of the tyrant.
• Rendering to God the things that are God's, and to Caesar the things that are Caesar's.
2.7:
**“So when the sun was down”** — Because the sun of justice sets for the dead.
**“he went and buried him.”** — He shows [one] buried under the mass of sin.
2.8:
**“Now all his neighbours blamed him”** — friends in the flesh of the name, not of the man; enemies of the soul. 'For no plague is more effective for harm than an enemy of one's own household.'
**“But Tobias fearing God more”** — who 'can destroy both soul and body in hell.'
**“than the king”** — who [can kill] the body only
**“carried off”** — hastily, secretly.
**“the bodies of them that were slain, and hid them in his house”** — so that he neither ceased from the duty of humanity nor offended the king indiscreetly.
**“IT HAPPENED”** — BEDE. Let no one wonder if sometimes a good thing typically signifies evil, and evil things good. For if this were not allowed, the name of God would never be written with black ink but always with shining gold, because God is light. But if you write the name of the devil with a white stone, it nonetheless signifies darkness. Tobias blinded, therefore, signifies the people of Israel: 'For blindness in part has happened in Israel.' Wearied from burying, he was blinded. For he who persists unwearied in good works does not lose the light of faith. So spiritually he sleeps wearied who neglects to watch, to stand, to act manfully and to be strengthened, to whom it is said: 'Rise, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead', etc.
**“OUT OF A SWALLOW'S NEST”** — Swallows, because of their light flight, signify pride and levity, whose uncleanness blinds those over whom it rules. He sleeps placed under the swallow's nest who incautiously subjects himself to levity, wantonness and pride. This blindness prevailed most in the people of Israel when the coming of the Lord in the flesh was at hand, when it labored under the yoke of Roman servitude and violated the precepts of the divine law by living evilly.
**“For whereas he had always feared God from his infancy, and kept his commandments, he repined not against God”** — as is said of Job: 'In all these things Job sinned not with his lips.'
**“because the evil of blindness had befallen him”** — when he was tempted
**“BUT IMMOVEABLE”** — Because the judgment of God begins from the house of God; hence: 'Begin ye at my sanctuary.' He who is not corrected is not a son: 'He that spareth the rod hateth his son.' Paul is buffeted like a boy lest he be exalted like a youth.
**“in the fear of God”** — filial; hence: 'Fear the Lord, all ye his saints.'
**“continued, giving thanks to God”** — Job: 'Blessed be the name of the Lord. As it hath pleased the Lord, so is it done.'
**“all the days of his life.”** — The whole life of the just is day; hence: 'In the days of Elias.' 'Job died, being full of days.'
**“For as the kings insulted over holy Job”** — Baldach, Sophar and Eliphaz.
**“INSULTED”** — BEDE. There were in that people those who rashly insulted the miseries of the people, namely that it now lacked the ancient happiness of the fathers who likewise served God; whom the same people corrected through its doctors and elect, and turned itself to imploring the mercy of God for eternal life. Tobias, blind and preaching the word of God, signifies the reprobate and the elect, as Jacob wrestling with the angel was made lame and blessed: in the lameness signifying the unbelief of his nation, that is [so the edition], in the blessing its faith. But Tobias, a holy man, though rebuked again, does not cease from charity; hence: 'Charity is patient, is kind', etc.
**“so his relations and kinsmen”** — in the flesh
**“mocked at his life”** — All that will live godly in Christ suffer reproaches.
**“Where”** — Nowhere
**“is thy hope”** — the reward or profit of hope
**“for which thou gavest alms”** — as a hireling. For the wicked either serve God as slaves out of fear, or seek wages as hirelings; therefore they will never receive the beatitude which is God himself.
2.10:
**“For we are the children of saints”** — We ought to be holy, like our fathers
**“and that life”**
• the future [life] we seek; for it we are faithful
• not this one
**“we look for, which God will give”** — through grace; and the grace of God, life everlasting
**“to those”** — to those who persevere, not to those who begin. The last day of a man is always to be awaited. Hence: 'He that shall persevere unto the end, he shall be saved.'
2.11: **“Now Anna his wife went daily to weaving work, and of the labour of her hands”** — 'For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands: blessed art thou', etc., and 'If any man will not work, neither let him eat.'
2.13: **“And when her husband heard it bleating, he said: Take heed, lest perhaps it be stolen”** — The husband corrects the wife, reason sensuality.
2.14:
**“At these words his wife being angry answered: It is evident thy hope is come to nothing”** — Reason seeks things to come and invisible; our Eve the contrary.
**“and thy alms”** — the fruit of alms.
**“have now perished.”** — have appeared to have perished.

3.3:
**“And now, O Lord, think of me, and take not revenge”** — because I take it [on myself]
**“of my sins”** — in the future
**“neither remember my offences”** — as if: spare me; I do not spare [myself]
**“nor those of my parents.”** — or of my parents. God will render the sins of the fathers unto the third and fourth generation to them that hate him and are like their wicked fathers.
3.4:
**“For we have not obeyed”** — as we ought
**“thy commandments, and we are delivered”** — therefore by thee, the just judge
**“to spoil”** — the plunder of enemies
**“and to captivity”** — exile
**“and death”** — of body and soul
**“and are made a fable and a reproach to all nations”** — the gentiles
**“amongst which thou hast scattered”** — thou, not they
**“us.”** — sinners
3.5:
**“And now, O Lord, great”** — upon us
**“are thy judgments, because we have not done according to thy precepts, and have not walked”** — from virtue to virtue
**“sincerely before thee.”** — although before men
3.6:
**“And now, O Lord, according to thy will”**
• which surpasseth all understanding
• which is just in all things
**“thy”**
• as if: not my will but thine be done
• not mine
**“do with me”** — when the Egyptians pressed them, the children of Israel cry to the Lord
**“and command”** — the angels
**“in peace”** — in the bosom, in the rest of the soul, of Abraham, who is himself [her] father as [he is] also of the faith
**“my spirit to be received; for it is better for me to die than to live.”** — 'I desire to be dissolved and to be' with thee, lest the malice of the wicked change my heart.
3.7:
**“Now on the same day”** — on which Tobias prayed, she also prayed
**“BEDE”** — Sara signifies the multitude of the nations, all of whose doctors knew only the life of this world, which unrolls in seven days; the eternal things they knew not. Therefore they were seized by the devil, as if made over to idolatry, until Christ came, the true bridegroom, who espoused her to himself in faith when the enemy was overcome, as [here] the devil was bound by the presence and cooperation of the angel; in whom the divinity of the Saviour is signified, as his humanity in Tobias. Nor is it to be wondered at that we say two persons, namely of an angel and of a man, figure the one person of Christ, because in the expositions of the fathers we read that his one person is figured in Isaac and in the ram: who in his humanity is slain like a sheep, in his divinity remains impassible with the Father, like Isaac, when he returns home unharmed with Abraham. For if the ram signifies the humanity of Christ and a man the divinity, why not more fitly a man the humanity, an angel the deity?
**“it happened that Sara”** — For we ought to pray in the upper part of our mind. Hence Christ prays on the mountain, Daniel in the upper room; and Eliseus has upper rooms, and Christ celebrates the Pasch in the upper room.
3.8: **“because she had been given to seven husbands, and a devil named Asmodeus”** — deserter; the proper name of the demon.
3.10:
**“Wilt thou kill me also, as thou hast already killed seven husbands? At these words she went into an upper chamber of her house”**
• of her mind; and for three days and three nights
• for in prosperity and in adversity we ought to direct our prayers to the holy Trinity
**“did neither eat nor drink,”** — she grows fat with prayer alone, which the leanness of the body feeds
**“but in prayer”** — prayer softens God, a tear compels him; the one anoints, the other pricks
**“continuing with tears besought the Lord that from this reproach”** — of unbelief
**“he would deliver her.”** — by the coming of the Son
3.11:
**“And it came to pass on the third day, WHEN SHE WAS MAKING AN END of her prayer, blessing the Lord,”**
• we are filled with the light of the holy Trinity so that we may complete our prayer
• WHEN SHE COMPLETED her prayer. The name of fulness is usually taken in a good sense; hence: 'When the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son', etc. And: 'The days of the purification of Mary were accomplished.' And of Moses: 'He completed it even to the end.'
**“she said: Blessed is thy name, O God”** — not recent
**“of our fathers”** — whom we ought to imitate, by whose merits we are helped
**“who when thou hast been angry”** — likewise, when thou art angry, thou wilt remember mercy
**“wilt shew mercy, and in the time of tribulation forgivest the sins”** — God does not forgive sins except in tribulation and contrition of heart; hence: 'A contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.'
**“to those”** — not others
**“that call upon”** — with mouth, heart and work
**“thee.”** — nothing other than thee
3.12:
**“To thee, O Lord,”** — not to idols, not to my merits
**“face”** — of the mind, which pleases thee alone
**“I turn my”** — because I have found my heart to pray to thee
**“to thee my eyes”** — the inner [eyes], of which it is said: 'Lift up thy eyes and see.' And elsewhere: 'Thy eyes are doves' eyes.'
3.14:
**“Thou knowest”** — that
**“O Lord, that I never coveted a husband”** — I would not know 'the bed in sin'
**“and have kept my soul clean from all lust.”** — of the flesh
3.15:
**“Never with them that play”** — because laughter shall be mingled with sorrow
**“have I joined myself, neither with them that in lightness”** — of mind
**“walk”** — from vice to vice
**“have I made myself partaker.”** — I did not consent
**“A husband”** — that I might bear fruit to thee
**“but with thy fear,”** — fearing the curse of barrenness
**“not with my lust,”** — of the flesh
**“And either I was unworthy of them,”** — let us define nothing rashly that is doubtful to us; let us reserve it for God to define
**“or they perhaps were not worthy of me, because perhaps for another man”** — which is true
**“thou hast kept me.”** — untouched
**“For not in man's power is”** — as if: I know not which of these, but thou knowest
**“thy counsel”** — Hence: 'Who hath been his counsellor?'
**“But this every one is sure of that worshippeth thee, that his life, if it be under trial,”** — shall have persevered
**“shall be crowned;”** — 'He that striveth lawfully shall be crowned', and 'He that shall persevere shall be saved.'
**“and if it be under tribulation, it shall be delivered;”** — by thee, lest it fail
**“and if it be under correction, to thy mercy”** — For thou correctest mercifully, who scourgest every son whom thou receivest.
**“For thou art not delighted”** — Thou who hast created wilt not destroy.
**“in the losing”** — tribulations
**“of us”** — which [comes] from us
**“because after a storm”** — of body or of mind
**“a calm”** — of both; hence: 'After darkness I hope for light.'
**“thou makest, and after tears and weeping,”** — 'Blessed are they that mourn, for they shall be comforted.'
**“Be thy name, O God,”** — to whom we owe all things
**“blessed for ever.”** — without end
3.16:
**“At that time were heard”** — fulfilled
**“the prayers of them both”** — of Tobias and Sara
**“in the sight”** — in good pleasure
3.17:
The just is first accuser of himself. He who hides his wounds nourishes [them]. Let us also, in all that we suffer, feel that God is just and merciful; hence: 'Mercy and judgment I will sing to thee, O Lord.'
**“And the angel of the Lord WAS SENT,”** — Christ
**“the holy Raphael”** — the medicine of God
**“WAS SENT”** — BEDE. Raphael, the medicine of God: the Lord was sent into the world, who says of himself: 'They that are well have no need of a physician, but they that are sick'; who would free both the Jewish people from the darkness of unbelief and the gentile from the servitude of idolatry; of whom vocabit [so the edition] 'the angel of great counsel'.

4.2:
**“And said to him: Hear, my son,”** — Hear, thou who oughtest to imitate me.
**“the words of my mouth, and [lay] them in thy heart”** — by understanding
**“as a foundation”** — of religion
4.3:
**“When God shall take my soul,”** — 'No man ever hated his own flesh.'
**“BURY MY BODY”** — By burying bodies we commit to the earth, as it were, a most sacred deposit, which we believe will be rendered back and glorified in the resurrection.
**“and thou shalt honour thy mother”** — 'Honour thy father and thy mother', etc. And 'He that curseth his father or mother, dying let him die.'
4.4:
**“For thou must be mindful”** — as if: lest thou be ungrateful for thy mother's labors; render thyself to her who with pain gave thee [birth].
**“And when she also shall have ended”** — in good
**“the time of her life, thou shalt bury her”** — The saints live together and are buried together, whose faith in life is the same and whose rest in death is the same.
4.5:
**“And all the days of thy life”** — He does not say 'nights', because the whole life of the just is day.
**“have God in thy mind”**
• or 'the Lord': the charity of God, hope, faith; and take heed lest thou ever consent to sin,
• I will not say 'do it'
• which is to cherish [it], or to be silent when thou canst reprove
4.7:
**“Out of thy substance”** — not from plunder
**“give alms,”** — mercy, which is first in the mind before it is in the work; hence: 'who sheweth mercy and lendeth'.
**“and turn not away”** — give to every one that asketh thee
**“thy face”** — hence: 'visiting thy beauty thou shalt not sin'
**“from any poor person.”** — For thou oughtest to love thy neighbor.
**“For so it shall come to pass”**
• judgment without mercy shall be to him that hath not done mercy: 'Give, and it shall be given to you.'
• 'For blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.'
4.8:
**“According to thy ability”** — according to thy means, not with sadness or of necessity. 'For God loveth a cheerful giver.'
**“If thou have much, give abundantly; if thou have little, take care even so to bestow willingly a little.”** — The will is weighed by God, not the quantity of the gift.
4.9:
**“For thou storest up to thyself a good reward”** — hence: 'Lay up to yourselves treasures in heaven'
**“for the day of necessity”** — of judgment, where no one will suffice if mercy fails,
4.10:
**“for alms”** — hence: 'Shut up alms in the bosom of the poor.'
**“from all sin and from death”** — eternal
**“deliver”** — 'The ransom of a man's life are his riches.' And elsewhere: 'Redeem thou thy sins with alms.' Also: 'As water quencheth fire, so alms quencheth sin.'
**“and will not suffer the soul to go into darkness”** — of hell
4.11: **“Alms shall be a great confidence before the most high God”** — although not before men
4.12:
**“Take heed”** — beware
**“to keep thyself, my son, from all fornication”**
• of mind and of body
• an exposition
**“and beside thy wife never endure a crime”** — of lust
**“to know”** — much less to do it
4.13:
**“Pride”** — 'Let not the foot of pride come to me.' 'Pride is the beginning of all sin.'
**“never in thy mind”** — mind
**“or in thy words”** — much less in deed
**“suffer to reign”** — and if at some time it be [there], let it not reign
**“For from it”** — there 'all they that work iniquity' fell.
**“all perdition took its beginning”** — of mind or of body, of man or of angel
4.14:
**“If any man”** — 'Let not the foot of pride come to me.'
**“hath done any work for thee,”** — 'The wages of him that hath been hired by thee shall not abide with thee until the morning.' Let not him who has earned by working have to earn [it] by waiting.
4.15: **“What”** — 'What thou wouldst not have done to thee, do not to another.'
4.16:
**“Thy bread”** — 'Deal thy bread to the hungry.'
**“with the hungry”**
• 'Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor.'
• Give alms, that by works of mercy even the sins of the unjust may be buried. 'For in many things we all offend.' Hence: Ob [so the edition]: 'I have not eaten my morsel alone.'
**“and the needy”** — who cannot repay
**“eat, and with thy garments”**
• not from plunder
• 'When thou shalt see one naked, cover him.'
**“the naked”** — who are in need
4.17:
**“Thy bread”** — of the Word of God
**“and thy wine”** — which 'cheereth the heart of man'.
**“upon the burial of a just man”** — there is no man who lives and sins not
**“lay out, and do not of it”** — 'Neither cast ye your pearls before swine, and give not that which is holy to dogs.'
**“eat”** — Thou shalt not feast with sinners, because manners are shaped by living together.
**“and drink with the wicked.”** — give not to the ungodly
4.18:
**“Counsel”** — Do all things with counsel
**“seek always of a wise man.”** — Not from a fool, in whom there is no wisdom
4.19:
**“At all times”** — 'He that shall persevere unto the end shall be saved.'
**“bless”** — with thoughts, words, works
**“God, and desire of him that thy ways”** — actions, thoughts
**“he may direct”** — to himself
**“and that all thy counsels in him”** — not in the world
**“may abide”** — firmly
4.21:
**“Fear not, my son. We lead indeed a poor life”** — in this world
**“but we shall have many good things”**
• in the future
• blessed is he that feareth the Lord
**“if we fear God”** — The fear of the Lord is to depart from evil or from sin; hence: 'Fear God and depart from evil.'
**“and depart from all sin”** — 'Decline from evil.'
**“and do that which is good.”** — 'And do good.'

5.1: **“Then Tobias answered his father, and said: All things thou hast commanded me.”** — An example is given us that we should obey holy fathers; hence: 'Honour thy father and mother.'
5.5: **“But he answered: Of the children of Israel.”** — Of the children of Israel. For he was of the number of the angels who are the sons of Israel, because they always see God face to face and are often sent for the guarding of the sons of Israel, that is, of those who see God; hence: 'I appointed the bounds of people according to the number of the children of Israel.'
5.6:
**“And he answered: I know it, and I have often walked through all the ways thereof, and I have abode”** — For angels abide with the saints.
**“with Gabelus our brother”** — For the good shall be equal to the angels, and co-heirs and fellow-citizens [with them].
**“who dwelleth at Rages of the Medes, which is situate in the mount of Ecbatana.”** — The city of the saints is set on a mountain, that of sinners in a valley.
5.7:
**“And Tobias said to him: Stay for me, I beseech thee, till I tell these same things to my father.”** — He resolved that nothing should be done without his father's counsel.
**“Then Tobias going in told all these things to his father. Upon which his father being in admiration”** — because what he wished came to meet him quickly, or because suddenly.
**“THEN TOBIAS GOING IN”** — BEDE. The angel appeared to Tobias and offered himself as his companion; and the Son of God assumed man and, conversing visibly with men, saved the human race. Tobias brought the angel in to his father, etc.; and the Lord, through the miracles which he did in the flesh, showed the people of the Jews, from whom he had taken flesh, that he is the son and the angel, that is, the messenger, of the Father's will; to whom also he preached the joy of everlasting salvation, saying: 'Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.' And to those despairing of the heavenly light: 'I am,' he says, 'the light of the world. He that followeth me walketh not in darkness.'
**“And Tobias said:”** — the people of the Jews
5.8: **“And the young man said to him: Be of good courage; thy cure from God is at hand.”** — 'For the kingdom of heaven will draw near.'
5.10: **“AND THE ANGEL SAID TO HIM”** — BEDE. The angel promises Tobias to lead his son into the city of the Medes and to bring him back. Christ promises the believing Jews, although most are blinded, that he will open the sacraments of his incarnation to the gentiles, and at the end of times will disclose them more widely to the people of the Jews, the faith of his divinity accompanying and cooperating. Led to the Medes, he says: 'Other sheep I have that are not of this fold.' Of the bringing back the Apostle says: 'Until the fulness of the gentiles should come in, and so all Israel should be saved.' When Tobias asked the angel whence he was, 'I am,' he said, 'Azarias, the son of the great Ananias.' Azarias is 'helper', Ananias 'glory of God'; Christ also shows his faithful that he himself is the one of whom it is said: 'Thou art my helper and my deliverer: O Lord, make no delay.' And: 'We saw his glory, the glory as it were of the only begotten of the Father.'
5.16:
**“And when all things were ready that were to be carried in their journey,”** — necessaries
**“AND WHEN [ALL THINGS] WERE READY”** — BEDE. When the Lord appeared in the flesh, all things were made ready that were necessary for our redemption, and by which the faith and life of the Church may be nourished and strengthened until the way of this world is ended: that is, his miracles, doctrine, temptation, passion, resurrection, ascension, the sending of the Holy Spirit, the faith of believers, the persecution of unbelievers. These being accomplished in Judea, the mediator of God and men preached through the apostles to the Jews his kinsmen and to the gentiles the joys of heavenly salvation and peace, and gave them by himself to those who were willing to receive and believe; and so he came through the apostles to the salvation of the gentiles.
5.17: **“And when they were departed, his mother began to weep and to say: The staff of our old age”** — a woman's impatience, a mother's affection
5.20: **“And Tobias said to her:”** — He trusts in the Lord, who committed him.

6.1:
**“WENT FORWARD”** — BEDE. When the Lord came to save the gentiles, the preachers followed his footsteps, because they fulfilled what he commanded; hence: Going, teach ye all nations, etc. The house of Cornelius also God himself first filled by himself with the Holy Spirit, and so Peter poured water over it. The preachers are called dogs because they defend the house of God and his substance, and the spiritual sheep, from thieves and beastly spirits and heretics.
**“and the dog”** — the preachers; hence: 'They shall suffer hunger like dogs, and shall go round about the city.'
**“HE LODGED”** — BEDE. The sacrament of the Lord's passion is plainly signified. For the fish which, desiring to devour Tobias, was killed at the angel's teaching, signifies the devil, who, while he sought the flesh in our Redeemer, was caught by the power of the divinity.
