The Tigris is a river which from its most rapid course is so named from the tiger, a most swift beast; it signifies the downward course of our mortality, in which the monstrous fish lay hid when the devil, the invisible seducer of the human race, held the empire of death. Tobias lodged by the streams of the Tigris because the Lord, appearing to the world, led his life among mortals; but the wave of sin did not flood him, nor did the prince of the world, coming, have anything in him.
**“by the river of Tigris.”** — the downward course of mortality
6.2: **“HE WENT OUT”** — BEDE. Christ accepted death, to which he owed nothing, that he might wash his feet, namely his members, from the contagion of sin and death. The fish ran at him desiring to devour him; and when the Lord suffered on the cross, the devil, at whose prompting he had been crucified, came, seeking whether he might find any sin in him.
6.3:
**“AND BEING AFRAID OF HIM”** — Christ, when the moment of death was at hand, began to fear and to be heavy, not at the devil but at death, which by the envy of the devil entered into the world, shuddering at it from the natural frailty of the flesh; hence: Father, remove this chalice from me.
**“TAKE”** — Christ seized the devil, who wished to take him on the cross, and by dying conquered him. He seized therefore the gill, that with the right hand of his power he might separate the most wicked head from the body; that is, that he might take away the wickedness of the ancient enemy from those whom he had made his body, and bring these into his own body, that is, the Church. For the fish has its gill at the border of the head and the body. And Christ is the head of the Church, which is his body, and the devil the head of the wicked, who are his body.
**“and draw him to thee.”** — The Lord, crushing the powers of the devil, exposed them confidently, [so the edition: 'paulum'] rescuing from the power of darkness those whom he foreknew and predestined as children of light
**“AND WHEN HE HAD DONE SO”** — Because when the Lord made manifest the wickedness of the devil, he strove still to stir up persecution against his elect. For these are HIS FEET, through which he who reigns over all in heaven walks on the earth.
6.4:
**“TAKE OUT THE ENTRAILS OF THIS FISH”** — BEDE. The Lord took out the entrails of the fish when he disclosed more widely to the saints the wickedness of the devil and, as it were, laid open the secrets of his snares. He laid up his heart for himself because he made known his craftiness in the Scriptures, of which it is said: 'The serpent was more subtle than any of the beasts of the earth.' And elsewhere: 'Are we ignorant of his devices?' He laid up the gall also, because he willed it to be written and kept, for the study of caution, with how great fury of malice he rages against the human race. He laid up the liver, because through the doctors of truth he made known his malignant counsels against us. For the physicians say that by the heat and hidden power of the liver foods are cooked and digested. And when with careful thought we search out in what order the things we plan to do are to be done, we as it were cook with the heat of the liver the foods received in the stomach.
**“FOR THESE ARE NECESSARY”** — The craft and wickedness of the devil, when known to us, profit us for healing. For the more surely we search them out, the more surely we avoid them.
6.5:
**“And when he had done so, he roasted the flesh thereof, and they took it with them in the way; the rest they salted,”** — with the salt of wisdom
**“as much as might serve them,”** — that is, the apostles, of whom it is said: 'You are the salt of the earth.'
**“till they came”** — Tobias and the angel, man and God
**“HE ROASTED THE FLESH”** — Whatever he took for himself from this fish signifies those who, having heard the word of God, prefer to remain among the rotten and dead members of their deceiver rather than to come into the body of Christ. He roasted the flesh, because those whom he found carnal he made spiritual and stronger by the fire of the Holy Spirit, who descended upon the apostles in the appearance of fire.
**“to Rages the city of the Medes.”** — The Lord gathered to the faith from Judea as many as would suffice for an example of living or for the ministry of preaching, until the foundations of the Church should be laid among the gentiles.
6.7:
**“Then the angel answering said to him: A little piece of its heart,”** — the craft of the heart understood and burned with the ardor of the spirit
**“if thou put it upon coals, the smoke thereof driveth away”** — puts to flight
**“all kind of devils, either from man”** — strong
**“or from woman,”** — weak
6.11:
**“All her substance is due to thee”** — The Father to the Son: 'Ask of me, and I will give thee.'
**“IT BEHOVETH”** — BEDE. Raguel signifies the people of the gentiles, which the Lord deigned to visit through his preachers and from its stock to take to himself a bride, the Church; which is well signified by Sara, namesake of the wife of Abraham, who bore Isaac, the son of promise, that is, the free people of the Church. Raguel is interpreted 'God his pasture' or 'friend': namely one who can say, 'The Lord ruleth me, and I shall want nothing', and who is worthy to hear, 'I will not now call you servants, but my friends.'
6.16: **“And the second night”** — not carnally, lest it contradict what he will say below, 'virgin'
6.17:
**“And the third night, a blessing”** — Perhaps blessings had been appointed for this, to be said either by a priest or by others.
**“thou shalt obtain, that”** — afterwards
**“And when the third night is past,”** — because carnal union had not yet taken place

7.1:
**“And they went in”** — the doctors of the word
**“to Raguel”** — the gentile people, to whom the Lord abiit [so the edition] through the doctors
**“and he received them”** — 'A people which I knew not hath served me: at the hearing of the ear they have obeyed me.'
7.3: **“And when he had said this, he said: Whence are ye, young men our brethren? And they said: We are of the tribe of Nephtali, of the captivity of Ninive”** — namely of those whom the Ninivites had taken captive
7.10:
**“Which word when Raguel heard”** — the gentile people
**“he was afraid, knowing what had happened to those seven husbands”** — all the doctors
**“WHICH WHEN HE HEARD”** — BEDE. The people of the gentiles, hearing the word of faith and admonished by the apostles to give Christ a wife from its stock, could not take up the laws of the new faith without sure examination, because it had once had many doctors who, all comprehended as it were in the number seven, knew this life only and said nothing certain of the eternal; and therefore, without hope of immortal life, the destruction of eternal death carried them off. But with the truth teaching within and sounding without through the mouths of the doctors, at length it understood that it is just that those who spoke foolish things should perish foolishly.
7.11:
**“the angel said to him: Be not afraid to give her to this man”** — to Christ
**“for to him who feareth”** — not to another
**“God is thy daughter due to be his wife. Therefore another”** — who did not teach rightly
7.12:
**“Then Raguel said:”** — confirmed in faith
**“And I believe he hath therefore made you come to me, that this maid might be married to one of her own kindred, according to the law of Moses.”** — foretelling: The Lord will raise up a prophet to you from among your brethren.
7.13:
**“And taking”** — For God works in us that we may work.
**“the right hand of his daughter,”** — of the Church
**“he gave it into the right hand of Tobias, saying: The God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob”** — of all the faithful, who are signified by these fathers
**“THE GOD OF ABRAHAM”** — BEDE. As in baptism we renounce the devil and all his works, and confess that we believe in the Father and in the Son and in the Holy Spirit, and receive the symbol of our faith as a charter.

8.1: **“AND AFTER THEY HAD SUPPED”** — BEDE. Tobias, being brought into the chamber, took out of, etc. God, about to receive the Church from the gentiles, at the beginning of the espousal commands her to renounce the devil and all his pomps, and to confess the faith of the holy Trinity unto the remission of sins; which is to burn the inmost entrails of the fish on live coals.
8.2: **“And Tobias remembering the angel's words, took out of his bag part of the liver, and laid it upon burning coals.”** — the Holy Spirit; of which it is said: 'Thou hast coals of fire, thou shalt sit upon them; these shall be a help to thee'; and elsewhere: 'Thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head.'
8.3:
**“RAPHAEL”** — BEDE. Because after the renunciation of the devil, after the confession of the true faith, there follows the remission of sins through the water of baptism, the devil having been driven out. He bound the devil because he restrained him so that he ceased from harming the faithful; whom, although he is sometimes permitted to tempt them for their proving, he is nevertheless forbidden to overcome.
**“BOUND HIM IN THE DESERT”** — The desert and Egypt signify the hearts of unbelievers, which are deserted by God because they are unworthy of his dwelling, and, according to the interpretation of Egypt, darkened with the darkness of their unbelief. And fittingly he who is deserted by God is filled by a demon. And the angel bound in the desert the demon who wished to kill Tobias: he who, having restrained the devil from the faithful, who are the members of Christ, permits him to rule only in unbelievers; in whom nevertheless he holds him bound, because he is not permitted to harm even them as much as he strives.
8.5: **“And Tobias said: Lord God of our fathers, may the heavens bless thee”** — either mystically or according to the letter.
8.9:
**“And it came to pass about the cockcrowing”** — of the preachers.
**“AND IT CAME TO PASS”** — The crowing of the cocks is the sound of the preachers, who after the darkness of errors announce the day of light to come. There were among the gentiles those who doubted whether the Lord had truly conquered the ancient enemy, and therefore thought it better to bury and hide the faith of his name; but afterwards, having recognized the light of truth, as with the dawn going before and the crowing of the cocks growing frequent, that is, by the voice of the preachers, they knew truly that Christ, the enemy being overcome, is the bridegroom of holy Church.
8.15: **“WE BLESS THEE, O LORD”** — BEDE. Raguel rejoices at the life of Tobias and the union of his daughter, and blessing God he kills two kine and four rams. He prepares a feast for all his friends and neighbors. The people of the gentiles rejoices at the faith of Christ and at the devotion of its nation advancing in the faith of the Lord, so that from among them also doctors should arise who afterwards would become martyrs. These are kine, because they bore the yoke of the gospel and by preaching begot others who would bear it. They are rams, as being leaders and fathers of the peoples; hence: 'Bring to the Lord the offspring of rams.' They are fat, filled with the grace of heavenly love; hence: 'Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness.'
8.20:
**“AND TWO FAT KINE”** — TWO KINE also. BEDE. The Apostle of the gentiles taught those who had come to the faith from its stock to be such that the envious enemy would tempt them for the excellence of their virtue, and having tempted them would not conquer them, but would make them victors and martyrs. He also caused to be killed those whom he taught to crucify their flesh for Christ with its vices and concupiscences. By their killing he prepared a feast, because the life, progress, passion and crown of the saints give gladness to many, who receive a feast from those by whose examples they are refreshed.
**“FOUR RAMS”** — Because the holy doctors and martyrs keep the four books of the gospel in faith and work; they are fortified with prudence, justice, fortitude and temperance; and they instruct the Church of God in the four parts of the world.
**“HE CAUSED TO BE KILLED”** — Because some of their own accord mortify their bodies that they may be a living sacrifice; others undergo martyrdom at the hands of unbelievers, conquering the ancient enemy by the armour of justice on the right hand and on the left, that is, in prosperity and in adversity.
**“AND HE ADJURED”** — BEDE. We adjure Christ to remain with us until through the grace of the Holy Spirit we obtain the perfection of rest, in which we may rest both from sins in the body and from wicked thoughts in the mind.
8.21: **“And of all things which Raguel possessed, one half”** — Hence Zacheus: 'The half of my goods I give to the poor.'

9.1:
**“Then Tobias called”** — the faithful, who are the members of Christ
**“the angel to him, whom a man”** — at first
**“he took to be,”** — only
9.2:
**“If I should give myself to be thy servant, I should not make a worthy return for thy care.”**
• I should not render thee a worthy reward
• 'The sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the glory to come', etc.
**“However, I beseech thee to take with thee beasts or servants, and to go to Gabelus to Rages the city of the Medes, and to restore to him his note of hand, and receive of him the money, and desire him to come to my wedding.”**
• of Christ and the Church, at which Christ makes new wine from water, that is, shows the spiritual understanding in the law.
• A new people is gathered daily in the Church. It can however be understood specially of those who received the letter of the law through the Seventy translators, and therefore received the faith more quickly.
**“HOWEVER, I BESEECH THEE”** — ISIDORE. Some of the believers serving thee, to whom thou mayest commit the office of preaching for gathering the nations, which have not yet received the mystery of faith but have nevertheless heard the report; and let them render, through the obedience of faith, the talent of the word which they learned by report.
9.5:
**“Then Raphael took four of Raguel's servants”**
• for the squareness of the soul, or the stability of the four virtues
• preachers from the gentiles, through whom others are gathered
• of those to whom he preached; hence the Apostle: 'I made myself the servant of all.'
**“and two camels,”** — who, subject in charity, carry the burdens of a brother's infirmity; such, with Raphael helping, lead Gabelus to the wedding of Tobias, when with Christ's aid preachers lead new peoples to the unity of the Church.
**“and went to Rages the city of the Medes; and finding Gabelus, gave him his note of hand, and received all the money.”** — the obedience of faith
9.6:
**“And he told him concerning Tobias”** — Christ
**“the son of Tobias all that had been done, and made him come with him to the wedding.”** — of Christ [and] the Church
**“And when he was come into Raguel's house he found Tobias”** — Christ feasting with the Church
**“sitting at the table; and leaping up they kissed each other.”**
• hence: 'Let him kiss me with the kiss of his mouth.'
• The faithful from the gentiles run to meet Christ; Christ runs to meet them, without whom we can do nothing.
**“And he wept”** — for joy
**“and may you see your children, and your children's children, unto the third and fourth generation, and may your seed be blessed”** — carnal, or works, or imitators

10.1:
**“But as he made longer stay”** — in the Church of the gentiles
**“Tobias”** — Christ
**“upon occasion of the marriage, his father was solicitous”** — those of the Jews who believe one by one grieve that Christ is slow to return to the remnant of Israel
10.5: **“Then his mother wept with tears past remedy, and said: Woe is me, my son; why did we send thee to go to a strange country, the light of our eyes,”** — the comfort of our life, the hope of our posterity
10.6:
**“And Tobias said to her:”** — BEDE. Tobias by his blindness designates the unbelievers, by his faith the faithful.
**“VERY TRUSTY”** — Namely those of the Jews who believe console themselves and their own, believing that the Lord will return to them and all Israel be saved. For God is faithful, who promised this.
10.8: **“BUT RAGUEL”** — When the fulness of the gentiles has come in, no one can prevent the Lord from granting salvation to Israel and regarding its blindness, which has happened in part. For the divine clemency has remembered that there is great sadness and continual sorrow to the believing Jews for their unbelieving brethren.
10.10: **“HE GAVE”** — At the end the doctors of the Church are sent back to Christ, together with the Church herself, full of the riches of virtues, to enlighten in faith and to enrich with the substance of good works the nation of the Jews, from which the Son of God took flesh.

11.3: **“LET US GO BEFORE”** — After the people of the gentiles has been enlightened, divine grace goes before to enlighten the blindness of the Jews, that in their books they may know Christ, true man and true God; and so at length, as having seen the angel and their son whom they had long not seen, they may greatly rejoice; that is, at length they may join themselves by communion of the mysteries to the Church gathered from the gentiles.
11.9:
**“Then the dog ran before”**
• because he foretells the gift of salvation, and so the Lord enlightens hearts
• the doctors of the Church, who drive heretics like wolves from the fold of the chief shepherd
**“which had been with them in the way, and coming as if he had brought the news, shewed his joy by the fawning of his tail.”** — The tail, the end of the body, signifies perfection, or the reward which is given at the end.
**“BY THE FAWNING”** — BEDE. The dog rejoiced as he saw again the long-unseen roofs of his masters. The doctors rejoice at the effect of their work, when they understand that Judea is to be gathered again by the Lord. They rejoice at the reward of eternal life, and foretell to all the elect that their hearts are to be gladdened with the same reward, and at once declare the grace of the Holy Spirit that is to come.
11.10:
**“And his father that was blind, rising up, began to run, stumbling with his feet; and giving his hand”** — by assent
**“to a servant,”** — to him who has known the light of truth
**“went to meet his son.”** — Christ
**“THE BLIND [FATHER] RISING UP”** — BEDE. Having heard the word of salvation from the doctors, the people of the Jews rises from the long blindness of its unbelief and runs with love to the Lord, but stumbling in the steps of its works, until, reborn and instructed in Christ, it receives the light of faith and of working.
11.11:
**“And receiving him he kissed him, as did also his wife, and they began to weep”** — because late
**“for joy.”** — because they believe in Christ
**“THEN TAKING”** — BEDE. The Lord openly reveals to believers how great is the malice of the ancient enemy, who longed to devour him in his passion, but being slain thereby lost his members, that is, those whom he formerly held.
11.12:
**“And he stayed about half an hour”** — The people of the Jews, after it has known the most bitter malice of the ancient enemy, recovered the light it had lost.
**“and a white skin began to come out of his eyes, like the skin of an egg.”**
• BEDE. In which hope is signified, because it does not yet live and is without soul, but is hoped for. 'But if we hope for that which we see not, we wait for it with patience.' The gospel parable also, under the name of bread and of wine [so the edition] and of an egg, expresses the three highest virtues, namely charity, faith and hope.
• WHITE SKIN etc. BEDE. The white skin designates the folly of a people pleasing itself, having a zeal of God but not according to knowledge, of whom it is said: 'Seeking to establish their own justice, they have not submitted themselves to the justice of God.' For the black pupil sees, the white is dark; and those who seem wise to themselves and say, 'Are we also blind?', in them the truth is not. But those who, conscious of frailty and ignorance, say, 'O Lord my God, enlighten my darkness', are enlightened by the Lord.
**“A WHITE SKIN OUT OF HIS EYES”** — BEDE. The people of the Jews still has a veil before the face of its heart, so that it does not understand the grace of Christ. It has a white skin, because it seems to itself white and just; like the skin of an egg, because it bears blindness of mind under the most foolish hope of a Christ still to be born, who will free the Jews and give them a great empire. But when the veil shall be taken away, they will acknowledge that Christ has already come and redeemed the world with his blood. Hence there follows that, having received sight, Tobias with his wife glorified God.
11.16:
**“And after seven days Sara his son's wife arrived, and all the family, and the flocks safe”** — BEDE. the various persons of the faithful
**“and the camels, and much money of the wife's”** — BEDE. the virtues of the Church.
**“and that money also”** — BEDE. the holy [money] of the Scriptures, which Judea had committed to the gentiles.
**“SHE WENT OUT [so the edition]”** — It signifies the light of spiritual grace, which is sevenfold. After seven days of enlightenment the wife comes in, because after Judea has been enlightened by faith, after it has received the grace of the Holy Spirit, the Church will come in to it, that there may be 'one fold and one shepherd', and that there may be one house of Christ, made firm by one corner stone.
11.18: **“And Achior and Nabath the kinsmen of Tobias came, rejoicing”** — hence: 'Rejoice, ye gentiles, with his people.'
11.19: **“And for seven days feasting,”** — in spiritual gifts and virtues

12.5: **“And calling him, to wit, the father and the son, they took him aside, and began to desire him that he would vouchsafe to accept of half of all things that they had brought.”** — to receive acceptably
12.6:
**“Then he said to them secretly: Bless ye the God of heaven”** — from whom are all things
**“and in the sight of all”** — for an example to others
**“that live give glory”** — praise
**“to him, because he hath shewn to you”** — to you doing well
12.7:
**“For it is good to hide the secret of a king.”** — mysteries are to be covered, the works of the Lord preached
**“But honourable to reveal and confess the works of God.”** — or honored
12.8:
**“Prayer is good with fasting and alms”** — 'hidden in the bosom of the poor'
**“more than to lay up treasures of gold,”** — 'in the bosom of the poor'
12.9: **“for alms from death”** — of the soul
12.10: **“But they that commit sin and iniquity”** — 'He that loveth iniquity hateth his own soul.'
12.11: **“I discover then the truth unto you, and I will not hide the secret from you”** — before
12.12: **“When thou didst pray with tears, and didst bury the dead, and didst leave thy dinner, and hide the dead by day in thy house, and bury them by night, I offered thy prayer to the Lord.”** — which was accepted together with these works of mercy
12.13: **“And because thou wast acceptable to God, it was necessary that temptation should prove thee.”** — God corrects 'the son whom he receiveth.' 'For what son is there whom the father doth not correct?'
12.14: **“AND NOW HE HATH SENT ME”** — BEDE. The angel, about to return to heaven, sets forth more openly what he is, and why he came, and whither he is to return; and Christ disclosed his condition to the same people as it advanced more widely, showing that he himself is in the Father and the Father in the Son. The angel returns to God, Tobias remains with his father; and Christ is understood by his faithful [to be] equal to the Father in divinity, consubstantial with men in humanity.
12.15:
**“For I am the angel Raphael, one of the seven”** — the number seven designates universality, because the whole world is carried on in the number seven.
**“who stand”** — We stand ready to serve wherever we are sent. For God is everywhere.
12.16:
**“And when they had heard these things they were troubled”** — with fear
**“and trembling they fell”** — humbled
**“upon the ground on their face.”** — not backward, as the wicked
12.19: **“I seemed indeed to eat and to drink with you”** — by necessity [so the edition]: I as it were ate, that I might be more familiar with you, not by necessity. 'For my food is the bread which came down from heaven.'
12.20:
**“It is time”** — the business being completed
**“therefore that I return to him that sent me; but bless ye God,”** — not me
**“tell all his wonderful works; bless him, and sing to him.”**
• because 'God is wonderful in his saints'
• out of gladness
12.22:
**“Then lying prostrate for three hours upon their face,”** — giving thanks to the Trinity
**“they blessed God; and rising up they told”** — being zealous for the profit of their neighbors

13.1:
**“OPENING”** — He confessed truth and mercy, teaching always to preach the benefits of God and to fear his scourges; filled with the Spirit of prophecy, he sings many things of the heavenly Jerusalem. And the people of the Jews, converted at the end of the world, will have many doctors and prophets, who kindle the minds of their neighbors to heavenly desires by preaching the joys of the heavenly fatherland.
**“and said:”** — The Canticle of the elder Tobias:
**“Thou art great, O Lord, for ever, and unto all ages”** — 'of his kingdom there shall be no end'
13.2:
**“for thou scourgest, and thou savest; thou leadest down to hell, and bringest up again”** — 'The Lord killeth and maketh alive; he bringeth down to hell and bringeth back again.'
**“and there is none that can escape thy hand.”** — which is everywhere
13.3:
**“Give glory to the Lord, ye children of Israel”** — seeing God
**“and in the sight of the Gentiles”** — for an example to others
13.4: **“because he hath therefore scattered you among the Gentiles, who know not him, that you may declare his wonderful works, and make them know that there is no other almighty God besides him.”** — There are many gods and many lords, but one almighty.
13.5:
**“He hath chastised us”** — justly
**“for our iniquities, and he will save us for his own mercy.”** — not for our merits
13.6:
**“See”** — wondering
**“then what he hath done with us, and with fear”** — yet not secure: 'Blessed are all they that fear the Lord.'
**“and fear”** — not you, but he: 'for it is he who worketh in you'
**“give ye glory to him, and extol the eternal King of worlds in your works.”** — whatever you do
**“As for me, I will praise him in the land of my captivity, because he hath shewn”** — to me
**“Be converted”** — from sin
**“therefore, ye sinners, and do justice”** — 'Decline from evil and do good.'
13.7:
**“I”** — reason
**“and my soul”** — sensuality
**“will rejoice in him.”**
• 'My heart and my flesh have rejoiced in the living God.'
• 'Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner.'
13.8:
**“Bless ye the Lord, all his elect, keep days of joy”** — namely in conscience
**“and give glory to him”** — saying.
13.9:
**“Jerusalem, city of God,”** — in which is the vision of peace
**“hath chastised”** — did not kill
13.10:
**“Give glory to the Lord for thy good things”** — for they are his, not thine
**“and bless the God eternal, that he may rebuild in thee”** — what had been destroyed by sin
**“his tabernacle”** — 'The temple of God is holy, which you are.'
**“and may call back all the captives to thee”** — of the devil; hence: 'He led captivity captive'
**“and thou mayst rejoice”** — in the future
**“for ever and ever.”** — without end
13.11:
**“Thou shalt shine with a glorious light”** — 'The just shall shine as the sun.'
**“and all the ends of the earth”** — the saints, their earthliness ended
**“shall worship”** — shall honor
**“Nations from afar”** — who were far off in the region of sin
**“shall come to thee, and bringing gifts shall adore the Lord in thee, and thy land”** — of the living
**“For the great name”** — of the great God
13.12:
**“They shall be cursed”**
• on the contrary
• 'Depart, ye cursed, into everlasting fire.'
**“that shall despise thee”** — in the world
**“and they shall be condemned”** — for ever
**“all that shall blaspheme thee; and blessed shall they be that shall build thee up.”** — with virtues
13.13:
**“But thou shalt rejoice in thy children”** — saved
**“because they shall all be blessed, and shall be gathered together”** — who were disciples before
13.14: **“Blessed are all they that love thee, and that rejoice in thy peace.”** — whatever others do
13.15: **“My soul, bless thou the Lord, because he hath delivered Jerusalem his city”** — the Church, 'seated on a mountain'.
13.16:
**“Happy shall I be if there shall remain of my seed”** — the reward of works, or some imitators of them, or of natural sons
**“The gates of Jerusalem”** — namely the saints, who lead into the heavenly Jerusalem
**“of sapphire”** — by heavenly conversation
**“and of emerald”**
• by the brightness of faith
• 'Blessed are they that dwell in thy house, O Lord: they shall praise thee for ever and ever.'
**“shall be built, and all the walls thereof round about of precious stones.”** — The walls going round, that is, fortifying holy Church, are the stones; precious, 'living stones', which in Zacharias are rolled upon the earth.
13.17:
**“With white and clean stones”** — 'In my Father's house there are many mansions.'
**“all its streets shall be paved”** — Those who are enlarged by charity are stones in the building, clean from evil and white in good.
13.18:
**“and Alleluia shall be sung in its streets.”**
• through the various assemblies of the faithful
• 'Praise ye the name of the Lord'
**“Blessed be the Lord,”**
• to whom all things are to be ascribed
• not man

14.1:
**“And the words of Tobias were ended.”** — Words of consummation are usually taken in a good sense: the speeches of the good are consummated, those of the wicked are consumed.
**“and saw the children of his grandchildren.”** — 'And mayst thou see thy children's children: peace upon Israel.'
14.2:
**“And after Tobias was restored to his sight, he lived two and forty years”** — And after. The number forty is the laborious [number] of fasting and abstinence. And we ought to bear all the labors of this life with the love of God and of neighbor, and so we shall bear fruit.
**“And after he had lived”** — in good; hence: 'The days of Mary were accomplished.'
**“a hundred and two years,”**
• which number is perfect and passes from the left hand to the right
• as if dead, he lived cleanly to God
**“he was buried”** — 'The bodies of the saints are buried in peace'
**“honourably in Ninive.”** — which is called 'beautiful', signifies the world, which is also beautiful; hence in Greek it is called coscos [so the edition] from its adornment.
**“For he was six and fifty years old when he lost the sight of his eyes, and sixty when he recovered it again.”** — in a perfect and hallowed number
**“FOR FIFTY”** — He had passed the hallowed number fifty and had not reached sixty, which signifies perfection (because of the six, in which all things were made).
**“And the rest of his life”** — having received the light
**“was in joy, and with good increase of the fear of God”** — ever growing from virtue to virtue
**“he departed in peace.”** — to God
14.3:
**“And at the hour of his death he called unto him Tobias his son”** — filled with the sevenfold spirit
**“and his children, seven young men, his grandsons”**
• reborn through the grace of God
• strong, conquering the wicked one
**“AND AT THE HOUR”** — Tobias, that is, the doctors of the Jews, who, about to depart from this world, announce to their kinsmen that the world draws near to its end, and that the goods of the future life are soon to come.
14.4:
**“The destruction of Ninive is at hand.”** — to the world
**“For the word of the Lord doth not fall; and our brethren, that are scattered abroad from the land of Israel,”** — of the living
14.5:
**“And all”** — before
**“the land thereof that is desert”** — many are the children of the desolate
14.6: **“And the Gentiles shall leave their idols, and shall come into Jerusalem”** — the Church
14.7: **“and all the kings of the earth shall rejoice in it”** — that is, of earthliness
14.9: **“Hearken therefore, my children, to your father. Serve the Lord in truth, and seek”** — consulting others
14.10:
**“Now therefore, children, hear me, and stay not here; but on whatever day you shall bury your mother”** — in the world, which shall pass away, and the concupiscence thereof
**“by me in one sepulchre, from that [day] direct your steps”** — the intention of the heart
**“to depart hence.”** — that you may leave earthly desires
**“For I see that its iniquity”** — the transgression of the commandments of God, which will end in the extermination of the world itself and of the whole human race
14.12: **“TOBIAS DEPARTED”** — This Christ does daily when, leaving the wicked, he turns to enlighten the hearts of the good, whom he finds in a good old age because they have long been zealous in good works. But he passes over others who, living long, are neither ripe in counsel nor venerable with the grey hairs of good action, but bowed down under the burden of sins; hence Isaias: The child shall die a hundred years old, and the sinner being a hundred years old shall be accursed; namely he who, living long, does not forsake levity of mind.
14.13:
**“And he found them in health in a good old age, and he took care of them”** — leading them to heavenly things
**“and he closed”** — from the love of the world
**“their eyes”** — directing them to the contemplation of everlasting light
**“and all the inheritance of Raguel's house”** — of which it is said: 'Thou shalt inherit among all the nations.'
**“came to him, and he saw the fifth generation, his children's children.”** — hence: 'And mayst thou see thy children's children: peace upon Israel.'
**“THEY BURIED”** — The burial of Tobias designates the end of the world, in which our Lord with his body, which is the Church, enters into rest, the angels rejoicing at the fellowship of men and placing each one in the various mansions according to the quality of their merits.
14.15:
**“And all his kindred, and all his generation”** — namely the one generation, through the whole world, of them that seek God, of which it is said: 'The generation of the righteous shall be blessed.'
**“in good life”** — what life is better, what conversation of the saints, than to remain for ever in the glory of God?
**“and in holy conversation continued, so that they were acceptable both to God and to men, and to all that dwelt”** — the angels, to whose number we are to be joined and to be united for ever in the heavenly fellowship
**“in the land.”** — 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land', and 'I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.'

1.1:
**“Arphaxad”** — the proud
**“ARPHAXAD”** — RABANUS. Mystically, by Arphaxat the proud are expressed, whose endeavor and labor, carried on through the waste of swelling and elation, easily falls into the power of Nabuchodonosor, that is, of the devil. For he is 'king over all the children of pride.'
**“now king of the Medes”** — by which the time of the history of Judith is noted at the outset
**“had brought many nations under his dominions,”** — for the proud desire to be over all
**“and he built”** — enlarged. For Deiocus founded it
**“ECBATANA”** — Which is the metropolis of the province of Media, which Deiocus, king of the Medes, founded, but Arphaxat wonderfully enlarged; as the prophet Daniel, according to Josephus, under king Darius, placed in the same city of Media a very splendid mausoleum built with wonderful art; which, on whatever day it is seen, is thought to have been built that same day, so new is its beauty and so solid its material. There the kings of the Persians and Medes are buried to this day, and he to whom this charge is committed is a Jewish priest.
1.2:
**“of stones”** — strength
**“squared”** — stable. For every square is stable
**“and hewed; he made the walls thereof seventy cubits high and thirty cubits broad,”** — beauty; in length seventy; for every square is stable; that it might be strong, beautiful, impregnable
1.3: **“On the square”** — greatness
1.4:
**“And he gloried”** — from this work
**“as a mighty one”** — not truly, because God alone is mighty, as he is 'alone good'
**“in the force of his army”** — not in that of God, from whom is all power
**“and in the glory of his chariots.”** — not of God; for there are chariots of God, of which it is said: 'the chariots of Aminadab', and elsewhere, 'the chariots of Salomon', of which it is spoken in the Canticles
**“IN THE GLORY OF HIS CHARIOTS”** — 'Some trust in chariots and some in horses', etc. But God 'cast pharaoh's chariots and his army into the sea'; therefore 'he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.'
1.5:
**“Now in the twelfth year of his reign, Nabuchodonosor”**
• whom others think to be Cambyses
• the devil
**“king of the Assyrians”** — of demons. For Assyria is 'directing' or 'convicting'
**“who reigned in Ninive the great city,”** — a strong man armed keepeth his court
**“IN THE GREAT PLAIN”** — By the names of places the regions of the nations are noted. For as the cosmographers write: 'From the river Indus, which is on the east, to the Tigris, which is on the west, these are the regions: Aracusia, Parthia, Assyria, Persis and Media, mountainous and rugged. On the north they have mount Caucasus, on the south the Red Sea and the Persian gulf. In their midst are the chief rivers Hydaspes and Ardinus. In these are twenty-two nations; but in general it is often called Parthia, and Media [so the edition]. From the Tigris to the Euphrates is Mesopotamia, beginning from the north between mount Taurus and the Caucasus; to which on the south succeeds Babylonia, then Chaldea, lastly Arabia, which stretches toward the east in a narrow tract of land between the Persian and the Arabian [gulfs]. In these are twenty-two nations.' And so it came about that two most powerful kingdoms, fighting each other, procured very many nations from their borders, and at last the victories went to the Chaldeans or Assyrians.
1.7:
**“THEN WAS EXALTED”** — When the devil subjects the multitude of the lost to his will, his heart is lifted up, assigning it to his own power and not to divine permission; and he burns the more for the destruction of very many lost ones, the more he sees himself prevail over some by wicked suggestion. Hence there follows: And he sent to all.
**“and his heart was elevated, and he sent to all”** — the crowd of evil spirits
**“that dwelt in Cilicia and Damascus and Libanus”** — AND HE SENT etc. The devil sends envoys through the various provinces when he scatters the crowd of evil spirits through the whole world to seduce the nations. He spares neither dignity nor honor; he desires to drag all to hell and to make them children of perdition. He does not suffer even the faithful, who are signified by the names of Jerusalem and Jordan, to be secure; nor is it enough for him to swallow up the heathen unless he can also devour Christians. Hence Job: 'He will drink up a river and not wonder, and he trusteth that the Jordan may run into his mouth.' And again: 'His meat is choice.' But although he overcomes many, he is despised by many. Hence: They all with one mind refused.
1.9: **“and to all that were in Samaria and beyond the river Jordan”** — nor does he suffer the faithful to be at rest
1.11:
**“but they all with one mind refused, and sent them back”** — the messengers
**“empty, and rejected them without honour.”** — the business undone
1.12:
**“Then king Nabuchodonosor being angry”**
• the malignant enemy, though overcome, does not desist from the malice he has begun, but again intends war and pours out the whole tumult of his fury
• of the children of pride
**“THEN BEING ANGRY”** — The devil, blinded by his own pride, gives himself the empire of the whole world, striving to make those drawn away from the worship of piety companions of his impiety; who, exulting in the power of his kingdom, says: 'I will ascend into heaven', etc. And in the gospel: 'All these will I give thee, if falling down thou wilt adore me.'
**“against all that land, swore by his throne and kingdom that he would revenge himself of all those countries.”** — he is a lover of power and glory

2.1: **“In the thirteenth year of king Nabuchodonosor, the two and twentieth day of the first month, the word was spoken”** — a sentence
2.2:
**“And he called all the ancients”** — the demons who are over the lesser, in whom he trusts, to whom he commits his secrets
**“and all his officers and his men of war, and communicated to them the secret”** — a secret
2.3:
**“And he said”** — he disclosed
**“that his thoughts were to bring all the earth”** — the good as much as the wicked
**“under his empire.”** — 'upon thy breast shalt thou go, and earth shalt thou eat'
2.4: **“And when this saying pleased them all,”** — for all demons are lovers of power
2.12:
**“Thy eye shall not spare any kingdom,”** — because the enemy, Antichrist, will stir up a great persecution in the whole world
**“and all the strong cities thou shalt bring under me.”** — for there shall be such a persecution as there was not before, nor shall be
2.14:
**“THEN HOLOFERNES”** — That Holophernes signifies the princes of the nations who persecuted the Church, or Antichrist, the son of perdition, into whom all Satan will enter, that he may do what 'his fathers have not done; and he shall not regard the God of his fathers', who 'shall rise up against all kingdoms'; and he will come with a great multitude 'to destroy and slay', and 'shall fix his tabernacle upon the glorious and holy mountain', where, crushed by God, he will fall. This is the beast to which, according to the Apocalypse, the dragon will give his strength and power, so that all will adore the dragon, which gave such power to the beast.
**“called the captains and officers of the power of the Assyrians”** — very many who seem to have firmness of faith and excellence of virtues
2.21:
**“And when he had passed through the borders of the Assyrians”** — AND WHEN HE HAD PASSED THROUGH THE BORDERS OF THE ASSYRIANS. RABANUS. By the various provinces and names of places contained in the history, distinctions of persons and of ranks and dignities are designated; from all of which the devil claims some part for himself; nor does he fear the difficulty of the fight, but strives to make a great ruin of great power.
**“he came to the great mountains Ange, which are on the left of Cilicia, and he went up to all their castles”** — the excellence of virtues
2.23: **“AND HE PILLAGED ALL”** — Taking away the usefulness of knowledge and the other things with which they ought to have served God, and turning them to the use of his own service, he slew those who resisted with the edge of the sword; because those whom he cannot bend to consent he kills bodily.
2.24: **“And he passed over the Euphrates and came into Mesopotamia, and he forced all the stately cities”** — for by his craft he breaks the very shepherds who are over the Lord's flock
2.26:
**“And he carried away all the children of Madian, and stripped them of all their riches”** — the virtue of knowledge
**“and all that resisted him”** — unwilling to acquiesce
2.27:
**“he slew with the edge of the sword.”** — by bodily punishment
**“And after these things”** — the luxurious are easily conquered
**“he went down into the plains of Damascus in the days of the harvest, and he set on fire”** — with the flame of envy
**“HE WENT DOWN INTO THE PLAINS OF DAMASCUS”** — Damascus is interpreted 'drink of blood', in which are expressed the princes of the nations who thirst for the blood of the faithful, most of all in the time of harvest, that is, in the consummation of the world, when the fury of Antichrist rages through the breadth of the world.
**“all the corn”** — the useful
**“and all the trees”**
• of which: 'The sower went out to sow his seed'
• the pleasant
**“and vineyards”** — the fruitful
**“he caused to be cut down”** — persecution, by the sword
2.28:
**“And”** — therefore
**“fell”** — suddenly
**“the fear of him upon all the inhabitants of the land.”**
• the carnal, lovers of earthly things; for others, seeing these things, joyfully await the very near coming of the Redeemer, they who are pilgrims and strangers upon the earth
• 'Woe to the inhabitants of the earth'

3.1:
**“THEN [THEY] SENT”** — The powerful of the world and the lovers of pleasures, who strive to reconcile the prince of the world to themselves, that they may escape the peril of death and the loss of pleasure; of whom it is said: 'Whosoever will be a friend of this world becometh an enemy of God.' 'For in these the care of this world and the deceitfulness of riches choketh up the word, and it becometh fruitless.' For these, according to the names of these provinces, are lifted up by pride, follow vanity, enter the land by two ways, and will be joined in hell to the company of those who mourn, or who pay the penalties of their luxury, where 'they shall pass from the snow waters to excessive heat', 'and their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched.'
**“Then the kings and the princes of all the cities and provinces, namely of Syria, Mesopotamia,”** — of elation
**“and Syria”** — lofty
**“Sobal”** — vain
**“and Libya”** — coming or entering
**“and Cilicia [sent] their ambassadors”** — the company of mourning, or his vomiting
3.2:
**“Let thy indignation towards us cease; for it is better for us to live and”** — for us, in the delights of the world
**“serve Nabuchodonosor the great king”**
• the devil
• 'the ruler of this darkness'
**“and be subject to thee”** — to Antichrist
3.3:
**“All our cities and our possessions, all mountains and hills and fields, and herds of oxen, and flocks of sheep and goats, and horses and camels, and all our goods and families are in thy sight,”**
• at thy will
• use them as it pleases thee
3.4:
**“Both we and our children”** — natural, or imitators, or works
**“Come to us a peaceable lord”**
• who are thy peaceable ones
• to those not resisting
3.6:
**“Then”** — his beast being made ready
**“he came down from the mountains”** — into open work
**“with horsemen”** — with the counsel of pride
**“in great power”**
• the crowd of persecutors
• as the sons suppose
**“and made himself master of every city”** — of Chaim
**“and all the inhabitants of the land.”** — the carnal, loving the earth
**“And from all the cities he took auxiliaries, valiant men,”** — strong in wit, excelling in strength of body
**“and chosen for war.”** — against the saints
**“And so great”** — therefore
**“a fear lay upon all those provinces, that the inhabitants of all the cities”** — going before
**“princes and nobles”** — whose ruin is easier
**“as well as the people”** — following
3.7: **“received him with crowns and lights, leading dances with timbrels and flutes.”** — 'Woe to you that now laugh', etc.
3.8:
**“For he both destroyed their cities, and cut down their groves.”** — the fortifications and hiding places of pretense, by which they imagined they sinned with impunity
**“For had commanded him”** — Antichrist
**“Nabuchodonosor the king,”** — the devil
**“to destroy all the gods of the earth, that is, that he only might be called God by those nations”** — for he wishes alone to be worshipped and adored; hence also he said to Christ: 'All these will I give thee, if falling down thou wilt adore me'
3.9:
**“And when he had passed through Syria”** — the proud
**“Sobal”** — following the vanity of oldness
**“and all Apamea, and all Mesopotamia”** — arrogance
**“he came to the Idumeans”** — the earthly
3.10:
**“and he took possession of their cities, and stayed there for thirty days, in which days to be united”** — against those who ought to fulfil the decalogue under faith in the Trinity
**“he commanded all the army”** — serving

4.1:
**“Then”** — in the time of persecution
**“the children of Israel hearing these things”** — Israelites, seeing God
**“who dwelt in the land of Juda”** — of confession
**“what he had done to other cities”** — the gentiles
4.2:
**“were exceedingly afraid of him.”** — at his pressing onset
**“Dread”** — of body
**“and horror also”** — of mind
**“seized upon the minds”** — spiritual
**“of them, lest he should do to Jerusalem and to the temple of the Lord”** — the Church, which is the temple of God
4.4:
**“And they sent”** — they preached
**“into all Samaria”** — to all those who ought to keep watch. For Samaria is interpreted 'keeper'
**“round about”** — lest there be anywhere an approach for the enemy
**“as far as Jericho”** — wherever the Church extends. For Jericho is interpreted 'moon', which signifies the Church
**“and seized upon”** — by admonitions
4.5:
**“all the tops of the mountains”**
• who guard others
• strong men, lofty in the pursuit of virtues
**“and they compassed with walls”** — of faith, of virtues
**“their towns”** — the flocks committed to them
**“and gathered together corn for provision for war.”** — the knowledge of the Scriptures, by which the faithful live
4.6:
**“And Eliachim the priest”** — Christ, 'the great priest', who says: 'I am the resurrection and the life.' For Eliachim is 'resurrection of God'
**“wrote to all that were over against Esdrelon, which faceth the great plain near Dothain”** — who is against the delight of the world, which leads to failing. For Dothaim sounds 'failing'
**“that they should take possession of the ascents of the mountains”** — the heights of men's wits
**“by which there might be any way to Jerusalem,”** — for in this the devil attacks the Church
**“and should keep watch there where it was narrow”** — subtle
4.8: **“And they did”** — being admonished
4.9:
**“And cried”** — with the intention of the heart
**“all the people”** — of one mind
**“to the Lord with great earnestness”** — for the continual prayer of a just man availeth much
**“and they humbled”** — in fastings
**“their souls in fastings and prayers, both they and their wives.”** — chastening their sensualities from unlawful desires
4.11:
**“And the priests put on haircloths”** — the doctors doing penance with the people
**“and the little children”** — innocent prayers in the sight of the Lord
**“they caused to lie prostrate before the temple of the Lord, and the altar of the Lord”** — themselves, who offer a victim to God
**“they covered with haircloth”** — with the compunction of penance
4.12:
**“And”** — so
**“they cried”** — with heart, mouth and work
**“to the God of Israel”** — who alone can save
**“with one accord,”** — what is asked with the unanimity of charity is quickly obtained
**“that there might not be given”** — by God, by whose permission it happens
**“for a prey”** — of the devil
**“their children”** — the innocent, the simple
**“and their wives to be divided”** — the weak subjects, through various vices
**“and their cities”** — of the Church
**“to destruction, and their holy things”** — those who seemed to be holy
**“to profanation”** — of sins
4.13:
**“Then Eliachim”** — Christ
**“the priest”** — 'according to the order of Melchisedech'
**“high of the Lord”** — 'above all'
**“went about all Israel”**
• by himself and by his messengers
• seeing God
**“saying: Know ye that the Lord hath heard your prayers”** — as if: be confident, your prayers are heard
**“if continuing”** — constantly
**“you persevere”** — in action
**“in fastings”** — the end, not the fight, crowns
**“and prayers in the sight of the Lord.”** — that you may please the Lord
4.14: **“Remember Moses the servant of the Lord”** — REMEMBER. He strengthens them by the examples of the saints; hence Job: 'Thou renewest thy witnesses against me'; and Paul to the Hebrews, praising the virtue of faith, brings in copious examples of the fathers, 'who by faith conquered kingdoms, wrought justice.'
4.15:
**“So shall be”** — laid low
**“all the enemies of Israel, if you persevere”** — 'he that shall persevere unto the end shall be saved'
**“So by this exhortation”** — of the preachers of Christ
**“of his, praying”** — the faithful
**“to the Lord, they continued”** — strengthened in prayer
**“in the sight of the Lord,”** — well pleasing
**“so that even they”** — the priests
**“HOLOCAUSTS”** — Crucifying their flesh with its vices and concupiscences, dedicating their life to God, offering the sacrifice of praise with mouth and mind.
**“girded with haircloths, offered the sacrifices to the Lord, and there was ashes”** — the remembrance of frailty
**“upon their heads”** — minds
**“And with all their heart”** — 'a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise'
**“they all begged of God”** — 'of one mind in prayer'

5.1:
**“And it was told Holofernes the general”** — spiritual
**“of the army of the Assyrians, that the children of Israel”** — the faithful
**“prepared themselves to resist”** — the wicked
**“and had shut up the ways of the mountains”** — with confident mind he detests all pride, through which most of all the adversaries strive to break in
5.2:
**“and he was transported with exceeding great fury and indignation, and he called all the princes”** — who are turbulent and inconsiderate
**“of Moab and the leaders of Ammon”** — who are without law
5.3:
**“and he said to them: Tell me what is this people”** — the persecutors ask this of one another: who they are, of how great constancy
**“that besetteth the mountains, or what are their cities, and of what sort, and how great”** — the fortifications of faith
**“also what is their power, or what is their multitude, or who is the king over their warfare,”** — how powerful
5.4:
**“and why they above all that dwell in the east have despised us, and have not come out to meet us”** — by the light of faith and knowledge, by which the princes of darkness are more easily overcome
**“that they might receive us with peace?”** — as it were the princes of the heretics
5.5:
**“Then Achior”** — any one given to idolatry
**“captain of all the children of Ammon”** — THEN ACHIOR. As it were a prince of the heretics, any one given to idolatry, who has known of the divine works and miracles, which he often tells to others, although he has not perfectly learned the catholic faith and has not been reborn in the baptism of Christ. Or by Achior heretics are designated, who, although they do not hold the way of truth in all things, yet in their doctrine preach many true things which agree with our faith. These fight against the catholic Church, but, overcome by reason, do not altogether hide the truth. For heretics mingle good with evil, because if they always spoke evil they could not lie hid; as he who offers a cup of poison touches the lip of the cup with honey, that what is sweet may be perceived first, lest what is deadly be feared. Sometimes, however, being corrected, they are saved; as Achior, seeing the victory of Judith, being joined to the people of God, circumcised the flesh of his foreskin. The lepers of the gospel also express the heretics, who, while they insert wrong things among right, as it were sprinkle a healthy color with spots.
**“answering said: If thou vouchsafe, my lord, to hear, I will tell the truth in thy sight concerning this people that dwelleth in the mountains”** — the people of God dwells in the mountains, the Egyptians in the plains
5.7:
**“They dwelt first in Mesopotamia, because they would not follow the gods”** — fire and others
**“of their fathers”** — of the gentiles
5.8:
**“Wherefore forsaking the ceremonies”** — the religion
**“of their fathers, which consisted in the worship of many gods,”** — the wicked are in multitude, the good in unity
5.9:
**“they worshipped one God of heaven, who also commanded them to depart”** — in mind and in body
**“from thence, and to dwell in Charan. And when a famine had covered all the land,”** — of the word of God
**“and there for four hundred years were so multiplied,”** — 'they are multiplied above number'
5.10: **“they went down into Egypt”** — one goes up to Jerusalem, one goes down into Egypt
5.11:
**“And when the king of Egypt oppressed them”** — pharao: the devil
**“and in the building”** — or: building
**“of his cities”** — not God's
**“in clay”** — with earthly works
**“and brick had made slaves of them, they cried”** — with heart and mouth
**“to their God”** — not to gods
5.12:
**“and he struck the whole land of Egypt with divers plagues.”** — avenging them
**“And when the Egyptians had cast them out from them”** — overcome by the plagues
5.13:
**“in their flight the God of heaven”** — the highest of all these
**“opened the sea”** — the Red [Sea], in which baptism is signified
5.14:
**“And when in that place an innumerable army of the Egyptians”** — the multitude of vices, of demons
**“pursued after them, it was so overwhelmed with the waters,”**
• of baptism
• of baptism, of those whose iniquities are forgiven
**“And after they came out of the Red Sea, they came upon the deserts of mount Sina, in which never man could dwell,”** — before
**“or son of man rested.”** — in the desert of this world men rest, not the sons of men
5.15:
**“There bitter fountains”** — of the law, which according to the letter is bitter
**“were made sweet for them to drink”** — sweetened by the wood of the cross, by the blood of Christ, understood spiritually
5.16:
**“Wheresoever they went in without bow and arrow”** — hence: 'For I will not trust in my bow.'
**“And there was no one that triumphed”** — with impunity
**“But as often as beside their own God they worshipped any other, they were given”** — by their God
**“for a prey”** — captivity
**“and to the sword”** — slaughter
**“and to reproach.”** — to the nations
**“And as often as they were penitent for having revolted from the worship of their God,”** — as if: he did not altogether cast them off, but corrected them
**“the God of heaven gave them power to resist.”** — their enemies
5.18:
**“Now before these years, when they had departed from the way”** — the precepts
**“which God had given them to walk”** — that they might advance
**“therein, they were destroyed”** — from their land
5.19:
**“But of late returning”** — through penance
**“to the Lord their God, from the dispersion wherein they were scattered they are come together, and are gone up into all these mountains, and possess Jerusalem again”** — the vision of peace
**“where are the holies of holies.”** — or: their [holies]
5.22: **“And it came to pass, when Achior had made an end of speaking these words, all the great men of Holofernes were angry, and they had a mind to kill him, saying to each other:”** — those who are proud with the haughtiness of the world cannot hear the proclamations of truth, and threaten death to the preachers together with the rest of the faithful
5.23:
**“Who is this”** — of what rashness
**“that the children of Israel”** — the faithful
**“saith can resist king Nabuchodonosor”** — the devil
**“and his armies”** — demons, vices, any evils whatever
**“men unarmed and without force”** — for they do not see 'the shield of faith, the helmet of hope, and the sword of the word of God'
**“and without skill in the art of war?”** — of fighting
5.24: **“That Achior therefore may know that he deceiveth us,”** — he thinks to deceive

6.1: **“that every nation may know that Nabuchodonosor is god of the earth”** — not of heaven
6.8: **“And that thou mayst know that thou shalt experience these things together with them, behold from this hour thou shalt be associated to their people,”** — they strive to join the heralds of truth to the crowd that is to perish; for they think those lost whom they separate from their company and associate with the faithful of Christ; hence: 'Be thou his disciple, but we are the disciples of Moses'
6.10:
**“Then Holofernes commanded his servants”** — the persecutors of the faith
**“to take Achior,”** — any confessor of Christ, a herald of the truth
**“and to lead him to Bethulia, and to deliver him”** — separated from himself
**“into the hands of the children of Israel.”** — whom he thought were to be destroyed
6.11:
**“And the servants of Holofernes taking him, went through the plains”** — for such men desire to draw [him] through unlawful desires and the broad way that leadeth to death
**“but when they came near the mountains, the slingers came out against them.”** — the preachers, hurling the testimonies of the Scriptures against them
6.13:
**“But they turning out of the way by the side of the mountain”** — not able to fulfil their wish
**“tied Achior to a tree hand and foot”** — because the soldier of Christ whom they cannot seduce they make a partner of his cross and passion
**“and so left him bound with ropes, and returned to their master.”**
• not corrected but worse, with increase of crimes
• to their former error
6.14: **“And the children of Israel came down from Bethulia, and came to him, and loosing him they brought him to Bethulia”** — LOOSING HIM. The doctors of the Church loose him who was tied to the tree when they teach their catechumens to fear neither the rage of persecutors nor death. They loose him as it were tied to the tree when they rescue the fearful mind from dread of the cross and instruct it to suffer. And this is done better if, after the example of Ozias and Charmi, who, comforting Achior, poured out devout prayers to the Lord with all the people, the masters of the Church with the rest of the faithful commend their hearers to the Lord with devout prayers, that by his gift may be had what human infirmity does not merit.
6.19:
**“saying: O Lord God of heaven and earth,”** — who hast made all things, canst do all things
**“behold their pride,”** — do not overlook their sins
**“and look on our low condition”** — who regardest the lowly
**“and have regard to the face of thy saints”** — of the mind, which alone pleases thee
**“and shew that thou forsakest not them that trust”** — confiding
**“on thee”** — not in themselves
**“and that thou humblest them that presume of themselves, and glory in their own strength.”** — 'He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord'
6.21:
**“saying:”** — confident that their prayer was heard
**“The God of our fathers, whose power thou hast set forth, himself”** — the rewarder
**“to thee”** — who hast merited
**“will make this return, that rather their”** — than they thine
**“And when the Lord our God shall give this liberty to his servants,”** — the enemies being slain
**“Then Ozias after the council was ended, took him into his house, and made him a great supper.”** — AND HE MADE A SUPPER. He makes a great supper, the fast being ended, who refreshes with evangelical doctrine and with the dishes of virtues a soul long languishing and in want of the bread of the word. To this banquet all the presbyters are called, that by their exhortations and examples the neophytes may be strengthened to receive or to keep the faith.
**“And afterwards all the people were called together”** — 'Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity'
**“and they prayed all the night long within the church,”** — 'My house shall be called the house of prayer'
**“desiring help of the God of Israel.”** — 'Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm'

7.1:
**“Holofernes”** — the mystical one
**“on the next day gave orders to his army”** — his accomplices
**“to go up against Bethulia.”** — the Church, which is the house of God
7.4:
**“Now the children of Israel,”** — the faithful
**“when they saw their multitude, prostrated themselves upon the ground,”** — praying humbly
**“putting ashes upon their heads,”** — keeping the remembrance of frailty; hence: 'Remember, man, that thou art dust'
7.5:
**“and taking their arms of war,”** — the pursuits of virtues
**“they posted themselves at the places”** — the inner places of the mind, lest the enemy find an approach by which to bring in the carnal delights of harmful thought
**“which by a narrow pathway lead between the mountains, and they guarded them all day”**
• constantly
• in prosperity
**“and night.”** — in adversity
7.7:
**“Now Holofernes, in going round about,”** — seeking whom he may devour
**“found that the fountain”** — living
**“which flowed in”** — abounded
**“ran through their aqueduct on the south side”** — by the heat of the Holy Spirit
**“without the city; and he commanded their aqueduct to be cut off.”** — HE COMMANDED TO BE CUT OFF. The doctrine of the gospel, which, proceeding from the living fountain, the doctors enlightened by the grace of the Holy Spirit bring into the city of the Church through the pipe of their mouth: this the persecutors of the faithful take away by forbidding it and threatening death, so that spiritual want may rather kill.
7.9:
**“Nevertheless there were springs not far from the walls,”**
• the dogmas of the philosophers, which give some comfort of knowledge and honesty
• THERE WERE NEVERTHELESS etc. As in the book of Kings the Philistines take away the smiths of iron, lest they make for the Hebrews either spear or sword; and all Israel went down to the Philistines to sharpen every man his ploughshare, and his spade, and his axe, and his rake. For the devil strives most for this: to take away the streams of doctrine and the arms of virtues, and so swiftly to accomplish his wickedness unto the destruction of the servants of God. Hence the princes of the gentiles and Julian the apostate forbade Christians not only divine but also human philosophy.
7.10:
**“But the children”** — wicked
**“of Ammon and Moab”**
• a turbulent people
• lawless
7.23: **“THEN TO OZIAS”** — The carnal, who say: 'Lord, Lord', 'but their heart is far from me.' For in the Lord's net there are both good and bad fish until the shore of the future judgment; who, bearing heavily the discomforts of the present life, prefer to enjoy present delights rather than that heavenly goods be reserved for them in the future; who afflict their masters with importunate complaints and compel them to assent to them for the luxury of the world. Hence there follows: And when they were wearied with these cries.
7.30:
**“And when they were wearied with these cries”** — of the people
**“Ozias rising up all in tears”** — the hireling shepherd, who 'leaveth the sheep and flieth'
**“said: Be of good courage, my brethren, and let us wait these five days for mercy from the Lord.”**
• temporal help
• AND THESE FIVE DAYS. The five days are the five senses of the body, by which the present life is led. The idle doctor asks as it were a truce of five days, who indiscreetly promises his hearers comfort for bodily vitium [so the edition], as if the magnificence of the supreme giver were in his power, whereas the time and manner of giving rest rather in the power of the giver than of the receiver. For if the comfort of the present life is denied, they desert their subjects, so that by yielding to persecutions they may avoid bodily punishment. This agreement our Judith, that is, the Church, rejects and despises.
7.31: **“For perhaps he will put a stop to his indignation, and will give glory to his own name.”** — 'Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to thy name'

8.1:
**“Now it came to pass, when Judith had heard these words”** — the Church; for it is interpreted 'confessing' or 'praising'
**“NOW IT CAME TO PASS”** — Daughter of Merari, that is, of bitterness. For the Church through bitterness and tribulation is begotten to the joys of the future life, where it will praise the Lord for ever. That she is related to have been born in the fifteenth generation signifies that the Church was brought forth from the patriarchs and apostles through the seven of the law and the eight of the gospel, and is to ascend to heavenly grace. Hence this number of steps is set in the psalter, figurative of the future ascension to heaven, at which the saints, coming, rightly say: 'Behold now bless ye.'
8.2:
**“and her husband was Manasses, who died in the time of the barley harvest,”** — AND HER HUSBAND MANASSES. Manasses is interpreted 'forgetful' or 'necessity'; joined to whom in wedlock Judith was as it were bound to the decalogue of the law or to the rites of the gentiles; but when Christ came and the light of the gospel shone in the world, all that observance gave way and, like a cheap gathering of harvest, swiftly passed. Hence the Apostle: 'After the faith is come, we are no longer under a pedagogue. For you are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.' And to the Romans he says: 'You also are become dead to the law by the body of Christ Jesus, that you may belong to another, who is risen again from the dead.'
**“AND HER HUSBAND”** — Manasses is Christ, the bridegroom of the Church. He is well called Manasses, because he makes us forget our former calamity through the consolation of the future life. He came in the time of the barley harvest, that is, of the gathering of the Jewish people, when he sent his apostles to preach and to gather the sheaves of believers. The heat of persecution [came] upon his head, that is, upon his divinity; for the head of Christ is God. For the Jews were most scandalized at this, that he said he was the Son of God. Hence: 'Thou makest thyself God.' And elsewhere: 'Because he made himself the Son of God.' Jesus suffered among his own nation and was buried in a garden. His bride, the bridegroom being taken away, gives herself to fasting and prayer until the consummation of the world, and does not deign to be polluted with heretical errors; to whom her husband left the riches of spiritual wisdom and virtue, and gathered a household, that is, the multitude of the gentiles.
8.4: **“And Judith his relict was a widow now three years and six months.”** — the Church, bereft of the allurements of the world, having the faith of the holy Trinity and the perfection of works
8.5:
**“And in the upper part of her house”** — in the citadel of the mind
**“she made herself a private chamber,”** — a firm guard, that she might not flow away through divers desires
**“in which she abode shut up with her maids”** — with clean companies
**“AND WEARING UPON HER LOINS”** — She who through continence of life and mortification of pleasures 'crucifies her flesh with its vices and concupiscences', that she may prepare herself in mind for the future solemnity and sabbath, where in return for present tribulation she would receive full joy with the holy angels.
8.7:
**“And she was exceedingly beautiful”** — hence: 'Thou art beautiful and comely as Jerusalem'
**“and her husband”** — TO WHOM HER HUSBAND etc. From the instruction of the old law and of philosophy, the Church, coming to Christ, brought manifold riches of moral discipline; hence Paul also glories that he was 'brought up at the feet of Gamaliel', and we read that 'Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians.'
**“had left her much riches, and very many servants, and possessions full of herds of oxen”** — of preachers
**“and flocks of sheep.”** — of the innocent, the obedient
8.8:
**“And she was among all”** — the good
**“greatly renowned, because she feared the Lord very much,”**
• in the fear of the Lord; hence: 'The woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised', and 'Let her works praise her in the gates'
• of this fear Isaias says: 'The fear of the Lord is his treasure'
**“neither was there any one that spoke an ill word of her.”** — 'From all appearance of evil refrain yourselves'
8.13:
**“THIS IS NOT A WORD”** — We ought to prescribe to the Lord neither time nor manner; rather let us leave all things to his judgment. Hence one of the fathers is read to have said in his prayer: Son of God, as thou knowest and as thou wilt, have mercy on me. We ought to seek the kingdom only, and all things shall be added. Let the present life be for the faithful in use, the future in fruit; let the temporal thing be for the journey; let the eternal be desired for the arriving.
**“But forasmuch as the Lord is patient”** — because he knows all things
**“let us be penitent for this same thing, and with tears let us beg his pardon,”** — which have the weight of a voice; which obtain without supplicating
8.15:
**“And therefore let us humble before him”** — 'He that exalteth himself shall be humbled', etc.
**“our souls”** — not only our bodies
**“and serving him in a contrite and humbled spirit”** — 'In a humble spirit and a contrite heart let us be received by thee, O Lord'
8.16: **“let us say to the Lord with tears, that according to his will”** — hence: 'thy will be done, not mine'
8.19: **“for which crime they were given up to the sword, and to pillage, and to confusion by their enemies; but we know no other God but him.”** — hence: 'I am the Lord, and there is none else'
8.20:
**“Let us humbly wait for his consolation”** — with long patience; hence: 'Expect the Lord, do manfully'
**“and he will require”** — by avenging
8.22:
**“And now, brethren,”** — for all of us there is one Father in heaven; hence: 'Call none your father upon earth'
**“as you are the ancients among the people of God”** — to whom they will render account for the sheep
**“their very soul resteth upon you,”** — namely, as watchmen and doctors
**“by your speech”** — exhortation, consolation
**“raise up their hearts, that they may be mindful”** — from despair, they who are now forgetful
**“that were tried”** — by God; hence: 'God tempted Abraham.'
**“our fathers,”** — whose imitators we ought to be, as of Abraham, Isaac
8.23: **“They must remember how our father Abraham was tempted”** — the brave deeds of the fathers are lessons for the sons
8.24: **“So Isaac, so Jacob, so Moses, and all that have pleased God, passed through many tribulations, remaining faithful.”** — hence: 'We have passed through fire and water'
8.25: **“But they that did not receive the trials with the fear of the Lord”** — as she admonishes by the example of the good, so she terrifies by the example of the wicked
8.26:
**“were destroyed by the destroyer”** — by the devil
**“and by serpents”** — bodily and spiritual
8.27:
**“As for us therefore let us not revenge ourselves”** — as if: doing these things you seem to seek vengeance from the Lord
**“for these things which we suffer,”** — this is the way of truth: that under scourges we humble our souls and strive to have patience
**“but esteeming, in respect of our sins,”** — according to that: 'We have done unjustly, we have wrought iniquity'
**“these very punishments to be less”** — than we deserve
**“let us believe that the scourges of the Lord, with which like servants of the Lord we are chastised, have happened for our amendment, and not for our destruction.”** — 'God willeth not the death of the sinner, but that he be converted and live.'
8.28: **“And Ozias and the ancients said to her: All things which thou hast spoken are true, and there is nothing to be reprehended in thy words.”** — AND OZIAS AND THE ANCIENTS SAID etc. Whatever the Church speaks in the confession of faith and in the doctrine of religion is praiseworthy and irreprehensible. These things she forewarns each of the faithful by praying, that each, as he has proved that what she teaches is true, may so fulfil it in works. Hence is added: And Judith said to them.
8.32: **“AND JUDITH SAID TO THEM”** — Judith, that is, the Church, commends to the presbyters the gate, that is, the careful guarding of the camp of God, that with watchful and skilful care they may stand always ready against the snares of the enemies, and fortified with prayers.
8.33:
**“so that which I intend to do,”** — 'do all things with counsel'
**“You shall stand at the gate this night, and I will go out with my maidservant; and pray ye, that as you have said, in five days the Lord may look down upon his people Israel.”** — his people
8.34: **“But I desire that you search not”** — lest you hinder
8.35: **“And Ozias the prince of Juda said to her: Go in peace, and the Lord”** — the leader and helper

9.1:
**“And when they were gone,”** — or: departing
**“AND WHEN THEY WERE GONE”** — After she has spoken to the presbyters, Judith enters her oratory, because the solicitude of the saints, after the service of preaching, returns to the secret of their heart, that there it may complete the incense of pure ascent, according to that: 'When thou shalt pray, enter into thy chamber.'
**“Judith went into her oratory, and putting on haircloth,”** — of penance
**“laid ashes on her head”** — the remembrance of frailty and of death
**“and falling down prostrate before the Lord, she cried to the Lord, saying:”** — hoping to be heard through the affection of humility: 'a sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit'
9.2:
**“O LORD GOD”** — Well does she recall in her prayer the deed of Simeon, who with his brother Levi avenged on the strangers the defilement of their sister. For it was to come about that Holophernes, who wished to fulfil in Judith the uncleanness of his lust, would be struck by the sword of vengeance.
**“who gavest him a sword to execute vengeance against strangers, who had been violators by their uncleanness, and uncovered the virgin unto confusion”** — of Dina, the daughter of Jacob
9.4:
**“and who gavest their wives to be made a prey, and their daughters into captivity, and all their spoils to be divided to thy servants”** — the sons of Jacob
**“who were zealous with thy zeal: assist, I beseech thee, O Lord my God, me a widow.”** — desolate
9.5: **“For thou hast done the things of old, and hast devised one thing after another”** — thou hast disposed all things in order
9.7:
**“LOOK UPON THE CAMP”** — As she compares the luxurious with the luxurious, so now the proud with the proud, namely the Assyrians with the Egyptians; because as the divine power was in those, so it can be made manifest when these too are overthrown; because it is the same Lord, the same power, the same justice.
**“as thou wast pleased then to look upon the camp of the Egyptians, when they pursued armed after thy servants, trusting in their chariots”** — not in the Lord
**“But thou lookedst over their camp, and darkness wearied them.”** — 'but the countenance of the Lord is against them that do evil things'
**“The deep held their feet”** — so that they could not escape
**“and the waters”** — of the sea
**“So may it be”** — like them
**“with these also, O Lord,”** — let them be punished
**“and they know not that thou art our God, who destroyest wars from the beginning, and the Lord is thy name.”** — alone
9.8:
**“Lift up thy arm”** — the power which thou seemest to have let go
**“as from the beginning, and crush their power with thy power; let their power fall in thy wrath, who promise”** — they boast
**“Bring to pass, O Lord, that his pride may be cut off with his own sword,”** — BRING TO PASS, O LORD. She does not say this with delight in punishment but with love of justice. So the prophets, whatever they see in the spirit will come to pass by just judgment, proclaim in the same spirit as to be done; nay rather, he himself foretold it through them who reveals it to them and does it; such as that: 'Let their table become as a snare before them', etc., and: 'God shall strike thee, thou whited wall.'
**“MYSTICALLY”** — Every heretic or schismatic or Jew or pagan who would corrupt the Church by word or example loses the head of his wicked will by the sword of his own pride. Hence: 'she shall crush thy head.'
9.9:
**“let him be caught in the net of his own eyes in my regard,”** — through the gate of the eyes let the affection of concupiscences enter; hence: 'whosoever shall look on a woman to lust after her hath already committed adultery with her'
**“and thou shalt strike him by the lips of my charity.”** — let my lips, that is, my words, seem sweet to him
