29.text: And Joseph lifting up his eyes, saw Benjamin his brother, by the same mother, and said: Is this your young brother, of whom you told me? And he said: God be gracious to thee, my son.

30.text: And he made haste because his heart was moved upon his brother, and tears gushed out: and going into his chamber he wept.

31.text: And when he had washed his face, coming out again, he refrained himself, and said: Set bread on the table.

32.text: And when it was set on, for Joseph apart, and for his brethren apart, for the Egyptians also that ate with him, apart, (for it is unlawful for the Egyptians to eat with the Hebrews, and they think such a feast profane):

33.text: They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his age. And they wondered very much:

34.text: Taking the messes which they received of him: and the greater mess came to Benjamin, so that it exceeded by five parts. And they drank, and were merry with him.

1.text: And Joseph commanded the steward of his house, saying: Fill their sacks with corn, as much as they can hold: and put the money of every one in the top of his sack.

2.text: And in the mouth of the younger’s sack put my silver cup, and the price which he gave for the wheat. And it was so done.

3.text: And when the morning arose, they were sent away with their asses.

4.text: And when they were now departed out of the city, and had gone forward a little way; Joseph sending for the steward of his house, said: Arise, and pursue after the men: and when thou hast overtaken them, say to them: Why have you returned evil for good?

5.text: The cup which you have stolen is that in which my lord drinketh, and in which he is wont to divine: you have done a very evil thing.

6.text: He did as he had commanded him. And having overtaken them, he spoke to them the same words.

7.text: And they answered: Why doth our lord speak so, as though thy servants had committed so heinous a fact?

8.text: The money, that we found in the top of our sacks, we brought back to thee from the land of Chanaan: how then should it be that we should steal out of thy lord’s house, gold or silver?

9.text: With whomsoever of thy servants shall be found that which thou seekest, let him die, and we will be the bondmen of my lord.

10.text: And he said to them: Let it be according to your sentence: with whomsoever it shall be found, let him be my servant, and you shall be blameless.

11.text: Then they speedily took down their sacks to the ground, and every man opened his sack.

12.text: Which when he had searched, beginning at the eldest and ending at the youngest, he found the cup in Benjamin’s sack.

13.text: Then they rent their garments, and loading their asses again, returned into the town.

14.text: And Juda at the head of his brethren went in to Joseph, (for he was not yet gone out of the place), and they altogether fell down before him on the ground.

15.text: And he said to them: Why would you do so? know you not that there is no one like me in the science of divining.

16.text: And Juda said to him: What shall we answer my lord? or what shall we say, or be able justly to allege? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold, we are all bondmen to my lord, both we, and he with whom the cup was found.

17.text: Joseph answered: God forbid that I should do so: he that stole the cup, he shall be my bondman: and go you away free to your father.

18.text: Then Juda coming nearer, said boldly: I beseech thee, my lord, let thy servant speak a word in thy ears, and be not angry with thy servant: for after Pharao thou art,

19.text: My lord. Thou didst ask thy servants the first time: Have you a father or a brother?

20.text: And we answered thee, my lord: We have a father an old man, and a young boy, that was born in his old age; whose brother by the mother is dead: and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loveth him tenderly.

21.text: And thou saidst to thy servants: Bring him hither to me, and I will set my eyes on him.

22.text: We suggested to my lord: The boy cannot leave his father: for if he leave him, he will die.

23.text: And thou saidst to thy servants: Except your youngest brother come with you, you shall see my face no more.

24.text: Therefore when we were gone up to thy servant our father, we told him all that my lord had said.

25.text: And our father said: Go again, and buy us a little wheat.

26.text: And we said to him: We cannot go: if our youngest brother go down with us, we will set out together: otherwise, without him we dare not see the man’s face.

27.text: Whereunto he answered: You know that my wife bore me two.

28.text: One went out, and you said: A beast devoured him: and hitherto he appeareth not.

29.text: If you take this also, and any thing befall him in the way you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow unto hell.

30.text: Therefore if I shall go to thy servant our father, and the boy be wanting, (whereas his life dependeth upon the life of him,)

31.text: And he shall see that he is not with us, he will die, and thy servants shall bring down his gray hairs with sorrow unto hell.

32.text: Let me be thy proper servant, who took him into my trust, and promised, saying: If I bring him not again, I will be guilty of sin against my father for ever.

33.text: Therefore I thy servant will stay instead of the boy in the service of my lord, and let the boy go up with his brethren.

34.text: For I cannot return to my father without the boy, lest I be a witness of the calamity that will oppress my father.

1.text: Joseph could no longer refrain himself before many that stood by: whereupon he commanded that all should go out, and no stranger be present at their knowing one another.

2.text: And he lifted up his voice with weeping, which the Egyptians and all the house of Pharao heard.

3.text: And he said to his brethren: I am Joseph: is my father yet living? His brethren could not answer him, being struck with exceeding great fear.

4.text: And he said mildly to them: Come nearer to me. And when they were come near him, he said: I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.

5.text: Be not afraid, and let it not seem to you a hard case that you sold me into these countries: for God sent me before you into Egypt for your preservation.

6.text: For it is two years since the famine began to be upon the land, and five years more remain, wherein there can be neither ploughing nor reaping.

7.text: And God sent me before, that you may be preserved upon the earth, and may have food to live.

8.text: Not by your counsel was I sent hither, but by the will of God: who hath made me as it were a father to Pharao, and lord of his whole house, and governor in all the land of Egypt.

9.text: Make haste, and go ye up to my father, and say to him: Thus saith thy son Joseph: God hath made me lord of the whole land of Egypt: come down to me, linger not.

10.text: And thou shalt dwell in the land of Gessen: and thou shalt be near me, thou and thy sons, and thy sons’ sons, thy sheep, and thy herds, and all things that thou hast.

11.text: And there I will feed thee, (for there are yet five years of famine remaining), lest both thou perish, and thy house, and all things that thou hast.

12.text: Behold, your eyes, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see that it is my mouth that speaketh to you.

13.text: You shall tell my father of all my glory, and all things that you have seen in Egypt: make haste and bring him to me.

14.text: And falling upon the neck of his brother Benjamin, he embraced him and wept: and Benjamin in like manner wept also on his neck.

15.text: And Joseph kissed all his brethren, and wept upon every one of them: after which they were emboldened to speak to him.

16.text: And it was heard, and the fame was spread abroad in the king’s court: The brethren of Joseph are come: and Pharao with all his family was glad.

17.text: And he spoke to Joseph that he should give orders to his brethren, saying: Load your beasts, and go into the land of Chanaan.

18.text: And bring away from thence your father and kindred, and come to me: and I will give you all the good things of Egypt, that you may eat the marrow of the land.

19.text: Give orders also that they take wagons out of the land of Egypt, for the carriage of their children and their wives: and say: Take up your father, and make haste to come with all speed:

20.text: And leave nothing of your household stuff: for all the riches of Egypt shall be yours.

21.text: And the sons of Israel did as they were bid. And Joseph gave them wagons according to Pharao’s commandment: and provisions for the way.

22.text: He ordered also to be brought out for every one of them two robes: but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver with five robes of the best:

23.text: Sending to his father as much money and raiment, adding besides ten he asses to carry off all the riches of Egypt, and as many she asses, carrying wheat and bread for the journey.

24.text: So he sent away his brethren, and at their departing said to them: Be not angry in the way.

25.text: And they went up out of Egypt, and came into the land of Chanaan to their father Jacob.

26.text: And they told him, saying: Joseph thy son is living: and he is ruler in all the land of Egypt. Which when Jacob heard, he awaked as it were out of a deep sleep, yet did not believe them.

27.text: They, on the other side, told the whole order of the thing. And when he saw the wagons and all that he had sent his spirit revived,

28.text: And he said: It is enough for me, if Joseph my son be yet living: I will go and see him before I die.

1.text: And Israel taking his journey, with all that he had, came to the well of the oath, and killing victims there to the God of his father Isaac,

2.text: He heard him by a vision in the night calling him, and saying to him: Jacob, Jacob. And he answered him: Lo, here I am.

3.text: God said to him: I am the most mighty God of thy father: fear not, go down into Egypt, for I will make a great nation of thee there.

4.text: I will go down with thee thither, and will bring thee back again from thence: Joseph also shall put his hands upon thy eyes.

5.text: And Jacob rose up from the well of the oath: and his sons took him up, with their children and wives in the wagons, which Pharao had sent to carry the old man,

6.text: And all that he had in the land of Chanaan, and he came into Egypt with all his seed:

7.text: His sons, and grandsons, daughters, and all his offspring together.

8.text: And these are the names of the children of Israel, that entered into Egypt, he and his children. His firstborn Ruben,

9.text: The sons of Ruben: Henoch and Phallu, and Hesron and Charmi.

10.text: The sons of Simeon: Jamuel and Jamin and Ahod, and Jachin and Sohar, and Saul the son of a woman of Chanaan.

11.text: The sons of Levi: Gerson and Caath and Merari.

12.text: The sons of Juda: Her and Onan and Sela and Phares and Zara. And Her and Onan died in the land of Chanaan. And sons were born to Phares: Hesron and Hamul.

13.text: The sons of Issachar: Thola and Phua and Job and Semron.

14.text: The sons of Zabulon: Sared and Elon and Jahelel.

15.text: These are the sons of Lia, whom she bore in Mesopotamia of Syria, with Dina his daughter. All the souls of her sons and daughters, thirty-three.

16.text: The sons of Gad: Sephian and Haggi and Suni and Esebon and Heri and Arodi and Areli.

17.text: The sons of Aser: Jamne and Jesua and Jessuri and Beria, and Sara their sister. The sons of Beria: Heber and Melchiel.

18.text: These are the sons of Zelpha, whom Laban gave to Lia his daughter. And these she bore to Jacob, sixteen souls.

19.text: The sons of Rachel Jacob’s wife: Joseph and Benjamin.

20.text: And sons were born to Joseph, in the land of Egypt, whom Aseneth the daughter of Putiphare priest of Heliopolis bore him: Manasses and Ephraim.

21.text: The sons of Benjamin: Bela and Bechor and Asbel and Gera and Naaman and Echi and Ros and Mophim and Ophim and Ared.

22.text: These are the sons of Rachel, whom she bore to Jacob: all the souls, fourteen.

23.text: The sons of Dan: Husim.

24.text: The sons of Nephtali: Jaziel and Guni and Jeser and Sallem.

25.text: These are the sons of Bala, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter: and these she bore to Jacob: all the souls, seven.

26.text: All the souls that went with Jacob into Egypt, and that came out of his thigh, besides his sons’ wives, sixty-six.

27.text: And the sons of Joseph, that were born to him in the land of Egypt, two souls. All the souls of the house of Jacob, that entered into Egypt, were seventy.

28.text: And he sent Juda before him to Joseph, to tell him; and that he should meet him in Gessen.

29.text: And when he was come thither, Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet his father, in the same place: and seeing him, he fell upon his neck, and embracing him wept.

30.text: And the father said to Joseph: Now shall I die with joy, because I have seen thy face, and leave thee alive.

31.text: And Joseph said to his brethren, and to all his father’s house: I will go up, and will tell Pharao, and will say to him: My brethren and my father’s house, that were in the land of Chanaan, are come to me:

32.text: And the men are shepherds, and their occupation is to feed cattle: their flocks and herds, and all they have, they have brought with them.

33.text: And when he shall call you, and shall say: What is your occupation?

34.text: You shall answer: We thy servants are shepherds, from our infancy until now, both we and our fathers. And this you shall say, that you may dwell in the land of Gessen, because the Egyptians have all shepherds in abomination.

1.text: Then Joseph went in and told Pharao, saying: My father and brethren, their sheep and their herds, and all that they possess, are come out of the land of Chanaan: and behold they stay in the land of Gessen.

2.text: Five men also the last of his brethren, he presented before the king:

3.text: And he asked them: What is your occupation? They answered: We thy servants are shepherds, both we, and our fathers.

4.text: We are come to sojourn in thy land, because there is no grass for the flocks of thy servants, the famine being very grievous in the land of Chanaan: and we pray thee to give orders that we thy servants may be in the land of Gessen.

5.text: The king therefore said to Joseph: Thy father and thy brethren are come to thee.

6.text: The land of Egypt is before thee: make them dwell in the best place, and give them the land of Gessen. And if thou knowest that there are industrious men among them, make them rulers over my cattle.

7.text: After this Joseph brought in his father to the king, and presented him before him: and he blessed him.

8.text: And being asked by him: How many are the days of the years of thy life?

9.text: He answered: The days of my pilgrimage are a hundred and thirty years, few, and evil, and they are not come up to the days of the pilgrimage of my fathers.

10.text: And blessing the king, he went out.

11.text: But Joseph gave a possession to his father and his brethren in Egypt, in the best place of the land, in Ramesses, as Pharao had commanded.

12.text: And he nourished them, and all his father’s house, allowing food to every one.

13.text: For in the whole world there was want of bread, and a famine had oppressed the land: more especially of Egypt and Chanaan.

14.text: Out of which he gathered up all the money for the corn which they bought, and brought it into the king’s treasure.

15.text: And when the buyers wanted money, all Egypt came to Joseph, saying: Give us bread: why should we die in thy presence, having now no money.

16.text: And he answered them: Bring me your cattle, and for them I will give you food, if you have no money.

17.text: And when they had brought them, he gave them food in exchange for their horses, and sheep, and oxen, and asses and he maintained them that year for the exchange of their cattle.

18.text: And they came the second year, and said to him: We will not hide from our lord, how that our money is spent, and our cattle also are gone: neither art thou ignorant that we have nothing now left but our bodies and our lands.

19.text: Why therefore shall we die before thy eyes? we will be thine, both we and our lands: buy us to be the king’s servants, and give us seed, lest for want of tillers the land be turned into a wilderness.

20.text: So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt, every man selling his possessions, because of the greatness of the famine. And he brought it into Pharao’s hands:

21.text: And all its people from one end of the borders of Egypt, even to the other end thereof,

22.text: Except the land of the priests, which had been given them by the king: to whom also a certain allowance of food was given out of the public stores, and therefore they were not forced to sell their possessions.

23.text: Then Joseph said to the people: Behold as you see, both you and your lands belong to Pharao: take seed and sow the fields,

24.text: That you may have corn. The fifth part you shall give to the king: the other four you shall have for seed, and for food for your families and children.

25.text: And they answered: Our life is in thy hand: only let my lord look favourably upon us, and we will gladly serve the king.

26.text: From that time unto this day, in the whole land of Egypt, the fifth part is paid to the king, and it is become as a law, except the land of the priests, which was free from this covenant.

27.text: So Israel dwelt in Egypt, that is, in the land of Gessen, and possessed it: and grew, and was multiplied exceedingly.

28.text: And he lived in it seventeen years: and all the days of his life came to a hundred and forty-seven years.

29.text: And when he saw that the day of his death drew nigh, he called his son Joseph, and said to him: If I have found favour in thy sight, put thy hand under my thigh; and thou shalt shew me this kindness and truth, not to bury me in Egypt:

30.text: But I will sleep with my fathers, and thou shalt take me away out of this land, and bury me in the burying place of my ancestors. And Joseph answered him: I will do what thou hast commanded.

31.text: And he said: Swear then to me. And as he was swearing, Israel adored God, turning to the bed’s head.

1.text: After these things, it was told Joseph that his father was sick: and he set out to go to him, taking his two sons Manasses and Ephraim.

2.text: And it was told the old man: Behold thy son Joseph cometh to thee. And being strengthened he sat on his bed.

3.text: And when Joseph was come in to him, he said: God Almighty appeared to me at Luza, which is in the land of Chanaan: and he blessed me,

4.text: And he said: I will cause thee to increase and multiply, and I will make of thee a multitude of people: and I will give this land to thee, and to thy seed after thee for an everlasting possession.

5.text: So thy two sons who were born to thee in the land of Egypt before I came hither to thee, shall be mine: Ephraim and Manasses shall be reputed to me as Ruben and Simeon.

6.text: But the rest whom thou shalt have after them, shall be thine, and shall be called by the name of their brethren in their possessions.

7.text: For, when I came out of Mesopotamia, Rachel died from me in the land of Chanaan in the very journey, and it was springtime: and I was going to Ephrata, and I buried her near the way of Ephrata, which by another name is called Bethlehem.

8.text: Then seeing his sons, he said to him: Who are these?

9.text: He answered: They are my sons, whom God hath given me in this place. And he said: Bring them to me that I may bless them.

10.text: For Israel’s eyes were dim by reason of his great age, and he could not see clearly. And when they were brought to him, he kissed and embraced them.

11.text: And said to his son: I am not deprived of seeing thee: moreover God hath shewed me thy seed.

12.text: And when Joseph had taken them from his father’s lap, he bowed down with his face to the ground.

13.text: And he set Ephraim on his right hand, that is, towards the left hand of Israel; but Manasses on his left hand, to wit, towards his father’s right hand, and brought them near to him.

14.text: But he stretching forth his right hand, put it upon the head of Ephraim the younger brother; and the left upon the head of Manasses who was the elder, changing his hands.

15.text: And Jacob blessed the sons of Joseph, and said: God, in whose sight my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, God that feedeth me from my youth until this day;

16.text: The angel that delivereth me from all evils, bless these boys: and let my name be called upon them, and the names of my fathers Abraham, and Isaac, and may they grow into a multitude upon the earth.

17.text: And Joseph seeing that his father had put his right hand upon the head of Ephraim, was much displeased: and taking his father’s hand he tried to lift it from Ephraim’s head, and to remove it to the head of Manasses.

18.text: And he said to his father: It should not be so, my father: for this is the firstborn, put thy right hand upon his head.

19.text: But he refusing, said: I know, my son, I know: and this also shall become peoples, and shall be multiplied: but this younger brother shall be greater than he: and his seed shall grow into nations.

20.text: And he blessed them at that time, saying: In thee shall Israel be blessed, and it shall be said: God do to thee as to Ephraim, and as to Manasses. And he set Ephraim before Manasses.

21.text: And he said to Joseph his son: Behold I die, and God will be with you, and will bring you back into the land of your fathers.

22.text: I give thee a portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorrhite with my sword and bow.

1.text: And Jacob called his sons, and said to them: Gather yourselves together that I may tell you the things that shall befall you in the last days.

2.text: Gather yourselves together, and hear, O ye sons of Jacob, hearken to Israel your father:

3.text: Ruben, my firstborn, thou art my strength, and the beginning of my sorrow: excelling in gifts, greater in command.

4.text: Thou art poured out as water, grow thou not: because thou wentest up to thy father’s bed, and didst defile his couch.

5.text: Simeon and Levi brethren: vessels of iniquity, waging war.

6.text: Let not my soul go into their counsel, nor my glory be in their assembly: because in their fury they slew a man, and in their selfwill they undermined a wall.

7.text: Cursed be their fury, because it was stubborn: and their wrath because it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and will scatter them in Israel.

8.text: Juda, thee shall thy brethren praise: thy hands shall be on the necks of thy enemies: the sons of thy father shall bow down to thee.

9.text: Juda is a lion’s whelp: to the prey, my son, thou art gone up: resting thou hast couched as a lion, and as a lioness, who shall rouse him?

10.text: The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations.

11.text: Tying his foal to the vineyard, and his ass, O my son, to the vine. He shall wash his robe in wine, and his garment in the blood of the grape.

12.text: His eyes are more beautiful than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.

13.text: Zabulon shall dwell on the sea shore, and in the road of ships, reaching as far as Sidon.

14.text: Issachar shall be a strong ass lying down between the borders.

15.text: He saw rest that it was good: and the land that it was excellent: and he bowed his shoulder to carry, and became a servant under tribute.

16.text: Dan shall judge his people like another tribe in Israel.

17.text: Let Dan be a snake in the way, a serpent in the path, that biteth the horse’s heels that his rider may fall backward.

18.text: I will look for thy salvation, O Lord.

19.text: Gad, being girded, shall fight before him: and he himself shall be girded backward.

20.text: Aser, his bread shall be fat, and he shall yield dainties to kings.

21.text: Nephtali, a hart let loose, and giving words of beauty.

22.text: Joseph is a growing son, a growing son and comely to behold; the daughters run to and fro upon the wall.

23.text: But they that held darts provoked him, and quarrelled with him, and envied him.

24.text: His bow rested upon the strong, and the bands of his arms and his hands were loosed, by the hands of the mighty one of Jacob: thence he came forth a pastor, the stone of Israel.

25.text: The God of thy father shall be thy helper, and the Almighty shall bless thee with the blessings of heaven above, with the blessings of the deep that lieth beneath, with the blessings of the breasts and of the womb.

26.text: The blessings of thy father are strengthened with the blessings of his fathers: until the desire of the everlasting hills should come; may they be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren.

27.text: Benjamin a ravenous wolf, in the morning shall eat the prey, and in the evening shall divide the spoil.

28.text: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel: these things their father spoke to them, and he blessed every one, with their proper blessings.

29.text: And he charged them, saying: I am now going to be gathered to my people: bury me with my fathers in the double cave, which is in the field of Ephron the Hethite,

30.text: Over against Mambre in the land of Chanaan, which Abraham bought together with the field of Ephron the Hethite for a possession to bury in.

31.text: There they buried him, and Sara his wife: there was Isaac buried with Rebecca his wife: there also Lia doth lie buried.

33.text: And when he had ended the commandments, wherewith he instructed his sons, he drew up his feet upon the bed, and died: and he was gathered to his people.

1.text: And when Joseph saw this, he fell upon his father’s face weeping and kissing him.

2.text: And he commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father.

3.text: And while they were fulfilling his commands, there passed forty days: for this was the manner with bodies that were embalmed, and Egypt mourned for him seventy days.

4.text: And the time of the mourning being expired, Joseph spoke to the family of Pharao: If I have found favour in your sight, speak in the ears of Pharao:

5.text: For my father made me swear to him, saying: Behold I die: thou shalt bury me in my sepulchre which I have digged for myself in the land of Chanaan. So I will go up and bury my father, and return.

6.text: And Pharao said to him: Go up and bury thy father according as he made thee swear.

7.text: So he went up, and there went with him all the ancients of Pharao’s house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,

8.text: And the house of Joseph with his brethren, except their children, and their flocks and herds, which they left in the land of Gessen.

9.text: He had also in his train chariots and horsemen: and it was a great company.

10.text: And they came to the threshingfloor of Atad, which is situated beyond the Jordan: where celebrating the exequies with a great and vehement lamentation, they spent full seven days.

11.text: And when the inhabitants of Chanaan saw this, they said: This is a great mourning to the Egyptians. And therefore the name of that place was called, The mourning of Egypt.

12.text: So the sons of Jacob did as he had commanded them.

13.text: And carrying him into the land of Chanaan, they buried him in the double cave which Abraham had bought together with the field for a possession of a buryingplace, of Ephron the Hethite over against Mambre.

14.text: And Joseph returned into Egypt with his brethren, and all that were in his company, after he had buried his father.

15.text: Now he being dead, his brethren were afraid, and talked one with another: Lest perhaps he should remember the wrong he suffered, and requite us all the evil that we did to him.

16.text: And they sent a message to him, saying: Thy father commanded us before he died,

17.text: That we should say thus much to thee from him: I beseech thee to forget the wickedness of thy brethren, and the sin and malice they practiced against thee: we also pray thee, to forgive the servants of the God of thy father this wickedness. And when Joseph heard this, he wept.

18.text: And his brethren came to him: and worshipping prostrate on the ground they said: We are thy servants.

19.text: And he answered them: Fear not: can we resist the will of God?

20.text: You thought evil against me: but God turned it into good, that he might exalt me, as at present you see, and might save many people.

21.text: Fear not: I will feed you and your children. And he comforted them, and spoke gently and mildly.

22.text: And he dwelt in Egypt with all his father’s house: and lived a hundred and ten years. And he saw the children of Ephraim to the third generation. The children also of Machir the son of Manasses were born on Joseph’s knees.

24.text: After which he told his brethren: God will visit you after my death, and will make you go up out of this land, to the land which he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

25.text: And he made them swear to him, saying: God will visit you, carry my bones with you out of this place:

26.text: And he died being a hundred and ten years old. And being embalmed he was laid in a coffin in Egypt.

1.text: These are the names of the children of Israel, that went into Egypt with Jacob: they went in, every man with his household:

2.text: Ruben, Simeon, Levi, Juda,

3.text: Issachar, Zabulon, and Benjamin,

4.text: Dan, and Nephtali, Gad and Aser.

5.text: And all the souls that came out of Jacob’s thigh, were seventy: but Joseph was in Egypt.

6.text: After he was dead, and all his brethren, and all that generation,

7.text: The children of Israel increased, and sprung up into multitudes, and growing exceedingly strong they filled the land.

8.text: In the mean time there arose a new king over Egypt, that knew not Joseph:

9.text: And he said to his people: Behold the people of the children of Israel are numerous and stronger than we.

10.text: Come, let us wisely oppress them, lest they multiply: and if any war shall rise against us, join with our enemies, and having overcome us, depart out of the land.

11.text: Therefore he set over them masters of the works, to afflict them with burdens, and they built for Pharao cities of tabernacles, Phithom and Ramesses.

12.text: But the more they oppressed them, the more they were multiplied, and increased:

13.text: And the Egyptians hated the children of Israel, and afflicted them and mocked them:

14.text: And they made their life bitter with hard works in clay, and brick, and with all manner of service, wherewith they were overcharged in the works of the earth.

15.text: And the king of Egypt spoke to the midwives of the Hebrews: of whom one was called Sephora, the other Phua,

16.text: Commanding them: When you shall do the office of midwives to the Hebrew women, and the time of delivery is come: if it be a man child, kill it: if a woman, keep it alive.

17.text: But the midwives feared God, and did not do as the king of Egypt had commanded, but saved the men children.

18.text: And the king called for them and said: What is that you meant to do, that you would save the men children?

19.text: They answered: The Hebrew women are not as the Egyptian women: for they themselves are skillful in the office of a midwife; and they are delivered before we come to them.

20.text: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied and grew exceedingly strong.

21.text: And because the midwives feared God, he built them houses.

22.text: Pharao therefore charged all his people, saying: Whatsoever shall be born of the male sex, ye shall cast into the river: whatsoever of the female, ye shall save alive.

1.text: After this there went a man of the house of Levi; and took a wife of his own kindred.

2.text: And she conceived, and bore a son; and seeing him a goodly child hid him three months.

3.text: And when she could hide him no longer, she took a basket made of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and pitch: and put the little babe therein, and laid him in the sedges by the river’s brink,

4.text: His sister standing afar off, and taking notice what would be done.

5.text: And behold the daughter of Pharao came down to wash herself in the river: and her maids walked by the river’s brink. And when she saw the basket in the sedges, she sent one of her maids for it: and when it was brought,

6.text: She opened it and seeing within it an infant crying, having compassion on it she said: This is one of the babes of the Hebrews.

7.text: And the child’s sister said to her Shall I go and call to thee a Hebrew woman, to nurse the babe?

8.text: She answered: Go. The maid went and called her mother.

9.text: And Pharao’s daughter said to her. Take this child and nurse him for me: I will give thee thy wages. The woman took, and nursed the child: and when he was grown up, she delivered him to Pharao’s daughter.

10.text: And she adopted him for a son, and called him Moses, saying: Because I took him out of the water.

11.text: In those days after Moses was grown up, he went out to his brethren: and saw their affliction, and an Egyptian striking one of the Hebrews his brethren.

12.text: And when he had looked about this way and that way, and saw no one there, he slew the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.

13.text: And going out the next day, he saw two Hebrews quarrelling: and he said to him that did the wrong: Why strikest thou thy neighbour?

14.text: But he answered: Who hath appointed thee prince and judge over us? Wilt thou kill me, as thou didst yesterday kill the Egyptian? Moses feared, and said: How is this come to be known?

15.text: And Pharao heard of this word and sought to kill Moses: but he fled from his sight, and abode in the land of Madian, and he sat down by a well.

16.text: And the priest of Madian had seven daughters, who came to draw water: and when the troughs were filled, desired to water their father’s flocks.

17.text: And the shepherds came and drove them away: and Moses arose, and defending the maids, watered their sheep.

18.text: And when they returned to Raguel their father, he said to them: Why are ye come sooner than usual?

19.text: They answered: A man of Egypt delivered us from the hands of the shepherds: and he drew water also with us, and gave the sheep to drink.

20.text: But he said: Where is he? why have you let the man go? call him that he may eat bread.

21.text: And Moses swore that he would dwell with him. And he took Sephora his daughter to wife:

22.text: And she bore him a son, whom he called Gersam, saying: I have been a stranger in a foreign country. And she bore another, whom he called Eliezer, saying: For the God of my father, my helper hath delivered me out of the hand of Pharao.

23.text: Now after a long time the king of Egypt died: and the children of Israel groaning, cried out because of the works: and their cry went up unto God from the works.

24.text: And he heard their groaning, and remembered the covenant which he made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

25.text: And the Lord looked upon the children of Israel, and he knew them.

1.text: Now Moses fed the sheep of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Madian: and he drove the flock to the inner parts of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, Horeb.

2.text: And the Lord appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he saw that the bush was on fire and was not burnt.

3.text: And Moses said: I will go and see this great sight, why the bush is not burnt.

4.text: And when the Lord saw that he went forward to see, he called to him out of the midst of the bush, and said: Moses, Moses. And he answered: Here I am.

5.text: And he said: Come not nigh hither, put off the shoes from thy feet: for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

6.text: And he said: I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. Moses hid his face: for he durst not look at God.

7.text: And the Lord said to him: I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, and I have heard their cry because of the rigour of them that are over the works:

8.text: And knowing their sorrow, I am come down to deliver them out of the hands of the Egyptians, and to bring them out of that land into a good and spacious land, into a land that floweth with milk and honey, to the places of the Chanaanite, and Hethite, and Amorrhite, and Pherezite, and Hevite, and Jebusite.

9.text: For the cry of the children of Israel is come unto me: and I have seen their affliction, wherewith they are oppressed by the Egyptians.

10.text: But come, and I will send thee to Pharao, that thou mayst bring forth my people, the children of Israel out of Egypt.

11.text: And Moses said to God: Who am I that I should go to Pharao, and should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt?

12.text: And he said to him: I will be with thee: and this thou shalt have for a sign, that I have sent thee: When thou shalt have brought my people out of Egypt, thou shalt offer sacrifice to God upon this mountain.

13.text: Moses said to God: Lo, I shall go to the children of Israel, and say to them: The God of your fathers hath sent me to you. If they should say to me: What is his name? what shall I say to them?

14.text: God said to Moses: I AM WHO AM. He said: Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: HE WHO IS, hath sent me to you.

15.text: And God said again to Moses: Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath sent me to you: This is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.

16.text: Go, gather together the ancients of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared to me, saying: Visiting I have visited you: and I have seen all that hath befallen you in Egypt.

17.text: And I have said the word to bring you forth out of the affliction of Egypt, into the land of the Chanaanite, the Hethite, and the Amorrhite, and Pherezite, and Hevite, and Jebusite, to a land that floweth with milk and honey.

18.text: And they shall hear thy voice: and thou shalt go in, thou and the ancients of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and thou shalt say to him: The Lord God of the Hebrews hath called us: we will go three days’ journey into the wilderness, to sacrifice unto the Lord our God.

19.text: But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go, but by a mighty hand.

20.text: For I will stretch forth my hand and will strike Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst of them: after these he will let you go.

21.text: And I will give favour to this people, in the sight of the Egyptians: and when you go forth, you shall not depart empty:

22.text: But every woman shall ask of her neighbour, and of her that is in her house, vessels of silver and of gold, and raiment: and you shall put them on your sons and daughters, and shall spoil Egypt.

1.text: Moses answered and said: They will not believe me, nor hear my voice, but they will say: The Lord hath not appeared to thee.

2.text: Then he said to him: What is that thou holdest in thy hand? He answered: A rod.

3.text: And the Lord said: Cast it down upon the ground. He cast it down, and it was turned into a serpent: so that Moses fled from it.

4.text: And the Lord said: Put out thy hand and take it by the tail. He put forth his hand, and took hold of it, and it was turned into a rod.

5.text: That they may believe, saith he, that the Lord God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared to thee.

6.text: And the Lord said again: Put thy hand into thy bosom. And when he had put it into his bosom, he brought it forth leprous as snow.

7.text: And he said: Put back thy hand into thy bosom. He put it back, and brought it out again, and it was like the other flesh.

8.text: If they will not believe thee, saith he, nor hear the voice of the former sign, they will believe the word of the latter sign.

9.text: But if they will not even believe these two signs, nor hear thy voice: take of the river water, and pour it out upon the dry land, and whatsoever thou drawest out of the river shall be turned into blood.

10.text: Moses said: I beseech thee, Lord. I am not eloquent from yesterday and the day before: and since thou hast spoken to thy servant, I have more impediment and slowness of tongue.

11.text: The Lord said to him: Who made man’s mouth? or who made the dumb and the deaf, the seeing and the blind? did not I?

12.text: Go therefore and I will be in thy mouth: and I will teach thee what thou shalt speak.

13.text: But he said: I beseech thee, Lord send whom thou wilt send.

14.text: The Lord being angry at Moses, said Aaron the Levite is thy brother, I know that he is eloquent: behold he cometh forth to meet thee, and seeing thee shall be glad at heart.

15.text: Speak to him, and put my words in his mouth: and I will be in thy mouth, and in his mouth, and will shew you what you must do.

16.text: He shall speak in thy stead to the people, and shall be thy mouth: but thou shalt be to him in those things that pertain to God.

17.text: And take this rod in thy hand, wherewith thou shalt do the signs.

18.text: Moses went his way, and returned to Jethro his father in law and said to him: I will go and return to my brethren into Egypt, that I may see if they be yet alive. And Jethro said to him: Go in peace.

19.text: And the Lord said to Moses, in Madian: Go, and return into Egypt: for they are all dead that sought thy life.

20.text: Moses therefore took his wife, and his sons, and set them upon an ass: and returned into Egypt, carrying the rod of God in his hand.

21.text: And the Lord said to him as he was returning into Egypt: See that thou do all the wonders before Pharao, which I have put in thy hand: I shall harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.

22.text: And thou shalt say to him: Thus saith the Lord: Israel is my son, my firstborn.

23.text: I have said to thee: Let my son go, that he may serve me, and thou wouldst not let him go: behold I will kill thy son, thy firstborn.

24.text: And when he was in his journey, in the inn, the Lord met him, and would have killed him.

25.text: Immediately Sephora took a very sharp stone, and circumcised the fore skin of her son, and touched his feet and said: A bloody spouse art thou to me.

26.text: And he let him go after she had said A bloody spouse art thou to me, because of the circumcision.

27.text: And the Lord said to Aaron: Go into the desert to meet Moses. And he went forth to meet him in the mountain of God, and kissed him.

28.text: And Moses told Aaron all the words of the Lord, by which he had sent him, and the signs that he had commanded.

29.text: And they came together, and they assembled all the ancients of the children of Israel.

30.text: And Aaron spoke all the words which the Lord had said to Moses: and he wrought the signs before the people,

31.text: And the people believed. And they heard that the Lord had visited the children of Israel: and that he had looked upon their affliction: and falling down they adored.

1.text: After these things Moses and Aaron went in, and said to Pharao: Thus saith the Lord God of Israel: Let my people go that they may sacrifice to me in the desert.

2.text: But he answered: Who is the Lord, that I should hear his voice, and let Israel go? I know not the Lord, neither will I let Israel go.

3.text: And they said: The God of the Hebrews hath called us, to go three days’ journey into the wilderness and to sacrifice to the Lord our God: lest a pestilence or the sword fall upon us.

4.text: The king of Egypt said to them: Why do you Moses and Aaron draw off the people from their works? Get you gone to your burdens.

5.text: And Pharao said: The people of the land is numerous: you see that the multitude is increased: how much more if you give them rest from their works?

6.text: Therefore he commanded the same day the overseers of the works, and the taskmasters of the people, saying:

7.text: You shall give straw no more to the people to make brick, as before: but let them go and gather straw.

8.text: And you shall lay upon them the task of bricks, which they did before, neither shall you diminish any thing thereof: for they are idle, and therefore they cry, saying: Let us go and sacrifice to our God.

9.text: Let them be oppressed, with works, and let them fulfill them: that they may not regard lying words.

10.text: And the overseers of the works and the taskmasters went out and said to the people: Thus saith Pharao, I allow you no straw:

11.text: Go, and gather it where you can find it: neither shall any thing of your work be diminished.

12.text: And the people was scattered through all the land of Egypt to gather straw.

13.text: And the overseers of the works pressed them, saying: Fulfill your work every day as before you were wont to do when straw was given you.

14.text: And they that were over the works of the children of Israel were scourged by Pharao’s taskmasters, saying: Why have you not made up the task of bricks both yesterday and today as before?

15.text: And the officers of the children of Israel came, and cried out to Pharao, saying: Why dealest thou so with thy servants?

16.text: Straw is not given us, and bricks are required of us as before: behold we thy servants are beaten with whips, and thy people is unjustly dealt withal.

17.text: And he said: You are idle, and therefore you say: Let us go and sacrifice to the Lord.

18.text: Go therefore, and work: straw shall not be given you, and you shall deliver the accustomed number of bricks.

19.text: And the officers of the children of Israel saw that they were in evil case, because it was said to them: There shall not a whit be diminished of the bricks for every day.

20.text: And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood over against them as they came out from Pharao:

21.text: And they said to them: The Lord see and judge, because you have made our savour to stink before Pharao and his servants, and you have given him a sword to kill us.

22.text: And Moses returned to the Lord, and said: Lord, why hast thou afflicted this people? wherefore hast thou sent me?

23.text: For since the time that I went in to Pharao to speak in thy name, he hath afflicted thy people: and thou hast not delivered them.

1.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Now thou shalt see what I will do to Pharao: for by a mighty hand shall he let them go, and with a strong hand shall he cast them out of his land.

2.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: I am the Lord,

3.text: That appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, by the name of God Almighty; and my name ADONAI I did not shew them.

4.text: And I made a covenant with them, to give them the land of Chanaan, the land of their pilgrimage wherein they were strangers.

5.text: I have heard the groaning of the children of Israel, wherewith the Egyptians have oppressed them: and I have remembered my covenant.

6.text: Therefore say to the children of Israel: I am the Lord who will bring you out from the work prison of the Egyptians, and will deliver you from bondage: and redeem you with a high arm, and great judgments.

7.text: And I will take you to myself for my people, I will be your God: and you shall know that I am the Lord your God who brought you out from the work prison of the Egyptians.

8.text: And brought you into the land, concerning which I lifted up my hand to give it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and I will give it you to possess, I am the Lord.

9.text: And Moses told all this to the children of Israel: but they did not hearken to him, for anguish of spirit, and most painful work.

10.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

11.text: Go in, and speak to Pharao king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.

12.text: Moses answered before the Lord Behold the children of Israel do not hearken to me; and how will Pharao hear me, especially as I am of uncircumcised lips?

13.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, and he gave them a charge unto the children of Israel, and unto Pharao the king of Egypt, that they should bring forth the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.

14.text: These are the heads of their house by their families. The sons of Ruben the firstborn of Israel: Henoch and Phallu, Hesron and Charmi.

15.text: These are the kindreds of Ruben. The sons of Simeon: Jamuel, and Jamin and Ahod, and Jachin, and Soar, and Saul the son of a Chanaanitess: these are the families of Simeon.

16.text: And these are the names of the sons of Levi by their kindreds: Gerson, and Caath, and Merari. And the years of the life of Levi were a hundred and thirty seven.

17.text: The sons of Gerson: Lobni and Semei, by their kindreds.

18.text: The sons of Caath: Amram, and Isaar, and Hebron, and Oziel. And the years of Caath’s life were a hundred and thirty-three.

19.text: The sons of Merari: Moholi and Musi. These are the kindreds of Levi by their families.

20.text: And Amram took to wife Jochabed his aunt by the father’s side: and she bore him Aaron and Moses. And the years of Amram’s life were a hundred and thirty-seven.

21.text: The sons also of Isaar: Core, and Nepheg, and Zechri.

22.text: The sons also of Oziel: Mizael, and Elizaphan, and Sethri.

23.text: And Aaron took to wife Elizabeth the daughter of Aminadab, sister of Nahason, who bore him Nadab, and Abiu, and Eleazar, and Ithamar.

24.text: The sons also of Core: Aser, and Elcana, and Abiasaph. These are the kindreds of the Corites.

25.text: But Eleazar the son of Aaron took a wife of the daughters of Phutiel: and she bore him Phinees. These are the heads of the Levitical families by their kindreds.

26.text: These are Aaron and Moses, whom the Lord commanded to bring forth the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their companies.

27.text: These are they that speak to Pharao king of Egypt, in order to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt: these are that Moses and Aaron,

28.text: In the day when the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt.

29.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: I am the Lord: speak thou to Pharao king of Egypt all that I say to thee.

30.text: And Moses said before the Lord: Lo I am of uncircumcised lips, how will Pharao hear me?

1.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Behold I have appointed thee the God of Pharao: and Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.

2.text: Thou shalt speak to him all that I command thee; and he shall speak to Pharao, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.

3.text: But I shall harden his heart, and shall multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt,

4.text: And he will not hear you: and I will lay my hand upon Egypt, and will bring forth my army and my people the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt, by very great judgments.

5.text: And the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, who have stretched forth my hand upon Egypt, and have brought forth the children of Israel out of the midst of them.

6.text: And Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had commanded: so did they.

7.text: And Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three, when they spoke to Pharao.

8.text: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:

9.text: When Pharao shall say to you, shew signs: thou shalt say to Aaron: Take thy rod, and cast it down before Pharao, and it shall be turned into a serpent.

10.text: So Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharao, and did as the Lord had commanded. And Aaron took the rod before Pharao, and his servants, and it was turned into a serpent.

11.text: And Pharao called the wise men and the magicians: and they also by Egyptian enchantments and certain secrets did in like manner.

12.text: And they every one cast down their rods, and they were turned into serpents: but Aaron’s rod devoured their rods.

13.text: And Pharao’s heart was hardened, and he did not hearken to them, as the Lord had commanded.

14.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Pharao’s heart is hardened, he will not let the people go.

15.text: Go to him in the morning, behold he will go out to the waters: and thou shalt stand to meet him on the bank of the river: and thou shalt take in thy hand the rod that was turned into a serpent.

16.text: And thou shalt say to him: The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to thee saying: Let my people go to sacrifice to me in the desert: and hitherto thou wouldst not hear.

17.text: Thus therefore saith the Lord: In this thou shalt know that I am the Lord: behold I will strike with the rod that is in my hand, the water of the river, and it shall be turned into blood.

18.text: And the fishes that are in the river shall die, and the waters shall be corrupted, and the Egyptians shall be afflicted when they drink the water of the river.

19.text: The Lord also said to Moses: Say to Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch forth thy hand upon the waters of Egypt, and upon their rivers, and streams and pools, and all the ponds of waters, that they may be turned into blood: and let blood be in all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood and of stone.

20.text: And Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had commanded: and lifting up the rod he struck the water of the river before Pharao and his servants: and it was turned into blood.

21.text: And the fishes that were in the river died: and the river corrupted, and the Egyptians could not drink the water of the river, and there was blood in all the land of Egypt.

22.text: And the magicians of the Egyptians with their enchantments did in like manner: and Pharao’s heart was hardened, neither did he hear them, as the Lord had commanded.

23.text: And he turned himself away and went into his house, neither did he set his heart to it this time also.

24.text: And all the Egyptians dug round about the river for water to drink: for they could not drink of the water of the river.

25.text: And seven days were fully ended, after that the Lord struck the river.

1.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharao, and thou shalt say to him: Thus saith the Lord: Let my people go to sacrifice to me.

2.text: But if thou wilt not let them go behold I will strike all thy coasts with frogs.

3.text: And the river shall bring forth an abundance of frogs: which shall come up, and enter into thy house, and thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and in the houses of thy servants, and to thy people, and into thy ovens, and into the remains of thy meats;

4.text: And the frogs shall come in to thee and to thy people, and to all thy servants.

5.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Say to Aaron, Stretch forth thy hand upon the streams and upon the rivers and the pools, and bring forth frogs upon the land of Egypt.

6.text: And Aaron stretched forth his hand upon the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up, and covered the land of Egypt.

7.text: And the magicians also by their enchantments did in like manner, and they brought forth frogs upon all the land of Egypt.

8.text: But Pharao called Moses and Aaron and said to them: Pray ye to the Lord to take away the frogs from me and from my people; and I will let the people go to sacrifice to the Lord.

9.text: And Moses said to Pharao: Set me a time when I shall pray for thee, and for thy servants, and for thy people, that the frogs may be driven away from thee and from thy house, and from thy servants, and from thy people: and may remain only in the river.

10.text: And he answered: Tomorrow. But he said: I will do according to thy word; that thou mayst know that there is none like to the Lord our God.

11.text: And the frogs shall depart from thee, and from thy house, and from thy servants, and from thy people; and shall remain only in the river.

12.text: And Moses and Aaron went forth from Pharao: and Moses cried to the Lord for the promise, which he had made to Pharao concerning the frogs.

13.text: And the Lord did according to the word of Moses: and the frogs died out of the houses, and out of the villages, and out of the fields:

14.text: And they gathered them together into immense heaps, and the land was corrupted.

15.text: And Pharao seeing that rest was given, hardened his own heart, and did not hear them, as the Lord had commanded.

16.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Say to Aaron, Stretch forth thy rod, and strike the dust of the earth: and may there be sciniphs in all the land of Egypt.

17.text: And they did so. And Aaron stretched forth his hand, holding the rod: and he struck the dust of the earth, and there came sciniphs on men and on beasts: all the dust of the earth was turned into sciniphs through all the land of Egypt.

18.text: And the magicians with their enchantments practiced in like manner, to bring forth sciniphs, and they could not and there were sciniphs as well on men as on beasts.

19.text: And the magicians said to Pharao This is the finger of God. And Pharao heart was hardened, and he hearkened not unto them, as the Lord had commanded.

20.text: The Lord also said to Moses: Arise early, and stand before Pharao: for he will go forth to the waters: and thou shalt say to him: Thus saith the Lord: Let my people go to sacrifice to me.

21.text: But if thou wilt not let them go, behold I will send in upon thee, and upon thy servants, and upon thy houses all kind of flies: and the houses of the Egyptians shall be filled with flies of divers kinds, and the whole land wherein they shall be.

22.text: And I will make the land of Gessen wherein my people is, wonderful in that day, so that flies shall not be there: and thou shalt know that I am the Lord in the midst of the earth.

23.text: And I will put a division between my people and thy people: tomorrow shall this sign be.

24.text: And the Lord did so. And there came a very grievous swarm of flies into the houses of Pharao and of his servants, and into all the land of Egypt: and the land was corrupted by this kind of flies.

25.text: And Pharao called Moses and Aaron, and said to them: Go, and sacrifice to your God in this land.

26.text: And Moses said: It cannot be so: for we shall sacrifice the abominations of the Egyptians to the Lord our God: now if we kill those things which the Egyptians worship, in their presence, they will stone us.

27.text: We will go three days’ journey into the wilderness: and we will sacrifice to the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.

28.text: And Pharao said: I will let you go to sacrifice to the Lord your God in the wilderness: but go no farther: pray for me.

29.text: And Moses said: I will go out from thee, and will pray to the Lord: and the flies shall depart from Pharao, and from his servants, and from his people tomorrow: but do not deceive any more, in not letting the people go to sacrifice to the Lord.

30.text: So Moses went out from Pharao, and prayed to the Lord.

31.text: And he did according to his word: and he took away the flies from Pharao, and from his servants, and from his people: there was not left so much as one.

32.text: And Pharao’s heart was hardened, so that neither this time would he let the people go.

1.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharao, and speak to him: Thus saith the Lord God of the Hebrews: Let my people go to sacrifice to me.

2.text: But if thou refuse, and withhold them still:

3.text: Behold my hand shall be upon thy fields: and a very grievous murrain upon thy horses, and asses, and camels, and oxen, and sheep.

4.text: And the Lord will make a wonderful difference between the possessions of Israel and the possessions of the Egyptians, that nothing at all shall die of those things that belong to the children of Israel.

5.text: And the Lord appointed a time, saying: Tomorrow will the Lord do this thing in the land.

6.text: The Lord therefore did this thing the next day: and all the beasts of the Egyptians died, but of the beasts of the children of Israel there died not one.

7.text: And Pharao sent to see: and there was not any thing dead of that which Israel possessed. And Pharao’s heart was hardened, and he did not let the people go.

8.text: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take to you handfuls of ashes out of the chimney, and let Moses sprinkle it in the air in the presence of Pharao.

9.text: And be there dust upon all the land of Egypt: for there shall be boils and swelling blains both in men and beasts in the whole land of Egypt.

10.text: And they took ashes out of the chimney, and stood before Pharao, and Moses sprinkled it in the air: and there came boils with swelling blains in men and beasts.

11.text: Neither could the magicians stand before Moses for the boils that were upon them, and in all the land of Egypt.

12.text: And the Lord hardened Pharao’s heart, and he hearkened not unto them, as the Lord had spoken to Moses.

13.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Arise in the morning, and stand before Pharao, and thou shalt say to him: Thus saith the Lord the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go to sacrifice to me.

14.text: For I will at this time send all my plagues upon thy heart, and upon thy servants, and upon thy people: that thou mayst know there is none like me in all the earth.

15.text: For now I will stretch out my hand to strike thee, and thy people with pestilence, and thou shalt perish from the earth.

16.text: And therefore have I raised thee, that I may shew my power in thee, and my name may be spoken of throughout all the earth.

17.text: Dost thou yet hold back my people: and wilt thou not let them go?

18.text: Behold I will cause it to rain tomorrow at this same hour, an exceeding great hail: such as hath not been in Egypt from the day that it was founded, until this present time.

19.text: Send therefore now presently, and gather together thy cattle, and all that thou hast in the field: for men and beasts, and all things that shall be found abroad, and not gathered together out of the fields, which the hail shall fall upon, shall die.

20.text: He that feared the word of the Lord among Pharao’s servants, made his servants and his cattle flee into houses:

21.text: But he that regarded not the word of the Lord, left his servants and his cattle in the fields:

22.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch forth thy hand towards heaven, that there may be hail in the whole land of Egypt, upon men, and upon beasts, and upon every herb of the field in the land of Egypt.

23.text: And Moses stretched forth his rod towards heaven, and the Lord sent thunder and hail, and lightning running along the ground: and the Lord rained hail upon the land of Egypt.

24.text: And the hail and fire mixed with it drove on together: and it was of so great bigness, as never before was seen in the whole land of Egypt since that nation was founded.

25.text: And the hail destroyed through all the land of Egypt all things that were in the fields, both man and beast: and the hail smote every herb of the field, and it broke every tree of the country.

26.text: Only in the land of Gessen, where the children of Israel were, the hail fell not.

27.text: And Pharao sent and called Moses and Aaron, saying to them: I have sinned this time also; the Lord is just: I and my people are wicked.

28.text: Pray ye to the Lord, that the thunderings of God and the hail may cease: that I may let you go, and that you may stay here no longer.

29.text: Moses said: As soon as I am gone out of the city, I will stretch forth my hands to the Lord, and the thunders shall cease, and the hail shall be no more: that thou mayst know that the earth is the Lord’s.

30.text: But I know that neither thou, nor thy servants do yet fear the Lord God.

31.text: The flax therefore and the barley were hurt, because the barley was green, and the flax was now boiled:

32.text: But the wheat, and other winter corn were not hurt, because they were lateward.

33.text: And when Moses was gone from Pharao out of the city, he stretched forth his hands to the Lord: and the thunders and the hail ceased, neither did there drop any more rain upon the earth.

34.text: And Pharao seeing that the rain and the hail, and the thunders were ceased, increased his sin.

35.text: And his heart was hardened, and the heart of his servants, and it was made exceeding hard: neither did he let the children of Israel go, as the Lord had commanded by the hand of Moses.

1.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Go in to Pharao; for I have hardened his heart, and the heart of his servants: that I may work these my signs in him.

2.text: And thou mayest tell in the ears of thy sons, and of thy grandsons, how often I have plagued the Egyptians, and wrought my signs amongst them: and you may know that I am the Lord:

3.text: Therefore Moses and Aaron went in to Pharao, and said to him: Thus saith the Lord God of the Hebrews: How long refusest thou to submit to me? let my people go, to sacrifice to me.

4.text: But if thou resist, and wilt not let them go, behold I will bring in tomorrow the locust into thy coasts:

5.text: To cover the face of the earth that nothing thereof may appear, but that which the hail hath left may be eaten: for they shall feed upon all the trees that spring in the fields.

6.text: And they shall fill thy houses, and the houses of thy servants, and of all the Egyptians: such a number as thy fathers have not seen, nor thy grandfathers, from the time they were first upon the earth, until this present day. And he turned himself away, and went forth from Pharao.

7.text: And Pharao’s servants said to him: How long shall we endure this scandal? let the men go to sacrifice to the Lord their God. Dost thou not see that Egypt is undone?

8.text: And they called back Moses and Aaron to Pharao: and he said to them: Go, sacrifice to the Lord your God: who are they that shall go?

9.text: Moses said: We will go with our young and old, with our sons and daughters, with our sheep and herds: for it is the solemnity of the Lord our God.

10.text: And Pharao answered: So be the Lord with you, as I shall let you and your children go: who can doubt but that you intend some great evil?

11.text: It shall not be so: but go ye men only, and sacrifice to the Lord: for this yourselves also desired. And immediately they were cast out from Pharao’s presence.

12.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch forth thy hand upon the land of Egypt unto the locust, that it may come upon it, and devour every herb that is left after the hail.

13.text: And Moses stretched forth his rod upon the land of Egypt: and the Lord brought a burning wind all that day, and night: and when it was morning, the burning wind raised the locusts:

14.text: And they came up over the whole land of Egypt: and rested in all the coasts of the Egyptians innumerable, the like as had not been before that time, nor shall be hereafter.

15.text: And they covered the whole face of the earth, wasting all things. And the grass of the earth was devoured, and what fruits soever were on the trees, which the hail had left: and there remained not any thing that was green on the trees, or in the herbs of the earth in all Egypt.

16.text: Wherefore Pharao in haste called Moses and Aaron, and said to them: I have sinned against the Lord your God, and against you.

17.text: But now forgive me my sin this time also, and pray to the Lord your God, that he take away from me this death.

18.text: And Moses going forth from the presence of Pharao, prayed to the Lord.

19.text: And he made a very strong wind to blow from the west, and it took the locusts and cast them into the Red Sea: there remained not so much as one in all the coasts of Egypt.

20.text: And the Lord hardened Pharao’s heart, neither did he let the children of Israel go.

21.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Stretch out thy hand towards heaven: and may there be darkness upon the land of Egypt, so thick that it may be felt.

22.text: And Moses stretched forth his hand towards heaven: and there came horrible darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days.

23.text: No man saw his brother, nor moved himself out of the place where he was: but wheresoever the children of Israel dwelt there was light.

24.text: And Pharao called Moses and Aaron, and said to them: Go sacrifice to the Lord: let your sheep only, and herds remain; let your children go with you.

25.text: Moses said: Thou shalt give us also sacrifices and burnt offerings, to the Lord our God.

26.text: All the flocks shall go with us: there shall not a hoof remain of them: for they are necessary for the service of the Lord our God: especially as we know not what must be offered, till we come to the very place.

27.text: And the Lord hardened Pharao’s heart, and he would not let them go.

28.text: And Pharao said to Moses: Get thee from me, and beware thou see not my face any more: in what day soever thou shalt come in my sight, thou shalt die.

29.text: Moses answered: So shall it be as thou hast spoken, I will not see thy face any more.

1.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Yet one plague more will I bring upon Pharao and Egypt, and after that he shall let you go and thrust you out.

2.text: Therefore thou shalt tell all the people that every man ask of his friend, and every woman of her neighbour, vessels of silver, and of gold.

3.text: And the Lord will give favour to his people in the sight of the Egyptians. And Moses was a very great man in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharao’s servants, and of all the people.

4.text: And he said: Thus said the Lord: At midnight I will enter into Egypt.

5.text: And every firstborn in the land of the Egyptians shall die, from the firstborn of Pharao who sitteth on his throne, even to the first born of the handmaid that is at the mill, and all the firstborn of beasts.

6.text: And there shall be a great cry in all the land of Egypt, such as neither hath been before, nor shall be hereafter.

7.text: But with all the children of Israel there shall not a dog make the least noise, from man even to beast: that you may know how wonderful a difference the Lord maketh between the Egyptians and Israel.

8.text: And all these thy servants shall come down to me, and shall worship me, saying: Go forth thou, and all the people that is under thee: after that we will go out.

9.text: And he went out from Pharao exceeding angry. But the Lord said to Moses: Pharao will not hear you, that many signs may be done in the land of Egypt.

10.text: And Moses and Aaron did all the wonders that are written, before Pharao. And the Lord hardened Pharao’s heart, neither did he let the children of Israel go out of his land.

1.text: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt:

2.text: This month shall be to you the beginning of months: it shall be the first in the months of the year.

3.text: Speak ye to the whole assembly of the children of Israel, and say to them: On the tenth day of this month let every man take a lamb by their families and houses.

4.text: But if the number be less than may suffice to eat the lamb, he shall take unto him his neighbour that joineth to his house, according to the number of souls which may be enough to eat the lamb.

5.text: And it shall be a lamb without blemish, a male, of one year: according to which rite also you shall take a kid.

6.text: And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month: and the whole multitude of the children of Israel shall sacrifice it in the evening.

7.text: And they shall take of the blood thereof, and put it upon both the side posts, and on the upper door posts of the houses, wherein they shall eat it.

8.text: And they shall eat the flesh that night roasted at the fire, and unleavened bread with wild lettuce.

9.text: You shall not eat thereof any thing raw, nor boiled in water, but only roasted at the fire: you shall eat the head with the feet and entrails thereof.

10.text: Neither shall there remain any thing of it until morning. If there be any thing left, you shall burn it with fire.

11.text: And thus you shall eat it: you shall gird your reins, and you shall have shoes on your feet, holding staves in your hands, and you shall eat in haste: for it is the Phase (that is the Passage) of the Lord.

12.text: And I will pass through the land of Egypt that night, and will kill every firstborn in the land of Egypt both man and beast: and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am the Lord.

13.text: And the blood shall be unto you for a sign in the houses where you shall be: and I shall see the blood, and shall pass over you: and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I shall strike the land of Egypt.

14.text: And this day shall be for a memorial to you: and you shall keep it a feast to the Lord in your generations with an everlasting observance.

15.text: Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread: in the first day there shall be no leaven in your houses: whosoever shall eat any thing leavened, from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall perish out of Israel.

16.text: The first day shall be holy and solemn, and the seventh day shall be kept with the like solemnity: you shall do no work in them, except those things that belong to eating.

17.text: And you shall observe the feast of the unleavened bread: for in this same day I will bring forth your army out of the land of Egypt, and you shall keep this day in your generations by a perpetual observance.

18.text: The first month, the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the one and twentieth day of the same month in the evening.

19.text: Seven days there shall not be found any leaven in your houses: he that shall eat leavened bread, his soul shall perish out of the assembly of Israel, whether he be a stranger or born in the land.

20.text: You shall not eat any thing leavened: in all your habitations you shall eat unleavened bread.

21.text: And Moses called all the ancients of the children of Israel, and said to them: Go take a lamb by your families, and sacrifice the Phase.

22.text: And dip a bunch of hyssop in the blood that is at the door, and sprinkle the transom of the door therewith, and both the door cheeks: let none of you go out of the door of his house till morning.

23.text: For the Lord will pass through striking the Egyptians: and when he shall see the blood on the transom, and on both the posts, he will pass over the door of the house, and not suffer the destroyer to come into your houses and to hurt you.

24.text: Thou shalt keep this thing as a law for thee and thy children for ever.

25.text: And when you have entered into the land which the Lord will give you as he hath promised, you shall observe these ceremonies.

26.text: And when your children shall say to you: What is the meaning of this service?

27.text: You shall say to them: It is the victim of the passage of the Lord, when he passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, striking the Egyptians, and saving our houses. And the people bowing themselves, adored.

28.text: And the children of Israel going forth did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.

29.text: And it came to pass at midnight, the Lord slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharao, who sat on his throne, unto the firstborn of the captive woman that was in the prison, and all the firstborn of cattle.

30.text: And Pharao arose in the night, and all his servants, and all Egypt: for there was not a house wherein there lay not one dead.

31.text: And Pharao calling Moses and Aaron, in the night, said: Arise and go forth from among my people, you and the children of Israel: go, sacrifice to the Lord as you say.

32.text: Your sheep and herds take along with you, as you demanded, and departing, bless me.

33.text: And the Egyptians pressed the people to go forth out of the land speedily, saying: We shall all die.

34.text: The people therefore took dough before it was leavened: and tying it in their cloaks, put it on their shoulders.

35.text: And the children of Israel did as Moses had commanded: and they asked of the Egyptians vessels of silver and gold, and very much raiment.

36.text: And the Lord gave favour to the people in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them: and they stripped the Egyptians.

37.text: And the children of Israel set forward from Ramesse to Socoth, being about six hundred thousand men on foot, beside children.

38.text: And a mixed multitude without number went up also with them, sheep and herds and beasts of divers kinds, exceeding many.

39.text: And they baked the meal, which a little before they had brought out of Egypt, in dough: and they made earth cakes unleavened: for it could not be leavened, the Egyptians pressing them to depart, and not suffering them to make any stay: neither did they think of preparing any meat.

40.text: And the abode of the children of Israel that they made in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.

41.text: Which being expired, the same day all the army of the Lord went forth out of the land of Egypt.

42.text: This is the observable night of the Lord, when he brought them forth out of the land of Egypt: this night all the children of Israel must observe in their generations.

43.text: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: This is the service of the Phase: No foreigner shall eat of it.

44.text: But every bought servant shall be circumcised, and so shall eat.

45.text: The stranger and the hireling shall not eat thereof.

46.text: In one house shall it be eaten, neither shall you carry forth of the flesh thereof out of the house, neither shall you break a bone thereof.

47.text: All the assembly of the children of Israel shall keep it.

48.text: And if any stranger be willing to dwell among you, and to keep the Phase of the Lord, all his males shall first be circumcised, and then shall he celebrate it according to the manner: and he shall be as he that is born in the land: but if any man be uncircumcised, he shall not eat thereof.

49.text: The same law shall be to him that is born in the land, and to the proselyte that sojourneth with you.

50.text: And all the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron.

51.text: And the same day the Lord brought forth the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their companies.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Sanctify unto me every firstborn that openeth the womb among the children of Israel, as well of men as of beasts: for they are all mine.

3.text: And Moses said to the people: Remember this day in which you came forth out of Egypt, and out of the house of bondage, for with a strong hand hath the Lord brought you forth out of this place: that you eat no leavened bread.

4.text: This day you go forth in the month of new corn.

5.text: And when the Lord shall have brought thee into the land of the Chanaanite, and the Hethite, and the Amorrhite, and the Hevite, and the Jebusite, which he swore to thy fathers that he would give thee, a land that floweth with milk and honey, thou shalt celebrate this manner of sacred rites in this month.

6.text: Seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread: and on the seventh day shall be the solemnity of the Lord.
