18.text: And the Lord, when he had ended these words in mount Sinai, gave to Moses two stone tables of testimony, written with the finger of God.

1.text: And the people seeing that Moses delayed to come down from the mount, gathering together against Aaron, said: Arise, make us gods, that may go before us: for as to this Moses, the man that brought us out of the land of Egypt, we know not what has befallen him.

2.text: And Aaron said to them: Take the golden earrings from the ears of your wives, and your sons and daughters, and bring them to me.

3.text: And the people did what he had commanded, bringing the earrings to Aaron.

4.text: And when he had received them, he fashioned them by founders’ work, and made of them a molten calf. And they said: These are thy gods, O Israel, that have brought thee out of the land of Egypt.

5.text: And when Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it, and made proclamation by a crier’s voice, saying: Tomorrow is the solemnity of the Lord.

6.text: And rising in the morning, they offered holocausts, and peace victims, and the people sat down to eat, and drink, and they rose up to play.

7.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Go, get thee down: thy people, which thou hast brought out of the land of Egypt, hath sinned.

8.text: They have quickly strayed from the way which thou didst shew them: and they have made to themselves a molten calf, and have adored it, and sacrificing victims to it, have said: These are thy gods, O Israel, that have brought thee out of the land of Egypt.

9.text: And again the Lord said to Moses: See that this people is stiffnecked:

10.text: Let me alone, that my wrath may be kindled against them, and that I may destroy them, and I will make of thee a great nation.

11.text: But Moses besought the Lord his God, saying: Why, O Lord, is thy indignation kindled against thy people, whom thou hast brought out of the land of Egypt, with great power, and with a mighty hand?

12.text: Let not the Egyptians say, I beseech thee: He craftily brought them out, that he might kill them in the mountains, and destroy them from the earth: let thy anger cease, and be appeased upon the wickedness of thy people.

13.text: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to whom thou sworest by thy own self, saying: I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven: and this whole land that I have spoken of, I will give to your seed, and you shall possess it for ever.

14.text: And the Lord was appeased from doing the evil which he had spoken against his people.

15.text: And Moses returned from the mount, carrying the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both sides,

16.text: And made by the work of God: the writing also of God was graven in the tables.

17.text: And Josue hearing the noise of the people shouting, said to Moses: The noise of battle is heard in the camp.

18.text: But he answered: It is not the cry of men encouraging to fight, nor the shout of men compelling to flee: but I hear the voice of singers.

19.text: And when he came nigh to the camp, he saw the calf, and the dances: and being very angry, he threw the tables out of his hand, and broke them at the foot of the mount:

20.text: And laying hold of the calf which they had made, he burnt it, and beat it to powder, which he strowed into water, and gave thereof to the children of Israel to drink.

21.text: And he said to Aaron: What has this people done to thee, that thou shouldst bring upon them a most heinous sin?

22.text: And he answered him: Let not my lord be offended: for thou knowest this people, that they are prone to evil.

23.text: They said to me: Make us gods, that may go before us: for as to this Moses, who brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, we know not what is befallen him.

24.text: And I said to them: Which of you hath any gold? and they took and brought it to me: and I cast it into the fire, and this calf came out.

25.text: And when Moses saw that the people were naked, (for Aaron had stripped them by occasion of the shame of the filth, and had set them naked among their enemies,)

26.text: Then standing in the gate of the camp, he said: If any man be on the Lord’s side let him join with me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him:

27.text: And he said to them: Thus saith the Lord God of Israel: Put every man his sword upon his thigh: go, and return from gate to gate through the midst of the camp, and let every man kill his brother, and friend, and neighbour.

28.text: And the sons of Levi did according to the words of Moses, and there were slain that day about three and twenty thousand men.

29.text: And Moses said: You have consecrated your hands this day to the Lord, every man in his son and in his brother, that a blessing may be given to you.

30.text: And when the next day was come, Moses spoke to the people: You have sinned a very great sin: I will go up to the Lord, if by any means I may be able to entreat him for your crime.

31.text: And returning to the Lord, he said: I beseech thee: this people hath sinned a heinous sin, and they have made to themselves gods of gold: either forgive them this trespass,

32.text: Or if thou do not, strike me out of the book that thou hast written.

33.text: And the Lord answered him: He that hath sinned against me, him will I strike out of my book:

34.text: But go thou, and lead this people whither I have told thee: my angel shall go before thee. And I in the day of revenge will visit this sin also of theirs.

35.text: The Lord therefore struck the people for the guilt on occasion of the calf which Aaron had made.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Go, get thee up from this place, thou and thy people which thou has brought out of the land of Egypt, into the land concerning which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying: To thy seed I will give it.

2.text: And I will send an angel before thee, that I may cast out the Chanaanite, and the Amorrhite, and the Hethite, and the Pherezite, and the Hevite, and the Jebusite.

3.text: That thou mayst enter into the land that floweth with milk and honey. For I will not go up with thee, because thou art a stiffnecked people: lest I destroy thee in the way.

4.text: And the people hearing these very bad tidings, mourned: and no man put on his ornaments according to custom.

5.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Say to the children of Israel: Thou are a stiffnecked people; once I shall come up in the midst of thee, and shall destroy thee. Now presently lay aside thy ornaments, that I may know what to do with thee.

6.text: So the children of Israel laid aside their ornaments by mount Horeb.

7.text: Moses also taking the tabernacle, pitched it without the camp afar off, and called the name thereof, The tabernacle of the covenant. And all the people that had any question, went forth to the tabernacle of the covenant, without the camp.

8.text: And when Moses went forth to the tabernacle, all the people rose up, and every one stood in the door of his pavilion, and they beheld the back of Moses, till he went into the tabernacle.

9.text: And when he was gone into the tabernacle of the covenant, the pillar of the cloud came down, and stood at the door, and he spoke with Moses.

10.text: And all saw that the pillar of the cloud stood at the door of the tabernacle. And they stood, and worshipped at the doors of their tents.

11.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses face to face, as a man is wont to speak to his friend. And when he returned into the camp, his servant Josue the son of Nun, a young man, departed not from the tabernacle.

12.text: And Moses said to the Lord; Thou commandest me to lead forth this people: and thou dost not let me know whom thou wilt send with me, especially whereas thou hast said: I know thee by name, and thou hast found favour in my sight.

13.text: If therefore I have found favour in thy sight, shew me thy face, that I may know thee, and may find grace before thy eyes: look upon thy people this nation.

14.text: And the Lord said: My face shall go before thee, and I will give thee rest.

15.text: And Moses said: If thou thyself dost not go before, bring us not out of this place.

16.text: For how shall we be able to know, I and thy people, that we have found grace in thy sight, unless thou walk with us, that we may be glorified by all people that dwell upon the earth?

17.text: And the Lord said to Moses: This word also, which thou hast spoken, will I do: for thou hast found grace before me, and thee I have known by name.

18.text: And he said: shew me thy glory.

19.text: He answered: I will shew thee all good, and I will proclaim in the name of the Lord before thee: and I will have mercy on whom I will, and I will be merciful to whom it shall please me.

20.text: And again he said: Thou canst not see my face: for man shall not see me and live.

21.text: And again he said: Behold there is a place with me, and thou shalt stand upon the rock.

22.text: And when my glory shall pass, I will set thee in a hole of the rock, and protect thee with my right hand, till I pass:

23.text: And I will take away my hand, and thou shalt see my back parts: but my face thou canst not see.

1.text: And after this he said: Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the former, and I will write upon them the words which were in the tables, which thou brokest.

2.text: Be ready in the morning, that thou mayst forthwith go up into mount Sinai, and thou shalt stand with me upon the top of the mount.

3.text: Let no man go up with thee: and let not any man be seen throughout all the mount: neither let the oxen nor the sheep feed over against it.

4.text: Then he cut out two tables of stone, such as had been before: and rising very early he went up into the mount Sinai, as the Lord had commanded him, carrying with him the tables.

5.text: And when the Lord was come down in a cloud, Moses stood with him, calling upon the name of the Lord.

6.text: And when he passed before him, he said: O the Lord, the Lord God, merciful and gracious, patient and of much compassion, and true,

7.text: Who keepest mercy unto thousands: who takest away iniquity, and wickedness, and sin, and no man of himself is innocent before thee. Who renderest the iniquity of the fathers to the children, and to the grandchildren, unto the third and fourth generation.

8.text: And Moses making haste, bowed down prostrate unto the earth, and adoring,

9.text: Said: If I have found grace in thy sight: O Lord, I beseech thee, that thou wilt go with us, (for it is a stiffnecked people,) and take away our iniquities and sin, and possess us.

10.text: The Lord answered: I will make a covenant in the sight of all. I will do signs such as were never seen upon the earth, nor in any nation: that this people, in the midst of whom thou art, may see the terrible work of the Lord which I will do.

11.text: Observe all things which this day I command thee: I myself will drive out before thy face the Amorrhite, and the Chanaanite, and the Hethite, and the Pherezite, and the Hevite, and the Jebusite.

12.text: Beware thou never join in friendship with the inhabitants of that land, which may be thy ruin:

13.text: But destroy their altars, break their statues, and cut down their groves:

14.text: Adore not any strange god. The Lord his name is Jealous, he is a jealous God.

15.text: Make no covenant with the men of those countries lest, when they have committed fornication with their gods, and have adored their idols, some one call thee to eat of the things sacrificed.

16.text: Neither shalt thou take of their daughters a wife for thy son, lest after they themselves have committed fornication, they make thy sons also to commit fornication with their gods.

17.text: Thou shalt not make to thyself any molten gods.

18.text: Thou shalt keep the feast of the unleavened bread. Seven days shalt thou eat unleavened bread, as I commanded thee in the time of the month of the new corn: for in the month of the springtime thou camest out from Egypt.

19.text: All of the male kind, that openeth the womb, shall be mine. Of all beasts, both of oxen and of sheep, it shall be mine.

20.text: The firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a sheep: but if thou wilt not give a price for it, it shall be slain. The firstborn of thy sons thou shalt redeem: neither shalt thou appear before me empty.

21.text: Six days shalt thou work, the seventh day thou shalt cease to plough, and to reap.

22.text: Thou shalt keep the feast of weeks with the firstfruits of the corn of thy wheat harvest, and the feast when the time of the year returneth that all things are laid in.

23.text: Three times in a year all thy males shall appear in the sight of the Almighty Lord the God of Israel.

24.text: For when I shall have taken away the nations from thy face, and shall have enlarged thy borders, no man shall lie in wait against thy land when thou shalt go up, and appear in the sight of the Lord thy God thrice in a year.

25.text: Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice upon leaven: neither shall there remain in the morning any thing of the victim of the solemnity of the Phase.

26.text: The first of the fruits of thy ground thou shalt offer in the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not boil a kid in the milk of his dam.

27.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Write these words by which I have made a covenant both with thee and with Israel.

28.text: And he was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights: he neither ate bread nor drank water, and he wrote upon the tables the ten words of the covenant.

29.text: And when Moses came down from the mount Sinai, he held the two tables of the testimony, and he knew not that his face was horned from the conversation of the Lord.

30.text: And Aaron and the children of Israel seeing the face of Moses horned, were afraid to come near.

31.text: And being called by him, they returned, both Aaron and the rulers of the congregation. And after that he spoke to them.

32.text: And all the children of Israel came to him: and he gave them in commandment all that he had heard of the Lord in mount Sinai.

33.text: And having done speaking, he put a veil upon his face.

34.text: But when he went in to the Lord, and spoke with him, he took it away until he came forth, and then he spoke to the children of Israel all things that had been commanded him.

35.text: And they saw that the face of Moses when he came out was horned, but he covered his face again, if at any time he spoke to them.

1.text: And all the multitude of the children of Israel being gathered together, he said to them: These are the things which the Lord hath commanded to be done.

2.text: Six days you shall do work: the seventh day shall be holy unto you, the sabbath, and the rest of the Lord: he that shall do any work on it, shall be put to death.

3.text: You shall kindle no fire in any of your habitations on the sabbath day.

4.text: And Moses said to all the assembly of the children of Israel: This is the word the Lord hath commanded, saying:

5.text: Set aside with you firstfruits to the Lord. Let every one that is willing and hath a ready heart, offer them to the Lord: gold, and silver, and brass,

6.text: Violet and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine linen, goats’ hair,

7.text: And rams’ skins dyed red, and violet coloured skins, setim wood,

8.text: And oil to maintain lights, and to make ointment, and most sweet incense.

9.text: Onyx stones, and precious stones, for the adorning of the ephod and the rational.

10.text: Whosoever of you is wise, let him come, and make that which the Lord hath commanded:

11.text: To wit, the tabernacle and the roof thereof, and the cover, the rings, and the board work with the bars, the pillars, and the sockets:

12.text: The ark and the staves, the propitiatory, and the veil that is drawn before it:

13.text: The table with the bars and the vessels, and the loaves of proposition:

14.text: The candlestick to bear up the lights, the vessels thereof and the lamps, and the oil for the nourishing of fires:

15.text: The altar of incense, and the bars, and the oil of unction and the incense of spices: the hanging at the door of the tabernacle:

16.text: The altar of holocaust, and its grate of brass, with the bars and vessels thereof: the laver and its foot:

17.text: The curtains of the court with the pillars and the sockets, the hanging in the doors of the entry,

18.text: The pins of the tabernacle and of the court with their little cords:

19.text: The vestments that are to be used in the ministry of the sanctuary, the vesture of Aaron the high priest, and of his sons, to do the office of priesthood to me.

20.text: And all the multitude of the children of Israel going out from the presence of Moses,

21.text: Offered firstfruits to the Lord with a most ready and devout mind, to make the work of the tabernacle of the testimony. Whatsoever was necessary to the service, and to the holy vestments,

22.text: Both men and women gave bracelets and earrings, rings and tablets: every vessel of gold was set aside to be offered to the Lord.

23.text: If any man had violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, fine linen and goats’ hair, rams’ skins dyed red, and violet coloured skins,

24.text: Metal of silver and brass, they offered it to the Lord, and setim wood for divers uses.

25.text: The skillful women also gave such things as they had spun, violet, purple, and scarlet, and fine linen,

26.text: And goats’ hair, giving all of their own accord.

27.text: But the princes offered onyx stone, and precious stones, for the ephod and the rational,

28.text: And spices and oil for the lights, and for the preparing of ointment, and to make the incense of most sweet savour.

29.text: All both men and women with devout mind offered gifts, that the works might be done which the Lord had commanded by the hand of Moses. All the children of Israel dedicated voluntary offerings to the Lord.

30.text: And Moses said to the children of Israel: Behold the Lord hath called by name Beseleel the son of Uri the son of Hur of the tribe of Juda.

31.text: And hath filled him with the spirit of God, with wisdom and understanding and knowledge and all learning.

32.text: To devise and to work in gold and silver and brass,

33.text: And in engraving stones, and in carpenters’ work. Whatsoever can be devised artificially,

34.text: He hath given in his heart: Ooliab also the son of Achisamech of the tribe of Dan:

35.text: Both of them hath he instructed with wisdom, to do carpenters’ work and tapestry, and embroidery in blue and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine linen, and to weave all things, and to invent all new things.

1.text: Beseleel, therefore, and Ooliab, and every wise man, to whom the Lord gave wisdom and understanding, to know how to work artificially, made the things that are necessary for the uses of the sanctuary, and which the Lord commanded.

2.text: And when Moses had called them, and every skillful man, to whom the Lord had given wisdom, and such as of their own accord had offered themselves to the making of the work,

3.text: He delivered all the offerings of the children of Israel unto them. And while they were earnest about the work, the people daily in the morning offered their vows.

4.text: Whereupon the workmen being constrained to come,

5.text: Said to Moses: The people offereth more than is necessary.

6.text: Moses therefore commanded proclamation to be made by the crier’s voice: Let neither man nor woman offer any more for the work of the sanctuary. And so they ceased from offering gifts,

7.text: Because the things that were offered did suffice, and were too much.

8.text: And all the men that were wise of heart, to accomplish the work of the tabernacle, made ten curtains of twisted fine linen, and violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, with varied work, and the art of embroidering:

9.text: The length of one curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the breadth four: all the curtains were of the same size.

10.text: And he joined five curtains, one to another, and the other five he coupled one to another.

11.text: He made also loops of violet in the edge of the curtain on both sides, and in the edge of the other curtain in like manner,

12.text: That the loops might meet one against another, and might be joined each with the other.

13.text: Whereupon also he cast fifty rings of gold, that might catch the loops of the curtains, and they might be made one tabernacle.

14.text: He made also eleven curtains of goats’ hair, to cover the roof of the tabernacle:

15.text: One curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits broad: all the curtains were of one measure.

16.text: Five of which he joined apart, and the other six apart.

17.text: And he made fifty loops in the edge of one curtain, and fifty in the edge of another curtain, that they might be joined one to another.

18.text: And fifty buckles of brass wherewith the roof might be knit together, that of all the curtains there might be made one covering.

19.text: He made also a cover for the tabernacle of rams’ skins dyed red: and another cover over that of violet skins.

20.text: He made also the boards of the tabernacle of setim wood standing.

21.text: The length of one board was ten cubits: and the breadth was one cubit and a half.

22.text: There were two mortises throughout every board, that one might be joined to the other. And in this manner he made for all the boards of the tabernacle.

23.text: Of which twenty were at the south side southward,

24.text: With forty sockets of silver, two sockets were put under one board on the two sides of the corners, where the mortises of the sides end in the corners.

25.text: At that side also of the tabernacle, that looketh toward the north, he made twenty boards.

26.text: With forty sockets of silver, two sockets for every board.

27.text: But against the west, to wit, at that side of the tabernacle, which looketh to the sea, he made six boards,

28.text: And two others at each corner of the tabernacle behind:

29.text: Which were also joined from beneath unto the top, and went together into one joint. Thus he did on both sides at the corners:

30.text: So there were in all eight boards and they had sixteen sockets of silver, to wit, two sockets under every board.

31.text: He made also bars of setim wood, five to hold together the boards of one side of the tabernacle,

32.text: And five others to join together the boards of the other side: and besides these, five other bars at the west side of the tabernacle towards the sea.

33.text: He made also another bar, that might come by the midst of the boards from corner to corner.

34.text: And the board works themselves he overlaid with gold, casting for them sockets of silver. And their rings he made of gold, through which the bars might be drawn: and he covered the bars themselves with plates of gold.

35.text: He made also a veil of violet, and purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen, varied and distinguished with embroidery:

36.text: And four pillars of setim wood, which with their heads he overlaid with gold, casting for them sockets of silver.

37.text: He made also a hanging in the entry of the tabernacle of violet, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen, with the work of an embroiderer.

38.text: And five pillars with their heads, which he covered with gold, and their sockets he cast of brass.

1.text: And Beseleel made also the ark of setim wood: it was two cubits and a half in length, and a cubit and a half in breadth, and the height was of one cubit and a half: and he overlaid it with the purest gold within and without.

2.text: And he made to it a crown of gold round about,

3.text: Casting four rings of gold at the four corners thereof: two rings in one side, and two in the other.

4.text: And he made bars of setim wood, which he overlaid with gold,

5.text: And he put them into the rings that were at the sides of the ark to carry it.

6.text: He made also the propitiatory, that is, the oracle, of the purest gold, two cubits and a half in length, and a cubit and a half in breadth.

7.text: Two cherubims also of beaten gold, which he set on the two sides of the propitiatory:

8.text: One cherub in the top of one side, and the other cherub in the top of the other side: two cherubims at the two ends of the propitiatory,

9.text: Spreading their wings, and covering the propitiatory, and looking one towards the other, and towards it.

10.text: He made also the table of setim wood, in length two cubits, and in breadth one cubit, and in height it was a cubit and a half.

11.text: And he overlaid it with the finest gold, and he made to it a golden ledge round about.

12.text: And to the ledge itself he made a polished crown of gold, of four fingers’ breadth, and upon the same another golden crown.

13.text: And he cast four rings of gold, which he put in the four corners at each foot of the table,

14.text: Over against the crown: and he put the bars into them, that the table might be carried.

15.text: And the bars also themselves he made of setim wood, and overlaid them with gold,

16.text: And the vessels for the divers uses of the table, dishes, bowls, and cups, and censers of pure gold, wherein the libations are to be offered.

17.text: He made also the candlestick of beaten work of the finest gold. From the shaft whereof its branches, its cups, and bowls, and lilies came out:

18.text: Six on the two sides: three branches on one side, and three on the other.

19.text: Three cups in manner of a nut on each branch, and bowls withal and lilies; and three cups of the fashion of a nut in another branch, and bowls withal and lilies. The work of the six branches that went out from the shaft of the candlestick was equal.

20.text: And in the shaft itself were four cups after the manner of a nut, and bowls withal at every one, and lilies:

21.text: And bowls under two branches in three places, which together made six branches going out from one shaft.

22.text: So both the bowls, and the branches were of the same, all beaten work of the purest gold.

23.text: He made also the seven lamps with their snuffers, and the vessels where the snuffings were to be put out, of the purest gold.

24.text: The candlestick with all the vessels thereof weighed a talent of gold.

25.text: He made also the altar of incense of setim wood, being a cubit on every side foursquare, and in height two cubits: from the corners of which went out horns.

26.text: And he overlaid it with the purest gold, with its grate and the sides, and the horns.

27.text: And he made to it a crown of gold round about, and two golden rings under the crown at each side, that the bars might be put into them, and the altar be carried.

28.text: And the bars themselves he made also of setim wood, and overlaid them with plates of gold.

29.text: He compounded also the oil for the ointment of sanctification, and incense of the purest spices, according to the work of a perfumer.

1.text: He made also the altar of holocaust of setim wood, five cubits square, and three in height:

2.text: The horns whereof went out from the corners, and he overlaid it with plates of brass.

3.text: And for the uses thereof, he prepared divers vessels of brass, cauldrons, tongs, fleshhooks, pothooks, and firepans.

4.text: And he made the grate thereof of brass, in manner of a net, and under it in the midst of the altar a hearth,

5.text: Casting four rings at the four ends of the net at the top, to put in bars to carry it.

6.text: And he made the bars of setim wood, and overlaid them with plates of brass:

7.text: And he drew them through the rings that stood out in the sides of the altar. And the altar itself was not solid, but hollow, of boards, and empty within.

8.text: He made also the laver of brass, with the foot thereof, of the mirrors of the women that watch at the door of the tabernacle.

9.text: He made also the court, in the south side whereof were hangings of fine twisted linen, of a hundred cubits,

10.text: Twenty pillars of brass with their sockets, the heads of the pillars, and the whole graving of the work, of silver.

11.text: In like manner at the north side the hangings, the pillars, and the sockets and heads of the pillars were of the same measure, and work and metal.

12.text: But on that side that looketh to the west, there were hangings of fifty cubits, ten pillars of brass with their sockets, and the heads of the pillars, and all the graving of the work, of silver.

13.text: Moreover towards the east he prepared hangings of fifty cubits:

14.text: Fifteen cubits of which were on one side with three pillars, and their sockets:

15.text: And on the other side (for between the two he made the entry of the tabernacle) there were hangings equally of fifteen cubits, and three pillars, and as many sockets.

16.text: All the hangings of the court were woven with twisted linen.

17.text: The sockets of the pillars were of brass, and their heads with all their gravings of silver: and he overlaid the pillars of the court also with silver.

18.text: And he made in the entry thereof an embroidered hanging of violet, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen, that was twenty cubits long, and five cubits high according to the measure of all the hangings of the court.

19.text: And the pillars in the entry were four with sockets of brass, and their heads and gravings of silver.

20.text: The pins also of the tabernacle and of the court round about he made of brass.

21.text: These are the instruments of the tabernacle of the testimony, which were counted according to the commandment of Moses, in the ceremonies of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest:

22.text: Which Beseleel the son of Uri the son of Hur of the tribe of Juda had made as the Lord commanded by Moses,

23.text: Having for his companion Ooliab the son of Achisamech of the tribe of Dan: who also was an excellent artificer in wood, and worker in tapestry and embroidery in violet, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.

24.text: All the gold that was spent in the work of the sanctuary, and that was offered in gifts was nine and twenty talents, and seven hundred and thirty sicles according to the standard of the sanctuary.

26.text: And it was offered by them that went to be numbered, from twenty years old and upwards, of six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty men able to bear arms.

27.text: There were moreover a hundred talents of silver, whereof were cast the sockets of the sanctuary, and of the entry where the veil hangeth. A hundred sockets were made of a hundred talents, one talent being reckoned for every socket.

28.text: And of the thousand seven hundred and seventy-five he made the heads of the pillars, which also he overlaid with silver.

29.text: And there were offered of brass also seventy-two thousand talents, and four hundred sicles besides.

30.text: Of which were cast the sockets in the entry of the tabernacle of the testimony, and the altar of brass with the grate thereof, and all the vessels that belong to the use thereof.

31.text: And the sockets of the court as well round about as in the entry thereof, and the pins of the tabernacle and of the court round about.

1.text: And he made, of violet and purple, scarlet and fine linen, the vestments for Aaron to wear when he ministered in the holy places, as the Lord commanded Moses.

2.text: So he made an ephod of gold, violet, and purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen.

3.text: With embroidered work: and he cut thin plates of gold, and drew them small into threads, that they might be twisted with the woof of the aforesaid colours,

4.text: And two borders coupled one to the other in the top on either side,

5.text: And a girdle of the same colours, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

6.text: He prepared also two onyx stones, fast set and closed in gold, and graven by the art of a lapidary, with the names of the children of Israel:

7.text: And he set them in the sides of the ephod for a memorial of the children of Israel, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

8.text: He made also a rational with embroidered work, according to the work of the ephod, of gold, violet, purple, and scarlet twice dyed, and fine twisted linen,

9.text: Foursquare, double, of the measure of a span.

10.text: And he set four rows of precious stones in it. In the first row was a sardius, a topaz, an emerald.

11.text: In the second, a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a jasper.

12.text: In the third, a ligurius, an agate, and an amethyst.

13.text: In the fourth, a chrysolite, an onyx, and a beryl, set and enclosed in gold by their rows.

14.text: And the twelve stones were engraved with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, each one with its several name.

15.text: They made also in the rational little chains linked one to another of the purest gold,

16.text: And two hooks, and as many rings of gold. And they set the rings on either side of the rational,

17.text: On which rings the two golden chains should hang, which they put into the hooks that stood out in the corners of the ephod.

18.text: These both before and behind so answered one another, that the ephod and the rational were bound together,

21.text: Being fastened to the girdle and strongly coupled with rings, which a violet fillet joined, lest they should flag loose, and be moved one from the other, as the Lord commanded Moses.

22.text: They made also the tunick of the ephod all of violet,

23.text: And a hole for the head in the upper part at the middle, and a woven border round about the hole:

24.text: And beneath at the feet pomegranates of violet, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen:

25.text: And little bells of the purest gold, which they put between the pomegranates at the bottom of the tunick round about:

26.text: To wit, a bell of gold, and a pomegranate, wherewith the high priest went adorned, when he discharged his ministry, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

27.text: They made also fine linen tunicks with woven work for Aaron and his sons:

28.text: And mitres with their little crowns of fine linen: And linen breeches of fine linen:

29.text: And a girdle of fine twisted linen, violet, purple, and scarlet twice dyed, of embroidery work, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

30.text: They made also the plate of sacred veneration of the purest gold, and they wrote on it with the engraving of a lapidary, The Holy of the Lord:

31.text: And they fastened it to the mitre with a violet fillet, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

32.text: So all the work of the tabernacle and of the roof of the testimony was finished: and the children of Israel did all things which the Lord had commanded Moses.

33.text: And they offered the tabernacle and the roof and the whole furniture, the rings, the boards, the bars, the pillars, and their sockets,

34.text: The cover of rams’ skins dyed red, and the other cover of violet skins,

35.text: The veil, the ark, the bars, the propitiatory,

36.text: The table, with the vessels thereof, and the loaves of proposition:

37.text: The candlestick, the lamps, and the furniture of them with the oil:

38.text: The altar of gold, and the ointment, and the incense of spices: And the hanging in the entry of the tabernacle:

39.text: The altar of brass, the grate, the bars, and all the vessels thereof: the laver with the foot thereof: the hangings of the court, and the pillars with their sockets:

40.text: The hanging in the entry of the court, and the little cords, and the pins thereof. Nothing was wanting of the vessels, that were commanded to be made for the ministry of the tabernacle, and for the roof of the covenant.

41.text: The vestments also, which the priests, to wit, Aaron and his sons, used in the sanctuary,

42.text: The children of Israel offered as the Lord had commanded.

43.text: And when Moses saw all things finished, he blessed them.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: The first month, the first day of the month, thou shalt set up the tabernacle of the testimony,

3.text: And shalt put the ark in it, and shalt let down the veil before it:

4.text: And thou shalt bring in the table, and set upon it the things that are commanded according to the rite. The candlestick shall stand with its lamps,

5.text: And the altar of gold whereon the incense is burnt, before the ark of the testimony. Thou shalt put the hanging in the entry of the tabernacle,

6.text: And before it the altar of holocaust:

7.text: The laver between the altar and the tabernacle, and thou shalt fill it with water.

8.text: And thou shalt encompass the court with hangings, and the entry thereof.

9.text: And thou shalt take the oil of unction and anoint the tabernacle with its vessels, that they may be sanctified:

10.text: The altar of holocaust and all its vessels:

11.text: The laver with its foot: thou shalt consecrate all with the oil of unction, that they may be most holy.

12.text: And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and having washed them with water,

13.text: Thou shalt put on them the holy vestments, that they may minister to me, and that the unction of them may prosper to an everlasting priesthood.

14.text: Thou shalt put on them the holy vestments, that they may minister to me, and that the unction of them may prosper to an everlasting priesthood.

16.text: And Moses did all that the Lord had commanded.

17.text: So in the first month of the second year, the first day of the month, the tabernacle was set up.

18.text: And Moses reared it up, and placed the boards and the sockets and the bars, and set up the pillars,

19.text: And spread the roof over the tabernacle, putting over it a cover, as the Lord had commanded.

20.text: And he put the testimony in the ark, thrusting bars underneath, and the oracle above.

21.text: And when he had brought the ark into the tabernacle, he drew the veil before it to fulfill the commandment of the Lord.

22.text: And he set the table in the tabernacle of the testimony at the north side without the veil,

23.text: Setting there in order the loaves of proposition, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

24.text: He set the candlestick also in the tabernacle of the testimony over against the table on the south side,

25.text: Placing the lamps in order, according to the precept of the Lord.

26.text: He set also the altar of gold under the roof of the testimony over against the veil,

27.text: And burnt upon it the incense of spices, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

28.text: And he put also the hanging in the entry of the tabernacle of the testimony,

29.text: And the altar of holocaust of the entry of the testimony, offering the holocaust, and the sacrifices upon it, as the Lord had commanded.

30.text: And he set the laver between the tabernacle of the testimony and the altar, filling it with water.

31.text: And Moses and Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet,

32.text: When they went into the tabernacle of the covenant, and went to the altar, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

33.text: He set up also the court round about the tabernacle and the altar, drawing the hanging in the entry thereof. After all things were perfected,

34.text: The cloud covered the tabernacle of the testimony, and the glory of the Lord filled it.

35.text: Neither could Moses go into the tabernacle of the covenant, the cloud covering all things and the majesty of the Lord shining, for the cloud had covered all.

36.text: If at any time the cloud removed from the tabernacle, the children of Israel went forward by their troops:

37.text: If it hung over, they remained in the same place.

38.text: For the cloud of the Lord hung over the tabernacle by day, and a fire by night, in the sight of all the children of Israel throughout all their mansions.

1.text: And the Lord called Moses, and spoke to him from the tabernacle of the testimony, saying:

2.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: The man among you that shall offer to the Lord a sacrifice of the cattle, that is, offering victims of oxen and sheep,

3.text: If his offering be a holocaust, and of the herd, he shall offer a male without blemish, at the door of the testimony, to make the Lord favourable to him:

4.text: And he shall put his hand upon the head of the victim, and it shall be acceptable, and help to its expiation.

5.text: And he shall immolate the calf before the Lord, and the priests the sons of Aaron shall offer the blood thereof, pouring it round about the altar, which is before the door of the tabernacle.

6.text: And when they have flayed the victim, they shall cut the joints into pieces,

7.text: And shall put fire on the altar, having before laid in order a pile of wood:

8.text: And they shall lay the parts that are cut out in order thereupon, to wit, the head, and all things that cleave to the liver,

9.text: The entrails and feet being washed with water: and the priest shall burn them upon the altar for a holocaust, and a sweet savour to the Lord.

10.text: And if the offering be of the flocks, a holocaust of sheep or of goats, he shall offer a male without blemish:

11.text: And he shall immolate it at the side of the altar that looketh to the north, before the Lord: but the sons of Aaron shall pour the blood thereof upon the altar round about:

12.text: And they shall divide the joints, the head, and all that cleave to the liver: and shall lay them upon the wood, under which the fire is to be put:

13.text: But the entrails and the feet they shall wash with water. And the priest shall offer it all and burn it all upon the altar for a holocaust, and most sweet savour to the Lord.

14.text: But if the oblation of a holocaust to the Lord be of birds, of turtles, or of young pigeons,

15.text: The priest shall offer it at the altar: and twisting back the neck, and breaking the place of the wound, he shall make the blood run down upon the brim of the altar.

16.text: But the crop of the throat, and the feathers he shall cast beside the altar at the east side, in the place where the ashes are wont to be poured out,

17.text: And he shall break the pinions thereof, and shall not cut, nor divide it with a knife, and shall burn it upon the altar, putting fire under the wood. It is a holocaust and oblation of most sweet savour to the Lord.

1.text: When any one shall offer an oblation of sacrifice to the Lord, his offering shall be of fine flour, and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense,

2.text: And shall bring it to the sons of Aaron the priests: and one of them shall take a handful of the flour and oil, and all the frankincense, and shall put it a memorial upon the altar for a most sweet savour to the Lord.

3.text: And the remnant of the sacrifice shall be Aaron’s, and his sons’, holy of holies of the offerings of the Lord.

4.text: But when thou offerest a sacrifice baked in the oven of flour, to wit, loaves without leaven, tempered with oil, and unleavened wafers, anointed with oil:

5.text: If thy oblation be from the fryingpan, of flour tempered with oil, and without leaven,

6.text: Thou shalt divide it into little pieces, and shalt pour oil upon it.

7.text: And if the sacrifice be from the gridiron, in like manner the flour shall be tempered with oil:

8.text: And when thou offerest it to the Lord, thou shalt deliver it to the hands of the priest.

9.text: And when he hath offered it, he shall take a memorial out of the sacrifice, and burn it upon the altar for a sweet savour to the Lord.

10.text: And whatsoever is left, shall be Aaron’s, and his sons’, holy of holies of the offerings of the Lord.

11.text: Every oblation that is offered to the Lord shall be made without leaven, neither shall any leaven or honey be burnt in the sacrifice to the Lord.

12.text: You shall offer only the firstfruits of them and gifts: but they shall not be put upon the altar, for a savour of sweetness,

13.text: Whatsoever sacrifice thou offerest, thou shalt season it with salt, neither shalt thou take away the salt of the covenant of thy God from thy sacrifice. In all thy oblations thou shalt offer salt.

14.text: But if thou offer a gift of the firstfruits of thy corn to the Lord, of the ears yet green, thou shalt dry it at the fire, and break it small like meal, and so shalt thou offer thy firstfruits to the Lord,

15.text: Pouring oil upon it and putting on frankincense, because it is the oblation of the Lord.

16.text: Whereof the priest shall burn for a memorial of the gift, part of the corn broken small and of the oil, and all the frankincense.

1.text: And if his oblation be a sacrifice of peace offerings, and he will offer of the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer them without blemish before the Lord.

2.text: And he shall lay his hand upon the head of his victim, which shall be slain in the entry of the tabernacle of the testimony, and the sons of Aaron the priests shall pour the blood round about upon the altar.

3.text: And they shall offer of the sacrifice of peace offerings, for an oblation to the Lord, the fat that covereth the entrails, and all the fat that is within.

4.text: The two kidneys with the fat wherewith the flanks are covered, and the caul of the liver with the two little kidneys.

5.text: And they shall burn them upon the altar, for a holocaust, putting fire under the wood: for an oblation of most sweet savour to the Lord.

6.text: But if his oblation and the sacrifice of peace offering be of the flock, whether he offer male or female, they shall be without blemish.

7.text: If he offer a lamb before the Lord,

8.text: He shall put his hand upon the head of his victim: and it shall be slain in the entry of the tabernacle of the testimony: and the sons of Aaron shall pour the blood thereof round about upon the altar.

9.text: And they shall offer of the victim of peace offerings a sacrifice to the Lord: the fat and the whole rump,

10.text: With the kidneys, and the fat that covereth the belly and all the vitals and both the little kidneys, with the fat that is about the flanks, and the caul of the liver with the little kidneys.

11.text: And the priest shall burn them upon the altar, for the food of the fire, and of the oblation of the Lord.

12.text: If his offering be a goat, and he offer it to the Lord,

13.text: He shall put his hand upon the head thereof: and shall immolate it in the entry of the tabernacle of the testimony. And the sons of Aaron shall pour the blood thereof round about upon the altar.

14.text: And they shall take of it for the food of the Lord’s fire, the fat that covereth the belly, and that covereth all the vital parts:

15.text: The two little kidneys with the caul that is upon them which is by the flanks, and the fat of the liver with the little kidneys:

16.text: And the priest shall burn them upon the altar, for the food of the fire, and of a most sweet savour. All the fat shall be the Lord’s.

17.text: By a perpetual law for your generations, and in all your habitations: neither blood nor fat shall you eat at all.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Say to the children of Israel: The soul that sinneth through ignorance, and doth any thing concerning any of the commandments of the Lord, which he commanded not to be done:

3.text: If the priest that is anointed shall sin, making the people to offend, he shall offer to the Lord for his sin a calf without blemish.

4.text: And he shall bring it to the door of the testimony before the Lord, and shall put his hand upon the head thereof, and shall sacrifice it to the Lord.

5.text: He shall take also of the blood of the calf, and carry it into the tabernacle of the testimony.

6.text: And having dipped his finger in the blood, he shall sprinkle with it seven times before the Lord, before the veil of the sanctuary.

7.text: And he shall put some of the same blood upon the horns of the altar of the sweet incense most acceptable to the Lord, which is in the tabernacle of the testimony. And he shall pour all the rest of the blood at the foot of the altar of holocaust in the entry of the tabernacle.

8.text: And he shall take off the fat of the calf for the sin offering, as well that which covereth the entrails, as all the inwards:

9.text: The two little kidneys, and the caul that is upon them, which is by the flanks, and the fat of the liver with the little kidneys,

10.text: As it is taken off from the calf of the sacrifice of peace offerings, and he shall burn them upon the altar of holocaust.

11.text: But the skin and all the flesh with the head and the feet and the bowels and the dung,

12.text: And the rest of the body he shall carry forth without the camp into a clean place where the ashes are wont to be poured out, and he shall burn them upon a pile of wood, they shall be burnt in the place where the ashes are poured out.

13.text: And if all the multitude of Israel shall be ignorant, and through ignorance shall do that which is against the commandment of the Lord,

14.text: And afterwards shall understand their sin, they shall offer for their sin a calf, and shall bring it to the door of the tabernacle.

15.text: And the ancients of the people shall put their hands upon the head thereof before the Lord. And the calf being immolated in the sight of the Lord,

16.text: The priest that is anointed shall carry of the blood into the tabernacle of the testimony.

17.text: And shall dip his finger in it and sprinkle it seven times before the veil.

18.text: And he shall put of the same blood on the horns of the altar that is before the Lord, in the tabernacle of the testimony: and the rest of the blood he shall pour at the foot of the altar of holocaust, which is at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony.

19.text: And all the fat thereof he shall take off, and shall burn it upon the altar:

20.text: Doing so with this calf, as he did also with that before: and the priest praying for them, the Lord will be merciful unto them.

21.text: But the calf itself he shall carry forth without the camp, and shall burn it as he did the former calf: because it is for the sin of the multitude.

22.text: If a prince shall sin, and through ignorance do any one of the things that the law of the Lord forbiddeth,

23.text: And afterwards shall come to know his sin, he shall offer a buck goat without blemish, a sacrifice to the Lord.

24.text: And he shall put his hand upon the head thereof: and when he hath immolated it in the place where the holocaust is wont to be slain before the Lord, because it is for sin,

25.text: The priest shall dip his finger in the blood of the victim for sin, touching therewith the horns of the altar of holocaust, and pouring out the rest at the foot thereof.

26.text: But the fat he shall burn upon it, as is wont to be done with the victims of peace offerings: and the priest shall pray for him, and for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.

27.text: And if any one of the people of the land shall sin through ignorance, doing any of those things that by the law of the Lord are forbidden, and offending,

28.text: And shall come to know his sin, he shall offer a she goat without blemish.

29.text: And he shall put his hand upon the head of the victim that is for sin, and shall immolate it in the place of the holocaust.

30.text: And the priest shall take of the blood with his finger, and shall touch the horns of the altar of holocaust, and shall pour out the rest at the foot thereof.

31.text: But taking off all the fat, as is wont to be taken away of the victims of peace offerings, he shall burn it upon the altar, for a sweet savour to the Lord: and he shall pray for him, and it shall be forgiven him.

32.text: But if he offer of the flock a victim for his sin, to wit, an ewe without blemish:

33.text: He shall put his hand upon the head thereof, and shall immolate it in the place where the victims of holocausts are wont to be slain.

34.text: And the priest shall take of the blood thereof with his finger, and shall touch the horns of the altar of holocaust, and the rest he shall pour out at the foot thereof.

35.text: All the fat also he shall take off, as the fat of the ram that is offered for peace offerings is wont to be taken away: and shall burn it upon the altar, for a burnt sacrifice of the Lord: and he shall pray for him and for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.

1.text: If any one sin, and hear the voice of one swearing, and is a witness either because he himself hath seen, or is privy to it: if he do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity.

2.text: Whosoever toucheth any unclean thing, either that which hath been killed by a beast, or died of itself, or any other creeping thing: and forgetteth his uncleanness, he is guilty, and hath offended:

3.text: And if he touch any thing of the uncleanness of man, according to any uncleanness wherewith he is wont to be defiled, and having forgotten it, come afterwards to know it, he shall be guilty of an offence.

4.text: The person that sweareth, and uttereth with his lips, that he would do either evil or good, and bindeth the same with an oath, and his word, and having forgotten it afterwards understandeth his offence,

5.text: Let him do penance for his sin,

6.text: And offer of the flocks an ewe lamb, or a she goat, and the priest shall pray for him and for his sin:

7.text: But if he be not able to offer a beast, let him offer two turtles, or two young pigeons to the Lord, one for sin, and the other for a holocaust,

8.text: And he shall give them to the priest: who shall offer the first for sin, and twist back the head of it to the little pinions, so that it stick to the neck, and be not altogether broken off.

9.text: And of its blood he shall sprinkle the side of the altar, and whatsoever is left, he shall let it drop at the bottom thereof, because it is for sin.

10.text: And the other he shall burn for a holocaust, as is wont to be done: and the priest shall pray for him, and for his sin, and it shall be forgiven him.

11.text: And if his hand be not able to offer two turtles, or two young pigeons, he shall offer for his sin the tenth part of an ephi of flour. He shall not put oil upon it, nor put any frankincense thereon, because it is for sin:

12.text: And he shall deliver it to the priest: who shall take a handful thereof, and shall burn it upon the altar for a memorial of him that offered it:

13.text: Praying for him and making atonement: but the part that is left, he himself shall have for a gift.

14.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

15.text: If any one shall sin through mistake, transgressing the ceremonies in those things that are sacrificed to the Lord, he shall offer for his offence a ram without blemish out of the flocks, that may be bought for two sicles, according to the weight of the sanctuary:

16.text: And he shall make good the damage itself which he hath done, and shall add the fifth part besides, delivering it to the priest, who shall pray for him, offering the ram, and it shall be forgiven him.

17.text: If any one sin through ignorance, and do one of those things which by the law of the Lord are forbidden, and being guilty of sin, understand his iniquity,

18.text: He shall offer of the flocks a ram without blemish to the priest, according to the measure and estimation of the sin: and the priest shall pray for him, because he did it ignorantly: and it shall be forgiven him,

19.text: Because by mistake he trespassed against the Lord.

1.text: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Whosoever shall sin, and despising the Lord, shall deny to his neighbour the thing delivered to his keeping, which was committed to his trust; or shall by force extort any thing, or commit oppression;

3.text: Or shall find a thing lost, and denying it, shall also swear falsely, or shall do any other of the many things, wherein men are wont to sin:

4.text: Being convicted of the offence, he shall restore

5.text: All that he would have gotten by fraud, in the principal, and the fifth part besides to the owner, whom he wronged.

6.text: Moreover for his sin he shall offer a ram without blemish out of the flock, and shall give it to the priest, according to the estimation and measure of the offence:

7.text: And he shall pray for him before the Lord, and he shall have forgiveness for every thing in doing of which he hath sinned.

8.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

9.text: Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of a holocaust: It shall be burnt upon the altar, all night until morning: the fire shall be of the same altar.

10.text: The priest shall be vested with the tunick and the linen breeches, and he shall take up the ashes of that which the devouring fire hath burnt, and putting them beside the altar,

11.text: Shall put off his former vestments, and being clothed with others, shall carry them forth without the camp, and shall cause them to be consumed to dust in a very clean place,

12.text: And the fire on the altar shall always burn, and the priest shall feed it, putting wood on it every day in the morning, and laying on the holocaust, shall burn thereupon the fat of the peace offerings.

13.text: This is the perpetual fire which shall never go out on the altar.

14.text: This is the law of the sacrifice and libations, which the children of Aaron shall offer before the Lord, and before the altar.

15.text: The priest shall take a handful of the flour that is tempered with oil, and all the frankincense that is put upon the flour: and he shall burn it on the altar for a memorial of most sweet odour to the Lord:

16.text: And the part of the flour that is left, Aaron and his sons shall eat, without leaven: and he shall eat it in the holy place of the court of the tabernacle.

17.text: And therefore it shall not be leavened, because part thereof is offered for the burnt sacrifice of the Lord. It shall be most holy, as that which is offered for sin and for trespass.

18.text: The males only of the race of Aaron shall eat it. It shall be an ordinance everlasting in your generations concerning the sacrifices of the Lord: Every one that toucheth them shall be sanctified.

19.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

20.text: This is the oblation of Aaron, and of his sons, which they must offer to the Lord, in the day of their anointing: They shall offer the tenth part of an ephi of flour for a perpetual sacrifice, half of it in the morning, and half of it in the evening:

21.text: It shall be tempered with oil, and shall be fried in a fryingpan.

22.text: And the priest that rightfully succeedeth his father, shall offer it hot, for a most sweet odour to the Lord, and it shall be wholly burnt on the altar.

23.text: For every sacrifice of the priest shall be consumed with fire, neither shall any man eat thereof.

24.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

25.text: Say to Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the victim for sin: in the place where the holocaust is offered, it shall be immolated before the Lord. It is holy of holies.

26.text: The priest that offereth it, shall eat it in a holy place, in the court of the tabernacle.

27.text: Whatsoever shall touch the flesh thereof, shall be sanctified. If a garment be sprinkled with the blood thereof, it shall be washed in a holy place.

28.text: And the earthen vessel, wherein it was sodden, shall be broken, but if the vessel be of brass, it shall be scoured, and washed with water.

29.text: Every male of the priestly race shall eat of the flesh thereof, because it is holy of holies.

30.text: For the victim that is slain for sin, the blood of which is carried into the tabernacle of the testimony to make atonement in the sanctuary, shall not be eaten, but shall be burnt with fire.

1.text: This also is the law of the sacrifice for a trespass, it is most holy:

2.text: Therefore where the holocaust is immolated, the victim also for a trespass shall be slain: the blood thereof shall be poured round about the altar.

3.text: They shall offer thereof the rump and the fat that covereth the entrails:

4.text: The two little kidneys, and the fat which is by the flanks, and the caul of the liver with the little kidneys.

5.text: And the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the burnt sacrifice of the Lord for a trespass.

6.text: Every male of the priestly race, shall eat this flesh in a holy place, because it is most holy.

7.text: As the sacrifice for sin is offered, so is also that for a trespass: the same shall be the law of both these sacrifices: it shall belong to the priest that offereth it.

8.text: The priest that offereth the victim of holocaust, shall have the skin thereof.

9.text: And every sacrifice of flour that is baked in the oven, and whatsoever is dressed on the gridiron, or in the fryingpan, shall be the priest’s that offereth it:

10.text: Whether they be tempered with oil, or dry, all the sons of Aaron shall have one as much as another.

11.text: This is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings that is offered to the Lord.

12.text: If the oblation be for thanksgiving, they shall offer loaves without leaven tempered with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and fine flour fried, and cakes tempered and mingled with oil:

13.text: Moreover loaves of leavened bread with the sacrifice of thanks, which is offered for peace offerings:

14.text: Of which one shall be offered to the Lord for firstfruits, and shall be the priest’s that shall pour out the blood of the victim.

15.text: And the flesh of it shall be eaten the same day, neither shall any of it remain until the morning.

16.text: If any man by vow, or of his own accord offer a sacrifice, it shall in like manner be eaten the same day: and if any of it remain until the morrow, it is lawful to eat it:

17.text: But whatsoever shall be found on the third day shall be consumed with fire.

18.text: If any man eat of the flesh of the victim of peace offerings on the third day, the oblation shall be of no effect, neither shall it profit the offerer: yea rather whatsoever soul shall defile itself with such meat, shall be guilty of transgression.

19.text: The flesh that hath touched any unclean thing, shall not be eaten, but shall be burnt with fire: he that is clean shall eat of it.

20.text: If any one that is defiled shall eat of the flesh of the sacrifice of peace offerings, which is offered to the Lord, he shall be cut off from his people.

21.text: And he that hath touched the uncleanness of man, or of beast, or of any thing that can defile, and shall eat of such kind of flesh, shall be cut off from his people.

22.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

23.text: Say to the children of Israel: The fat of a sheep, and of an ox, and of a goat you shall not eat.

24.text: The fat of a carcass that hath died of itself, and of a beast that was caught by another beast, you shall have for divers uses.

25.text: If any man eat the fat that should be offered for the burnt sacrifice of the Lord, he shall perish out of his people.

26.text: Moreover you shall not eat the blood of any creature whatsoever, whether of birds or beasts.

27.text: Every one that eateth blood, shall perish from among the people.

28.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

29.text: Speak to the children of Israel, saying: He that offereth a victim of peace offerings to the Lord, let him offer therewith a sacrifice also, that is, the libations thereof.

30.text: He shall hold in his hands the fat of the victim, and the breast: and when he hath offered and consecrated both to the Lord, he shall deliver them to the priest,

31.text: Who shall burn the fat upon the altar, but the breast shall be Aaron’s and his sons’.

32.text: The right shoulder also of the victims of peace offerings shall fall to the priest for firstfruits.

33.text: He among the sons of Aaron, that offereth the blood, and the fat, he shall have the right shoulder also for his portion.

34.text: For the breast that is elevated and the shoulder that is separated I have taken of the children of Israel, from off their victims of peace offerings, and have given them to Aaron the priest, and to his sons, by a law for ever, from all the people of Israel.

35.text: This is the anointing of Aaron and his sons, in the ceremonies of the Lord, in the day when Moses offered them, that they might do the office of priesthood,

36.text: And the things that the Lord commanded to be given them by the children of Israel, by a perpetual observance in their generations.

37.text: This is the law of holocaust, and of the sacrifice for sin, and for trespass, and for consecration, and the victims of peace offerings:

38.text: Which the Lord appointed to Moses in mount Sinai, when he commanded the children of Israel, that they should offer their oblations to the Lord in the desert of Sinai.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Take Aaron with his sons, their vestments, and the oil of unction, a calf for sin, two rams, a basket with unleavened bread,

3.text: And thou shalt gather together all the congregation to the door of the tabernacle.

4.text: And Moses did as the Lord had commanded. And all the multitude being gathered together before the door of the tabernacle,

5.text: He said: This is the word that the Lord hath commanded to be done.

6.text: And immediately he offered Aaron and his sons: and when he had washed them,

7.text: He vested the high priest with the strait linen garment, girding him with the girdle, and putting on him the violet tunick, and over it he put the ephod,

8.text: And binding it with the girdle, he fitted it to the rational, on which was Doctrine and Truth.

9.text: He put also the mitre upon his head: and upon the mitre over the forehead, he put the plate of gold, consecrated with sanctification, as the Lord had commanded him.

10.text: He took also the oil of unction, with which he anointed the tabernacle, with all the furniture thereof.

11.text: And when he had sanctified and sprinkled the altar seven times, he anointed it, and all the vessels thereof, and the laver with the foot thereof, he sanctified with the oil.

12.text: And he poured it upon Aaron’s head, and he anointed and consecrated him:

13.text: And after he had offered his sons, he vested them with linen tunicks, and girded them with girdles, and put mitres on them as the Lord had commanded.

14.text: He offered also the calf for sin: and when Aaron and his sons had put their hands upon the head thereof,

15.text: He immolated it: and took the blood, and dipping his finger in it, he touched the horns of the altar round about. Which being expiated, and sanctified, he poured the rest of the blood at the bottom thereof.

16.text: But the fat that was upon the entrails, and the caul of the liver, and the two little kidneys, with their fat, he burnt upon the altar:

17.text: And the calf with the skin, and the flesh and the dung, he burnt without the camp, as the Lord had commanded.

18.text: He offered also a ram for a holocaust: and when Aaron and his sons had put their hands upon its head,

19.text: He immolated it, and poured the blood thereof round about upon the altar.

20.text: And cutting the ram into pieces, the head thereof, and the joints, and the fat he burnt in the fire,

21.text: Having first washed the entrails, and the feet, and the whole ram together he burnt upon the altar, because it was a holocaust of most sweet odour to the Lord, as he had commanded him.

22.text: He offered also the second ram, in the consecration of priests: and Aaron, and his sons put their hands upon the head thereof:

23.text: And when Moses had immolated it, he took of the blood thereof, and touched the tip of Aaron’s right ear, and the thumb of his right hand, and in like manner also the great toe of his right foot.

24.text: He offered also the sons of Aaron: and when with the blood of the ram that was immolated, he had touched the tip of the right ear of every one of them, and the thumbs of their right hands, and the great toes of their right feet, the rest he poured on the altar round about:

25.text: But the fat, and the rump, and all the fat that covereth the entrails, and the caul of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and with the right shoulder, he separated.

26.text: And taking out of the basket; of unleavened bread, which was before the Lord, a loaf without leaven, and a cake tempered with oil and a wafer, he put them upon the fat, and the right shoulder,

27.text: Delivering all to Aaron, and to his sons: Who having lifted them up before the Lord,

28.text: He took them again from their hands, and burnt them upon the altar of holocaust, because it was the oblation of consecration, for a sweet odour of sacrifice to the Lord.

29.text: And he took of the ram of consecration, the breast for his portion, elevating it before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded him.

30.text: And taking the ointment, and the blood that was upon the altar, he sprinkled Aaron, and his vestments, and his sons, and their vestments with it.

31.text: And when he had sanctified them in their vestments, he commanded them, saying: Boil the flesh before the door of the tabernacle, and there eat it. Eat ye also the loaves of consecration, that are laid in the basket, as the Lord commanded me, saying: Aaron and his sons shall eat them:

32.text: And whatsoever shall be left of the flesh and the loaves, shall be consumed with fire.

33.text: And you shall not go out of the door of the tabernacle for seven days, until the day wherein the time of your consecration shall be expired. For in seven days the consecration is finished:

34.text: As at this present it hath been done, that the rite of the sacrifice might be accomplished.

35.text: Day and night shall you remain in the tabernacle observing the watches of the Lord, lest you die: for so it hath been commanded me.

36.text: And Aaron and his sons did all things which the Lord spoke by the hand of Moses.

1.text: And when the eighth day was come, Moses called Aaron and his sons, and the ancients of Israel, and said to Aaron:

2.text: Take of the herd a calf for sin, and a ram for a holocaust, both without blemish, and offer them before the Lord.

3.text: And to the children of Israel thou shalt say: Take ye a he goat for sin, and a calf, and a lamb, both of a year old, and without blemish for a holocaust,

4.text: Also a bullock and a ram for peace offerings: and immolate them before the Lord, offering for the sacrifice of every one of them flour tempered with oil; for today the Lord will appear to you.

5.text: They brought therefore all things that Moses had commanded before the door of the tabernacle: where when all the multitude stood,

6.text: Moses said: This is the word, which the Lord hath commanded: do it, and his glory will appear to you.

7.text: And he said to Aaron: Approach to the altar, and offer sacrifice for thy sin: offer the holocaust, and pray for thyself and for the people: and when thou hast slain the people’s victim, pray for them, as the Lord hath commanded.

8.text: And forthwith Aaron, approaching to the altar, immolated the calf for his sin:

9.text: And his sons brought him the blood of it: and he dipped his finger therein, and touched the horns of the altar, and poured the rest at the foot thereof.

10.text: And the fat, and the little kidneys, and the caul of the liver, which are for sin, he burnt upon the altar, as the Lord had commanded Moses:

11.text: But the flesh and skins thereof he burnt with fire without the camp.

12.text: He immolated also the victim of holocaust: and his sons brought him the blood thereof, which he poured round about on the altar.

13.text: And the victim being cut into pieces, they brought to him the head and all the members, all which he burnt with fire upon the altar,

14.text: Having first washed the entrails and the feet with water.

15.text: Then offering for the sin of the people, he slew the he goat: and expiating the altar,

16.text: He offered the holocaust:

17.text: Adding in the sacrifice the libations, which are offered withal, and burning them upon the altar, besides the ceremonies of the morning holocaust.

18.text: He immolated also the bullock and the ram, the peace offerings of the people: and his sons brought him the blood, which he poured upon the altar round about.

19.text: The fat also of the bullock, and the rump of the ram, and the two little kidneys, with their fat, and the caul of the liver,

20.text: They put upon the breasts. And after the fat was burnt upon the altar,

21.text: Aaron separated their breasts, and the right shoulders, elevating them before the Lord, as Moses had commanded.

22.text: And stretching forth his hands to the people, he blessed them. And so the victims for sin, and the holocausts, and the peace offerings being finished, he came down.

23.text: And Moses and Aaron went into the tabernacle of the testimony, and afterwards came forth and blessed the people. And the glory of the Lord appeared to all the multitude:

24.text: And behold a fire, coming forth from the Lord, devoured the holocaust, and the fat that was upon the altar: which when the multitude saw, they praised the Lord, falling on their faces.

1.text: And Nadab and Abiu, the sons of Aaron, taking their censers, put fire therein, and incense on it, offering before the Lord strange fire: which was not commanded them.

2.text: And fire coming out from the Lord destroyed them, and they died before the Lord.

3.text: And Moses said to Aaron: This is what the Lord hath spoken: I will be sanctified in them that approach to me, and I will be glorified in the sight of all the people. And when Aaron heard this, he held his peace.

4.text: And Moses called Misael and Elisaphan, the sons of Oziel, the uncle of Aaron, and said to them: Go and take away your brethren from before the sanctuary, and carry them without the camp.

5.text: And they went forthwith and took them as they lay, vested with linen tunicks, and cast them forth, as had been commanded them.

6.text: And Moses said to Aaron, and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons: Uncover not your heads, and rend not your garments, lest perhaps you die, and indignation come upon all the congregation. Let your brethren, and all the house of Israel, bewail the burning which the Lord has kindled:

7.text: But you shall not go out of the door of the tabernacle, otherwise you shall perish, for the oil of the holy unction is on you. And they did all things according to the precept of Moses.

8.text: The Lord also said to Aaron:

9.text: You shall not drink wine nor any thing that may make drunk, thou nor thy sons, when you enter into the tabernacle of the testimony, lest you die: because it is an everlasting precept through your generations:

10.text: And that you may have knowledge to discern between holy and unholy, between unclean and clean:

11.text: And may teach the children of Israel all my ordinances which the Lord hath spoken to them by the hand of Moses.

12.text: And Moses spoke to Aaron, and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons that were left: Take the sacrifice that is remaining of the oblation of the Lord, and eat it without leaven beside the altar, because it is holy of holies.

13.text: And you shall eat it in a holy place: which is given to thee and thy sons of the oblations of the Lord, as it hath been commanded me.

14.text: The breast also that is offered, and the shoulder that is separated, you shall eat in a most clean place, thou and thy sons, and thy daughters with thee. For they are set aside for thee and thy children, of the victims of peace offerings of the children of Israel:

15.text: Because they have elevated before the Lord the shoulder and the breast, and the fat that is burnt on the altar, and they belong to thee and to thy sons by a perpetual law, as the Lord hath commanded.

16.text: While these things were a doing, when Moses sought for the buck goat, that had been offered for sin, he found it burnt: and being angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron that were left, he said:

17.text: Why did you not eat in the holy place the sacrifice for sin, which is most holy, and given to you, that you may bear the iniquity of the people, and may pray for them in the sight of the Lord,

18.text: Especially whereas none of the blood thereof hath been carried within the holy places, and you ought to have eaten it in the sanctuary, as was commanded me?

19.text: Aaron answered: This day hath been offered the victim for sin, and the holocaust before the Lord: and to me what thou seest has happened: how could I eat it, or please the Lord in the ceremonies, having a sorrowful heart?

20.text: Which when Moses had heard he was satisfied.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

2.text: Say to the children of Israel: These are the animals which you are to eat of all the living things of the earth.

3.text: Whatsoever hath the hoof divided, and cheweth the cud among the beasts, you shall eat.

4.text: But whatsoever cheweth indeed the cud, and hath a hoof, but divideth it not, as the camel, and others, that you shall not eat, but shall reckon it among the unclean.

5.text: The cherogrillus which cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof, is unclean.

6.text: The hare also: for that too cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof.

7.text: And the swine, which, though it divideth the hoof, cheweth not the cud.

8.text: The flesh of these you shall not eat, nor shall you touch their carcasses, because they are unclean to you.

9.text: These are the things that breed in the waters, and which it is lawful to eat. All that hath fins, and scales, as well in the sea, as in the rivers, and the pools, you shall eat.

10.text: But whatsoever hath not fins and scales, of those things that move and live in the waters, shall be an abomination to you,

11.text: And detestable: their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall avoid.

12.text: All that have not fins and scales, in the waters, shall be unclean.

13.text: Of birds these are they which you must not eat, and which are to be avoided by you: The eagle, and the griffon, and the osprey,

14.text: And the kite, and the vulture, according to their kind,

15.text: And all that is of the raven kind, according to their likeness.

16.text: The ostrich, and the owl, and the larus, and the hawk according to its kind.

17.text: The screech owl, and the cormorant, and the ibis,

18.text: And the swan, and the bittern, and the porphyrion,

19.text: The heron, and the charadrion according to its kind, the houp also, and the bat.

20.text: Of things that fly, whatsoever goeth upon four feet, shall be abominable to you.

21.text: But whatsoever walketh upon four feet, but hath the legs behind longer, wherewith it hoppeth upon the earth,

22.text: That you shall eat, as the bruchus in its kind, the attacus, and ophiomachus, and the locust, every one according to their kind.

23.text: But of flying things whatsoever hath four feet only, shall be an abomination to you:

24.text: And whosoever shall touch the carcasses of them, shall be defiled, and shall be unclean until the evening:

25.text: And if it be necessary that he carry any of these things when they are dead, he shall wash his clothes, and shall be unclean until the sun set.

26.text: Every beast that hath a hoof, but divideth it not, nor cheweth the cud, shall be unclean: and he that toucheth it, shall be defiled.
