27.text: That which walketh upon hands of all animals which go on all four, shall be unclean: he that shall touch their carcasses shall be defiled until evening.

28.text: And he that shall carry such carcasses, shall wash his clothes, and shall be unclean until evening: because all these things are unclean to you.

29.text: These also shall be reckoned among unclean things, of all that move upon the earth, the weasel, and the mouse, and the crocodile, every one according to their kind:

30.text: The shrew, and the chameleon, and the stellio, and the lizard, and the mole:

31.text: All these are unclean. He that toucheth their carcasses shall be unclean until the evening.

32.text: And upon what thing soever any of their carcasses shall fall, it shall be defiled, whether it be a vessel of wood, or a garment, or skins or haircloths; or any thing in which work is done, they shall be dipped in water, and shall be unclean until the evening, and so afterwards shall be clean.

33.text: But an earthen vessel, into which any of these shall fall, shall be defiled, and therefore is to be broken.

34.text: Any meat which you eat, if water from such a vessel be poured upon it, shall be unclean; and every liquor that is drunk out of any such vessel, shall be unclean.

35.text: And upon whatsoever thing any of these dead beasts shall fall, it shall be unclean: whether it be oven, or pots with feet, they shall be destroyed, and shall be unclean.

36.text: But fountains and cisterns, and all gatherings together of waters shall be clean. He that toucheth their carcasses shall be defiled.

37.text: If it fall upon seed corn, it shall not defile it.

38.text: But if any man pour water upon the seed, and afterwards it be touched by the carcasses, it shall be forthwith defiled.

39.text: If any beast die, of which it is lawful for you to eat, he that toucheth the carcass thereof, shall be unclean until the evening:

40.text: And he that eateth or carrieth any thing thereof, shall wash his clothes, and shall be unclean until the evening.

41.text: All that creepeth upon the earth shall be abominable, neither shall it be taken for meat.

42.text: Whatsoever goeth upon the breast on four feet, or hath many feet, or traileth on the earth, you shall not eat, because it is abominable.

43.text: Do not defile your souls, nor touch aught thereof, lest you be unclean,

44.text: For I am the Lord your God: be holy because I am holy. Defile not your souls by any creeping thing, that moveth upon the earth.

45.text: For I am the Lord, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might be your God.

46.text: You shall be holy, because I am holy. This is the law of beasts and fowls, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and creepeth on the earth:

47.text: That you may know the differences of the clean, and unclean, and know what you ought to eat, and what to refuse.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: If a woman having received seed shall bear a man child, she shall be unclean seven days, according to the days of the separation of her flowers.

3.text: And on the eighth day the infant shall be circumcised:

4.text: But she shall remain three and thirty days in the blood of her purification. She shall touch no holy thing, neither shall she enter into the sanctuary, until the days of her purification be fulfilled.

5.text: But if she shall bear a maid child, she shall be unclean two weeks, according to the custom of her monthly courses, and she shall remain in the blood of her purification sixty-six days.

6.text: And when the days of her purification are expired, for a son, or for a daughter, she shall bring to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, a lamb of a year old for a holocaust, and a young pigeon or a turtle for sin, and shall deliver them to the priest:

7.text: Who shall offer them before the Lord, and shall pray for her, and so she shall be cleansed from the issue of her blood. This is the law for her that beareth a man child or a maid child.

8.text: And if her hand find not sufficiency, and she is not able to offer a lamb, she shall take two turtles, or two young pigeons, one for a holocaust, and another for sin: and the priest shall pray for her, and so she shall be cleansed.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

2.text: The man in whose skin or flesh shalt arise a different colour or a blister, or as it were something shining, that is, the stroke of the leprosy, shall be brought to Aaron the priest, or any one of his sons.

3.text: And if he see the leprosy in his skin, and the hair turned white, and the place where the leprosy appears lower than the skin and the rest of the flesh: it is the stroke of the leprosy, and upon his judgment he shall be separated.

4.text: But if there be a shining whiteness in the skin, and not lower than the other flesh, and the hair be of the former colour, the priest shall shut him up seven days.

5.text: And the seventh day he shall look on him: and if the leprosy be grown no farther, and hath not spread itself in the skin, he shall shut him up again other seven days.

6.text: And on the seventh day, he shall look on him: if the leprosy be somewhat obscure, and not spread in the skin, he shall declare him clean, because it is but a scab: and the man shall wash his clothes, and shall be clean.

7.text: But if the leprosy grow again, after he was seen by the priest and restored to cleanness, he shall be brought to him,

8.text: And shall be condemned of uncleanness.

9.text: If the stroke of the leprosy be in a man, he shall be brought to the priest,

10.text: And he shall view him. And when there shall be a white colour in the skin, and it shall have changed the look of the hair, and the living flesh itself shall appear:

11.text: It shall be judged an inveterate leprosy, and grown into the skin. The priest therefore shall declare him unclean, and shall not shut him up, because he is evidently unclean.

12.text: But if the leprosy spring out running about in the skin, and cover all the skin from the head to the feet, whatsoever falleth under the sight of the eyes,

13.text: The priest shall view him, and shall judge that the leprosy which he has is very clean: because it is all turned into whiteness, and therefore the man shall be clean.

14.text: But when the live flesh shall appear in him,

15.text: Then by the judgment of the priest he shall be defiled, and shall be reckoned among the unclean: for live flesh, if it be spotted with leprosy, is unclean.

16.text: And if again it be turned into whiteness, and cover all the man,

17.text: The priest shall view him, and shall judge him to be clean.

18.text: When also there has been an ulcer in the flesh and the skin, and it has been healed,

19.text: And in the place of the ulcer, there appeareth a white scar, or somewhat red, the man shall be brought to the priest:

20.text: And when he shall see the place of the leprosy lower than the other flesh, and the hair turned white, he shall declare him unclean, for the plague of leprosy is broken out in the ulcer.

21.text: But if the hair be of the former colour, and the scar somewhat obscure, and be not lower than the flesh that is near it, he shall shut him up seven days.

22.text: And if it spread, he shall judge him to have the leprosy:

23.text: But if it stay in its place, it is but the scar of an ulcer, and the man shall be clean.

24.text: The flesh also and skin that hath been burnt, and after it is healed hath a white or a red scar,

25.text: The priest shall view it, and if he see it turned white, and the place thereof is lower than the other skin: he shall declare him unclean, because the evil of leprosy is broken out in the scar.

26.text: But if the colour of the hair be not changed, nor the blemish lower than the other flesh, and the appearance of the leprosy be somewhat obscure, he shall shut him up seven days,

27.text: And on the seventh day he shall view him: if the leprosy be grown farther in the skin, he shall declare him unclean.

28.text: But if the whiteness stay in its place, and be not very clear, it is the sore of a burning, and therefore he shall be cleansed, because it is only the scar of a burning.

29.text: If the leprosy break out in the head or the beard of a man or woman, the Priest shall see them,

30.text: And if the place be lower than the other flesh, and the hair yellow, and thinner than usual: he shall declare them unclean, because it is the leprosy of the head and the beard;

31.text: But if he perceive the place of the spot is equal with the flesh that is near it, and the hair black: he shall shut him up seven days,

32.text: And on the seventh day he shall look upon it. If the spot be not grown, and the hair keep its colour, and the place of the blemish be even with the other flesh:

33.text: The man shall be shaven all but the place of the spot, and he shall be shut up other seven days:

34.text: If on the seventh day the evil seem to have stayed in its place, and not lower than the other flesh, he shall cleanse him, and his clothes being washed he shall be clean.

35.text: But if after his cleansing the spot spread again in the skin,

36.text: He shall seek no more whether the hair be turned yellow, because he is evidently unclean.

37.text: But if the spot be stayed, and the hair be black, let him know that the man is healed, and let him confidently pronounce him clean.

38.text: If a whiteness appear in the skin of a man or a woman,

39.text: The priest shall view them. If he find that a darkish whiteness shineth in the skin, let him know that it is not the leprosy, but a white blemish, and that the man is clean.

40.text: The man whose hair falleth off from his head, he is bald and clean:

41.text: And if the hair fall from his forehead, he is bald before and clean.

42.text: But if in the bald head or in the bald forehead there be risen a white or reddish colour,

43.text: And the priest perceive this, he shall condemn him undoubtedly of leprosy which is risen in the bald part.

44.text: Now whosoever shall be defiled with the leprosy, and is separated by the judgment of the priest,

45.text: Shall have his clothes hanging loose, his head bare, his mouth covered with a cloth, and he shall cry out that he is defiled and unclean.

46.text: All the time that he is a leper and unclean, he shall dwell alone without the camp.

47.text: A woollen or linen garment that shall have the leprosy

48.text: In the warp, and the woof, or a skin. or whatsoever is made of a skin,

49.text: If it be infected with a white or red spot, it shall be accounted the leprosy, and shall be shewn to the priest.

50.text: And he shall look upon it and shall shut it up seven days:

51.text: And on the seventh day when he looketh on it again, if he find that it is grown, it is a fixed leprosy: he shall judge the garment unclean, and every thing wherein it shall be found:

52.text: And therefore it shall be burnt with fire.

53.text: But if he see that it is not grown,

54.text: He shall give orders, and they shall wash that part wherein the leprosy is, and he shall shut it up other seven days.

55.text: And when he shall see that the former colour is not returned, nor yet the leprosy spread, he shall judge it unclean, and shall burn it with fire, for the leprosy has taken hold of the outside of the garment, or through the whole.

56.text: But if the place of the leprosy be somewhat dark, after the garment is washed, he shall tear it off, and divide it from that which is sound.

57.text: And if after this there appear in those places that before were without spot, a flying and wandering leprosy: it must be burnt with fire.

58.text: If it cease, he shall wash with water the parts that are pure, the second time, and they shall be clean.

59.text: This is the law touching the leprosy of any woollen or linen garment, either in the warp or woof, or any thing of skins, how it ought to be cleansed, or pronounced unclean.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: This is the rite of a leper, when he is to be cleansed: he shall be brought to the priest:

3.text: Who going out of the camp when he shall find that the leprosy is cleansed,

4.text: Shall command him that is to be purified, to offer for himself two living sparrows, which it is lawful to eat, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.

5.text: And he shall command one of the sparrows to be immolated in an earthen vessel over living waters:

6.text: But the other that is alive he shall dip, with the cedar wood, and the scarlet and the hyssop, in the blood of the sparrow that is immolated:

7.text: Wherewith he shall sprinkle him that is to be cleansed seven times, that he may be rightly purified: and he shall let go the living sparrow, that it may fly into the field.

8.text: And when the man hath washed his clothes, he shall shave all the hair of his body, and shall be washed with water: and being purified, he shall enter into the camp, yet so that he tarry without his own tent seven days:

9.text: And on the seventh day he shall shave the hair of his head, and his beard and his eyebrows, and the hair of all his body. And having washed again his clothes, and his body,

10.text: On the eighth day he shall take two lambs without blemish, and an ewe of a year old without blemish, and three tenths of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice, and a sextary of oil apart.

11.text: And when the priest that purifieth the man, hath presented him, and all these things before the Lord, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony,

12.text: He shall take a lamb, and offer it for a trespass offering with the sextary of oil: and having offered all before the Lord,

13.text: He shall immolate the lamb, where the victim for sin is wont to be immolated, and the holocaust, that is, in the holy place: for as that which is for sin, so also the victim for a trespass offering pertaineth to the priest: it is holy of holies.

14.text: And the priest taking of the blood of the victim that was immolated for trespass, shall put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand and the great toe of his right foot:

15.text: And he shall pour of the sextary of oil into his own left hand,

16.text: And shall dip his right finger in it, and sprinkle it before the Lord seven times.

17.text: And the rest of the oil in his left hand, he shall pour upon the tip of the right ear of him that is cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand and the great toe of his right foot, and upon the blood that was shed for trespass,

18.text: And upon his head.

19.text: And he shall pray for him before the Lord, and shall offer the sacrifice for sin: then shall he immolate the holocaust,

20.text: And put it on the altar with the libations thereof, and the man shall be rightly cleansed.

21.text: But if he be poor, and his hand cannot find the things aforesaid: he shall take a lamb for an offering for trespass, that the priest may pray for him, and a tenth part of flour tempered with oil for a sacrifice, and a sextary of oil,

22.text: And two turtles or two young pigeons, of which one may be for sin, and the other for a holocaust:

23.text: And he shall offer them on the eighth day of his purification to the priest, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony before the Lord.

24.text: And the priest receiving the lamb for trespass, and the sextary of oil, shall elevate them together.

25.text: And the lamb being immolated, he shall put of the blood thereof upon the tip of the right ear of him that is cleansed, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and the great toe of his right foot:

26.text: But he shall pour part of the oil into his own left hand,

27.text: And dipping the finger of his right hand in it, he shall sprinkle it seven times before the Lord:

28.text: And he shall touch the tip of the right ear of him that is cleansed, and the thumb of his right hand and the great toe of his right foot, in the place of the blood that was shed for trespass.

29.text: And the other part of the oil that is in his left hand, he shall pour upon the head of the purified person, that he may appease the Lord for him.

30.text: And he shall offer a turtle, or young pigeon,

31.text: One for trespass, and the other for a holocaust, with their libations.

32.text: This is the sacrifice of a leper, that is not able to have all things that appertain to his cleansing.

33.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

34.text: When you shall be come into the land of Chanaan, which I will give you for a possession, if there be the plague of leprosy in a house,

35.text: He whose house it is, shall go and tell the priest, saying: It seemeth to me, that there is the plague of leprosy in my house,

36.text: And he shall command, that they carry forth all things out of the house, before he go into it, and see whether it have the leprosy, lest all things become unclean that are in the house. And afterwards he shall go in to view the leprosy of the house.

37.text: And if he see in the walls thereof as it were little dints, disfigured with paleness or redness, and lower than all the rest,

38.text: He shall go out of the door of the house, and forthwith shut it up seven days,

39.text: And returning on the seventh day, he shall look upon it. If he find that the leprosy is spread,

40.text: He shall command, that the stones wherein the leprosy is, be taken out, and cast without the city into an unclean place:

41.text: And that the house be scraped on the inside round about, and the dust of the scraping be scattered without the city into an unclean place:

42.text: And that other stones be laid in the place of them that were taken away, and the house be plastered with other mortar.

43.text: But if, after the stones be taken out, and the dust scraped off, and it be plastered with other earth,

44.text: The priest going in perceive that the leprosy is returned, and the walls full of spots, it is a lasting leprosy, and the house is unclean:

45.text: And they shall destroy it forthwith, and shall cast the stones and timber thereof, and all the dust without the town into an unclean place.

46.text: He that entereth into the house when it is shut, shall be unclean until evening,

47.text: And he that sleepeth in it, and eateth any thing, shall wash his clothes.

48.text: But if the priest going in perceive that the leprosy is not spread in the house, after it was plastered again, he shall purify it, it being cured,

49.text: And for the purification thereof he shall take two sparrows, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop:

50.text: And having immolated one sparrow In an earthen vessel over living waters,

51.text: He shall take the cedar wood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet, and the living sparrow, and shall dip all in the blood of the sparrow that is immolated, and in the living water, and he shall sprinkle the house seven times:

52.text: And shall purify it as well with the blood of the sparrow, as with the living water, and with the living sparrow, and with the cedar wood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet.

53.text: And when he hath let go the sparrow to fly freely away into the field, he shall pray for the house, and it shall be rightly cleansed.

54.text: This is the law of every kind of leprosy and stroke.

55.text: Of the leprosy of garments and houses,

56.text: Of a scar and of blisters breaking out, of a shining spot, and when the colours are diversely changed:

57.text: That it may be known when a thing is clean or unclean.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

2.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: The man that hath an issue of seed, shall be unclean.

3.text: And then shall he be judged subject to this evil, when a filthy humour, at every moment, cleaveth to his flesh, and gathereth there.

4.text: Every bed on which he sleepeth, shall be unclean, and every place on which he sitteth.

5.text: If any man touch his bed, he shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.

6.text: If a man sit where that man hath sitten, he also shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, shall be unclean until the evening.

7.text: He that toucheth his flesh, shall wash his clothes: and being himself washed with water shall be unclean until the evening.

8.text: If such a man cast his spittle upon him that is clean, he shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.

9.text: The saddle on which he hath sitten shall be unclean.

10.text: And whatsoever has been under him that hath the issue of seed, shall be unclean until the evening. He that carrieth any of these things, shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, he shall be unclean until the evening.

11.text: Every person whom such a one shall touch, not having washed his hands before, shall wash his clothes: and being washed with water, shall be unclean until the evening.

12.text: If he touch a vessel of earth, it shall be broken: but if a vessel of wood, if shall be washed with water.

13.text: If he who suffereth this disease be healed, he shall number seven days after his cleansing, and having washed his clothes, and all his body in living water, he shall be clean.

14.text: And on the eighth day he shall take two turtles, or two young pigeons, and he shall come before the Lord, to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and shall give them to the priest:

15.text: Who shall offer one for sin, and the other for a holocaust: and he shall pray for him before the Lord, that he may be cleansed of the issue of his seed.

16.text: The man from whom the seed of copulation goeth out, shall wash all his body with water: and he shall be unclean until the evening.

17.text: The garment or skin that he weareth, he shall wash with water, and it shall be unclean until the evening.

18.text: The woman, with whom he copulateth, shall be washed with water, and shall be unclean until the evening.

19.text: The woman, who at the return of the month, hath her issue of blood, shall be separated seven days. Every one that toucheth her, shall be unclean until the evening.

20.text: And every thing that she sleepeth on, or that she sitteth on in the days of her separation, shall be defiled.

21.text: He that toucheth her bed shall wash his clothes: and being himself washed with water, shall be unclean until the evening.

22.text: Whosoever shall touch any vessel on which she sitteth, shall wash his clothes: and himself being washed with water, shall be defiled until the evening.

24.text: If a man copulateth with her in the time of her flowers, he shall be unclean seven days: and every bed on which he shall sleep shall be defiled.

25.text: The woman that hath an issue of blood many days out of her ordinary time, or that ceaseth not to flow after the monthly courses, as long as she is subject to this disease, shall be unclean, in the same manner as if she were in her flowers.

26.text: Every bed on which she sleepeth, and every vessel on which she sitteth, shall be defiled.

27.text: Whosoever toucheth them shall wash his clothes: and himself being washed with water, shall be unclean until the evening.

28.text: If the blood stop and cease to run, she shall count seven days of her purification:

29.text: And on the eighth day she shall offer for herself to the priest, two turtles, or two young pigeons, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony:

30.text: And he shall offer one for sin, and the other for a holocaust, and he shall pray for her before the Lord, and for the issue of her uncleanness.

31.text: You shall teach therefore the children of Israel to take heed of uncleanness, that they may not die in their filth, when they shall have defiled my tabernacle that is among them.

32.text: This is the law of him that hath the issue of seed, and that is defiled by copulation.

33.text: And of the woman that is separated in her monthly times, or that hath a continual issue of blood, and of the man that sleepeth with her.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they were slain upon their offering strange fire:

2.text: And he commanded him, saying, Speak to Aaron thy brother, that he enter not at all into the sanctuary, which is within the veil before the propitiatory, with which the ark is covered, lest he die, (for I will appear in a cloud over the oracle,)

3.text: Unless he first do these things: He shall offer a calf for sin, and a ram for a holocaust.

4.text: He shall be vested with a linen tunick, he shall cover his nakedness with linen breeches: he shall be girded with a linen girdle, and he shall put a linen mitre upon his head: for these are holy vestments: all which he shall put on, after he is washed.

5.text: And he shall receive from the whole multitude of the children of Israel two buck goats for sin, and one ram for a holocaust.

6.text: And when he hath offered the calf and prayed for himself, and for his own house,

7.text: He shall make the two buck goats to stand before the Lord in the door of the tabernacle of the testimony:

8.text: And casting lots upon them both, one to be offered to the Lord, and the other to be the emissary goat:

9.text: That whose lot fell to be offered to the Lord, he shall offer for sin:

10.text: But that whose lot was to be the emissary goat, he shall present alive before the Lord, that he may pour out prayers upon him, and let him go into the wilderness.

11.text: After these things are duly celebrated, he shall offer the calf, and praying for himself and for his own house, he shall immolate it:

12.text: And taking the censer, which he hath filled with the burning coals of the altar, and taking up with his hand the compounded perfume for incense, he shall go in within the veil into the holy place:

13.text: That when the perfumes are put upon the fire, the cloud and vapour thereof may cover the oracle, which is over the testimony, and he may not die.

14.text: He shall take also of the blood of the calf, and sprinkle with his finger seven times towards the propitiatory to the east.

15.text: And when he hath killed the buck goat for the sin of the people, he shall carry in the blood thereof within the veil, as he was commanded to do with the blood of the calf, that he may sprinkle it over against the oracle,

16.text: And may expiate the sanctuary from the uncleanness of the children of Israel, and from their transgressions, and all their sins. According to this rite shall he do to the tabernacle of the testimony, which is fixed among them in the midst of the filth of their habitation.

17.text: Let no man be in the tabernacle when the high priest goeth into the sanctuary, to pray for himself and his house, and for the whole congregation of Israel, until he come out.

18.text: And when he is come out to the altar that is before the Lord, let him pray for himself, and taking the blood of the calf, and of the buck goat, let him pour it upon the horns thereof round about:

19.text: And sprinkling with his finger seven times, let him expiate, and sanctify it from the uncleanness of the children of Israel.

20.text: After he hath cleansed the sanctuary, and the tabernacle, and the altar, then let him offer the living goat:

21.text: And putting both hands upon his head, let him confess all the iniquities of the children of Israel, and all their offences and sins: and praying that they may light on his head, he shall turn him out by a man ready for it, into the desert.

22.text: And when the goat hath carried all their iniquities into an uninhabited land, and shall be let go into the desert,

23.text: Aaron shall return into the tabernacle of the testimony, and putting off the vestments, which he had on him before when he entered into the sanctuary, and leaving them there,

24.text: He shall wash his flesh in the holy place, and shall put on his own garments. And after that he has come out and hath offered his own holocaust, and that of the people, he shall pray both for himself, and for the people:

25.text: And the fat that is offered for sins, he shall burn upon the altar.

26.text: But he that hath let go the emissary goat, shall wash his clothes, and his body with water, and so shall enter into the camp.

27.text: But the calf and the buck goat, that were sacrificed for sin, and whose blood was carried into the sanctuary, to accomplish the atonement, they shall carry forth without the camp, and shall burn with fire, their skins and their flesh, and their dung:

28.text: And whosoever burneth them shall wash his clothes, and flesh with water, and so shall enter into the camp.

29.text: And this shall be to you an everlasting ordinance: The seventh month, the tenth day of the month, you shall afflict your souls, and shall do no work, whether it be one of your own country, or a stranger that sojourneth among you.

30.text: Upon this day shall be the expiation for you, and the cleansing from all your sins: you shall be cleansed before the Lord.

31.text: For it is a sabbath of rest, and you shall afflict your souls by a perpetual religion.

32.text: And the priest that is anointed, and whose hands are consecrated to do the office of the priesthood in his father’s stead, shall make atonement; and he shall be vested with the linen robe and the holy vestments,

33.text: And he shall expiate the sanctuary and the tabernacle of the testimony and the altar, the priest also and all the people.

34.text: And this shall be an ordinance for ever, that you pray for the children of Israel, and for all their sins once in a year. He did therefore as the Lord had commanded Moses.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Speak to Aaron and his sons, and to all the children of Israel, saying to them: This is the word, which the Lord hath commanded, saying:

3.text: Any man whosoever of the house of Israel if he kill an ox, or a sheep, or a goat in the camp, or without the camp,

4.text: And offer it not at the door of the tabernacle an oblation to the Lord, shall be guilty of blood: as if he had shed blood, so shall he perish from the midst of his people.

5.text: Therefore the children of Israel shall bring to the priest their victims, which they kill in the field, that they may be sanctified to the Lord before the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and they may sacrifice them for peace offerings to the Lord.

6.text: And the priest shall pour the blood upon the altar of the Lord, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, and shall burn the fat for a sweet odour to the Lord.

7.text: And they shall no more sacrifice their victims to devils, with whom they have committed fornication. It shall be an ordinance for ever to them and to their posterity.

8.text: And thou shalt say to them: The man of the house of Israel, and of the strangers who sojourn among you, that offereth a holocaust or a victim,

9.text: And bringeth it not to the door of the tabernacle of the testimony, that it may be offered to the Lord, shall perish from among his people.

10.text: If any man whosoever of the house of Israel, and of the strangers that sojourn among them, eat blood, I will set my face against his soul, and will cut him off from among his people:

11.text: Because the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you, that you may make atonement with it upon the altar for your souls, and the blood may be for an expiation of the soul.

12.text: Therefore I have said to the children of Israel: No soul of you, nor of the strangers that sojourn among you, shall eat blood.

13.text: Any man whosoever of the children of Israel, and of the strangers that sojourn among you, if by hunting or fowling, he take a wild beast or a bird, which is lawful to eat, let him pour out its blood, and cover it with earth.

14.text: For the life of all flesh is in the blood: therefore I said to the children of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any flesh at all, because the life of the flesh is in the blood, and whosoever eateth it, shall be cut off.

15.text: The soul that eateth that which died of itself, or has been caught by a beast, whether he be one of your own country or a stranger, shall wash his clothes and himself with water, and shall be defiled until the evening: and in this manner he shall be made clean.

16.text: But if he do not wash his clothes, and his body, he shall bear his iniquity.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: I am the Lord your God.

3.text: You shall not do according to the custom of the land of Egypt, in which you dwelt: neither shall you act according to the manner of the country of Chanaan, into which I will bring you, nor shall you walk in their ordinances.

4.text: You shall do my judgments, and shall observe my precepts, and shall walk in them. I am the Lord your God.

5.text: Keep my laws and my judgments, which if a man do, he shall live in them. I am the Lord.

6.text: No man shall approach to her that is near of kin to him, to uncover her nakedness. I am the Lord.

7.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother: she is thy mother, thou shalt not uncover her nakedness.

8.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father’s wife: for it is the nakedness of thy father.

9.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy sister by father or by mother, whether born at home or abroad.

10.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy son’s daughter, or thy daughter’s daughter: because it is thy own nakedness.

11.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father’s wife’s daughter, whom she bore to thy father, and who is thy sister.

12.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father’s sister: because she is the flesh of thy father.

13.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy mother’s sister: because she is thy mother’s flesh.

14.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy father’s brother: neither shalt thou approach to his wife, who is joined to thee by affinity.

15.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy daughter in law: because she is thy son’s wife, neither shalt thou discover her shame.

16.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy brother’s wife: because it is the nakedness of thy brother.

17.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy wife and her daughter. Thou shalt not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter, to discover her shame: because they are her flesh, and such copulation is incest.

18.text: Thou shalt not take thy wife’s sister for a harlot, to rival her, neither shalt thou discover her nakedness, while she is yet living.

19.text: Thou shalt not approach to a woman having her flowers, neither shalt thou uncover her nakedness.

20.text: Thou shalt not lie with thy neighbour’s wife, nor be defiled with mingling of seed.

21.text: Thou shalt not give any of thy seed to be consecrated to the idol Moloch, nor defile the name of thy God: I am the Lord.

22.text: Thou shalt not lie with mankind as with womankind, because it is an abomination.

23.text: Thou shalt not copulate with any beast, neither shalt thou be defiled with it. A woman shall not lie down to a beast, nor copulate with it: because it is a heinous crime.

24.text: Defile not yourselves with any of these things with which all the nations have been defiled, which I will cast out before you,

25.text: And with which the land is defiled: the abominations of which I will visit, that it may vomit out its inhabitants.

26.text: Keep ye my ordinances and my judgments, and do not any of these abominations: neither any of your own nation, nor any stranger that sojourneth among you.

27.text: For all these detestable things the inhabitants of the land have done, that; were before you, and have defiled it.

28.text: Beware then, lest in like manner, it vomit you also out, if you do the like things, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.

29.text: Every soul that shall commit any of these abominations, shall perish from the midst of his people.

30.text: Keep my commandments. Do not the things which they have done, that have been before you, and be not defiled therein. I am the Lord your God.

1.text: The Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: Be ye holy, because I the Lord your God am holy.

3.text: Let every one fear his father, and his mother. Keep my sabbaths. I am the Lord your God.

4.text: Turn ye not to idols, nor make to yourselves molten gods. I am the Lord your God.

5.text: If ye offer in sacrifice a peace offering to the Lord, that he may be favourable,

6.text: You shall eat it on the same day it was offered, and the next day: and whatsoever shall be left until the third day, you shall burn with fire.

7.text: If after two days any man eat thereof, he shall be profane and guilty of impiety:

8.text: And shall bear his iniquity, because he hath defiled the holy thing of the Lord, and that soul shall perish from among his people.

9.text: When thou reapest the corn of thy land, thou shalt not cut down all that is on the face of the earth to the very ground: nor shalt thou gather the ears that remain.

10.text: Neither shalt thou gather the bunches and grapes that fall down in thy vineyard, but shalt leave them to the poor and the strangers to take. I am the Lord your God.

11.text: You shall not steal. You shall not lie, neither shall any man deceive his neighbour.

12.text: Thou shalt not swear falsely by my name, nor profane the name of thy God. I am the Lord.

13.text: Thou shalt not calumniate thy neighbour, nor oppress him by violence. The wages of him that hath been hired by thee shall not abide with thee until the morning.

14.text: Thou shalt not speak evil of the deaf, nor put a stumblingblock before the blind: but thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, because I am the Lord.

15.text: Thou shalt not do that which is unjust, nor judge unjustly. Respect not the person of the poor, nor honour the countenance of the mighty. But judge thy neighbour according to justice.

16.text: Thou shalt not be a detractor nor a whisperer among the people. Thou shalt not stand against the blood of thy neighbour. I am the Lord.

17.text: Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thy heart, but reprove him openly, lest thou incur sin through him.

18.text: Seek not revenge, nor be mindful of the injury of thy citizens. Thou shalt love thy friend as thyself. I am the Lord.

19.text: Keep ye my laws. Thou shalt not make thy cattle to gender with beasts of any other kind. Thou shalt not sow thy field with different seeds. Thou shalt not wear a garment that is woven of two sorts.

20.text: If a man carnally lie with a woman that is a bondservant and marriageable, and yet not redeemed with a price, nor made free: they both shall be scourged, and they shall not be put to death, because she was not a free woman.

21.text: And for his trespass he shall offer a ram to the Lord, at the door of the tabernacle of the testimony:

22.text: And the priest shall pray for him and for his sin before the Lord, and he shall have mercy on him, and the sin shall be forgiven.

23.text: When you shall be come into the land, and shall have planted in it fruit trees, you shall take away the firstfruits of them: the fruit that comes forth shall be unclean to you, neither shall you eat of them.

24.text: But in the fourth year, all their fruit shall be sanctified, to the praise of the Lord.

25.text: And in the fifth year you shall eat the fruits thereof, gathering the increase thereof. I am the Lord your God.

26.text: You shall not eat with blood. You shall not divine nor observe dreams.

27.text: Nor shall you cut your hair roundwise: nor shave your beard.

28.text: You shall not make any cuttings in your flesh, for the dead, neither shall you make in yourselves any figures or marks: I am the Lord.

29.text: Make not thy daughter a common strumpet, lest the land be defiled, and filled with wickedness.

30.text: Keep ye my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary. I am the Lord.

31.text: Go not aside after wizards, neither ask any thing of soothsayers, to be defiled by them: I am the Lord your God.

32.text: Rise up before the hoary head, and honour the person of the aged man: and fear the Lord thy God. I am the Lord.

33.text: If a stranger dwell in your land, and abide among you, do not upbraid him:

34.text: But let him be among you as one of the same country: and you shall love him as yourselves: for you were strangers in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

35.text: Do not any unjust thing in judgment, in rule, in weight, or in measure.

36.text: Let the balance be just and the weights equal, the bushel just, and the sextary equal. I am the Lord your God, that brought you out of the land of Egypt.

37.text: Keep all my precepts, and all my judgments, and do them. I am the Lord.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel: If any man of the children of Israel, or of the strangers, that dwell in Israel, give of his seed to the idol Moloch, dying let him die: the people of the land shall stone him.

3.text: And I will set my face against him: and I will cut him off from the midst of his people, because he hath given of his seed to Moloch, and hath defiled my sanctuary, and profaned my holy name.

4.text: And if the people of the land neglecting, and as it were little regarding my commandment, let alone the man that hath given of his seed to Moloch, and will not kill him:

5.text: I will set my face against that man, and his kindred, and will cut off both him and all that consented with him, to commit fornication with Moloch, out of the midst of their people.

6.text: The soul that shall go aside after magicians, and soothsayers, and shall commit fornication with them, I will set my face against that soul, and destroy it out of the midst of its people.

7.text: Sanctify yourselves, and be ye holy because I am the Lord your God.

8.text: Keep my precepts, and do them. I am the Lord that sanctify you.

9.text: He that curseth his father, or mother, dying let him die: he hath cursed his father, and mother, let his blood be upon him.

10.text: If any man commit adultery with the wife of another, and defile his neighbour’s wife, let them be put to death, both the adulterer and the adulteress.

11.text: If a man lie with his stepmother, and discover the nakedness of his father, let them both be put to death: their blood be upon them.

12.text: If any man lie with his daughter in law, let both die, because they have done a heinous crime: their blood be upon them.

13.text: If any one lie with a man as with a woman, both have committed an abomination, let them be put to death: their blood be upon them.

14.text: If any man after marrying the daughter, marry her mother, he hath done a heinous crime: he shall be burnt alive with them: neither shall so great an abomination remain in the midst of you.

15.text: He that shall copulate with any beast or cattle, dying let him die, the beast also ye shall kill.

16.text: The woman that shall lie under any beast, shall be killed together with the same: their blood be upon them.

17.text: If any man take his sister, the daughter of his father, or the daughter of his mother, and see her nakedness, and she behold her brother’s shame: they have committed a crime: they shall be slain, in the sight of their people, because they have discovered one another’s nakedness, and they shall bear their iniquity.

18.text: If any man lie with a woman in her flowers, and uncover her nakedness, and she open the fountain of her blood, both shall be destroyed out of the midst of their people.

19.text: Thou shalt not uncover the nakedness of thy aunt by thy mother, and of thy aunt by thy father: he that doth this, hath uncovered the shame of his own flesh, both shall bear their iniquity.

20.text: If any man lie with the wife of his uncle by the father, or of his uncle by the mother, and uncover the shame of his near akin, both shall bear their sin: they shall die without children.

21.text: He that marrieth his brother’s wife, doth an unlawful thing, he hath uncovered his brother’s nakedness: they shall be without children.

22.text: Keep my laws and my judgments, and do them: lest the land into which you are to enter to dwell therein, vomit you also out.

23.text: Walk not after the laws of the nations, which I will cast out before you. For they have done all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.

24.text: But to you I say: Possess their land which I will give you for an inheritance, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God, who have separated you from other people.

25.text: Therefore do you also separate the clean beast from the unclean, and the clean fowl from the unclean: defile not your souls with beasts, or birds, or any things that move on the earth, and which I have shewn you to be unclean.

26.text: You shall be holy unto me, because I the Lord am holy, and I have separated you from other people, that you should be mine.

27.text: A man, or woman, in whom there is a pythonical or divining spirit, dying let them die: they shall stone them: their blood be upon them.

1.text: The Lord said also to Moses: Speak to the priests the sons of Aaron, and thou shalt say to them: Let not a priest incur an uncleanness at the death of his citizens:

2.text: But only for his kin, such as are near in blood, that is to say, for his father and for his mother, and for his son, and for his daughter, for his brother also,

3.text: And for a maiden sister, who hath had no husband:

4.text: But not even for the prince of his people shall he do any thing that may make him unclean.

5.text: Neither shall they shave their head, nor their beard, nor make incisions in their flesh.

6.text: They shall be holy to their God, and shall not profane his name: for they offer the burnt offering of the Lord, and the bread of their God, and therefore they shall be holy.

7.text: They shall not take to wife a harlot or a vile prostitute, nor one that has been put away from her husband: because they are consecrated to their God,

8.text: And offer the loaves of proposition. Let them therefore be holy, because I also am holy, the Lord, who sanctify them.

9.text: If the daughter of a priest be taken in whoredom, and dishonour the name of her father, she shall be burnt with fire.

10.text: The high priest, that is to say, the priest, is the greatest among his brethren, upon whose head the oil of unction hath been poured, and whose hands have been consecrated for the priesthood, and who hath been vested with the holy vestments, shall not uncover his head, he shall not rend his garments:

11.text: Nor shall he go in at all to any dead person: not even for his father, or his mother, shall he be defiled:

12.text: Neither shall he go out of the holy places, lest he defile the sanctuary of the Lord, because the oil of the holy unction of his God is upon him. I am the Lord.

13.text: He shall take a virgin unto his wife:

14.text: But a widow or one that is divorced, or defiled, or a harlot, he shall not take, but a maid of his own people:

15.text: He shall not mingle the stock of his kindred with the common people of his nation: for I am the Lord who sanctify him.

16.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

17.text: Say to Aaron: Whosoever of thy seed throughout their families, hath a blemish, he shall not offer bread to his God.

18.text: Neither shall he approach to minister to him: If he be blind, if he be lame, if he have a little, or a great, or a crooked nose,

19.text: If his foot, or if his hand be broken,

20.text: If he be crookbacked, or blear eyed, or have a pearl in his eye, or a continual scab, or a dry scurf in his body, or a rupture:

21.text: Whosoever of the seed of Aaron the priest hath a blemish, he shall not approach to offer sacrifices to the Lord, nor bread to his God.

22.text: He shall eat nevertheless of the loaves, that are offered in the sanctuary,

23.text: Yet so that he enter not within the veil, nor approach to the altar, because he hath a blemish, and he must not defile my sanctuary. I am the Lord who sanctify them.

24.text: Moses therefore spoke to Aaron, and to his sons and to all Israel, all the things that had been commanded him.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they beware of those things that are consecrated of the children of Israel, and defile not the name of the things sanctified to me, which they offer. I am the Lord.

3.text: Say to them and to their posterity: Every man of your race, that approacheth to those things that are consecrated, and which the children of Israel have offered to the Lord, in whom there is uncleanness, shall perish before the Lord. I am the Lord.

4.text: The man of the seed of Aaron, that is a leper, or that suffereth a running of the seed, shall not eat of those things that are sanctified to me, until he be healed. He that toucheth any thing unclean by occasion of the dead, and he whose seed goeth from him as in generation,

5.text: And he that toucheth a creeping thing, or any unclean thing, the touching of which is defiling,

6.text: Shall be unclean until the evening, and shall not eat those things that are sanctified: but when he hath washed his flesh with water,

7.text: And the sun is down, then being purified, he shall eat of the sanctified things, because it is his meat.

8.text: That which dieth of itself, and that which was taken by a beast, they shall not eat, nor be defiled therewith, I am the Lord.

9.text: Let them keep my precepts, that they may not fall into sin, and die in the sanctuary, when they shall have defiled it. I am the Lord who sanctify them.

10.text: No stranger shall eat of the sanctified things: a sojourner of the priests, or a hired servant, shall not eat of them.

11.text: But he whom the priest hath bought, and he that is his servant, born in his house, these shall eat of them.

12.text: If the daughter of a priest be married to any of the people, she shall not eat of those things that are sanctified, nor of the firstfruits.

13.text: But if she be a widow, or divorced, and having no children return to her father’s house, she shall eat of her father’s meats, as she was wont to do when she was a maid, no stranger hath leave to eat of them.

14.text: He that eateth of the sanctified things through ignorance, shall add the fifth part with that which he ate, and shall give it to the priest into the sanctuary.

15.text: And they shall not profane the sanctified things of the children of Israel, which they offer to the Lord:

16.text: Lest perhaps they bear the iniquity of their trespass, when they shall have eaten the sanctified things. I am the Lord who sanctify them.

17.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

18.text: Speak to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: The man of the house of Israel, and of the strangers who dwell with you, that offereth his oblation, either paying his vows, or offering of his own accord, whatsoever it be which he presenteth for a holocaust of the Lord,

19.text: To be offered by you, it shall be a male without blemish of the calves, or of the sheep, or of the goats.

20.text: If it have a blemish you shall not offer it, neither shall it be acceptable.

21.text: The man that offereth a victim of peace offerings to the Lord, either paying his vows, or offering of his own accord, whether of calves or of sheep, shall offer it without blemish, that it may be acceptable: there shall be no blemish in it.

22.text: If it be blind, or broken, or have a scar or blisters, or a scab, or a dry scurf: you shall not offer them to the Lord, nor burn any thing of them upon the Lord’s altar.

23.text: An ox or a sheep, that hath the ear and the tail cut off, thou mayst offer voluntarily: but a vow may not be paid with them.

24.text: You shall not offer to the Lord any beast that hath the testicles bruised, or crushed, or cut and taken away: neither shall you do any such thing in your land.

25.text: You shall not offer bread to your God, from the hand of a stranger, nor any other thing that he would give: because they are all corrupted, and defiled: you shall not receive them.

26.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

27.text: When a bullock, or a sheep, or a goat, is brought forth, they shall be seven days under the udder of their dam: but the eighth day, and thenceforth, they may be offered to the Lord.

28.text: Whether it be a cow, or a sheep, they shall not be sacrificed the same day with their young ones.

29.text: If you immolate a victim for thanksgiving to the Lord, that he may be favourable,

30.text: You shall eat it the same day, there shall not any of it remain until the morning of the next day. I am the Lord.

31.text: Keep my commandments, and do them. I am the Lord.

32.text: Profane not my holy name, that I may be sanctified in the midst of the children of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctify you,

33.text: And who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might be your God: I am the Lord.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall call holy.

3.text: Six days shall ye do work: the seventh day, because it is the rest of the sabbath, shall be called holy. You shall do no work on that day: it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your habitations.

4.text: These also are the holy days of the Lord, which you must celebrate in their seasons.

5.text: The first month, the fourteenth day of the month at evening, is the phase of the Lord:

6.text: And the fifteenth day of the same month is the solemnity of the unleavened bread of the Lord. Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread.

7.text: The first day shall be most solemn unto you, and holy: you shall do no servile work therein:

8.text: But you shall offer sacrifice in fire to the Lord seven days. And the seventh day shall be more solemn, and more holy: and you shall do no servile work therein.

9.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

10.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: When you shall have entered into the land which I will give you, and shall reap your corn, you shall bring sheaves of ears, the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest:

11.text: Who shall lift up the sheaf before the Lord, the next day after the sabbath, that it may be acceptable for you, and shall sanctify it.

12.text: And on the same day that the sheaf is consecrated, a lamb without blemish of the first year shall be killed for a holocaust of the Lord.

13.text: And the libations shall be offered with it, two tenths of flour tempered with oil for a burnt offering of the Lord, and a most sweet odour: libations also of wine, the fourth part of a hin.

14.text: You shall not eat either bread, or parched corn, or frumenty of the harvest, until the day that you shall offer thereof to your God. It is a precept for ever throughout your generations, and all your dwellings.

15.text: You shall count therefore from the morrow after the sabbath, wherein you offered the sheaf of the firstfruits, seven full weeks.

16.text: Even unto the morrow after the seventh week be expired, that is to say, fifty days, and so you shall offer a new sacrifice to the Lord.

17.text: Out of all your dwellings, two loaves of the firstfruits, of two tenths of flour leavened, which you shall bake for the firstfruits of the Lord.

18.text: And you shall offer with the loaves seven lambs without blemish of the first year, and one calf from the herd, and two rams, and they shall be for a holocaust with their libations for a most sweet odour to the Lord.

19.text: You shall offer also a buck goat for sin, and two lambs of the first year for sacrifices of peace offerings.

20.text: And when the priest hath lifted them up with the loaves of the firstfruits before the Lord, they shall fall to his use.

21.text: And you shall call this day most solemn, and most holy. You shall do no servile work therein. It shall be an everlasting ordinance in all your dwellings and generations.

22.text: And when you reap the corn of your land, you shall not cut it to the very ground: neither shall you gather the ears that remain; but you shall leave them for the poor and for the strangers. I am the Lord your God.

23.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

24.text: Say to the children of Israel: The seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall keep a sabbath, a memorial, with the sound of trumpets, and it shall be called holy.

25.text: You shall do no servile work therein, and you shall offer a holocaust to the Lord.

26.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

27.text: Upon the tenth day of this seventh month shall be the day of atonement, it shall be most solemn, and shall be called holy: and you shall afflict your souls on that day, and shall offer a holocaust to the Lord.

28.text: You shall do no servile work in the time of this day: because it is a day of propitiation, that the Lord your God may be merciful unto you.

29.text: Every soul that is not afflicted on this day, shall perish from among his people:

30.text: And every soul that shall do any work, the same will I destroy from among his people.

31.text: You shall do no work therefore on that day: it shall be an everlasting ordinance unto you in all your generations, and dwellings.

32.text: It is a sabbath of rest, and you shall afflict your souls beginning on the ninth day of the month: from evening until evening you shall celebrate your sabbaths.

33.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

34.text: Say to the children of Israel: From the fifteenth day of this same seventh month, shall be kept the feast of tabernacles seven days to the Lord.

35.text: The first day shall be called most solemn and most holy: you shall do no servile work therein. And seven days you shall offer holocausts to the Lord.

36.text: The eighth day also shall be most solemn and most holy, and you shall offer holocausts to the Lord: for it is the day of assembly and congregation: you shall do no servile work therein.

37.text: These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall call most solemn and most holy, and shall offer on them oblations to the Lord, holocausts and libations according to the rite of every day,

38.text: Besides the sabbaths of the Lord, and your gifts, and those things that you offer by vow, or which you shall give to the Lord voluntarily.

39.text: So from the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you shall have gathered in all the fruits of your land, you shall celebrate the feast of the Lord seven days: on the first day and the eighth shall be a sabbath, that is a day of rest.

40.text: And you shall take to you on the first day the fruits of the fairest tree, and branches of palm trees, and boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook, and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God.

41.text: And you shall keep the solemnity thereof seven days in the year. It shall be an everlasting ordinance in your generations. In the seventh month shall you celebrate this feast.

42.text: And you shall dwell in bowers seven days: every one that is of the race of Israel, shall dwell in tabernacles:

43.text: That your posterity may know, that I made the children of Israel to dwell in tabernacles, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

44.text: And Moses spoke concerning the feasts of the Lord to the children of Israel.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee the finest and clearest oil of olives, to furnish the lamps continually,

3.text: Without the veil of the testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant. And Aaron shall set them from evening until morning before the Lord, by a perpetual service and rite in your generations.

4.text: They shall be set upon the most pure candlestick before the Lord continually.

5.text: Thou shalt take also fine flour, and shalt bake twelve loaves thereof, two tenths shall be in every loaf:

6.text: And thou shalt set them six and six one against another upon the most clean table before the Lord:

7.text: And thou shalt put upon them the clearest frankincense, that the bread may be for a memorial of the oblation of the Lord.

8.text: Every sabbath they shall be changed before the Lord, being received of the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant:

9.text: And they shall be Aaron’s and his sons’, that they may eat them in the holy place: because it is most holy of the sacrifices of the Lord by a perpetual right.

10.text: And behold there went out the son of a woman of Israel, whom she had of an Egyptian, among the children of Israel, and fell at words in the camp with a man of Israel.

11.text: And when he had blasphemed the name, and had cursed it, he was brought to Moses: (now his mother was called Salumith, the daughter of Dabri, of the tribe of Dan:)

12.text: And they put him into prison, till they might know what the Lord would command.

13.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses,

14.text: Saying: Bring forth the blasphemer without the camp, and let them that heard him, put their hands upon his head, and let all the people stone him.

15.text: And thou shalt speak to the children of Israel: the man that curseth his God, shall bear his sin:

16.text: And he that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, dying let him die: all the multitude shall stone him, whether he be a native or a stranger. He that blasphemeth the name of the Lord, dying let him die.

17.text: He that striketh and killeth a man, dying let him die.

18.text: He that killeth a beast, shall make it good, that is to say, shall give beast for beast.

19.text: He that giveth a blemish to any of his neighbours: as he hath done, so shall it be done to him:

20.text: Breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, shall he restore. What blemish he gave, the like shall he be compelled to suffer.

21.text: He that striketh a beast, shall render another. He that striketh a man shall be punished.

22.text: Let there be equal judgment among you, whether he be a stranger, or a native that offends: because I am the Lord your God.

23.text: And Moses spoke to the children of Israel: and they brought forth him that had blasphemed, without the camp, and they stoned him. And the children of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses in mount Sinai, saying:

2.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: When you shall have entered into the land which I will give you, observe the rest of the sabbath to the Lord.

3.text: Six years thou shalt sow thy field and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and shalt gather the fruits thereof:

4.text: But in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath to the land, of the resting of the Lord: thou shalt not sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard.

5.text: What the ground shall bring forth of itself, thou shalt not reap: neither shalt thou gather the grapes of the firstfruits as a vintage: for it is a year of rest to the land:

6.text: But they shall be unto you for meat, to thee and to thy manservant, to thy maidservant and thy hireling, and to the strangers that sojourn with thee:

7.text: All things that grow shall be meat to thy beasts and to thy cattle.

8.text: Thou shalt also number to thee seven weeks of years, that is to say, seven times seven, which together make forty-nine years:

9.text: And thou shalt sound the trumpet in the seventh month, the tenth day of the month, in the time of the expiation in all your land.

10.text: And thou shalt sanctify the fiftieth year, and shalt proclaim remission to all the inhabitants of thy land: for it is the year of jubilee. Every man shall return to his possession, and every one shall go back to his former family:

11.text: Because it is the jubilee and the fiftieth year. You shall not sow, nor reap the things that grow in the field of their own accord, neither shall you gather the firstfruits of the vines,

12.text: Because of the sanctification of the jubilee: but as they grow you shall presently eat them.

13.text: In the year of the jubilee all shall return to their possessions.

14.text: When thou shalt sell any thing to thy neighbour, or shalt buy of him; grieve not thy brother: but thou shalt buy of him according to the number of years from the jubilee.

15.text: And he shall sell to thee according to the computation of the fruits.

16.text: The more years remain after the jubilee, the more shall the price increase: and the less time is counted, so much the less shall the purchase cost. For he shall sell to thee the time of the fruits.

17.text: Do not afflict your countrymen, but let every one fear his God: because I am the Lord your God.

18.text: Do my precepts, and keep my judgments, and fulfill them: that you may dwell in the land without any fear,

19.text: And the ground may yield you its fruits, of which you may eat your fill, fearing no man’s invasion.

20.text: But if you say: What shall we eat the seventh year, if we sow not, nor gather our fruits?

21.text: I will give you my blessing the sixth year, and it shall yield the fruits of three years:

22.text: And the eighth year you shall sow, and shall eat of the old fruits, until the ninth year: till new grow up, you shall eat the old store.

23.text: The land also shall not be sold for ever: because it is mine, and you are strangers and sojourners with me.

24.text: For which cause all the country of your possession shall be under the condition of redemption.

25.text: If thy brother being impoverished sell his little possession, and his kinsman will, he may redeem what he had sold.

26.text: But if he have no kinsman, and he himself can find the price to redeem it:

27.text: The value of the fruits shall be counted from that time when he sold it: and the overplus he shall restore to the buyer, and so shall receive his possession again.

28.text: But if his hands find not the means to repay the price, the buyer shall have what he bought, until the year of the jubilee. For in that year all that is sold shall return to the owner, and to the ancient possessor.

29.text: He that selleth a house within the walls of a city, shall have the liberty to redeem it, until one year be expired:

30.text: If he redeem it not, and the whole year be fully out, the buyer shall possess it, and his posterity for ever, and it cannot be redeemed, not even in the jubilee.

31.text: But if the house be in a village, that hath no walls, it shall be sold according to the same law as the fields: if it be not redeemed before, in the jubilee it shall return to the owner.

32.text: The houses of Levites, which are in cities, may always be redeemed:

33.text: If they be not redeemed, in the jubilee they shall all return to the owners, because the houses of the cities of the Levites are for their possessions among the children of Israel.

34.text: But let not their suburbs be sold, because it is a perpetual possession.

35.text: If thy brother be impoverished, and weak of hand, and thou receive him as a stranger and sojourner, and he live with thee,

36.text: Take not usury of him nor more than thou gavest: fear thy God, that thy brother may live with thee.

37.text: Thou shalt not give him thy money upon usury, nor exact of him any increase of fruits.

38.text: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that I might give you the land of Chanaan, and might be your God.

39.text: If thy brother constrained by poverty, sell himself to thee, thou shalt not oppress him with the service of bondservants:

40.text: But he shall be as a hireling, and a sojourner: he shall work with thee until the year of the jubilee,

41.text: And afterwards he shall go out with his children, and shall return to his kindred and to the possession of his fathers,

42.text: For they are my servants, and I brought them out of the land of Egypt: let them not be sold as bondmen:

43.text: Afflict him not by might, but fear thy God.

44.text: Let your bondmen, and your bondwomen, be of the nations that are round about you.

45.text: And of the strangers that sojourn among you, or that were born of them in your land, these you shall have for servants:

46.text: And by right of inheritance shall leave them to your posterity, and shall possess them for ever. But oppress not your brethren the children of Israel by might.

47.text: If the hand of a stranger or a sojourner grow strong among you, and thy brother being impoverished sell himself to him, or to any of his race:

48.text: After the sale he may be redeemed. He that will of his brethren shall redeem him:

49.text: Either his uncle, or his uncle’s son, or his kinsman, by blood, or by affinity. But if he himself be able also, he shall redeem himself,

50.text: Counting only the years from the time of his selling unto the year of the jubilee: and counting the money that he was sold for, according to the number of the years and the reckoning of a hired servant,

51.text: If there be many years that remain until the jubilee, according to them shall he also repay the price.

52.text: If few, he shall make the reckoning with him according to the number of the years, and shall repay to the buyer of what remaineth of the years,

53.text: His wages being allowed for which he served before: he shall not afflict him violently in thy sight.

54.text: And if by these means he cannot be redeemed, in the year of the jubilee he shall go out with his children.

55.text: For the children of Israel are my servants, whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt.

1.text: I am the Lord your God: you shall not make to yourselves any idol or graven thing, neither shall you erect pillars, nor set up a remarkable stone in your land, to adore it: for I am the Lord your God.

2.text: Keep my sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary: I am the Lord.

3.text: If you walk in my precepts, and keep my commandments, and do them, I will give you rain in due seasons.

4.text: And the ground shall bring forth its increase, and the trees shall be filled with fruit.

5.text: The threshing of your harvest shall reach unto the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto the sowing time: and you shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in your land without fear.

6.text: I will give peace in your coasts: you shall sleep, and there shall be none to make you afraid. I will take away evil beasts: and the sword shall not pass through your quarters.

7.text: You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you.

8.text: Five of yours shall pursue a hundred others, and a hundred of you ten thousand: your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.

9.text: I will look on you, and make you increase: you shall be multiplied, and I will establish my covenant with you.

10.text: You shall eat the oldest of the old store, and, new coming on, you shall cast away the old.

11.text: I will set my tabernacle in the midst of you, and my soul shall not cast you off.

12.text: I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you shall be my people.

13.text: I am the Lord your God: who have brought you out of the land of the Egyptians, that you should not serve them, and who have broken the chains of your necks, that you might go upright.

14.text: But if you will not hear me, nor do all my commandments,

15.text: If you despise my laws, and contemn my judgments so as not to do those things which are appointed by me, and to make void my covenant:

16.text: I also will do these things to you: I will quickly visit you with poverty, and burning heat, which shall waste your eyes, and consume your lives. You shall sow your seed in vain, which shall be devoured by your enemies.

17.text: I will set my face against you, and you shall fall down before your enemies, and shall be made subject to them that hate you, you shall flee when no man pursueth you.

18.text: But if you will not yet for all this obey me: I will chastise you seven times more for your sins,

19.text: And I will break the pride of your stubbornness, and I will make to you the heaven above as iron, and the earth as brass:

20.text: Your labour shall be spent in vain, the ground shall not bring forth her increase, nor the trees yield their fruit.

21.text: If you walk contrary to me, and will not hearken to me, I will bring seven times more plagues upon you for your sins:

22.text: And I will send in upon you the beasts of the field, to destroy you and your cattle, and make you few in number, and that your highways may be desolate.

23.text: And if even so you will not amend, but will walk contrary to me:

24.text: I also will walk contrary to you, and will strike you seven times for your sins.

25.text: And I will bring in upon you the sword that shall avenge my covenant. And when you shall flee into the cities, I will send the pestilence in the midst of you, and you shall be delivered into the hands of your enemies,

26.text: After I shall have broken the staff of your bread: so that ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and give it out by weight: and you shall eat, and shall not be filled.

27.text: But if you will not for all this hearken to me, but will walk against me:

28.text: I will also go against you with opposite fury, and I will chastise you with seven plagues for your sins,

29.text: So that you shall eat the flesh of your sons and of your daughters.

30.text: I will destroy your high places, and break your idols. You shall fall among the ruins of your idols, and my soul shall abhor you.

31.text: Insomuch that I will bring your cities to be a wilderness, and I will make your sanctuaries desolate, and will receive no more your sweet odours.

32.text: And I will destroy your land, and your enemies shall be astonished at it, when they shall be the inhabitants thereof.

33.text: And I will scatter you among the Gentiles, and I will draw out the sword after you, and your land shall be desert, and your cities destroyed.

34.text: Then shall the land enjoy her sabbaths all the days of her desolation: when you shall be

35.text: In the enemy’s land, she shall keep a sabbath, and rest in the sabbaths of her desolation, because she did not rest in your sabbaths when you dwelt therein.

36.text: And as to them that shall remain of you I will send fear in their hearts in the countries of their enemies, the sound of a flying leaf shall terrify them, and they shall flee as it were from the sword: they shall fall, when no man pursueth them,

37.text: And they shall every one fall upon their brethren as fleeing from wars, none of you shall dare to resist your enemies.

38.text: You shall perish among the Gentiles, and an enemy’s land shall consume you.

39.text: And if of them also some remain, they shall pine away in their iniquities, in the land of their enemies, and they shall be afflicted for the sins of their fathers, and their own:

40.text: Until they confess their iniquities and the iniquities of their ancestors, whereby they have transgressed me, and walked contrary unto me.

41.text: Therefore I also will walk against them, and bring them into their enemies’ land until their uncircumcised mind be ashamed: then shall they pray for their sins.

42.text: And I will remember my covenant, that I made with Jacob, and Isaac, and Abraham. I will remember also the land:

43.text: Which when she shall be left by them, shall enjoy her sabbaths, being desolate for them. But they shall pray for their sins, because they rejected my judgments, and despised my laws.

44.text: And yet for all that when they were in the land of their enemies, I did not cast them off altogether, neither did I so despise them that they should be quite consumed, and I should make void my covenant with them. For I am the Lord their God.

45.text: And I will remember my former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, in the sight of the Gentiles, to be their God. I am the Lord. These are the judgments, and precepts, and laws, which the Lord gave between him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.

46.text: And I will remember my former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, in the sight of the Gentiles, to be their God. I am the Lord. These are the judgments, and precepts, and laws, which the Lord gave between him and the children of Israel in mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: The man that shall have made a vow, and promised his soul to God, shall give the price according to estimation.

3.text: If it be a man from twenty years old unto sixty years old, he shall give fifty sicles of silver, after the weight of the sanctuary:

4.text: If a woman, thirty.

5.text: But from the fifth year until the twentieth, a man shall give twenty sicles: a woman ten.

6.text: From one month until the fifth year. for a male shall be given five sicles: for a female three.

7.text: A man that is sixty years old or upward, shall give fifteen sicles: a woman ten.

8.text: If he be poor, and not able to pay the estimation, he shall stand before the priest: and as much as he shall value him at, and see him able to pay, so much shall he give.

9.text: But a beast that may be sacrificed to the Lord, if any one shall vow, shall be holy,

10.text: And cannot be changed, that is to say, neither a better for a worse, nor a worse for a better. And if he shall change it: both that which was changed, and that for which it was changed, shall be consecrated to the Lord.

11.text: An unclean beast, which cannot be sacrificed to the Lord, if any man shall vow, shall be brought before the priest:

12.text: Who judging whether it be good or bad, shall set the price:

13.text: Which if he that offereth it will give, he shall add above the estimation the fifth part.

14.text: If a man shall vow his house, and sanctify it to the Lord, the priest shall consider it, whether it be good or bad, and it shall be sold according to the price, which he shall appoint.

15.text: But if he that vowed, will redeem it, he shall give the fifth part of the estimation over and above, and shall have the house.

16.text: And if he vow the field of his possession, and consecrate it to the Lord, the price shall be rated according to the measure of the seed. If the ground be sowed with thirty bushels of barley, let it be sold for fifty sicles of silver.

17.text: If he vow his field immediately from the year of jubilee that is beginning, as much as it may be worth, at so much it shall be rated.

18.text: But if some time after, the priest shall reckon the money according to the number of years that remain until the jubilee, and the price shall be abated.

19.text: And if he that had vowed, will redeem his field, he shall add the fifth part of the money of the estimation, and shall possess it.

20.text: And if he will not redeem it, but it be sold to any other man, he that vowed it, may not redeem it any more:

21.text: For when the day of jubilee cometh, it shall be sanctified to the Lord, and as a possession consecrated, pertaineth to the right of the priests.
