9.text: Is it a small thing unto you, that the God of Israel hath spared you from all the people, and joined you to himself, that you should serve him in the service of the tabernacle, and should stand before the congregation of the people, and should minister to him?

10.text: Did he therefore make thee and all thy brethren the sons of Levi to approach unto him, that you should challenge to yourselves the priesthood also,

11.text: And that all thy company should stand against the Lord? for what is Aaron that you murmur against him?

12.text: Then Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiron the sons of Eliab. But they answered: We will not come.

13.text: Is it a small matter to thee, that thou hast brought us out of a land that flowed with milk and honey, to kill us in the desert, except thou rule also like a lord over us?

14.text: Thou hast brought us indeed into a land that floweth with rivers of milk and honey, and hast given us possessions of fields and vineyards; wilt thou also pull out our eyes? We will not come.

15.text: Moses therefore being very angry, said to the Lord: Respect not their sacrifices: thou knowest that I have not taken of them so much as a young ass at any time, nor have injured any of them.

16.text: And he said to Core: Do thou and thy congregation stand apart before the Lord tomorrow, and Aaron apart.

17.text: Take every one of you censers, and put incense upon them, offering to the Lord two hundred and fifty censers: let Aaron also hold his censer.

18.text: When they had done this, Moses and Aaron standing,

19.text: And had drawn up all the multitude against them to the door of the tabernacle, the glory of the Lord appeared to them all.

20.text: And the Lord speaking to Moses and Aaron, said:

21.text: Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may presently destroy them.

22.text: They fell flat on their face, and said: O most mighty, the God of the spirits of all flesh, for one man’s sin shall thy wrath rage against all?

23.text: And the Lord said to Moses:

24.text: Command the whole people to separate themselves from the tents of Core and Dathan and Abiron.

25.text: And Moses arose, and went to Dathan and Abiron: and the ancients of Israel following him,

26.text: He said to the multitude: Depart from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest you be involved in their sins.

27.text: And when they were departed from their tents round about, Dathan and Abiron coming out stood in the entry of their pavilions with their wives and children, and all the people.

28.text: And Moses said: By this you shall know that the Lord hath sent me to do all things that you see, and that I have not forged them of my own head:

29.text: If these men die the common death of men, and if they be visited with a plague, wherewith others also are wont to be visited, the Lord did not send me.

30.text: But if the Lord do a new thing, and the earth opening her mouth swallow them down, and all things that belong to them, and they go down alive into hell, you shall know that they have blasphemed the Lord.

31.text: And immediately as he had made an end of speaking, the earth broke asunder under their feet:

32.text: And opening her mouth, devoured them with their tents and all their substance.

33.text: And they went down alive into hell the ground closing upon them, and they perished from among the people.

34.text: But all Israel, that was standing round about, fled at the cry of them that were perishing: saying: Lest perhaps the earth swallow us up also.

35.text: And a fire coming out from the Lord, destroyed the two hundred and fifty men that offered the incense.

36.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

37.text: Command Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers that lie in the burning, and to scatter the fire of one side and the other: because they are sanctified

38.text: In the deaths of the sinners: and let him beat them into plates, and fasten them to the altar, because incense hath been offered in them to the Lord, and they are sanctified, that the children of Israel may see them for a sign and a memorial.

39.text: Then Eleazar the priest took the brazen censers, wherein they had offered, whom the burning fire had devoured, and beat them into plates, fastening them to the altar:

40.text: That the children of Israel might have for the time to come wherewith they should be admonished, that no stranger or any one that is not of seed of Aaron should come near to offer incense to the Lord, lest he should suffer as Core suffered, and all his congregation, according as the Lord spoke to Moses.

41.text: The following day all the multitude of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and Aaron, saying: You have killed the people of the Lord.

42.text: And when there arose a sedition, and the tumult increased,

43.text: Moses and Aaron fled to the tabernacle of the covenant. And when they were gone into it, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.

44.text: And the Lord said to Moses:

45.text: Get you out from the midst of this multitude, this moment will I destroy them. And as they were lying on the ground,

46.text: Moses said to Aaron: Take the censer, and putting fire in it from the altar, put incense upon it, and go quickly to the people to pray for them: for already wrath is gone out from the Lord, and the plague rageth.

47.text: When Aaron had done this, and had run to the midst of the multitude which the burning fire was now destroying, he offered the incense:

48.text: And standing between the dead and the living, he prayed for the people, and the plague ceased.

49.text: And the number of them that were slain was fourteen thousand and seven hundred men, besides them that had perished in the sedition of Core.

50.text: And Aaron returned to Moses to the door of the tabernacle of the covenant after the destruction was over.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Speak to the children of Israel, and take of every one of them a rod by their kindreds, of all the princes of the tribes, twelve rods, and write the name of every man upon his rod.

3.text: And the name of Aaron shall be for the tribe of Levi, and one rod shall contain all their families:

4.text: And thou shalt lay them up in the tabernacle of the covenant before the testimony, where I will speak to thee.

5.text: Whomsoever of these I shall choose, his rod shall blossom: and I will make to cease from me the murmurings of the children of Israel, wherewith they murmur against you.

6.text: And Moses spoke to the children of Israel: and all the princes gave him rods one for every tribe: and there were twelve rods besides the rod of Aaron.

7.text: And when Moses had laid them up before the Lord in the tabernacle of the testimony:

8.text: He returned on the following day, and found that the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi, was budded: and that the buds swelling it had bloomed blossoms, which spreading the leaves, were formed into almonds.

9.text: Moses therefore brought out all the rods from before the Lord to all the children of Israel: and they saw, and every one received their rods.

10.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Carry back the rod of Aaron into the tabernacle of the testimony, that it may be kept there for a token of the rebellious children of Israel, and that their complaints may cease from me lest they die.

11.text: And Moses did as the Lord had commanded.

12.text: And the children of Israel said to Moses: Behold we are consumed, we all perish.

13.text: Whosoever approacheth to the tabernacle of the Lord, he dieth. Are we all to a man to be utterly destroyed?

1.text: And the Lord said to Aaron: Thou, and thy sons, and thy father’s house with thee shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary: and thou and thy sons with thee shall bear the sins of your priesthood.

2.text: And take with thee thy brethren also of the tribe of Levi, and the sceptre of thy father, and let them be ready in hand, and minister to thee: but thou and thy sons shall minister in the tabernacle of the testimony.

3.text: And the Levites shall watch to do thy commands, and about all the works of the tabernacle: only they shall not come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary nor the altar, lest both they die, and you also perish with them.

4.text: But let them be with thee, and watch in the charge of the tabernacle, and in all the ceremonies thereof. A stranger shall not join himself with you.

5.text: Watch ye in the charge of the sanctuary, and in the ministry of the altar: lest indignation rise upon the children of Israel.

6.text: I have given you your brethren the Levites from among the children of Israel, and have delivered them for a gift to the Lord, to serve in the ministries of the tabernacle.

7.text: But thou and thy sons look ye to the priesthood: and all things that pertain to the service of the altar, and that are within the veil, shall be executed by the priests. If any stranger shall approach, he shall be slain.

8.text: And the Lord said to Aaron: Behold I have given thee the charge of my firstfruits. All things that are sanctified by the children of Israel, I have delivered to thee and to thy sons for the priestly office, by everlasting ordinances.

9.text: These therefore shalt thou take of the things that are sanctified, and are offered to the Lord. Every offering, and sacrifice, and whatsoever is rendered to me for sin and for trespass, and becometh holy of holies, shall be for thee and thy sons.

10.text: Thou shalt eat it in the sanctuary: the males only shall eat thereof, because it is a consecrated thing to thee.

11.text: But the firstfruits, which the children of Israel shall vow and offer, I have given to thee, and to thy sons, and to thy daughters, by a perpetual law. He that is clean in thy house, shall eat them.

12.text: All the best of the oil, and of the wine, and of the corn, whatsoever firstfruits they offer to the Lord, I have given them to thee.

13.text: All the firstripe of the fruits, that the ground bringeth forth, and which are brought to the Lord, shall be for thy use: he that is clean in thy house, shall eat them.

14.text: Every thing that the children of Israel shall give by vow, shall be thine.

15.text: Whatsoever is firstborn of all flesh, which they offer to the Lord, whether it be of men, or of beasts, shall belong to thee: only for the firstborn of man thou shalt take a price, and every beast that is unclean thou shalt cause to be redeemed,

16.text: And the redemption of it shall be after one month, for five sicles of silver, by the weight of the sanctuary. A sicle hath twenty obols.

17.text: But the firstling of a cow and of a sheep and of a goat thou shalt not cause to be redeemed, because they are sanctified to the Lord. Their blood only thou shalt pour upon the altar, and their fat thou shalt burn for a most sweet odour to the Lord.

18.text: But the flesh shall fall to thy use, as the consecrated breast, and the right shoulder shall be thine.

19.text: All the firstfruits of the sanctuary which the children of Israel offer to the Lord, I have given to thee and to thy sons and daughters, by a perpetual ordinance. It is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord, to thee and to thy sons.

20.text: And the Lord said to Aaron: You shall possess nothing in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them: I am thy portion and inheritance in the midst of the children of Israel.

21.text: And I have given to the sons of Levi all the tithes of Israel for a possession for the ministry wherewith they serve me in the tabernacle of the covenant:

22.text: That the children of Israel may not approach any more to the tabernacle, nor commit deadly sin,

23.text: But only the sons of Levi may serve me in the tabernacle, and bear the sins of the people. It shall be an everlasting ordinance in your generations. They shall not possess any other thing,

24.text: But be content with the oblation or tithes, which I have separated for their uses and necessities.

25.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

26.text: Command the Levites, and declare unto them: When you shall receive of the children of Israel the tithes, which I have given you, offer the firstfruits of them to the Lord, that is to say, the tenth part of the tenth:

27.text: That it may be reckoned to you as an oblation of firstfruits, as well of the barnfloors as of the winepresses:

28.text: And of all the things of which you receive tithes, offer the firstfruits to the Lord, and give them to Aaron the priest.

29.text: All the things that you shall offer of the tithes, and shall separate for the gifts of the Lord, shall be the best and choicest things.

30.text: And thou shalt say to them: If you offer all the goodly and the better things of the tithes, it shall be reckoned to you as if you had given the firstfruits of the barnfloor and the winepress:

31.text: And you shall eat them in all your places, both you and your families: because it is your reward for the ministry, wherewith you serve in the tabernacle of the testimony.

32.text: And you shall not sin in this point, by reserving the choicest and fat things to yourselves, lest you profane the oblations of the children of Israel, and die.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:

2.text: This is the observance of the victim, which the Lord hath ordained. Command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee a red cow of full age, in which there is no blemish, and which hath not carried the yoke:

3.text: And you shall deliver her to Eleazar the priest, who shall bring her forth without the camp, and shall immolate her in the sight of all:

4.text: And dipping his finger in her blood, shall sprinkle it over against the door of the tabernacle seven times,

5.text: And shall burn her in the sight of all, delivering up to the fire her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, and her dung.

6.text: The priest shall also take cedar wood, and hyssop, and scarlet twice dyed, and cast it into the flame, with which the cow is consumed.

7.text: And then after washing his garments, and body, he shall enter into the camp, and shall be unclean until the evening.

8.text: He also that hath burned her, shall wash his garments, and his body, and shall be unclean until the evening.

9.text: And a man that is clean shall gather up the ashes of the cow, and shall pour them forth without the camp in a most clean place, that they may be reserved for the multitude of the children of Israel, and for a water of aspersion: because the cow was burnt for sin.

10.text: And when he that carried the ashes of the cow, hath washed his garments, he shall be unclean until the evening. The children of Israel, and the strangers that dwell among them, shall observe this for a holy thing by a perpetual ordinance.

11.text: He that toucheth the corpse of a man, and is therefore unclean seven days,

12.text: Shall be sprinkled with this water on the third day, and on the seventh, and so shall be cleansed. If he were not sprinkled on the third day, he cannot be cleansed on the seventh.

13.text: Every one that toucheth the corpse of a man, and is not sprinkled with mixture, shall profane the tabernacle of the Lord, and shall perish out of Israel: because he was not sprinkled with the water of expiation, he shall be unclean, and his uncleanness shall remain upon him.

14.text: This is the law of a man that dieth in a tent: All that go into his tent and all the vessels that are there, shall be unclean seven days.

15.text: The vessel that hath no cover, nor binding over it, shall be unclean.

16.text: If any man in the field touch the corpse of a man that was slain, or that died of himself, or his bone, or his grave, he shall be unclean seven days.

17.text: And they shall take of the ashes of the burning and of the sin offering, and shall pour living waters upon them into a vessel.

18.text: And a man that is clean shall dip hyssop in them, and shall sprinkle therewith all the tent, and all the furniture, and the men that are defiled with touching any such thing:

19.text: And in this manner he that is clean shall purify the unclean on the third and on the seventh day. And being expiated the seventh day, he shall wash both himself and his garments, and be unclean until the evening.

20.text: If any man be not expiated after this rite, his soul shall perish out of the midst of the church: because he hath profaned the sanctuary of the Lord, and was not sprinkled with the water of purification.

21.text: This precept shall be an ordinance for ever. He also that sprinkled the water, shall wash his garments. Every one that shall touch the waters of expiation, shall be unclean until the evening.

22.text: Whatsoever a person toucheth who is unclean, he shall make it unclean: and the person that toucheth any of these things, shall be unclean until the evening.

1.text: And the children of Israel, and all the multitude came into the desert of Sin, in the first month: and the people abode in Cades. And Mary died there, and was buried in the same place.

2.text: And the people wanting water, came together against Moses and Aaron:

3.text: And making a sedition, they said: Would God we had perished among our brethren before the Lord.

4.text: Why have you brought out the church of the Lord into the wilderness, that both we and our cattle should die?

5.text: Why have you made us come up out of Egypt, and have brought us into this wretched place which cannot be sowed, nor bringeth forth figs, nor vines, nor pomegranates, neither is there any water to drink?

6.text: And Moses and Aaron leaving the multitude, went into the tabernacle of the covenant, and fell flat upon the ground, and cried to the Lord, and said: O Lord God, hear the cry of this people, and open to them thy treasure, a fountain of living water, that being satisfied, they may cease to murmur. And the glory of the Lord appeared over them.

7.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

8.text: Take the rod, and assemble the people together, thou and Aaron thy brother, and speak to the rock before them, and it shall yield waters. And when thou hast brought forth water out of the rock, all the multitude and their cattle shall drink.

9.text: Moses therefore took the rod, which was before the Lord, as he had commanded him,

10.text: And having gathered together the multitude before the rock, he said to them: Hear, ye rebellious and incredulous: Can we bring you forth water out of this rock?

11.text: And when Moses had lifted up his hand, and struck the rock twice with the rod, there came forth water in great abundance, so that the people and their cattle drank,

12.text: And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Because you have not believed me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, you shall not bring these people into the land, which I will give them.

13.text: This is the Water of contradiction, where the children of Israel strove with words against the Lord, and he was sanctified in them.

14.text: In the mean time Moses sent messengers from Cades to the king of Edom, to say: Thus saith thy brother Israel: Thou knowest all the labour that hath come upon us:

15.text: In what manner our fathers went down into Egypt, and there we dwelt a long time, and the Egyptians afflicted us and our fathers.

16.text: And how we cried to the Lord, and he heard us, and sent an angel, who hath brought us out of Egypt. Lo, we are now in the city of Cades, which is in the uttermost of thy borders,

17.text: And we beseech thee that we may have leave to pass through thy country. We will not go through the fields, nor through the vineyards, we will not drink the waters of thy wells, but we will go by the common highway, neither turning aside to the right hand, nor to the left, till we are past thy borders.

18.text: And Edom answered them: Thou shalt not pass by me: if thou dost I will come out armed against thee.

19.text: And the children of Israel said: We will go by the beaten way: and if we and our cattle drink of thy waters, we will give thee what is just: there shall be no difficulty in the price, only let us pass speedily.

20.text: But he answered: Thou shalt not pass. And immediately he came forth to meet them with an infinite multitude, and a strong hand,

21.text: Neither would he condescend to their desire to grant them passage through his borders. Wherefore Israel turned another way from him.

22.text: And when they had removed the camp from Cades, they came to mount Hor, which is in the borders of the land of Edom:

23.text: Where the Lord spoke to Moses:

24.text: Let Aaron, saith he, go to his people: for he shall not go into the land which I have given the children of Israel, because he was incredulous to my words, at the waters of contradiction.

25.text: Take Aaron and his son with him, and bring them up into mount Hor:

26.text: And when thou hast stripped the father of his vesture, thou shalt vest therewith Eleazar his son: Aaron shall be gathered to his people, and die there.

27.text: Moses did as the Lord had commanded: and they went up into mount Hor before all the multitude.

28.text: And when he had stripped Aaron of his vestments, he vested Eleazar his son with them. And Aaron being dead in the top of the mountain, he came down with Eleazar.

29.text: And all the multitude seeing that Aaron was dead, mourned for him thirty days throughout all their families.

1.text: And when king Arad the Chanaanite, who dwelt towards the south, had heard this, to wit, that Israel was come by the way of the spies, he fought against them, and overcoming them carried off their spoils.

2.text: But Israel binding himself by vow to the Lord, said: If thou wilt deliver this people into my hand, I will utterly destroy their cities.

3.text: And the Lord heard the prayers of Israel, and delivered up the Chanaanite, and they cut them off and destroyed their cities: and they called the name of that place Horma, that is to say, Anathema.

4.text: And they marched from mount Hor, by the way that leadeth to the Red Sea, to compass the land of Edom. And the people began to be weary of their journey and labour:

5.text: And speaking against God and Moses, they said: Why didst thou bring us out of Egypt, to die in the wilderness? There is no bread, nor have we any waters: our soul now loatheth this very light food.

6.text: Wherefore the Lord sent among the people fiery serpents, which bit them and killed many of them.

7.text: Upon which they came to Moses, and said: We have sinned, because we have spoken against the Lord and thee: pray that he may take away these serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people.

8.text: And the Lord said to him: Make a brazen serpent, and set it up for a sign: whosoever being struck shall look on it, shall live.

9.text: Moses therefore made a brazen serpent, and set it up for a sign: which when they that were bitten looked upon, they were healed.

10.text: And the children of Israel setting forwards camped in Oboth.

11.text: And departing thence they pitched their tents in Jeabarim, in the wilderness, that faceth Moab toward the east.

12.text: And removing from thence, they came to the torrent Zared:

13.text: Which they left and encamped over against Arnon, which is in the desert and standeth out on the borders of the Amorrhite. For Arnon is the border of Moab, dividing the Moabites and the Amorrhites.

14.text: Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the Lord: As he did in the Red Sea, so will he do in the streams of Arnon.

15.text: The rocks of the torrents were bowed down that they might rest in Ar, and lie down in the borders of the Moabites.

16.text: When they went from that place, the well appeared whereof the Lord said to Moses: Gather the people together, and I will give them water.

17.text: Then Israel sung this song: Let the well spring up. They sung thereto:

18.text: The well, which the princes dug, and the chiefs of the people prepared by the direction of the lawgiver, and with their staves. And they marched from the wilderness to Mathana.

19.text: From Mathana unto Nahaliel: from Nahaliel unto Bamoth.

20.text: From Bamoth, is a valley in the country of Moab, to the top of Phasga, which looked towards the desert.

21.text: And Israel sent messengers to Sehon king of the Amorrhites, saying:

22.text: I beseech thee that I may have leave to pass through thy land: we will not go aside into the fields or the vineyards, we will not drink waters of the wells, we will go the king’s highway, till we be past thy borders.

23.text: And he would not grant that Israel should pass by his borders: but rather gathering an army, went forth to meet them in the desert, and came to Jasa, and fought against them.

24.text: And he was slain by them with the edge of the sword, and they possessed his land from the Arnon unto the Jeboc, and to the confines of the children of Ammon: for the borders of the Ammonites, were kept with a strong garrison.

25.text: So Israel took all his cities, and dwelt in the cities of the Amorrhite, to wit, in Hesebon, and in the villages thereof.

26.text: Hesebon was the city of Sehon the king of the Amorrhites, who fought against the king of Moab: and took all the land, that had been of his dominions, as far as the Arnon.

27.text: Therefore it is said in the proverb: Come into Hesebon, let the city of Sehon be built and set up:

28.text: A fire is gone out of Hesebon, a flame from the city of Sehon, and hath consumed Ar of the Moabites, and the inhabitants of the high places of the Arnon.

29.text: Woe to thee Moab: thou art undone, O people of Chamos. He hath given his sons to flight, and his daughters into captivity to Sehon the king of the Amorrhites.

30.text: Their yoke is perished from Hesebon unto Dibon, they came weary to Nophe, and unto Medaba.

31.text: So Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorrhite.

32.text: And Moses sent some to take a view of Jazer: and they took the villages of it, and conquered the inhabitants.

33.text: And they turned themselves, and went up by the way of Basan, and Og the king of Basan came against them with all his people, to fight in Edrai.

34.text: And the Lord said to Moses: Fear him not, for I have delivered him and all his people, and his country into thy hand: and thou shalt do to him as thou didst to Sehon the king of the Amorrhites, the inhabitant of Hesebon.

35.text: So they slew him also with his sons, and all his people, not letting any one escape, and they possessed his land.

1.text: And they went forward and encamped in the plains of Moab, over against where Jericho is situate beyond the Jordan.

2.text: And Balac the son of Sephor, seeing all that Israel had done to the Amorrhite,

3.text: And that the Moabites were in great fear of him, and were not able to sustain his assault,

4.text: He said to the elders of Madian: So will this people destroy all that dwell in our borders, as the ox is wont to eat the grass to the very roots. Now he was at that time king in Moab.

5.text: He sent therefore messengers to Balaam the son of Beor, a soothsayer, who dwelt by the river of the land of the children of Ammon, to call him, and to say: Behold a people is come out of Egypt, that hath covered the face of the earth, sitting over against me.

6.text: Come therefore, and curse this people, because it is mightier than I: if by any means I may beat them and drive them out of my land: for I know that he whom thou shalt bless is blessed, and he whom thou shalt curse is cursed.

7.text: And the ancients of Moab, and the elders of Madian, went with the price of divination in their hands. And when they were come to Balaam, and had told him all the words of Balac:

8.text: He answered: Tarry here this night, and I will answer whatsoever the Lord shall say to me. And while they stayed with Balaam, God came and said to him:

9.text: What mean these men that are with thee?

10.text: He answered: Balac the son of Sephor king of the Moabites hath sent to me,

11.text: Saying: Behold a people that is come out of Egypt, hath covered the face of the land: come and curse them, if by any means I may fight with them and drive them away.

12.text: And God said to Balaam: Thou shalt not go with them, nor shalt thou curse the people: because it is blessed.

13.text: And he rose in the morning and said to the princes: Go into your country, because the Lord hath forbid me to come with you.

14.text: The princes returning, said to Balac: Balaam would not come with us.

15.text: Then he sent many more and more noble than he had sent before:

16.text: Who, when they were come to Balaam, said: Thus saith Balac the son of Sephor, Delay not to come to me:

17.text: For I am ready to honour thee, and will give thee whatsoever thou wilt: come and curse this people.

18.text: Balaam answered: If Balac would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot alter the word of the Lord my God, to speak either more or less.

19.text: I pray you to stay here this night also, that I may know what the Lord will answer me once more.

20.text: God therefore came to Balaam in the night, and said to him: If these men be come to call thee, arise and go with them: yet so, that thou do what I shall command thee.

21.text: Balaam arose in the morning, and saddling his ass went with them.

22.text: And God was angry. And an angel of the Lord stood in the way against Balaam, who sat on the ass, and had two servants with him.

23.text: The ass seeing the angel standing in the way, with a drawn sword, turned herself out of the way, and went into the field. And when Balaam beat her, and had a mind to bring her again to the way,

24.text: The angel stood in a narrow place between two walls, wherewith the vineyards were enclosed.

25.text: And the ass seeing him, thrust herself close to the wall, and bruised the foot of the rider. But he beat her again:

26.text: And nevertheless the angel going on to a narrow place, where there was no way to turn aside either to the right hand or to the left, stood to meet him.

27.text: And when the ass saw the angel standing, she fell under the feet of the rider: who being angry beat her sides more vehemently with a staff.

28.text: And the Lord opened the mouth of the ass, and she said: What have I done to thee? Why strikest thou me, lo, now this third time?

29.text: Balaam answered: Because thou hast deserved it, and hast served me ill: I would I had a sword that I might kill thee.

30.text: The ass said: Am not I thy beast, on which thou hast been always accustomed to ride until this present day? tell me if I ever did the like thing to thee. But he said: Never.

31.text: Forthwith the Lord opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel standing in the way with a drawn sword, and he worshipped him falling flat on the ground.

32.text: And the angel said to him: Why beatest thou thy ass these three times? I am come to withstand thee, because thy way is perverse, and contrary to me:

33.text: And unless the ass had turned out of the way, giving place to me who stood against thee, I had slain thee, and she should have lived.

34.text: Balaam said: I have sinned, not knowing that thou didst stand against me: and now if it displease thee that I go, I will return.

35.text: The angel said: Go with these men, and see thou speak no other thing than what I shall command thee. He went therefore with the princes.

36.text: And when Balac heard it he came forth to meet him in a town of the Moabites, that is situate in the uttermost borders of Arnon.

37.text: And he said to Balaam: I sent messengers to call thee, why didst thou not come immediately to me? was it because I am not able to reward thy coming?

38.text: He answered him: Lo, here I am: shall I have power to speak any other thing but that which God shall put in my mouth?

39.text: So they went on together, and came into a city, that was in the uttermost borders of his kingdom.

40.text: And when Balac had killed oxen and sheep, he sent presents to Balaam, and to the princes that were with him.

41.text: And when morning was come, he brought him to the high places of Baal, and he beheld the uttermost part of the people.

1.text: And Balaam said to Balac: Build me here seven altars, and prepare as many calves, and the same number of rams.

2.text: And when he had done according to the word of Balaam, they laid together a calf and a ram upon every altar.

3.text: And Balaam said to Balac: Stand a while by thy burnt offering, until I go, to see if perhaps the Lord will meet me, and whatsoever he shall command, I will speak to thee.

4.text: And when he was gone with speed, God met him. And Balaam speaking to him, said: I have erected seven altars, and have laid on everyone a calf and a ram.

5.text: And the Lord put the word in his mouth, and said: Return to Balac, and thus shalt thou speak.

6.text: Returning he found Balac standing by his burnt offering, with all the princes of the Moabites:

7.text: And taking up his parable, he said: Balac king of the Moabites hath brought me from Aram, from the mountains of the east: Come, said he, and curse Jacob: make haste and detest Israel.

8.text: How shall I curse him, whom God hath not cursed? By what means should I detest him, whom the Lord detesteth not?

9.text: I shall see him from the tops of the rocks, and shall consider him from the hills. This people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations.

10.text: Who can count the dust of Jacob, and know the number of the stock of Israel? Let my soul die the death of the just, and my last end be like to them.

11.text: And Balac said to Balaam: What is this that thou dost? I sent for thee to curse my enemies: and thou contrariwise blessest them.

12.text: He answered him: Can I speak any thing else but what the Lord commandeth?

13.text: Balac therefore said: Come with me to another place from whence thou mayest see part of Israel, and canst not see them all: curse them from thence.

14.text: And when he had brought him to a high place, upon the top of mount Phasga, Balaam built seven altars, and laying on every one a calf and a ram,

15.text: He said to Balac: Stand here by thy burnt offering while I go to meet him.

16.text: And when the Lord had met him, and had put the word in his mouth, he said: Return to Balac, and thus shalt thou say to him.

17.text: Returning he found him standing by his burnt sacrifice, and the princes of the Moabites with him. And Balac said to him: What hath the Lord spoken?

18.text: But he taking up his parable, said: Stand, O Balac, and give ear: hear, thou son of Sephor:

19.text: God is not a man, that he should lie, nor as the son of man, that he should be changed. Hath he said then, and will he not do? hath he spoken, and will he not fulfill?

20.text: I was brought to bless, the blessing I am not able to hinder.

21.text: There is no idol in Jacob, neither is there an image god to be seen in Israel. The Lord his God is with him, and the sound of the victory of the king in him.

22.text: God hath brought him out of Egypt, whose strength is like to the rhinoceros.

23.text: There is no soothsaying in Jacob, nor divination in Israel. In their times it shall be told to Jacob and to Israel what God hath wrought.

24.text: Behold the people shall rise up as a lioness, and shall lift itself up as a lion: it shall not lie down till it devour the prey, and drink the blood of the slain.

25.text: And Balac said to Balaam: Neither curse, nor bless him.

26.text: And he said: Did I not tell thee, that whatsoever God should command me, that I would do?

27.text: And Balac said to him: Come and I will bring thee to another place; if peradventure it please God that thou mayest curse them from thence.

28.text: And when he had brought him upon the top of mount Phogor, which looketh towards the wilderness,

29.text: Balaam said to him: Build me here seven altars, and prepare as many calves, and the same number of rams.

30.text: Balac did as Balaam had said: and he laid on every altar, a calf and a ram.

1.text: And when Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord that he should bless Israel. he went not as he had gone before, to seek divination: but setting his face towards the desert,

2.text: And lifting up his eyes, he saw Israel abiding in their tents by their tribes: and the spirit of God rushing upon him,

3.text: He took up his parable and said: Balaam the son of Beor hath said: The man hath said, whose eye is stopped up:

4.text: The hearer of the words of God hath said, he that hath beheld the vision of the Almighty, he that falleth, and so his eyes are opened:

5.text: How beautiful are thy tabernacles, O Jacob, and thy tents, O Israel!

6.text: As woody valleys, as watered gardens near the rivers, as tabernacles which the Lord hath pitched, as cedars by the waterside.

7.text: Water shall flow out of his bucket, and his seed shall be in many waters. For Agag his king shall be removed, and his kingdom shall be taken awry.

8.text: God hath brought him out of Egypt, whose strength is like to the rhinoceros. They shall devour the nations that are his enemies, and break their bones, and pierce them with arrows.

9.text: Lying down he hath slept as a lion, and as a lioness, whom none shall dare to rouse. He that blesseth thee, shall also himself be blessed: he that curseth thee shall be reckoned accursed.

10.text: And Balac being angry against Balaam, clapped his hands together and said: I called thee to curse my enemies, and thou on the contrary hast blessed them three times.

11.text: Return to thy place. I had determined indeed greatly to honour thee, but the Lord hath deprived thee of the honour designed for thee.

12.text: Balaam made answer to Balac: Did I not say to thy messengers, whom thou sentest to me:

13.text: If Balac would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of the Lord my God, to utter any thing of my own head either good or evil: but whatsoever the Lord shall say, that I will speak?

14.text: But yet going to my people, I will give thee counsel, what this people shall do to thy people in the latter days.

15.text: Therefore taking up his parable, again he said: Balaam the son of Beor hath said: The man whose eye is stopped up, hath said:

16.text: The hearer of the words of God hath said, who knoweth the doctrine of the Highest, and seeth the visions of the Almighty, who falling hath his eyes opened:

17.text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not near. A STAR SHALL RISE out of Jacob and a sceptre shall spring up from Israel: and shall strike the chiefs of Moab, and shall waste all the children of Seth.

18.text: And he shall possess Idumea: the inheritance of Seir shall come to their enemies, but Israel shall do manfully.

19.text: Out of Jacob shall he come that shall rule, and shall destroy the remains of the city.

20.text: And when he saw Amalec, he took up his parable, and said: Amalec the beginning of nations, whose latter ends shall be destroyed.

21.text: He saw also the Cinite: and took up his parable, and said: Thy habitation indeed is strong: but though thou build thy nest in a rock,

22.text: And thou be chosen of the stock of Cin, how long shalt thou be able to continue? For Assur shall take thee captive.

23.text: And taking up his parable, again he said: Alas, who shall live when God shall do these things?

24.text: They shall come in galleys from Italy, they shall overcome the Assyrians, and shall waste the Hebrews, and at the last they themselves also shall perish.

25.text: And Balaam rose, and returned to his place: Balac also returned the way that he came.

1.text: And Israel at that time abode in Settim, and the people committed fornication with the daughters of Moab,

2.text: Who called them to their sacrifices. And they ate of them, and adored their gods.

3.text: And Israel was initiated to Beelphegor: upon which the Lord being angry,

4.text: Said to Moses: Take all the princes of the people, and hang them up on gibbets against the sun: that my fury may be turned away from Israel.

5.text: And Moses said to the judges of Israel: Let every man kill his neighbours, that have been initiated to Beelphegor.

6.text: And behold one of the children of Israel went in before his brethren to a harlot of Madian, in the sight of Moses, and of all the children of Israel, who were weeping before the door of the tabernacle.

7.text: And when Phinees the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest saw it, he rose up from the midst; of the multitude, and taking a dagger,

8.text: Went in after the Israelite into the brothel house, and thrust both of them through together, to wit, the man and the woman in the genital parts. And the scourge ceased from the children of Israel:

9.text: And there were slain four and twenty thousand men.

10.text: And the Lord said to Moses:

11.text: Phinees the son of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned away my wrath from the children of Israel: because he was moved with my zeal against them, that I myself might not destroy the children of Israel in my zeal.

12.text: Therefore say to him: Behold I give him the peace of my covenant,

13.text: And the covenant of the priesthood for ever shall be both to him and his seed, because he hath been zealous for his God, and hath made atonement for the wickedness of the children of Israel.

14.text: And the name of the Israelite, that was slain with the woman of Madian, was Zambri the son of Salu, a prince of the kindred and tribe of Simeon.

15.text: And the Madianite woman, that was slain with him, was called Cozbi the daughter of Sur, a most noble prince among the Madianites.

16.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

17.text: Let the Madianites find you enemies, and slay you them:

18.text: Because they also have acted like enemies against you, and have guilefully deceived you by the idol Phogor, and Cozbi their sister, a daughter of a prince of Madian, who was slain in the day the plague for the sacrilege of Phogor.

1.text: After the blood of the guilty was shed, the Lord said to Moses and to Eleazar the son of Aaron, the priest:

2.text: Number the whole sum of the children of Israel from twenty years old and upward, by their houses and kindreds, all that are able to go forth to war.

3.text: Moses therefore and Eleazar the priest, being in the plains of Moab upon the Jordan over against Jericho, spoke to them that were

4.text: From twenty years old and upward, as the Lord had commanded: and this is the number of them:

5.text: Ruben the firstborn of Israel. His sons were Henoch, of whom is the family of the Henochites: and Phallu, of whom is the family of the Phalluites:

6.text: And Hesron, of whom is the family of the Hesronites: and Charmi, of whom is the family of the Charmites.

7.text: These are the families of the stock of Ruben: whose number was found to be forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.

8.text: The son of Phallu was Eliab.

9.text: His sons, were Namuel and Dathan and Abiron. These are Dathan and Abiron the princes of the people, that rose against Moses and Aaron in the sedition of Core, when they rebelled against the Lord:

10.text: And the earth opening her mouth swallowed up Core, many others dying, when the fire burned two hundred and fifty men. And there was a great miracle wrought,

11.text: That when Core perished, his sons did not perish.

12.text: The sons of Simeon by their kindreds: Namuel, of him is the family of the Namuelites: Jamin, of him is the family of the Jaminites: Jachin, of him is the family of the Jachinites:

13.text: Zare, of him is the family of the Zarites: Saul, of him is the family of the Saulites.

14.text: These are the families of the stock of Simeon, of which the whole number was twenty-two thousand two hundred.

15.text: The sons of Gad by their kindreds: Sephon, of him Is the family of the Sephonites: Aggi, of him is the family of the Aggites: Suni, of him is the family of the Sunites:

16.text: Ozni, of him is the family of the Oznites: Her, of him is the family of the Herites:

17.text: Arod, of him is the family of the Arodites: Ariel, of him is the family of the Arielites.

18.text: These are the families of Gad, of which the whole number was forty thousand five hundred.

19.text: The sons of Juda, Her and Onan, who both died in the land of Chanaan.

20.text: And the sons of Juda by their kindreds were: Sela, of whom is the family of the Selaites: Phares, of whom is the family of the Pharesites: Zare, of whom is the family of the Zarites.

21.text: Moreover the sons of Phares were: Hesron, of whom is the family of the Hesronites: and Hamul, of whom is the family of the Hamulites.

22.text: These are the families of Juda, of which the whole number was seventy-six thousand five hundred.

23.text: The sons of Issachar, by their kindreds: Thola, of whom is the family of the Tholaites: Phua, of whom is the family of the Phuaites:

24.text: Jasub, of whom is the family of the Jasubites: Semran, of whom is the family of the Semranites.

25.text: These are the kindreds of Issachar, whose number was sixty-four thousand three hundred.

26.text: The sons of Zabulon by their kindreds: Sared, of whom is the family of the Saredites: Elon, of whom is the family of the Elonites: Jalel, of whom is the family of the Jalelites.

27.text: These are the kindreds of Zabulon, whose number was sixty thousand five hundred.

28.text: The sons of Joseph by their kindred, Manasses and Ephraim.

29.text: Of Manasses was born Machir, of whom is the family of the Machirites. Machir begot Galaad, of whom is the family of the Galaadites.

30.text: Galaad had sons: Jezer, of whom is the family of the Jezerites: and Helec, of whom is the family of the Helecites:

31.text: And Asriel, of whom is the family of the Asrielites: and Sechem, of whom is the family of the Sechemites:

32.text: And Semida, of whom is the family of the Semidaites: and Hepher, of whom is the family of the Hepherites.

33.text: And Hepher was the father of Salphaad, who had no sons, but only daughters, whose names are these: Maala, and Noa, and Hegla, and Melcha, and Thersa.

34.text: These are the families of Manasses, and the number of them fifty-two thousand seven hundred.

35.text: And the sons of Ephraim by their kindreds were these: Suthala, of whom is the family of the Suthalaites: Becher, of whom is the family of the Becherites: Thehen, of whom is the family of the Thehenites.

36.text: Now the son of Suthala was Heran, of whom is the family of the Heranites.

37.text: These are the kindreds of the sons of Ephraim: whose number was thirty-two thousand five hundred.

38.text: These are the sons of Joseph by their families. The sons of Benjamin in their kindreds: Bela, of whom is the family of the Belaites: Asbel, of whom is the family of the Asbelites: Ahiram, of whom is the family of the Ahiramites:

39.text: Supham, of whom is the family of the Suphamites: Hupham, of whom is the family of the Huphamites.

40.text: The sons of Bela: Hered, and Noeman. Of Hered, is the family of the Heredites: of Noeman, the family of the Noemanites.

41.text: These are the sons of Benjamin by their kindreds, whose number was forty-five thousand six hundred.

42.text: The sons of Dan by their kindreds: Suham, of whom is the family of the Suhamites: These are the kindreds of Dan by their families.

43.text: All were Suhamites, whose number was sixty-four thousand four hundred.

44.text: The sons of Aser by their kindreds: Jemna, of whom is the family of the Jemnaites: Jessui, of whom is the family of the Jessuites: Brie, of whom is the family of the Brieites.

45.text: The sons of Brie: Heber, of whom is the family of the Heberites: and Melchiel, of whom is the family of the Melchielites.

46.text: And the name of the daughter of Aser, was Sara.

47.text: These are the kindreds of the sons of Aser, and their number fifty-three thousand four hundred.

48.text: The sons of Nephtali by their kindreds: Jesiel, of whom is the family of the Jesielites: Guni, of whom is the family of the Gunites:

49.text: Jeser, of whom is the family of the Jeserites: Sellem, of whom is the family of the Sellemites.

50.text: These are the kindreds of the sons of Nephtali by their families: whose number was forty-five thousand four hundred.

51.text: This is the sum of the children of Israel, that were reckoned up, six hundred and one thousand seven hundred and thirty.

52.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

53.text: To these shall the land be divided for their possessions according to the number of names.

54.text: To the greater number thou shalt give a greater portion, and to the fewer a less: to every one, as they have now been reckoned up, shall a possession be delivered:

55.text: Yet so that by lot the land be divided to the tribe and families.

56.text: Whatsoever shall fall by lot, that shall be taken by the more, or the fewer.

57.text: This also is the number of the sons of Levi by their families: Gerson, of whom is the family of the Gersonites: Caath, of whom is the family of the Caathites: Merari, of whom is the family of the Merarites.

58.text: These are the families of Levi: The family of Lobni, the family of Hebroni, the family of Moholi, the family of Musi, the family of Core. Now Caath beget Amram:

59.text: Who had to wife Jochabed the daughter of Levi, who was born to him in Egypt. She bore to her husband Amram sons, Aaron and Moses, and Mary their sister.

60.text: Of Aaron were born Nadab and Abiu, and Eleazar and Ithamar:

61.text: Of whom Nadab and Abiu died, when they had offered the strange fire before the Lord.

62.text: And all that were numbered, were twenty-three thousand males from one month old and upward: for they were not reckoned up among the children of Israel, neither was a possession given to them with the rest.

63.text: This is the number of the children of Israel, that were enrolled by Moses and Eleazar the priest, in the plains of Moab upon the Jordan, over against Jericho.

64.text: Among whom there was not one of them that were numbered before by Moses and Aaron in the desert of Sinai.

65.text: For the Lord had foretold that they should die in the wilderness. And none remained of them, but Caleb the son of Jephone, and Josue the son of Nun.

1.text: Then came the daughters of Salphaad, the son of Hepher, the son of Galaad, the son of Machir, the son of Manasses, who was the son of Joseph: and their names are Maala, and Noa, and Hegla, and Melcha, and Thersa.

2.text: And they stood before Moses and Eleazar the priest, and all the princes of the people at the door of the tabernacle of the covenant, and said:

4.text: Our father died in the desert, and was not in the sedition, that was raised against the Lord under Core, but he died in his own sin: and he had no male children. Why is his name taken away out of his family, because he had no son? Give us a possession among the kinsmen of our father.

5.text: And Moses referred their cause to the judgment of the Lord.

6.text: And the Lord said to him:

7.text: The daughters of Salphaad demand a just thing: Give them a possession among their father’s kindred, and let them succeed him in his inheritance.

8.text: And to the children of Israel thou shalt speak these things: When a man dieth without a son, his inheritance shall pass to his daughter.

9.text: If he have no daughter, his brethren shall succeed him.

10.text: And if he have no brethren, you shall give the inheritance to his father’s brethren.

11.text: But if he have no uncles by the father, the inheritance shall be given to them that are the next akin. And this shall be to the children of Israel sacred by a perpetual law, as the Lord hath commanded Moses.

12.text: The Lord also said to Moses: Go up into this mountain Abarim, and view from thence the land which I will give to the children of Israel.

13.text: And when thou shalt have seen it, thou also shalt go to thy people, as thy brother Aaron is gone:

14.text: Because you offended me in the desert of Sin in the contradiction of the multitude, neither would you sanctify me before them at the waters. These are the waters of contradiction in Cades of the desert of Sin.

15.text: And Moses answered him:

16.text: May the Lord the God of the spirits of all flesh provide a man, that may be over this multitude:

17.text: And may go out and in before them, and may lead them out, or bring them in: lest the people of the Lord be as sheep without a shepherd.

18.text: And the Lord said to him: Take Josue the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and put thy hand upon him.

19.text: And he shall stand before Eleazar the priest and all the multitude:

20.text: And thou shalt give him precepts in the sight of all, and part of thy glory, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may hear him.

21.text: If any thing be to be done, Eleazar the priest shall consult the Lord for him. He and all the children of Israel with him, and the rest of the multitude shall go out and go in at his word.

22.text: Moses did as the Lord had commanded. And when he had taken Josue, he set him before Eleazar the priest, and all the assembly of the people,

23.text: And laying his hands on his head, he repeated all things that the Lord had commanded.

1.text: The Lord also said to Moses:

2.text: Command the children of Israel, and thou shalt say to them: Offer ye my oblation and my bread, and burnt sacrifice of most sweet odour, in their due seasons.

3.text: These are the sacrifices which you shall offer: Two lambs of a year old without blemish every day for the perpetual holocaust:

4.text: One you shall offer in the morning, and the other in the evening:

5.text: And the tenth part of an ephi of flour, which shall be tempered with the purest oil, of the measure of the fourth part of a hin.

6.text: It is the continual holocaust which you offered in mount Sinai for a most sweet odour of a sacrifice by fire to the Lord.

7.text: And for a libation you shall offer of wine the fourth part of a hin for every lamb in the sanctuary of the Lord.

8.text: And you shall offer the other lamb in like manner in the evening according to all the rites of the morning sacrifice, and of the libations thereof, an oblation of most sweet odour to the Lord.

9.text: And on the sabbath day you shall offer two lambs of a year old without blemish, and two tenths of flour tempered with oil in sacrifice, and the libations,

10.text: Which regularly are poured out every sabbath for the perpetual holocaust.

11.text: And on the first day of the month you shall offer a holocaust to the Lord, two calves of the herd, one ram, and seven lambs of a year old, without blemish,

12.text: And three tenths of flour tempered with oil in sacrifice for every calf: and two tenths of flour tempered with oil for every ram:

13.text: And the tenth of a tenth of flour tempered with oil in sacrifice for every lamb. It is a holocaust of most sweet odour and an offering by fire to the Lord.

14.text: And these shall be the libations of wine that are to be poured out for every victim: Half a hin for every calf, a third for a ram, and a fourth for a lamb. This shall be the holocaust for every month, as they succeed one another in the course of the year.

15.text: A buck goat also shall be offered to the Lord for a sin offering over and above the perpetual holocaust with its libations.

16.text: And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, shall be the phase of the Lord,

17.text: And on the fifteenth day the solemn feast: seven days shall they eat unleavened bread.

18.text: And the first day of them shall be venerable and holy: you shall not do any servile work therein.

19.text: And you shall offer a burnt sacrifice a holocaust to the Lord, two calves of the herd, one ram, seven lambs of a year old, without blemish:

20.text: And for the sacrifices of every one three tenths of flour which shall be tempered with oil to every calf, and two tenths to every ram,

21.text: And the tenth of a tenth, to every lamb, that is to say, to all the seven lambs:

22.text: And one buck goat for sin, to make atonement for you,

23.text: Besides the morning holocaust which you shall always offer.

24.text: So shall you do every day of the seven days for the food of the fire, and for a most sweet odour to the Lord, which shall rise from the holocaust, and from the libations of each.

25.text: The seventh day also shall be most solemn and holy unto you: you shall do no servile work therein.

26.text: The day also of firstfruits, when after the weeks are accomplished, you shall offer new fruits to the Lord, shall be venerable and holy: you shall do no servile work therein.

27.text: And you shall offer a holocaust for a most sweet odour to the Lord, two calves of the herd, one ram, and seven lambs of a year old, without blemish:

28.text: And in the sacrifices of them three tenths of flour tempered with oil to every calf, two to every ram,

29.text: The tenth of a tenth to every lamb, which in all are seven lambs: a buck goat also,

30.text: Which is slain for expiation: besides the perpetual holocaust and the libations thereof.

31.text: You shall offer them all without blemish with their libations.

1.text: The first day also of the seventh month shall be venerable and holy unto you; you shall do no servile work therein, because it is the day of the sounding and of trumpets.

2.text: And you shall offer a holocaust for a most sweet odour to the Lord, one calf of the herd, one ram and seven lambs of a year old, without blemish.

3.text: And for their sacrifices, three tenths of flour tempered with oil to every calf, two tenths to a ram,

4.text: One tenth to a lamb, which in all are seven lambs:

5.text: And a buck goat for sin, which is offered for the expiation of the people,

6.text: Besides the holocaust of the first day of the month with the sacrifices thereof, and the perpetual holocaust with the accustomed libations. With the same ceremonies you shall offer a burnt sacrifice for a most sweet odour to the Lord.

7.text: The tenth day also of this seventh month shall be holy and venerable unto you, and you shall afflict your souls: you shall do no servile work therein.

8.text: And you shall offer a holocaust to the Lord for a most sweet odour, one calf of the herd, one ram, and seven lambs of a year old, without blemish:

9.text: And for their sacrifices, three tenths of flour tempered with oil to every calf, two tenths to a ram,

10.text: The tenth of a tenth to every lamb, which are in all seven lambs:

11.text: And a buck goat for sin, besides the things that are wont to be offered for sin, for expiation, and for the perpetual holocaust with their sacrifice and libations.

12.text: And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, which shall be unto you holy and venerable, you shall do no servile work, but shall celebrate a solemnity to the Lord seven days.

13.text: And you shall offer a holocaust for a most sweet odour to the Lord, thirteen calves of the herd, two rams, and fourteen lambs of a year old, without blemish:

14.text: And for their libations three tenths of flour tempered with oil to every calf, being in all thirteen calves: and two tenths to each ram, being two rams,

15.text: And the tenth of a tenth to every lamb, being in all fourteen lambs:

16.text: And a buck goat for sin, besides the perpetual holocaust, and the sacrifice and the libation thereof.

17.text: On the second day you shall offer twelve calves of the herd, two rams and fourteen lambs of a year old, without blemish:

18.text: And the sacrifices and the libations for every one, for the calves and for the rams and for the lambs you shall duly celebrate:

19.text: And a buck goat for a sin offering besides the perpetual holocaust, and the sacrifice and the libation thereof.

20.text: The third day you shall offer eleven calves, two rams, and fourteen lambs of a year old, without blemish:

21.text: And the sacrifices and the libations of every one for the calves and for the rams and for the lambs you shall offer according to the rite:

22.text: And a buck goat for sin, besides the perpetual holocaust, and the sacrifice, and the libation thereof.

23.text: The fourth day you shall offer ten calves, two rams, and fourteen lambs of a year old, without blemish:

24.text: And the sacrifices and the libations of every one for the calves and for the rams and for the lambs you shall celebrate in right manner:

25.text: And a buck goat for sin, besides the perpetual holocaust, and the sacrifice and the libation thereof.

26.text: The fifth day you shall offer nine calves, two rams, and fourteen lambs of a year old, without blemish:

27.text: And the sacrifices and the libations of every one for the calves and for the rams and for the lambs you shall celebrate according to the rite:

28.text: And a buck goat for sin, besides the perpetual holocaust, and the sacrifice and the libation thereof.

29.text: The sixth day you shall offer eight calves, two rams, and fourteen lambs of a year old, without blemish:

30.text: And the sacrifices and the libations of every one for the calves and for the rams and for the lambs you shall celebrate according to the rite:

31.text: And a buck goat for sin, besides the perpetual holocaust, and the sacrifice and the libation thereof.

32.text: The seventh day you shall offer seven calves and two rams, and fourteen lambs of a year old, without blemish:

33.text: And the sacrifices and the libations of every one for the calves and for the rams and for the lambs you shall celebrate according to the rite:

34.text: And a buck goat for sin, besides the perpetual holocaust, and the sacrifice and the libation thereof.

35.text: On the eighth day, which is most solemn, you shall do no servile work:

36.text: But you shall offer a holocaust for a most sweet odour to the Lord, one calf, one ram, and seven lambs of a year old, without blemish:

37.text: And the sacrifices and the libations of every one for the calves and for the rams and for the lambs you shall celebrate according to the rite:

38.text: And a buck goat for sin, besides the perpetual holocaust, and the sacrifice and the libation thereof.

39.text: These things shall you offer to the Lord in your solemnities: besides your vows and voluntary oblations for holocaust, for sacrifice, for libation, and for victims of peace offerings.

40.text: And Moses told the children of Israel all that the Lord had commanded him:

1.text: And he said to the princes of the tribes of the children of Israel: This is the word that the Lord hath commanded:

2.text: If any man make a vow to the Lord, or bind himself by an oath: he shall not make his word void but shall fulfill all that he promised.

3.text: If a woman vow any thing, and bind herself by an oath, being in her father’s house, and but yet a girl in age: if her father knew the vow that she hath promised, and the oath wherewith she hath bound her soul, and held his peace, she shall be bound by the vow:

4.text: Whatsoever she promised and swore, she shall fulfill in deed.

5.text: But if her father, immediately as soon as he heard it, gainsaid it, both her vows and her oaths shall be void, neither shall she be bound to what she promised, because her father hath gainsaid it.

6.text: If she have a husband, and shall vow any thing, and the word once going out of her mouth shall bind her soul by an oath:

7.text: The day that her husband shall hear it, and not gainsay it, she shall be bound to the vow, and shall give whatsoever she promised.

8.text: But if as soon as he heareth he gainsay it, and make her promises and the words wherewith she had bound her soul of no effect: the Lord will forgive her.

9.text: The widow, and she that is divorced, shall fulfill whatsoever they vow.

10.text: If the wife in the house of her husband, hath bound herself by vow and by oath,

11.text: If her husband hear, and hold his peace, and doth not disallow the promise, she shall accomplish whatsoever she had promised.

12.text: But if forthwith he gainsay it, she shall not be bound by the promise: because her husband gainsaid it, and the Lord will be merciful to her.

13.text: If she vow and bind herself by oath, to afflict her soul by fasting, or abstinence from other things, it shall depend on the will of her husband, whether she shall do it, or not do it.

14.text: But if the husband hearing it hold his peace, and defer the declaring his mind till another day: whatsoever she had vowed and promised, she shall fulfill: because immediately as he heard it, he held his peace.

15.text: But if he gainsay it after that he knew it, he shall bear her iniquity.

16.text: These are the laws which the Lord appointed to Moses between the husband and the wife, between the father and the daughter that is as yet but a girl in age, or that abideth in her father’s house.

1.text: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:

2.text: Revenge first the children of Israel on the Madianites, and so thou shalt be gathered to thy people.

3.text: And Moses forthwith said: Arm of you men to fight, who may take the revenge of the Lord on the Madianites.

4.text: Let a thousand men be chosen out of every tribe of Israel to be sent to the war.

5.text: And they gave a thousand of every tribe, that is to say, twelve thousand men well appointed for battle.

6.text: And Moses sent them with Phinees the son of Eleazar the priest, and he delivered to him the holy vessels, and the trumpets to sound.

7.text: And when they had fought against the Madianites and had overcome them, they slew all the men.

8.text: And their kings Evi, and Recem, and Sur, and Hur, and Rebe, five princes of the nation: Balaam also the son of Beer they killed with the sword.

9.text: And they took their women, and their children captives, and all their cattle, and all their goods: and all their possessions they plundered:

10.text: And all their cities, and their villages, and castles, they burned.

11.text: And they carried away the booty, and all that they had taken both of men and of beasts.

12.text: And they brought them to Moses, and Eleazar the priest, and to all the multitude of the children of Israel. But the rest of the things for use they carried to the camp on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan over against Jericho.

13.text: And Moses and Eleazar the priest and all the princes of the synagogue went forth to meet them without the camp.

14.text: And Moses being angry with the chief officers of the army, the tribunes, and the centurions that were come from the battle,

15.text: Said: Why have you saved the women?

16.text: Are not these they, that deceived the children of Israel by the counsel of Balaam, and made you transgress against the Lord by the sin of Phogor, for which also the people was punished?

17.text: Therefore kill all that are of the male sex, even of the children: and put to death the women, that have carnally known men.

18.text: But the girls, and all the women that are virgins save for yourselves:

19.text: And stay without the camp seven days. He that hath killed a man, or touched one that is killed, shall be purified the third day and the seventh day.

20.text: And of all the spoil, every garment, or vessel, or any thing made for use, of the skins, or hair of goats, or of wood, shall be purified.

21.text: Eleazar also the priest spoke to the men of the army, that had fought, in this manner: This is the ordinance of the law, which the Lord hath commanded Moses:

22.text: Gold, and silver, and brass, and iron, and lead, and tin,

23.text: And all that may pass through the fire, shall be purified by fire, but whatsoever cannot abide the fire, shall be sanctified with the water of expiation:

24.text: And you shall wash your garments the seventh day, and being purified, you shall afterwards enter into the camp.

25.text: And the Lord said to Moses:

26.text: Take the sum of the things that were taken both of man and beast, thou and Eleazar the priest and the princes of the multitude:

27.text: And thou shalt divide the spoil equally, between them that fought and went out to the war, and between the rest of the multitude.

28.text: And thou shalt separate a portion to the Lord from them that fought and were in the battle, one soul of five hundred as well of persons as of oxen and asses and sheep.

29.text: And thou shalt give it to Eleazar the priest, because they are the firstfruits of the Lord.

30.text: Out of the moiety also of the children of Israel thou shalt take the fiftieth head of persons, and of oxen, and asses, and sheep, and of all beasts, and thou shalt give them to the Levites that watch in the charge of the tabernacle of the Lord.

31.text: And Moses and Eleazar did as the Lord had commanded.

32.text: And the spoil which the army had taken, was six hundred seventy-five thousand sheep,

33.text: Seventy-two thousand oxen,

34.text: Sixty-one thousand asses:

35.text: And thirty-two thousand persons of the female sex, that had not known men.

36.text: And one half was given to them that had been in the battle, to wit, three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep:

37.text: Out of which, for the portion of the Lord, were reckoned six hundred seventy-five sheep.

38.text: And out of the thirty-six thousand oxen, seventy-two oxen:

39.text: Out of the thirty thousand five hundred asses, sixty-one asses:

40.text: Out of the sixteen thousand persons, there fell to the portion of the Lord, thirty-two souls.

41.text: And Moses delivered the number of the firstfruits of the Lord to Eleazar the priest, as had been commanded him,

42.text: Out of the half of the children of Israel, which he had separated for them that had been in the battle.

43.text: But out of the half that fell to the rest of the multitude, that is to say, out of the three hundred thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,

44.text: And out of the thirty-six thousand oxen,

45.text: And out of the thirty thousand five hundred asses,

46.text: And out of the sixteen thousand persons,

47.text: Moses took the fiftieth head, and gave it to the Levites that watched in the tabernacle of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded.

48.text: And when the commanders of the army, and the tribunes and centurions were come to Moses, they said:

49.text: We thy servants have reckoned up the number of the fighting men, whom we had under our hand, and not so much as one was wanting.

50.text: Therefore we offer as gifts to the Lord what gold every one of us could find in the booty, in garters and tablets, rings and bracelets, and chains, that thou mayst pray to the Lord for us.

51.text: And Moses and Eleazar the priest received all the gold in divers kinds,

52.text: In weight sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty sicles, from the tribunes and from the centurions.

53.text: For that which every one had taken in the booty was his own.

54.text: And that which was received they brought into the tabernacle of the testimony, for a memorial of the children of Israel before the Lord.

1.text: And the sons of Ruben and Gad had many flocks of cattle, and their substance in beasts was infinite. And when they saw the lands of Jazer and Galaad fit for feeding cattle,

2.text: They came to Moses and Eleazar the priest, and the princes of the multitude, and said:

3.text: Ataroth, and Dibon, and Jazer, and Nemra, Hesebon, and Eleale, and Saban, and Nebo, and Beon,

4.text: The land, which the Lord hath conquered in the sight of the children of Israel, is a very fertile soil for the feeding of beasts: and we thy servants have very much cattle:

5.text: And we pray thee, if we have found favour in thy sight, that thou give it to us thy servants in possession, and make us not pass over the Jordan.

6.text: And Moses answered them: What, shall your brethren go to fight, and will you sit here?

7.text: Why do ye overturn the minds of the children of Israel, that they may not dare to pass into the place which the Lord hath given them?

8.text: Was it not thus your fathers did, when I sent from Cadesbarne to view the land?

9.text: And when they were come as far as the valley of the cluster, having viewed all the country, they overturned the hearts of the children of Israel, that they should not enter into the coasts, which the Lord gave them.

10.text: And he swore in his anger, saying:

11.text: If these men, that came up out of Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, shall see the land, which I promised with an oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: because they would not follow me,

12.text: Except Caleb the son of Jephone the Cenezite, and Josue the son of Nun: these have fulfilled my will.

13.text: And the Lord being angry against Israel, led them about through the desert forty years, until the whole generation, that had done evil in his sight, was consumed.

14.text: And behold, said he, you are risen up instead of your fathers, the increase and offspring of sinful men, to augment the fury of the Lord against Israel.

15.text: For if you will not follow him, he will leave the people in the wilderness, and you shall be the cause of the destruction of all.

16.text: But they coming near, said: We will make sheepfolds, and stalls for our cattle, and strong cities for our children:

17.text: And we ourselves will go armed and ready for battle before the children of Israel, until we bring them in unto their places. Our little ones, and all we have, shall be in walled cities, for fear of the ambushes of the inhabitants.

18.text: We will not return into our houses until the children of Israel possess their inheritance:

19.text: Neither will we seek any thing beyond the Jordan, because we have already our possession on the east side thereof,

20.text: And Moses said to them: If you do what you promise, go on well appointed for war before the Lord:

21.text: And let every fighting man pass over the Jordan, until the Lord overthrow his enemies:

22.text: And all the land be brought under him, then shall you be blameless before the Lord and before Israel, and you shall obtain the countries that you desire, before the Lord.

23.text: But if you do not what you say, no man can doubt but you sin against God: and know ye, that your sin shall overtake you.

24.text: Build therefore cities for your children, and folds and stalls for your sheep and beasts, and accomplish what you have promised.

25.text: And the children of Gad and Ruben said to Moses: We are thy servants, we will do what my lord commandeth.

26.text: We will leave our children, and our wives and sheep and cattle, in the cities of Galaad:

27.text: And we thy servants all well appointed will march on to the war, as thou, my lord, speakest.

28.text: Moses therefore commanded Eleazar the priest, and Josue the son of Nun, and the princes of the families of all the tribes of Israel, and said to them:

29.text: If the children of Gad, and the children of Ruben pass with you over the Jordan, all armed for war before the Lord, and the land be made subject to you: give them Galaad in possession.

30.text: But if they will not pass armed with you into the land of Chanaan, let them receive places to dwell in among you.

31.text: And the children of Gad, and the children of Ruben answered: As the Lord hath spoken to his servants, so will we do:

32.text: We will go armed before the Lord into the land of Chanaan, and we confess that we have already received our possession beyond the Jordan.

33.text: Moses therefore gave to the children of Gad and of Ruben, and to the half tribe of Manasses the son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sehon king of the Amorrhites, and the kingdom of Og king of Basan, and their land and the cities thereof round about.

34.text: And the sons of Gad built Dibon, and Ataroth, and Aroer,

35.text: And Etroth, and Sophan, and Jazer, and Jegbaa,

36.text: And Bethnemra, and Betharan, fenced cities, and folds for their cattle.

37.text: But the children of Ruben built Hesebon, and Eleale, and Cariathaim,

38.text: And Nabo, and Baalmeon (their names being changed) and Sabama: giving names to the cities which they had built.

39.text: Moreover the children of Machir, the son of Manasses, went into Galaad, and wasted it, cutting off the Amorrhites, the inhabitants thereof.

40.text: And Moses gave the land of Galaad to Machir the son of Manasses, and he dwelt in it.

41.text: And Jair the son of Manasses went, and took the villages thereof, and he called them Havoth Jair, that is to say, the villages of Jair.

42.text: Nobe also went, and took Canath with the villages thereof: and he called it by his own name, Nobe.

1.text: These are the mansions of the children of Israel, who went out of Egypt by their troops under the conduct of Moses and Aaron,

2.text: Which Moses wrote down according to the places of their encamping, which they changed by the commandment of the Lord.

3.text: Now the children of Israel departed from Ramesses the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after the phase, with a mighty hand, in the sight of all the Egyptians,

4.text: Who were burying their firstborn, whom the Lord had slain (upon their gods also he had executed vengeance,)

5.text: And they camped in Soccoth.

6.text: And from Soccoth they came into Etham, which is in the uttermost borders of the wilderness.

7.text: Departing from thence they came over against Phihahiroth, which looketh towards Beelsephon, and they camped before Magdalum.

8.text: And departing from Phihahiroth, they passed through the midst of the sea into the wilderness: and having marched three days through the desert of Etham, they camped in Mara.

9.text: And departing from Mara, they came into Elim, where there were twelve fountains of waters, and seventy palm trees: and there they camped.

10.text: But departing from thence also, they pitched their tents by the Red Sea. And departing from the Red Sea,

11.text: They camped in the desert of Sin.

12.text: And they removed from thence, and came to Daphca.

13.text: And departing from Daphca, they camped in Alus.

14.text: And departing from Alus, they pitched their tents in Raphidim, where the people wanted water to drink.

15.text: And departing from Raphidim, they camped in the desert of Sinai.

16.text: But departing also from the desert of Sinai, they came to the graves of lust.

17.text: And departing from the graves of lust, they camped in Haseroth.

18.text: And from Haseroth they came to Rethma.

19.text: And departing from Rethma, they camped in Remmomphares.

20.text: And they departed from thence and came to Lebna.

21.text: Removing from Lebna they camped in Ressa.

22.text: And departing from Ressa, they came to Ceelatha.

23.text: And they removed from thence and camped in the mountain Sepher.

24.text: Departing from the mountain Sepher, they came to Arada.

25.text: From thence they went and camped in Maceloth.

26.text: And departing from Maceloth, they came to Thahath.

27.text: Removing from Thahath they camped in Thare.

28.text: And they departed from thence, and pitched their tents in Methca.

29.text: And removing from Methca, they camped in Hesmona.

30.text: And departing from Hesmona, they came to Moseroth.

31.text: And removing from Moseroth, they camped in Benejaacan.

32.text: And departing from Benejaacan, they came to mount Gadgad.

33.text: From thence they went and camped in Jetebatha.

34.text: And from Jetebatha they came to Hebrona.

35.text: And departing from Hebrona, they camped in Asiongaber.

36.text: They removed from thence and came into the desert of Sin, which is Cades.
