5.text: The servants answered: Aman standeth in the court, and the king said: Let him come in.

6.text: And when he was come in, he said to him: What ought to be done to the man whom the king is desirous to honour? But Aman thinking in his heart, and supposing that the king would honour no other but himself,

7.text: Answered: The man whom the king desireth to honour,

8.text: Ought to be clothed with the king’s apparel, and to be set upon the horse that the king rideth upon, and to have the royal crown upon his head,

9.text: And let the first of the king’s princes and nobles hold his horse, and going through the street of the city, proclaim before him and say: Thus shall he be honoured, whom the king hath a mind to honour.

10.text: And the king said to him: Make haste and take the robe and the horse, and do as thou hast spoken to Mardochai the Jew, who sitteth before the gates of the palace. Beware thou pass over any of those things which thou hast spoken.

11.text: So Aman took the robe and the horse, and arraying Mardochai in the street of the city, and setting him on the horse, went before him, and proclaimed: This honour is he worthy of, whom the king hath a mind to honour.

12.text: But Mardochai returned to the palace gate: and Aman made haste to go to his house, mourning and having his head covered:

13.text: And he told Zares his wife, and his friends, all that had befallen him. And the wise men whom he had in counsel, and his wife answered him: If Mardochai be of the seed of the Jews, before whom thou hast begun to fall, thou canst not resist him, but thou shalt fall in his sight.

14.text: As they were yet speaking, the king’s eunuchs came, and compelled him to go quickly to the banquet which the queen had prepared.

1.text: So the king and Aman went in, to drink with the queen.

2.text: And the king said to her again the second day, after he was warm with wine: What is thy petition, Esther, that it may be granted thee? and what wilt thou have done: although thou ask the half of my kingdom, thou shalt have it.

3.text: Then she answered: If I have found Favour in thy sight, O king, and if it please thee, give me my life for which I ask, and my people for which I request.

4.text: For we are given up, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. And would God we were sold for bondmen and bondwomen: the evil might be borne with, and I would have mourned in silence: but now we have an enemy, whose cruelty redoundeth upon the king.

5.text: And king Assuerus answered and said: Who is this, and of what power, that he should do these things?

6.text: And Esther said: It is this Aman that is our adversary and most wicked enemy. Aman hearing this was forthwith astonished, not being able to bear the countenance of the king and of the queen.

7.text: But the king being angry rose up, and went from the place of the banquet into the garden set with trees. Aman also rose up to entreat Esther the queen for his life, for he understood that evil was prepared for him by the king.

8.text: And when the king came back out of the garden set with trees, and entered into the place of the banquet, he found Aman was fallen upon the bed on which Esther lay, and he said: He will force the queen also in my presence, in my own house. The word was not yet gone out of the king’s mouth, and immediately they covered his face.

9.text: And Harbona, one of the eunuchs that stood waiting on the king, said: Behold the gibbet which he hath prepared for Mardochai, who spoke for the king, standeth in Aman’s house, being fifty cubits high. And the king said to him: Hang him upon it.

10.text: So Aman was hanged on the gibbet, which he had prepared for Mardochai: and the king’s wrath ceased.

1.text: On that day king Assuerus gave the house of Aman, the Jews’ enemy, to queen Esther, and Mardochai came in before the king. For Esther had confessed to him that he was her uncle.

2.text: And the king took the ring which he had commanded to be taken again from Aman, and gave it to Mardochai. And Esther set Mardochai over her house.

3.text: And not content with these things, she fell down at the king’s feet and wept, and speaking to him besought him, that he would give orders that the malice of Aman the Agagite, and his most wicked devices which he had invented against the Jews, should be of no effect.

4.text: But he, as the manner was, held out the golden sceptre with his hand, which was the sign of clemency: and she arose up and stood before him,

5.text: And said: If it please the king, and if I have found favour in his sight, and my request be not disagreeable to him, I beseech thee, that the former letters of Aman the traitor and enemy of the Jews, by which he commanded that they should be destroyed in all the king’s provinces, may be reversed by new letters.

6.text: For how can I endure the murdering and slaughter of my people?

7.text: And king Assuerus answered Esther the queen, and Mardochai the Jew: I have given Aman’s house to Esther, and I have commanded him to be hanged on a gibbet, because he durst lay hands on the Jews.

8.text: Write ye therefore to the Jews, as it pleaseth you, in the king’s name, and seal the letters with my ring. For this was the custom, that no man durst gainsay the letters which were sent in the king’s name, and were sealed with his ring.

9.text: Then the king’s scribes and secretaries were called for (now it was the time of the third month which is called Siban) the three and twentieth day of the month, and letters were written, as Mardochai had a mind, to the Jews, and to the governors, and to the deputies, and to the judges, who were rulers over the hundred and twenty-seven provinces, from India even to Ethiopia: to province and province, to people and people, according to their languages and characters, and to the Jews, according as they could read and hear.

10.text: And these letters which were sent in the king’s name, were sealed with his ring, and sent by posts: who were to run through all the provinces, to prevent the former letters with new messages.

11.text: And the king gave orders to them, to speak to the Jews in every city, and to command them to gather themselves together, and to stand for their lives, and to kill and destroy all their enemies with their wives and children and all their houses, and to take their spoil.

12.text: And one day of revenge was appointed through all the provinces, to wit, the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar.

13.text: And this was the content of the letter, that it should be notified in all lands and peoples that were subject to the empire of king Assuerus, that the Jews were ready to be revenged of their enemies.

14.text: So the swift posts went out carrying the messages, and the king’s edict was hung up in Susan.

15.text: And Mardochai going forth out of the palace, and from the king’s presence, shone in royal apparel, to wit, of violet and sky colour, wearing a golden crown on his head, and clothed with a cloak of silk and purple. And all the city rejoiced and was glad.

16.text: But to the Jews a new light seemed to rise, joy, honour, and dancing.

17.text: And in all peoples, cities, and provinces, whithersoever the king’s commandments came, there was wonderful rejoicing, feasts and banquets, and keeping holy day: insomuch that many of other nations and religion, joined themselves to their worship and ceremonies. For a great dread of the name of the Jews had fallen upon all.

1.text: So on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which as we have said above is called Adar, when all the Jews were designed to be massacred, and their enemies were greedy after their blood, the case being altered, the Jews began to have the upper hand, and to revenge themselves of their adversaries.

2.text: And they gathered themselves together in every city, and town, and place, to lay their hands on their enemies, and their persecutors. And no one durst withstand them, for the fear of their power had gone through every people.

3.text: And the judges of the provinces, and the governors, and lieutenants, and every one in dignity, that presided over every place and work, extolled the Jews for fear of Mardochai:

4.text: For they knew him to be prince of the palace, and to have great power: and the fame of his name increased daily, and was spread abroad through all men’s mouths.

5.text: So the Jews made a great slaughter of their enemies, and killed them, repaying according to what they had prepared to do to them:

6.text: Insomuch that even in Susan they killed five hundred men, besides the ten sons of Aman the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews: whose names are these:

7.text: Pharsandatha, and Delphon, and Esphatha,

8.text: And Phoratha, and Adalia, and Aridatha,

9.text: And Phermesta, and Arisai, and Aridai, and Jezatha.

10.text: And when they had slain them, they would not touch the spoils of their goods.

11.text: And presently the number of them that were killed in Susan was brought to the king.

12.text: And he said to the queen: The Jews have killed five hundred men in the city of Susan, besides the ten sons of Aman: how many dost thou think they have slain in all the provinces? What askest thou more, and what wilt thou have me to command to be done?

13.text: And she answered: If it please the king, let it be granted to the Jews, to do tomorrow in Susan as they have done today, and that the ten sons of Aman may be hanged upon gibbets.

14.text: And the king commanded that it should be so done. And forthwith the edict was hung up in Susan, and the ten sons of Aman were hanged.

15.text: And on the fourteenth day of the month Adar the Jews gathered themselves together, and they killed in Susan three hundred men: but they took not their substance.

16.text: Moreover through all the provinces which were subject to the king’s dominion the Jews stood for their lives, and slew their enemies and persecutors: insomuch that the number of them that were killed amounted to seventy-five thousand, and no man took any of their goods.

17.text: Now the thirteenth day of the month Adar was the first day with them all of the slaughter, and on the fourteenth day they left off. Which they ordained to be kept holy day, so that all times hereafter they should celebrate it with feasting, joy, and banquets.

18.text: But they that were killing in the city of Susan, were employed in the slaughter on the thirteenth and fourteenth day of the same month: and on the fifteenth day they rested. And therefore they appointed that day to be a holy day of feasting and gladness.

19.text: But those Jews that dwelt in towns not walled and in villages, appointed the fourteenth day of the month Adar for banquets and gladness, so as to rejoice on that day, and send one another portions of their banquets and meats.

20.text: And Mardochai wrote all these things, and sent them comprised in letters to the Jews that abode in all the king’s provinces, both those that lay near and those afar off,

21.text: That they should receive the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the month Adar for holy days, and always at the return of the year should celebrate them with solemn honour:

22.text: Because on those days the Jews revenged themselves of their enemies, and their mourning and sorrow were turned into mirth and joy, and that these should be days of feasting and gladness, in which they should send one to another portions of meats; and should give gifts to the poor.

23.text: And the Jews undertook to observe with solemnity all they had begun to do at that time, which Mardochai by letters had commanded to be done.

24.text: For Aman, the son of Amadathi of the race of Agag, the enemy and adversary of the Jews, had devised evil against them, to kill them and destroy them: and had cast Phur, that is, the lot.

25.text: And afterwards Esther went in to the king, beseeching him that his endeavours might be made void by the king’s letters: and the evil that he had intended against the Jews, might return upon his own head. And so both he and his sons were hanged upon gibbets.

26.text: And since that time these days are called Phurim, that is, of lots: because Phur, that is, the lot, was cast into the urn. And all things that were done, are contained in the volume of this epistle, that is, of this book:

27.text: And the things that they suffered, and that were afterwards changed, the Jews took upon themselves and their seed, and upon all that had a mind to be joined to their religion, so that it should be lawful for none to pass these days without solemnity: which the writing testifieth, and certain times require, as the years continually succeed one another.

28.text: These are the days which shall never be forgot: and which all provinces in the whole world shall celebrate throughout all generations: neither is there any city wherein the days of Phurim, that is, of lots, must not be observed by the Jews, and by their posterity, which is bound to these ceremonies.

29.text: And Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mardochai the Jew, wrote also a second epistle, that with all diligence this day should be established a festival for the time to come.

30.text: And they sent to all the Jews that were in the hundred and twenty-seven provinces of king Assuerus, that they should have peace, and receive truth,

31.text: And observe the days of lots, and celebrate them with joy in their proper time: as Mardochai and Esther had appointed, and they undertook them to be observed by themselves and by their seed, fasts, and cries, and the days of lots,

32.text: And all things which are contained in the history of this book, which is called Esther.

1.text: And king Assuerus made all the land, and all the islands of the sea tributary.

2.text: And his strength and his empire, and the dignity and greatness wherewith he exalted Mardochai, are written in the books of the Medes, and of the Persians:

3.text: And how Mardochai of the race of the Jews, was next after king Assuerus: and great among the Jews, and acceptable to the people of his brethren, seeking the good of his people, and speaking those things which were for the welfare of his seed.

4.text: Then Mardochai said: God hath done these things.

5.text: I remember a dream that I saw, which signified these same things: and nothing thereof hath failed.

6.text: The little fountain which grew into a river, and was turned into a light, and into the sun, and abounded into many waters, is Esther, whom the king married, and made queen.

7.text: But the two dragons are I and Aman.

8.text: The nations that were assembled are they that endeavoured to destroy the name of the Jews.

9.text: And my nation is Israel, who cried to the Lord, and the Lord saved his people: and he delivered us from all evils, and hath wrought great signs and wonders among the nations:

10.text: And he commanded that there should be two lots, one of the people of God, and the other of all the nations.

11.text: And both lots came to the day appointed already from that time before God to all nations:

12.text: And the Lord remembered his people, and had mercy on his inheritance.

13.text: And these days shall be observed in the month of Adar on the fourteenth, and fifteenth day of the same month. with all diligence, and joy of the people gathered into one assembly, throughout all the generations hereafter of the people of Israel.

1.text: In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemy and Cleopatra, Dositheus, who said he was a priest, and of the Levitical race, and Ptolemy his son brought this epistle of Phurim, which they said Lysimachus the son of Ptolemy had interpreted in Jerusalem.

2.text: In the second year of the reign of Artaxerxes the great, in the first day of the month Nisan, Mardochai the son of Jair, the son of Semei, the son of Cis, of the tribe of Benjamin:

3.text: A Jew who dwelt in the city of Susan, a great man and among the first of the king’s court, had a dream.

4.text: Now he was of the number of the captives, whom Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon had carried away from Jerusalem with Jechonias king of Juda:

5.text: And this was his dream: Behold there were voices, and tumults, and thunders, and earthquakes, and a disturbance upon the earth.

6.text: And behold two great dragons came forth ready to fight one against another.

7.text: And at their cry all nations were stirred up to fight against the nation of the just.

8.text: And that was a day of darkness and danger, of tribulation and distress, and great fear upon the earth.

9.text: And the nation of the just was troubled fearing their own evils, and was prepared for death.

10.text: And they cried to God: and as they were crying, a little fountain grew into a very great river, and abounded into many waters.

11.text: The light and the sun rose up, and the humble were exalted, and they devoured the glorious.

12.text: And when Mardochai had seen this, and arose out of his bed, he was thinking what God would do: and he kept it fixed in his mind, desirous to know what the dream should signify.

1.text: And he abode at that time in the king’s court with Bagatha and Thara the king’s eunuchs, who were porters of the palace.

2.text: And when he understood their designs, and had diligently searched into their projects, he learned that they went about to lay violent hands on king Artaxerxes, and he told the king thereof.

3.text: Then the king had them both examined, and after they had confessed, commanded them to be put to death.

4.text: But the king made a record of what was done: and Mardochai also committed the memory of the thing to writing.

5.text: And the king commanded him, to abide in the court of the palace, and gave him presents for the information.

6.text: But Aman the son of Amadathi the Bugite was in great honour with the king, and sought to hurt Mardochai and his people, because of the two eunuchs of the king who were put to death.

1.text: And this was the copy of the letter: Artaxerxes the great king who reigneth from India to Ethiopia, to the princes and governors of the hundred and twenty-seven provinces, that are subject to his empire, greeting.

2.text: Whereas I reigned over many nations, and had brought all the world under my dominion, I was not willing to abuse the greatness of my power, but to govern my subjects with clemency and lenity, that they might live quietly without any terror. and might enjoy peace, which is desired by all men.

3.text: But when I asked my counsellors how this might be accomplished, one that excelled the rest in wisdom and fidelity, and was second after the king, Aman by name,

4.text: Told me that there was a people scattered through the whole world, which used new laws, and acted against the customs of all nations, despised the commandments of kings, and violated by their opposition the concord of all nations.

5.text: Wherefore having learned this, and seeing one nation in opposition to all mankind using perverse laws, and going against our commandments, and disturbing the peace and concord of the provinces subject to us,

6.text: We have commanded that all whom Aman shall mark out, who is chief over all the provinces, and second after the king, and whom we honour as a father, shall be utterly destroyed by their enemies, with their wives and children, and that none shall have pity on them. on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar of this present year:

7.text: That these wicked men going down to hell in one day, may restore to our empire the peace which they had disturbed.

8.text: But Mardochai besought the Lord, remembering all his works,

9.text: And said: O Lord, Lord, almighty king, for all things are in thy power, and there is none that can resist thy will, if thou determine to save Israel.

10.text: Thou hast made heaven and earth, and all things that are under the cope of heaven.

11.text: Thou art Lord of all, and there is none that can resist thy majesty.

12.text: Thou knowest all things, and thou knowest that it was not out of pride and contempt, or any desire of glory, that I refused to worship the proud Aman,

13.text: (For I would willingly and readily for the salvation of Israel have kissed even the steps of his feet,)

14.text: But I feared lest I should transfer the honour of my God to a man, and lest I should adore any one except my God.

15.text: And now, O Lord, O king, O God of Abraham, have mercy on thy people, because our enemies resolve to destroy us, and extinguish thy inheritance.

16.text: Despise not thy portion, which thou hast redeemed for thyself out of Egypt.

17.text: Hear my supplication, and be merciful to thy lot and inheritance, and turn our mourning into joy, that we may live and praise thy name, O Lord, and shut not the mouths of them that sing to thee.

18.text: And all Israel with like mind and supplication cried to the Lord, because they saw certain death hanging over their heads.

1.text: Queen Esther also, fearing the danger that was at hand, had recourse to the Lord.

2.text: And when she had laid away her royal apparel, she put on garments suitable for weeping and mourning: instead of divers precious ointments, she covered her head with ashes and dung, and she humbled her body with fasts: and all the places in which before she was accustomed to rejoice, she filled with her torn hair.

3.text: And she prayed to the Lord the God of Israel, saying: O my Lord, who alone art our king, help me a desolate woman, and who have no other helper but thee.

4.text: My danger is in my hands.

5.text: I have heard of my father that thou, O Lord, didst take Israel from among all nations, and our fathers from all their predecessors, to possess them as an everlasting inheritance, and thou hast done to them as thou hast promised.

6.text: We have sinned in thy sight, and therefore thou hast delivered us into the hands of our enemies:

7.text: For we have worshipped their gods. Thou art just, O Lord.

8.text: And now they are not content to oppress us with most hard bondage, but attributing the strength of their hands to the power of their idols,

9.text: They design to change thy promises, and destroy thy inheritance, and shut the mouths of them that praise thee, and extinguish the glory of thy temple and altar,

10.text: That they may open the mouths of Gentiles, and praise the strength of idols, and magnify for ever a carnal king.

11.text: Give not, O Lord, thy sceptre to them that are not, lest they laugh at our ruin: but turn their counsel upon themselves, and destroy him that hath begun to rage against us.

12.text: Remember, O Lord, and shew thyself to us in the time of our tribulation, and give me boldness, O Lord, king of gods, and of all power:

13.text: Give me a well ordered speech in my mouth in the presence of the lion, and turn his heart to the hatred of our enemy, that both he himself may perish, and the rest that consent to him.

14.text: But deliver us by thy hand, and help me, who have no other helper, but thee, O Lord, who hast the knowledge of all things.

15.text: And thou knowest that I hate the glory of the wicked, and abhor the bed of the uncircumcised, and of every stranger.

16.text: Thou knowest my necessity, that I abominate the sign of my pride and glory, which is upon my head in the days of my public appearance, and detest it as a menstruous rag, and wear it not in the days of my silence,

17.text: And that I have not eaten at Aman’s table, nor hath the king’s banquet pleased me, and that I have not drunk the wine of the drink offerings:

18.text: And that thy handmaid hath never rejoiced, since I was brought hither unto this day, but in thee, O Lord, the God of Abraham.

19.text: O God, who art mighty above all, hear the voice of them, that have no other hope, and deliver us from the hand of the wicked, and deliver me from my fear.

1.text: And he commanded her (no doubt but he was Mardochai) to go to the king, and petition for her people, and for her country.

2.text: Remember, (said he,) the days of thy low estate, how thou wast brought up by my hand, because Aman the second after the king hath spoken against us unto death.

3.text: And do thou call upon the Lord, and speak to the king for us, and deliver us from death.

4.text: And on the third day she laid away the garments she wore, and put on her glorious apparel.

5.text: And glittering in royal robes, after she had called upon God the ruler and Saviour of all, she took two maids with her,

6.text: And upon one of them she leaned, as if for delicateness and overmuch tenderness she were not able to bear up her own body.

7.text: And the other maid followed her lady, bearing up her train flowing on the ground.

8.text: But she with a rosy colour in her face, and with gracious and bright eyes, hid a mind full of anguish, and exceeding great fear.

9.text: So going in she passed through all the doors in order, and stood before the king, where he sat upon his royal throne, clothed with his royal robes, and glittering with gold, and precious stones, and he was terrible to behold.

10.text: And when he had lifted up his countenance, and with burning eyes had shewn the wrath of his heart, the queen sunk down, and her colour turned pale, and she rested her weary head upon her handmaid.

11.text: And God changed the king’s spirit into mildness, and all in haste and in fear he leaped from his throne, and holding her up in his arms, till she came to herself, caressed her with these words:

12.text: What is the matter, Esther? I am thy brother, fear not.

13.text: Thou shalt not die: for this law is not made for thee, but for all others.

14.text: Come near then, and touch the sceptre.

15.text: And as she held her peace, he took the golden sceptre, and laid it upon her neck, and kissed her, and said: Why dost thou not speak to me?

16.text: She answered: I saw thee, my lord, as an angel of God, and my heart was troubled for fear of thy majesty.

17.text: For thou, my lord, art very admirable, and thy. face is full of graces.

18.text: And while she was speaking, she fell down again, and was almost in a swoon.

19.text: But the king was troubled, and all his servants comforted her.

1.text: The great king Artaxerxes, from India to Ethiopia, to the governors and princes of a hundred and twenty-seven provinces, which obey our command, sendeth greeting.

2.text: Many have abused unto pride the goodness of princes, and the honour that hath been bestowed upon them:

3.text: And not only endeavour to oppress the king’s subjects, but not bearing the glory that is given them, take in hand to practise also against them that gave it.

4.text: Neither are they content not to return thanks for benefits received, and to violate in themselves the laws of humanity, but they think they can also escape the justice of God who seeth all things.

5.text: And they break out into so great madness, as to endeavour to undermine by lies such as observe diligently the offices committed to them, and do all things in such manner as to be worthy of all men’s praise,

6.text: While with crafty fraud they deceive the ears of princes that are well meaning, and judge of others by their own nature.

7.text: Now this is proved both from ancient histories, and by the things which are done daily, how the good designs of kings are depraved by the evil suggestions of certain men.

8.text: Wherefore we must provide for the peace of all provinces.

9.text: Neither must you think, if we command different things, that it cometh of the levity of our mind, but that we give sentence according to the quality and necessity of times, as the profit of the commonwealth requireth.

10.text: Now that you may more plainly understand what we say, I Aman the son of Amadathi, a Macedonian both in mind and country, and having nothing of the Persian blood, but with his cruelty staining our goodness, was received being a stranger by us:

11.text: And found our humanity so great towards him, that he was called our father, and was worshipped by all as the next man after the king:

12.text: But he was so far puffed up with arrogancy, as to go about to deprive us of our kingdom and life.

13.text: For with certain new and unheard of devices he hath sought the destruction of Mardochai, by whose fidelity and good services our life was saved, and of Esther the partner of our kingdom, with all their nation:

14.text: Thinking that after they were slain, he might work treason against us left alone without friends, and might transfer the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians.

15.text: But we have found that the Jews, who were by that most wicked man appointed to be slain, are in no fault at all, but contrariwise, use just laws,

16.text: And are the children of the highest and the greatest, and the ever living God, by whose benefit the kingdom was given both to our fathers and to us, and is kept unto this day.

17.text: Wherefore know ye that those letters which he sent in our name, are void and of no effect.

18.text: For which crime both he himself that devised it, and all his kindred hang on gibbets, before the gates of this city Susan: not we, but God repaying him as he deserved.

19.text: But this edict, which we now send, shall be published in all cities, that the Jews may freely follow their own laws.

20.text: And you shall aid them that they may kill those who had prepared themselves to kill them, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is called Adar.

21.text: For the almighty God hath turned this day of sadness and mourning into joy to them.

22.text: Wherefore you shall also count this day among other festival days, and celebrate it with all joy, that it may be known also in times to come,

23.text: That all they who faithfully obey the Persians, receive a worthy reward for their fidelity: but they that are traitors to their kingdom, are destroyed for their wickedness.

24.text: And let every province and city, that will not be partaker of this solemnity, perish by the sword and by fire, and be destroyed in such manner as to be made unpassable, both to men and beasts, for an example of contempt, and disobedience.

1.text: There was a man in the land of Hus, whose name was Job, and that man was simple and upright, and fearing God, and avoiding evil.

2.text: And there were born to him seven sons and three daughters.

3.text: And his possession was seven thousand sheep, and three thousand camels, and five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred she asses, and a family exceeding great: and this man was great among all the people of the east.

4.text: And his sons went, and made a feast by houses every one in his day. And sending they called their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

5.text: And when the days of their feasting were gone about, Job sent to them, and sanctified them: and rising up early offered holocausts for every one of them. For he said: Lest perhaps my sons have sinned, and have blessed God in their hearts. So did Job all days.

6.text: Now on a certain day when the sons of God came to stand before the Lord, Satan also was present among them.

7.text: And the Lord said to him: Whence comest thou? And he answered and said: I have gone round about the earth, and walked through it.

8.text: And the Lord said to him: Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a simple and upright man, and fearing God, and avoiding evil?

9.text: And Satan answering, said: Doth Job fear God in vain?

10.text: Hast not thou made a fence for him, and his house, and all his substance round about, blessed the works of his hands, and his possession hath increased on the earth?

11.text: But stretch forth thy hand a little, and touch all that he hath, and see if he blesseth thee not to thy face.

12.text: Then the Lord said to Satan: Behold, all that he hath is in thy hand: only put not forth thy hand upon his person. And Satan went forth from the presence of the Lord.

13.text: Now upon a certain day when his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their eldest brother,

14.text: There came a messenger to Job, and said: The oxen were ploughing, and the asses feeding beside them,

15.text: And the Sabeans rushed in, and took all away, and slew the servants with the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell thee.

16.text: And while he was yet speaking, another came, and said: The fire of God fell from heaven, and striking the sheep and the servants, hath consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell thee.

17.text: And while he also was yet speaking, there came another, and said: The Chaldeans made three troops, and have fallen upon the camels, and taken them, moreover they have slain the servants with the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell thee.

18.text: He was yet speaking, and behold another came in, and said: Thy sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their elder brother:

19.text: A violent wind came on a sudden from the side of the desert, and shook the four corners of the house, and it fell upon thy children and they are dead, and I alone have escaped to tell thee.

20.text: Then Job rose up, and rent his garments, and having shaven his head fell down upon the ground and worshipped,

21.text: And said: Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away: as it hath pleased the Lord so is it done: blessed be the name of the Lord.

22.text: In all these things Job sinned not by his lips, nor spoke he any foolish thing against God.

1.text: And it came to pass, when on a certain day the sons of God came, and stood before the Lord, and Satan came among them, and stood in his sight,

2.text: That the Lord said to Satan: Whence comest thou? And he answered and said: I have gone round about the earth, and walked through it.

3.text: And the Lord said to Satan: Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a man simple, and upright, and fearing God, and avoiding evil, and still keeping his innocence? But thou hast moved me against him, that I should afflict him without cause.

4.text: And Satan answered, and said: Skin for skin, and all that a man hath he will give for his life:

5.text: But put forth thy hand, and touch his bone and his flesh, and then thou shalt see that he will bless thee to thy face.

6.text: And the Lord said to Satan: Behold he is in thy hand, but yet save his life.

7.text: So Satan went forth from the presence Of the Lord, and struck Job with a very grievous ulcer, from the sole of the foot even to the top of his head:

8.text: And he took a potsherd and scraped the corrupt matter, sitting on a dunghill.

9.text: And his wife said to him: Dost thou still continue in thy simplicity? bless God and die.

10.text: And he said to her: Thou hast spoken like one of the foolish women: if we have received good things at the hand of God, why should we not receive evil? In all these things Job did not sin with his lips.

11.text: Now when Job’s three friends heard all the evil that had befallen him, they came every one from his own place, Eliphaz, the Themanite, and Baldad the Suhite, and Sophar the Naamathite. For they had made an appointment to come together and visit him, and comfort him.

12.text: And when they had lifted up their eyes afar off, they knew him not, and crying out they wept, and rending their garments they sprinkled dust upon their heads towards heaven.

13.text: And they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no man spoke to him a word: for they saw that his grief was very great.

1.text: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed his day,

2.text: And he said:

3.text: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said: A man child is conceived.

4.text: Let that day be turned into darkness, let not God regard it from above, and let not the light shine upon it.

5.text: Let darkness, and the shadow of death cover it, let a mist overspread it, and let it be wrapped up in bitterness.

6.text: Let a darksome whirlwind seize upon that night, let it not be counted in the days of the year, nor numbered in the months.

7.text: Let that night be solitary, and not worthy of praise.

8.text: Let them curse it who curse the day. who are ready to raise up a leviathan:

9.text: Let the stars be darkened with the mist thereof: let it expect light and not see it, nor the rising of the dawning of the day:

10.text: Because it shut not up the doors of the womb that bore me, nor took away evils from my eyes.

11.text: Why did I not die in the womb, why did I not perish when I came out of the belly?

12.text: Why received upon the knees? why suckled at the breasts?

13.text: For now I should have been asleep and still, and should have rest in my sleep.

14.text: With kings and consuls of the earth, who build themselves solitudes:

15.text: Or with princes, that possess gold, and fill their houses with silver:

16.text: Or as a hidden untimely birth I should not be, or as they that being conceived have not seen the light.

17.text: There the wicked cease from tumult, and there the wearied in strength are at rest.

18.text: And they sometime bound together without disquiet, have not heard the voice of the oppressor.

19.text: The small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master.

20.text: Why is light given to him that is in misery, and life to them that are in bitterness of soul?

21.text: That look for death, and it cometh not, as they that dig for a treasure:

22.text: And they rejoice exceedingly when they have found the grave.

23.text: To a man whose way is hidden, and God hath surrounded him with darkness?

24.text: Before I eat I sigh: and as overflowing waters, so is my roaring:

25.text: For the fear which I feared hath come upon me: and that which I was afraid of, hath befallen me.

26.text: Have I not dissembled? have I not kept silence? have I not been quiet? and indignation is come upon me.

1.text: Then Eliphaz the Themanite answered, and said:

2.text: If we begin to speak to thee, perhaps thou wilt take it ill, but who can withhold the words he hath conceived?

3.text: Behold thou hast taught many, and thou hast strengthened the weary hands:

4.text: Thy words have confirmed them that were staggering, and thou hast strengthened the trembling knees:

5.text: But now the scourge is come upon thee, and thou faintest: it hath touched thee, and thou art troubled.

6.text: Where is thy fear, thy fortitude, thy patience, and the perfection of thy ways?

7.text: Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished being innocent? or when were the just destroyed?

8.text: On the contrary I have seen those who work iniquity, and sow sorrows, and reap them,

9.text: Perishing by the blast of God, and consumed by the spirit of his wrath.

10.text: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the lioness, and the teeth of the whelps of lions are broken:

11.text: The tiger hath perished for want of prey, and the young lions are scattered abroad.

12.text: Now there was a word spoken to me in private, and my ears by stealth as it were received the veins of its whisper.

13.text: In the horror of a vision by night, when deep sleep is wont to hold men,

14.text: Fear seized upon me, and trembling, and all my bones were affrighted:

15.text: And when a spirit passed before me, the hair of my flesh stood up.

16.text: There stood one whose countenance I knew not, an image before my eyes, and I heard the voice as it were of a gentle wind:

17.text: Shall man be justified in comparison of God, or shall a man be more pure than his maker?

18.text: Behold they that serve him are not steadfast, and in his angels he found wickedness:

19.text: How much more shall they that dwell in houses of clay, who have an earthly foundation, be consumed as with the moth?

20.text: From morning till evening they shall be cut down: and because no one understandeth, they shall perish for ever.

21.text: And they that shall be left, shall be taken away from them: they shall die, and not in wisdom.

1.text: Call now if there be any that will answer thee, and turn to some of the saints.

2.text: Anger indeed killeth the foolish, and envy slayeth the little one.

3.text: I have seen a fool with a strong root, and I cursed his beauty immediately.

4.text: His children shall be far from safety, and shall be destroyed in the gate, and there shall be none to deliver them.

5.text: Whose harvest the hungry shall eat, and the armed man shall take him by violence, and the thirsty shall drink up his riches.

6.text: Nothing upon earth is done without a cause, and sorrow doth not spring out of the ground.

7.text: Man is born to labour and the bird to fly.

8.text: Wherefore I will pray to the Lord, and address my speech to God:

9.text: Who doth great things and unsearchable and wonderful things without number:

10.text: Who giveth rain upon the face of the earth, and watereth all things with waters:

11.text: Who setteth up the humble on high, and comforteth with health those that mourn.

12.text: Who bringeth to nought the designs of the malignant, so that their hands cannot accomplish what they had begun:

13.text: Who catcheth the wise in their craftiness, and disappointeth the counsel of the wicked:

14.text: They shall meet with darkness in the day, and grope at noonday as in the night.

15.text: But he shall save the needy from the sword of their mouth, and the poor from the hand of the violent.

16.text: And to the needy there shall be hope, but iniquity shall draw in her mouth.

17.text: Blessed is the man whom God correcteth: refuse not therefore the chastising of the lord:

18.text: For he woundeth, and cureth: he striketh, and his hands shall heal.

19.text: In six troubles he shall deliver thee, and in the seventh, evil shall not touch thee.

20.text: In famine he shall deliver thee from death: and in battle, from the hand of the sword.

21.text: Thou shalt be hidden from the scourge of the tongue: and thou shalt not fear calamity when it cometh.

22.text: In destruction and famine then shalt laugh: and thou shalt not be afraid of the beasts of the earth.

23.text: But thou shalt have a covenant with the stones of the lands, and the beasts of the earth shall be at peace with thee.

24.text: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle is in peace, and visiting thy beauty thou shalt not sin.

25.text: Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be multiplied, and thy offspring like the grass of the earth.

26.text: Thou shalt enter into the grave in abundance, as a heap of wheat is brought in its season.

27.text: Behold, this is even so, as we have searched out: which thou having heard, consider it thoroughly in thy mind.

1.text: But Job answered, and said:

2.text: O that my sins, whereby I have deserved wrath, and the calamity that I suffer, were weighed in a balance.

3.text: As the sand of the sea this would appear heavier: therefore my words are full of sorrow:

4.text: For the arrows of the Lord are in me, the rage whereof drinketh up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord war against me.

5.text: Will the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or will the ox low when he standeth before a full manger?

6.text: Or can an unsavoury thing be eaten, that is not seasoned with salt? or can a man taste that which when tasted bringeth death?

7.text: The things which before my soul would not touch, now, through anguish are my meats.

8.text: Who will grant that my request may come: and that God may give me what I look for?

9.text: And that he that hath begun may destroy me, that he may let loose his hand, and cut me off?

10.text: And that this may be my comfort, that afflicting me with sorrow, he spare not, nor I contradict the words of the Holy One.

11.text: For what is my strength, that I can hold out? or what is my end that I should keep patience?

12.text: My strength is not the strength of stones, nor is my flesh of brass.

13.text: Behold there is no help for me in myself, and my familiar friends also are departed from me.

14.text: He that taketh away mercy from his friend, forsaketh the fear of the Lord.

15.text: My brethren have passed by me, as the torrent that passeth swiftly in the valleys.

16.text: They that fear the hoary frost, the snow shall fall upon them.

17.text: At the time when they shall be scattered they shall perish: and after it groweth hot they shall be melted out of their place.

18.text: The paths of their steps are entangled: they shall walk in vain, and shall perish.

19.text: Consider the paths of Thema, the ways of Saba, and wait a little while.

20.text: They are confounded, because I have hoped: they are come also even unto me, and are covered with shame.

21.text: Now you are come: and now seeing my affliction you are afraid.

23.text: Or deliver me from the hand of the enemy, and rescue me out of the hand of the mighty?

24.text: Teach me, and I will hold my peace: and if I have been ignorant in any thing, instruct me.

25.text: Why have you detracted the words of truth, whereas there is none of you that can reprove me?

26.text: You dress up speeches only to rebuke, and you utter words to the wind.

27.text: You rush in upon the fatherless, and you endeavour to overthrow your friend.

28.text: However finish what you have begun, give ear, and see whether I lie.

29.text: Answer, I beseech you, without contention: and speaking that which is just, judge ye.

30.text: And you shall not find iniquity in my tongue, neither shall folly sound in my mouth.

1.text: The life of man upon earth is a warfare, and his days are like the days of a hireling.

2.text: As a servant longeth for the shade, as the hireling looketh for the end of his work;

3.text: So I also have had empty months, and have numbered to myself wearisome nights.

4.text: If I lie down to sleep, I shall say: When shall I arise? and again I shall look for the evening, and shall be filled with sorrows even till darkness.

5.text: My flesh is clothed with rottenness and the filth of dust, my skin is withered and drawn together.

6.text: My days have passed more swiftly than the web is cut by the weaver, and are consumed without any hope.

7.text: Remember that my life is but wind, and my eyes shall not return to see good things.

8.text: Nor shall the sight of man behold me: thy eyes are upon me, and I shall be no more.

9.text: As a cloud is consumed, and passeth away: so he that shall go down to hell shall not come up.

10.text: Nor shall he return any more into his house, neither shall his place know him any more.

11.text: Wherefore I will not spare my mouth, I will speak in the affliction of my spirit: I will talk with the bitterness of my soul.

12.text: Am I a sea, or a whale, that thou hast enclosed me in a prison?

13.text: If I say: My bed shall comfort me, and I shall be relieved speaking with myself on my couch:

14.text: Thou wilt frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions.

15.text: So that my soul rather chooseth hanging, and my bones death.

16.text: I have done with hope, I shall now live no longer: spare me, for my days are nothing.

17.text: What is a man that thou shouldst magnify him? or why dost thou set thy heart upon him?

18.text: Thou visitest him early in the morning, and thou provest him suddenly.

19.text: How long wilt thou not spare me, nor suffer me to swallow down my spittle?

20.text: I have sinned: what shall I do to thee, O keeper of men? why hast thou set me opposite to thee, and I am become burdensome to myself?

21.text: Why dost thou not remove my sin, and why dost thou not take away my iniquity? Behold now I shall sleep in the dust: and if thou seek me in the morning, I shall not be.

1.text: Then Baldad the Suhite answered, and said:

2.text: How long wilt thou speak these things, and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind?

3.text: Doth God pervert judgment, or doth the Almighty overthrow that which is just?

4.text: Although thy children have sinned against him, and he hath left them in the hand of their iniquity:

5.text: Yet if thou wilt arise early to God, and wilt beseech the Almighty:

6.text: If thou wilt walk clean and upright, he will presently awake unto thee, and will make the dwelling of thy justice peaceable:

7.text: Insomuch, that if thy former things were small, thy latter things would be multiplied exceedingly.

8.text: For inquire of the former generation, and search diligently into the memory of the fathers:

9.text: (For we are but of yesterday, and are ignorant that our days upon earth are but a shadow:)

10.text: And they shall teach thee: they shall speak to thee, and utter words out of their hearts.

11.text: Can the rush be green without moisture? or a sedge-bush grow without water?

12.text: When it is yet in flower, and is not plucked up with the hand, it withereth before all herbs.

13.text: Even so are the ways of all that forget God, and the hope of the hypocrite shall perish:

14.text: His folly shall not please him, and his trust shall be like the spider’s web.

15.text: He shall lean upon his house, and it shall not stand: he shall prop it up, and it shall not rise:

16.text: He seemeth to have moisture before the sun cometh, and at his rising his blossom shall shoot forth.

17.text: His roots shall be thick upon a heap of stones, and among the stones he shall abide.

18.text: If one swallow him up out of his place, he shall deny him, and shall say: I know thee not.

19.text: For this is the joy of his way, that others may spring again out of the earth.

20.text: God will not cast away the simple, nor reach out his hand to the evildoer:

21.text: Until thy mouth be filled with laughter, and thy lips with rejoicing.

22.text: They that hate thee, shall be clothed with confusion: and the dwelling of the wicked shall not stand.

1.text: And Job answered, and said:

2.text: Indeed I know it is so, and that man cannot be justified compared with God.

3.text: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one for a thousand.

4.text: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath resisted him, and hath had peace?

5.text: Who hath removed mountains, and they whom he overthrew in his wrath, knew it not.

6.text: Who shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.

7.text: Who commandeth the sun and it riseth not: and shutteth up the stars as it were under a seal:

8.text: Who alone spreadeth out the heavens, and walketh upon the waves of the sea.

9.text: Who maketh Arcturus, and Orion, and Hyades, and the inner parts of the south.

10.text: Who doth things great and incomprehensible, and wonderful, of which there is no number.

11.text: If he come to me, I shall not see him: if he depart I shall not understand.

12.text: If he examine on a sudden, who shall answer him? or who can say: Why dost thou so?

13.text: God, whose wrath no man can resist, and under whom they stoop that bear up the world.

14.text: What am I then, that I should answer him, and have words with him?

15.text: I, who although I should have any just thing, would not answer, but would make supplication to my judge.

16.text: And if he should hear me when I call, I should not believe that he had heard my voice.

17.text: For he shall crush me in a whirlwind, and multiply my wounds even without cause.

18.text: He alloweth not my spirit to rest, and he filleth me with bitterness.

19.text: If strength be demanded, he is most strong: if equity of judgment, no man dare bear witness for me.

20.text: If I would justify myself, my own mouth shall condemn me: if I would shew myself innocent, he shall prove me wicked.

21.text: Although I should be simple, even this my soul shall be ignorant of, and I shall be weary of my life.

22.text: One thing there is that I have spoken, both the innocent and the wicked he consumeth.

23.text: If he scourge, let him kill at once, and not laugh at the pains of the innocent.

24.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked, he covereth the face of the judges thereof: and if it be not he, who is it then?

25.text: My days have been swifter than a post: they have fled away and have not seen good.

26.text: They have passed by as ships carrying fruits, as an eagle flying to the prey.

27.text: If I say: I will not speak so: I change my face, and am tormented with sorrow.

28.text: I feared all my works, knowing that thou didst not spare the offender.

29.text: But if so also I am wicked, why have I laboured in vain?

30.text: If I be washed as it were with snow waters, and my hands shall shine ever so clean:

31.text: Yet thou shalt plunge me in filth, and my garments shall abhor me,

32.text: For I shall not answer a man that is like myself: nor one that may be heard with me equally in judgment.

33.text: There is none that may be able to reprove both, and to put his hand between both.

34.text: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me.

35.text: I will speak, and will not fear him: for I cannot answer while I am in fear.

1.text: My soul is weary of my life, I will let go my speech against myself, I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

2.text: I will say to God: Do not condemn me: tell me why thou judgest me so.

3.text: Doth it seem good to thee that thou shouldst calumniate me, and oppress me, the work of thy own hands, and help the counsel of the wicked?

4.text: Hast thou eyes of flesh: or, shalt thou see as man seeth?

5.text: Are thy days as the days of man, and are thy years as the times of men:

6.text: That thou shouldst inquire after my iniquity, and search after my sin?

7.text: And shouldst know that I have done no wicked thing, whereas there is no man that can deliver out of thy hand.

8.text: Thy hands have made me, and fashioned me wholly round about, and dost thou thus cast me down headlong on a sudden?

9.text: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay, and thou wilt bring me into dust again.

10.text: Hast thou not milked me as milk, and curdled me like cheese?

11.text: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh: thou hast put me together with bones and sinews:

12.text: Thou hast granted me life and mercy, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.

13.text: Although thou conceal these things in thy heart, yet I know that thou rememberest all things.

14.text: If I have sinned and thou hast spared me for an hour: why dost thou not suffer me to be clean from my iniquity?

15.text: And if I be wicked, woe unto me: and if just, I shall not lift up my head, being filled with affliction and misery.

16.text: And for pride thou wilt take me as a lioness, and returning thou tormentest me wonderfully.

17.text: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and multipliest thy wrath upon me, and pains war against me.

18.text: Why didst thou bring me forth out of the womb: O that I had been consumed that eye might not see me!

19.text: I should have been as if I had not been, carried from the womb to the grave.

20.text: Shall not the fewness of my days be ended shortly? suffer me, therefore, that I may lament my sorrow a little:

21.text: Before I go, and return no more, to a land that is dark and covered with the mist of death:

22.text: A land of misery and darkness, where the shadow of death, and no order, but everlasting horror dwelleth.

1.text: Then Sophar the Naamathite answered, and said:

2.text: Shall not he that speaketh much, hear also? or shall a man full of talk be justified?

3.text: Shall men hold their peace to thee only? and when thou hast mocked others, shall no man confute thee?

4.text: For thou hast said: My word is pure, and I am clean in thy sight.

5.text: And I wish that God would speak with thee, and would open his lips to thee,

6.text: That he might shew thee the secrets of wisdom, and that his law is manifold, and thou mightest understand that he exacteth much less of thee, than thy iniquity deserveth.

7.text: Peradventure thou wilt comprehend the steps of God, and wilt find out the Almighty perfectly?

8.text: He is higher than heaven, and what wilt thou do? he is deeper than hell, and how wilt thou know?

9.text: The measure of him is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.

10.text: If he shall overturn all things, or shall press them together, who shall contradict him?

11.text: For he knoweth the vanity of men, and when he seeth iniquity, doth he not consider it?

12.text: A vain man is lifted up into pride, and thinketh himself born free like a wild ass’s colt.

13.text: But thou hast hardened thy heart, and hast spread thy hands to him.

14.text: If thou wilt put away from thee the iniquity that is in thy hand, and let not injustice remain in thy tabernacle:

15.text: Then mayst thou lift up thy face without spot, and thou shalt be steadfast, and shalt not fear.

16.text: Thou shalt also forget misery, and remember it only as waters that are passed away.

17.text: And brightness like that of the noonday, shall arise to thee at evening: and when thou shalt think thyself consumed, thou shalt rise as the day star.

18.text: And thou shalt have confidence, hope being set before thee, and being buried thou shalt sleep secure.

19.text: Thou shalt rest, and there shall be none to make thee afraid: and many shall entreat thy face.

20.text: But the eyes of the wicked shall decay, and the way to escape shall fail them, and their hope the abomination of the soul.

1.text: When Job answered, and said:

2.text: Are you then men alone, and shall wisdom die with you?

3.text: I also have a heart as well as you: for who is ignorant of these things, which you know?

4.text: He that is mocked by his friends as I, shall call upon God and he will hear him: for the simplicity of the just man is laughed to scorn.

5.text: The lamp despised in the thoughts of the rich, is ready for the time appointed.

6.text: The tabernacles of robbers abound, and they provoke God boldly; whereas it is he that hath given all into their hands:

7.text: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee: and the birds of the air, and they shall tell thee.

8.text: Speak to the earth, and it shall answer thee: and the fishes of the sea shall tell.

9.text: Who is ignorant that the hand of the Lord hath made all these things?

10.text: In whose hand is the soul of every living thing, and the spirit of all flesh of man.

11.text: Doth not the ear discern words, and the palate of him that eateth, the taste?

12.text: In the ancient is wisdom, and in length of days prudence.

13.text: With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding.

14.text: If he pull down, there is no man that can build up: if he shut up a man, there is none that can open.

15.text: If he withhold the waters, all things shall be dried up: and if he send them out, they shall overturn the earth.

16.text: With him is strength and wisdom: he knoweth both the deceiver, and him that is deceived.

17.text: He bringeth counsellors to a foolish end, and judges to insensibility.

18.text: He looseth the belt of kings, and girdeth their loins with a cord.

19.text: He leadeth away priests without glory, and overthroweth nobles.

20.text: He changeth the speech of the true speakers, and taketh away the doctrine of the aged.

21.text: He poureth contempt upon princes, and relieveth them that were oppressed.

22.text: He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth up to light the shadow of death.

23.text: He multiplieth nations, and destroyeth them, and restoreth them again after they were overthrown.

24.text: He changeth the heart of the princes of the people of the earth, and deceiveth them that they walk in vain where there is no way.

25.text: They shall grope as in the dark, and not in the light, and he shall make them stagger like men that are drunk.

1.text: Behold my eye hath seen all these things, and my ear hath heard them, and I have understood them all.

2.text: According to your knowledge I also know: neither am I inferior to you.

3.text: But yet I will speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God.

4.text: Having first shewn that you are forgers of lies, and maintainers of perverse opinions.

5.text: And I wish you would hold your peace, that you might be thought to be wise men.

6.text: Hear ye therefore my reproof, and attend to the judgment of my lips.

7.text: Hath God any need of your lie, that you should speak deceitfully for him?

8.text: Do you accept his person, and do you endeavour to judge for God?

9.text: Or shall it please him, from whom nothing can be concealed? or shall he be deceived as a man, with your deceitful dealings?

10.text: He shall reprove you, because in secret you accept his person.

11.text: As soon as he shall move himself, he shall trouble you: and his dread shall fall upon you.

12.text: Your remembrance shall be compared to ashes, and your necks shall be brought to clay.

13.text: Hold your peace a little while, that I may speak whatsoever my mind shall suggest to me.

14.text: Why do I tear my flesh with my teeth, and carry my soul in my hands?

15.text: Although he should kill me, I will trust in him: but yet I will reprove my ways in his sight.

16.text: And he shall be my saviour: for no hypocrite shall come before his presence.

17.text: Hear ye my speech, and receive with your ears hidden truths.

18.text: If I shall be judged, I know that I shall be found just.

19.text: Who is he that will plead against me? let him come: why am I consumed holding my peace?

20.text: Two things only do not to me, and then from thy face I shall not be hid:

21.text: Withdraw thy hand far from me, and let not thy dread terrify me.

22.text: Call me, and I will answer thee: or else I will speak, and do thou answer me.

23.text: How many are my iniquities and sins? make me know my crimes and offences.

24.text: Why hidest thou thy face, and thinkest me thy enemy?

25.text: Against a leaf, that is carried away with the wind, thou shewest thy power, and thou pursuest a dry straw.

26.text: For thou writest bitter things against me, and wilt consume me for the sins of my youth.

27.text: Thou hast put my feet in the stocks, and hast observed all my paths, and hast considered the steps of my feet:

28.text: Who am to be consumed as rottenness, and as a garment that is moth-eaten.

1.text: Man born of a woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries.

2.text: Who cometh forth like a flower, and is destroyed, and fleeth as a shadow, and never continueth in the same state.

3.text: And dost thou think it meet to open thy eyes upon such an one, and to bring him into judgment with thee?

4.text: Who can make him clean that is conceived of unclean seed? is it not thou who only art?

5.text: The days of man are short, and the number of his months is with thee: thou hast appointed his bounds which cannot be passed.

6.text: Depart a little from him, that he may rest, until his wished for day come, as that of the hireling.

7.text: A tree hath hope: if it be cut, it groweth green again, and the boughs thereof sprout.

8.text: If its root be old in the earth, and its stock be dead in the dust:

9.text: At the scent of water, it shall spring, and bring forth leaves, as when it was first planted.

10.text: But man when he shall be dead, and stripped and consumed, I pray you where is he?

11.text: As if the waters should depart out of the sea, and an emptied river should be dried up:

12.text: So man when he is fallen asleep shall not rise again; till the heavens be broken, he shall not awake, nor rise up out of his sleep.

13.text: Who will grant me this, that thou mayst protect me in hell, and hide me till thy wrath pass, and appoint me a time when thou wilt remember me?

14.text: Shall man that is dead, thinkest thou, live again? all the days in which I am now in warfare, I expect until my change come.

15.text: Thou shalt call me, and I will answer thee: to the work of thy hands thou shalt reach out thy right hand.

16.text: Thou indeed hast numbered my steps, but spare my sins.

17.text: Thou hast sealed up my offences as it were in a bag, but hast cured my iniquity.

18.text: A mountain falling cometh to nought, and a rock is removed out of its place.

19.text: Waters wear away the stones, and with inundation the ground by little and little is washed away: so in like manner thou shalt destroy man.

20.text: Thou hast strengthened him for a little while, that he may pass away for ever: thou shalt change his face, and shalt send him away.

21.text: Whether his children come to honour or dishonour, he shall not understand.

22.text: But yet his flesh, while he shall live, shall have pain, and his soul shall mourn over him.

1.text: And Eliphaz the Themanite, answered, and said:

2.text: Will a wise man answer as if he were speaking in the wind, and fill his stomach with burning heat?

3.text: Thou reprovest him by words, who is not equal to thee, and thou speakest that which is not good for thee.

4.text: As much as is in thee, thou hast made void fear, and hast taken away prayers from before God.

5.text: For thy iniquity hath taught thy mouth, and thou imitatest the tongue of blasphemers.

6.text: Thy own mouth shall condemn thee, and not I: and thy own lips shall answer thee.

7.text: Art thou the first man that was born, or wast thou made before the hills?

8.text: Hast thou heard God’s counsel, and shall his wisdom be inferior to thee?

9.text: What knowest thou that we are ignorant of? what dost thou understand that we know not?

10.text: There are with us also aged and ancient men, much elder than thy fathers.

11.text: Is it a great matter that God should comfort thee? but thy wicked words hinder this.

12.text: Why doth thy heart elevate thee, and why dost thou stare with thy eyes, as if they were thinking great things?

13.text: Why doth thy spirit swell against God, to utter such words out of thy mouth?

14.text: What is man that he should be without spot, and he that is born of a woman that he should appear just?

15.text: Behold among his saints none is unchangeable, and the heavens are not pure in his sight.

16.text: How much more is man abominable, and unprofitable, who drinketh iniquity like water?

17.text: I will shew thee, hear me: and I will tell thee what I have seen.

18.text: Wise men confess and hide not their fathers.

19.text: To whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger hath passed among them.

20.text: The wicked man is proud all his days, and the number of the years of his tyranny is uncertain.

21.text: The sound of dread is always in his ears: and when there is peace, he always suspecteth treason.

22.text: He believeth not that he may return from darkness to light, looking round about for the sword on every side.

23.text: When he moveth himself to seek bread, he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.

24.text: Tribulation shall terrify him, and distress shall surround him, as a king that is prepared for the battle.

25.text: For he hath stretched out his hand against God, and hath strengthened himself against the Almighty.

26.text: He hath run against him with his neck raised up, and is armed with a fat neck.

27.text: Fatness hath covered his face, and the fat hangeth down on his sides.

28.text: He hath dwelt in desolate cities, and in desert houses that are reduced into heaps.

29.text: He shall not be enriched, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he push his root in the earth.

30.text: He shall not depart out of darkness: the flame shall dry up his branches, and he shall be taken away by the breath of his own mouth.

31.text: He shall not believe, being vainly deceived by error, that he may be redeemed with any price.

32.text: Before his days be full he shall perish: and his hands shall wither away.

33.text: He shall be blasted as a vine when its grapes are in the first flower, and as an olive tree that casteth its flower.

34.text: For the congregation of the hypocrite is barren, and fire shall devour their tabernacles, who love to take bribes.

35.text: He hath conceived sorrow, and hath brought forth iniquity, and his womb prepareth deceits.

1.text: Then Job answered, and said:

2.text: I have often heard such things as these: you are all troublesome comforters.

3.text: Shall windy words have no end? or is it any trouble to thee to speak?

4.text: I also could speak like you: and would God your soul were for my soul. I would comfort you also with words, and would wag my head over you.

5.text: I would strengthen you with my mouth, and would move my lips, as sparing you.

6.text: But what shall I do? If I speak, my pain will not rest: and if I hold my peace, it will not depart from me.

7.text: But now my sorrow hath oppressed me, and all my limbs are brought to nothing.

8.text: My wrinkles bear witness against me, and a false speaker riseth up against my face, contradicting me.

9.text: He hath gathered together his fury against me, and threatening me he hath gnashed with his teeth upon me: my enemy hath beheld me with terrible eyes.

10.text: They have opened their mouths upon me, and reproaching me they have struck me on the cheek, they are filled with my pains.

11.text: God hath shut me up with the unjust man, and hath delivered me into the hands of the wicked.

12.text: I that was formerly so wealthy, am all on a sudden broken to pieces: he hath taken me by my neck, he hath broken me, and hath set me up to be his mark.

13.text: He hath compassed me round about with his lances, he hath wounded my loins, he hath not spared, and hath poured out my bowels on the earth.

14.text: He hath torn me with wound upon wound, he hath rushed in upon me like a giant.

15.text: I have sowed sackcloth upon my skin, and have covered my flesh with ashes.

16.text: My face is swollen with weeping, and my eyelids are dim.

17.text: These things have I suffered without the iniquity of my hand, when I offered pure prayers to God.

18.text: O earth, cover not thou my blood, neither let my cry find a hiding place in thee.

19.text: For behold my witness is in heaven, and he that knoweth my conscience is on high.

20.text: My friends are full of words: my eye poureth out tears to God.

21.text: And O that a man might so be judged with God, as the son of man is judged with his companion!

22.text: For behold short years pass away and I am walking in a path by which I shall not return.

1.text: My spirit shall be wasted, my days shall be shortened, and only the grave remaineth for me.

2.text: I have not sinned, and my eye abideth in bitterness.

3.text: Deliver me O Lord, and set me beside thee, and let any man’s hand fight against me.

4.text: Thou hast set their heart far from understanding, therefore they shall not be exalted.

5.text: He promiseth a prey to his companions, and the eyes of his children shall fail.

6.text: He hath made me as it were a byword of the people, and I am an example before them.

7.text: My eye is dim through indignation, and my limbs are brought as it were to nothing.

8.text: The just shall be astonished at this, and the innocent shall be raised up against the hypocrite.

9.text: And the just man shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger.

10.text: Wherefore be you all converted, and come, and I shall not find among you any wise man.

11.text: My days have passed away, my thoughts are dissipated, tormenting my heart.

12.text: They have turned night into day, and after darkness I hope for light again.

13.text: If I wait hell is my house, and I have made my bed in darkness.

14.text: If I have said to rottenness: Thou art my father; to worms, my mother and my sister.

15.text: Where is now then my expectation, and who considereth my patience?

16.text: All that I have shall go down into the deepest pit: thinkest thou that there at least I shall have rest?

1.text: Then Baldad the Suhite answered, and said:

2.text: How long will you throw out words? understand first, and so let us speak.

3.text: Why are we reputed as beasts, and counted vile before you?

4.text: Thou that destroyest thy soul in thy fury, shall the earth be forsaken for thee, and shall rocks be removed out of their place?

5.text: Shall not the light of the wicked be extinguished, and the flame of his fire not shine?

6.text: The light shall be dark in his tabernacle, and the lamp that is over him, shall be put out.

7.text: The step of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down headlong.

8.text: For he hath thrust his feet into a net, and walketh in its meshes.

9.text: The sole of his foot shall be held in a snare, and thirst shall burn against him.

10.text: A gin is hidden for him in the earth, and his trap upon the path.

11.text: Fears shall terrify him on every side, and shall entangle his feet.

12.text: Let his strength be wasted with famine, and let hunger invade his ribs.

13.text: Let it devour the beauty of his skin, let the firstborn death consume his arms.

14.text: Let his confidence be rooted out of his tabernacle, and let destruction tread upon him like a king.

15.text: Let the companions of him that is not, dwell in his tabernacle, let brimstone be sprinkled in his tent.

16.text: Let his roots be dried up beneath, and his harvest destroyed above.

17.text: Let the memory of him perish from the earth and let not his name be renowned in the streets.

18.text: He shall drive him out of light into darkness, and shall remove him out of the world.

19.text: His seed shall not subsist, nor his offspring among his people, nor any remnants in his country.

20.text: They that come after him shall be astonished at his day, and horror shall fall upon them that went before.

21.text: These men are the tabernacles of the wicked, and this the place of him that knoweth not God.

1.text: Then Job answered, and said:

2.text: How long do you afflict my soul, and break me in pieces with words?

3.text: Behold, these ten times you confound me, and are not ashamed to oppress me.

4.text: For if I have been ignorant, my ignorance shall be with me.

5.text: But you have set yourselves up against me, and reprove me with my reproaches.

6.text: At least now understand, that God hath not afflicted me with an equal judgment, and compassed me with his scourges.

7.text: Behold I cry suffering violence, and no one will hear: I shall cry aloud, and there is none to judge.

8.text: He hath hedged in my path round about, and I cannot pass, and in my way he hath set darkness.

9.text: He hath stripped me of my glory, and hath taken the crown from my head.

10.text: He hath destroyed me on every side, and I am lost, and he hath taken away my hope, as from a tree that is plucked up.

11.text: His wrath is kindled against me, and he hath counted me as his enemy.

12.text: His troops have come together, and have made themselves a way by me, and have besieged my tabernacle round about.

13.text: He hath put my brethren far from me, and my acquaintance like strangers have departed from me.

14.text: My kinsmen have forsaken me, and they that knew me, have forgotten me.

15.text: They that dwelt in my house, and my maidservants have counted me a stranger, and I have been like an alien in their eyes.

16.text: I called my servant, and he gave me no answer, I entreated him with my own mouth.

17.text: My wife hath abhorred my breath, and I entreated the children of my womb.

18.text: Even fools despise me; and when I was gone from them, they spoke against me.

19.text: They that were sometime my counsellors, have abhorred me: and he whom I love most is turned against me.

20.text: The flesh being consumed. My bone hath cleaved to my skin, and nothing but lips are left about my teeth.

21.text: Have pity on me, have pity on me, at least you my friends, because the hand of the Lord hath touched me.

22.text: Why do you persecute me as God, and glut yourselves with my flesh?

23.text: Who will grant me that my words may be written? Who will grant me that they may be marked down in a book?

24.text: With an iron pen and in a plate of lead, or else be graven with an instrument in flint stone.

25.text: For I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth.

26.text: And I shall be clothed again with my skin, and in my flesh I will see my God.

27.text: Whom I myself shall see, and my eyes shall behold, and not another: this my hope is laid up in my bosom.

28.text: Why then do you say now: Let us persecute him, and let us find occasion of word against him?

29.text: Flee then from the face of the sword, for the sword is the revenger of iniquities: and know ye that there is judgment.

1.text: Then Sophar the Naamathite answered, and said:

2.text: Therefore various thoughts succeed one another in me, and my mind is hurried away to different things.

3.text: The doctrine with which thou reprovest me, I will hear, and the spirit of my understanding shall answer for me.

4.text: This I know from the beginning, since man was placed upon the earth,

5.text: That the praise of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment.

6.text: If his pride mount up even to heaven, and his head touch the clouds:

7.text: In the end he shall be destroyed like a dunghill, and they that has seen him shall say: Where is he?

8.text: As a dream that fleeth away he shall not be found, he shall pass as a vision of the night:

9.text: The eyes that had seen him, shall see him no more, neither shall his place any more behold him.

10.text: His children shall be oppressed with want, and his hands shall render him his sorrow.

11.text: His bones shall be filled with the vices of his youth, and they shall sleep with him in the dust.

12.text: For when evil shall be sweet in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue.

13.text: He will spare it, and not leave it, and will hide it in his throat.

14.text: His bread in his belly shall be turned into the gall of asps within him.

15.text: The riches which he hath swallowed; he shall vomit up, and God shall draw them out of his belly.

16.text: He shall suck the head of asps, and the viper’s tongue shall kill him.

17.text: (Let him not see the streams of the river, the brooks of honey and of butter.)

18.text: He shall be punished for all that he did, and yet shall not be consumed: according to the multitude of his devices so also shall he suffer.

19.text: Because he broke in and stripped the poor: he hath violently taken away a house which he did not build.

20.text: And yet his belly was not filled: and when he hath the things he coveted, he shall not be able to possess them.

21.text: There was nothing left of his meat, and therefore nothing shall continue of his goods:

22.text: When he shall be filled, he shall be straitened, he shall burn, and every sorrow shall fall upon him.

23.text: May his belly be filled, that God may send forth the wrath of his indignation upon him, and rain down his war upon him.

24.text: He shall flee from weapons of iron, and shall fall upon a bow of brass.

25.text: The sword is drawn out, and cometh forth from its scabbard, and glittereth in his bitterness: the terrible ones shall go and come upon him.

26.text: All darkness is hid in his secret places: a fire that is not kindled shall devour him, he shall be afflicted when left in his tabernacle.

27.text: The heavens shall reveal his iniquity, and the earth shall rise up against him.

28.text: The offspring of his house shall be exposed, he shall be pulled down in the day of God’s wrath.

29.text: This is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the inheritance of his doings from the Lord.

1.text: Then Job answered, and said:
