2.text: Hear, I beseech you, my words, and do penance.

3.text: Suffer me, and I will speak, and after, if you please, laugh at my words.

4.text: Is my debate against man, that I should not have just reason to be troubled?

5.text: Hearken to me and be astonished, and lay your finger on your mouth.

6.text: As for me, when I remember, I am afraid, and trembling taketh hold on my flesh.

7.text: Why then do the wicked live, are they advanced, and strengthened with riches?

8.text: Their seed continueth before them, a multitude of kinsmen, and of children’s children in their sight.

9.text: Their houses are secure and peaceable, and the rod of God is not upon them.

10.text: Their cattle have conceived, and failed not: their cow has calved, and is not deprived of her fruit.

11.text: Their little ones go out like a flock, and their children dance and play.

12.text: They take the timbrel, and the harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.

13.text: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment they go down to hell.

14.text: Who have said to God: Depart from us, we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.

15.text: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what doth it profit us if we pray to him?

16.text: Yet because their good things are not in their hand, may the counsel of the wicked be far from me.

17.text: How often shall the lamp of the wicked be put out, and a deluge come upon them, and he shall distribute the sorrows of his wrath?

18.text: They shall be as chaff before the face of the wind, and as ashes which the whirlwind scattereth.

19.text: God shall lay up the sorrow of the father for his children: and when he shall repay, then shall he know.

20.text: His eyes shall see his own destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

21.text: For what is it to him what befalleth his house after him: and if the number of his months be diminished by one half?

22.text: Shall any one teach God knowledge, who judgeth those that are high?

23.text: One man dieth strong, and hale, rich and happy.

24.text: His bowels are full of fat, and his bones are moistened with marrow.

25.text: But another dieth in bitterness of soul without any riches:

26.text: And yet they shall sleep together in the dust, and worms shall cover them.

27.text: Surely I know your thoughts, and your unjust judgments against me.

28.text: For you say: Where is the house of the prince? and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?

29.text: Ask any one of them that go by the way, and you shall perceive that he knoweth these same things.

30.text: Because the wicked man is reserved to the day of destruction, and he shall be brought to the day of wrath.

31.text: Who shall reprove his way to his face? and who shall repay him what he hath done?

32.text: He shall be brought to the graves, and shall watch in the heap of the dead.

33.text: He hath been acceptable to the gravel of Cocytus, and he shall draw every man after him, and there are innumerable before him.

34.text: How then do ye comfort me in vain, whereas your answer is shewn to be repugnant to truth?

1.text: Then Eliphaz the Themanite answered, and said:

2.text: Can man be compared with God, even though he were of perfect knowledge?

3.text: What doth it profit God if thou be just? or what dost thou give him if thy way be unspotted?

4.text: Shall he reprove thee for fear, and come with thee into judgment:

5.text: And not for thy manifold wickedness, and thy infinite iniquities?

6.text: For thou hast taken away the pledge of thy brethren without cause, and stripped the naked of their clothing.

7.text: Thou hast not given water to the weary, thou hast withdrawn bread from the hungry.

8.text: In the strength of thy arm thou didst possess the land, and being the most mighty thou holdest it.

9.text: Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless thou hast broken in pieces.

10.text: Therefore art thou surrounded with snares, and sudden fear troubleth thee.

11.text: And didst thou think that thou shouldst not see darkness, and that thou shouldst not be covered with the violence of overflowing waters?

12.text: Dost not thou think that God is higher than heaven, and is elevated above the height of the stars?

13.text: And thou sayst: What doth God know? and he judgeth as it were through a mist.

14.text: The clouds are his covert, and he doth not consider our things, and he walketh about the poles of heaven.

15.text: Dost thou desire to keep the path of ages, which wicked men have trodden?

16.text: Who were taken away before their time, and a flood hath overthrown their foundation.

17.text: Who said to God: Depart from us: and looked upon the Almighty as if he could do nothing:

18.text: Whereas he had filled their houses with good things: whose way of thinking be far from me.

19.text: The just shall see, and shall rejoice, and the innocent shall laugh them to scorn.

20.text: Is not their exaltation cut down, and hath not fire devoured the remnants of them?

21.text: Submit thyself then to him, and be at peace: and thereby thou shalt have the best fruits.

22.text: Receive the law of his mouth, and lay up his words in thy heart.

23.text: If thou wilt return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, and shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacle.

24.text: He shall give for earth flint, and for flint torrents of gold.

25.text: And the Almighty shall be against thy enemies, and silver shall be heaped together for thee.

26.text: Then shalt thou abound in delights in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face to God.

27.text: Thou shalt pray to him, and he will hear thee, and thou shalt pay vows.

28.text: Thou shalt decree a thing, and it shall come to thee, and light shall shine in thy ways.

29.text: For he that hath been humbled, shall be in glory: and he that shall bow down his eyes, he shall be saved.

30.text: The innocent shall be saved, and he shall be saved by the cleanness of his hands.

1.text: Then Job answered, and said:

2.text: Now also my words are in bitterness, and the hand of my scourge is more grievous than my mourning.

3.text: Who will grant me that I might know and find him, and come even to his throne?

4.text: I would set judgment before him, and would fill my mouth with complaints.

5.text: That I might know the words that he would answer me, and understand what he would say to me.

6.text: I would not that he should contend with me with much strength, nor overwhelm me with the weight of his greatness.

7.text: Let him propose equity against me, and let my judgment come to victory.

8.text: But if I go to the east, he appeareth not; if to the west, I shall not understand him.

9.text: If to the left hand, what shall I do? I shall not take hold on him: if I turn myself to the right hand, I shall not see him.

10.text: But he knoweth my way, and has tried me as gold that passeth through the fire:

11.text: My foot hath followed his steps, I have kept his way, and have not declined from it.

12.text: I have not departed from the commandments of his lips, and the words of his mouth I have hid in my bosom.

13.text: For he is alone, and no man can turn away his thought: and whatsoever his soul hath desired, that hath he done.

14.text: And when he shall have fulfilled his will in me, many other like things are also at hand with him.

15.text: And therefore I am troubled at his presence, and when I consider him I am made pensive with fear.

16.text: God hath softened my heart, and the Almighty hath troubled me.

17.text: For I have not perished because of the darkness that hangs over me, neither hath the mist covered my face.

1.text: Times are not hid from the Almighty: but they that know him, know not his days.

2.text: Some have removed landmarks, have taken away flocks by force, and fed them.

3.text: They have driven away the ass of the fatherless, and have taken away the widow’s ox for a pledge.

4.text: They have overturned the way of the poor, and have oppressed together the meek of the earth.

5.text: Others like wild asses in the desert go forth to their work: by watching for a prey they get bread for their children.

6.text: They reap the field that is not their own, and gather the vintage of his vineyard whom by violence they have oppressed.

7.text: They send men away naked, taking away their clothes who have no covering in the cold:

8.text: Who are wet, with the showers of the mountains, and having no covering embrace the stones.

9.text: They have violently robbed the fatherless, and stripped the poor common people.

10.text: From the naked and them that go without clothing, and from the hungry they have taken away the ears of corn.

11.text: They have taken their rest at noon among the stores of them, who after having trodden the winepresses suffer thirst.

12.text: Out of the cities they have made men to groan, and the soul of the wounded hath cried out, and God doth not suffer it to pass unrevenged.

13.text: They have been rebellious to the light, they have not known his ways, neither have they returned by his paths.

14.text: The murderer riseth at the very break of day, he killeth the needy, and the poor man: but in the night he will be as a thief.

15.text: The eye of the adulterer observeth darkness, saying: No eye shall see me: and he will cover his face.

16.text: He diggeth through houses in the dark, as in the day they had appointed for themselves, and they have not known the light.

17.text: If the morning suddenly appear, it is to them the shadow of death: and they walk in darkness as if it were in light.

18.text: He is light upon the face of the water: cursed be his portion on the earth, let him not walk by the way of the vineyards.

19.text: Let him pass from the snow waters to excessive heat, and his sin even to hell.

20.text: Let mercy forget him: may worms be his sweetness: let him be remembered no more, but be broken in pieces as an unfruitful tree.

21.text: For he hath fed the barren that beareth not, and to the widow he hath done no good.

22.text: He hath pulled down the strong by his might: and when he standeth up, he shall not trust to his life.

23.text: God hath given him place for penance, and he abuseth it unto pride: but his eyes are upon his ways.

24.text: They are lifted up for a little while and shall not stand, and shall be brought down as all things, and shall be taken away, and as the tops of the ears of corn they shall be broken.

25.text: And if it be not so, who can convince me that I have lied, and set my words before God?

1.text: Then Baldad the Suhite answered, and I said:

2.text: Power and terror are with him, who maketh peace in his high places.

3.text: Is there any numbering of his soldiers? and upon whom shall not his light arise?

4.text: Can man be justified compared with God, or he that is born of a woman appear clean?

5.text: Behold even the moon doth not shine, and the stars are not pure in his sight.

6.text: How much less man that is rottenness and the son of man who is a worm?

1.text: Then Job answered, and said:

2.text: Whose helper art thou? is it of him that is weak? and dost thou hold up the arm of him that has no strength?

3.text: To whom hast thou given counsel? perhaps to him that hath no wisdom, and thou hast shewn thy very great prudence.

4.text: Whom hast thou desired to teach? was it not him that made life?

5.text: Behold the giants groan under the waters, and they that dwell with them.

6.text: Hell is naked before him, and there is no covering for destruction.

7.text: He stretched out the north over the empty space, and hangeth the earth upon nothing.

8.text: He bindeth up the waters in his clouds, so that they break not out and fall down together.

9.text: He withholdeth the face of his throne, and spreadeth his cloud over it.

10.text: He hath set bounds about the waters, till light and darkness come to an end.

11.text: The pillars of heaven tremble, and dread at his beck.

12.text: By his power the seas are suddenly gathered together, and his wisdom has struck the proud one.

13.text: His spirit hath adorned the heavens, and his obstetric hand brought forth the winding serpent.

14.text: Lo, these things are said in part of his ways: and seeing we have heard scarce a little drop of his word, who shall be able to behold the thunder of his greatness?

1.text: Job also added, taking up his parable, and said:

2.text: As God liveth, who hath taken away my judgment, and the Almighty, who hath brought my soul to bitterness,

3.text: As long as breath remaineth in me, and the spirit of God in my nostrils,

4.text: My lips shall not speak iniquity, neither shall my tongue contrive lying.

5.text: God forbid that I should judge you to be just: till I die I will not depart from my innocence.

6.text: My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not forsake: for my heart doth not reprehend me in all my life.

7.text: Let my enemy be as the ungodly, and my adversary as the wicked one.

8.text: For what is the hope of the hypocrite if through covetousness he take by violence, and God deliver not his soul?

9.text: Will God hear his cry, when distress shall come upon him?

10.text: Or can he delight himself in the Almighty, and call upon God at all times?

11.text: I will teach you by the hand of God, what the Almighty hath, and I will not conceal it.

12.text: Behold you all know it, and why do you speak vain things without cause?

13.text: This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the inheritance of the violent, which they shall receive of the Almighty.

14.text: If his sons be multiplied, they shall be for the sword, and his grandsons shall not be filled with bread.

15.text: They that shall remain of him, shall be buried in death, and his widows shall not weep.

16.text: If he shall heap together silver as earth, and prepare raiment as clay,

17.text: He shall prepare indeed, but the just man shall be clothed with it: and the innocent shall divide the silver.

18.text: He hath built his house as a moth, and as a keeper he hath made a booth.

19.text: The rich man when he shall sleep shall take away nothing with him: he shall open his eyes and find nothing.

20.text: Poverty like water shall take hold on him, a tempest shall oppress him in the night.

21.text: A burning wind shall take him up, and carry him away, and as a whirlwind shall snatch him from his place.

22.text: And he shall cast upon him, and shall not spare: out of his hand he would willingly flee.

23.text: He shall clasp his hands upon him, and shall hiss at him, beholding his place.

1.text: Silver hath beginnings of its veins, and gold hath a place wherein it is melted.

2.text: Iron is taken out of the earth, and stone melted with heat is turned into brass.

3.text: He hath set a time for darkness, and the end of all things he considereth, the stone also that is in the dark and the shadow of death.

4.text: The flood divideth from the people that are on their journey, those whom the food of the needy man hath forgotten, and who cannot be come at.

5.text: The land, out of which bread grew in its place, hath been overturned with fire.

6.text: The stones of it are the place of sapphires, and the clods of it are gold.

7.text: The bird hath not known the path, neither hath the eye of the vulture beheld it.

8.text: The children of the merchants have not trodden it, neither hath the lioness passed by it.

9.text: He hath stretched forth his hand to the flint, he hath overturned mountains from the roots.

10.text: In the rocks he hath cut out rivers, and his eye hath seen every precious thing.

11.text: The depths also of rivers he hath searched, and hidden things he hath brought forth to light.

12.text: But where is wisdom to be found, and where is the place of understanding?

13.text: Man knoweth not the price thereof, neither is it found in the land of them that live in delights.

14.text: The depth saith: It is not in me: and the sea saith: It is not with me.

15.text: The finest gold shall not purchase it, neither shall silver be weighed in exchange for it.

16.text: It shall not be compared with the dyed colours of India, or with the most precious stone sardonyx, or the sapphire.

17.text: Gold or crystal cannot equal it, neither shall any vessels of gold be changed for it.

18.text: High and eminent things shall not be mentioned in comparison of it: but wisdom is drawn out of secret places.

19.text: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not be equal to it, neither shall it be compared to the cleanest dyeing.

20.text: Whence then cometh wisdom? and where is the place of understanding?

21.text: It is hid from the eyes of all living. and the fowls of the air know it not.

22.text: Destruction and death have said: With our ears we have heard the fame thereof.

23.text: God understandeth the way of it, and he knoweth the place thereof.

24.text: For he beholdeth the ends of the world: and looketh on all things that are under heaven.

25.text: Who made a weight for the winds and weighed the waters by measure.

26.text: When he gave a law for the rain, and a way for the sounding storms.

27.text: Then he saw it, and declared, and prepared, and searched it.

28.text: And he said to man: Behold the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom: and to depart from evil, is understanding.

1.text: Job also added, taking up his parable, and said:

2.text: Who will grant me, that I might be according to the months past, according to the days in which God kept me?

3.text: When his lamp shined over my head, and I walked by his light in darkness?

4.text: As I was in the days of my youth, when God was secretly in my tabernacle?

5.text: When the Almighty was with me: and my servants round about me?

6.text: When I washed my feet with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil?

7.text: When I went out to the gate of the city, and in the street they prepared me a chair?

8.text: The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the old men rose up and stood.

9.text: The princes ceased to speak, and laid the finger on their mouth.

10.text: The rulers held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to their throat.

11.text: The ear that heard me blessed me, and the eye that saw me gave witness to me:

12.text: Because I had delivered the poor man that cried out; and the fatherless that had no helper.

13.text: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me, and I comforted the heart of the widow.

14.text: I was clad with justice: and I clothed myself with my judgment, as with a robe and a diadem.

15.text: I was an eye to the blind, and a foot to the lame.

16.text: I was the father of the poor: and the cause which I knew not, I searched out most diligently.

17.text: I broke the jaws of the wicked man, and out of his teeth I took away the prey.

18.text: And I said: I shall die in my nest, and as a palm tree shall multiply my days.

19.text: My root is opened beside the waters, and dew shall continue in my harvest.

20.text: My glory shall always be renewed, and my bow in my hand shall be repaired.

21.text: They that heard me, waited for my sentence, and being attentive held their peace at my counsel.

22.text: To my words they durst add nothing, and my speech dropped upon them.

23.text: They waited for me as for rain, and they opened their mouth as for a latter shower.

24.text: If at any time I laughed on them, they believed not, and the light of my countenance fell not on earth.

25.text: If I had a mind to go to them, I sat first, and when I sat as a king, with his army standing about him, yet I was a comforter of them that mourned.

1.text: But now the younger in time scorn me, whose fathers I would not have set with the dogs of my flock:

2.text: The strength of whose hands was to me as nothing, and they were thought unworthy of life itself.

3.text: Barren with want and hunger, who gnawed in the wilderness, disfigured with calamity and misery.

4.text: And they ate grass, and barks of trees, and the root of junipers was their food.

5.text: Who snatched up these things out of the valleys, and when they had found any of them, they ran to them with a cry.

6.text: They dwelt in the desert places of torrents, and in caves of earth, or upon the gravel.

7.text: They pleased themselves among these kind of things, and counted it delightful to be under the briers.

8.text: The children of foolish and base men, and not appearing at all upon the earth.

9.text: Now I am turned into their song, and am become their byword.

10.text: They abhor me, and flee far from me, and are not afraid to spit in my face.

11.text: For he hath opened his quiver, and hath afflicted me, and hath put a bridle into my mouth.

12.text: At the right hand of my rising, my calamities forthwith arose: they have overthrown my feet, and have overwhelmed me with their paths as with waves.

13.text: They have destroyed my ways, they have lain in wait against me, and they have prevailed, and there was none to help.

14.text: They have rushed in upon me, as when a wall is broken, and a gate opened, and have rolled themselves down to my miseries.

15.text: I am brought to nothing: as a wind thou hast taken away my desire: and my prosperity hath passed away like a cloud.

16.text: I am brought to nothing: as a wind thou hast taken away my desire: and my prosperity hath passed away like a cloud.

17.text: In the night my bone is pierced with sorrows: and they that feed upon me, do not sleep.

18.text: With the multitude of them my garment is consumed, and they have girded me about, as with the collar of my coat.

19.text: I am compared to dirt, and am likened to embers and ashes.

20.text: I cry to thee, and thou hearest me not: I stand up, and thou dost not regard me.

21.text: Thou art changed to be cruel toward me, and in the hardness of thy hand thou art against me.

22.text: Thou hast lifted me up, and set me as it were upon the wind, and thou hast mightily dashed me.

23.text: I know that thou wilt deliver me to death, where a house is appointed for every one that liveth.

24.text: But yet thou stretchest not forth thy hand to their consumption: and if they shall fall down thou wilt save.

25.text: I wept heretofore for him that was afflicted, and my soul had compassion on the poor.

26.text: I expected good things, and evils are come upon me: I waited for light, and darkness broke out.

27.text: My inner parts have boiled without any rest, the days of affliction have prevented me.

28.text: I went mourning without indignation; I rose up, and cried in the crowd.

29.text: I was the brother of dragons, and companion of ostriches.

30.text: My skin is become black upon me, and my bones are dried up with heat.

31.text: My harp is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of those that weep.

1.text: I made a covenant with my eyes, that I would not so much as think upon a virgin.

2.text: For what part should God from above have in me, and what inheritance the Almighty from on high?

3.text: Is not destruction to the wicked, and aversion to them that work iniquity?

4.text: Doth not he consider my ways, and number all my steps?

5.text: If I have walked in vanity, and my foot hath made haste to deceit:

6.text: Let him weigh me in a just balance, and let God know my simplicity.

7.text: If my step hath turned out of the way, and if my heart hath followed my eyes, and if a spot hath cleaved to my hands:

8.text: Then let me sow and let another eat: and let my offspring be rooted out.

9.text: If my heart hath been deceived upon a woman, and if I have laid wait at my friend’s door:

10.text: Let my wife be the harlot of another, and let other men lie with her.

11.text: For this is a heinous crime, and a most grievous iniquity.

12.text: It is a fire that devoureth even to destruction, and rooteth up all things that spring.

13.text: If I have despised to abide judgment with my manservant, or my maidservant, when they had any controversy against me:

14.text: For what shall I do when God shall rise to judge? and when he shall examine, what shall I answer him?

15.text: Did not he that made me in the womb make him also: and did not one and the same form me in the womb?

16.text: If I have denied to the poor what they desired, and have made the eyes of the widow wait:

17.text: If I have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof:

18.text: (For from my infancy mercy grew up with me: and it came out with me from my mother’s womb:)

19.text: If I have despised him that was perishing for want of clothing, and the poor man that had no covering:

20.text: If his sides have not blessed me, and if he were not warmed with the fleece of my sheep:

21.text: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, even when I saw myself superior in the gate:

22.text: Let my shoulder fall from its joint, and let my arm with its bones be broken.

23.text: For I have always feared God as waves swelling over me, and his weight I was not able to bear.

24.text: If I have thought gold my strength, and have said to fine gold: My confidence:

25.text: If I have rejoiced over my great riches, and because my hand had gotten much.

26.text: If I beheld the sun when it shined, and the moon going in brightness:

27.text: And my heart in secret hath rejoiced, and I have kissed my hand with my mouth:

28.text: Which is a very great iniquity, and a denial against the most high God.

29.text: If I have been glad at the downfall of him that hated me, and have rejoiced that evil had found him.

30.text: For I have not given my mouth to sin, by wishing a curse to his soul.

31.text: If the men of my tabernacle have not said: Who will give us of his flesh that we may be filled?

32.text: The stranger did not stay without, my door was open to the traveller.

33.text: If as a man I have hid my sin, and have concealed my iniquity in my bosom.

34.text: If I have been afraid at a very great multitude, and the contempt of kinsmen hath terrified me: and I have not rather held my peace, and not gone out of the door.

35.text: Who would grant me a hearer, that the Almighty may hear my desire; and that he himself that judgeth would write a book,

36.text: That I may carry it on my shoulder, and put it about me as a crown?

37.text: At every step of mine I would pronounce it, and offer it as to a prince.

38.text: If my land cry against me, and with it the furrows thereof mourn:

39.text: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, and have afflicted the soul of the tillers thereof:

40.text: Let thistles grow up to me instead of wheat, and thorns instead of barley.

1.text: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he seemed just to himself.

2.text: And Eliu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram, was angry and was moved to indignation: now he was angry against Job, because he said he was just before God.

3.text: And he was angry with his friends because they had not found a reasonable answer, but only had condemned Job.

4.text: So Eliu waited while Job was speaking, because they were his elders that were speaking.

5.text: But when he saw that the three were not able to answer, he was exceedingly angry.

6.text: Then Eliu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said: I am younger in days, and you are more ancient; therefore hanging down my head, I was afraid to shew you my opinion.

7.text: For I hoped that greater age would speak, and that a multitude of years would teach wisdom.

8.text: But, as I see, there is a spirit in men, and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth understanding.

9.text: They that are aged are not the wise men, neither do the ancients understand judgment.

10.text: Therefore I will speak: Hearken to me, I also will shew you my wisdom.

11.text: For I have waited for your words, I have given ear to your wisdom, as long as you were disputing in words.

12.text: And as long as I thought you said some thing, I considered: but, as I see, there is none of you that can convince Job, and answer his words.

13.text: Lest you should say: We have found wisdom, God hath cast him down, not man.

14.text: He hath spoken nothing to me, and I will not answer him according to your words.

15.text: They were afraid, and answered no more, and they left off speaking.

16.text: Therefore because I have waited, and they have not spoken: they stood, and answered no more:

17.text: I also will answer my part, and will shew my knowledge.

18.text: For I am full of matter to speak of, and the spirit of my bowels straiteneth me.

19.text: Behold, my belly is as new wine which wanteth vent, which bursteth the new vessels.

20.text: I will speak and take breath a little: I will open my lips, and will answer.

21.text: I will not accept the person of man, and I will not level God with man.

22.text: For I know not how long I shall continue, and whether after a while my Maker may take me away.

1.text: Hear therefore, O Job, my speeches, and hearken to all my words.

2.text: Behold now I have opened my mouth, let my tongue speak within my jaws.

3.text: My words are from my upright heart, and my lips shall speak a pure sentence.

4.text: The spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gave me life.

5.text: If thou canst, answer me, and stand up against my face.

6.text: Behold God hath made me as well as thee, and of the same clay I also was formed.

7.text: But yet let not my wonder terrify thee, and let not my eloquence be burdensome to thee.

8.text: Now thou has said in my hearing, and I have heard the voice of thy words:

9.text: I am clean, and without sin: I am unspotted, and there is no iniquity in me.

10.text: Because he hath found complaints against me, therefore he hath counted me for his enemy.

11.text: He hath put my feet in the stocks, he hath observed all my paths.

12.text: Now this is the thing in which thou art not justified: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.

13.text: Dost thou strive against him, because he hath not answered thee to all words?

14.text: God speaketh once, and repeateth not the selfsame thing the second time.

15.text: By a dream in a vision by night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, and they are sleeping in their beds:

16.text: Then he openeth the ears of men, and teaching instructeth them in what they are to learn.

17.text: That he may withdraw a man from the things he is doing, and may deliver him from pride.

18.text: Rescuing his soul from corruption: and his life from passing to the sword.

19.text: He rebuketh also by sorrow in the bed, and he maketh all his bones to wither.

20.text: Bread becometh abominable to him in his life, and to his soul the meat which before he desired.

21.text: His flesh shall be consumed away, and his bones that were covered shall be made bare.

22.text: His soul hath drawn near to corruption, and his life to the destroyers.

23.text: If there shall be an angel speaking for him, one among thousands, to declare man’s uprightness,

24.text: He shall have mercy on him, and shall say: Deliver him, that he may not go down to corruption: I have found wherein I may be merciful to him.

25.text: His flesh is consumed with punishment, let him return to the days of his youth.

26.text: He shall pray to God, and he will be gracious to him: and he shall see his face with joy, and he will render to man his justice.

27.text: He shall look upon men, and shall say: I have sinned, and indeed I have offended, and I have not received what I have deserved.

28.text: He hath delivered his soul from going into destruction, that it may live and see the light.

29.text: Behold, all these things God worketh three times within every one.

30.text: That he may withdraw their souls from corruption, and enlighten them with the light of the living.

31.text: Attend, Job, and hearken to me: and hold thy peace, whilst I speak.

32.text: But if thou hast any thing to say, answer me, speak: for I would have thee to appear just.

33.text: And if thou have not, hear me: hold thy peace, and I will teach thee wisdom.

1.text: And Eliu continued his discourse, and said:

2.text: Hear ye, wise men, my words, and ye learned, hearken to me:

3.text: For the ear trieth words, and the mouth discerneth meats by the taste.

4.text: Let us choose to us judgment, and let us see among ourselves what is the best.

5.text: For Job hath said: I am just, and God hath overthrown my judgment.

6.text: For in judging me there is a lie: my arrow is violent without any sin.

7.text: What man is there like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water?

8.text: Who goeth in company with them that work iniquity, and walketh with wicked men?

9.text: For he hath said: Man shall not please God, although he run with him.

10.text: Therefore, ye men of understanding, hear me: far from god be wickedness, and iniquity from the Almighty.

11.text: For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one he will reward them.

12.text: For in very deed God will not condemn without cause, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.

13.text: What other hath he appointed over the earth? or whom hath he set over the world which he made?

14.text: If he turn his heart to him, he shall draw his spirit and breath unto himself.

15.text: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall return into ashes.

16.text: If then thou hast understanding, hear what is said, and hearken to the voice of my words.

17.text: Can he be healed that loveth not judgment? and how dost thou so far condemn him that is just?

18.text: Who saith to the king: Thou art an apostate: who calleth rulers ungodly?

19.text: Who accepteth not the persons of princes: nor hath regarded the tyrant, when he contended against the poor man: for all are the work of his hands.

20.text: They shall suddenly die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and they shall pass, and take away the violent without hand.

21.text: For his eyes are upon the ways of men, and he considereth all their steps.

22.text: There is no darkness, and there is no shadow of death, where they may be hid who work iniquity.

23.text: For it is no longer in the power of man to enter into judgment with God.

24.text: He shall break in pieces many and innumerable, and shall make others to stand in their stead.

25.text: For he knoweth their works: and therefore he shall bring night on them, and they shall be destroyed.

26.text: He hath struck them, as being wicked, in open sight.

27.text: Who as it were on purpose have revolted from him, and would not understand all his ways:

28.text: So that they caused the cry of the needy to come to him, and he heard the voice of the poor.

29.text: For when he granteth peace, who is there that can condemn? When he hideth his countenance, who is there that can behold him, whether it regard nations, or all men?

30.text: Who maketh a man that is a hypocrite to reign for the sins of the people?

31.text: Seeing then I have spoken of God, I will not hinder thee in thy turn.

32.text: If I have erred, teach thou me: if I have spoken iniquity, I will add no more.

33.text: Doth God require it of thee, because it hath displeased thee? for thou begannest to speak, and not I: but if thou know any thing better, speak.

34.text: Let men of understanding speak to me, and let a wise man hearken to me.

35.text: But Job hath spoken foolishly, and his words sound not discipline.

36.text: My father, let Job be tried even to the end: cease not from the man of iniquity.

37.text: Because he addeth blasphemy upon his sins, let him be tied fast in the mean time amongst us: and then let him provoke God to judgment with his speeches.

1.text: Moreover Eliu spoke these words:

2.text: Doth thy thought seem right to thee, that thou shouldst say: I am more just than God?

3.text: For thou saidst: That which is right doth not please thee: or what will it profit thee if I sin?

4.text: Therefore I will answer thy words, and thy friends with thee.

5.text: Look up to heaven and see, and behold the sky, that it is higher than thee.

6.text: If thou sin, what shalt thou hurt him? and if thy iniquities be multiplied, what shalt thou do against him?

7.text: And if thou do justly, what shalt thou give him, or what shall he receive of thy hand?

8.text: Thy wickedness may hurt a man that is like thee: and thy justice may help the son of man.

9.text: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they shall cry out: and shall wail for the violence of the arm of tyrants.

10.text: And he hath not said: Where is God, who made me, who hath given songs in the night?

11.text: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and instructeth us more than the fowls of the air.

12.text: There shall they cry, and he will not hear, because of the pride of evil men.

13.text: God therefore will not hear in vain, and the Almighty will look into the causes of every one.

14.text: Yea when thou shalt say: He considereth not: be judged before him, and expect him.

15.text: For he doth not now bring on his fury, neither doth he revenge wickedness exceedingly.

16.text: Therefore Job openeth his mouth in vain, and multiplieth words without knowledge.

1.text: Eliu also proceeded, and said:

2.text: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee: for I have yet somewhat to speak in God’s behalf.

3.text: I will repeat my knowledge from the beginning, and I will prove my Maker just.

4.text: For indeed my words are without a lie, and perfect knowledge shall be proved to thee.

5.text: God doth not cast away the mighty, whereas he himself also is mighty.

6.text: But he saveth not the wicked, and he giveth judgment to the poor.

7.text: He will not take away his eyes from the just, and he placeth kings on the throne for ever, and they are exalted.

8.text: And if they shall be in chains, and be bound with the cords of poverty:

9.text: He shall shew them their works, and their wicked deeds, because they have been violent.

10.text: He also shall open their ear, to correct them: and shall speak, that they may return from iniquity.

11.text: If they shall hear and observe, they shall accomplish their days in good, and their years in glory.

12.text: But if they hear not, they shall pass by the sword, and shall be consumed in folly.

13.text: Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God, neither shall they cry when they are bound.

14.text: Their soul shall die in a storm, and their life among the effeminate.

15.text: He shall deliver the poor out of his distress, and shall open his ear in affliction.

16.text: Therefore he shall set thee at large out of the narrow mouth, and which hath no foundation under it: and the rest of thy table shall be full of fatness.

17.text: Thy cause hath been judged as that of the wicked, cause and judgment thou shalt recover.

18.text: Therefore let not anger overcome thee to oppress any man: neither let multitude of gifts turn thee aside.

19.text: Lay down thy greatness without tribulation, and all the mighty of strength.

20.text: Prolong not the night that people may come up for them.

21.text: Beware thou turn not aside to iniquity: for this thou hast begun to follow after misery.

22.text: Behold, God is high in his strength, and none is like him among the lawgivers.

23.text: Who can search out his ways? or who can say to him: Thou has wrought iniquity?

24.text: Remember that thou knowest not his work, concerning which men have sung.

25.text: All men see him, every one beholdeth afar off.

26.text: Behold, God is great, exceeding our knowledge: the number of his years is inestimable.

27.text: He lifteth up the drops of rain, and poureth out showers like floods:

28.text: Which flow from the clouds that cover all above.

29.text: If he will spread out clouds as his tent,

30.text: And lighten with his light from above, he shall cover also the ends of the sea.

31.text: For by these he judgeth people, and giveth food to many mortals.

32.text: In his hands he hideth the light, and commandeth it to come again.

33.text: He sheweth his friend concerning it, that it is his possession, and that he may come up to it.

1.text: At this my heart trembleth, and is moved out of its place.

2.text: Hear ye attentively the terror of his voice, and the sound that cometh out of his mouth.

3.text: He beholdeth under all the heavens, and his light is upon the ends of the earth.

4.text: After it a noise shall roar, he shall thunder with the voice of his majesty, and shall not be found out, when his voice shall be heard.

5.text: God shall thunder wonderfully with his voice, he that doth great and unsearchable things.

6.text: He commandeth the snow to go down upon the earth, and the winter rain, and the shower of his strength.

7.text: He sealeth up the hand of all men, that every one may know his works.

8.text: Then the beast shall go into his covert, and shall abide in his den.

9.text: Out of the inner parts shall a tempest come, and cold out of the north.

10.text: When God bloweth there cometh frost, and again the waters are poured out abundantly.

11.text: Corn desireth clouds, and the clouds spread their light:

12.text: Which go round about, whithersoever the will of him that governeth them shall lead them, to whatsoever he shall command them upon the face of the whole earth:

13.text: Whether in one tribe, or in his own land, or in what place soever of his mercy he shall command them to be found.

14.text: Hearken to these things, Job: Stand, and consider the wondrous works of God.

15.text: Dost thou know when God commanded the rains, to shew his light of his clouds?

16.text: Knowest thou the great paths of the clouds, and the perfect knowledges?

17.text: Are not thy garments hot, when the south wind blows upon the earth?

18.text: Thou perhaps hast made the heavens with him, which are most strong, as if they were of molten brass.

19.text: shew us what we may say to him: for we are wrapped up in darkness.

20.text: Who shall tell him the things I speak? even if a man shall speak, he shall be swallowed up.

21.text: But now they see not the light: the air on a sudden shall be thickened into clouds, and the wind shall pass and drive them away.

22.text: Cold cometh out of the north, and to God praise with fear.

23.text: We cannot find him worthily: he is great in strength, and in judgment, and in justice, and he is ineffable.

24.text: Therefore men shall fear him, and all that seem to themselves to be wise, shall not dare to behold him.

1.text: Then the Lord answered Job out of a whirlwind, and said:

2.text: Who is this that wrappeth up sentences in unskillful words?

3.text: Gird up thy loins like a man: I will ask thee, and answer thou me.

4.text: Where wast thou when I laid up the foundations of the earth? tell me if thou hast understanding.

5.text: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?

6.text: Upon what are its bases grounded? or who laid the corner stone thereof,

7.text: When the morning stars praised me together, and all the sons of God made a joyful melody?

8.text: Who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke forth as issuing out of the womb:

9.text: When I made a cloud the garment thereof, and wrapped it in a mist as in swaddling bands?

10.text: I set my bounds around it, and made it bars and doors:

11.text: And I said: Hitherto thou shalt come, and shalt go no further, and here thou shalt break thy swelling waves.

12.text: Didst thou since thy birth command the morning, and shew the dawning of the day its place?

13.text: And didst thou hold the extremities of the earth shaking them, and hast thou shaken the ungodly out of it?

14.text: The seal shall be restored as clay, and shall stand as a garment:

15.text: From the wicked their light shall be taken away, and the high arm shall be broken.

16.text: Hast thou entered into the depths of the sea, and walked in the lowest parts of the deep?

17.text: Have the gates of death been opened to thee, and hast thou seen the darksome doors?

18.text: Hast thou considered the breadth of the earth? tell me, if thou knowest all things?

19.text: Where is the way where light dwelleth, and where is the place of darkness:

20.text: That thou mayst bring every thing to its own bounds, and understand the paths of the house thereof.

21.text: Didst thou know then that thou shouldst be born? and didst thou know the number of thy days?

22.text: Hast thou entered into the storehouses of the snow, or has thou beheld the treasures of the hail:

23.text: Which I have prepared for the time of the enemy, against the day of battle and war?

24.text: By what way is the light spread, and heat divided upon the earth?

25.text: Who gave a course to violent showers, or a way for noisy thunder:

26.text: That it should rain on the earth without man in the wilderness, where no mortal dwelleth:

27.text: That it should fill the desert and desolate land, and should bring forth green grass?

28.text: Who is the father of rain? or who begot the drops of dew?

29.text: Out of whose womb came the ice; and the frost from heaven who hath gendered it?

30.text: The waters are hardened like a stone, and the surface of the deep is congealed.

31.text: Shalt thou be able to join together the shining stars the Pleiades, or canst thou stop the turning about of Arcturus?

32.text: Canst thou bring forth the day star in its time, and make the evening star to rise upon the children of the earth?

33.text: Dost thou know the order of heaven, and canst thou set down the reason thereof on the earth?

34.text: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that an abundance of waters may cover thee?

35.text: Canst thou send lightnings, and will they go, and will they return and say to thee: Here we are?

36.text: Who hath put wisdom in the heart of man? or who gave the cock understanding?

37.text: Who can declare the order of the heavens, or who can make the harmony of heaven to sleep?

38.text: When was the dust poured on the earth, and the clods fastened together?

39.text: Wilt thou take the prey for the lioness, and satisfy the appetite of her whelps,

40.text: When they couch in the dens and lie in wait in holes?

41.text: Who provideth food for the raven, when her young ones cry to God, wandering about, because they have no meat?

1.text: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats bring forth among the rocks, or hast thou observed the hinds when they fawn?

2.text: Hast thou numbered the months of their conceiving, or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

3.text: They bow themselves to bring forth young, and they cast them, and send forth roarings.

4.text: Their young are weaned and go to feed: they go forth, and return not to them.

5.text: Who hath sent out the wild ass free, and who hath loosed his bonds?

6.text: To whom I have given a house in the wilderness, and his dwellings in the barren land.

7.text: He scorneth the multitude of the city, he heareth not the cry of the driver.

8.text: He looketh round about the mountains of his pasture, and seeketh for every green thing.

9.text: Shall the rhinoceros be willing to serve thee, or will he stay at thy crib?

10.text: Canst thou bind the rhinoceros with thy thong to plough, or will he break the clods of the valleys after thee?

11.text: Wilt thou have confidence in his great strength, and leave thy labours to him?

12.text: Wilt thou trust him that he will render thee the seed, and gather it into thy barnfloor?

13.text: The wing of the ostrich is like the wings of the heron, and of the hawk.

14.text: When she leaveth her eggs on the earth, thou perhaps wilt warm them in the dust.

15.text: She forgetteth that the foot may tread upon them, or that the beasts of the field may break them.

16.text: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers, she hath laboured in vain, no fear constraining her.

17.text: For God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he given her understanding.

18.text: When time shall be, she setteth up her wings on high: she scorneth the horse and his rider.

19.text: Wilt thou give strength to the horse, or clothe his neck with neighing?

20.text: Wilt thou lift him up like the locusts? the glory of his nostrils is terror.

21.text: He breaketh up the earth with his hoof, he pranceth boldly, he goeth forward to meet armed men.

22.text: He despiseth fear, he turneth not his back to the sword,

23.text: Above him shall the quiver rattle, the spear and shield shall glitter.

24.text: Chasing and raging he swalloweth the ground, neither doth he make account when the noise of the trumpet soundeth.

25.text: When he heareth the trumpet he saith: Ha, ha: he smelleth the battle afar off, the encouraging of the captains, and the shouting of the army.

26.text: Doth the hawk wax feathered by thy wisdom, spreading her wings to the south?

27.text: Will the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest in high places?

28.text: She abideth among the rocks, and dwelleth among cragged flints, and stony hills, where there is no access.

29.text: From thence she looketh for the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.

30.text: Her young ones shall suck up blood: and wheresoever the carcass shall be, she is immediately there.

1.text: And the Lord went on, and said to Job:

2.text: Shall he that contendeth with God be so easily silenced? surely he that reproveth God, ought to answer him.

3.text: Then Job answered the Lord, and said:

4.text: What can I answer, who hath spoken inconsiderately? I will lay my hand upon my mouth.

5.text: One thing I have spoken, which I wish I had not said: and another, to which I will add no more.

6.text: And the Lord answering Job out of the whirlwind, said:

7.text: Gird up thy loins like a man: I will ask thee, and do thou tell me.

8.text: Wilt thou make void my judgment: and condemn me, that thou mayst be justified?

9.text: And hast thou an arm like God, and canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

10.text: Clothe thyself with beauty, and set thyself up on high and be glorious, and put on goodly garments.

11.text: Scatter the proud in thy indignation, and behold every arrogant man, and humble him.

12.text: Look on all that are proud, and confound them, and crush the wicked in their place.

13.text: Hide them in the dust together, and plunge their faces into the pit.

14.text: Then I will confess that thy right hand is able to save thee.

15.text: Behold behemoth whom I made with thee, he eateth grass like an ox.

16.text: His strength is in his loins, and his force in the navel of his belly.

17.text: He setteth up his tail like a cedar, the sinews of his testicles are wrapped together.

18.text: His bones are like pipes of brass, his gristle like plates of iron.

19.text: He is the beginning of the ways of God, who made him, he will apply his sword.

20.text: To him the mountains bring forth grass: there all the beasts of the field shall play.

21.text: He sleepeth under the shadow, in the covert of the reed, and in moist places.

22.text: The shades cover his shadow, the willows of the brook shall compass him about.

23.text: Behold, he will drink up a river, and not wonder: and he trusteth that the Jordan may run into his mouth.

24.text: In his eyes as with a hook he shall take him, and bore through his nostrils with stakes.

1.text: Canst thou draw out the leviathan with a hook, or canst thou tie his tongue with a cord?

2.text: Canst thou put a ring in his nose, or bore through his jaw with a buckle?

3.text: Will he make many supplications to thee, or speak soft words to thee?

4.text: Will he make a covenant with thee, and wilt thou take him to be a servant for ever?

5.text: Shalt thou play with him as with a bird, or tie him up for thy handmaids?

6.text: Shall friends cut him in pieces, shall merchants divide him?

7.text: Wilt thou fill nets with his skin, and the cabins of fishes with his head?

8.text: Lay thy hand upon him: remember the battle, and speak no more.

9.text: Behold his hope shall fail him, and in the sight of all he shall be cast down.

10.text: I will not stir him up, like one that is cruel: for who can resist my countenance?

11.text: Who hath given me before that I should repay him? All things that are under heaven are mine.

12.text: I will not spare him, nor his mighty words, and framed to make supplication.

13.text: Who can discover the face of his garment? or who can go into the midst of his mouth?

14.text: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth are terrible round about.

15.text: His body is like molten shields, shut close up with scales pressing upon one another.

16.text: One is joined to another, and not so much as any air can come between them:

17.text: They stick one to another and they hold one another fast, and shall not be separated.

18.text: His sneezing is like the shining of fire, and his eyes like the eyelids of the morning.

19.text: Out of his mouth go forth lamps, like torches of lighted fire.

20.text: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, like that of a pot heated and boiling.

21.text: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame cometh forth out of his mouth.

22.text: In his neck strength shall dwell, and want goeth before his face.

23.text: The members of his flesh cleave one to another: he shall send lightnings against him, and they shall not be carried to another place.

24.text: His heart shall be as hard as a stone, and as firm as a smith’s anvil.

25.text: When he shall raise him up, the angels shall fear, and being affrighted shall purify themselves.

26.text: When a sword shall lay at him, it shall not be able to hold, nor a spear, nor a breastplate.

27.text: For he shall esteem iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.

28.text: The archer shall not put him to flight, the stones of the sling are to him like stubble.

29.text: As stubble will he esteem the hammer, and he will laugh him to scorn who shaketh the spear.

30.text: The beams of the sun shall be under him, and he shall strew gold under him like mire.

31.text: He shall make the deep sea to boil like a pot, and shall make it as when ointments boil.

32.text: A path shall shine after him, he shall esteem the deep as growing old.

33.text: There is no power upon earth that can be compared with him who was made to fear no one.

34.text: He beholdeth every high thing, he is king over all the children of pride.

1.text: Then Job answered the Lord, and said:

2.text: I know that thou canst do all things, and no thought is hid from thee.

3.text: Who is this that hideth counsel without knowledge? Therefore I have spoken unwisely, and things that above measure exceeded my knowledge.

4.text: Hear, and I will speak: I will ask thee, and do thou tell me.

5.text: With the hearing of the ear, I have heard thee, but now my eye seeth thee.

6.text: Therefore I reprehend myself, and do penance in dust and ashes.

7.text: And after the Lord had spoken these words to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Themanite: My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends, because you have not spoken the thing that is right before me, as my servant Job hath.

8.text: Take unto you therefore seven oxen, and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer for yourselves a holocaust: and my servant Job shall pray for you: his face I will accept, that folly be not imputed to you: for you have not spoken right things before me, as my servant Job hath.

9.text: So Eliphaz the Themanite, and Baldad the Suhite, and Sophar the Naamathite went, and did as the Lord had spoken to them, and the Lord accepted the face of Job.

10.text: The Lord also was turned at the penance of Job, when he prayed for his friends. And the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.

11.text: And all his brethren came to him, and all his sisters, and all that knew him before, and they ate bread with him in his house: and bemoaned him, and comforted him upon all the evil that God had brought upon him. And every man gave him one ewe, and one earring of gold.

12.text: And the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. And he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.

13.text: And he had seven sons, and three daughters.

14.text: And he called the names of one Dies, and the name of the second Cassia, and the name of the third Cornustibil.

15.text: And there were not found in all the earth women so beautiful as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.

16.text: And Job lived after these things, a hundred and forty years, and he saw his children, and his children’s children, unto the fourth generation, and he died an old man, and full of days.

1.text: The parables of Solomon, the son of David, king of Israel.

2.text: To know wisdom, and instruction:

3.text: To understand the words of prudence: and to receive the instruction of doctrine, justice, and judgment, and equity:

4.text: To give subtilty to little ones, to the young man knowledge and understanding.

5.text: A wise man shall hear and shall be wiser: and he that understandeth, shall possess governments.

6.text: He shall understand a parable, and the interpretation, the words of the wise, and their mysterious sayings.

7.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. Fools despise wisdom and instruction.

8.text: My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother:

9.text: That grace may be added to thy head, and a chain of gold to thy neck.

10.text: My son, if sinners shall entice thee, consent not to them.

11.text: If they shall say: Come with us, let us lie in wait for blood, let us hide snares for the innocent without cause:

12.text: Let us swallow him up alive like hell, and whole as one that goeth down into the pit.

13.text: We shall find all precious substance, we shall fill our houses with spoils.

14.text: Cast in thy lot with us, let us all have one purse.

15.text: My son, walk not thou with them, restrain thy foot from their paths.

16.text: For their feet run to evil, and make haste to shed blood.

17.text: But a net is spread in vain before the eyes of them that have wings.

18.text: And they themselves lie in wait for their own blood, and practise deceits against their own souls.

19.text: So the ways of every covetous man destroy the souls of the possessors.

20.text: Wisdom preacheth abroad, she uttereth her voice in the streets:

21.text: At the head of multitudes she crieth out, in the entrance of the gates of the city she uttereth her words, saying:

22.text: O children, how long will you love childishness, and fools covet those things which are hurtful to themselves, and the unwise hate knowledge?

23.text: Turn ye at my reproof: behold I will utter my spirit to you, and will shew you my words.

24.text: Because I called, and you refused: I stretched out my hand, and there was none that regarded.

25.text: You have despised all my counsel, and have neglected my reprehensions.

26.text: I also will laugh in your destruction, and will mock when that shall come to you which you feared.

27.text: When sudden calamity shall fall on you, and destruction, as a tempest, shall be at hand: when tribulation and distress shall come upon you:

28.text: Then shall they call upon me, and I will not hear: they shall rise in the morning and shall not find me:

29.text: Because they have hated instruction and received not the fear of the Lord,

30.text: Nor consented to my counsel, but despised all my reproof.

31.text: Therefore they shall eat the fruit of their own way, and shall be filled with their own devices.

32.text: The turning away of little ones shall kill them, and the prosperity of fools shall destroy them.

33.text: But he that shall hear me, shall rest without terror, and shall enjoy abundance, without fear of evils.

1.text: My son, if thou wilt receive my words, and wilt hide my commandments with thee,

2.text: That thy ear may hearken to wisdom: Incline thy heart to know prudence:

3.text: For if thou shalt call for wisdom, and incline thy heart to prudence:

4.text: If thou shalt seek her as money, and shalt dig for her as for a treasure:

5.text: Then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord, and shalt find the knowledge of God.

6.text: Because the Lord giveth wisdom: and out of his mouth cometh prudence and knowledge.

7.text: He will keep the salvation of the righteous, and protect them that walk in simplicity.

8.text: Keeping the paths of justice, and guarding the ways of saints.

9.text: Then shalt thou understand justice, and judgment, and equity, and every good path.

10.text: If wisdom shall enter into thy heart, and knowledge please thy soul:

11.text: Counsel shall keep thee, and prudence shall preserve thee,

12.text: That thou mayst be delivered from the evil way, and from the man that speaketh perverse things:

13.text: Who leave the right way, and walk by dark ways:

14.text: Who are glad when they have done evil, and rejoice in most wicked things:

15.text: Whose ways are perverse, and their steps infamous.

16.text: That thou mayst be delivered from the strange women, and from the stranger, who softeneth her words:

17.text: And forsaketh the guide of her youth,

18.text: And hath forgotten the covenant of her God: for her house inclineth unto death, and her paths to hell.

19.text: None that go in unto her shall return again, neither shall they take hold of the paths of life,

20.text: That thou mayst walk in a good way: and mayst keep the paths of the just.

21.text: For they that are upright shall dwell in the earth, and the simple shall continue in it.

22.text: But the wicked shall be destroyed from the earth: and they that do unjustly shall be taken away from it.

1.text: My son, forget not my law, and let thy heart keep my commandments.

2.text: For they shall add to thee length of days, and years of life and peace.

3.text: Let not mercy and truth leave thee, put them about thy neck, and write them in the tables of thy heart:

4.text: And thou shalt find grace and good understanding before God and men.

5.text: Have confidence in the Lord with all thy heart, and lean not upon thy own prudence.

6.text: In all thy ways think on him, and he will direct thy steps.

7.text: Be not wise in thy own conceit: fear God, and depart from evil:

8.text: For it shall be health to thy navel, and moistening to thy bones.

9.text: Honour the Lord with thy substance, and give him of the first of all thy fruits:

10.text: And thy barns shall be filled with abundance, and thy presses shall run over with wine.

11.text: My son, reject not the correction of the Lord: and do not faint when thou art chastised by him:

12.text: For whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth: and as a father in the son he pleaseth himself.

13.text: Blessed is the man that findeth wisdom and is rich in prudence:

14.text: The purchasing thereof is better than the merchandise of silver, and her fruit than the chiefest and purest gold:

15.text: She is more precious than all riches: and all the things that are desired, are not to be compared with her.

16.text: Length of days is in her right hand, and in her left hand riches and glory.

17.text: Her ways are beautiful ways, and all her paths are peaceable.

18.text: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her: and he that shall retain her is blessed.

19.text: The Lord by wisdom hath founded the earth, hath established the heavens by prudence.

20.text: By his wisdom the depths have broken out, and the clouds grow thick with dew.

21.text: My son, let not these things depart from thy eyes: keep the law and counsel:

22.text: And there shall be life to thy soul, and grace to thy mouth.

23.text: Then shalt thou walk confidently in thy way, and thy foot shall not stumble:

24.text: If thou sleep, thou shalt not fear: thou shalt rest, and thy sleep shall be sweet.

25.text: Be not afraid of sudden fear, nor of the power of the wicked falling upon thee.

26.text: For the Lord will be at thy side, and will keep thy foot that thou be not taken.

27.text: Do not withhold him from doing good, who is able: if thou art able, do good thyself also.

28.text: Say not to thy friend: Go, and come again: and tomorrow I will give to thee: when thou canst give at present.

29.text: Practise not evil against thy friend, when he hath confidence in thee.

30.text: Strive not against a man without cause, when he hath done thee no evil.

31.text: Envy not the unjust man, and do not follow his ways:

32.text: For every mocker is an abomination to the Lord, and his communication is with the simple.

33.text: Want is from the Lord in the house of the wicked: but the habitations of the just shall be blessed.

34.text: He shall scorn the scorners, and to the meek he will give grace.

35.text: The wise shall possess glory: the promotion of fools is disgrace.

1.text: Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father, and attend that you may know prudence.

2.text: I will give you a good gift, forsake not my law.

3.text: For I also was my father’s son, tender and as an only son in the sight of my mother:

4.text: And he taught me, and said: Let thy heart receive my words, keep my commandments, and thou shalt live.

5.text: Get wisdom, get prudence: forget not, neither decline from the words of my mouth.

6.text: Forsake her not, and she shall keep thee: love her, and she shall preserve thee.

7.text: The beginning of wisdom, get wisdom, and with all thy possession purchase prudence.

8.text: Take hold on her, and she shall exalt thee: thou shalt be glorified by her, when thou shalt embrace her.

9.text: She shall give to thy head increase of graces, and protect thee with a noble crown.

10.text: Hear, O my son, and receive my words, that years of life may be multiplied to thee.

11.text: I will shew thee the way of wisdom, I will lead thee by the paths of equity:

12.text: Which when thou shalt have entered, thy steps shall not be straitened, and when thou runnest thou shalt not meet a stumblingblock.

13.text: Take hold on instruction, leave it not: keep it, because it is thy life.

14.text: Be not delighted in the paths of the wicked, neither let the way of evil men please thee.

15.text: Flee from it, pass not by it: go aside, and forsake it.

16.text: For they sleep not except they have done evil: and their sleep is taken away unless they have made some to fall.

17.text: They eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of iniquity.

18.text: But the path of the just, as a shining light, goeth forwards and increaseth even to perfect day.

19.text: The way of the wicked is darksome: they know not where they fall.

20.text: My son, hearken to my words, and incline thy ear to my sayings.

21.text: Let them not depart from thy eyes, keep them in the midst of thy heart:

22.text: For they are life to those that find them, and health to all flesh.

23.text: With all watchfulness keep thy heart, because life issueth out from it.

24.text: Remove from thee a froward mouth, and let detracting lips be far from thee.

25.text: Let thy eyes look straight on, and let thy eyelids go before thy steps.

26.text: Make straight the path for thy feet, and all thy ways shall be established.

27.text: Decline not to the right hand, nor to the left: turn away thy foot from evil. For the Lord knoweth the ways that are on the right hand: but those are perverse which are on the left hand. But he will make thy courses straight, he will bring forward thy ways in peace.

1.text: My son, attend to my wisdom, and incline thy ear to my prudence.

2.text: That thou mayst keep thoughts, and thy lips may preserve instruction. Mind not the deceit of a woman.

3.text: For the lips of a harlot are like a honeycomb dropping, and her throat is smoother than oil.

4.text: But her end is bitter as wormwood, and sharp as a two-edged sword.

5.text: Her feet go down into death, and her steps go in as far as hell.

6.text: They walk not by the path of life, her steps are wandering, and unaccountable.

7.text: Now therefore, my son, hear me, and depart not from the words of my mouth.

8.text: Remove thy way far from her, and come not nigh the doors of her house.

9.text: Give not thy honour to strangers, and thy years to the cruel.

10.text: Lest strangers be filled with thy strength, and thy labours be in another man’s house,

11.text: And thou mourn it the last, when thou shalt have spent thy flesh and thy body, and say:

12.text: Why have I hated instruction, and my heart consented not to reproof,

13.text: And have not heard the voice of them that taught me, and have not inclined my ear to masters?

14.text: I have almost been in all evil, in the midst of the church and of the congregation.

15.text: Drink water out of thy own cistern, and the streams of thy own well:

16.text: Let thy fountains be conveyed abroad, and in the streets divide thy waters.

17.text: Keep them to thyself alone, neither let strangers be partakers with thee.

18.text: Let thy vein be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of thy youth:

19.text: Let her be thy dearest hind, and most agreeable fawn: let her breasts inebriate thee at all times; be thou delighted continually with her love.

20.text: Why art thou seduced, my son, by a strange woman, and art cherished in the bosom of another?

21.text: The Lord beholdeth the ways of man, and considereth all his steps.

22.text: His own iniquities catch the wicked, and he is fast bound with the ropes of his own sins.

23.text: He shall die, because he hath not received instruction, and in the multitude of his folly he shall be deceived.

1.text: My son, if thou be surety for thy friend, thou hast engaged fast thy hand to a stranger.

2.text: Thou art ensnared with the words of thy mouth, and caught with thy own words.

3.text: Do therefore, my son, what I say, and deliver thyself: because thou art fallen into the hand of thy neighbour. Run about, make haste, stir up thy friend:

4.text: Give not sleep to thy eyes, neither let thy eyelids slumber.

5.text: Deliver thyself as a doe from the hand, and as a bird from the hand of the fowler.

6.text: Go to the ant, O sluggard, and consider her ways, and learn wisdom:

7.text: Which, although she hath no guide, nor master, nor captain,

8.text: Provideth her meat for herself in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.

9.text: How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou rise out of thy sleep?

10.text: Thou wilt sleep a little, thou wilt slumber a little, thou wilt fold thy hands a little to sleep:

11.text: And want shall come upon thee, as a traveller, and poverty as a man armed. But if thou be diligent, thy harvest shall come as a fountain, and want shall flee far from thee.

12.text: A man that is an apostate, an unprofitable man, walketh with a perverse mouth,

13.text: He winketh with the eyes, presseth with the foot, speaketh with the finger.

14.text: With a wicked heart he deviseth evil, and at all times he soweth discord.

15.text: To such a one his destruction shall presently come, and he shall suddenly be destroyed, and shall no longer have any remedy.

16.text: Six things there are, which the Lord hateth, and the seventh his soul detesteth:

17.text: Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood,

18.text: A heart that deviseth wicked plots, feet that are swift to run into mischief,

19.text: A deceitful witness that uttereth lies, and him that soweth discord among brethren.

20.text: My son, keep the commandments of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother.

21.text: Bind them in thy heart continually, and put them about thy neck.

22.text: When thou walkest, let them go with thee: when thou sleepest, let them keep thee; and when thou awakest, talk with them.

23.text: Because the commandment is a lamp, and the law a light, and reproofs of instruction are the way of life:

24.text: That they may keep thee from the evil woman, and from the flattering tongue of the stranger.

25.text: Let not thy heart covet her beauty, be not caught with her winks:

26.text: For the price of a harlot is scarce one loaf: but the woman catcheth the precious soul of a man.

27.text: Can a man hide fire in his bosom, and his garments not burn?

28.text: Or can he walk upon hot coals, and his feet not be burnt?

29.text: So he that goeth in to his neighbour’s wife, shall not be clean when he shall touch her.

30.text: The fault is not so great when a man hath stolen: for he stealeth to fill his hungry soul:

31.text: And if he be taken he shall restore sevenfold, and shall give up all the substance of his house.

32.text: But he that is an adulterer, for the folly of his heart shall destroy his own soul:

33.text: He gathereth to himself shame and dishonour, and his reproach shall not be blotted out:

34.text: Because the jealousy and rage of the husband will not spare in the day of revenge,

35.text: Nor will he yield to any man’s prayers, nor will he accept for satisfaction ever so many gifts.

1.text: My son, keep my words, and lay up my precepts with thee. Son,

2.text: Keep my commandments, and thou shalt live: and my law as the apple of thy eye:

3.text: Bind it upon thy fingers, write it upon the tables of thy heart.

4.text: Say to wisdom: Thou art my sister: and call prudence thy friend,

5.text: That she may keep thee from the woman that is not thine, and from the stranger who sweeteneth her words.

6.text: For I look out of the window of my house through the lattice,

7.text: And I see little ones, I behold a foolish young man,

8.text: Who passeth through the street by the corner, and goeth nigh the way of her house.

9.text: In the dark, when it grows late, in the darkness and obscurity of the night,

10.text: And behold a woman meeteth him in harlot’s attire prepared to deceive souls; talkative and wandering,

11.text: Not bearing to be quiet, not able to abide still at home,

12.text: Now abroad, now in the streets, now lying in wait near the corners.

13.text: And catching the young man, she kisseth him, and with an impudent face, flattereth, saying:

14.text: I vowed victims for prosperity, this day I have paid my vows.

15.text: Therefore I am come out to meet thee, desirous to see thee, and I have found thee.

16.text: I have woven my bed with cords, I have covered it with painted tapestry, brought from Egypt.

17.text: I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.

18.text: Come, let us be inebriated with the breasts, and let us enjoy the desired embraces, till the day appear.

19.text: For my husband is not at home, he is gone a very long journey.

20.text: He took with him a bag of money: he will return home the day of the full moon.

21.text: She entangled him with many words, and drew him away with the flattery of her lips.

22.text: Immediately he followeth her as an ox led to be a victim, and as a lamb playing the wanton, and not knowing that he is drawn like a fool to bonds,

23.text: Till the arrow pierce his liver: as if a bird should make haste to the snare, and knoweth not that his life is in danger.

24.text: Now therefore, my son, hear me, and attend to the words of my mouth.

25.text: Let not thy mind be drawn away in her ways: neither be thou deceived with her paths.

26.text: For she hath cast down many wounded, and the strongest have been slain by her.

27.text: Her house is the way to hell, reaching even to the inner chambers of death.

1.text: Doth not wisdom cry aloud, and prudence put forth her voice?

2.text: Standing in the top of the highest places by the way, in the midst of the paths.

3.text: Beside the gates of the city, in the very doors she speaketh, saying:

4.text: O ye men, to you I call, and my voice is to the sons of men.

5.text: O little ones, understand subtilty, and ye unwise, take notice.

6.text: Hear, for I will speak of great things: and my lips shall be opened to preach right things.

7.text: My mouth shall meditate truth, and my lips shall hate wickedness.

8.text: All my words are just, there is nothing wicked nor perverse in them.

9.text: They are right to them that understand, and just to them that find knowledge.

10.text: Receive my instruction, and not money: choose knowledge rather than gold.

11.text: For wisdom is better than all the most precious things: and whatsoever may be desired cannot be compared to it.

12.text: I wisdom dwell in counsel, and am present in learned thoughts.

13.text: The fear of the Lord hateth evil: I hate arrogance, and pride, and every wicked way, and a mouth with a double tongue.

14.text: Counsel and equity is mine, prudence is mine, strength is mine.

15.text: By me kings reign, and lawgivers decree just things,

16.text: By me princes rule, and the mighty decree justice.

17.text: I love them that love me: and they that in the morning early watch for me, shall find me.

18.text: With me are riches and glory, glorious riches and justice.

19.text: For my fruit is better than gold and the precious stone, and my blossoms than choice silver.

20.text: I walk in the way of justice, in the midst of the paths of judgment,

21.text: That I may enrich them that love me, and may fill their treasures.

22.text: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made any thing from the beginning.

23.text: I was set up from eternity, and of old before the earth was made.

24.text: The depths were not as yet, and I was already conceived. neither had the fountains of waters as yet sprung out:

25.text: The mountains with their huge bulk had not as yet been established: before the hills I was brought forth:

26.text: He had not yet made the earth, nor the rivers, nor the poles of the world.

27.text: When he prepared the heavens, I was present: when with a certain law and compass he enclosed the depths:

28.text: When he established the sky above, and poised the fountains of waters:

29.text: When he compassed the sea with its bounds, and set a law to the waters that they should not pass their limits: when he balanced the foundations of the earth;

30.text: I was with him forming all things: and was delighted every day, playing before him at all times;

31.text: Playing in the world: and my delights were to be with the children of men.

32.text: Now therefore, ye children, hear me: Blessed are they that keep my ways.

33.text: Hear instruction and be wise, and refuse it not.

34.text: Blessed is the man that heareth me, and that watcheth daily at my gates, and waiteth at the posts of my doors.

35.text: He that shall find me, shall find life, and shall have salvation from the Lord:

36.text: But he that shall sin against me, shall hurt his own soul. All that hate me love death.

1.text: Wisdom hath built herself a house, she hath hewn her out seven pillars.

2.text: She hath slain her victims, mingled her wine, and set forth her table.

3.text: She hath sent her maids to invite to the tower, and to the walls of the city:

4.text: Whosoever is a little one, let him come to me. And to the unwise she said:

5.text: Come, eat my bread, and drink the wine which I have mingled for you.

6.text: Forsake childishness, and live, and walk by the ways of prudence.

7.text: He that teacheth a scorner, doth an injury to himself: and he that rebuketh a wicked man, getteth himself a blot.

8.text: Rebuke not a scorner lest he hate thee. Rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.

9.text: Give an occasion to a wise man, and wisdom shall be added to him. Teach a just man, and he shall make haste to receive it.

10.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is prudence.

11.text: For by me shall thy days be multiplied, and years of life shall be added to thee.
